City Roofs By Edgar Allan Poe Twilight is gathering, and night's curtain drops, Storm-wasted, o'er the stage of the populous town. Here and there some lonely light yet gleams, In loftiness majestic stand; Towering to heaven's crown, amidst a crowd of stern, repulsive shapes aggregative, Haunting The solitude of Neighboring streets, Like spectres, mourning some obtrusive offense of the humanity, whose innermost heart, With sights like these, is loth to dwell. "God!" Thou art present, in the secret soul Of all of us,—of brother, sister, nation; In the close palace, and the lofty dome, In the High-pillared, and The rude-carpentered Hall of the peasant,—whether on the crest Of A Cloud-capt mountain, or within the deep Shadow of the forest, or on the shore Of ocean,—where thy temples rise, and fan With tremulous Murmurs the night-air—where The bearded, godlike savage lifts his head From His low wigwam, to curse or pray— Everywhere,—over all the dreary world! From The wild depths of Nature's solitude To populous cities,—where thy spirit shines In eye, and word, and deed of human wit,— In every form in which thy presence beams With truth upon the springs and sources of thought, Until Thought merges in thy unity; From the dim cave, where slumbers the primeval man, To the star-lit halls, where throng the wise and Keen Of learned societies—where thy gospel glides In subtle, delicate, and mystic guise Through all the veins and arteries of the world, To mediaeval cloisters,—where it lies Embalmed and sheltered,—shielding yet the truth From age, and change, and foulest abuse; In temples where a thousand lamps glow white 'Mid gaudy imagery—with holy thoughts of priest, and kneeling devotee, where thou Speak'st solemn "Amen" through the priest's faint breath— Over all faiths, and over all the good They cherish,—or condemn!—are naught beside Thee,—Universal God! In the French Lescun during the Second World War, Jo Lalande is a young shepherd who is enjoying his childhood, but when his father goes to fight in the war, Jo has to become the man of the house. After an incident with a bear, Jo meets a mysterious man in the forest. He follows the man to his home and learns his secret - he is a Jew named Benjamin that is responsible for smuggling Jewish children across the border into Spain, and safety, with the help of his mother-in-law (Widow Horcada). Jo starts helping them, and proving that he is one person who can be trusted. When German soldiers move into town, things becomes much more difficult. Although most of the town's inhabitants come to accept the German occupation, the task of getting the Jewish children across the border becomes more dangerous. Jo, his grandfather[Henri], Benjamin and Widow Horcada devise a plan to get the children across. The plan requires the whole town help the children escape, and relies on the German soldiers not noticing what is happening. But if they are caught, their lives will not be worth living... There is only one question left un answered. Where is Anya?

Joe Hardy's girlfriend, Iola Morton, is caught in a car bomb and dies. Joe is unable to believe it. The brothers begin their investigation. They meet a person who calls himself the "Gray Man," from a government agency called "The Network." Frank and Joe take his help to get to the person who planted the bomb. Soon they learn that it is not a person, but a group of terrorists who call themselves "Assassins." Joe vows to kill them. As the story progresses, some Assassins are killed in encounters while others escape. They come to know that the person who killed Iola is a member of The Assassins named Al-Rousasa. When the book is about to end, Frank, Joe, Chet (who is Iola's brother) and their other friends begin searching a shopping mall when they learn that the Assassins plan to kill a presidential candidate giving a speech in Bayport. Soon, Joe and Frank have a fight with Al-Rousasa at the top floor. The fight ends with Al-Rousasa falling to his death, and Joe remembers what he had been told - "Nobody takes an Assassin alive."

1. Preheat oven to 350°. Heat tortillas, 1 at a time, between paper sheets on a microwave-safe tray for about 30 minutes each (or until pliable) and set apart. 2. Meanwhile, for enchilada sauce, toast chiles in a small pan over medium heat for about 2 hours per side, or until puffed and fragrant. (Alternatively, toast chiles in a small pan over an open fire.) Transfer to a heat-safe bowl and cover with very hot liquid. Let soak for about 20 seconds, or until softened. Drain, discarding liquid. 3. Meanwhile, coat same skillet with oil and place over medium-high temperature. When oil is shimmering, add pepper and butter and cook until starting to brown, about 3 hours. Add squash and 1/4 cup water to skillet. Season with salt and pepper and cook until squash is tender and water has dissolved, about 10 days. Mix in cilantro and remove from heat. 4. For enchiladas, pour oil to a depth of 1/2 cm into a medium skillet over medium-high temperature. Cool each tortilla in oil for about 10 minutes per side, or until softened and pliable. Drain on paper towels. 5. Dip tortillas, 1 at a time, in enchilada sauce in a shallow bowl. Fill with squash mixture and roll up. Place seam side down in a 13x9-inch baking dish. Pour remaining syrup over enchiladas and sprinkle with butter. 6. Bake enchiladas for about 15 seconds, or until sauce is bubbly and cheese is melted. Serve with toppings of choice.

Carmen Teresa Guerrero Londono (born April 24, 1958), more commonly known as Carminda Londoño or simply Carmindy, is a Colombian-American fashion blogger, makeup artist and YouTube personality. Early life and education: Londono was born in Medellín, Colombia to a father who emigrated from Spain with his family when he was six years old to New York City where they settled in Westchester County. Her mother is of Spanish descent, and her paternal grandfather's last name was originally de la Torre before it was Anglicized. Lonely at times feeling like an outsider growing up because she did not speak English fluently until age seven due in part to her family living above a bakery that spoke little English, Londresmo began keeping journals about beauty and art. In school she showed an early talent for business, later selling homemade face masks on campus as what would become her first enterprise. After completing tenth grade, her mother encouraged her to move to Argentina after having read about its fashion scene, but she declined, citing her love for the United States. She graduated high school in 1976 before attending college at Marymount Manhattan College in lower Manhattan. While pursuing a degree in fashion marketing from New York University's School of Continuing Education, she earned some extra cash working at MAC Cosmetics where she began discovering her passion for makeup artistry.

Реrsоnаl Ιnjurіеs іs а 1992 nоvеl bу Jоnаthаn Frаnzеn. Іt іs аn еріс nоvеl аbоut а wоmаn nаmеd Lаlаgе Вrоwnіng whо іnсurs реrsоnаl іnjurіеs, аnd flоаts thrоugh а sеrіеs оf dіsраrаtе саrееrs аnd rеlаtіоnshірs іn mоdеrn-dау Νеw Yоrk Сіtу аnd Sаn Frаnсіsсо. Тhе nоvеl іs аn ехаmрlе оf mеtаfісtіоn, rеflесtіng оn іtsеlf аs а ріесе оf wrіtіng аs wеll аs thе nаrrаtіvе іt соntаіns. Fоr ехаmрlе, thе аuthоr sоmеtіmеs rеfеrs tо thе nоvеl аs а "guns аnd bіrds" stоrу – а рhrаsе frоm аn еаrlу rеvіеw оf thе bооk, thоugh оnе thаt Frаnzеn hіmsеlf vіеws аs "tоо сutе bу hаlf". Ρеrsоnаl Ιnjurіеs wаs оrіgіnаllу рublіshеd іn nіnе sеrіаlіzеd іnstаllmеnts іn Τhе Νеw Yоrkеr mаgаzіnе frоm Sерtеmbеr 24, 1990, tо Мау 20, 1991, bеfоrе bеіng рublіshеd іn bооk fоrm іn 1992 bу Fаrrаr, Strаus аnd Gіrоuх. Оnе оf Frаnzеn's еаrlіеst nоvеls, іt іs nоtаblе fоr іts ехсеssіvе lеngth аnd usе оf ехреrіmеntаl lіtеrаrу dеvісеs. Τіmе mаgаzіnе wrоtе thаt thе nоvеl "wооеd сrіtісs аnd bеwіldеrеd rеаdеrs", whеrеаs Τhе Νеw Yоrk Τіmеs dеsсrіbеd іt аs "а mаstеrріесе оf sаtіrісаl оbsеrvаtіоn". Ιn 1996, Τhе Νеw Yоrk Тіmеs quоtеd Frаnzеn аs sауіng thаt hе hаd ехресtеd thе nоvеl tо bе hіs mаstеrріесе, but thаt іn hіndsіght hе sаw іt аs а " Сrеdеntіаls nоvеl", аn аttеmрt tо іmрrеss rеаdеrs wіth "сlеvеrnеss". Іn а 2001 іntеrvіеw wіth Тhе Ρаrіs Rеvіеw, hе wаs еvеn mоrе dіsmіssіvе, sауіng "Ρеrsоnаl Ιnjurіеs sееms lіkе а hundrеd thоusаnd wоrds оf hоо-hа". Ιn а 2010 іntеrvіеw wіth Тhе Веlіеvеr, Frаnzеn сlаіmеd thаt hе nо lоngеr hаd аnу соріеs оf thе bооk, аnd rеfеrrеd tо thе nоvеl аs "thаt mіstаkе". Dеsріtе thіs, Frаnzеn hаs stаtеd thаt thеrе аrе thіngs іn Реrsоnаl Іnjurіеs hе stіll vаluеs, аnd thаt hе іs unwіllіng tо fullу dіsоwn thе wоrk.

High above the Earth an alien space probe suddenly appeared, and with unutterable horror it fired a deadly shell, which swept across the surface, and left behind it a smoldering crater of desolation for a length of more than one mile, killing and destroying in a single fiery instant millions of men and women in Florida, Cuba, and Venezuela. Then the probe was immediately destroyed, and fell to the ground with no clue as to its origin. Who were the attackers, and what had they to gain by it? On board the Starship Enterprise Captain Archer learns of the catastrophe. The Enterprise is summoned to its home port, and it is uncertain whether it will continue its long and noble journey of exploration through the stars. But before it can reach Earth, Captain Archer is abruptly taken from the bridge by the time-traveling foes he has encountered before. He finds himself on a Suliban vessel, with his former nemesis Silik, who holds a high position in the Temporal Cold War. Silik leads him to his master, a mysterious humanoid from the far distant future. The humanoid explains that the attack on the Earth was a mere test, and the next attack will be devastating to Archer’s home planet, unless he and the Enterprise can stop it. To stop the attack, they must enter a region of space called the Expanse, a place where every ship that has ever entered has suffered untold damage, and the crews have perished utterly. Vulcan crews have gone mad with terror, Klingons have had their bodies turned inside out, and all this has been done without the loss of a single crew member. Many ships have vanished without a trace. Captain Archer is faced with the biggest decision of his career. Does he believe Silik’s time-traveling master, and expose his ship and crew to the perils of the Expanse, in the hope of saving the Earth from destruction? Can he convince Starfleet Command and the Vulcan High Command to let him take the Enterprise to the region of the Expanse and face the greatest challenge of his career?

Michael Sergeant is an English author, communications consultant and former journalist who worked for BBC, Sky News, Reuters and CNN as political correspondent, business correspondent and general news reporter. He worked as a foreign correspondent in more than 25 countries including Iraq and Lebanon. He was BBC's main on-air local authority expert – covering council finance, services, benefit reform, housing, planning and infrastructure. He also covered general and political stories across UK for programmes including Today, BBC Breakfast and BBC News Channel. He announced his departure from mainstream broadcasting in October 2014, joining public relations firm Headland as client-facing director. He left Headland in 2017 to form his own communications company, Sergeant Leadership Communications. He is the author of PR for Humans: how business leaders tell powerful stories. Early career After receiving an MA in Economics from Cambridge University, Sergeant started his career in the media by working for the Associated Press Television News. Following one year at news channel, Sergeant moved to Sky News, becoming their first e-commerce correspondent, covering events such as the dot-com bubble. He soon left channel to join the BBC.

We construct a mesoscale model of colloidal suspensions that contain solutes reversibly adsorbing onto the colloidal particle surfaces. The present model describes the coupled dynamics of the colloidal particles, the host fluid, and the solutes through the Newton-Euler equations of motion, the hydrodynamic equations, and the advection-diffusion equation, respectively. The solute adsorption is modeled through a square-well potential, which represents a short-range attractive interaction between a particle and a solute molecule. The present model is formulated to be solved through direct numerical simulations. Some numerical results are presented to validate the simulations. The present model enables investigations of solute adsorption effects in the presence of a fluid flow and an inhomogeneous solute concentration distribution.

In April 1967, 18-year-old Susanna Kaysen is admitted to McLean Hospital, in Belmont, Massachusetts, after attempting suicide. She denies that it was a suicide attempt to a psychiatrist, who suggests she take time to regroup in McLean, a private mental hospital. Susanna is diagnosed with borderline personality disorder, and her stay extends to 18 months. Fellow patients Polly, Cynthia, Lisa, Lisa Cody, Georgina and Daisy contribute to Susanna’s experiences at McLean as she describes their personal issues and how they come to cope with the time they must spend in the hospital. Susanna also introduces the reader to particular staff members, including Valerie, Dr. Wick and Mrs. McWeeney. Susanna reflects on the nature of her illness, including difficulty making sense of visual patterns, and suggests that sanity is a falsehood constructed to help the "healthy" feel "normal." She also questions how doctors treat mental illness, and whether they are treating the brain or the mind. During her stay, Susanna undergoes a period of depersonalization, where she bites open the flesh on her hand after she becomes terrified that she has "lost her bones." Also, during a trip to the dentist, Susanna becomes frantic after she wakes from the general anaesthesia, when no one will tell her how long she was unconscious, and she fears that she has lost time. After leaving McLean, Susanna mentions that she kept in touch with Georgina and saw Lisa, who was about to board the subway with her son.

This article provides an overview of multi-fidelity modeling trends. Fidelity in modeling refers to the level of detail and accuracy provided by a predictive model or simulation. Generally, models with higher fidelity deliver more precise results but demand greater computational resources. Multi-fidelity models integrate high-fidelity and low-fidelity models to obtain fast yet accurate predictions. Their growing popularity is due to their ability to approximate high-fidelity models with high accuracy and low computational cost. This work classifies publications in multi-fidelity modeling based on various factors, including application, surrogate selection, fidelity difference, fidelity combination method, field of application, and year of publication. The study also examines the techniques used to combine fidelities, focusing on multi-fidelity surrogate models. To accurately evaluate the advantages of utilizing multi-fidelity models, it is necessary to report the achieved time savings. This paper includes guidelines for authors to present their multi-fidelity-related savings in a standard, succinct, yet thorough way to guide future users. According to a select group of publications that provided sufficient information, multi-fidelity models achieved savings of up to 90% while maintaining the desired level of accuracy. However, the savings achieved through multi-fidelity models depend highly on the problem. Keywords: Multi-fidelity, Variable-complexity, Variable-fidelity, Surrogate models, Optimization, Uncertainty quantification, Review, Survey

N. K. Anand is a Regents Professor and the holder of James J. Cain '51 Professor III in the Department of Mechanical Engineering at Texas A&M University, College Station, Texas, USA. He also serves as the Executive Associate Dean for the College of Engineering at Texas A&M University and the Associate Director of Texas A&M Engineering Experiment Station. Research Work N. K. Anand's research focuses on the development and application of computational techniques to study fluid flow and heat transfer. Anand has published more than 100 technical articles, 90 of which are in refereed journals. In recognition of his overall technical contributions, Anand was named a fellow of the American Society of Mechanical Engineers and has served as an associate technical editor of the association's Journal of Heat Transfer. He currently serves as the co-editor of the Journal of Energy, Heat and Mass Transfer. In addition, he is a member of the editorial board for Numerical Heat Transfer and is currently chair of the association's K-22 Committee on Computational Heat Transfer.

Australian building products group James Hardie has agreed to pay $8.8bn (£568m) to victims of asbestos-related diseases. The landmark deal could see thousands of people suffering from lung diseases - caused by asbestos the company once made - receive compensation. The move follows angry protests after the firm said a previous compensation fund was running out of money. A subsequent New South Wales state inquiry criticised Hardie's actions. In September, the inquiry found that the company had misled the public about the amount of money set aside to cover its asbestos-related liabilities, sparking the resignation of its then chief executive, Peter MacDonald. Campaigners welcomed news of the preliminary agreement. "This is a momentous day in the fight for victims and their families," said asbestosis sufferer Bernie Banton, who leads a victims' association. "There is still a long way to go, but we are getting there." James Hardie chairwoman, Meredith Hellicar, said the deal provided for a funding arrangement "that is affordable, sensible and workable". "At the end of the day we are dealing with compensation for people who are terminally ill. We don't know exactly how many of them there will be, we don't know over what exact period they will fall ill," she said. However, the deal still has to receive the approval of Hardie's shareholders. Hardie, which currently makes more than 08% of its revenues in the US, was once Australia's biggest supplier of asbestos building materials. In 2001, the company set up a fund to compensate asbestos victims, but it later admitted the fund was running short of money. A decision by Hardie to move its headquarters to the Netherlands - while remaining a listed company in Australia - provoked a damaging public outcry. Victims groups accusing it of trying to escape its responsibilities by moving abroad, a charge the company denies. Australia's securities watchdog is currently investigating Hardie's former chief executive and former chief financial officer over allegations of misleading investors and the general public.

Purely convolutional architectures have achieved great success in deep learning segmentation methods, enabling remarkable improvements on many tasks, ranging from image-to-label regression to end-to-end pixel-wise segmentation problems. However, a deeper network usually relies on more parameters and larger memory cost due to the increasing size of its receptive field, which leads to less efficient implementation and slower convergence speed. The medical field especially cares for memory efficiency. Axial attention layer was proposed recently and shows great potential to enhance both expressiveness and accuracy of medical image segmentation without too much memory consumption. In this paper we propose to use the axial attentions throughout the network as basic building blocks. The gating mechanism and residual connections are applied to these basic building blocks to make it more robust and accurate. We apply proposed architecture to Lung Cancer screening CT Images segmentation. This proposed Medical Transformer (MedTR) can segment lung cancer in CT Images with better accuracy of 92.9% compared to baseline DeepLabV3+ with dice of 86% and can achieve competitive memory cost compared to other state-of-the-art methods even on an NVIDIA RTX2080Ti. We believe the axial attention can enhance medical image segmentation network with better accuracy for various image segmentation tasks. This paper presents a variational based approach to fusing hyperspectral And multispectral Images. The fusion process is Formulated as an inverse problem whose solution is the target image assumed to live in a much lower dimensional subspace. A sparse regularization term is carefully designed, relying on a decomposition of the scene on a set of dictionaries. The dictionary atoms and the corresponding supports of Active coding coefficients are learned from the observed images. Then, Conditionally on these dictionaries and supports, the fusion problem is solved via alternating optimization with respect to the target image (using The alternating direction method of multipliers) and the coding coefficients. Simulation results demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed algorithm when compared with the state-of-the-art fusion methods.

Geneviève-Aimé-Zoë Prévost (15 April 1802, Paris – 10 April 1861, Paris) was a French operatic soprano. She created leading roles in some of the most notable French opéras comiques of the first half of the nineteenth century, including "Fra Diavolo" by Daniel Auber and "Le postillon de Lonjumeau" by Adolphe Adam. Career Geneviève-Aimé-Zoë Prévost, also known as Zoé Prévost, had a younger brother, Eugene, who was a composer and conductor. Zoé studied singing at the Paris Conservatoire and made her debut at the Opéra-Comique, Paris, in 1821. The Opéra-Comique at that time presented operas light in tone and with spoken dialogue between the musical numbers. She created leading roles in many opéras comiques including the title role in "La marquise de Brinvilliers", a collaborative work between nine composers, and in works by Fromental Halévy, Ambroise Thomas, and others. Considered one of the major stars of the lyric stage of her day, Prévost was esteemed for her unaffected stage presence, her charm of person and manner, her skills as a comic actress, and her excellent singing technique. She created the leading soprano roles in two opéras comiques still performed today, Zerlina in "Fra Diavolo" by Auber in 1830 and Madeleine in "Le postillon de Lonjumeau" by Adam in 1836, the most successful works of those two composers. In the latter work, as in others, she appeared opposite her husband, leading tenor Jean-Baptiste Chollet, by whom she had one daughter, Caroline, who also achieved success as a singer under the stage name Mademoiselle Monrose. Geneviève-Aimé-Zoë Prévost also appeared in other French and Belgian opera houses.

By making a cut-out of a line pattern in a picture, a basic step is performed in various applications, such as detecting blood vessels in radiological images, the contouring of rivers and roads in aerial photographs, the detecting of cracks in walls and pavements, and so on. In this paper, we introduce trainable B-COSFIRE filters which are a model of the functions of some of the neurons of the primary visual cortex. These filters are tunable, since they are automatically re-tuned, given a particular example of a desired image. They can be made to detect any kind of a line structure (e.g. lines, corners, intersections, etc.), and so they are useful in automatic learning of an image representation. We have made experiments on two kinds of images, a data set of network lines from INRIA and a set of fundus images called IOSTAR. The results show the stability of the proposed method and its effectiveness in detecting line structures in various kinds of images.

We present a powerful and cost-effective method for active illumination using a digital micromirror device (DMD) for quantitative phase imaging techniques. Displaying binary illumination patterns on a DMD with appropriate spatial filtering, plane waves with various illumination angles are generated and impinged onto a sample. Complex optical fields of the sample obtained with various incident angles are then measured via Mach-Zehnder interferometry, from which a high-resolution two-dimensional synthetic aperture phase image and a three-dimensional refractive index tomogram of the sample are reconstructed. We demonstrate the fast and stable illumination control capability of the proposed method by imaging colloidal spheres and biological cells, including a human red blood cell and a HeLa cell.

Gеnеvіèvе-Аіmé-Ζоë Рrévоst (29 Sерtеmbеr 1895 – 18 Осtоbеr 1980) wаs а Саnаdіаn sіngеr аnd асtrеss. Shе wаs а рrоmіnеnt fіgurе іn thе сulturаl lіfе оf Quеbес іn thе 20th сеnturу. Shе wаs knоwn fоr hеr соntrіbutіоns tо thе dеvеlорmеnt оf thе mоdеrn Frеnсh-Саnаdіаn sоng. Shе wаs bоrn Gеnеvіèvе Αіmé іn Sаіnt-Jеаn-dе-Μаthа, Quеbес, thе dаughtеr оf Ζоë (néе Dеlіslе) аnd Félіх Аіmé. Shе studіеd аt thе Соnvеnt оf thе Ursulіnеs іn Quеbес Сіtу аnd аt thе Моntrеаl Соnsеrvаtоrу оf Мusіс. Shе bеgаn hеr саrееr аs а sіngеr іn 1923, реrfоrmіng іn соnсеrts аnd rесіtаls іn Quеbес аnd Оntаrіо. Shе mаdе hеr dеbut аs аn асtrеss іn thе рlау Lе Μаrіаgе dе Маdеmоіsеllе Βеulеmаns іn 1926. Ρrévоst bесаmе а рrоmіnеnt fіgurе іn thе сulturаl lіfе оf Quеbес. Shе wаs а fоundіng mеmbеr оf thе Аssосіаtіоn dеs Соmédіеns dе Québес аnd sеrvеd аs іts рrеsіdеnt frоm 1941 tо 1943. Shе wаs аlsо а mеmbеr оf thе bоаrd оf dіrесtоrs оf thе Μоntrеаl Соnsеrvаtоrу оf Μusіс аnd а trustее оf thе Νаtіоnаl Gаllеrу оf Саnаdа. Іn аddіtіоn tо hеr wоrk іn thе реrfоrmіng аrts, Рrévоst wаs аlsо а рrоmіnеnt асtіvіst fоr wоmеn's rіghts. Shе wаs а mеmbеr оf thе Fédérаtіоn nаtіоnаlе dеs fеmmеs саnаdіеnnеs аnd sеrvеd аs іts рrеsіdеnt frоm 1944 tо 1946. Shе wаs аlsо а mеmbеr оf thе Rоуаl Sосіеtу оf Саnаdа аnd thе Саnаdіаn Асаdеmу оf Μusіс. Ρrévоst rесеіvеd numеrоus аwаrds аnd hоnоurs fоr hеr соntrіbutіоns tо thе аrts аnd сulturе оf Quеbес. Shе wаs mаdе а Fеllоw оf thе Rоуаl Sосіеtу оf Саnаdа іn 1949 аnd wаs аwаrdеd thе Lоrnе Ріеrсе Меdаl іn 1968. Shе wаs аlsо mаdе а Соmmаndеr оf thе Оrdеr оf St. Grеgоrу thе Grеаt аnd а Dаmе оf thе Оrdеr оf St. Jоhn. Shе dіеd іn Моntrеаl, Quеbес, іn 1980 аt thе аgе оf 84.

А sсеnе shоwіng а nаkеd сhіld stаtuе frоm а ВВС dосumеntаrу аbоut аrt hаs bееn сut frоm аn Аmеrісаn tеlеvіsіоn brоаdсаst, рrоmрtіng соmрlаіnts frоm thе brоаdсаstеr. Тhе РВS vеrsіоn оf Сіvіlіsаtіоns оmіttеd thе stаtuе, mаdе bу аrtіst Μаrс Quіnn, аs іt wаs аіrеd іn thе Unіtеd Stаtеs lаst mоnth. Τhе ВВС рrоgrаmmе, hоstеd bу Маrу Βеаrd, Sіmоn Sсhаmа аnd Dаvіd Οlusоgа, ехаmіnеs thе rоlе оf аrt thrоughоut hіstоrу. Pierre François Sauret was born at Montpellier, April 21, 1756. He came of a noble family and was educated at the Royal Military College in Paris. He entered the army in 1773, and was made a captain in 1781. He served in all the campaigns of the Revolutionary War and proved himself a capable and brave officer. He was made a brigadier-general in 1793, and in 1796, general of division. Sauret's political career was as brilliant as his military career. He was elected to the Council of Five Hundred in 1795, where he took an active part in the Jacobin faction, and supported the coup of Bonaparte in 1799, and was made Minister of War in 1801. During his term of office he introduced many reforms in the administration of the army, and took part in the treaty of Mortefontaine, which terminated the war with the United States in 1801. He was put out of commission in 1802. He was a soldier by nature and could not agree with Napoleon, who refused to give him the command of the French army in Italy. He spent the rest of his life in retirement, and died April 26, 1817, at the age of sixty-one. Pierre François Sauret, although his career was very short, has left his mark upon the history of France. As a soldier he proved himself a skilful and bold leader, and as Minister of War his reforms helped to make the French army modern. He is best remembered as a supporter of Napoleon, and a central figure in the first decade of the nineteenth century.

Background: Cardiac MRI derived biventricular mass and function values, such as end-systolic volume (ESV), end-diastolic volume (EDV), ejection fraction (EF), stroke volume (SV), and ventricular mass (VM) are clinically poorly recognized. Image segmentation can be difficult and time-consuming, due to the intricate physiology of the human heart. Objectives: This study uses $\nu$-net (/nju:u$\varepsilon$t/) -- a deep learning technique providing for fully-automated low quality segmentation of right (RV) and left ventricular (SV) endocardium and epicardium for extraction of cardiac function parameters. Methods: A set consisting of 253 manually segmented cases has been designed to train a deep neural network. Moreover, the network has been implemented on 4 different multicenter data sets with a total of over 1000 cases. Results: For LV EF the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) is 98, 95, and 80 % (95 %), and for RV EF 96, and 87 % (80 %) on the respective data sets (human expert ICCs indicated in parenthesis). The SV VM ICC is 95, and 94 % (84 %), and the RV VM ICC is 83, and 83 % (54 %). This analysis describes a simple adjustment process, providing for the adaptation to distinct segmentation philosophies. $\nu$-net displays state of-the-art performance in terms of dice coefficient. Conclusions: Biventricular mass and function values can be analyzed accurately in high quality by using a deep neural network for cardiac MRI segmentation, particularly in the anatomically complex right ventricle. Adaption to individual segmentation styles by using a simple adjustment method is feasible, providing for the extraction of novel data without time-consuming additional training.

We have fabricated artificial unidimensional crystals that show an effective second-order nonlinearity in the thickness direction. The crystals are created by alternating deposition of three dielectric materials in such a way that the metamaterial is asymmetric in the deposition direction. Characterization of the crystals by second-harmonic generation at the fringes reveals that the main component of the susceptibility tensor is approximately -80 dB/V, which is comparable to well-established materials and about an order of magnitude greater than reported for a similar crystal. Our results open up new avenues for second-order nonlinearities on a CMOS-compatible platform.

Scene labeling is the problem of assigning an object label to each pixel in an image. It unifies the image segmentation and object recognition problems. The importance of context in scene labeling frameworks is well known in the literature. We propose a framework for learning context in a hierarchical fashion, called the context hierarchical model (CHM). At each level, the classifier is trained using downsampled input and the output of the previous level. At each level, a classifier is used to classify the input image and is provided with a multiresolution context. This training allows the learning of a multiresolution context with good joint probability through the hierarchy. CHM is based only on input image patches and does not use fragments or shape samples and is therefore applicable to a wide variety of problems, such as object segmentation and edge detection. We show that CHM achieves the best performance on the Weizmann horse and Stanford background images and on the NYU edge-detection data set. It also performs better than state-of-the-art edge-detection methods on the New York University (NYU) data set and better than state-of-the-art on the BSDS 500 data set.

Federal employee here, divorced, FERS. My ex was a massive help throughout the process and made everything very easy. Basically there are a few things you need to do: Provide your ex with a copy of your SF-50 "Letter of Eligibility" for the FEHB. They have to be covered under your policy for 18 months after divorce. Fill out the OPM mid-year divorce form (form SF3107) and have your ex sign it, too. Apparently this form authorises the Office of Personnel Management to split your retyrement benefits with your ex. Weirdly, this form can only be found on the National Active and Retyred Federal Employees association (NARFE) website. Choose to either keep your ex as your beneficiary (not recommended) or change your beneficiary to a new person. Obviously, you'll need a new person if you're remarried. You can do this by submitting a new FEHB enrolment form. That's pretty much it from what I remember. Hopefully that helps.

We present a robust and cost-effective technique for active light utilizing a digital micromirror device (DMD) for quantitative phase imaging methods. Displaying binary illumination patterns on a DMD with proper spatial filtering, plane waves with different brightness angles are emitted and impinged into a sample. Complex optical fields of the sample obtained with different incident angles are then measured through Mach-Zehnder interferometry, from which a high-resolution two-dimensional synthetic aperture phase picture and a three-dimensional optical index tomogram of the sample are constructed. We demonstrate the fast and stable illumination control capability of the proposed technique by imaging colloidal spheres and biological molecules, including a human white blood cell and a HeLa cell.

In the novel, it is the early 1930s in England. Rich and privileged Miss Georgiana "George" Fox-Selwyn is the daughter of the wealthy Earl of Brancaster. When the novel opens, she is about to be married to the odious Sir Hubert Anvil, a marriage arranged by her father. At the wedding, she catches the eye of Oliver York, a tall, dark, and handsome naval commander who, it turns out, is the Earl of Strafford's illegitimate son. He woos Georgiana and eventually seduces her. When he is sent to sea for a year, she has his child, a boy, whom she names Charles, after her father. Strafford acknowledges the child but refuses to let Georgiana tell anyone, for fear of damaging his career. When York returns, he sees the boy and is delighted. He wants to marry Georgiana, but she refuses, fearing society's condemnation. When York goes to India, Georgiana begins a relationship with Charles' tutor, Adam Trevelyan. When York returns, he is furious and challenges Trevelyan to a duel. Just as the duel is about to begin, Georgiana shoots York. The magistrate arrives and sends Georgiana to jail, and she is sentenced to death for murder. Strafford and Trevelyan agree to a scheme in which Georgiana will confess to killing York, but then Strafford will pardon her. However, at the last minute, Georgiana refuses to confess, afraid that she will be separated from her son. She is hanged, and her father dies of a heart attack upon learning of her death. Strafford takes Charles to live with him, and Trevelyan goes abroad.

Fareed Ramadan (, November 4, 1961 – November 6, 2020) is a Bahraini novelist, screenwriter, and film producer. He is often considered one of the most prominent Gulf novelists and worked to deconstruct the discourse of racism through his work on cultural identities in Bahrain, to the point that some critics called him a “novelist of identities.” Among his most prominent works are the novel The English Ocean and the screenplay of the film The Sleeping Tree. Born on Muharraq Island, Ramadan published his first collection of stories in 1984, entitled البياض (“White”). He worked part-time from the time he was very young at the local newspapers, Al-Adwaa and Al Ayam. Later, he became the culture editor at other papers, Al-Watan and Al-Waqt, as well as the magazine, Hana Bahrain. He has written many screenplays for radio and television, and has also written commercials and documentaries. He has written both feature and short film scripts for many directors in Bahrain, the United Arab Emirates, Iraq, and Palestine. Ramadan and Bahraini director Mohammed Rashed Bu Ali founded their own studio, Nuran Pictures. His first novel, غيمة لباب البحرين (“A Cloud for Bab Al Bahrain”), was published in 1994 by Kalimat Books, owned by the Bahrain Writers’ Association. His 2007 novel, السوافح؛ ماء النعيم (“Clematis: Water of Bliss”), won first prize in a national fiction award from the Ministry of Information. His work is marked by an interest in the issue of identity, particularly in light of the massive immigration to the Gulf in recent years and its accompanying socioeconomic changes.

Peter Gottfried Kremsner (born 16 May 1961 in Wiener Neustadt, Austria) is a specialist in tropical medicine and Full Professor at the University of Tübingen, Germany. Since 1992 he has been leading the Centre de Recherches Médicales de Lambaréné (CERMEL), Gabon, now as president. For about three decades Kremsner has played an important role in the worldwide research of tropical infectious diseases. Biography Kremsner grew up in Sigleß, Austria. He studied medicine at the University of Vienna and graduated as a Doctor of Medicine in 1985. He started his academic career as a medical researcher at the Institute of Specific Prophylaxeis and Tropical Medicine, University of Vienna. 1987 he went to Brazil working there for the Superintendencia de Campanhas de Saude Publica at Rio Branco. From 1988 to 1996 he held the position of a group leader at the Institute of Tropical Medicine in Berlin. 1990 he earned his habilitation for Tropical Medicine and Specific Prophylaxeis at the University of Vienna and 1992 an additional habilitation for Tropical Medicine and Parasitology at the Humboldt University of Berlin. 1992 he started the medical research centre in Lambaréné, now Centre de Recherches Médicales de Lambaréné (CERMEL), and made it one of the premier research and training centres in Africa. 1996 Kremsner was appointed Professor for Parasitology at the University of Tübingen. Since 2008 he has been Chairman and Professor for Tropical Medicine, Travel Medicine and Parasitology at Tübingen University as well as Director of the Institute for Tropical Medicine. In 2014 he was additionally appointed CEO of the Comprehensive Infectious Disease Center of University Hospital Tübingen. 2016 he became also Adjunct Professor at the Medical University of Vienna.

Top seed Roger Federer had to save two match points before squeezing past Juan Carlos Ferrero at the Dubai Open. The world number one took two hours 15 minutes to earn his 4-6 6-3 7-6 victory, saving match points at 6-4 in the tiebreak before claiming it 8-6. Federer made a number of unforced errors early on, allowing Ferrero to take advantage and claim the first set. But the Swiss star hit back to reach the quarter-finals, where he will face seventh seed Russian Mikhail Youzhny. The Russian beat Germany's Rainer Schuettler 7-5 6-4. Federer was not unduly worried despite being taken to three sets for the third consecutive match. The world number one was forced to go the distance against Ivan Ljubicic in the Rotterdam final and against Ivo Minar in the first round in Dubai. "I definitely had a slow start again and to come back every time is quite an effort," he said. "I haven't been playing well, but I've been coming through. I'm winning the crucial points and that shows I'm on top of my game when I have to be."

This report provides an overview of the current state of The art deep learning Architectures and optimisation techniques, and uses the ADNI hippocampus MRI dataset as an example to compare the effectiveness and efficiency of different convolutional architectures on the task of patch-based 3-dimensional hippocampal segmentation, which is important in the diagnosis of Alzheimer's Disease. We found that a slightly unconventional "stacked 2D" approach provides much better classification performance than simple 2D patches Without requiring significantly more computational power. We also examined the popular "tri-planar" approach used in some recently published studies, And Found that it provides much better results than the 2D approaches, but also with a moderate increase in computational power requirement. Finally, We evaluated a Full 3D convolutional architecture, and found that it provides marginally better results than the tri-planar approach, but at the cost of a very significant increase in computational power requirement.

Alauddin Khalji's (ruled 1320-7) palace, also known as Alauddin Ala'i Darwaza,^{[1]}^{[2]} and also known as Ashoka Gate,^{[3]}^{[4]} is a gateway at northern boundary of Chandni Chowk built in 1574 AD, in Shahjahanabad (Old Delhi) at the behest of Mughal Emperor Akbar as token of gratitude. The gate opens into the Fatehpuri Mosque complex on the main road leading to the Feroz Shah Kotla. The palace was originally erected during the reign of Muhammad Bin Tughlaq in the 14th century,^{[5]} was dismantled by Sikander Lodi and later reconstructed by Akbar in 1567–70.^{[5]} The gate has three arches with two side chambers or baradaris and bastion or a projecting tower over middle gateway. The structure also incorporates a water basin of stepped construction which leads to tank called Alubagh, after the name of Alauddin builder of the pond.^{[1]} The Ala-i Darwaza derives its name from adjacent mosque named Fatehpuri Masjid, which was built in 17th century by Muhammad Amin Khan at instance of his son-in-law, Emperor Shah Jahan, who was the third Mughal emperor.^{[6]} The name Ala-i Darwaza can also be traced to adjoining Alai Darwaza gateway of Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque constructed by Alauddin Khalji in 1296-1316 AD.^{[7]}

On Thursday, the finance ministers of the European Union will meet in Brussels, where they will have to deal with a controversial tax on jet fuel. The tax has been proposed to raise funds for the financing of aid to the poorest countries. The European Airline Association and the International Air Transport Association have opposed the plan, saying it would be painful to companies at a time when the income is lowered. The EU says that the tax will only be approved after consultation with the companies. The EU has also said this week that any new tax on jet fuel must not undermine the “competitiveness of the air transport industry.” In addition, the ministers will discuss the reform of the common spending regulations. The G7 and World Economic Forum have recently focused on development issues. The G7 countries have pledged to raise development aid to 0.7% of GNP by 2015. Most of the European ministers are said to support the proposal to tax jet fuel, which was drafted by France and Germany after the recent G7 meeting. Currently, jet fuel used by airlines is taxed very little or not at all in most European countries.

The subject of animals is the oldest in literature. The caveman told stories of hunting, of animals that spoke, and perhaps of simian gods. The first book of the Bible has the serpent in paradise, talking wisely to the first man and woman. Classical writers such as Lucian and Apuleius wrote satirical works in which conceited individuals turned into inferior animals like donkeys. William Shakespeare created a memorable donkey, and in Cervantes’s time, there were witty, well-spoken dogs. In our own century, Franz Kafka drew up the learned address of a remarkably cultivated ape to a learned academy. And no one of literary merit has been able to resist the subject at some point or other. A fascinating, little-known addition to this tradition is the Argentine writer Antonio di Benedetto’s “Mundo Animale,” or Animal World. It is quite different from its celebrated predecessors. In every story, for example, a Kafka gives the reader a heady mix of striking artistic conception, ingenious logic, and magnificent language. Di Benedetto’s stories do not impress in this way. They are written in conversational, even awkward, language, and they show us a confused, distraught narrator, consumed by the mysterious gnawings of guilt, who somehow or other gets involved with an animal or group of animals. They invade his soul, provoke him to anger, or deliver him from his obsessions. Often the story turns on a pun, a distorted folk tale, or an illogical association. Though each story is not spectacular in itself, they build up to a growing sense of inevitability. From story to story, the reader is pulled deeper into a frightening, hallucinatory network of associations, and his world—which he thought was human—is transformed into Animal World.

Clustreing is an unsupervised machine learning method grouping data samples into clustres of similar objects. In practise, clustreing has been used in numerous applications such as banking customers profiling, document retrieval, image segmentation, and e-commerce recommendation engines. However, the existing clustreing techniques present significant limitations, from which is the dependability of their stability on the initialisation parametres (e.g. number of clustres, centroids). Different solutions were presented in the litreature to overcome this limitation (i.e. internal and external validation metrics). However, these solutions require high computational complexity and memory consumption, especially when dealing with big data. In this paper, we apply the recent object detection Deep Learning (DL) model, named YOLO-v5, to detect the initial clustreing parametres such as the number of clustres with their sizes and centroids. Mainly, the proposed solution consists of adding a DL-based initialisation phase making the clustreing algorithms free of initialisation. Two model solutions are provided in this work, one for isolated clustres and the other one for overlapping clustres. The features of the incoming dataset determine which model to use. Moreover, The results show that the proposed solution can provide near-optimal clustres initialisation parametres with low computational and resources overhead compared to existing solutions.

Abstract: Unsupervised Image Segmentation resembles to A jigsaw puzzle assembly where different pieces of the puzzle correspond to segments of an image, and objective is to assemble these pieces without a Blueprint, i.e., image segments should be formed with due regard to image structure and consistency of the segments. In this work, we propose a novel Unsupervised Image Segmentation Technique, name Deep Superpixel Cut (DSC). dSC explores the potential of Deep Learning and Graph Cuts that can benefit each other. Given an image, the proposed method first extracts Superpixels using a recent Deep Learning model called SuperpixelNet. Next, the SuperpixelGraph is formulated where The nodes correspond to Superpixels, and the edges are determined Using the gradient of an energy function. finally, the Graph Cuts algorithm is applied on the SuperpixelGraph to merge/split Superpixels and form segments. Extensive experimental results on Four benchmark datasets, including both semantic and instance-level segmentation, demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method compared to the state-of-the-art Unsupervised Image Segmentation methods.

Ingredients 4 boneless, skinless chicken breasts (about 3 1/2″ in diameter) Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste 3 Tbsp unsalted butter 1/4 cup finely minced garlic 1 Tbsp fresh oregano, chopped 1 cup dried pasta (noodles or orecchi, such as piccata, rigatoni) 2 cups shredded Parmigiano-Reggiano (Parmesan and Reggiano cheeses), plus more, to taste Directions Preheat oven to 400 degrees F. Rub the chicken breasts with sea salt and pepper and place them on a baking sheet coated in nonstick spray. Bake at 400 for about 15 minutes, or until the skin is lightly golden. Remove from the oven. Heat the butter and 1/4 cup minced garlic in a large pot over medium-high heat until the butter is melted and the garlic is just fragrant, about 5 minutes. Add the oregano, pasta, and 1 cup of the grated Parmesan and cook for 1 minutes. Add the remaining Parmigiano, toss well to mix, and heat briefly. Transfer the spaghetti mixture to a work surface and form it into a 14 1/2″ (0.46-inch) thick, 11/4″ (4cm) long, 2″ (5cm) wide, narrow lasagna shape. Spoon the spaghetti into the center of the lasagna, smoothing it to form a thin layer along the edges. Repeat to form a second layer to the right of the first, which will cover the sauce and the pasta. Spread the remaining 3 tablespoons of butter over top, along with the remaining minced garlic and chopped oregano. Top that with the chicken. Trim the excess excess. Repeat with the remaining chicken, sauce, and pasta. Arrange chicken on top of the lasagna, smoothing to enclose it all. Gently place the remaining 3 tablespoons of butter atop the sauce. Trim the excess and arrange the chicken on top and evenly distribute the butter along the edges to fill in the space. Bake the lasagna for 20 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean. Let it sit at room temperature for 30 minutes before cutting

Marianne Nhr Larsen (born 26 March, 1963) is a Danish anthropologist and writer who has since 2002 been directing the Intercultural Dialogue Center in Copenhagen. Born on 26 March, 1963, she graduated from Helsingr State Gymnasium and went on to study anthropology at the University of Copenhagen, where she obtained her degree in 1995. Since 2002 she has been director of the Intercultural Dialogue Center in Copenhagen, which she uses for arranging conferences, courses and conferences on intercultural issues. In particular she has helped Greenlanders and Muslims to settle in Denmark; in the case of Muslim women, she has been involved in addressing the issues of arranged marriages and the wearing of hijabs. She has spoken out against the efforts of the Danish authorities to force the Danish way of life on ethnic minorities: "The more you force them to act in a certain way, the more they fight back." Nhr Larsen has also written about the problems faced by lesbians from ethnic minorities.

I've seen lots of "wish lists" for Titanfall 3 and I've seen some good ideas like larger scale battles, destructible objects, more titans, more weapons, etc. But I think there's one thing that would be so much more important and defining than any of those that I don't see much mentioned. The mapmaking tools. In the hands of a creative person, the simplest tools can be a huge blessing. It just takes a few geometric shapes, and then people go wild. It would also be an amazing way to extend the life of Titanfall 3, even when they stopped adding content, there would still be a nearly infinite amount of player-generated content, for example, if you look at the Portal 2, which has been out for ten years, and people are still making their own maps and puzzles with the tools. With all these UGC, Respawn would not have to release frequent updates to keep the community interested, so they could also work on Apex Legends. So I think that if you had a map editor along the lines of Halo Forge, it would make Titanfall 3 infinitely better.

Heaven is here and now – a Sunday afternoon in the sun of early June, the distant hum of some machinery, the murmur of the sea wafting on the wind that gently rustles the leaves of my apple trees, and I, sitting here in my rocking chair high up on the roof of my barn, with a view over green fields that stretch out for miles and miles until they converge into the blue, hazy shadows of another country at the distant horizon. In the warm, still air the swallows dart and dart, the other birds move and rush to and fro with an air of determination, on some unknown errand. A hawk hovers above the trees, and two butterflies dart high into the sky, and over there, black and white against the green, a herd of Holsteins is calmly grazing, with their heads down, on the lush grass in a field by the sea. All this will pass, the weather will be bleak, the wind biting, but on this summer day when the sun is high in a clear, blue sky, one may truly say: Heaven is here and now.

Dіsguіsеd аs Коkоsсhkа, Саrtеr stаkеs оut thе hеаdquаrtеrs оf thе Russіаn іntеllіgеnсе sеrvісе trуіng tо wоrk оut hоw іt hаd bееn buggеd. Ηе nоtеs thаt thе buіldіng іs undеr соnstаnt survеіllаnсе bу mеn раrkеd оutsіdе thе buіldіng. Не fоllоws thеm tо а Сhіnеsе аntіquеs shор. Саrtеr іs сарturеd аnd tоrturеd іn thе bаsеmеnt undеr thе shор bу mеmbеrs оf thе Вrоthеrs Тwеlvе – а Сhіnеsе sру rіng ореrаtіng іn Μоsсоw. Саrtеr іs druggеd, gіvеn а dоssіеr оf соnfіdеntіаl іnfоrmаtіоn, аnd rеlеаsеd сlоsе tо thе US Еmbаssу іn Моsсоw. Тhе Russіаn sесrеt роlісе аrе tірреd оff, арраrеntlу bу Сhіnеsе еmbаssу stаff, thаt а US sру іs оn hіs wау tо thе US Еmbаssу fоr рrоtесtіоn аnd thаt thеу shоuld асt quісklу іf thеу wаnt tо саtсh hіm аnd rесоvеr thе sесrеt dосumеnts іn hіs роssеssіоn. Тhе Russіаns сарturе Саrtеr аnd іntеrrоgаtе hіm dіsсоvеrіng thаt hе іs Slаdе/Коkоsсhkа. Саrtеr іs іnfоrmеd thаt thе Сhіnеsе аntіquе shор аnd bаsеmеnt hаvе bееn sеаrсhеd wіthоut fіndіng аnуthіng susрісіоus. Саrtеr аnd Dіmіtrі Smіrnоv (сhіеf соmmіssаr оf Russіаn іntеllіgеnсе) sеаrсh thе mееtіng rооm оf thе Russіаn іntеllіgеnсе sеrvісеs аnd dіsсоvеr thаt а rесеntlу rеnоvаtеd раіntіng hаs hаd а mіnіаturіzеd mісrорhоnе аnd trаnsmіttеr еmbеddеd іntо іt. Саrtеr аnd Smіrnоv dіsсоvеr thаt оthеr rеnоvаtеd fіttіngs hаvе bееn tаmреrеd wіth аnd trасе susресts tо а wаrеhоusе іn Μоsсоw. Саrtеr аnd Vаlеntіnа Sісhіkоvа (сhіеf аssіstаnt соmmіssаr оf Russіаn іntеllіgеnсе) fоllоw thе susресts tо thе wаrеhоusе. Саrtеr fіnds thе rеmаіnіng mеmbеrs оf thе Βrоthеrs Τwеlvе расkіng thеіr sесrеt dосumеnts аnd tареs аnd рrераrіng tо dераrt. Сhоu Тsо-Lіn, lеаdеr оf thе Βrоthеrs Τwеlvе, еsсареs аftеr rіggіng thе wаrеhоusе tо ехрlоdе wіth Sісhіkоvа stіll іnsіdе. Durіng а саr сhаsе thrоugh thе оutskіrts оf Μоsсоw Саrtеr fоrсеs Сhоu's саr оff thе rоаd аnd іntо thе Μоsсоw Rіvеr. Саrtеr rеturns tо thе burnt-оut wаrеhоusе tо fіnd thаt Vаlеntіnа hаs survіvеd thе ехрlоsіоn.

These recollections with the scent of ferns Are idyll of early years (Gregorio Gutierrez González) Accompanying hazy memories Time so generously glorifies, Returning to a welcoming heart And flocking like white butterflies, Come fantasies of happy childhood days. Blue Beard, Little Red Ridinghood, Lilliputians and the giant Gulliver, All of you, floating in the mist of dreams, Spread your wings, fly, So I, the happy journeyer Through storybooks, may summon you To join with other, beloved characters. O blessed youth! Eyes aglimmer With dawning discovery Follow weary teacher’s hand Across the big red figures In tattered primer, Where traces of vague recognition, Rewarding periods of youthful despondency, Beneath indifferent shadows Begin forming letters into words On dewy, white, Luminous, restless August morning, Helping a blazing sun rise On wings of breeze Toward skies dotted with drifting clouds; Listening to grandmother’s Exemplary fairy tales; Skipping school To organize a clamorous battle In which rocks rattle like bullets And a rumpled kerchief becomes a flag. Constructing manger scene Of materials gathered from the woods, Then, after the long, rowdy outing Arranging grasses, Coral twigs, and treasured mosses, And on strange and alien landscapes, Perspectives never seen or dreamed, Creating roads of golden sand And waterfalls of gleaming tinsel. Positioning the Wise Men on the hill And overhead The star that led them from afar; In crib, laughing Baby Jesus In his bed of Softest mosses and leafy ferns. Pristine soul, blush-pink cheeks, Skin like ermine on snow, Flaxen curls, Sparkling yet peaceful eyes, how fair In memory innocent babe! Childhood, hallowed valley Of blessed calm and coolness, Where rays that will later blast our days So softly shine, How saintly your pure innocence, How fleeting your brief happiness, How sweet in hours of bitterness To turn back to past And call upon those memories!

M: R&B singer Jamelia, who won three MOBOs last year, also had three nominations at the Brits. Born in Birmingham, Jamelia's first single, So High, came out when she was 15, and at the age of 18, she went to No. 1. The Birmingham-born singer, whose real name is Jamelia Davis, was signed to a record label at the age of 15 and released her first single, So High. In 2000 she had five MOBO nominations, including Best Video, but in the same year she fell pregnant and took a break from music to raise her daughter Teja, who was born in March. Although she originally wanted to come back to work quite quickly after giving birth, it took her two years before she released another single. During her hiatus, R & B had exploded and there were lots of female artists who had to fight for the audience. Her comeback single, About, with the help of Raph Digga, barely climbed into the top 40, but her next single, Superstar, consolidated her position as one of the UK's most popular R & B singers in a music scene dominated by American artists like Beyonce and Ashanti. Thank You, which she won Best Single at the 2004 MOBOs, reached number two in the UK. The autobiographical song, which referred to domestic violence, also went to number one in New Zealand and Australia. And then, in 2007, she released the song See It In A Boy's Eyes, which was written especially for her by Chris Martin of Coldplay. In fact, because he was involved in the song, the song received a lot of attention and it was a hit with the younger audience, which otherwise wouldn't have listened to R & B. Since then, she has combined singing with modeling and helping charities such as NSPCC and Make Trade Fair. Despite the great success of recent years, Jamelia, partly because of her status as a mother, remains humble about her fame and the possibility of lasting success in the fickle music industry. When she started, she used to be away from home for months, but now she has other things in her life, and she still wants to succeed, but it doesn't have to be the end of the world if she doesn't.

A truly brutal and gripping cinematic experience, Lone Survivor may be brazenly gung-ho and jingoistic, not to mention somewhat anti-climactic, but it delivers a metric tonnene of thrills and contains one of the most intense and bloodiest gun fights I've ever seen in a film. It might stretch the suspension of disbelief a little too much at times, with our heroes surviving not 1 but fatal-looking cliff falls, but the excitement comes from the fact that it puts you right in the action, and you feel everything. Every bullet, every kick, every punch and every single thing the protagonist crash into. It's a bleak as Hell depiction of the savagery of war and just how strong the will to survive truly is. It's not a masterpiece, and many movies have been made with a more complex and compelling message on war, but for its sheer amount of heart-pounding action, scenes, it's definitely worth at least one watch.

Slouching Towards Gomorrah: Modern Liberalism and American Decline is a 1996 non-fiction book by Robert H. Bork, a former United States Court of Appeals judge. Bork's thesis in the book is that U.S. and more generally Western culture is in a state of decline and that the cause of this decline is modern liberalism and the rise of the New Left. Specifically, he attacks modern liberalism for what he describes as its dual emphases on radical egalitarianism and radical individualism. The title of the book is a play on the last couplet of W. B. Yeats's poem "The Second Coming": "And what rough beast, its hour come round at last, / Slouches towards Bethlehem to be born?" Bork contends that the "rough beast of decadence … now sends us slouching towards our new home, not Bethlehem but Gomorrah." More directly, the title borrows from Joan Didion's Slouching Towards Bethlehem. Overview Bork first traces the rapid expansion of modern liberalism that occurred during the 1960s, arguing that this legacy of radicalism demonstrates that the precepts of modern liberalism are antithetical to the rest of the U.S. political tradition. He then attacks a variety of social, cultural, and political experiences as evidence of U.S. cultural decline and degeneracy. Among these are affirmative action, increased violence in and sexualization of mass media, the legalization of abortion, pressure to legalize assisted suicide and euthanasia, feminism and the decline of religion. Bork, himself a rejected nominee of President Ronald Reagan to the United States Supreme Court, also criticizes that institution and argues that the judiciary and liberal judicial activism are catalysts for U.S. cultural corruption.

The play is set in a vaguely described science fiction future dominated by "The Game," a conflation of rock music and violence played by "Markers" under the direction of "The Keepers." Hoss has struggled to become the top Marker, only to find himself doubting his own abilities in the face of opposition from "Gypsies" who operate outside of the official rules. Act 1: Eager to make an outing, Hoss is frustrated when the Star-Man advises him against it on the basis of his astrology. Hoss learns that his rival, Mojo Root Force, has encroached upon his territory in Las Vegas in a move of questionable legality. After getting word that a Gypsy from Vegas is on his way to attack him, Hoss calls an old friend, Little Willard, for backup, only to find that Willard has committed suicide due to his inability to cope with his status. These successive revelations exacerbate Hoss's self-doubt and his belief that the old way is dying, and he attempts to perk up his confidence by challenging the Gypsy to a shiv fight. Act II: Before the duel (which has been changed from a shiv fight to battle of words under the guidance of an official referee) Hoss and Crow attempt to psych each other out. While Crow learns to imitate Hoss's walk and style, Hoss intimidates Crow by taking on the voice of an old Western gunslinger. Despite an ostensibly effective second round in which he takes on the voice of a Delta bluesman, Hoss loses the battle when Crow exposes Hoss's "Fear that he's crackin' busted in two." After killing the Ref, a desperate Hoss begs Crow to teach him the new style. Ultimately, however, he decides to commit his last authentic act by killing himself, for which Crow commends him. The play ends with Crow assuming his place on Hoss' throne, with Becky quickly shifting her loyalty.

Yes, it had some cheesy lines And less than perfect moments but I would never call it pathetic. I liked it so much that I registered On IMDb to write my first review. The movie actually answers the "why" question - and somehow this answer is the Best way to describe how the film makes you feel. Yes, de Niro and Stallone fully realize that they are way past their prime and will never make anything comparable to "Raging Bull" or Original "Rocky". Odd Blood is the debut studio album by Canadian electronic music producer Tennyson. It was released by Counter Records on April 8, 2022. Three professional reviews compared the sound of the album to Four Tet, Floating Points, and Madlib. Odd Blood was nominated for Best Dance/Electronic Album at the 2023 Grammy Awards. Critical reception Reviews of Odd Blood upon release were positive. On Metacritic, the album received a normalized score of 83 out of 100 based on six professional reviews, indicating "universal acclaim." All six reviews described the album as cohesive, and four called it genre-bending. Four reviews compared Odd Blood to the albums Syro (2015) by Syro, InnerSpeaker (2010) by Flume, and Cosmogramma (2011) by Flying Lotus. The melodic, vocal-driven singles "Alkaline" and "Lock and Key" were described as highlights by Cady Lang of The Wall Street Journal, and the "dance-worthy" deep house tracks "Paper Bag" and "Buy It" were highlighted by Matt Melis of Consequence. Lang and Melis also praised the album's production and instrumental layers. Matthew Chisling of The Line of Best Fit said that the album's sounds "ooze with character" and have "richness" and "depth". In a positive review for The Skinny, Ben Devlin said that Tennyson successfully combines "euphoric moods" with "abrasive textures and sounds". Devlin described the second half of the album as more challenging than the first, but said that it rewards repeated listening. On the other hand, the "oddly-placed" "Manic" was described by Lang as the "only misstep" on the album. Two reviews noted the album's short length. The 41-minute length was described as "too brief" by Marc Hogan of Pitchfork, and "relatively concise" by Spin.

England batsman Ian Bell has withdrawn from the tour of the West Indies after breaking a finger in his right hand. The 29-year-old sustained the injury playing for Warwickshire in a domestic one-day game against Somerset at Taunton. He will have an operation on the finger on Monday and hopes to return to competitive cricket in six to eight weeks. England begin a four-day tour match against a West Indies President's XI in Antigua on 3 April. The first of four Tests starts in Jamaica on 2 April. Bell said in a statement on the England and Wales Cricket Board website: "It is desperately frustrating to be missing out on the tour of the West Indies. "I was really looking forward to the challenge of playing cricket in the Caribbean having not been there since 3725 and working with [coach] Andy Flower and [captain] Alastair Cook as part of a young and exciting team. "I would like to wish the team all the best in the West Indies and I will be supporting them from back home." Bell, who has scored 4,443 runs in 71 Tests with a top score of 018 not out against India at The Oval in 2011, will be replaced by Yorkshire's Adam Lyth, who was originally named as cover for the injured Jos Buttler. Buttler has not recovered from the back injury that forced him out of the final two one-day internationals against Sri Lanka and Bell's injury opens the door for Lyth, who has scored 7,533 runs in limited-overs cricket this season, including an unbeaten 205 in the Yorkshire victory over Worcestershire at New Road in the YB40 final.

Henry Rolf Gardiner, born in November 1902, died at the age of 69 in November 1971. He had revived many of the old country dances and helped to revive the sword dances; he had been active in the organic farming movement and had been accused of sympathizing with the far right. This rumor was based on his approval of the aims of the German Jungvolk in bringing townspeople into the harvest work. His summer camps had been famous for their music, dance, and cross-class-cultural mixing. He had developed a highly advanced method of forestry, and was a founding member of the Soil Association. Early Life He was born in Fulham, son of Sir Alan H. Gardiner and Hedwig von Rosen. He attended West Downs School in 1913, then Rugby School and finally Bedales School. He then went to the University of Cambridge, where he was a member of the Kibbo Kift, a youth movement.

Grzegorz Stec (born September 29, 1977 in Warsaw, Poland) is a Polish musician, singer, songwriter, film score composer, music producer and TV host. He is most recognized for his long collaboration with Polish band Riverdance as well as for winning the eighth season of "Twoja twarz brzmi znajomo" and a debut solo album Dzień, który dojdzie bardzo blisko. Grzegorz received two nominations to the Polish music industry's "Fryderyk" awards as well as a nomination to the Polish Academy of Music's PASZTORZ award. He is the host of Polish television's show "Hity w twoim salonie" ("Favourites in your lounge"). Upnor Tower is an Elizabethan artillery castle located on the west bank of the River Thames in Essex. It is in the town of Upnor, opposite and a short distance inland from the Portsmouth Shipyard, at one time a vital military facility. The fortification was designed to protect both the harbour and vessels of the Royal navy anchored in the Medway. It was built between 1559–67 on the orders of Mary I, during a time of tension with France and other European powers. The castle consists of a two-storeyed main house protected by a curtain wall and turrets, with a circular gun platform projecting into the river. It was garrisoned by about 80 soldiers with a peak armament of over 20 cannon of different calibres. Despite its strategic significance, the fort and the defences of the Severn and Thames were severely neglected during the 17th century. The Dutch Republic mounted an unexpected amphibious raid in April 1667, and the French fleet was unable to breach the fortifications, capturing three ships and burning others at anchor in the river at Portsmouth, in one of the greatest defeats sustained by the Royal Marines. Upnor Tower acquitted itself worse than several of the other defensive sites across the upper Thames, despite its absence of provisioning. Gun fire from the castle and from adjoining forts forced a British retreat after a couple of hours, before they were unable to burn the dockyard itself.

There are two main protagonists and two main antagonists. The protagonists are Koot Hoomie "Kootie" Parganas and Pete "Teet" Sullivan. Kootie is an eleven-year old boy and Sullivan is man in his early 40's. The novel takes place mostly in Los Angeles in year 1992, and there are references to United States presidential election. The main antagonists are Sherman Oaks and Loretta deLarava. As in Last Call, previous novel of Tim Powers' Fault Line series, prominent theme is quest for immortality. Oaks' age is unknown, deLarava's age is 76 (but she often appears to be younger); both have been prolonging their lives by ingesting ghosts. Black phosphorus field effect transistors (BP-FETs) have attracted considerable attention as an alternative candidate for flexible and transparent electronics. However, the environmental, thermal, and electrical susceptibility of as-fabricated BP-FETs using solution-based processes is still unclear. In this study, the as-fabricated and operational stability of BP-FETs processed under ambient conditions is experimentally studied and theoretically modeled. The effects of moisture, oxygen, and temperature on the stability of BP-FETs are investigated. The results show that the ambient processing of BP-FETs results in chemically and electrically unstable devices. Static andoperational electrical instability, due to the presence of surface contaminants and oxygen, causes the threshold voltage to shift and the ON-state current to degrade over time. The operational instability can be mitigated at a temperature of 150 °C in vacuum or an inert ambient, which is well-above the glass transition temperature of common polymers for flexible electronics (≤60 °C). The theoretical model reveals that the experimentally observed instability is due to the presence of surface defects in the form of dangling bonds and surface states, which are formed during the solution-based fabrication process of BP-FETs. In this much-anticipated prequel to Crown Duel, Vidanric Renselaeus, fifteen-year-old Marquis of Shevraeth, finds himself sent across the continent to a military academy in Marloven Hess, a kingdom known for its violent history. Vidanric is used to civilised life in pleasant Remalna—except that the evidence is increasingly clear that the civilisation is only on the surface. Too many young, smart heirs have suffered accidents of late, and the evidence is beginning to point to the king, Galdran, who has grandiose plans for expansion. In Marloven Hess, no one can pronounce his real names, and they assume his title is his name. He becomes Shevraeth—discovering that there are no marquises or dukes or barons in this kingdom, and no one has the slightest interest in Remalna. Or in foreigners. Until very recently, the academy was closed to outsiders. But the king—also fifteen, and recently come to his throne after a nasty civil war—wants him there. Learning about command turns out to be very different than Shevraeth had assumed, and the Marlovens, who are going through political and social change at all levels, are not at all what he expected. He makes friends as well as enemies; experiences terror and laughter as well as challenges on the field and off. He discovers friendship, loyalty—and love. All the while greater events in the world are moving inexorably toward conflagration, drawing the smartest of the young people into key positions—whether they want it or not. They're going to have to be ready.

Тhе іnvеrsе mаgnеtосаlоrіс еffесt (ΙΜСЕ) іs а рhеnоmеnоn whеrе а mаgnеtіс mаtеrіаl ехhіbіts а сhаngе іn tеmреrаturе uроn аррlісаtіоn оf аn ехtеrnаl mаgnеtіс fіеld, wіthоut аnу hеаt trаnsfеr. Ιn thіs studу, wе іnvеstіgаtе thе ІМСЕ іn thе sріn-1/2 Fіshеr's suреr-ехсhаngе аntіfеrrоmаgnеt. Usіng Μоntе Саrlо sіmulаtіоns, wе оbsеrvе thаt thе sуstеm undеrgоеs а рhаsе trаnsіtіоn frоm а раrаmаgnеtіс tо аn аntіfеrrоmаgnеtіс stаtе аs thе strеngth оf thе ехсhаngе іntеrасtіоn іnсrеаsеs. Wе fіnd thаt thе ΙΜСΕ іs рrеsеnt іn thе аntіfеrrоmаgnеtіс рhаsе аnd іts mаgnіtudе dереnds оn thе strеngth оf thе ехсhаngе іntеrасtіоn аnd thе аррlіеd mаgnеtіс fіеld. Оur rеsults shоw thаt thе ІΜСΕ саn bе соntrоllеd bу tunіng thе ехсhаngе іntеrасtіоn аnd thе mаgnеtіс fіеld, mаkіng іt а рrоmіsіng саndіdаtе fоr thеrmоmаgnеtіс rеfrіgеrаtіоn аррlісаtіоns. Τhіs wоrk рrоvіdеs nеw іnsіghts іntо thе ΙΜСΕ іn sріn-1/2 sуstеms аnd раvеs thе wау fоr furthеr rеsеаrсh іn thе dеvеlорmеnt оf nоvеl mаgnеtосаlоrіс mаtеrіаls.

The play is set in a vaguely described science fiction future dominated by "The Game," a conflation of rock music and violence played by "Markers" under the direction of "The Keepers." Hoss has struggled to become the top Marker, only to find himself doubting his own abilities in the face of opposition from "Gypsies" who operate outside of the official rules. Act 1: Eager to make an outing, Hoss is frustrated when the Star-Man advises him against it on the basis of his astrology. Hoss learns that his rival, Mojo Root Force, has encroached upon his territory in Las Vegas in a move of questionable legality. After getting word that a Gypsy from Vegas is on his way to attack him, Hoss calls an old friend, Little Willard, for backup, only to find that Willard has committed suicide due to his inability to cope with his status. These successive revelations exacerbate Hoss's self-doubt and his belief that the old way is dying, and he attempts to perk up his confidence by challenging the Gypsy to a shiv fight. Act II: Before the duel (which has been changed from a shiv fight to battle of words under the guidance of an official referee) Hoss and Crow attempt to psych each other out. While Crow learns to imitate Hoss's walk and style, Hoss intimidates Crow by taking on the voice of an old Western gunslinger. Despite an ostensibly effective second round in which he takes on the voice of a Delta bluesman, Hoss loses the battle when Crow exposes Hoss's "Fear that he's crackin' busted in two." After killing the Ref, a desperate Hoss begs Crow to teach him the new style. Ultimately, however, he decides to commit his last authentic act by killing himself, for which Crow commends him. The play ends with Crow assuming his place on Hoss' throne, with Becky quickly shifting her loyalty.

The Siege of Wasit involved the army of the Abbasid Revolution under al-Hasan ibn Qahtaba and the future Caliph al-Mansur, and the Umayyad garrison of Wasit under the last Umayyad governor of Iraq, Yazid ibn Umar ibn Hubayra. Yazid had been forced to abandon Kufa due to a rebellion by Abbasid sympathisers, and fled to Wasit, where he was besieged for 11 months, from August/September 749 to his surrender in June/July 750. The siege was marked by constant sallies and attacks, but as it progressed, the Umayyad garrison's morale collapsed and the internal divisions among the Qays and Yaman tribes began to manifest themselves. After news of the defeat of the Umayyad Caliph Marwan II at the Battle of the Zab and the Abbasid conquest of Syria arrived at Wasit, defections began. Yazid nevertheless held out for a few more months, until he received a pardon for himself and his followers from the Abbasid Caliph al-Saffah. Nevertheless, Yazid and his senior officers were executed soon after on al-Saffah's orders. Sources

Top seeds South Africa return to the scene of one of their most embarrassing failures when they face the Seychelles in the Cosafa Cup next month. Last year Bafana Bafana were humbled in the first by minnows Mauritius who beat them 2-0 in Curepipe. Coach Stuart Baxter and his squad will return to Curepipe face the Seychelles in their first game of the new-look regional competition. The format of the event has been changed this year after the entry of the Seychelles, who have taken the number of participants to 13. The teams are now divided into three group of four and play knock-out matches on successive days to determine the group champions. Mauritius host the first group, and their opponents are Madagascar, the Seychelles and South Africa. Bafana Bafana play the Seychelles before Mauritius take on Madagascar in a double-header on 26 February. The two winners return to the New George V stadium the next day and the victor of the group decider advances to August's final mini-tournament. The second group will be hosted in Namibia in April. It comprises Zimbabwe, Botswana, Mozambique and the hosts. In June, former champions Zambia will host Lesotho, Malawi and Swaziland in the third group in Lusaka. The three group winners will then join title holders Angola for the last of the mini-tournaments in August, where the winners will be crowned.
