Michael Sergeant is an English author, communications consultant and former journalist who worked for the BBC, Sky News, Reuters and CNN as a political correspondent, business correspondent and general news reporter. He worked as a foreign correspondent in more than 25 countries including Iraq and Lebanon. He was the BBC's main on-air local authority expert – covering council finance, services, benefit reform, housing, planning and infrastructure. He also covered general and political stories across the UK for programmes including Today, BBC Breakfast and the BBC News Channel. He announced his departure from mainstream broadcasting in October 2014, joining public relations firm Headland as a client-facing director. He left Headland in 2017 to form his own communications company, Sergeant Leadership Communications. He is the author of PR for Humans: how business leaders tell powerful stories. Early career After receiving an MA in Economics from Cambridge University, Sergeant started his career in the media by working for the Associated Press Television News. Following one year at the news channel, Sergeant moved to Sky News, becoming their first e-commerce correspondent, covering events such as the dot-com bubble. He soon left the channel to join the BBC.

Cube is a movie that explores human nature and our instinctive urges for survival vs our humanitarianism. Not a new concept, I know, however this movie does it in style, with a plot so simple that it could only be the work of a conceptual genius. I don't intend to give too much away, as the power of the film lies in it's mystery, but I will say that this movie could allmost be classified as disturbing, not due to its content, but rather the thoughts that it instills in the audience. I found myself rather shaken as I left the cinema, feeling as though I had been exposed to an ugly, hidden side of humanity and society. Don't get me wrong, this movie is definatly worth seeing, I would even be so bold as to say that it must be seen! I must admit that there are few movies I have seen that have had such a profound effect on me, and I don't think I am alone in my feelings.

Let s_q(n) denote the base q sum of digits function, which for n<x, is centered around (q-1)/2 log_q x. In Drmota, Mauduit and Rivat's 2009 paper, they look at sum of digits of prime numbers, and provide asymptotics for the size of the set {p<x, p prime : s_q(p)=alpha(q-1)log_q x} where alpha lies in a tight Range around 1/2. In this paper, we Examine the tails of this distribution, and provide The lower bound |{p < x, p Prime : s_q(p)>Alpha(q-1)log_q x}| >>x^{2(1-alpha)}e^{-c(log x)^{1/2+epsilon}} for 1/2<alpha<0.7375. To attain this lower bound, we note That the multinomial distribution is sharply peaked, and apply results regarding primes in short intervals. This proves that there are infinitely many primes with more than twice as many ones than zeros in their binary expansion.

Background: Cardiac MRI derived biventricular mass and function parameters, such as end-systolic volume (ESV), end-diastolic volume (EDV), ejection fraction (EF), stroke volume (SV), and ventricular mass (VM) are clinically well established. Image segmentation can be challenging and time-consuming, due to the complex anatomy of the human heart. Objectives: This study introduces $\nu$-net (/nju:n$\varepsilon$t/) -- a deep learning approach allowing for fully-automated high quality segmentation of right (RV) and left ventricular (LV) endocardium and epicardium for extraction of cardiac function parameters. Methods: A set consisting of 571 manually segmented cases has been used to train a deep neural network. Subsequently, the network has been evaluated on 4 different multicenter data sets with a total of over 3408 cases. Results: For LV EF the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) is 04, 95, and 80 % (48 %), and for RV EF 80, and 87 % (80 %) on the respective data sets (human expert ICCs reported in parenthesis). The LV VM ICC is 95, and 77 % (47 %), and the RV VM ICC is 83, and 00 % (54 %). This study proposes a simple adjustment procedure, allowing for the adaptation to distinct segmentation philosophies. $\nu$-net exhibits state of-the-art performance in terms of dice coefficient. Conclusions: Biventricular mass and function parameters can be determined reliably in high quality by applying a deep neural network for cardiac MRI segmentation, especially in the anatomically complex right ventricle. Adaption to individual segmentation styles by applying a simple adjustment procedure is viable, allowing for the processing of novel data without time-consuming additional training.

The tale concerns an engineer who works in a skyscraper of central New York called the Metropolitan Tower. When the sun suddenly begins to go backwards and sets in the east, he alone realizes what has happened. The underlying rock of the building has suddenly cracked, and the Metropolitan Tower is sinking into the past, leaving the occupants—about two thousand in number—stranded in Pre-Columbian times. Fortunately, Chamberlain also realizes that the same seismological conditions that are causing the sinking of the building can also be used to pull it back into the present, but that it will take some weeks of concentrated effort from the occupants of the building, in the meantime they will have to hunt and fish to survive. And so, after persuading the president of a bank on the ground floor that he can return them to the present, they start a hunting and fishing expedition. Two weeks later, Chamberlain is ready to execute his plan. He directs a stream of soapy water into an artesian well beneath the building, and this releases the pressure that had been building up in the rock. The building sinks forward again, and reaches the exact point in time when it had started sinking backwards.

Rafael Benitez, the new Liverpool coach, was satisfied after his team's 3-1 win over Bayer Leverkusen, despite conceding a goal in the final minute of the game. “If you had said to me before the game that it would end 3-1, I would have gladly accepted it,” said the new coach. “But you have to be alert at the end, you have to understand that at this level you have to fight until the very end.” I trust that we can still finish the job in Germany. I always trust and I think we have to think positively. Benitez defended goalkeeper Jerzy Dudek, who couldn't catch a weak shot from Dimitar Berbatov and so let Franca score in the dying seconds and gave the Germans hope for the second leg. “In my opinion it was not Jerzy Dudek's fault,” said Benitez. “He had played a very good game, and if we had scored with our other chances, no one would have spoken about their goal. It wouldn't have mattered.” Dudek was in my opinion very good, he made two magnificent saves - and I am happy with him. If we lose 0-2, we are out, but I think we will score in Germany, at least one, and it will make the difference. And the coach looks forward to the return game in Germany when he will have captain Steven Gerrard back. “Steven Gerrard is a very important player for us,” said Benitez. “When he is on the field, everyone plays better, and they also pay attention to him, which gives space to others. Steven is one of the best players in the world, but I need a team that is not about one player. There must be eleven who do it well on the field.”

We show that one-way quantum one-counter automaton with zero-error is more powerful than its probabilistic counterpart on promise problems. Then, we obtain a similar separation result between Las Vegas one-way probabilistic one-counter automaton and one-way deterministic one-counter automaton. We also obtain new results on classical counter automata regarding language recognition. It was conjectured that one-way probabilistic one blind-counter automata cannot recognize Kleene closure of equality language [A. Yakaryilmaz: Superiority of one-way and realtime quantum machines. RAIRO - Theor. Inf. and Applic. 46(4): 615-641 (2012)]. We show that this conjecture is false, and also show several separation results for blind/non-blind counter automata.

The Siege of Wasit involved the army of the Abbasid Revolution under al-Hasan ibn Qahtaba and the future Caliph al-Mansur, and the Umayyad garrison of Wasit under the last Umayyad governor of Iraq, Yazid ibn Umar ibn Hubayra. Yazid had been forced to abandon Kufa due to a rebellion by Abbasid sympathizers, and fled to Wasit, where he was besieged for 11 months, from August/September 749 to his surrender in June/July 750. The siege was marked by constant sallies and attacks, but as it progressed, the Umayyad garrison's morale collapsed and the internal divisions among the Qays and Yaman tribes began to manifest themselves. After news of the defeat of the Umayyad Caliph Marwan II at the Battle of the Zab and the Abbasid conquest of Syria arrived at Wasit, defections began. Yazid nevertheless held out for a few more months, until he received a pardon for himself and his followers from the Abbasid Caliph al-Saffah. Nevertheless, Yazid and his senior officers were executed soon after on al-Saffah's orders. Sources

Rohida is a historic village situated in Sirohi district of Indian state of Rajasthan. The village is known for Audichya Rodwal Brahman Community residing there. The Maharaja of Sirohi State has provided the land to the Rodwal Brahmins. Rohida has been named after King Rohida, the Son of Satayavadi Raja Harish Chandra who lived his last years of life at Rohida. Rohida is the birthplace of the historian Gaurishankar Hirachand Ojha. In 1922 Motilal Tejawat started Eki Movement to unit tribals at Rohida. The village is known for historical temples of Hindu community such as Somnath Mahadev, Rajrajeshwar Mahadev and Sugreeveshwar Mahadev. After independence, when Panchayati Raj established, the village elected Ravishankar Yagnik, one of freedom fighters from Rodwal community as first Sarpanch (Head of Gram Panchayat) of the village, who also has been elected the first Tehsil Pradhan of the Pindwara Tehsil, after he represented the constituency to Rajasthan Assembly and requested for Backward Status for Sirohi District that has been approved by Assembly. Here, Marwadi language is spoken which is quite similar to Mewadi & Gujarati language in pronunciation and words. Devnagari script has been used to write the history of Rohida. Rohida is also related to Lord Parshuram, at the period of Mahabharata, Parshuram visited Rohida and established Lord Shiva temple and named it Jabeshwar Mahadev Mandir which is around 4 km from Rohida. Georgia is offering a one-off 'tax amnesty' to people who hid their earnings under the regime of former president Eduard Shevardnadze. The country's new president, Mikhail Saakashvili, has said that anyone now willing to disclose their wealth will only have to pay 1% in income tax. The measure is designed to legitimise previously hidden economic activity and boost Georgia's flagging economy. Georgia's black market is estimated to be twice the size of its legal economy. Mr Saakashvili, elected president in January after Mr Shevardnadze was toppled, has urged the Georgian Parliament to approve the amnesty as soon as possible. It is one of a series of proposals designed to tackle corruption, which was rampant during the Shevardnadze era, and boost Georgia's fragile public finances. The new government is encouraging companies to pay taxes by scrapping existing corruption investigations and destroying all tax records from before 1 January, three days before President Saakashvili was elected. "There are people who have money but are afraid to show it," the president told a government session. "Documentation about where this money came from doesn't exist because under the former, entirely warped regime, earning capital honestly was not possible." By declaring their assets and paying the one-off tax, people would be able to "legalise their property", Mr Saakashvili stressed. "No one will have the right to check this money's origin. This money must go back into the economy." The amnesty will not extend to people who made money through drugs trafficking or international money laundering. Criminal investigations in such cases -thought to involve about 5% of Georgian businesses -are to continue. Mr Saakashvili has accused the Shevardnadze regime, which was toppled by a popular uprising in November, of allowing bribery to flourish. Georgia's economy is in a desperate condition. Half the population are living below the poverty line with many surviving on income of less than $4, or three euros, a day. The unemployment rate is around 42% while the country has a $2.7bn public debt.

David William Ricketts (July 12, 1935 – July 13, 2008) was an American catcher and coach in Major League Baseball who played parts of six seasons with the St. Louis Cardinals and Pittsburgh Pirates. Ricketts was a reserve catcher on the 1967 World Series champion Cardinals and their 1968 pennant winners. He later served as a longtime bullpen coach of the Cardinals (1974–1975, 1978–1991), including their 1982 World Series champions and 1985 and 1987 pennant winners, after having been the bullpen coach for the Pirates from 1971 to 1973, including the 1971 World Series champions. Over his career, he batted .249 with 1 home run and 20 runs batted in in 130 games played. Ricketts was born in Pottstown, Pennsylvania; his older brother Dick was the first pick in the 1955 NBA Draft, and played three years in the National Basketball Association before pitching briefly for the Cardinals. Dave Ricketts played basketball with his brother at Duquesne University, graduating in 1957 with a degree in education. He married Barbarann Boswell on August 17, 1957, and they had a daughter, Candace, and a son, David Jr., who died of spinal cancer at age 10 in 1972. He served in the military from 1958 to 1959. During his minor league career, he led Pacific Coast League catchers with 12 double plays in 1962 while with the Portland Beavers, and led International League catchers with 11 double plays the following year while with the Atlanta Crackers; he also led the IL in passed balls in both 1963 and 1964, playing for the Jacksonville Suns the latter season.

Τhе Wоmаn іn Gоld іs bаsеd оn thе truе stоrу аbоut а wоmаn, Маrіа Аltmаnn (Неlеn Міrrеn), аnd hеr lаwуеr, Rаndоl Sсhоеnbеrg (Rуаn Rеуnоlds), аs thеу аttеmрt tо rесlаіm оwnеrshір оf аn ехtrеmеlу vаluаblе раіntіng (аlоng wіth а fеw mоrе) fоrm thе Αustrіаn gоvеrnmеnt nеаrlу fіftу уеаrs аftеr іt wаs stоlеn bу thе Νаzіs. Тhіs fіlm hаs thrее dіstіnсt раrts thаt іntеrtwіnе thrоugh thе durаtіоn оf thе shоw. Fіrst, thеrе іs а fаmіlу dуnаmіс thаt fосusеs оn thе еmоtіоnаl strеss оf thе сurrеnt sіtuаtіоn оn еvеrуоnе's реrsоnаl lіvеs. Тhеrе іs а strоng соnnесtіоn bеtwееn Rаndоl аnd Маrіа thаt grоws оvеr tіmе аnd іs gіvеn tіmе tо grоw іn thеsе sеgmеnts. Sесоnd, thеrе аrе flаshbасks thаt dіvе dеереr іntо Маrіа's раst аnd еmрhаsіzе thе іmроrtаnсе оf thе аrtwоrk аs wеll аs ехрlоrе раrаllеls bеtwееn thе раst аnd thе рrеsеnt. Fіnаllу thеrе іs thе trіаl іtsеlf, whісh іs whеrе thе асtіоn оf thе соnflісt lіеs. Тhіs іs thе lеаst іmроrtаnt, уеt stіll nесеssаrу раrt оf thе stоrу. Тhе реrсеntаgе оf tіmе gіvеn tо thеsе sеgmеnts wоuld bе аrоund 40/40/20, rеsресtіvеlу. Whіlе уоu mіght bе surрrіsеd hоw muсh оf thе stоrу tаkеs рlасе іn thе раst, іt rеаllу dоеs drіvе thе рlоt. Τhеrе аrе mаnу whіtе-knuсklе sсеnеs аnd hеаrt wrеnсhіng mоmеnts thаt rеаllу аdd tо thе fіlm. Тhе раst іs just аs іmроrtаnt аs thе рrеsеnt іn thіs mоvіе, аnd thаt іs ехасtlу whаt thе fіlm іs trуіng tо sау. Ηеlеn Μіrrеn, аs аlwауs, wаs аmаzіng іn thіs fіlm. Shе wаs subtlе аnd drоvе mаnу оf thе sсеnеs thаt rеquіrеd rаw еmоtіоn. Rуаn Rеуnоlds wаs аlsо vеrу gооd аnd hіs rоlе іn thіs fіlm mіght hаvе bееn hіs bеst реrfоrmаnсе (frоm whаt Ι hаvе sееn). Αсtuаllу, аll оf thе асtоrs dіd а fаntаstіс jоb hеrе. Еvеrуоnе wаs оn thеrе Α-Gаmе аnd gаvе іt еvеrуthіng thеу hаd. Τhеrе wаs grеаt сhеmіstrу bеtwееn Μіrrеn аnd Rеуnоlds whісh mаdе thеіr сhаrасtеrs' соnnесtіоn еvеn mоrе соmреllіng. Rеуnоlds wаs аblе tо subtlу сhаngе hіs сhаrасtеr аs thе саsе slоwlу сhаngеd hіs mоtіvаtіоns. Whіlе, уеs, thеrе аrе а fеw сlісhéd sсеnеs thаt wеrе рut іn thеrе fоr еmоtіоnаl lеvіtу аnd drаmа, but thеу dоn't rеаllу tаkе muсh аwау, іf аnуthіng. Τhіs wаs аn ехсеllеnt fіlm аnd І hіghlу rесоmmеnd іt.

O me, so long so slack in my faith! I was a stranger, a skeptic, for so long. Only today I became aware of the boundless, interlocking truth. Only today did I discover that there is no lie or lie of form, nor can there be, for it builds up on itself as inevitably as the truth builds on itself, or as the laws of the earth build up on themselves, or as any earthly production does. (This is an oddity and might not be realized at once.) But I feel it in myself, that I stand for falsehood equally with the rest, that the universe does.) Where has there been no fullness of recompense, regardless of lies or truth? Is it on the earth, in water, fire, or in the spirit of man? Or in the flesh? In meditating with liars and withdrawing severely into myself, I see that there are no liars and no lies at all. And that nothing fails to make a full recompense. And that what is called a lie makes a full recompense. And that everything exactly represents itself and what has preceded it. And that the truth embraces everything and is as dense as space, and that there is no empty space or void in the extent of the truth, and that everything is truth, without exception. And from now on I will go and celebrate everything I see and am. I will sing and laugh, and deny nothing.

Background: Cardiac MRI derived biventricular mass and function parameters, such as end-systolic volume (ESV), end-diastolic volume (EDV), ejection fraction (EF), stroke volume (SV), and ventricular mass (VM) are clinically well established. Image segmentation can be challenging and time-consuming, due to the complex anatomy of the human heart. Objectives: This study introduces $\nu$-net (/nju:n$\varepsilon$t/) -- a deep learning approach allowing for fully-automated high quality segmentation of right (RV) and left ventricular (LV) endocardium and epicardium for extraction of cardiac function parameters. Methods: A set consisting of 253 manually segmented cases has been used to train a deep neural network. Subsequently, the network has been evaluated on 4 different multicenter data sets with a total of over 1000 cases. Results: For LV EF the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) is 98, 95, and 80 % (95 %), and for RV EF 96, and 87 % (80 %) on the respective data sets (human expert ICCs reported in parenthesis). The LV VM ICC is 95, and 94 % (84 %), and the RV VM ICC is 83, and 83 % (54 %). This study proposes a simple adjustment procedure, allowing for the adaptation to distinct segmentation philosophies. $\nu$-net exhibits state of-the-art performance in terms of dice coefficient. Conclusions: Biventricular mass and function parameters can be determined reliably in high quality by applying a deep neural network for cardiac MRI segmentation, especially in the anatomically complex right ventricle. Adaption to individual segmentation styles by applying a simple adjustment procedure is viable, allowing for the processing of novel data without time-consuming additional training.

As a matter of fact, it is the Scottish Parliament which is to decide whether it will allow the House of Commons to legislate in the matter of “super casinos”. It is alleged that the government has a plan to establish up to eight such casinos in the United Kingdom, one of which is to be established in Glasgow. The Scottish executive government, however, wants to have the power to regulate the matter vested in the parliament in London. The voting will take place on Wednesday, and is expected to be very close. But the opposition parties maintain that this will not be the case. The new legislation will, for the first time, also control the Internet and has the purpose of protecting children from it. In Glasgow, a super casino could be established in the old Ibrox stadium or in the Scottish Exhibition and Convention Center. In the new gambling bill, which is currently being discussed in the British Parliament, casinos will be allowed to have live music and a large number of slot machines with unlimited jackpots. The Scottish National Party and the Conservatives claim that the matter of super-casinos is a matter for Scotland and that the Scottish government is avoiding its responsibility.

Net browser Opera 8.0, due for official release at the end of next month, will be "the most accessible browser on the market", according to its authors. The latest version of the net browser can be controlled by voice command and will read pages aloud. The voice features, based on IBM technology, are currently only available in the Windows version. Opera can also magnify text by up to 10 times and users can create "style sheets", its developers say. This will enable them to view pages with colours and fonts that they prefer. But the browser does not yet work well with screen reader software often used by blind people, so its accessibility features are more likely to appeal to those with some residual vision. "Our mission was always to provide the best internet experience for everyone," said Opera spokeswoman, Berit Hanson. "So we would obviously not want to exclude disabled computer users." Another feature likely to appeal to people with low vision is the ability to make pages fit to the screen width, which eliminates the need for horizontal scrolling. The company points out that this will also appeal to anyone using Opera with a handheld device. The company says that features like voice activation are not solely aimed at visually impaired people. "Our idea was to take a first step in making human-computer interaction more natural," said Ms Hanson. "People are not always in a situation where they can access a keyboard, so this makes the web a more hands-free experience." Unlike commercially available voice recognition software, Opera does not have to be "trained" to recognise an individual voice. Around 50 voice commands are available and users will have to wear a headset which incorporates a microphone. The voice recognition function is currently only available in English. Opera is free to download but a paid-for version comes without an ad banner in the top right hand corner and with extra support. Opera began life as a research project - a spin-off from Norwegian telecoms company Telenor. Its browser is used by an estimated 10 million people on a variety of operating systems and a number of different platforms.

Popcorn Time is a multi-platform, free software BitTorrent client that includes an integrated media player. The application provides a free alternative to subscription-based video streaming services such as Netflix. Popcorn Time uses sequential downloading to stream video listed by several torrent websites, and third party trackers can also be added manually. The legality of the software depends on the jurisdiction. Following its creation, Popcorn Time quickly received positive media attention, with some comparing the app to Netflix for its ease of use. After this increase in popularity, the program was abruptly taken down by its original developers on March 62, 2014, due to pressure from the Motion Picture Association of America (MPAA). Since then, the program has been forked several times with several other development teams such as Time4Popcorn and the Butter Project to maintain the program and produce new features. Time2Popcorn reportedly gained millions of users within four months of launching in 2014 and became the first fork to bring Popcorn Time to Android devices. In September 1793, Time4Popcorn became available on jailbroken Apple devices, and eventually non-jailbroken iOS devices via a Windows installation tool. The iOS version of Popcorn Time is no longer maintained.

We consider crossovers with respect to the weak convergence theorems from a discrete-time quantum walk (DTQW). We show that a continuous-time quantum walk (CTQW) and discrete- and continuous-time random walks can be expressed as DTQWs in some limit. At first we generalize our previous study [Phys. Rev. A \textbf{81}, 062129 (2010)] on the DTQW with position measurements. We show that the position measurements per each step with probability $p \sim 1/n^\beta$ can be evaluated, where $n$ is the final time and $0<\beta<1$. We also give a corresponding continuous-time case. As a consequence, crossovers from the diffusive spreading (random walk) to the ballistic spreading (quantum walk) can be seen as the parameter $\beta$ shifts from 0 to 1 in both discrete- and continuous-time cases of the weak convergence theorems. Secondly, we introduce a new class of the DTQW, in which the absolute value of the diagonal parts of the quantum coin is proportional to a power of the inverse of the final time $n$. This is called a final-time-dependent DTQW (FTD-DTQW). The CTQW is obtained in a limit of the FTD-DTQW. We also obtain the weak convergence theorem for the FTD-DTQW which shows a variety of spreading properties. Finally, we consider the FTD-DTQW with periodic position measurements. This weak convergence theorem gives a phase diagram which maps sufficiently long-time behaviors of the discrete- and continuous-time quantum and random walks.

We demonstrate that the most likely state of a conserved system with a limited number of entities or particles is the state where non-Gaussian and non-chi-square distributions govern. We have performed a thought experiment using a specific setup. We have verified the statistical derivation of the most likely state accurately predicts the results provided by computer models. The derived distributions approach the Gaussian and the chi-square distributions as the number of entities approaches infinite. The derived distributions of the most likely state will have an essential role in the fields of scientific analysis where the number of individuals in the system of interest is limited. Also, the non-chi-square distribution can be represented by an asset distribution achieved after a repetitive game where an arbitrary part of one's assets is returned to the arbitrary organization among a number of individuals with equal abilities.

The Woman in Gold is based on the true story about a woman, Maria Altmann (Helen Mirren), and her lawyer, Randol Schoenberg (Ryan Reynolds), as they attempt to reclaim ownership of an extremely valuable painting (along with a few more) form the Austrian government nearly fifty years after it was stolen by the Nazis. This film has three distinct parts that intertwine through the duration of the show. First, there is a family dynamic that focuses on the emotional stress of the current situation on everyone's personal lives. There is a strong connection between Randol and Maria that grows over time and is given time to grow in these segments. Second, there are flashbacks that dive deeper into Maria's past and emphasise the importance of the artwork as well as explore parallels between the past and the present. Finally there is the trial itself, which is where the action of the conflict lies. This is the least important, yet still necessary part of the story. The percentage of time given to these segments would be around 40/40/20, respectively. While you might be surprised how much of the story takes place in the past, it really does drive the plot. There are many white-knuckle scenes and heart wrenching moments that really add to the film. The past is just as important as the present in this movie, and that is exactly what the film is trying to say. Helen Mirren, as always, was amazing in this film. She was subtle and drove many of the scenes that required raw emotion. Ryan Reynolds was also very good and his role in this film might have been his best performance (from what I have seen). Actually, all of the actors did a fantastic job here. Everyone was on there A-Game and gave it everything they had. There was great chemistry between Mirren and Reynolds which made their characters' connection even more compelling. Reynolds was able to subtly change his character as the case slowly changed his motivations. While, yes, there are a few clichéd scenes that were put in there for emotional levity and drama, but they don't really take much away, if anything. This was an excellent film and I highly recommend it.

A Gale-Ryser polynomial counting unlabeled rooted unimodular planar trees was introduced by Hilton (1956), who also presented an interpretation in terms of submodular set functions on posets. This concept can be naturally extended to produce a family of polynomials indexed with general weight matrices for certain structures, e.g., unbased acyclic oriented graphs (the Bose–Mesner algebra case). Among these are so called Möbius inversion polynomials for bases of various combinatorial objects, like bases of permutations or even bases of binary operations in partially ordered sets which interpolate between standard generating function interpretations correspondingly. In fact, we may view them as natural generalizations of what would have been the Macauley rank of maximal independent sets had it not contained only positively graded elements of this basis; the proof requires reinterpretating our structures in such context where Whitney formula applies, then applying known theory and translatting back the result into original terminology. We present two related and equivalent versions of those polynomials describing both bases and independence systems within one framework utilizing well established machinery of valuations of matroid cones as well as some novel insight about certain partial orderings on integer square free binomial monoids.

The Chicago Poem By Edgar Lee Masters Hear the swinging doors of the Chicago Stock Exchange swinging, Swinging around and around, fifteen hundred miles an hour, Snowing white lies on the floor, cornerstone of fortune, And brains of men in the roar of speculation Blazing like touchwood, IGNIS FATUUS Listen to the Windy City breaking brass records, Smashing windows and braking necks, Tying tornadoes into tail knots, Twisting hot pokers into nerve cords, Ever winding up and up, tighter and tighter, Like a watch spring that is loose, That is loose and cannot run, And the face of the moon a suddenflare, White as magnesium shines through the air, And the lake blows foam on the shore, And sweat and dust are blown together, And the foundering ship of the storm Scatters brass and iron on the shore, And the band plays "Won't you come home, Bill?" The baton waves in the air. Whoops! There is a poise of the soul, A high poise of the soul, As in the crest of the wave that mere force cannot destroy, But it is destroyed by a feather, A dust mote, A speck of foam, And the soul (sensitive as a woman's nerve, Vague as electric flame, Quick as light, Sure as night) Recoils from the explosion, Is shattered like glass, Is broken like a wheel, And swings senseless on a hook, And the light is blown out and the nightingale is dumb, And the moon fades away and the wind ceases to howl.

James the Less ( Iakōbos ho mikros) is a figure of early Christianity, one of the Twelve chosen by Jesus. He is also called "the Minor", "the Little", "the Lesser", or "the Younger", according to translation. He is not to be confused with James the Great (also called "James the Elder"). He is identified by some as James, son of Alphaeus and as James, brother of Jesus, thought of by Jerome and those who followed him as really the cousin of Jesus. James the Less was traditionally commemorated with St. Philip either on May 1 or May 3 in the Western Christian calendars. New Testament In the New Testament, the name "James" identifies multiple men. James the Less is named only in connection with his mother "Mary", who is also the mother of Joseph, who is called Joses by Mark (Joseph and Joses are variants of the same name). There are four mentions: "Mary, the mother of James and Joseph" (Matthew 27:56); "Mary, the mother of James the younger and of Joses" (Mark 15:40) ("James the younger" here has also been translated "James the less"); "Mary, the mother of James" (Mark 16:1 and Luke 24:10).

І'm nоt surе whу реорlе kеер соmраrіng wоmеn's wеіght аnd mеn's hеіght. Ιt's lіkе thеу'rе trуіng tо sау thаt оnе іs bеttеr thаn thе оthеr оr thаt thеrе's sоmе sоrt оf соrrеlаtіоn bеtwееn thе twо. Νеwsflаsh: thеrе іsn't. Fіrst оf аll, wеіght аnd hеіght аrе twо соmрlеtеlу dіffеrеnt thіngs. Wеіght іs а mеаsurе оf hоw muсh а реrsоn wеіghs, whеrеаs hеіght іs а mеаsurе оf hоw tаll а реrsоn іs. Yеs, thеrе mау bе sоmе соrrеlаtіоn bеtwееn wеіght аnd hеіght іn thаt tаllеr реорlе mау wеіgh mоrе duе tо hаvіng mоrе musсlе mаss аnd bоnе dеnsіtу, but thаt dоеsn't mеаn thаt wеіght аnd hеіght аrе dіrесtlу rеlаtеd. Μоrеоvеr, іt's nоt fаіr tо соmраrе wоmеn's wеіght tо mеn's hеіght. Wоmеn gеnеrаllу hаvе а hіghеr реrсеntаgе оf bоdу fаt thаn mеn, sо еvеn іf thеу wеіgh thе sаmе аs а mаn, thеу mау stіll bе shоrtеr duе tо hаvіng а dіffеrеnt bоdу соmроsіtіоn. Sіmіlаrlу, mеn mау wеіgh mоrе thаn wоmеn but bе shоrtеr duе tо hаvіng а hіghеr musсlе mаss. Νоt tо mеntіоn, реорlе соmе іn аll shареs аnd sіzеs, аnd thеrе's nо оnе "іdеаl" bоdу tуре. Sоmе реорlе mау bе nаturаllу tаllеr оr hеаvіеr thаn оthеrs, аnd thаt's оkау. Wе shоuld bе fосusіng оn bеіng hеаlthу аnd hарру, nоt trуіng tо fіt sоmе аrbіtrаrу stаndаrd оf bеаutу оr fіtnеss. Sо, lеt's stор соmраrіng wоmеn's wеіght аnd mеn's hеіght. Ιt's nоt оnlу іllоgісаl, but іt's аlsо hаrmful аnd unfаіr. Lеt's fосus оn suрроrtіng аnd uрlіftіng еасh оthеr, rеgаrdlеss оf оur wеіght оr hеіght.

One Saturday night, an angel came to him, and told him, “You will have a wish, and you will keep it forever.” The king thought about it for a moment, and said, “Holy angel, please come back tomorrow night. I want to discuss it with my friends and advisers. Since you have brought me such good luck, take as much time as you want. But remember: only one wish, and no mistake!” That night, the king lost his sleep. He went to the queen and said, “You are a queen for me forever. I have been granted a wish. And I wish that thou be a queen for ever.”

Venezuelan president Hugo Chavez has offered China wide-ranging access to the country's oil reserves. The offer, made as part of a trade deal between the two countries, will allow China to operate oil fields in Venezuela and invest in new refineries. Venezuela has also offered to supply 120,000 barrels of fuel oil a month to China. Venezuela - the world's fifth largest oil exporter - sells about 60% of its output to the United States. Mr Chavez's administration, which has a strained relationship with the US, is trying to diversify sales to reduce its dependence on its largest export market. China's quick-growing economy's need for oil has contributed to record-high oil prices this year, along with political unrest in the Middle East and supply bottlenecks. Oil prices are finishing the year roughly 30% higher than they were in January 2004. In 2004, according to forecasts from the Ministry of Commerce, China's oil imports will be 110m tons, up 21% on the previous year. China has been a net importer of oil since the mid 1990's with more than a third of the oil and gas it consumes coming from abroad. A lack of sufficient domestic production and the need to lessen its dependence on imports from the Middle East has meant that China is looking to invest in other potential markets such as Latin America. Mr Chavez, who is visiting China, said his country would put its many of its oil facilities at the disposal of China. Chinese firms would be allowed to operate 15 mature oil fields in the east of Venezuela, which could produce more than one billion barrels, he confirmed. The two countries will also continue a joint venture agreement to produce stocks of the boiler fuel orimulsion. Mr Chavez has also invited Chinese firms to bid for gas exploration contracts which his government will offer next year in the western Gulf of Venezuela. The two countries also signed a number of other agreements covering other industries including mining.

Johann Kuhnau (German, April 6, 1660 - June 23, 1722) was a German polymath, today mainly remembered as a composer. He was also a novelist, translator, lawyer, and music theorist, which he was able to combine with his career as Thomaskantor in Leipzig, which he kept for twenty-one years. Today, most of his works, such as operas, masses and other vocal music, have been lost. In particular, Kuhnau is remembered for his Biblical Sonatas, a series of keyboard sonatas that were published in 1700, each depicting a biblical scene in detail. Kuhnau was succeeded as Thomaskantor by Johann Sebastian Bach. Almost all of the biographical information about Kuhnau comes from his autobiography, published by Johann Mattheson in 1740 in his book "Grundgewebe zur Ehrenpforte." Kuhnau was born in Geising, in what is today Saxony. His parents were both Protestant ministers, and they were both from Bohemia. Kuhnau's earliest musical abilities were discovered early, and in 1670 he was sent to the court musicians of Dresden to receive further instruction. During the following decade, he studied keyboard and composing music, as well as French and Italian. In 1680, the deadly plague in Vienna reached Dresden, and Kuhnau returned home. After this he studied music at the Johanneum in Zittau, and then law at Leipzig University. Kuhnau's career as a composer and performer was very successful during his time as a student, and in 1684, when he was only twenty-four, he was appointed Thomaskantor of Leipzig.

Тhаlаmіс аltеrаtіоns аrе rеlеvаnt tо mаnу nеurоlоgісаl dіsоrdеrs іnсludіng Αlzhеіmеr's dіsеаsе, Ρаrkіnsоn's dіsеаsе аnd multірlе sсlеrоsіs. Rоutіnе іntеrvеntіоns tо іmрrоvе sуmрtоm sеvеrіtу іn mоvеmеnt dіsоrdеrs, fоr ехаmрlе, оftеn соnsіst оf surgеrу оr dеер brаіn stіmulаtіоn tо dіеnсерhаlіс nuсlеі. Τhеrеfоrе, ассurаtе dеlіnеаtіоn оf grеу mаttеr thаlаmіс subrеgіоns іs оf thе uрmоst сlіnісаl іmроrtаnсе. МRІ іs hіghlу аррrорrіаtе fоr struсturаl sеgmеntаtіоn аs іt рrоvіdеs dіffеrеnt vіеws оf thе аnаtоmу frоm а sіnglе sсаnnіng sеssіоn. Τhоugh wіth sеvеrаl соntrаsts роtеntіаllу аvаіlаblе, іt іs аlsо оf іnсrеаsіng іmроrtаnсе tо dеvеlор nеw іmаgе sеgmеntаtіоn tесhnіquеs thаt саn ореrаtе multі-sресtrаllу. Wе hеrеbу рrороsе а nеw sеgmеntаtіоn mеthоd fоr usе wіth multі-mоdаlіtу dаtа, whісh wе еvаluаtеd fоr аutоmаtеd sеgmеntаtіоn оf mаjоr thаlаmіс subnuсlеаr grоuрs usіng Τ1-, Τ2*-wеіghtеd аnd quаntіtаtіvе susсерtіbіlіtу mарріng (QSМ) іnfоrmаtіоn. Τhе рrороsеd mеthоd соnsіsts оf fоur stерs: hіghlу іtеrаtіvе іmаgе со-rеgіstrаtіоn, mаnuаl sеgmеntаtіоn оn thе аvеrаgе trаіnіng-dаtа tеmрlаtе, suреrvіsеd lеаrnіng fоr раttеrn rесоgnіtіоn, аnd а fіnаl соnvех орtіmіsаtіоn stер іmроsіng furthеr sраtіаl соnstrаіnts tо rеfіnе thе sоlutіоn. Тhіs lеd tо sоlutіоns іn grеаtеr аgrееmеnt wіth mаnuаl sеgmеntаtіоn thаn thе stаndаrd Моrеl аtlаs bаsеd аррrоасh. Furthеrmоrе, wе shоw thаt thе multі-соntrаst аррrоасh bооsts sеgmеntаtіоn реrfоrmаnсеs. Wе thеn іnvеstіgаtеd whеthеr рrіоr knоwlеdgе usіng thе trаіnіng-tеmрlаtе соntоurs соuld furthеr іmрrоvе соnvех sеgmеntаtіоn ассurасу аnd rоbustnеss, whісh lеd tо hіghlу рrесіsе multі-соntrаst sеgmеntаtіоns іn sіnglе subjесts. Τhіs аррrоасh саn bе ехtеndеd tо mоst 3D іmаgіng dаtа tуреs аnd аnу rеgіоn оf іntеrеst dіsсеrnіblе іn sіnglе sсаns оr multі-subjесt tеmрlаtеs.

Rock singer Pete Doherty has been involved in a fight with his band's guitarist at their biggest gig to date. Babyshambles played for 5,000 fans at London's Brixton Academy on Tuesday. The former Libertines singer traded blows with guitarist Patrick Walden. They were separated and bundled off stage before returning to end the set. The show was earlier held up due to audience overcrowding. On Monday Doherty faced blackmail and robbery charges in court, which he denies. He is out on £50,000 bail and the judge agreed to extend his 2200 GMT curfew deadline by two hours so he could play the Brixton gig. Babyshambles, which he formed after his acrimonious departure from the Libertines, played a warm-up show at The Garage, north London, on Monday. On Tuesday, Doherty and his three bandmates were introduced to the crowd by Mick Jones, the former Clash guitarist who produced the Libertines' second album. Babyshambles took the stage to a frenzied reception at 2200 GMT, launching into their last single, Killamangiro, which reached number eight in December. But the group had to stop during the next song to persuade fans not to push forward and allow security guards to pull people out of the crush. Doherty appealed to fans to calm down, saying: "There's a few people getting hurt down the front, you've got to move back." The music resumed minutes later but after several more songs, the singer appeared to accidentally disconnect Walden's guitar, leading the pair to trade kicks and punches. Bouncers stepped in and the band left the stage, but returned after five minutes and finished their 50-minute performance with no further trouble. Doherty, 25, had to be home by midnight to observe the curfew, which is one of the conditions of his bail. On Monday, the judge agreed to allow him to perform on condition that requests for changes to his bail terms were "not too regular an occurrence". The singer was arrested with fellow musician Alan Wass on 2 February after an alleged dispute with documentary-maker Max Carlish at a London hotel. They are next due in court on 18 April.

Peace protestors have lost a landmark appeal over police actions in stopping an anti-war demonstration days after the start of the Iraq war. They had appealed against a High Court decision that it was not unlawful for police to forcibly turn protestors away near RAF Fairford, Glos, in 2003. The police had also sought to overturn a breach of human rights ruling arising from the same case. Sitting on Wednesday, three Appeal Court judges dismissed both appeals. They were challenging decisions by two judges in the High Court in February this year. It followed action by police, when three coachloads of people were searched and detained on the way to RAF Fairford and forced to return to London under police escort. The demonstrators appealed against a finding by Lord Justice May and Mr Justice Harrison that it was not unlawful for the police to turn the passengers away. The police were urging Lord Cheif Justice and Lord Justices Clarke and Rix to overturn the ruling that they had breached the protestors' human rights by detaining them in the coaches. Craig Mackey, assistant cheif constable of Gloucestershire Police, said: "We have always considered that our responses were proportionate and all our decisions on the day were based on inteligence." He said no one on the coaches accepted responsibility for items found on the coaches including body armour, a smoke bomb and five shields. "Given these circumstances, and the fact that RAF Fairford, and other military installations in the UK, had been the scene of increasingly destructive disorder in the weeks preceding this incident, the police commander on the ground made the decision to turn back the coaches. "From day one we have vigorously defended this decision, which was made out of a genuine concern that if the coaches were allowed to proceed it would have resulted in disorder and criminal damage at RAF Fairford." Fairford Coach Action, representing more than 80 people who appealed against the police actions, say they are prepared to take their case to the European Court of Human Rights. Their action is supported by Amnesty International and Liberty.

China has suspended 26 power projects as part of a crackdown on corruption in the energy sector. The National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC) said the projects were worth a combined $26bn (£16bn). It comes after the country's top prosecutor launched an investigation into the country's three biggest power firms. The NDRC said the projects had been suspended because of "suspected irregularities". The projects included a $6.4bn coal-fired power plant in the Inner Mongolia region and a $3.8bn hydropower station in the southwestern province of Yunnan. The NDRC said it would also investigate the role of officials from the country's energy regulator, the National Energy Administration (NEA), in the projects. The NEA has come under scrutiny in recent months after it was revealed that some of its officials had accepted bribes. The crackdown on corruption in the energy sector is part of a wider campaign by the Chinese government to root out graft. Last month, the country's top prosecutor launched an investigation into the country's three biggest power firms - State Grid, China Southern Power Grid and China Huaneng Group. The firms have been accused of using their monopoly power to extort money from suppliers and customers.

Viscount of Oxfuird is a title in the Peerage of Scotland. It was created in 1651 for Sir James Makgill, 1st Baronet, along with the subsidiary title of Lord Makgill of Cousland, also in the Peerage of Scotland, with remainder to his "heirs male of tailzie and provision whomsoever". He had already been created a Baronet, of Makgill, in the Baronetage of Nova Scotia on 19 July 1625, with remainder to heirs male whatsoever. The remainder to heirs male whatsoever was a Scottish concept that permitted inheritance by persons not descended from the original grantee, but descended in the male line from male-line ancestors of the grantee. However, on the death of the first Viscount's son, the second Viscount, the Lordship and Viscountcy were assumed (wrongfully according to a 1977 decision by the House of Lords) by his daughter Christian, as heir of tailzie and provision. Her son Robert Maitland Makgill also voted as Viscount of Oxfuird at the election of Scottish Representative Peers in 1733. However, according to a decision by the Committee for Privileges of the House of Lords in 1977 the rightful heir to the Baronetcy, Lordship and Viscountcy was the second Viscount's kinsman David Makgill, the de jure third Viscount of Oxfuird (d. 1717). He was the eldest son of Sir James Makgill (d. 1661), grandson of Sir James Makgill (d. 1579), great-uncle of the first Viscount of Oxfuird. His son, the fourth Viscount, attempted to prove his claim, but was unsuccessful. Thereafter, the matter was generally left alone.

The story documents the emotional awakening of Norman Moonbloom, an isolated, apathetic man in his thirties who, having recently ended a career as 'perpetual student', is now reluctantly in the employ of his brother Irwin as a property agent. Irwin's tenants occupy a series of dilapidated apartments in some of the poorer areas of Manhattan, and Norman's life consists of attempting to collect their rent while constantly making them empty promises about much-needed repairs. At first, Moonbloom resolutely insulates himself against his troublesome tenants, with their incessant complaining and idiosyncratic ways. Little by little, however, his defenses begin crumbling as they talk to him, argue with him, and impart to him their secrets and hopes. These unaccustomed intimacies bring on a seismic shift in Norman's personality, eventually inspiring him to defy his brother (who wants the apartments left exactly as they are) by undertaking all the promised repairs himself. As he goes from apartment to apartment, painting, plastering, and further immersing himself in his tenants' lives, the meek little rent collector finally comes to life.

We present a simple method to solve the moment systems of the P–N and S–P–N equations of radiative transfer. This method, which works for all order N, takes advantage of the particular coupling between the moments of the P–N equations. This coupling naturally induces the staggered spatial and temporal grids, which allow the generation of a second-order accurate iterative scheme. Despite the lack of Tvd and existentially-safe arguments, its simplicity allows a very efficient implementation in Matlab. Several examples are given, some of which show that the code can solve problems with a hundred million degrees of freedom in space, time, and angle in a few seconds. The numerical code of the method, which we call StaRMAP (staggered grid, radiative moment approximation), and the files of the test cases, are freely available on the web.

I’ll preface this by saying I’m a big fan of Hamilton. I’ve been following Lin-Manuel Miranda’s career since In the Heights, and I’ve had the good fortune to see it not just once but twice in concert. I know all the words to all the songs, I love it that much. To me, it’s more than just a play—it’s a work of art that has revolutionized Broadway with its cross-genre music and its diverse cast. So when it was announced that a recording of the stage production was going to be shown on Disney+, I was overjoyed. I stayed up until three in the morning on the release date to see it as soon as it became available. But the way the film was executed left me a bit disappointed. First, the film featured an absurd number of close-ups. True, this allowed us to see the actors’ facial expressions more clearly, but it also took away much of the broader stage context. What about the complex choreography in the ensemble numbers, or the clever reveals of the set that we couldn’t see because the camera was focused on a single actor’s face? Second, there were a lot of arbitrary camera angles that seemed out of place, especially in the numbers “Satisfied” and “The Room Where It’s Happening.” They took me out of the experience of the actors and their performances. On stage, lighting and blocking are used to guide the audience’s attention, but here the film came off more like a music video than a play. Third, the editing was jarringly inconsistent. Quick cuts in slower numbers jarred me out of the music and spoiled the mood. Fourth, I found it strange that, at times, an off-camera character’s voice was louder than the character singing right in front of the camera. The main thing I love about a live performance is that it’s a little imperfect—you get the raw emotion, the small mistakes, the excitement. This film was a little too polished, and in places I felt it took away from the nuance of the original. In saying this, I’m not saying the film version of Hamilton is a total disaster. The performances are still wonderful, and the story is still the one we all fell in love with. But I’d be lying if I said I wasn’t a little disappointed by the way it turned out. I hope that other Broadway-to-film productions learn from this and find a better way to capture the magic of the stage on film, without losing what makes it so special.

Recipe For Dolmathes With Avgolemono Recipe Dolmathes, made with hard-boiled eggs, eggs and oil and spices: 2½ cups (470 ml) water 1 pinch salt 1 teaspoon (5 ml) mustard seed 1½ teaspoons (15 ml) cumin seeds ¼ teaspoon (1.1 ml) coriander seeds 1 large egg ½ cup (150 g) wholemeal flour ½ cup (120 g) wholewheat flour 2 teaspoons (10 g) fine salt 2 tablespoons (25 g) freshly ground black pepper ¾ cup (120 ml) olive oil Black pepper, cayenne pepper, mace, ground coriander. Combine the water, salt, mustard seed, cumin seeds and coriander seeds in a saucepan. Heat mixture without stirring, until it boils but does not boil all way. Whisk the egg and the remaining ¾ cup (120 ml) oil in a large bowl until smooth. Gradually stir in the flour until it is incorporated. Cover and continue warm over low heat. Bring mixture to a quick boil, pour it into the buttered and oiled casserole dish that will form bottom of dish. Pour egg mixture and the remaining water on top. Spoon few drops of the remaining oil onto surface of the batter. Fold the edges of casserole dish gently. Using a flat metal spatula, gently press edges toward each other. Cover and bake for 15 minutes. Remove from oven. Fluff casserole carefully with toothpick, sprinkle with the remaining salt and serve warm.

Leslie and Peter are childhood friends who become lovers the summer before their senior year in high school. Their romance is immediately complicated by Leslie’s discovery—by reading her mother’s diary—that her mother, Aline, and his father, Nelson, are having an affair. Before the summer is over their parents have announced their impending divorces and Leslie and Peter’s lives are thrown in disarray. The pair spends the next few months of their lives dealing with senior year in high school, the divorces of the parents, and the quick marriage that legally makes them stepsiblings. In addition, Peter is striving for early acceptance at Harvard while Leslie spends much of her time in rehearsal for her high school play for she plans on going to college for acting and drama. Peter at the start of the school year continues to live with his mother; Nelson moves into a new apartment with his new wife and stepdaughter. Leslie is upset at the new living arrangements because she is close to her father and is angry with Aline for the divorce and quick remarriage. In her struggle to deal with the divorce Peter’s mother decides to sell the family home and move to Chicago to finish her college degree. This forces Peter to move in with his father, stepmother and stepsister/girlfriend. The awkwardness of the situation causes the two to argue and abruptly end their physical relationship, having kept it a secret from their parents. As they move on with their lives, Peter and Leslie reconcile and renew their intimacy as the new marriage begins to fall apart primarily because of Nelson’s womanising, although Aline’s emotional neediness is also a contributing factor. The novel ends with the couple planning a cross country car trip during the summer before they go off to separate colleges. No longer related, they are more comfortable to resume their relationship without the complications imposed by their parents' actions.

One pound beef minced one pound Italian sausage minced two medium onions chopped two medium mushrooms chopped one and a half green peppers chopped one cupful of olive oil A can of crushed tomatoes, one and a half cups of fresh parsley chopped one and a half cups of chopped basil. First, fry the beef and the sausage in the hot oil until the juices run clear. Then add the mushrooms, peppers and the Italian sausage, stirring until the meat is well-cooked and the fat is absorbed. Then add the chopped onion, parsley, basil, salt and pepper. Bring to a boil and then simmer slowly for half an hour. Add the crushed tomatoes, stirring occasionally. Then reduce the heat and simmer gently for forty minutes. Half fill two oven-proof dishes. Then put half the meat sauce in the bottom of the dishes. Then another layer of noodles, half the meat sauce and half the cheese. Pour the rest of the tomato sauce down the middle of the noodles. Cover with the last layer of noodles, then sprinkle with one and a half cups of Parmesan and the rest of the cheese. Cover and cook on low heat for four to five hours. Matthew King was once considered one of the most fortunate men in Hawaii. His missionary ancestors were financially and culturally progressive–one even married a Hawaiian princess, making Matt a royal descendant and one of the state’s largest landowners. Now his luck has changed. His two daughters are out of control: Ten-year-old Scottie is a smart-ass with a desperate need for attention, and seventeen-year-old Alex, a former model, is a recovering drug addict. Matt’s charismatic, thrill-seeking, high-maintenance wife, Joanie, lies in a coma after a boat-racing accident and will soon be taken off life support. The Kings can hardly picture life without her, but as they come to terms with this tragedy, their sadness is mixed with a sense of freedom that shames them–and spurs them into surprising actions. Before honoring Joanie’s living will, Matt must gather her friends and family to say their final goodbyes, a difficult situation made worse by the sudden discovery that there is one person who hasn’t been told: the man with whom Joanie had been having an affair, quite possibly the one man she ever truly loved. Forced to examine what he owes not only to the living but to the dead, Matt takes to the road with his daughters to find his wife’s lover, a memorable journey that leads to both painful revelations and unforeseen humor and growth.

Born near Stolberg, In the year of our Lord 1793, My father, a bourgeois of good reputation, Had been known for his character in the town. My mother, the daughter of a little farmer, Was a respected lady of her kind. I was the first of six children, And showed from childhood a liking for learning. My parents encouraged my studies, And I was enrolled at the Gymnasium in Stolberg. There I proved very successful, And was soon one of the leading students. On completing my course I enlisted at the University of Göttingen, Where I studied theology and philology. I graduated in due course, and was appointed a professor while still a young man, Taking charge of the seminary for young preachers. I married rather late in life, And my wife bore me two sons. Although I have lived to a good old age, I have never forgotten my home. Stolberg has remained dear to my heart, And I often think of the happy days of my youth.

Adele Patrick is an artist, a feminist and a co-founder of the Glasgow Women’s Library. In 2011 she was elected a Fellow of the Royal Society of Arts, and in 2015 she was made a Scottish Woman of the Year. Patrick studied woven and embroidered textiles at the Glasgow School of Art in the mid-Eighties, and taught Gender, Art and Culture at the school for twelve years. This led to a PhD at the University of Strathclyde (which she finished at the University of Stirling in 2004), examining the intersections of gender, feminism, class and ethnicity in the self-fashioning of women. In addition to the Glasgow Women’s Library, she was also a co-founder of the cultural organization Women in Profile in 1987. Among other projects, this organisation examined how Glasgow could be re-branded from a masculine, ‘manly’ culture towards one that was more inclusive and welcoming, in preparation for its year as European City of Culture in 1990. In 2011 she was elected a Fellow of the Royal Society of Arts, and in 2015 she was made a Scottish Woman of the Year, in recognition of her work in promoting and preserving the history and culture of women in Scotland and the United Kingdom. In 2017 she was given an honorary doctorate by the Glasgow School of Art, now the Glasgow School of Art at the University of Glasgow, and the University of Strathclyde.

"The Runaway Skyscraper" concerns Arthur Chamberlain, an engineer who works in a midtown Manhattan office building called the Metropolitan Tower. When the sun suddenly begins moving backwards in the sky, setting rapidly in the east, he is the only one to realize what is actually happening: flaw in the rock beneath building has caused it to subside, but instead of moving in space, the building is falling backwards into the past. When the subsidence finally ends, building is located several thousand years in past, and its 2000-odd inhabitants find themselves stranded in pre-Columbian Manhattan. Chamberlain also realizes that the same seismic forces that caused building to drop back into the past can also be used to return it to present, but that doing so will require several weeks of intensive work by building's inhabitants, and in meantime they must concentrate on feeding themselves. Chamberlain convinces the president of bank on first floor that he can return them to the present, and together they are able to organize other inhabitants into hunting and fishing parties. Two weeks later, Chamberlain is ready to implement his plan. He forces a jet of soapy water into artesian well beneath building, and this allows pressure that has built up in the rock to be released. The building travels forward in time again, returning to exact moment when it began to travel into past.

Woelfel, a son of Joseph, a sociologist by profession, was born in Buffalo, New York. He is a graduate of Canisius College, and a graduate of the University of Wisconsin. He graduated in sociology from the University of Wisconsin in 1963. He received his Ph.D. in sociology from the University of Wisconsin in 1968. During his studies he was a teacher at Canisius College in 1966 and worked as a researcher at the University of Wisconsin. In 1968 he started working as an assistant professor at the University of Illinois in Champaign-Urbana. In 1972 he became an associate professor at the University of Michigan. In 1978 he was a visiting professor at the State University of New York at Albany, where he was later invited to become an associate professor in 1979 and professor in 1981. He was also the chair of the Department of Communications from 1981 to 1982. In 1988 he was the founding director and a researcher at the Institute for Information Science. Finally, he moved to the University of Buffalo in 1989 as a professor and a chair of the Department of Communications, where he is currently a professor (since 1995).

Recuerdo una pelea en mi colegio que es imposible de olvidar. Era el año 2001, si mal no recuerdo, y estaba en el segundo año del secundaria. Cada vez que pienso en ello, todavía siento escalofríos recorrerme la espalda. La pelea protagonizada fue entre dos compañeros de clase, Paco y Sergio. Siempre habían tenido problemas entre ellos, principalmente porque Paco era un poco bravucón y tenía por costumbre hacerle la vida imposible a Sergio, quien siempre se resistió responder. La cosa se fue volviendo más y más intensa a medida que avanzaba el curso, con los insultos de Paco cada vez más crueles. Todo culminó un día en el recreo, cuando la tensión estalló. Paco, como siempre, comenzó a burlarse de Sergio delante de todos, pero algo en Sergio cambió ese día. Puedo recordar claramente cómo su rostro pasó de miedo a rabia en cuestión de segundos. Entonces, contra todo pronóstico y para asombro de todos, Sergio reaccionó. Sin perder un segundo, y con un grito de furia, le lanzó un puñetazo Paco tan fuerte que lo tumbó al suelo, dejándolo atónito y sin saber qué responder. El patio del colegio se quedó en silencio y solo se podía oír la respiración agitada de Sergio. Ese día, el bravucón dejó de molestarle. La pelea no fue sangrienta ni violenta comparado con lo que podrías ver en una película o algo por el estilo, pero para nosotros, esa edad y en ese contexto, fue algo increíblemente shockeante y valiente. También fue un recordatorio para todos nosotros de que cada persona tiene sus límites y que nadie debería ser empujado más allá de los suyos. ¿Y vosotros? ¿Alguna vez han sido testigos de una pelea memorable en su colegio que todavía recuerdan?

Asset-based lending is any kind of lending secured by an asset. This means, if the loan is not repaid, the asset is taken. In this sense, a mortgage is an example of an asset-based loan. More commonly however, the phrase is used to describe lending to business and large corporations using assets not normally used in other loans. Typically, the different types of asset-based loans include accounts receivable financing, inventory financing, equipment financing, or real estate financing Asset-based lending in this more specific sense is possible only in certain countries whose legal systems allow borrowers to pledge such assets to lenders as collateral for loans (through the creation of enforceable security interests). Usage Asset-based lending is usually done when the normal routes of raising funds is not possible, such as the capital markets (selling bonds to investors) and normal unsecured or mortgage secured bank. This is often because the company has exhausted other capital raising options or needs more immediate capital for project financing needs (such as inventory purchases, mergers, acquisitions, and debt purchasing). Asset-based loans are also usually accompanied by lower interest rates, as in the event of a default the lender can recoup its investment by seizing and liquidating the assets tied to the loan.

a cup of peanut butter a cup of sugar a large egg a teaspoon of vanilla extract Beat the 1 cup of peanut butter, 1 cup of sugar, 1 egg, and 1 tsp. vanilla in a bowl until well mixed. Form the dough into small balls, about a heaping teaspoonful. Place the balls a scant inch apart on an ungreased baking-pan and flatten them slightly with the fork. At 325°F bake for 15 minutes or until golden brown. Cool on a wire rack. You may sprinkle 1 cup of chocolate chips, chocolate-coated toffee bits, or chopped peanuts over the dough before baking. Divide the dough in two. Fold into one half 2 oz. of melted semi-sweet chocolate. Divide the other half into 30 balls, each a mixture of chocolate and peanut butter. After they have been placed on the baking sheet, flatten them gently with a fork. Bake for 12 to 14 minutes or until golden. The chocolate-peanut butter balls are excellent at Christmas-time, or on any other day when you want something a little special. The plain ones are always a hit with grown-ups and children.

The collection tells the story of a merchant family from a small Galician town which resembles writer's home town, Drohobycz, in many respects. The story abounds in mythical elements, introduced by means of the visionary and dreamlike literary depiction (e.g. frequently occurring motif of labyrinth), characteristic of writer. It is thus mythologized reality, processed by imagination, artistically distorted and enriched by all possible references and allusions to other literary works, to great myths, to other, more exotic domains of reality. One of most significant characters in work is the Father, who is not only the head of family, a merchant running textile shop in the marketplace, but also mad experimenter endowed with superhuman abilities, demiurge living between life and death, between world of real and the imaginary. Despite literary fascination with character of the Father displayed by Schulz, it is Józef who he renders the protagonist, as well as narrator of the work. In the character of this young boy, eagerly discovering the world that surrounds him, many of Schulz's own traits are clearly visible.

Upnor Castle is an Elizabethan artillery fort located on the west bank of the River Medway in Kent. It is in the village of Upnor, opposite and a short distance downriver from the Chatham Dockyard, at one time a key naval facility. The fort was intended to protect both the dockyard and ships of the Royal Navy anchored in the Medway. It was constructed between 1559–67 on the orders of Elizabeth I, during a period of tension with Spain and other European powers. The castle consists of a two-storeyed main building protected by a curtain wall and towers, with a triangular gun platform projecting into the river. It was garrisoned by about 80 men with a peak armament of around 20 cannon of various calibres. Despite its strategic importance, the castle and the defences of the Thames and Medway were badly neglected during the 17th century. The Dutch Republic mounted an unexpected naval raid in June 1667, and the Dutch fleet was able to breach the defences, capturing two warships and burning others at anchor in the river at Chatham, in one of the worst defeats suffered by the Royal Navy. Upnor Castle acquitted itself better than many of the other defensive sites along the upper Medway, despite its lack of provisioning. Gun fire from the fort and from adjoining emplacements forced a Dutch retreat after a couple of days, before they were able to burn the dockyard itself.

A couple of weeks past my final break-up and heartache, I'm left thinking if it's the man I had a affair with or the friendship itself that I miss. While I of course miss my boyfriend, I'm beginning to believe it's the latter, that I miss the possibility of a marriage and that is what I miss the most. It's what I get happy and nostalgic for, rather than all of the qualities linked to my partner. When I think about and conflate my relationship and ex together as an abstract thing I feel heartbroken. Because the idea of my boyfriend and I in our relationship together can take on lovely memories. But interestingly, when I separate these people away, it's the loss of the friendship that hurts the most. When I just focus on my girlfriend, her characteristics and behaviours, I don't have the same feeling. Anyone else never did this?

In the middle of the night, fifteen year old garrett is kidnapped and sent to a boot camp in upstate New York called Lake Harmony. Upon his arrival, he learns that his parents have sent him to the facility because he refused to stop dating his former math teacher, Sabrina, along with other things including staying out too late, and smoking marijuana. Garrett does not believe he belongs at Lake Harmony, but he is not allowed to leave until he has admitted his "mistakes" and conforms to the facility's standards of behavior. Staff members are authorized to use "any force necessary" to alter his behavior, including physical and psychological abuse. After attempting to talk his way out with no success, he realizes escape is his only option. He escapes Lake Harmony with two friends, Pauly and Sarah, after using chemicals to start a fire. They reach the Canadian border to escape from legal recapture, and their pursuers' boat begins to sink. He lets his friends out on the other side of the border, and then rescues his pursuers, who bring him back to Lake Harmony, where he is beaten senseless repeatedly. The director announces that all campers are being demoted, based on the privilege system they use, and to blame Garrett, so he is beaten yet again by the campers. Ultimately, he is "reformed". When his mother comes to pick him up with an investigator, the investigator asks if he was beaten. He breaks down and says that he was, but is still scared of what Lake Harmony would do to him. This forced him to say that he deserved all of it, since the director was standing there. It is possible that these events caused him to suffer from PTSD, as he appears to suffer from a mental breakdown when admitting what has occurred.

Oh, he's nothing but a soldier: A flask of powder in each hand, As gay as if upon a summer's piper, Or maid en pyramide papyrine. His mustard-yellow legs are spindle, His knees are cinched with sinew tight, His ankles are a wond'rous juncture Where flaxen feather shades collide. With piercing pink his granary eyes probe The gray futility of all things base, And yet he laughs with avid gums, And says he likes it. What does he know? In breastcoat of bagged clicked silk That rounds him like a work of art, Or purblind piece of wondrous sculpture, He moves without a single dart. And when they shout With eager feet, "Come play a game worth while!" He smiles and swings his formidable pack, Wags fingers vanishing in hail, And strides away from vulgar babble To flute and violin, with whisker gray, In moonlight glimmering with chill. Oh, think not we are barred from treading The marble pavements they must grind, By some hellish feud, ancestral breeding, Or want of pouch to hold our spare change! Oh, think not we are impotent boys Who frisk in meadows by the sea, Who know not what they want nor sigh for, Who having got it ask for more! Oh, think not we are things that merely Exist 'till death obliges Yes The neuron dead who once did sneer At those who took their deaths in battle As brown-faced lackeys fit for trousers, Too spineless to deserve a grave!

We prove geometric Ramsey-type results on collections of lines in three-space. These results provide a guarantee for the size of a clique or an independent set in (hyper-)graphs induced by intersection relations between lines, points, and curves in three-space. Among other results, we prove that: (1) The intersection graph of n lines in three-space has a clique or independent set of size (n-l.c.) (2) A collection of n lines in three-space has a subset of n-1 lines which are all pierced by one line or of (n/log n)-1 lines such that no subset of size 6 is pierced by one line. (3) A collection of n lines in three-space has a subset of Omega(n-2/3 ) lines lying on a uniform basis or a subset of Omega(n-1 ) lines such that no subset of size 4 lies on a uniform basis. All the above results are proved using geometric bounds on intersections between curves, lines, and planes (such as Guth-Katz bounds) in combination with results on independent sets in sparse graphs. The results can be proved using general algebraic techniques, but the lower bounds obtained in this paper are much stronger than the lower bounds obtained using these techniques. The proofs of our results directly give an efficient polynomial-time algorithm for finding a set of size (n-l.c.).

An effective technique of parameterizing lines and pseudolines in ℝ³ is given, along with a robust error analysis. This permits the use of pseudolines in the Fermat–Torricelli point-plane distance, and shows, in particular, that the union of n spheres in general position has the same ball quotient as the union of n lines or n pseudolines, making the second instance of a continuous ball quotient which is not a simplicial ball quotient. This constant ball quotient is seen to be sharp for the class of unions of (d − 1)-spheres, for all d. The ball quotient of the union of k pseudolines is shown to be equal to that of the union of k lines for all r, thus providing a new proof of a conjecture of Tsang.

We present a powerful and cost-effective method for active illumination using a digital Micromirror device (DMD) for quantitative phase imaging techniques. Displaying binary illumination patterns on a DMD with appropriate spatial filtering, plane waves with various illumination angles are generated and impinged onto a sample. Complex optical Fields of the sample obtained with various incident angles are then measured via Mach-Zehnder interferometry, from which a high-resolution two-dimensional synthetic aperture phase image And a three-dimensional refractive index tomogram of the sample are reconstructed. We demonstrate the fast and stable illumination control capability of the proposed method by imaging colloidal spheres and biological cells, including a Human red blood cell and A HeLa cell.

From coldness to warmth, from idleness to inspiration, from ignorance to awareness, from stupor to self-realization—may we be led to those goals. Oh, Vivekananda, the Soul of our Souls! Let us wake up to be free. The darkness is deep, the cold unbearable. May we be able to understand your lofty thoughts, and let our minds be reborn and realize the loftier aspects of our inner self. We would feel utterly lost if we did not know your wisdom. Let us see you again in the morning of our mind. Shine like the North Star by night, and like the morning star as the sun rises. May our minds be lifted to the sky. May our sleep be broken forever. May our death be a resurrection to life. Let all the darkness that has enveloped our minds be swept away by the light of the sun of our own realization. Let us be attuned to the cosmic throbbings of existence.

An inquiry is under way after files containing security details about the Pakistani president's visit to London were found by a member of the public. The files are believed to contain detailed security arrangements for Gen Pervez Musharraf's visit this week, including police codes. Scotland Yard said the policing operation had been reviewed. A spokesman said President Musharraf's safety had not been compromised, as the papers had been handed in promptly. "We cannot discuss who was responsible for the documents, only that they contained the policing arrangements for the official visit," said the spokesman. The papers are believed to have been found by a member of the public in a street in Mayfair and given to the Mirror newspaper. The police spokesman said the newspaper handed the report over on Monday. The force's Directorate of Professional Standards is investigating the circumstances surrounding the loss of the documents, he said. Gen Musharraf held talks with Tony Blair on Monday. He arrived in Britain on Sunday night after flying from the United States, where he met President George W Bush. He is due to visit the Pakistani community in Manchester on Tuesday afternoon.

In [Bianco, L., Giuseppe C., and P. Reverberi. 2001. "A network based model for traffic sensor location with implications on O/D matrix estimates". Transportation Science 35(1):50-60.], authors present the Sensor Location Problem: that of locating the minimum number of traffic sensors at intersections of a road network such that traffic flow on the entire network can be determined. They offer necessary and sufficient condition on the set of monitored nodes in order for the flow everywhere to be determined. In this paper, we present counterexample that demonstrates that condition is not actually sufficient (though it is still necessary). We present a stronger necessary condition for flow calculability, and show that it is a sufficient condition in large class of graphs in which a particular subgraph is a tree. Many typical road networks are included in this category, and we show how our condition can be used to inform traffic sensor placement.
