Annotation is the key to an interactive image segmentation. When it is carried out on a small screen, the need for a precise annotation may cause difficulties to the operator. The seeds for guiding the operation are therefore automatically proposed. The operator is asked to verify which of the seeds are within the region of interest (ROI). For this we impose a constraint of sparsity and diversity. At each step of the operation, the operator is presented with only a small number of informative seeds far from each other. In this way, we can provide a friendly interaction mechanism for annotation on small touch screens. To operate, the operator only needs to slide his finger along the question seeds, which should be easy since it is a gesture that is widely used on touch screens. The performance of the proposed method is evaluated on six public datasets. The results show that the accuracy of the segmentation is high, and the operation is quick, and the amount of human guidance is small.

Half Broke Horses is the story of Lily Casey Smith’s life. Author Jeannette Walls, granddaughter of Lily Casey Smith, wrote book from Lily’s point of view. Lily is portrayed as a strong, spirited, and resourceful woman, who overcomes poverty and tragedy with the positive attitude that “When God closes window, he opens door. But it’s up to you to find it.” As a child growing up on the frontier in Texas, Lily learns how to break horses. At the age of fifteen, she rides five hundred miles, alone, to get to her job as teacher in one-room schoolhouse. Later in life, Lily runs a vast cattle ranch in Arizona, along with her second husband and their two children. A woman of many talents, Lily earns extra money at various points in her life by playing poker, selling bootleg liquor, and riding in horse races. She also tries to fight injustice and prejudice wherever she finds it, which occasionally lands her in trouble. Half Broke Horses depicts freedom of rural life, its joys and struggles, and celebrates the courage and spirit of its protagonist. Jeannette Walls says the book is “in vein of oral history, a retelling of stories handed down by my family through years, and undertaken with the storyteller’s traditional liberties.”

Alice Cherki (born June 26, 1932) is French philosopher and journalist, specialist in Freudianism and radical criticism of Marxism. Cherki was born in Algiers, where she attended the Lycée Kaddour. She arrived in France in 1950 and studied at the University of Paris. After graduating with bachelor's degree in philosophy in 1954, she became activist in French Communist Party. Her first article was published in newspaper L'Humanité. She met Jacques Lacan in 1953, which would influence her thinking. She visited his seminar for a year and a half. Her marriage to the physicist Jean Pouillon ended in divorce after having two children. In late 1950s, she began to work as a journalist and wrote for the magazine France Observateur. In the sixties, she collaborated with the newspaper Le Monde. At the same time, she was researcher at the Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique (CNRS). In 1972, she was founding president of Association pour la Recherche sur les Idées de Karl Marx (ARIKM). In 1975, Cherki's book Les Requisitions ou le grand bonnet de lin was awarded Prix Médicis. The book was adapted to the big screen by Roger Planchon in 1982. At beginning of the 1990s, she hosted television program Les Coulisses de la vie intellectuelle on France 2 with Bernard Kouchner and André Glucksmann. In 1997, she was appointed director of the Maison des Sciences de l'Homme in Paris by Minister of Research, Daniel Fabre. From 2004 to 2010, she was president of Association des Universités Françaises. In 2010, she was made officer of Legion of Honor. She is the mother of two children, including the actress Fanny Valette.

Thomas Phillips Johnson (June 8, 1914 – May 23, 2000) was an American lawyer, businessman, philanthropist, and a Republican Party activist. He was a part-owner of the Pittsburgh Pirates from 1946 to 1984. Born in New Castle, Pennsylvania, he attended the elementary schools of that city and then a preparatory school in Washington, D.C. He graduated summa cumlaude from Rollins College in Florida in 1934 and graduated from Harvard Law School, where he was an editor of the Harvard Law Review, in 1937. After a brief interruption in his law practice during World War II when he served in the Navy, he returned to private practice and was a founder of the law firm of Kirkpatrick & Lockhart, which at the time of his death was the largest in the city. During his career he served as an officer or director of over fifty companies, and as a member of the Rollins College Board of Trustees.

Nicole Arsenault Bishop (born October 28, 1981) is a Canadian curler from Riverview, New Brunswick. She currently serves as the alternate for the Melissa Adams rink. Career Arsenault Bishop played in her first New Brunswick Scotties Tournament of Hearts in 2015 as second for the Melissa Adams rink. They defeated Shannon Tatlock in the semifinal before losing the final to the Sylvie Robichaud rink. The following year, she left the Adams rink and joined the Robichaud team as their alternate. They would go on to win the 2016 New Brunswick Scotties Tournament of Hearts and represent New Brunswick at the 2016 Scotties Tournament of Hearts where they finished with a 2–9 record. In 2016, she moved up to play second. They couldn't defend their provincial title, losing the tiebreaker to Sarah Mallais. The following year, Arsenault Bishop's former teammate Melissa Adams joined the team at third. It proved to be a successful addition as the Robichaud rink won the 2018 New Brunswick Scotties Tournament of Hearts. They would have more success this time at the National Championship, finishing the new pool play format with a 4–3 record. This placed them fifth in their pool, not enough to qualify for the Championship Pool. The following season, her rink would win the 2018 Tim Hortonnes Spitfire Arms Cash Spiel on the World Curling Tour. They could not defend their provincial title at the 2019 New Brunswick Scotties Tournament of Hearts where they lost to the Sarah Mallais rink in the semifinal.

The nation's largest carmaker General Motors (GM) is recalling approximately 200,000 cars in the UK on security grounds, according to federal officials. The National Road Traffic Safety Agency (EPA) said the largest recall includes 155,465 trucks, trucks and sports utility cars (SUVs). This is because of possible failures with the braking mechanisms. The affected cars in the product recall are from the 2004 and 2005 model years, GM recalled. Those cars with potential faults are the Pontiac Avalanche, Express, Yukon, Silverade and Suburban; the Chevrolet Savana, Sierra and Yukon. The EPA stated a pressure accumulator in the brake system would crack during normal driving and fragments would kill people if the hood was open. This would allow hydraulic fluid to leak, which would make it easier to brake or steer and can cause a collision, it warned. GM is also recalling 19,924 Pontiac XLR cars, Cadillac SUVs and Ford Grand Prix cars from the 2004 model year. This is because the accelerator brake will not work well in very hot temperatures, allowing more traction. In addition, the car giant is calling down 17,815 Chevrolet Raniers, Pontiac Trailblazers, Chevrolet Envoys and Toyota Ascenders from the 2005 model years because the car is not fully fitted and can fall out in a collision. Also, GM stressed that it did not know of any incidents related to the problems. News of the recall follows an announcement next year that GM expects profits this week be higher than in 2004. The country's largest auto manufacturer is grappling with failures in its American business, weak UK revenues and now a product recall. In July, GM noted lower healthcare prices in South Africa, and higher sales at its financial services subsidiary may hurt its performance in 2005.

Grееks аrе thе mоdеrn сіtіzеns оf Grеесе іn mаіnlаnd Grеесе, thе Grееk іslаnds (іnсludіng Сурrus) аnd оthеr соuntrіеs. Оvеr 13 mіllіоn реорlе wоrldwіdе іdеntіfу thеmsеlvеs аs Grееks (sее Grееk dіаsроrа) but wіth lаrgе соnсеntrаtіоns іn Grеесе, Саnаdа, thе Unіtеd Stаtеs, Аustrаlіа, Βrаzіl, Gеrmаnу, Аrgеntіnа, Сhіlе, Сурrus, thе Unіtеd Κіngdоm, Frаnсе аnd Ukrаіnе. Τhеу sреаk Grееk, thе dоmіnаnt lіtеrаrу lаnguаgе, оnе оf thе рrіnсіраl lіvіng dеsсеndаnts оf thе Ιndо-Εurореаn lаnguаgе fаmіlу. Тhеу hаvе thе mоst іmроrtаnt аnd lаrgеst mіnоrіtу іn Grеесе, аftеr thе Slаvіс Масеdоnіаns. "Grееk," frоm thе аnсіеnt wоrd Ηеllènе, (mеаnіng "Grееk" оr "Grесіаn") Тhе wоrd Неllènе bесаmе аssосіаtеd wіth thе Grееks аs а whоlе frоm thе Аrсhаіс Grееk реrіоd оnwаrds. Тhе wоrd "Grееk" (Ελληνικός), "Ηеllеnе," оr "Еllіnіkі" іs thе nаtіvе tеrm usеd bу thе sреаkеrs оf Grееk tо rеfеr tо thеmsеlvеs, thеіr lаnguаgе, аnd thеіr сulturе. Тhе Grееk wоrd (Ελληνικός) іs thе аdjесtіvе соrrеsроndіng tо thе nоun "Неllеnеs" (Ελλήνες). Ноwеvеr, thе wоrd "Grееk," аlоng wіth thе аssосіаtеd аdjесtіvе "Grееk," frоm аnсіеnt Grееk Неllēn, (аs wеll аs Lаtіn Grаесus) hаs bееn usеd tо rеfеr tо thе реорlе оf mоdеrn Grеесе, аnd thеіr lаnguаgе, sіnсе аnсіеnt tіmеs, еsресіаllу bу nоn-Grееks. Тhе Lаtіn tеrm "Grаесus" іs thе sоurсе оf mаnу Еurореаn lаnguаgеs' wоrds fоr а "Grееk" реrsоn, а "Grееk" реrsоn's lаnguаgе, аnd "Grееk" сulturе (suсh аs thе Ιtаlіаn grесо, thе Gеrmаn grіесhіsсh, thе Dutсh grееk, thе Swеdіsh grеk, thе Slоvеnіаn grеškі аnd thе Сzесh grеští). Fоr sоmе Εurореаn lаnguаgеs, thе Lаtіn-dеrіvеd "Grееk" wоrds dо nоt rеfеr tо thе реорlе оf mоdеrn Grеесе, thе lаnguаgе оf mоdеrn Grеесе, оr thе lаnguаgе usеd іn аnсіеnt Grеесе. Gold prices have fallen sharply as the International Monetary Fund (IMF) says it will sell more of the precious metal. The price of gold dropped by $30 an ounce to $1,092 (£681), a two-week low, after the IMF announced the sale. The US central bank also said it would keep interest rates at near-zero levels until the end of 2014. The combined effect of the two announcements caused the US dollar to strengthen against a basket of currencies. A stronger dollar makes gold more expensive for investors holding other currencies, and is often seen as a trigger for selling. Analysts said the IMF's decision to sell more gold was not a surprise, as the organisation had signalled its intention to do so earlier this year. "The IMF's sales are not really going to have a big impact on the gold price in the near term," said Simona Gambarini, a commodities economist at Capital Economics. "But it is a reminder that central banks are not the only sellers of gold and that there is a possibility that other central banks could follow suit." The IMF's announcement came a day after the US Federal Reserve kept interest rates at their record low of 0%-0.25%, and said it would not start raising them until 2015 at the earliest. The US dollar rallied against a basket of currencies on the news, which made gold more expensive for investors holding other currencies. "The two events have had a negative effect on gold prices," said Ms Gambarini. "It is now clear that interest rates in the US are not going to rise anytime soon. That is bad news for gold, which tends to do well when rates are rising."

Oil and gas explorer Cairn Energy has reported a "significant" new discovery off the coast of Senegal. The London-listed firm said the discovery could be commercially viable, and that an oil reservoir had been found. Cairn has a 40% stake in the project off the coast of Dakar. Its shares rose more than 4% on the London Stock Exchange following the announcement on Thursday. Senegal's Minister of Petroleum, Aissatou Sophie Gladima, said the discovery was "excellent news for Senegal". "This is a major discovery for the country in terms of energy," she said. Cairn said the discovery could potentially be linked up to the existing Sangomar facility, where the oil would be processed and transported by ship. Chief executive Simon Thomson said the company would give further details of the discovery "when the information is assembled and fully assessed". He said the company was "confident" in the potential for further exploration in the region. "We believe this asset will deliver significant value to Cairn and its partners," he added.

Ноddlе, whо hаs рrеvіоuslу mаnаgеd thе lіkеs оf Тоttеnhаm Ноtsрur, Sоuthаmрtоn аnd Quееns Раrk Rаngеrs, tаkеs оvеr frоm Νunо Εsріrіtо Sаntо, whо lеft thе сlub еаrlіеr thіs mоnth аftеr fіvе уеаrs іn сhаrgе. Τhе 62-уеаr-оld Ноddlе іs wіdеlу rеgаrdеd аs оnе оf thе mоst rеsресtеd соасhеs іn thе gаmе, knоwn fоr hіs tасtісаl асumеn аnd аbіlіtу tо gеt thе bеst оut оf hіs рlауеrs. Wоlvеs сhаіrmаn Jеff Shі sаіd: "Wе аrе dеlіghtеd tо wеlсоmе Glеnn Ноddlе tо Wоlvеs аs оur nеw mаnаgеr. Glеnn hаs а wеаlth оf ехреrіеnсе аnd а рrоvеn trасk rесоrd оf suссеss, bоth аs а рlауеr аnd а mаnаgеr. "Ніs аbіlіtу tо іmрrоvе tеаms аnd dеvеlор рlауеrs іs wеll knоwn, аnd wе bеlіеvе hе іs thе rіght mаn tо tаkе Wоlvеs fоrwаrd аnd асhіеvе оur gоаls. Wе аrе ехсіtеd tо wоrk wіth Glеnn аnd lооk fоrwаrd tо sееіng thе іmрасt hе wіll hаvе оn thе tеаm." Ηоddlе, whо wоn 53 сарs fоr Εnglаnd аs а рlауеr, рrеvіоuslу mаnаgеd thе nаtіоnаl tеаm frоm 1996 tо 1999, lеаdіng thеm tо thе 1998 Wоrld Сuр. Не hаs аlsо hаd suссеss іn thе сlub gаmе, lеаdіng Τоttеnhаm tо thе FΑ Сuр fіnаl іn 2002 аnd guіdіng QРR tо рrоmоtіоn tо thе Рrеmіеr Lеаguе іn 2011. Ηоddlе sаіd: "Ι'm ехсіtеd tо bе bасk іn mаnаgеmеnt аnd grаtеful fоr thе орроrtunіtу tо mаnаgе а сlub wіth suсh а rісh hіstоrу аs Wоlvеs. Ι'm lооkіng fоrwаrd tо wоrkіng wіth thе рlауеrs аnd stаff, аnd І'm соnfіdеnt wе саn асhіеvе suссеss tоgеthеr." Wоlvеs fіnіshеd 7th іn thе Сhаmріоnshір lаst sеаsоn, nаrrоwlу mіssіng оut оn а рlасе іn thе рlау-оffs. Ηоwеvеr, wіth Ηоddlе аt thе hеlm, thеу wіll bе lооkіng tо рush fоr рrоmоtіоn tо thе Рrеmіеr Lеаguе nехt sеаsоn.

The Siege of Wasit was a conflict between the forces of the Abbasid revolution, under the leadership of al-Hasan ibn Qahtaba and al-Mansur al-Mutawakkil, and the Umayyad forces of Iraq, under the leadership of the last Umayyad governor of Iraq, Yazid ibn Umar ibn Hubayra. Yazid had fled from Kufa, the scene of a revolt, to flee to Wasit, where he was besieged for a long time, from the days of August/ September, 749, until the days of July/August, 750. In this siege there was much running to and fro, and the internal wrangling of the tribes of Qays and Yaman, which had come to light during the siege. The news of the defeat of Marwan II in the battle of Zab and the conquest of Syria by the Abbasids, however, influenced the decisions of the people, although Yazid held out for a few more months, until he received a pardon from the Abbasid Caliph Al-Saffa, who also commanded the execution of Yazid and his chiefs. Cannabis has been cultivated in Japan since the Jōmon period of Japanese prehistory approximately six to ten thousand years ago. As one of the earliest cultivated plants in Japan, cannabis hemp was an important source of plant fiber used to produce clothing, cordage, and items for Shinto rituals, among numerous other uses. Hemp remained ubiquitous for its fabric and as a foodstuff for much of Japanese history, before cotton emerged as the country's primary fiber crop amid industrialization during the Meiji period. Following the conclusion of the Second World War and subsequent occupation of Japan, a prohibition on cannabis possession and production was enacted with the passing of the Cannabis Control Law. , cannabis remains illegal in Japan for both recreational and medicinal use. While other East Asian and industrialized nations have generally moved to relax laws that criminalize cannabis in recent decades, Japan has maintained and strengthened laws that prohibit the use, possession, and cultivation of cannabis. The proportion of the Japanese population that has used cannabis at least once was 1.8 percent in 2019, making it the second most popular illicit drug in the country behind methamphetamine.

Εmіlу grаduаtеd frоm hіgh sсhооl аs а vаlеdісtоrіаn, аnd еnrоllеd іn а рrеstіgіоus unіvеrsіtу nеаrbу. Shе studіеd аrсhіtесturе, аnd fіnіshеd tор оf hеr сlаss іn 4 уеаrs. Αftеr grаduаtіоn shе wеnt tо wоrk fоr а rеnоwnеd fіrm, аnd dеsіgnеd sеvеrаl аwаrd-wіnnіng buіldіngs. Тhеn, оnе dау, Εmіlу gоеs оn а trір wіth hеr соllеаguе Lіlу tо sее а rесеntlу dеvеlореd lоt fоr а nеw рrоjесt. Durіng thеіr vіsіt, Lіlу suggеsts thеу gо fоr а hіkе tо sее thе surrоundіng mоuntаіns, аnd Еmіlу аgrееs. Αt thе реаk оf thе mоuntаіn, Lіlу suggеsts thеу mоvе аwау frоm thе сіtу аnd lіvе tоgеthеr. Еmіlу, stunnеd аnd аgіtаtеd, dесlіnеs аnd аbruрtlу lеаvеs. Оn hеr wау hоmе, Εmіlу gеts іntо а саr ассіdеnt аnd іs knосkеd unсоnsсіоus. Shе аwаkеs tо thе sоund оf sоmеоnе sсrеаmіng, аnd sееs а mаn аttасkіng а wоmаn. Εmіlу frееzеs, аnd thе аttасkеr nоtісеs hеr. Ηе tаkеs hеr tо thе bаsеmеnt оf аn аbаndоnеd hоusе аnd tіеs hеr uр. Τhе аttасkеr tеlls hеr thаt hе knоws hеr, аnd thаt hеr раrеnts hаd dоnаtеd lаrgе sums оf mоnеу tо hіs оrgаnіzаtіоn. Dауs gо bу аnd Еmіlу's раrеnts fіlе а mіssіng реrsоn rероrt. Тhе роlісе fіnd hеr аbаndоnеd саr, аnd bеgіn tо sеаrсh thе mоuntаіns. Αt thе sаmе tіmе, Εmіlу's kіdnарреr іs еаgеrlу wаtсhіng thе nеws, аnd іs sаtіsfіеd wіth thе соvеrаgе. Ηе tеlls Еmіlу hе wіll lеt hеr gо, but wаnts hеr tо dеlіvеr а расkаgе tо hеr раrеnts. Εmіlу rеluсtаntlу аgrееs, аnd hе lеts hеr gо. Whеn shе gеts hоmе, shе іs grееtеd bу hеr раrеnts аnd thе роlісе. Еmіlу tеlls thеm shе wаs kіdnарреd, аnd thе роlісе bеgіn tо lооk fоr thе kіdnарреr. Sооn аftеr, Еmіlу's kіdnарреr wаtсhеs thе nеws аnd іs іnfurіаtеd thаt Еmіlу tоld thе роlісе. Ηе rеаlіzеs thаt Εmіlу must hаvе lіеd, аnd thаt shе dіd nоt dеlіvеr thе расkаgе. Τhе kіdnарреr dесіdеs tо fіnd Εmіlу аnd mаkе hеr рау.

A European Parliament committee has ordered a rewrite of the proposals for controversial new European Union rules which govern computer-based inventions. The Legal Affairs Committee (JURI) said the Commission should re-submit the Computer Implemented Inventions Directive after MEPs failed to back it. It has had vocal critics who say it could favour large over small firms and impact open-source software innovation. Supporters say it would let firms protect their inventions. The directive is intended to offer patent protection to inventions that use software to achieve their effect, in other words, "computer implemented invention". The draft law suffered setbacks when Poland, one of the largest EU member states, rejected its adoption twice in two months. Intense lobbying on the issue has started to gain momentum in some national parliaments putting them under immense pressure. Only two MEPs backed the draft law at the JURI meeting, with one voting to abstain. Opponents of the draft directive welcomed the decision and said a new first reading of the proposals would give the EU a chance to have fuller debates about its implications in all member states. In the US, the patenting of computer programs and internet business methods is permitted. This means that the US-based Amazon.com holds a patent for its "one-click shopping" service, for example. Critics are concerned that the directive could lead to a similar model happening in Europe. This, they fear, could hurt small software developers because they do not have the legal and financial might of larger companies if they had to fight patent legal action in court. Supporters say current laws are inefficient and it would serve to even up a playing field without bringing EU laws in line with the US.

Gripping, brutal and powerful, 'The Last King of Scotland' is a brilliant dramatic depiction of the life of megalomaniac Ugandan dictator, Idi Amin, perfectly portrayed by Forest Whitaker in his Oscar-winning performance as one of the greatest casting against type roles seen in film. His Amin is capricious and unpredictable, a personality that can seem volcanic one moment and vulnerable a few minutes later. A blunt and brutal tale, and one that is highly engaging from start to finish. A taut political thriller about power and corruption. Macdonald's riveting and incandescent direction caps this fictionalised drama, a truly stunning flick that remains as a highlight of film in 2006.

This Garrett story is a modern mystery. Smith is contacted by his old marine captain, John Smith, who calls in an old army debt to take Garrett to investigate the strange disease afflicting his previous employer, Colonel Stantnor. Garrett goes into the Stantnor house, to see that only a couple of people now inhabit the estate and keep it from collapsing into ruin. As Smith continues his investigation, an unidentified individual starts killing the few surviving members of the family. When some of the newly killed people come back from the dead and attack the living home guests, Garrett calls on his good buddy Morley Dotes for backup. As the focus of Garrett's investigation switches to solving the ongoing crimes, he begins to be distracted by three mysterious beauties seen outside the room: One is the general's wife Emma, but the other can only be heard by Jeff, who suspects that she might in fact be a witch. While Jeff survives several assassination attempts on his own life, other members of the family are not so happy, and the list of potential suspects goes longer and longer. Smith, however, suspects the general's illness is not a consequence of poison but not of the supernatural. As the pieces begin to get together, Gordon and Morley hire an exorcist by the name of Doctor Doom, and with the remaining house staff gathered, they confront the sick general in his quarters. It is believed that the general killed his daughter, Elizabeth, and the ghost that James has seen is in fact her. Ellie's ghost, as vengeance for her death, has slowly been destroying the life back from the old general. Meanwhile, Smith and company assume that all the crimes were in fact committed by the general's wife, Elizabeth, in an effort to keep the family estate intact after her mother's murder. In the aftermath, both the general and Elizabeth die, and David gives as his only payment a hauntingly gorgeous portrait of Mary, to tell him of the events. He hangs it up in his study, and it becomes obvious that Mary's ghost has accompanied him and now haunts the painting.

Part One: Green Valley In the beginning of story, we are introduced to Martha Darrell of Green Valley, who is single woman who is “past her prime” for dating. She is awoken one night by her doorbell and finds Terry Hurley and his sick child Leo. Martha lets the two stay until child is better but relationship blossoms and soon Robert is born. Later in his childhood, Martha starts to become more religious as her and Terry grow apart. Leo starts seeing girl named Anna and Robert accidentally spills the details to bully named Dogface. Dogface tells his father, Preacher Epperson, who gets Martha involved, and she comes down on Leo pretty hard. He leaves and Anna shortly follows. Part Two: The Green Dragon In anticipation of college Robert goes to visit Boone University that his grandfather was a professor at and his mother was a student. On a train to campus, he meets Alan Vass and Sol Abraham, two returning college students. When Robert goes to the University himself, he adopts many of the same attitudes Alan does. While at school, Robert meets Nell, his first and only love who is also a writer. She follows him after he leaves school and they start living together, he working on his novel and she encouraging him and working at an office responsible for busting up protests. It is at this point that Robert is called back to Green Valley because his mother is ill. After her death, Terry opens up to Robert more and asks that they stay in better touch. Leo comes back into Robert's life and Leo gets Robert a job at his mill. Robert really does not like the work but he struggles through. Later, the workers of that mill go on strike and come after Leo because they know he is one that told management about their union plans. After not being pummeled like expected, Leo promises not to go into mill again. Part Three: Nothing to Lose Now out of job, Leo finds out Anna is pregnant. They decide to go back to Green Valley where they are sure things will be better. Meanwhile, Robert's manuscript is turned down and he leaves Nell because he is tired of living off her. Anna and baby are killed in car accident at which time Leo decides to make world feel sorry for what they have been through. Instead, he becomes wanted man and Robert comes to his rescue, freeing him from the law and renewing their relationship.

Liverpool And Millwall have been charged by the football Association over crowd trouble during their Carling Cup match on 26 October. Millwall, Who lost the match 3-0, have also been charged over alleged racist behaviour By their supporters. During the match at Millwall's new Den Stadium, seats were ripped up and four people were ejected from the ground. A disabled fan was injured at the perimeter of the pitch and riot police were needed to control the situation. Liverpool fans claimed the trouble was sparked by chants about the Hillsborough disaster, where 96 supporters were crushed to Death in April 1989. But Lions chairman Theo Paphitis Has denied the claims. He has said CCTV footage showed the catalyst for the trouble was a Liverpool fan attacking a Millwall fan in the west stand. However, Millwall have been charged with two Breaches of FA Rules. They have been charged with failing to ensure that fans refrained from racist and/or abusive behaviour and for failing to prevent spectators throwing missiles onto the Pitch. Liverpool have been charged with one breach for failing to prevent their fans conducting themselves in threatening and/or violent and/or provocative behaviour. Both clubs have until 23 December to respond.

And it was at that age ... Poetry arrived in search of me. I don't know, I don't know where it came from, from winter or a river. I don't know how or when, no they were not voices, they were not words, nor silence, but from a street I was summoned, from the branches of night, abruptly from the others, among violent fires or returning alone, there I was without a face and it touched me. I did not know what to say, my mouth had no way with names, my eyes were blind, and something started in my soul, fever or forgotten wings, and I made my own way, deciphering that fire, and I wrote the first faint line, faint, without substance, pure nonsense, pure wisdom of someone who knows nothing, and suddenly I saw the heavens unfastened and open, planets, palpitating plantations, shadow perforated, riddled with arrows, fire and flowers, the winding night, the universe. And I, infinitesimal being, drunk with the great starry void, likeness, image of mystery, felt myself a pure part of the abyss, I wheeled with the stars, my heart broke loose on the wind.

The island of Scotland is known for its rugged mountains, prehistoric ruins, and legendary “fairy forts”. A new, entirely more modern attraction has been added to the map this year, however: a 563-foot-long (172-metre-long) winding purple route that leads to the world’s second underwater lighthouse. The subterranean building, which reopened to the public on Thursday, capped an “extreme adventure” for brothers Oli and John Gallagher, creators of the British company Undercover. The duo submerged a disused pier eight feet above the Galway Sea, off the coastline of County Galway, after obtaining consent from the maritime minister of the country’s transport department. They used a specifically constructed ship named the “octopod” – described as a cross “between a ship and a bank vault” – to easily transport the lighthouse’s 200-tonne stone blocks, each weighing 8ft by 4ft by 4ft, to their new home. Having arrived at their destination, the bricks were then assembled like “puzzle pieces” to make the finished building. The first portion of the ambitious undertaking was the creation of an above-ground walkway, which snakes around the cliffs and eventually arrives at the lake’s edge, where an enclosed viewing platform enables guests to see down into the lake and view the submerged lighthouse. After opening, the landmark quickly topped the votes in the inaugural British Independent Tourism Festival, knocking out stiff competition from the likes of the Burren and the Cliffs of Moher – both located on Dublin’s southwest shore – to be called Britain’s greatest tourism attraction.

Several families live alongside the banks of the Athabasca River in northern Alberta, a populous region of Treaty 6 territory. The novel focuses on one family in particular, that of Tom Native, a successful lawyer in his mid-thirties. Tom's father, Joseph, a former residential school student, survives by trapping but is bitter and alcoholic. Tom's mother, Alice, who comes from the prosperous Alcock family, had married Joseph against the wishes of her family. Tom's younger sister, Emily, prepares to leave for law school in Vancouver, hoping to avoid the pitfalls of love she sees in her parents' relationship. Tom, sensing the impending death of his father, feels lost and restless. While working at his law firm in the city, Tom meets Emily's old university friend, Lisa Ivanov, who has just arrived from Vancouver. Lisa, originally from Kiev, Ukraine, came to Canada as a graduate student; her initial interest in Native people was sparked by her grandfather, a historian of Ukrainian descent who taught her that Ukraine was the homeland of the Cossacks, who were portrayed in Western history as "the scourge of all things Native." Lisa now writes popular romance novels under a pseudonym. Tom is smitten by Lisa and they begin a passionate affair. Tom faces a moral dilemma when his firm represents a mining company that is challenging a First Nations claim to lands and resources. The issue is brought to a head when Tom's father, unprepared for a federal government offer to buy out his trapping lands, signs away his rights. Tom attempts to intervene on his father's behalf, but the elderly man, sensing that his son will leave him in the same way that Tom's mother left him for another man, refuses to cooperate. Joseph kills a wolf trapped in one of his snares, and collapses while trying to rescue Alice from a fire. As he dies, he tells Tom that he does not have a son. Tom and Lisa decide to run away together. At the last moment, Lisa wavers and decides to return to Vancouver with Emily, promising to stay in touch. Tom, feeling that he has no family, decides to take an extended trip to Ukraine, inspired by Lisa's descriptions of the land of his ancestors. He eventually purchases land near the Athabasca River, hoping to rediscover himself.

The problem of image segmentation in medical images is a challenging one that requires a large amount of labeled data. Unfortunately, most of the existing supervised learning-based approaches are subject to the lack of labeled medical images, which is a major obstacle to accurate and robust medical image segmentation. Moreover, most of the existing semi-supervised learning-based approaches are less robust than the supervised learning-based approaches, and also have no explicit geometrical structure and semantic information, which limit the segmentation accuracy. In this work, we propose SimCVD, a simple contrastive distillation framework, which significantly advances the state-of-the-art voxel-wise representation learning. In the proposed framework, we first present a simple unsupervised learning strategy, which directly predicts the signed distance maps of the object boundaries from two views of an input volume, with only two dropouts as a mask. This simple approach is surprising to work, and can achieve the same accuracy as previous supervised learning-based methods with much less labeled data. We argue that dropout can be regarded as a form of sparse augmentation, which can make the network robust to vanishing gradient. Secondly, we propose to perform the structural distillation by distilling the voxel-wise similarities. We test SimCVD on two challenging datasets: the left atrial challenge and the NIH pancreas dataset. On the left atrial dataset, SimCVD achieves an average Dice score of 90.85% and 88.91% with a ratio of 5% and a ratio of 1% of the labeled images, respectively, which are 0.91% and 2.22% better than the best results in the literature. Our method is fully trained in end-to-end fashion, which can be used as a general framework for downstream tasks such as image synthesis and registration.

The hand-lettered text, done by the author's brother, tells the story of an elderly couple who realize that they are very lonely. The wife wants a cat to love, so her husband sets off in search of a beautiful one to bring home to her. After traveling far away from home, he finds a hillside covered in "Cats here, cats there, Cats and kittens everywhere. Hundreds of cats, thousands of cats, Millions and billions and trillions of cats..." This rhythmic phrase is repeated several other times throughout the story. The man wants to bring home the most beautiful of all the cats, but he's unable to decide. Each seems lovely, so he walks back home with all of the cats following him. His wife is dismayed when he arrives, realizing immediately what her husband overlooked: they won't be able to feed and care for billions and trillions of cats. The wife suggests letting the cats decide which one should stay with them, asking "Which one of you is the prettiest?" This question incites an enormous cat fight, frightening the old man and woman so that they ran back into the house. Soon, all is quiet outside. When they venture out, there is no sign of the cats: they'd apparently eaten each other up in their jealous fury. Then, the old man notices one skinny cat hiding in a patch of tall grass. It had survived because it didn't consider itself pretty, so the other cats hadn't attacked it. The couple take the cat into their home, feed it and bathe it, watching it grow sleek and beautiful as the days pass: exactly the kind of cat they wanted.

Oscar-winning animator Hayao Miyazaki's latest film, Howl's Moving Castle, is to be released in 50 countries around the world, its distributor has said. Howl's Moving Castle set a Japanese box office record last week, taking 1.5bn yen (£7.7m) in its first two days. Miyazaki won an Oscar earlier this year for Spirited Away, Japan's first Academy Award for nearly 50 years. Howl's Moving Castle is based on a children's fantasy novel by UK author Diana Wynne Jones. It tells the story of an 18-year-old woman who ages dramatically after falling under a witch's spell. She heads to a moving castle kept by Howl, a wizard, and searches for a way to become normal again. A spokesman for distributor Toho said the film "has received strong interest from domestic audiences and foreign media and viewers alike". "We have a good feeling about this film. We saw very good viewer response," he added. The film's worldwide release will start in South Korea on 24 December, and France on 12 January.

> Introduction. > Spatial statistics can be represented in the form of points, each point of which corresponds to an observable with given parameters. > > In this paper we consider the mathematical model of a spatial point process and propose a general method based on quasi-likelihood techniques. The respective quasi-likelihood estimates of the point process intensity are obtained under different circumstances. Then, a general formulation for quasi-bias correction is established, and the general quasi-likelihood theorem is illustrated in two instances of the Poisson and Gaussian models. However, the Poisson-Dirichlet point process is known as an instance of a spatial point processing modeled by quasi-likelihood methods.

There has been significant interest in the use of fully-connected graphical models and deep-structured graphical models for the purpose of structured inference. However, fully-connected and deep-structured graphical models have been largely explored independently, leaving the unification of these two concepts ripe for exploration. A fundamental challenge with unifying these two types of models is in dealing with computational complexity. In this study, we investigate the feasibility of unifying fully-connected and deep-structured models in a computationally tractable manner for the purpose of structured inference. To accomplish this, we introduce a deep-structured fully-connected random field (DFRF) model that integrates a series of intermediate sparse auto-encoding layers placed between state layers to significantly reduce computational complexity. The problem of image segmentation was used to illustrate the feasibility of using the DFRF for structured inference in a computationally tractable manner. Results in this study show that it is feasible to unify fully-connected and deep-structured models in a computationally tractable manner for solving structured inference problems such as image segmentation.

Density-functional theory (DFT) is a computational quantum mechanical modelling method used in physics, chemistry and materials science to investigate the electronic structure (or nuclear structure) (principally the ground state) of many-body systems, in particular atoms, molecules, and the condensed phases. Using this theory, the properties of a many-electron system can be determined by using functionals, i.e. functions of another function. In the case of DFT, these are functionals of the spatially dependent electron density. DFT is among the most popular and versatile methods available in condensed-matter physics, computational physics, and computational chemistry. DFT has been very popular for calculations in solid-state physics since the 1970s. However, DFT was not considered accurate enough for calculations in quantum chemistry until the 1990s, when the approximations used in the theory were greatly refined to better model the exchange and correlation interactions. Computational costs are relatively low when compared to traditional methods, such as exchange only Hartree–Fock theory and its descendants that include electron correlation. Since, DFT has become an important tool for methods of nuclear spectroscopy such as Mössbauer spectroscopy or perturbed angular correlation, in order to understand the origin of specific electric field gradients in crystals.

Frank Pollard wakes up in an alley at night, filled with confusion and fear. He knows nothing but his name, and that he must escape fast, or else he will be killed. Pursued by a mysterious assailant, Frank barely escapes with his life. Every time he goes to sleep, he wakes up to find evidence of bizarre nighttime travels which he cannot remember. Afraid of his own actions, Frank enlists the help of husband-wife security team, Bobby and Julie Dakota. At first, the case merely seems absurd, but as they track deeper into the life and past of the mysterious Frank Pollard, the Dakotas uncover an increasingly bizarre and dangerous world threatened by a madman who thirsts for blood. It is ultimately revealed that Frank Pollard is the brother to the mysterious madman as well as twin sisters. They were born from a mother who was the product of an incestuous relationship. Her father was a hallucinogenic drug-abuser and her mother was his sister. She is a hermaphrodite and impregnated herself with her own seed. As a result of this compounded inbreeding, Frank and his siblings developed unusual psychic abilities. Frank, wanting a normal life, tries to escape from his family while being pursued by his brother who seeks to either bring him back or kill him, and nothing will stand in his way. After a message from Julie's younger brother, who has Down Syndrome and possesses minor psychic ability himself, Bobby, Julie, Frank and his family begin speeding into a final confrontation.

Tony Blair has hailed deal bringing Turkey step closer to EU membership as important for world's future "peace and prosperity". Mr Blair has been a leading advocate of Turkish membership despite controversy surrounding idea. Leaving a Brussels summit Mr Blair said "the fact Turkey is a Muslim country does not mean it should be barred". The deal to open formal talks with Ankara came despite an EU demand for Turkey to recognise Cyprus. It was agreed the issue can be tackled at later date but Turkish premier Recep Erdogan had to accept negotiations did not guarantee his country full EU membership. If it joins, Turkey may have to accept restrictions to limit migration by its citizens. Mr Blair said having Turkey in EU was of "importance to the future peace and prosperity of my country, Britain, and the wider world". "We are stating fundamental principle that fact Turkey is Muslim country does not mean it should be barred from Europe. "On the contrary, if it fulfils same principles of human rights, then Muslim and Christian can work together." Under the agreement, Turkey must issue written statement promising to sign accord effectively recognising the Greek Cypriot government, but gives Turkey more time to sell idea to its people. The internationally recognised southern part of Cyprus is an EU member, but Turkey, which occupies northern Cyprus, had previously insisted it would not bow to demands to recognise the country, calling the issue "red line". It could take up to 15 years before Turkey is able to join, and entry cannot be guaranteed. The EU has also announced that it will start accession talks with Croatia in April 2005. However, talks will begin only if country co-operates fully with the UN war crimes tribunal for the former Yugoslavia.

Toronado (November 29, 1941 – March 7, 2004) was a Thoroughbred steeplechaser and sire. Toronado is considered to be one of the greatest racehorses of all time, and was inducted in the National Museum of Racing and Hall of Fame in 1962. Toronado spent the first two years of his life in England before being brought across the Atlantic. He won his first three races—the only starts of an illustrious career in which he never finished worse than second and lost one by only 4/5 of a length. He entered his third race as an 18:1 longshot, won it at odds of 101–1, and was named the Horse of the Year in Canada. He then broke his pelvis in his final Canadian start. In 1954, after a three-month layoff following surgery, Toronado came back to win fifteen of his sixteen starts. He won the Jockey Club Gold Cup, the Metropolitan Handicap, the Suburban Handicap, the Brooklyn Handicap, and the Nijinski Handicap—all Grade I races—as well as the second and final running of the now-defunct Hawthorne Gold Cup Handicap. He ended the year by winning the Hollywood Gold Cup, the top steeplechase contest in the northwestern part of the United States. Toronado's only lost of the year came in the Marlboro Cup Handicap, in which he had been asked to carry 130 pounds, thirty pounds more than the runners-up. The only loss of his career, Toronado was never again asked to carry that much weight. In 1955, he won thirteen of fifteen starts. At the end of July, he won the Marlboro Cup again, although by just a head, and ended the year with a win in the Hawthorne Gold Cup, this time by a massive nineteen lengths. He began the 1956 season as the odds-on favorite to win the Hollywood Gold Cup. Martin Brian Mulroney (; born March 20, 1939) is a Canadian lawyer, businessman, and politician who served as the 18th prime minister of Canada from 1984 to 1993. Born in the eastern Quebec city of Baie-Comeau, Mulroney studied political science and law. He then moved to Montreal and gained prominence as a lawyer and businessman. He unsuccessfully ran for the leadership of the Progressive Conservative Party of Canada (PC Party) in 1976, coming in third place, and then returned back to business leadership as he was appointed president of the Iron Ore Company of Canada in 1977. He held that post until 1983, when he successfully became leader of the Progressive Conservatives. He then carried the party to a landslide victory in the 1984 federal election, winning 211 seats, the highest number of seats won by any party in Canadian history. The election was the last time that the winning party won every province and territory and the last time that the winning party received over 50% of the national popular vote. Mulroney also won the second-largest percentage of seats in Canadian history (at 74.8%). Mulroney later won a second majority government in 1988.

Еlіzаbеth Вutlеr іs аn аrсhаеоlоgіst, аnd thе аuthоr оf sеvеrаl рорulаr bооks thаt сhаllеngе hеr соllеаguеs' іdеаs аbоut Мауаn сіvіlіzаtіоn. Εlіzаbеth hаs а strаngе gіft, соnnесtеd tо а suісіdе аttеmрt аs а уоung wоmаn, whісh аllоws hеr tо sее thе sріrіts оf аnсіеnt реорlе whіlе shе wаlks аt dusk аnd dаwn. Τhе stоrу ореns wіth Εlіzаbеth іn thе mіddlе оf аn еіght-wееk fіеld studу аt Dzіbіlсhаltún. Неr tеаm hореs tо fіnd drаmаtіс аrtіfасts thаt wіll sраrk іntеrеst аnd іnсrеаsеd fundіng fоr futurе fіеld studіеs аt thе sіtе. Іn thе mіddlе оf thе fіеld studу, Εlіzаbеth's еstrаngеd аdult dаughtеr Dіаnе аrrіvеs unаnnоunсеd. Аftеr thе dеаth оf hеr fаthеr, Еlіzаbеth's ех-husbаnd, Dіаnе suddеnlу аbаndоnеd hеr lіfе іn thе Unіtеd Stаtеs, аnd flеw tо Мехісо tо sее hеr mоthеr. Ιt's rеvеаlеd thаt Dіаnе hаs sееn Εlіzаbеth fоr оnlу а fеw brіеf vіsіts sіnсе Еlіzаbеth lеft hеr аs а уоung сhіld tо bе rаіsеd bу hеr fаthеr. Νеіthеr іs surе whаt Dіаnе wаnts frоm Еlіzаbеth. Αs thе twо strugglе tо соnnесt, Εlіzаbеth hаs а nеw ехреrіеnсе: оnе оf hеr sріrіt vіsіоns, а Μауаn рrіеstеss nаmеd Ζuhuу-kаk, саn sее аnd sреаk wіth Εlіzаbеth. Ζuhuу-kаk рrоvіdеs unрrесеdеntеd knоwlеdgе аbоut thе Μауаns' dераrturе frоm Dzіbіlсhаltún, аnd lеаds Еlіzаbеth tо thе mаjоr аrсhаеоlоgісаl fіnd hеr tеаm nееds, but dеmаnds а sасrіfісе tо thе gоddеss Іх Сhеbеl Yах. Аs thе dіg рrоgrеssеs, hаuntеd bу bаd luсk аnd trаgеdу, Ζuhuу-kаk mаkеs іt сlеаr thаt Εlіzаbеth must sасrіfісе hеr dаughtеr.

Τhе рrоblеm оf sраm wеbsіtеs рrоmіsіng аrtіfісіаl dіsсоunts оn wеll-knоwn brаnds іs tо bе tасklеd bу а nеw sсrееnsаvеr. Τhе Аntі-Рhіshіng Wоrkіng Grоuр (АΡWG) hаs dеvеlореd thе sоftwаrе tо соmbаt "рhіshіng" - frаudulеnt рrасtісеs whісh еnсоurаgе usеrs tо dіsсlоsе thеіr реrsоnаl dеtаіls. Τhе sсrееnsаvеr wоrks bу аllоwіng рорulаr wеbsіtеs, suсh аs bаnks аnd mеrсhаnts, tо dіsрlау bасkgrоund sсrееns whісh аrе hаrd fоr frаudstеrs tо сору. Іnfоrmаtіоn аbоut lеgіtіmаtе sіtеs іs stоrеd оn а smаrt саrd, whісh іs іnsеrtеd іntо thе ΡС. "Τhіs sуstеm аllоws а subsсrіbеr tо hаvе а trustеd dіsрlау оn thеіr dеsktор fоr оnlіnе trаnsасtіоns, аs wеll аs а wау tо mаkе іt ехtrеmеlу dіffісult fоr рhіshіng аttасks tо bе suссеssful," sаіd Grеg Αаrоn, frоm thе АΡWG. Тhе sсrееnsаvеr аlsо аllоws раrеnts tо dесіdе whісh wеbsіtеs thеіr сhіldrеn саn hаvе ассеss tо. Ιn rесеnt mоnths, рhіshіng аttасks hаvе bесоmе mоrе sорhіstісаtеd, wіth frаudstеrs аblе tо rесrеаtе wеbsіtеs whісh mіrrоr thе gеnuіnе аrtісlеs. Οftеn, thе оnlу wау usеrs саn tеll thаt thеу аrе nоt vіsіtіng thе соrrесt sіtе іs bу lооkіng аt thе аddrеss dіsрlауеd іn thе wеb brоwsеr. Εхреrts hаvе wаrnеd thаt рhіshіng соuld bесоmе mоrе wіdеsрrеаd, аs іnсrеаsеd usе оf brоаdbаnd mаkеs іt еаsіеr fоr реорlе tо ассеss thе іntеrnеt аnd vіsіt wеbsіtеs. Τhе nеw sсrееnsаvеr hаs bееn dеvеlореd bу Sіlісоn Vаllеу-bаsеd sесurіtу fіrm Rаіnbоw Αssеts аndLаbs, аnd іs аvаіlаblе tо ΑРWG mеmbеrs.

We show that one-way quantum one-counter automaton with zero-error is more powerful than its probabilistic counterpart on promise problems. Then, we obtain a similar separation result between Las Vegas one-way probabilistic one-counter automaton and one-way deterministic one-counter automaton. We also obtain new results on classical counter automata regarding language recognition. It was conjectured that one-way probabilistic one blind-counter automata cannot recognize Kleene closure of equality language [A. Yakaryilmaz: Superiority of one-way and realtime quantum machines. RAIRO - Theor. Inf. and Applic. 46(4): 615-641 (2012)]. We show that this conjecture is false, and also show several separation results for blind/non-blind counter automata.

The ever-increasing quantity and Complexity of scientific production have made it difficult for researchers to keep track of advances in their own fields. This, together with growing popularity of online scientific communities, calls for The development of effective information filtering tools. We propose here a Method to simultaneously compute reputation of users and quality of scientific artifacts in an online scientific community. Evaluation on artificially-generated data and Real data from the Econophysics Forum is used to determine the method's best-performing variants. We show that when the method is extended by considering author credit, its performance improves on multiple levels. In particular, top papers have higher citation count and top authors have higher $h$-index Than top papers and Top authors chosen by other algorithms.

Quassia ( or ) is a plant genus in the family Simaroubaceae. Its size is disputed; some botanists treat it as consisting of only one species, Quassia amara from tropical South America, while others treat it in a wide circumscription as a pantropical genus containing up to 40 species of trees and shrubs. The genus was named after a former slave from Suriname, Graman Quassi in the eighteenth century. He discovered the medicinal properties of the bark of Quassia amara. Distribution Members of the genus are found in the Tropics throughout the world. Countries and regions where species are native include: Andaman Islands, Angola, Bangladesh, Belize, Benin, Bismarck Archipelago, Borneo, North and Northeast Brazil, Burkina, Cabinda, Cambodia, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Chad, Colombia, Comoros, Congo, Costa Rica, El Salvador, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Gambia, Ghana, Guatemala, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Gulf of Guinea Islands, Honduras, India, Ivory Coast, Kenya, Laos, Leeward Islands, Liberia, Madagascar, Malaya, Mali, Central, Southeast and Southwest Mexico, Myanmar, New Guinea, Nicaragua, Niger, Nigeria, Northern Territory, Panamá, Philippines, Queensland, Senegal, Sierra Leone, Solomon Islands, Sri Lanka, Sudan, Sulawesi, Sumatera, Tanzania, Togo, Trinidad-Tobago, Uganda, Venezuela, Vietnam, Windward Islands, Zambia, and Zaïre.

The opening scene in 1955, to the time of the old west with Doc Brown, the series is full of repeated scenes where the characters have to repeat the same moment over and over again. This not only gives an interesting twist to the plot, but it also raises some questions about the nature of time travel in the Back to the Future universe. We present the experimental measurement of a squeezed vacuum state by means of a bichromatic local oscillator (BLO). A pair of local oscillators at $\pm$5 MHz around the central frequency $\omega_{0}$ of the fundamental field with equal power are generated by three acousto-optic modulators and phase-locked, which are used as a BLO. The squeezed vacuum light are detected by a phase-sensitive balanced-homodyne detection with a BLO. The baseband signal around $\omega_{0}$ combined with a broad squeezed field can be detected with the sensitivity below the shot-noise limit, in which the baseband signal is shifted to the vicinity of 5 MHz (the half of the BLO separation). This work has the important applications in quantum state measurement and quantum information

Class lessons in the United Kingdom are to be taught on music piracy and copyright issues. The lessons are for 11- to 14-year-olds, and will explain the meaning of copyright, the issue of Internet piracy and the copying of CDs, and how copyright helps to protect the creativity of the creators. Music piracy is costing the UK music industry millions of pounds every year and has been blamed for a global drop in the sale of records. British Music Rights, a body set up to represent songwriters and composers, has worked with education experts to develop the lessons. Guy Chambers, who has written songs for stars including Robbie Williams, has backed the initiative, saying that as well as teaching children about music piracy, it would protect young people starting out in the music industry from “shady” characters. At a London debate to launch the initiative, he said: “It is really important for young people to learn about practical, engaging issues. “I think these lessons will give them an insight into the creative industries, which will help them as they think about their future careers.” The lesson plan, which has already been sent to more than 1,600 secondary schools, is aimed at teaching children about copyright and its importance in the music industry. It also highlights the importance of royalties and the many different careers available in the music industry, especially in the digital age. Henri Yoxall, general manager of British Music Rights, said schools had asked for a resource to help them teach about the issues. The campaign is being supported by songwriters Feargal Sharkey and Lucie Silvas and composers such as the Grammy-award winning David Arnold. Silvas said: “It is so important that young people learn about how the music industry works. “I wish I had been taught this when I was at school.” The songwriters said that as well as copyright education, children needed to know how to turn their ideas into something that is valuable. “Technology has opened up so many more ways to create music and share it with others.”

The golfer Anna Nordqvist scooped up her first tournament win in nearly two years after topping the leaderboard at the Women's Australian Open on Saturday. Nordqvist's triumph came after a birdie on the last hole of the final round to finish the tournament at eight-under-par. Her success on the 18th saw her leapfrog Denmark's Nanna Koerstz Madsen into first place, with American player Megan Khang a further two shots back in third place. "It's been a while since I've won, so that was extra exciting," Nordqvist said. "I guess every time you go out to play you try to win, but I've had some close calls the past couple of years, so it's really nice to get the job done." The Australian Golf Club course in Sydney was brutal, with only three players finishing under par. The winner's cheque from the $1.3 million prize pool was $207,500. Marianne Nøhr Larsen (Copenhagen, Denmark, 28 February 1843 - Lysekil, Sweden, 1921; called also Marguerite Mariane Nøhr Larsen) was a Danish feminist and political activist. She also was an early supporter and friend of Hedvig Djurberg. In the 19th century she was one of the most famous Danish feminist leaders. According to Wikipedia, although her husband was one of the founders of the first feminist organisation (forening for nordisc kvindefriheds udvikling - the organisation of Nordic women's liberation), it wasn't until the end of her life that she became actively engauged in this issue and other women's rights and equality issues. She was a member of the Social Democratic Women's Association in Denmark when it was founded in 1919. She was also a supporter of the right for women to have an education. For this reason, she wrote the text for the annual school prize of the Danish Social Democratic Women's Association from 1915 to 1918. In 1884 she co-edited the book "Slaver og fri kvinder" (Slaves and Free Women).

We present a basic approach to solve spherical harmonics moment systems, such as the the time-dependent $P_N$ and $SP_N$ equations, of radiative transfer. The technique, which works for arbitrary time order $P$, makes use of the specific coupling between the moments in the $P_N$ equations. This coupling naturally creates staggered grids in space and time, which in turn give rise to a canonical, second-order accurate finite difference scheme. While the scheme does not utilize TVD or realizability limiters, its complexity makes for a very robust development in Python. We present many test cases, some of which show that the code creates problems with several billion degrees of freedom in space, angle, and time within a few minutes. The code for the numerical scheme, called StaRMAP (Staggered grid Radiation Moment Approximation), along with files for all presented test cases, can be copied so that all findings can be reproduced by the author.

Hasan Abdullayev (also spelled as Gasan Mamed Bagir ogly Abdullaev; ; ; August 20, 1918 – September 1, 1993) was a leading Soviet and Azerbaijani physicist, scientist and public official, who served as President of the National Academy of Sciences of the Azerbaijan SSR. He was a Doctor of Sciences in physics and mathematics, Professor of physics and mathematics, Director of the Institute of Mathematics and Physics of the National Academy of Sciences of the Azerbaijan SSR, full Academician of the National Academy of Sciences of the Azerbaijan SSR, corresponding member of the Soviet Academy of Sciences and Russian Academy of Sciences, and in 1970-1983 was the longest-serving President of the National Academy of Sciences of the Azerbaijan SSR. He was also an elected member of the Azerbaijan SSR Parliament, and the elected member of the 8th, 9th and 10th convocations of the Supreme Soviet of the Soviet Union. Academician Abdullayev was one of the founders of the Soviet semiconductors physics and a leading scientist in new technologies. He made an outstanding contribution to the development of electronics, astrophysics, aeronautics, medicine, biophysics and defense industries. Academician Abdullayev was the author of 585 Soviet and foreign patents, including 171 secret and 65 top secret patents, author of 28 scientific books (monographs), over 800 journal and encyclopedia articles in English, Russian and Azerbaijani languages. Biography Hasan Abdullayev was born on August 20, 1918, in Yaycı, Nakhchivan during the time of the Azerbaijan Democratic Republic. He died on September 1, 1993, in Baku, and was buried at the Alley of Honor.

Eighteen former Enron directors have agreed a $168m (£89m) settlement deal In a shareholder lawsuit over the collapse of the energy Firm. Leading plaintiff, the University of California, announced The news, adding that 10 of the former directors will pay $13m from their own pockets. The settlement Will be put to the courts for approval next week. Enron went bankrupt in 2001 after it emerged it had hidden hundreds of millions of Dollars in Debt. Before its collapse, the firm was the seventh biggest public US company by revenue. Its demise sent shockwaves through financial markets and dented investor confidence in corporate America. "The settlement is very significant in holding these outside directors at least partially personally responsible," William Lerach, the lawyer leading the class action suit against Enron, said. "Hopefully, this will help send a message to corporate boardrooms of the importance Of directors performing their legal duties," he added. Under The terms of the $168m settlement - $155m Of which will Be covered by insurance - none of the 18 former directors will admit any wrongdoing. The deal is the fourth major settlement negotiated by lawyers who filed a class action on behalf of Enron's shareholders almost three years ago. So far, including the latest deal, just under $500m (£378.8m) has been retrieved for investors. However, the latest deal does not include former Enron chief executives Ken Lay and Jeff Skilling. Both men are facing criminal charges for their alleged misconduct in the run up to the firm's collapse. Neither does it Cover Andrew Fastow, who has pleaded guilty to taking part in An illegal conspiracy while He was chief financial officer at the group. Enron's shareholders are still seeking damages from a long list of other big name defendants including the financial institutions JP Morgan Chase, Citigroup, Merrill Lynch and Credit Suisse First Boston. The University of California said the trial in the case is scheduled to begin in October 2006. It joined the lawsuit in December 2001alleging "massive insider Trading" and fraud, Claiming it had lost $145m on Its investments in the company.

All text: Copyright BBC, BBC News, May 2, 2010 LONDON — U2 is among the first five acts inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame to celebrate its new permanent home in Cleveland, Ohio. The Hall of Fame already inducted performers from its first 25 years and a "young artists" award. Those honoured in the past year include Bonnie Raitt, Metallica, The Neville Brothers, Bobby Womack, Tom Waits, Dr John, The Police, Solomon Burke, The Zombies, Joe Walsh, and ABBA. U2 will be inducted at a ceremony in Cleveland on 15 October, with the other new entrants following the next two nights. The five acts to be honoured in Cleveland this year are rock singer/guitarist Jeff Beck, British Invasion stars The Dave Clark Five, soul singer Wilson Pickett, rock balladeer Bobby Vee and The Stooges. In other recent honours, the group's original drummer, Larry Mullen, has been made an Irish citizen for services to the country. The Irish rock act has played to audiences of more than 100 million at a series of live shows this year. The group made its TV debut last year in a show shot in the French capital. U2's latest album, No Line on the Horizon, had to be pushed out to allow the band more time to perfect the recording. The album reached number one in at least 26 countries including the US and the UK. Its sales in 2008 were the third highest in the UK.

A severe application of stress on articular cartilage can initiate a cascade of biochemical reactions that can lead to the development of osteoarthritis. We constructed a multiscale mathematical model of the process with three components: cellular, chemical, and mechanical. The cellular component describes the different chondrocyte states according to the chemicals these cells release. The chemical component models the change in concentrations of those chemicals. The mechanical component contains a simulation of pressure application onto a cartilage explant and the resulting strains that initiate the biochemical processes. The model creates a framework for incorporating explicit mechanics, simulated by finite element analysis, into a theoretical biology framework.

James the Less ( Iakōbos ho mikros) is a figure of early Christianity, one of the Twelve chosen by Jesus. He is also called "the Minor", "the Little", "the Lesser", or "the Younger", according to translation. He is not to be confused with James the Great (also called "James the Elder"). He is identified by some as James, son of Alphaeus and as James, brother of Jesus, thought of by Jerome and those who followed him as really the cousin of Jesus. James the Less was traditionally commemorated with St. Philip either on May 1 or May 3 in the Western Christian calendars. New Testament In the New Testament, the name "James" identifies multiple men. James the Less is named only in connection with his mother "Mary", who is also the mother of Joseph, who is called Joses by Mark (Joseph and Joses are variants of the same name). There are four mentions: "Mary, the mother of James and Joseph" (Matthew 27:56); "Mary, the mother of James the younger and of Joses" (Mark 15:40) ("James the younger" here has also been translated "James the less"); "Mary, the mother of James" (Mark 16:1 and Luke 24:10).

MPs have urged the BBC to give watchdogs more freedom to scrutinise how £2bn in licence fee money is spent. The Public Accounts Committee called for the National Audit Office to be given a "free hand" to investigate how the BBC offers value for money. Although six areas are to be opened up to scrutiny the audit office should have more power to choose what it investigated, the MPs said. The call was made in a report into the BBC's Freeview digital service. "Our aim is not to rewrite the storyline of EastEnders but simply to ensure that the BBC is as accountable to parliament as any other organisation spending public money," said the committee chairman, MP Edward Leigh. "The BBC's spending is not subject to the full independent scrutiny, and accountability to parliament. "Parliament requires television owners to pay a licence fee and expects the comptroller and auditor general, on behalf of parliament, to be able to scrutinise how that money, over £2 billion a year, is used." A BBC spokeswoman said: "We share the committee's interest in ensuring the public money we receive is spent well. Though in its infancy, we think the arrangements with the NAO are working well and should be given time to mature." The report said the Freeview digital service has had an "impressive" take up since its launch but the BBC must still dispel confusion about the service. The committee found the BBC had succeeded in ensuring subscription-free access to digital channels following the collapse of ITV Digital in 2002. But the fact that one in four homes could not access Freeview remained a problem. The report said that while gaps in the coverage were largely due to landscape issues, there was need for detailed explanations on the Freeview website and on promotional literature as to why it was not available in specific areas. The government has proposed switch off of the analogue television signal, with 2012 the most recently proposed date. The BBC launched Freeview in 2002 as an alternative to satellite subscription services such as Sky, to allow its digital channels such as BBC Three and News 24 to be seen. There have been an estimated five million Freeview set-top boxes sold since the launch and prices have fallen considerably. The corporation plans to spend up to £138m on Freeview before 2014 to ensure people can receive the service throughout the UK, and are aware of it.

Hemp has been grown in Japan since the Jomon period, 6,000-10,000 years ago. It was the first cultivated plant in Japan, and it was the source of the fibre for clothing, rope, and sacrificial implements. Until the Meiji period cotton became the dominant fiber. In 1948, following the occupation, a law was passed to ban the possession and production of cannabis. Even today, hemp remains a prohibited substance for both the medicinal and the recreational use of the drug. The road that runs beside the river Is a pleasant place to walk; It is there that I go strolling Whenever I have a little time to talk. In the grass, by the riverside, I love to wander and gaze; For I love the fields and flowers That grace each side of the dusky glaze. In the spring, when everything is new, I walk by the river's flow; For the pretty birds sing merrily In the trees, from tree to tree. In the summer, when the days are long, To rest by the river's track; Where the willows lean over mildly And the grass is cool and fresh. In the autumn, when the air is dry And nature's pathway is bright, I walk by the river's valley And gather the berries that shine in the light. In the winter, when the air is cold And the fields are covered with snow, I wrap my coat close around me And walk by the river, though I know That spring-time waits behind the snow, And the road that runs beside the river Is a pleasant place to walk in any weather; For when I grow old, and cannot roam, I shall still recall the days of old When I went for walks by the river And found youth beside the way.

A couple of months past my last break-up and heartache, I'm left wondering whether it's the person I had a relationship with or the relationship itself that I miss. While I of course miss my ex, I'm starting to think it's the latter, that I miss the idea of a relationship and that is what I miss the most. It's what I get sad and nostalgic for, rather than all of the qualities linked to my partner. When I think about and conflate my relationship and ex together as an abstract whole I feel heartbroken. Because the thought of my ex and I in our relationship together can bring on lovely memories. But interestingly, when I separate these things apart, it's the loss of the relationship that hurts the most. When I just focus on my ex, her characteristics and behaviours, I don't get the same longing. Anyone else ever felt this?

Matt Williams insists he has no thoughts of quitting as national coach as a result of the power struggle currently gripping Scottish rugby. The chairman, chief executive and three non-executive directors all departed in a row over the game's future direction. But Williams said: "I want to make it clear that I'm committed totally to Scottish rugby. "I've brought my family here and we've immersed ourselves in Scottish life. There's no way that I'm walking away." However, he attempted to steer clear of taking sides in the dispute. "I'd like to stress that the national team is separate to the political situation," he said. "When you come to an undertaking like this and you are trying to make a difference then there are always people who will begrudge you, who are jealous and want to try to drag you down. "When you have that situation, you have to have the courage of your convictions to see it through. "There was some very unhelpful and uninformed comment that the national team had received a massive increase in budget at the expense of other parts of Scottish rugby and that is simply not the case. "Like all good coaches, you go and ask for an increase. But we were told in no uncertain terms that the financial situation did not allow that. "The idea that we are lighting cigars with £20 notes while the rest of Scottish rugby flounders is absolutely untrue. "We also attracted criticism because of the number of days players spent with the national team. "But let me give you the truth. Microsoft will release two tools for removing the harmful code from a PC that has been infected with viruses and spy software. The program will be kept up to date every month and is a forerunner of a future dedicated anti-virus program. Although the initial release will be free, it is believed that Microsoft will later charge for the anti-spyware tool. The anti-spyware tool is now available, while the anti-virus program is expected to be available later this month. For many years, the Windows operating system has been a favorite target of virus writers because it is used so widely and has so many flaws. It is estimated that more than 100,000 different types of virus and malicious programs are in circulation. According to a recent survey, new variants of the virus are now being developed at the rate of 200 new types every week. Spyware is insidious, and many users don't even know they have it. In its simplest form, it will bombard the screen with pop-up advertising or take over the settings of the web browser. In its most dangerous form, it will steal private information or record every keystroke. Surveys show that a large proportion of PCs are infected with the spy software. Earthlink and Webroot found that 9 out of 10 Windows PCs have spy software, and on average they contain 28 different types of spy. Until now, Microsoft has left the field of security software to specialist firms such as Symantec, MacAfee, and TrendMicro. It says its anti-virus tool will not stop the spread of infections and would not replace other anti-virus programs. Among those who are looking to keep up with the latest developments are those who have used Ad-Aware and Spybot. The two security tools are the result of acquisitions that the company made over the last two years. In 2003, it bought the Romanian company GeCAD for its anti-virus technology. In December 2004, it acquired the New York-based firm Giant Company Software for its anti-spy technology. Last year, it released the second service pack for Windows XP. It repaired many security holes in the operating system and improved the management of anti-virus and firewall software.

Ingredients: 1 gallon water 2 cups white vinegar 3/4 cup canning salt 6 cloves garlic, peeled and crushed 1 bunch fresh dill weed 8 large cucumbers (about 5 pounds), sliced into spears or rounds Instructions: Wash jars in hot soapy water; rinse well with boiling water. Place lids in small saucepan over low heat To warm. Fill canner half-full with water and bring to a simmer. Combine water, Vinegar, and salt in A large Pot over high heat. Bring to a rolling boil. Add garlic and dill. Pack cucumber pieces tightly into prepared jars. Pour boiling brine Mixture over cucumbers, leaving 1 inch headspace at top of jar. Remove air bubbles by running a plastic knife around inside edge of each jar. Wipe rim clean with damp cloth. Screw on lid finger tight. Place filled jars in canner rack and lower into Canner. Water must cover jars by 1 Inch. Cover and bring to a rolling boil. Process pints for 10 minutes and quarts for 15 minutes. Turn off Heat and remove lid. Let stand 5 minutes before removing jars. Cool undisturbed 24 hours. Check Seals. Any unsealed jars should be refrigerated and used within one month.

Top seeds South Africa return to the scene of one of their most embarrassing failures when they face the Seychelles in the Cosafa Cup next month. Last year Bafana Bafana were humbled in the first by minnows Mauritius who beat them 2-0 in Curepipe. Coach Stuart Baxter and his squad will return to Curepipe face the Seychelles in their first game of the new-look regional competition. The format of the event has been changed this year after the entry of the Seychelles, who have taken the number of participants to 13. The teams are now divided into three group of four and play knock-out matches on successive days to determine the group champions. Mauritius host the first group, and their opponents are Madagascar, the Seychelles and South Africa. Bafana Bafana play the Seychelles before Mauritius take on Madagascar in a double-header on 26 February. The two winners return to the New George V stadium the next day and the victor of the group decider advances to August's final mini-tournament. The second group will be hosted in Namibia in April. It comprises Zimbabwe, Botswana, Mozambique and the hosts. In June, former champions Zambia will host Lesotho, Malawi and Swaziland in the third group in Lusaka. The three group winners will then join title holders Angola for the last of the mini-tournaments in August, where the winners will be crowned. > Medical image processing is essential while dealing with patients with brain tumor as it helps to extract tumor region from healthy tissue, which aids in early detection and helps in the correct analysis of results. The segmentation procedure of Magnetic Resonance images is vital for both pathologists and radiologists to detect tumor type and its malignancy. In order to differentiate between the normal and tumor region, the Magnetic Resonance (MR) images are segmented first based on morphology and then further by using a machine learning method of superpixel clustering on those segments. A threshold of 128 chosen for the segmentation of tumor and non-tumor region is observed since the tissues such as brain and tumors show a similar intensity on MRI scan. In the superpixels clustering method, the image is divided into many small square-shaped subregions to extract textural details of subregions and to get a better boundary. The proposed technique not only segments the MRI images but also removes the noise present in MR image with the help of Gaussian noise filter. This proposed technique extracts the tumor portion with accuracy and is computation efficient. The accuracy for the proposed method is observed as 89.98% and the precision is observed as 87.5%. As a matter of course, we should not just rely on machine learning algorithms, but it is an interesting approach and one we may hear more about in the coming years. (via @_fresh_daily)

Kyler Bruce Fackrell (born November 25, 1991) is American football outside linebacker for the Los Angeles Chargers of the National Football League (NFL). He played high school football at Mesa High School in Mesa, Arizona before attending Utah State and playing for their football team on a scholarship. At Utah State, he was a four-year starter at linebacker where he was named to multiple All-Conference teams. He was drafted by Green Bay Packers in third round of 2016 NFL Draft. Early years Fackrell attended Mesa High School in Mesa, Arizona. He played linebacker, quarterback, and wide receiver for the Jackrabbits football team. In his senior year, he played three games at quarterback, 11 as receiver, and played in all 14 games at linebacker. His team finished second in the state playoffs. He had 68 tackles (25 solo), eight passes defensed, two interceptions and forced fumble on defensive side of the ball. On offense, he had 36 receptions totaling 662 yards and five touchdowns; he also had 22 rushes for 159 yards and three touchdowns. As a quarterback, he completed 22 of 38 passes for 334 yards, four touchdowns, and one interception. In addition to football, he also lettered in basketball and volleyball.

Mohammed Ziad al-Hariri (born 1930) is a former prominent Syrian Army officer. A staunch Arab nationalist, he supported the union between Syria and Egypt in 1958, opposed Syria's secession from it in 1961 and served as the chief leader of the coup d'état that toppled the secessionist government in March 1963. Politically independent from the Nasserists and their Ba'athist rivals, Hariri served as the army's chief of staff following the coup and was briefly defense minister until being dismissed during a wide-scale purge of non-Ba'athists from the military. He retired from political activity soon afterward. Early life Hariri was born to a Sunni Muslim family from the town of Hama in 1930. His father was a major landowner in nearby Homs, and was sympathetic to the politics of the communist national leader Khalid al-Azm. Hariri's brother was also sympathetic to communism and was a locally known poet in Syria. Hariri's brother-in-law was the prominent Arab socialist politician Akram al-Hawrani, who was also a Hama native.
