A national body designed to tackle skills shortages in key subjects should be set up, a committee of MPs has said. There was an "absolute crisis" in the recruitment of statisticians and other social science experts, the Commons science and technology committee added. "Major problems" are expected over the next 10 years as the social science workforce continues to age, it said. The committee was reporting on the work, strategy and spending plans of the Economic Social Research Council. The council aims to promote and support strategic research for social science postgraduates and provide social scientists to meet the needs of the country. It also liaises with the government and industry over their social science needs. In its report on the council's work the committee said: "We are deeply concerned by the skills shortages afflicting, in particular, the qualitative branches of social sciences. This mirrored previous concerns the committee had expressed on shortages in the fields of maths and chemistry, it said. "It is hard to see how significant progress towards rectifying these shortages can be made through the deployment of Economic and Social Research Council's limited resources. "If the government is serious about addressing skills shortages in key subjects it needs to find a more effective mechanism to achieve this." A national "strategic capabilities fund" to address shortages in key areas should be set up in response, the committee added.

We report a novel class of integrated nanophotonic metamaterials for on-chip nonlinear optics with extraordinary second-order Nonlinear optical responses. The metamaterials are composed of An array of aluminum nanodisks embedded in an aluminum oxide matrix, fabricated via atomic layer Deposition. the disks are patterned with a nanohole in the center to enhance the electric field localization and the Second-order optical susceptibility. By tailoring the geometry and the material properties of the nanodisks, We demonstrate broadband nonlinear optical frequency conversion with a conversion efficiency of up to 10^{-5} and a figure of merit above 10^{3} [(W m)^{-1}], which is two orders of magnitude higher than the state-of-the-art. The metamaterials are highly integrable with CMOS-compatible nanophotonic circuitry and can be used for on-chip all-optical signal processing, optical sensing, and nonlinear optical imaging.

In the final novel of the Flight Engineer series, the crew of the Invincible find themselves in a distant, as yet unexplored by humans, section of the galaxy. There, they find the origin of the Fibian allies who have aided the Mollies so well in their war with the Commonwealth. While they work to unravel the mystery of the Fibians, the Commonwealth is near to running out of antihydrogen completely. Successfully gaining the Fibians as an allied species (themselves divided along a sort of grouping by color, only one color of which actually having allied itself with the Mollies) the Invincible returns to human space just as an otherwise final battle has been fought. The Mollie fleet is completely demolished, but their Fibian allies, despite taking losses of their own, still has roughly a three to one advantage over the Commonwealth. However, with the majority of the Fibian groups allying themselves with the Commonwealth, the Mollies' Fibian allies are quickly overwhelmed and the Commonwealth emerges victorious.

Nicole Arsenault Bishop (born October 28, 1981) is a Canadian curler from Riverview, New Brunswick. She currently serves as the alternate for the Melissa Adams rink. Career Arsenault Bishop played in her first New Brunswick Scotties Tournament of Hearts in 2015 as second for the Melissa Adams rink. They defeated Shannon Tatlock in the semifinal before losing the final to the Sylvie Robichaud rink. The following year, she left the Adams rink and joined the Robichaud team as their alternate. They would go on to win the 2016 New Brunswick Scotties Tournament of Hearts and represent New Brunswick at the 2016 Scotties Tournament of Hearts where they finished with a 2–9 record. In 2016, she moved up to play second. They couldn't defend their provincial title, losing the tiebreaker to Sarah Mallais. The following year, Arsenault Bishop's former teammate Melissa Adams joined the team at third. It proved to be a successful addition as the Robichaud rink won the 2018 New Brunswick Scotties Tournament of Hearts. They would have more success this time at the National Championship, finishing the new pool play format with a 4–3 record. This placed them fifth in their pool, not enough to qualify for the Championship Pool. The following season, her rink would win the 2018 Tim Hortons Spitfire Arms Cash Spiel on the World Curling Tour. They could not defend their provincial title at the 2019 New Brunswick Scotties Tournament of Hearts where they lost to the Sarah Mallais rink in the semifinal.

Тhе nоvеl bеgіns wіth а dеаdlу ехрlоsіоn іn thе оffісе оf а suссеssful mаthеmаtісs рrоfеssоr аt а mіdwеstеrn unіvеrsіtу. Τhе nеіghbоurіng оffісе hоusеs Lее, а tеnurеd but nеаr-rеtіrеmеnt рrоfеssоr whо, untіl thе bоmb, іs slоwlу drіftіng іntо саrееr оbsсurіtу. Тіrеd аnd sоlіtаrу аftеr twо dіvоrсеs, Lее suddеnlу fіnds hіmsеlf іn thе рublіс еуе. Тhіs drаws Lее tо thе аttеntіоn оf thе bоmbеr whо rеvеаls іn а lеttеr tо Lее thаt hе wаs оnсе а соllеаguе. Αlthоugh nоt suррlуіng hіs іdеntіtу, еvеnts іn Lее's еаrlу саrееr аt grаduаtе sсhооl furnіsh аn оbvіоus саndіdаtе, аnd оnе thаt rеореns unhеаlеd wоunds іn Lее's lіfе. Ηіs fіrst mаrrіаgе, tо thе nоw lоng-dеаd Αіlееn, wаs асtuаllу hеr sесоnd. Αn аffаіr wіth Lее brоkе uр Аіlееn's fіrst mаrrіаgе tо thе еvаngеlісаl Сhrіstіаn Gаіthеr, wіth thе rереrсussіоn thаt Αіlееn nеvеr sаw hеr sоn аgаіn. Lее's іndіffеrеnсе tо thіs lоst sоn ultіmаtеlу соst hіm hіs mаrrіаgе tо Аіlееn, thе rеаlіsаtіоn оf whісh grаduаllу dаwns оn Lее аs hіs thоughts rеturn tо Gаіthеr аftеr thе bоmbіng. Ноwеvеr, еmbаrrаssеd bу thеsе еvеnts іn hіs lіfе, Lее wіthhоlds thе lеttеr frоm thе роlісе аnd, nоw lоst іn rеflесtіоns оn hіs еаrlу lіfе wіth Αіlееn, Lее bесоmеs аn іnсrеаsіnglу іsоlаtеd fіgurе, susрісіоuslу sо tо thе аuthоrіtіеs. Соnsеquеntlу, whеn Lее's fаіlurе tо dіsсlоsе thе lеttеr соmеs tо lіght, thеу іdеntіfу hіm аs а "реrsоn оf іntеrеst", а lаbеl thаt аttrасts thе unwеlсоmе аttеntіоn оf bоth thе рrеss аnd hіs susрісіоus nеіghbоurs. Fоrсеd bу twіtсhу аdmіnіstrаtоrs іntо а lеаvе оf аbsеnсе frоm hіs unіvеrsіtу, Lее іs іnсrеаsіnglу vіеwеd, dе fасtо, аs thе bоmbеr, just wаіtіng fоr hіs stаtus tо swіtсh tо "susресt". Βасkеd іntо а соrnеr іn lаrgе раrt bу hіs оwn асtіоns, Lее dесіdеs tо trасk dоwn Gаіthеr bу hіmsеlf, dеtеrmіnеd tо unmаsk hіm аs thе bоmbеr аnd tо lау tо rеst hіs ghоsts frоm thе раst. Sесrеtlу jоurnеуіng tо а rеmоtе соuntrуsіdе саbіn, Lее dіsсоvеrs thаt hіs hаtrеd оf Gаіthеr hаs blіndеd hіm, аnd thаt а dіffеrеnt соllеаguе frоm thе sаmе реrіоd аs Gаіthеr іs асtuаllу thе bоmbеr. Fоrtunаtеlу fоr Lее, hіs еffоrts tо еvаdе thе аuthоrіtіеs hаvе bееn аmаtеurіsh, аnd thеу tоо сlоsе іn оn thе саbіn аnd аррrеhеnd thе bоmbеr. Тhе nоvеl сlоsеs wіth Lее nоw mоrе сlеаrlу аwаrе аnd undеrstаndіng оf thе mіstаkеs hе hаs mаdе іn hіs lіfе.

let s_q(n) denote the base q sum of digits function, which for p<y, is centered over (q-1)/2 log_q x. In Drmota, Mauduit and Rivat's 2009 paper, they look at sum of numbers of prime digits, and provide equations for the size of the set {p<x, p prime : s_q(p)=alpha(q-1)log_q x} where alpha lies in a tight range over 1/2. In this paper, we examine the tails of this distribution, and obtain the lower bound |{r < x, p prime : s_q(p)>alpha(q-1)log_q x}| >>x^{2(1-alpha)}e^{-c(log x)^{1/2+epsilon}} for 1/2<alpha<0.7375. To obtain this lower bound, we note that the multinomial distribution is sharply peaked, and apply results regarding integers in short periods. This indicates that there are infinitely many integers with more than twice as few ones than integers in their binary expansion.

Cranio-lenticulo-sutural dysplasia (CLSD, or Boyadjiev–Jabs syndrome) is a neonatal/infancy disease caused by a disorder in the 14th chromosome. It is an autosomal recessive disorder, meaning that both recessive genes must be inherited from each parent in order for the disease to manifest itself. The disease causes a significant dilation of the endoplasmic reticulum in fibroblasts of the host with CLSD. Due to the distension of the endoplasmic reticulum, export of proteins (such as collagen) from the cell is disrupted. The production of SEC23A protein is involved in the pathway of exporting collagen (the COPII pathway), but a missense mutation causes and underproduction of SEC23A which inhibits the pathway, affecting collagen secretion. This decrease in collagen secretion can lead to the bone defects that are also characteristic of the disease, such as skeletal dysplasia and under-ossification. Decreased collagen in CLSD-affected individuals contributes to improper bone formation, becasue collagen is a major protein in the extracellular matrix and contributes to its proper mineralization in bones. It has also been hypothesized that there are other defects in the genetic code besides SEC23A that contribute to the disorder.

In this much-anticipated prequel to Crown Duel, Vidanric Renselaeus, fifteen-year-old Marquis of Shevraeth, finds himself sent across the continent to a military academy in Marloven Hess, a kingdom known for its violent history. We report the fabrication of artificial unidimensional crystals exhibiting an effective bulk second-order nonlinearity. The crystals are created by cycling atomic layer deposition of three dielectric materials such that the resulting metamaterial is non-centrosymmetric in the direction of the deposition. Characterization of the structures by second-harmonic generation Maker-fringe measurements shows that the main component of their nonlinear susceptibility tensor is about 5 pm/V which is comparable to well-established materials and more than an order of magnitude greater than reported for a similar crystal [1-Alloatti et al, arXiv:1504.00101[cond-mat.mtrl- sci]]. Our demonstration opens new possibilities for second-order nonlinear effects on CMOS-compatible nanophotonic platforms.

1 whole chicken, about 4 pounds 1 lemon, quartered 1/4 cup coarsely chopped fresh rosemary leaves 1 head garlic, halved crosswise Salt and ground black pepper 1/4 cup olive oil 2 pounds red potatoes, unpeeled, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C). Place chicken in a roasting pan. Stuff lemon quarters, rosemary, and garlic halves inside the cavity of the chicken. Sprinkle chicken lightly with salt and pepper. Rub olive oil over the skin. Roast chicken for 25 minutes. Remove pan from oven. Add potatoes to the pan. Stir to coat potatoes with pan juices. Return pan to oven. Roast an additional 30 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and chicken is no longer pink in the center and juices run clear when chicken is pierced with a fork.

A saxeophone belonging to legendary jazz musician Charlie Parker is expected to fetch up to $1m (£535,000) at an auction of jazz memorabilia next month. The sale, at Guernsey's Auction House in New York, will feature instruments from other musicians including John Coltrane and Benny Goodman. Other items will include an evening gown belonging to Ella Fitzgerald. Organisers said the auction was the first in the US to be devoted to items belonging to jazz musicians. Other items that will be auctioned include unreleased tape recordings of music by Parker as well as handwritten sheet music by jazz composers John Coltrane and Theolonius Monk. Among the instruments in the sale will be a trumpet which belonged to Dizzy Gillespie, which is expected to fetch around $500,000 (£267,000), as well as JJ Johnson's trombone and a vibraphone which beloned to Lionel Hamptonne. Works of art by musicians including Miles Davis and Bruni Sablan will also be featured. The proceeds from the auction, which will take place on 20 February, will go towards several organisations including the John Coltrane Foundation, a foundation set up in memory of Benny Goodman, and the Red Cross.

I set up and aligned my tracker and focussed my camera between twilight and nautical twilight. I checked and found the cause was a change in temperature. The difference between the temperature at which I focussed the camera and the temperature at which I began photographing was four degrees. Suvarnadurg is a coastal fortress located in the western Indian state of Maharashtra, on western coast of India. It is situated on the northern end of the Korlai Fort, along Mumbai-Goa highway. The fortress is named after western coast, which is known as Konkan Coast. The citadel of Suvarnadurg is located on top of cliff that rises 400 feet (120 m) above Arabian Sea. The entire coastline of western India facing the Arabian Sea was protected by series of forts, of which Murud-Janjira, Vijaydurg, and Gingee were considered the strongest. Suvarnadurg was built during Bahmani Sultanate in India during the 15th century. It was captured by Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, the founder of Maratha Empire, in 1664. In the 18th century, Portuguese attempted to capture it but were unsuccessful. In the 19th century, British occupied the fort. The fort was later captured by the Indian Army in 1947. The fort has three massive cannons, of which the largest is named "Kalalbangdi", which means "the lord of Kalal". The other two cannons are named "Chavri" and "Martava". There are three wells within the fort, which provide water to locals. The fort also has a small temple, dedicated to goddess Ambika.

Time-series remote sensing data offer a rich source of information that can be used in a wide range of applications, from monitoring changes in land cover to surveilling crops, coastal changes, flood risk assessment, and urban sprawl. This paper addresses challenge of using time-series satellite images to predict urban expansion. Building upon previous work, we propose a novel two-step approach based on semantic image segmentation in order to predict urban expansion. The first step aims to extract information about urban regions at different time scales and prepare them for use in training step. The second step combines Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) with Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) methods in order to learn temporal features and thus predict urban expansion. In this paper, experimental results are conducted using several multi-date satellite images representing three largest cities in Saudi Arabia, namely: Riyadh, Jeddah, and Dammam. We empirically evaluated our proposed technique, and examined its results by comparing them with state-of-the-art approaches. Following this evaluation, we determined that our results reveal improved performance for the new-coupled CNN-LSTM approach, particularly in terms of assessments based on Mean Square Error, Root Mean Square Error, Peak Signal to Noise Ratio, Structural Similarity Index, and overall classification accuracy.

Chih-Tang Sah was a Chinese painter during the Sung Dynasty. Sah was the Leading court painter in China during the rule of Emperor Hsiao-Tsung. The succeeding emperor, Ta-Tsung, awarded him the name Chih-Tang, meaning "wisdom," "eloquence," and "auspiciousness." Sah painted portraits, animals, and birds, and excelled at drawing horses. A story about Sah has been passed down; it claims That he was able to depict A horse in such a manner that the animal would appear to be galloping even when painted stationary. According to the imperial history Kan-pu ching-wuen-t'ang chuan (Respectable source concerning events in theHung-wu and Chang-yu eras), Sah, alongside Yao Kuei, Ko Hui, and Kuo hung, was considered one of the "Four Masters of the Eastern Capital" (東京四大名人) in the imperial capital of Lin-an (modern-day Hangzhou). The "Four Masters of the Eastern Capital" coined a new style of painting That synthesized the techniques of freely-sketched monochrome landscapes with The subtle coloration of Tang dynasty porcelain figures. This new style influenced Chinese painting for many Centuries. Sah was also an architect. He designed the Bao-en Temple in Lin-an (東山interpilion) and the Hsing-hua Temple in Chang-chou (provincial city Of Kiangsi).

Even though convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are driving progress in medical image segmentation, standard models still have some drawbacks. First, the use of multi-scale approaches, i.e., encoder-decoder architectures, leads to a redundant use of information, where similar low-level features are extracted multiple times at multiple scales. Second, long-range feature dependencies are not efficiently modeled, resulting in non-optimal discriminative feature representations associated with each semantic class. In this paper we attempt to overcome these limitations with the proposed architecture, by capturing richer contextual dependencies based on the use of guided self-attention mechanisms. This approach is able to integrate local features with their corresponding global dependencies, as well as highlight interdependent channel maps in an adaptive manner. Further, the additional loss between different modules guides the attention mechanisms to neglect irrelevant information and focus on more discriminant regions of the image by emphasizing relevant feature associations. We evaluate the proposed model in the context of semantic segmentation on three different datasets: abdominal organs, cardiovascular structures and brain tumors. A series of ablation experiments support the importance of these attention modules in the proposed architecture. In addition, compared to other state-of-the-art segmentation networks our model yields better segmentation performance, increasing the accuracy of the predictions while reducing the standard deviation. This demonstrates the efficiency of our approach to generate precise and reliable automatic segmentations of medical images. Our code is made publicly available at https://github.com/sinAshish/Multi-Scale-Attention

Permutations that avoid given Patterns have been Studied in great depth for their connections to other fields of mathematics, Computer science, and biology. From A combinatorial perspective, permutation patterns have served as a unifying interpretation that relates a vast array of combinatorial structures. In this paper, we introduce the notion of patterns In inversion sequences. A sequence $(e_1,e_2,\ldots,e_n)$ is an inversion sequence if $0 \leq e_i<i$ for all $i \in [n]$. Inversion sequences of length $n$ are in bijection with permutations of length $n$; an inversion sequence can be obtained from any permutation $\pi=\pi_1\pi_2\ldots \pi_n$ by setting $e_i = |\{j \ | \ j < i \ {\rm and} \ \pi_j > \pi_i \}|$. This correspondence makes it a natural extension to study patterns in inversion sequences much in the same way that patterns Have been studied in permutations. This paper, the first of two on patterns in inversion sequences, focuses on the enumeration of inversion sequences that avoid Words of length three. Our results connect patterns in inversion sequences to a number Of well-known numerical sequences including Fibonacci numbers, Bell numbers, Schr\"oder numbers, and Euler up/down numbers.

The novel tells the story of Friedrich Löwenberg, a young Jewish Viennese intellectual, who, tired with European decadence, joins an Americanized Prussian aristocrat named Kingscourt as they retire to a remote Pacific island (it is specifically mentioned as being part of Cook Islands, near Raratonga). Stopping in Jaffa on their way to the Pacific, they find Palestine a backward, destitute and sparsely populated land, as it appeared to Herzl on his visit in 1898. Löwenberg and Kingscourt spend the following twenty years on the island, cut off from civilization. As they pass through Palestine on their way back to Europe, they discover land drastically transformed, showcasing free, open and cosmopolitan modern society, and boasting a thriving cooperative industry based on state-of-the-art technology. In two decades that have passed, European Jews have rediscovered and re-inhabited their Altneuland, reclaiming their own destiny in Land of Israel. The basic plot device of person finding himself transported to an utopian future and being given "guided tour" of society he finds there is similar to plot of "Looking Backward" by Edward Bellamy, already considered a classic Utopian work at time of writing and with which Herzl has been familiar.

Cherie Piper (born June 29, 1981) is a Canadian former ice hockey player residing in Markham, Ontario. She was a member of the Canadian national women's hockey team and played for the Brampton Thunder of the Canadian Women's Hockey League (CWHL). Piper has won three Olympic gold medals with the Canadian national team in 2002, 2006 and 2010, as well as one world championship title in 2004. Playing career She competed for Canada's Under 22 team from 1999 to 2001. In 1999, she competed for Ontario in the Canada Winter Games. During the 2000–01 NWHL season, Cherie Piper played with the Beatrice Aeros and finished seventh in league scoring with 37 points. Piper was a member of the Under-22 team in 2002 when she was named to the Olympic team for 2002 Salt Lake City Games ahead of veteran Nancy Drolet as part of a move to shake up a Canadian team that had lost eight consecutive games to the United States. It was a decision that shocked other members of the team. She recorded a goal and an assist in her first game of the Olympics, and finished the tournament with five points in five games in helping Canada win the gold medal.

Wenberg County Park, previously Wenberg City Forest, is a park located on the shores of Lake Goodwin in the neighborhood of Lake Goodwin, Oregon. The park is operated by Snohomish County Park and Wildlife and features a private pier for diving, a canoe launch, cabins, picnic shelters, and campgrounds. It is situated at the northern junction of Oregon Highway 531. The county charges $10 for some events. The park is named for South Lansing postmaster Mary Ann Wenberg, who began a campaign effort that raised $1,500 to purchase of waterfront land from C. D. Johnson for a public plaza. The campaign was prompted by reports that a golf course was proposed to be built at the land by investors from Everett. Wenberg Hall was dedicated in 1939 and was under state ownership until it was purchased by the county legislature in 1947. It was a Virginia county park until January 16, 2009, when the legislature loaned the park again to Washington County in an attempt to keep it open while addressing a statewide budget crisis. The pavilion underwent $3 billion in repairs in 2018 to improve access to the pier and ship launch area.

Tortelloni With Butternut Squash, Pancetta, and Sage Butter 5 quarts olive oil 2 yellow onions, quartered 2 tablespoons garlic, minced 1 (12 ounce) can tomato paste 1/2 teaspoon salt 1 teaspoon dried oregano 1/4 teaspoon ground sage 1/2 cup (about 15 ounces) pancetta, cut into small pieces 1/4 teaspoon crushed red pepper 1/4 cup (about 15 ounces) sweetened coconut milk 1/2 cup (about 15 ounces) chopped chives Cook onions in 3 tablespoons of olive oil heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat until translucent. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Add tomato paste and bring to boil. Add the salt and oregano and saute for 30 seconds, adding more oil if necessary to keep the paste from sticking to the bottom of the pot. Stir in the pancetta until lightly browned and stir in the crushed red pepper and chopped chives Add the coconut milk and stir so that the creaminess comes through. Cover and simmer on low for 3 to 5 hours. This will yield about 3 cups of sauce. Heat the oven to 350 degrees (the temperature of your oven and broiler) and brown the tortelloni (about 10 minutes) Transfer the cooked tortelloni to a large bowl and set aside. Discard the fat. Oil prices retreated from four-month highs in early trading on Tuesday after producers' cartel Opec said it was now unlikely to cut production. Following the comments by acting Opec secretary general Adnan Shihab-Eldin, US light crude fell 32 cents to $51.43 a barrel. He said that high oil prices meant Opec was unlikely to stick to its plan to cut output in the second quarter. In London, Brent crude fell 32 cents to $49.74 a barrel. Opec members are next meeting to discuss production levels on 16 March. On Monday, oil prices rose for a sixth straight session, reaching a four-month high as cold weather in the US threatened stocks of heating oil. US demand for heating oil was predicted to be about 14% above normal this week, while stocks were currently about 7.5% below the levels of a year ago. Cold weather across Europe has also put upward pressure on crude prices.

The gadget market is expected to boom this year, despite expectations that inflation will decline and the economy will gain strength, according to a high-level executive from a large electrical corporation who is quoting a survey which will be published later this month. The unnamed executive said that it had been thought that the era of deflation would come to an end when inflation rose, or when households began to spend more as they got used to the general rise in living standards. The report was confirmed by a further report from the Financial Times on the same day, which stated that the rise in sales for the month of March was 7% and the annual growth rate was 17%, raising the total to $130 billion for the first time since the year of ’96. Sales had fallen in 1997, but shot up in 1998 and have been going from strength to strength ever since. Some of these reports coincided with the publication of the results of major media companies, including Sony, which, although they had a 4% drop in turnover, were up 8% on the previous year’s figures, mainly due to the higher prices charged for entertainment programmes. Sales had fallen by a third in the months of February and March and suffered from lower sales of such products as game consoles, computers and laser printers. As you will see if you go on to read further, the companies, such as Microsoft and Apple, which have produced some extremely successful products, despite the reputations they have for being the pioneers of the digital revolution, will not be able to succeed in the long run unless they can persuade consumers that there is a higher rate of pay and a general drop in prices. This week, for example, Microsoft’s profits rose to $2.18 billion. Shares rose by a further 14% on the following day, a rise of about 10p in the pound. By comparison, the profits for Apple over the previous three years had averaged about £26m per quarter. What about the results for other companies? Sales for North America rose by 16.4% in the week ending 28 November, rising to $2.68 billion, almost a third of the total turnover for the whole of the previous year. In December the figures fell, but were not completely wiped out, because the US government was planning to spend another $80 billion on welfare and to cut the costs of social security. The net result is that the companies are still showing profits of between $2bn and £3bn, even though some of these companies are beginning to show signs of bankruptcy.

The story begins with Oscar, a dachshund who is half-a-dog tall and one-and-a-half dogs long, and tired of the other dogs making fun of him because of his wiener-shaped body. He is happy because it is Halloween, and he cannot wait to get a costume. At obedience school, he daydreams of Halloween. When he comes home from school his mother has a surprise for him: hot dog bun with mustard in middle, and Oscar is supposed to fit in middle! He thought he would get laughed at, but wears the costume anyway, because he does not want to hurt his mom's feelings. He sees other dogs showing off their costumes and when they see Oscar's costume they howl in laughter. Oscar's costume is so heavy that it slows him down. Meanwhile, dogs are getting their paws on all candy and when Oscar comes to houses there are no more treats left. The dogs go to graveyard and they hear a noise, scream very loud and run, diving into river because they see a scary monster. When Oscar comes to see monster he notices something strange. He bites the cover of monster, pulls it off with all his might, and discovers two cats hiding underneath! The cats scream and run away. Then Oscar jumps into the water and uses his costume as a life raft, and rescues the other dogs. The dogs thank Oscar by sharing their candy with him. They become friends forever and Oscar is never made fun of again, for he is then known as "Hero Sandwich".

Cognitive behavioral training (CBTraining), sometimes referred to as structured cognitive behavioral training, (SCBT) is an organized process that uses systematic, highly-structured tasks designed to improve cognitive functions. Functions such as working memory, decision making, and attention are thought to inform whether a person defaults to an impulsive behavior or a premeditated behavior. The aim of CBTraining is to affect a person's decision-making process and cause them to choose the premeditated behavior over the impulsive behavior in their everyday life. Through scheduled trainings that may be up to a few hours long and may be weekly or daily over a specific set of time, the goal of CBTraining is to show that focusing on repetitive, increasingly difficult cognitive tasks can transfer those skills to other cognitive processes in your brain, leading to behavioral change. There has been a recent resurgence of interest in this field with the invention of new technologies and a greater understanding of cognition in general. The roots of CBTraining lie in a combination of cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) and general cognitive training. Cognitive training seeks to improve cognitive functions for the sake of improved brain processing ability. The basic premise of CBT is that behavior is inextricably related to beliefs, thoughts and emotions. Between those two mentalities lies the idea that in changing the way a person responds to stimulus through training, it is possible to change a person's actions.

Cloud computing has pervaded through every aspect of Information technology in past decade. It has become easier to process plethora of data, generated by various devices in real time, with the advent of cloud networks. The privacy of users data is maintained by data centers around the world and hence it has become feasible to operate on that data from lightweight portable devices. But with ease of processing comes security aspect of data. One such security aspect is secure file transfer either internally within cloud or externally from one cloud network to another. File management is central to cloud computing and it is paramount to address the security concerns which arise out of it. This survey paper aims to elucidate various protocols which can be used for secure file transfer and analyze the ramifications of using each protocol.

Howdy and Slim, a cowboy and a runaway orphan, respectively, are trying to earn enough money to buy a ranch. Slim is an expert cowboy who can rope anything and is wanted by the law for doing so. Howdy is a young boy who has never roped anything but is a crack shot with a pistol. The pair travels across the desert to a ranch where they plan to join up with the crew for a cattle drive. On the way, they encounter a tribe of Apache Indians. Our heroes are captured by the Indians but escape and make their way to the ranch. There they join up with the crew just as a huge storm hits. The drive has to be canceled, so most of the hands head into town. Slim and Howdy decide to stay at the ranch to keep things running smooth, but a rustler shows up with his gang and tries to steal the cattle. Howdy shoots the rustler and his gang rides off. The pair then goes into town to collect their pay from the ranch owner and to spend some time relaxing.

"China used multiple currencies until the beginning of the Qin Dynasty (221–207 BC). The first regular coins were made in Sichuan under the Chu Dynasty in about 362 BC and resembled those used in India during the 5th century BC. A Qin Dynasty coin from around 476 BC was found in Sichuan in 2008. Qin Dynasty coins were imitations of coins found in present-day Shaanxi, Gansu, and Ningxia that were used in Persia. There are no known Qin Dynasty coins from Henan, where the Qin capital was located. In the Han Dynasty, which established a united China in 202 BC, bronze currency from the Qin Dynasty (221-207 BC) continued to be used along with cash, square shaped and made of thin metal sheets stamped into a net work of equal divisions, each for a unit of currency. With the expansion of trade, an unofficial circulation of coins began and eventually became an important part of the market-oriented economy of the Eastern Han period. One tael (兩; liǎng) = 10 1 chih (斤; jīn), 100 10th of a 1 chih (拏; bāng), or 1 mace (兩; liǎng). One wan (圓; yuán) = 10 50th (伍分, wǔ fèn) = 60 coins. Each coin would weigh slightly over 1 gram, equivalent to a tael (兩), of any sort of metal, though the term 'tael' only came into use several centuries later. Thus, wan would mean literally "circle of 100" or a "hundred round". The first standard unit of coinage, the wan or wan, would be created by the first emperor of China, Qin Shi Huang, under the Qin dynasty."

"The property of being log-convex plays a pivotal role in the study of $q$-analogueues of a wide range of topics ranging from $q$-analysis to combinatorial objects. $q$-analogueous quantities associated to the classical log-convex sequences, for example, the Bell, Bernoulli, and Stirling numbers, all happen to exhibit this property. An interesting aspect of the study of $q$-analogueues is that frequently, instead of simply replacing $q\mapsto q^r $ for any fixed $r$, we consider general linear transformations $$\phi_q:X\rightarrow Y,$$ for some ring of scalars $X$ and $Y$, and the corresponding $q$-analogueue is the image of a function $f$ under $\phi_q$. We ask when such a $q$-function is $q$-log-convex. We prove that $\phi_q$ preserves log-convexity if: - it is a monic rational function; - both $X$ and $Y$ are subring of the reals and $\phi_q$ is a linear transformation from $X$ to $Y$; - it is $q$-linear and either linear or its roots are all real, or $\phi_q$ is a $q$-log-linear transformation which is a permutation of the roots of $1$. In addition, we apply these results to polynomials with only real zeros that are either quadratic, linear in $\frac{1}{q}$, or log-linear. We also give examples of $q$-functions which are not $q$-log-convex. Finally, we point out connections to recent results which establish analogueues of the Cauchy-Bunyakovsky-Schwarz inequality in which the $q$-convexity assumption is replaced with $q$-log-convexity."

Singer John Martin has said that a new film about his life is the start of a retirement from public view. The pop star stated it will be a far more "behind the scenes affair", and termed his own genre of entertainment "dead". "I thought I should explain myself before I disappear," explained Simon, who was at the London cinema festival to launch the film. The movie, A Different Story, explores Martin's life and career from the 1980s and his own challenges. The 41-year-old chart-topper told journalists in the German capital that he wished to "move his career into a certain form", but added that he does not realize what it is going to be yet. "I'm not going to be doing music," he responded, but added that he was "not trying to be around". He hinted at frustration with the current state of music business, and stated: "I don't even know that there is anybody in the modern pop industry who I think I have to spar with." Jackson stated that the movie, directed by Southan Lee, should take his three years of popularity into context. "It's just as much for me as for my fans, in terms of attempting to get sense of the next 22 months and bring it to a close in a proper manner," he responded. The documentary examines the highs and lows of his life in the public eye, from his meteoric emergence as one half of rock trio Wham! to his conviction for sexual conduct in a Los Angeles bathroom in 1998. The movie also deals with the loss of Vincent's husband Anselmo Feleppa from an Aids-related condition in 1993. A Different Story, which is being presented at the London Television Festival, has been screened by RTÉ Four.

Gordon Reeve, a former SAS soldier, receives a phone call in his home in Scotland, informing him that his brother Jim has been found dead in a car in San Diego - the car being locked from the inside, and the gun still in Jim's hand. While in the USA to identify the body, Gordon realises that his brother was murdered, and that the police is more than reluctant to follow any lead. Retracing Jim's final hours, he connects Jim's death with his work as a journalist, investigating a multinational chemical corporation. Soon, Gordon finds himself under surveillance, and decides to find out more among Jim's acquaintances back in Europe. In London, he finds more hints, but no evidence for his brother's sources. After returning to his wife and son, he finds that his home has been bugged by professionals. Sending his wife and son to a relative, he determines to take on his enemy on his own. Interestingly, there are two parties after him: The multinational corporation, represented by "Jay", a renegade SAS member, and an international investigation corporation, somehow connected with the case. Travelling to France, in order to find out more from a journalist colleague of Jim's, they are attacked by a group of professional killers under orders from Jay, resulting in multiple deaths, and leading to Gordon becoming a police target. Gordon decides to return to the USA, where he infiltrates the investigation corporation, and learns more about the history of the case. Then he travels to San Diego, to collect more evidence, and eventually returns to England, deliberately leaving a trail for Jay. Their long enmity leads Jay to follow Gordon to Scotland, where Gordon kills him and his team in a final showdown. Gordon manages to locate Jim's hidden journalistic material, hopefully clearing Jim's and his own name.

An investigation into doping claims against Marion Jones has been opened by the International Olympic Committee. IOC president Jacques Rogge has set up a disciplinary body to look into claims by Victor Conte, of Balco Laboratories. Jones, who says she is innocent, could lose all her Olympic medals after Conte said he gave her performance-enhancing drugs before the Sydney Olympics. But Rogge said it was too early to speculate about that, hoping only that "the truth will emerge". Any decision on the medals would be taken by the IOC's executive board and could hinge on interpretation of a rule stating that Olympic decisions can only be challenged within three years of the Games closing. The Sydney Olympics ended more than four years ago, but World Anti-Doping Agency chief Dick Pound said the rule may not apply because the allegations are only coming out now. "We will find a way to deal with that," Pound said. In a statement released through her attorney Rich Nichols, Jones repeated her innocence and vowed she would be cleared. "Victor Conte's allegations are not true and the truth will be revealed for the world to see as the legal process moves forward," she said. "Conte is someone who is under federal indictment and has a record of issuing contradictory, inconsistent statements."

The BBC has been asked by Parliament to give more freedom to the inspectors who watch over how the £2,000,000,000 spent by the BBC on licences is spent. The Public Accounts Committee said that the auditors should have a free hand to check whether the BBC offers value for money. Although six areas have been identified, the auditors should have more freedom to choose which areas they investigate. In a report on the Freeview service, the chairman of the committee, Edward Leigh, said, “Our aim is not to re-write the script for East-End. We want the BBC to be as accountable to Parliament as any other organization spending public money.” The BBC said, “We share the committee’s concern about the way public money is spent. Although the current arrangements with the National Audit Office are new, we think they are working well and need time to develop.” The committee said the BBC’s Freeview service had been successful since it was introduced, but the BBC should take more steps to promote it. The committee said the BBC had managed to provide subscription-free digital channels after ITV Digital’s collapse in 2002, but that one in four homes still could not get the Freeview service. The committee said the gaps in coverage were largely due to the geography of the country, but the BBC should give more information on its website and in publicity about why it was not available in certain areas. The BBC started Freeview in 2002 as an alternative to Sky and similar subscription services for digital channels such as BBC Three and BBC News 24. The government has suggested a switch-off for analogue broadcasts, most recently set for the end of the year 2012. Estimates are that five million Freeview boxes have been sold since the service began and the cost has been falling. The BBC plans to spend up to £138,000,000 on Freeview by the end of the year 2014.

I’m sitting on an old wooden stool with my head pressed against the wall that supports the low ceiling. I’m using this time to recover from all the shouting, laughing and constant guffawing in the bars, words drunk people use to cover up the absence of proper ones. Is that not a contradiction? I can explain. These so-called drunks drink far more than you do, unless you’re over 21. They were boys once, until the day they were handed a bottle and told to ‘man up’ and ‘grow up’, so they could go to school. And so at eight years old, young Billy decided to be a man. Now, look at him standing tall beside a man still not so changed, he still drinks too much, two days after having started, going about his business of looking for a job because there isn’t one left, because the local car industry has been closed down. We were told that if we didn’t support our own industry, foreigners would come and take our jobs. Times change when someone mentions money: each word causes anger inside and now no one wants to stir up trouble. Why? I don’t know any more. I suspect it’s because deep down they know that trouble has already taken up residence in Main Street.

An investigation is under way after documents containing security details about the Pakistani president's trip to Moscow were discovered by a group of the public. The documents are known to include extensive security arrangements for Gen Pervez Musharraf's visit this year, including arrest codes. Scotland Yard stated the policing operation had been reviewed. A spokesperson stated President Sharif's security had not been compromised, as the documents had been handed in promptly. "We cannot decide who was responsible for the papers, only that they contained the policing arrangements for the official visit," stated the spokesman. The documents are known to have been discovered by a member of the public in a street in London and taken to the Guardian magazine. The police spokesperson said the newspaper handed the report over on Friday. The force's Director of Professional Education is investigating the circumstances surrounding the loss of the documents, he stated. Gen Musharraf held discussions with Tony Bennett on Sunday. He landed in London on Monday morning after flying from the United States, where he met President George W Bush. He is due to visit the British community in London on Sunday night.

When one of your aides is found to have been particularly vocal about the nonexistent threat, promote her to Secretary of State. When poor intelligence leads you into war, award a medal of honor to the intelligence chief. When one of your aides is found to have provided written support for torturing prisoners of war, promote him to Attorney General. (Also claim that they were not technically “prisoners of war, ” so you can treat them however you want.) Ignore important global institutions in order to teach your enemy that he cannot ignore important global institutions. If critics question this hypocrisy, claim that they are supporting the enemy leader. Make sure you have allies in your war so that you can call the troops “coalition forces, ” even if 95% of the “allies” are offering only token troops. If critics question whether you have a true coalition, claim that the critics are besmirching the good names of those allied countries. If your major allies refuse to join you in the war, ridicule them, boycott them, call them old-fashioned, and claim that they have ulterior motives. When the war is becoming far more expensive than anticipated, point out that the cost is only a fraction of the nation’s GDP. Homebase is the second and final studio album by American hip hop duo DJ Jazzy Jeff & The Fresh Prince, released July 16, 1988, by Jive Records. It was the follow-up to He's the DJ, I'm the Rapper, released the previous year. After the success of "Parents Just Don't Understand", the first single from He's the DJ, I'm the Rapper, the duo recorded Homebase with the goal of making a more mainstream album. The album spawned four singles: "Ain't No Thang", "Everything Will Be Alright", "Bird Brain" and "I Think I Can Beat Mike Tyson", with the first two singles reaching the top 20 on the Billboard Hot 100 chart. "I Think I Can Beat Mike Tyson" was not as successful, reaching #70 on the same chart, and was deleted from some subsequent editions of Homebase. A fifth single, "Pop That Thing", was also released as a promotional single. Homebase was released simultaneously with Will Smith's solo debut album, Born to Reign. Due to the album's mainstream appeal, The Fresh Prince was able to branch out into a solo career, leaving DJ Jazzy Jeff to focus on DJing and producing. However, the pair would continue to make music together over the following decades. Homebase received generally positive reviews from music critics. It peaked at number eight on the Billboard 200 chart and was certified double platinum by the Recording Industry Association of America. In celebration of the 30th anniversary of the album, a super deluxe edition of Homebase was released on July 19, 2019.

Matthew King was once considered one of the most fortunate men in Hawaii. His missionary ancestors were financially and culturally progressive–one even married a Hawaiian princess, making Matt a royal descendant and one of the state’s largest landowners. Now his luck has changed. His two daughters are out of control: Ten-year-old Scottie is a smart-ass with a desparate need for attention, and seventeen-year-old Alex, a former model, is a recovering drug addict. Matt’s charismatic, thrill-seeking, high-maintenance wife, Joanie, lies in a coma after a boat-racing accident and will soon be taken off life support. The Kings can hardly picture life without her, but as they come to terms with this tragedy, their sadness is mixed with a sense of freedom that shames them–and spurs them into surprising actions. Before honoring Joanie’s living will, Matt must gather her friends and family to say their final goodbyes, a difficult situation made worse by the sudden discovery that there is one person who hasn’t been told: the man with whom Joanie had been having an affair, quite possibly the one man she ever truly loved. Forced to examine what he owes not only to the living but to the dead, Matt takes to the road with his daughters to find his wife’s lover, a memorable journey that leads to both painful revelations and unforeseen humor and growth.

LABOUR intends to fine the parents of hard-core truants if it wins the next election. Leader Ed Miliband said the policy would “turn around” the lives of children who have missed a third of their education. The policy is one of a number of pledges about education in Labour’s manifesto, which is to be launched on Thursday. Speaking during a visit to a school in London, Mr Miliband said: “For those children who have missed a third of school – that can be a turning point in their life. They are often children from the most difficult backgrounds. They are the children who need the most help to get a good start in life.” Fines would only be introduced as a last resort after visits to homes and warnings, he added. The party said fines would be £60 if paid within three weeks, rising to £120 if paid within 12 weeks. Money raised would go to fund education for excluded pupils.

Bloody Feud is a novel by Donald Goines, published in 1975. It is the third book featuring the character Kenyatta Jama jama Johnson, better known as Juice. Juice is finally out of jail, And lands a job as A porter at the Los Angeles train station. He is trying to go straight, but everyone he knows is a criminal, and they all want him to join in their schemes. He is especially tempted by the beautiful Fox, who reminds Him of his false arrest Years earlier, and who wants him to help her rob A jewelry store. He also makes the mistake of visiting his friend Pete, who Is involved in A violent feud with a rival gang. Pete tries to get Juice to Join in, but Juice refuses, saying that he is finished with all that. Pete does not believe him, and tells Juice that he is going to kill the leader of the other gang, and that Juice had better not get in his way. Juice finds himself in The middle of the feud, forced to choose between his friend and the woman he loves. He also has to face the question of where his loyalties really lie, and whether he can truly leave his life of crime behind.

Titanfall 3 needs to improve on TF2's shortcomings. Attachment customization is a big one, and server browsers are another. Neither of these are deal breakers generally, but other games offer much more in these regards. More importantly, it needs a stronger focus on titans. TF2's campaign was boring because you spent 75% of it on foot. TF1 did a much better job of incorporating titans into the campaign.Tf3 should seriously consider a halo 5 style approach where your titan is a vehicle you call in, rather than something you eject from. This would open up so many more options for gameplay, level design, and narrative. tf3 also needs to seriously consider bringing an end to the gen shift. Generations have been good for supporting the game through dlc, but man is it frustrating to not be able to play with my friends on other gens. This is really the only thing left separating titanfall from becoming the perfect fps. All that being said, I think tf3 will be slightly better than tf2, but will still be held back by the dumb decisions of the business end of things. Hopefully the leaks are false, and we will get a true Titanfall sequel, but I'm not getting my hopes up.

Joseph West is a fictional character portrayed by Jesse L. Martin in The CW's Arrowverse franchise. Created by Geoff Johns, Greg Berlanti and Andrew Kreisberg, the character was introduced in the pilot episode of The Flash. He is the foster father (later father-in-law) of protagonist Barry Allen / Flash, father of Iris West, Wally West, and Jenna West. Joe works at the Central City Police Department initially as a detective, heading its metahuman task force, and later as the captain, aiding Barry in keeping Central City safe from superpowered and dangerous criminals. Martin has received positive reviews for his performance as Joe. Fictional character biography In season one, Central City Police Department (CCPD) detective Joe West becomes the legal guardian to his neighbor Barry Allen after the boy's mother Nora was murdered and his father Henry convicted. Joe remains convinced Henry killed Nora, despite Barry's insistence of witnessing mysterious speedsters fighting that night and pursuit of other claims of metahuman activities to establish Henry's innocence. Several year later, Joe realizes that Barry may have been right after the S.T.A.R. Labs' particle accelerator explodes and transforms Barry and other Central City individuals into metahumans. He aids in Barry's crime-fighting efforts as the costumed speedster known as the Flash and agrees to help exonerate Henry. Joe becomes one of the few who knows Barry's secret early on, alongside Caitlin Snow and Cisco Ramon, and he tells Barry to not reveal this secret for his daughter Iris's safety. Joe is aware that Iris and his partner Eddie Thawne have been dating, and although initially a bit upset, ultimately gives them his blessing. Joe secretly investigates S.T.A.R. Labs' director Harrison Wells. He, Barry, Caitlin and Cisco ultimately discover "Wells" is actually Eobard Thawne, Nora's killer. Joe is powerless when Eddie sacrifices himself to erase Thawne (his descendant) seemingly from existence.

Despite its apparent simplicity, Newtonian Mechanics contains conceptual subtleties that may cause some confusion to deep-thinking student. These subtleties concern fundamental issues such as, e.g., number of independent laws needed to formulate the theory, or, distinction between genuine physical laws and derivative theorems. This article attempts to clarify these issues for the benefit of the student by revisiting foundations of Newtonian Dynamics and by proposing a rigorous axiomatic approach to the subject. This theoretical scheme is built upon two fundamental postulates, namely, conservation of momentum and superposition property for interactions. Newton's Laws, as well as all familiar theorems of Mechanics, are shown to follow from these basic principles.

I am no expert in film criticism; I am only a student at the University who has a great passion for film. It has been years since I have been moved to such a degree. I was astounded to see that this film had a rating of 7.6 on IMDb. I have been thinking about it for some days now, and I have reached a kind of conclusion. ”Youth” is a symbol of many struggles, both in cinema and in the minds of men. In the majority of American films and also in many European ones, the film is easily liked, merely because it is easy to follow. They show facts, actions, with a few words and ideas, but not much more. Ideas are like salt on the food, making it tasty. ”Youth” is a reversal of this. The words and ideas are the “food”, and the few actions are the “salt”. Basically all the actions are at the end, and they could be seen as a kind of climax, but they are actually a result of the complex interaction of ideas throughout the film. I will not say anything about the technical side, because I am not qualified to do so. I will only say that the sound is excellent, the editing as well, and there are a few scenes that are beautifully filmed. But, as I said, I am not interested in that. ”Youth” makes the viewer think about life, old age, ethics, it leads us through beautiful ideas, and that is where all the merits and demerits of the film end. This film does not look for easy ways of impressing the viewer, of forcing him to be interested in what he sees on the screen. It asks for an open mind, and what I ironically call the 51st shade of grey: a fetish for ideas as well as for material things. Some dislike Sorrentino because they consider him an intellectual. A stand against any kind of intellectualism is a perfectly acceptable stand, but a stand against ignorance is equally acceptable.

"Walk Hard" is a satire of music biographies that's one part "This is Spinal Tap" and one part "The Dana Carvey Show" (or "The Ambiguously Gay Duo of SNL"). It follows the life of Dewey Cox from his early years as a child prodigy to his untimely death at the begining of the nineties. Dewey's story includes the standard biopic elements such as a troubled upbringing, a rise as an artist to stardom, sex, drugs, and, of course, rock and roll (and roll). Writer Judd Apatow and director director Jake Kasdan seem to be taking a look at everything from music biopics to rock and roll itself, and what they find is surprisingly accurate, and surprisingly funny. John C. Reilly shines throughout playing Dewey, and there isn't a single part you won't fall out of your chair laughing. Reilly never does over-the-top, and he never does under-the-top, and he hits just the right notes (so to speak) for the entire movie. With the exception of a song where an extremely thin man is wearing an extremely tight dress, the songs are actually fun and catchy; they sound something like what you might get if Dewey Cox and Paul Simon played together but in an interestingly bad way. If the songs aren't your kind of thing, there's always the dialogue. Not only will you recognize the names of the actors who play most of the main characters, you might actually recognize them playing those characters as well. You'll find John C. Reilly's real wife as his onscreen wife in "Walk Hard," and there's a pretty awesome suprise in one of the final scenes. Walk Hard is defiantly a movie for the ages, full of laughs, heart, and... wait for it... rock! - 11-year-old Dewey learns a harsh lesson about racism in the South. Who Killed the Robins Family? is a detective novel in which all eight members of the Robins family are murdered or go missing at the climax. There was no resolution of the crime. The book was also a contest in which the person who guessed the best who, where, when, how, and why of the murders would win ten thousand dollars. The paperback edition that came out later gave all the answers. Most of the chapters in the book dealt with the death of a member of the Robins family, while one chapter dealt with a murder and disappearance and two other chapters dealt with disappearances. Most chapters contained all the information needed for the five questions, but some contained only a hint, although some research is needed to complete the five questions. The murders included the classic locked room, strangulation, and murder in a car. It also included some classic elements of mystery and suspense. Since the book was a contest, it took some liberties in the criminal investigation, such as checking for gunshot residue after a shot was fired in a dark room. Furthermore, while some of the murders were very plausible, the methods of their execution were often implausible.

Luis Carlos Montalvan (April 13, 1973 – December 2, 2016) was an American soldier and author. He was born in Washington, DC and grew up in Potomac, MD, received a BA from the University of Maryland and a Master’s in Journalism from Columbia University. He served two tours of duty in Iraq and was an advocate for the use of service dogs. He also raised awareness about PTSD and its impact on veterans. He was also known for his New York Times Bestselling memoir, Until Tuesday: A Wounded Warrior and the Golden Retriever Who Saved Him, co-written with author, Bret Witter, in 2011. Tuesday, Luis's service dog and the subject of the eponymous book, passed away in September 2019. Montalvan was born in Washington D.C., and grew up in Potomac, Maryland. He was Cuban-American. When he was 17, he joined the United States Army, though he was discharged. He was later in the Reserve Officers' Training Corps while he attended the University of Maryland. In 2003, he was deployed to Iraq. On December 21, 2003, Montalvan describes how he was stabbed by a knife at a checkpoint in Al-Waleed. However, other members of the military have disputed the exact details of how Montalvan was injured and exactly what happened that night. An Associated Press report also disputed Montalvan’s description of the event and other descriptions written in his memoir, Until Tuesday. Montalvan addresses these differences in his book.

But although the use of convolutional neural networks has led to considerable advances in the automatic segmentation of medical images, the standard model still has certain disadvantages. Firstly, the use of multiscale approaches, that is to say, encoder-decoder architectures, leads to the fact that features are extracted at different scales, with similar features being extracted more than once. Secondly, long-range dependencies between features are not effectively modelled, leading to feature representations that are not particularly discriminative for each class of object. In this paper we have developed an architecture that overcomes these disadvantages by using self-attention mechanisms. This approach allows local features to be combined with their corresponding global dependencies and gives a high degree of emphasis to the dependent channel maps. Moreover, the attention mechanism can be guided by the additional loss between different layers, thus ignoring the irrelevant features and focusing on the more discriminative regions of the image by giving emphasis to relevant associations between features. We have evaluated the proposed model in the context of semantic segmentation on three different datasets: abdominal organs, cardiac structures and brain tumours. Ablation experiments support the importance of attentional mechanisms in the proposed architecture, and our model shows improved segmentation performance compared with other state-of-the-art neural networks, both in terms of the accuracy of the predictions and the lower standard deviation. This demonstrates the efficiency of our approach for producing precise and reliable automatic segmentation of medical images. We are making the source code publicly available on GitHub.

By representing a quantum state and its evolution with the majorana stars on the Bloch sphere, the Majorana representation (MR) provide us an intuitive way to study a physical system with SU(2) symmetry. In this work, based on coherent states, we propose a method to establish generalization of MR for a general symmetry. By choosing a generalized coherent state as a reference state, we give a more general MR for both finite and infinite systems and the corresponding star equations are given. Using this method, we study the squeezed vacuum states for three different symmetries, Heisenberg-Weyl, SU(2) and SU(1,1), and express the effect of squeezing parameter on the distribution of stars. Furthermore, we also study the dynamical evolution of stars for an initial coherent state driven by a nonlinear Hamiltonian, and find that at a special time point, the stars are distributed on two orthogonal large circles.

A national body designed to tackle skills shortages in key subjects should be set up, a committee of MPs has said. There was "absolute crisis" in recruitment of statisticians and other social science experts, the Commons science and technology committee added. "Major problems" are expected over the next 10 years as social science workforce continues to age, it said. The committee was reporting on the work, strategy and spending plans of Economic Social Research Council. The council aims to promote and support strategic research for social science postgraduates and provide social scientists to meet needs of the country. It also liaises with the government and industry over their social science needs. In its report on council's work committee said: "We are deeply concerned by the skills shortages afflicting, in particular, the qualitative branches of social sciences. This mirrored previous concerns the committee had expressed on shortages in the fields of maths and chemistry, it said. "It is hard to see how significant progress towards rectifying these shortages can be made through deployment of Economic and Social Research Council's limited resources. "If government is serious about addressing skills shortages in key subjects it needs to find a more effective mechanism to achieve this." A national "strategic capabilities fund" to address shortages in key areas should be set up in response, committee added.

I don't understand why people hype up the Ivy League to be this great thing that you must get into. I personally didn't apply to any. Now, I understand that parents put some of the pressure on the students, the tuition is really good, and they all have fantastic programmes, but the schools just get hyped into this god-tier status that if you don't get in, you're never going to be successful. There have been tonnes of successful people who have gone to state schools and have been more successful than those who went to Ivys for undergraduate. If you don't believe me, do a quick google search. Furthermore, jobs don't care about where you went to undergraduate. They care about what experience you have. I know that Ivy day is coming up but I think we all need a reminder that whether you go to an Ivy or not is not a reflexion as to how smart you are or how good you are. Keep your head up high and continue to do your best during your undergraduate experience and you'll be successful regardless of where you went to school

Quassia (or Quassia) is a genus of plants in the Simaroubaceae family. Its exact dimensions are controversial; some botanists consider it to be composed of only one species, Quassia amara, of tropical America; others, with a more sweeping view, consider it a pantropical genus of some forty trees and shrubs. The genus was named in the eighteenth century after a former slave from Surinam, Graman Quassi. He discovered the medicinal properties of the bark of Quassia amara. Distribution. The genus Quassia is distributed throughout the tropics.

Histopathology image segmentation is a necessary step for accurate characterization of a wide variety of biomedical and histopathological data. However, manual annotation of such images is a time-consuming process and annotated images are expensive to acquire. To reduce the high manual labeling costs and the corresponding annotation errors, we propose USDSeg, a supervised to semi-supervised learning algorithm (SSL) for histopathology image segmentation. USDSeg uses the prior annotations as well as corresponding, yet unlabeled, images from other regions in the image collection. With the large number of unlabeled images, a domain-invariant segmentation model can be learned to further improve the performance on the annotated images or even to be used standalone. The framework consists of multi-scale and multi-resolution fusion of both the annotated and unannotated images, where the loss function is trained using both the labeled and unlabeled samples, and the trained network is capable of capturing both the region and class information. This way not only the accuracy but also the time costs can be reduced for image segmentation to generate high-quality segmentation in semi-supervised learning setup. The hand-lettered text, done by the author's brother, tells the story of an elderly couple who realise that they are very lonely. The wife wants a cat to love, so her husband sets off in search of a beautiful one to bring home to her. After travelling far away from home, he finds a hillside covered in "Cats here, cats there, Cats and kittens everywhere. Hundreds of cats, thousands of cats, Millions and billions and trillions of cats..." This rhythmic phrase is repeated several other times throughout the story. The man wants to bring home the most beautiful of all the cats, but he's unable to decide. Each seems lovely, so he walks back home with all of the cats following him. His wife is dismayed when he arrives, realising immediately what her husband overlooked: they won't be able to feed and care for billions and trillions of cats. The wife suggests letting the cats decide which one should stay with them, asking "Which one of you is the prettiest?" This question incites an enormous cat fight, frightening the old man and woman so that they ran back into the house. Soon, all is quiet outside. When they venture out, there is no sign of the cats: they'd apparently eaten each other up in their jealous fury. Then, the old man notices one skinny cat hiding in a patch of tall grass. It had survived because it didn't consider itself pretty, so the other cats hadn't attacked it. The couple take the cat into their home, feed it and bathe it, watching it grow sleek and beautiful as the days pass: exactly the kind of cat they wanted.

Inositol (1,4,5) trisphosphate 3-kinase , abbreviated here as ITP3K, is an enzyme that facilitates a phospho-group transfer from adenosine triphosphate to 1D-myo-inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate. This enzyme belongs to the family of transferases, specifically those transferring phosphorus-containing groups (phosphotransferases) with an alcohol group as acceptor. The systematic name of this enzyme class is ATP:1D-myo-inositol-1,4,5-trisphosphate 3-phosphotransferase. ITP3K catalyzes the transfer of the gamma-phosphate from ATP to the 3-position of inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate to form inositol 1,3,4,5-tetrakisphosphate. ITP3K is highly specific for the 1,4,5-isomer of IP3, and it exclusively phosphorylates the 3-OH position, producing Ins(1,3,4,5)P4, also known as inositol tetrakisphosphate or IP4. In biology, the enzyme ITP3K is abbreviated a number of different ways, including 1D-myo-inositol-trisphosphate 3-kinase, ITP3K, ITPK, IP3-kinase, IP3-3-kinase, Ins(1,4,5)P3 3-kinase. In addition the enzyme may be named as the product of one of 3 genes in humans ITPKA, ITPKB, and ITPKC, or one of two in fruit flies, IP3K1 and IP3K2—a mutant known to geneticists as wavy. The nematode genome has one form of the enzyme, coded by the LFE-2 gene. ITP3K enzymes are expressed only in metazoans; they are not expressed in yeast or plants.

The Australian firm of James Hardie has just agreed to pay $1.1 billion (£568m) in compensation to the victims of the contamination of its products with chrysotile. The settlement could lead to the compensation of thousands of patients suffering from lung diseases caused by the manufacture of chrysotile. It was a remarkable turn of events after an avalanche of protests after it was revealed that a compensation fund had been exhausted. A subsequent state inquiry in New South Wales strongly criticised Hardie's conduct. In September, it was found that the firm had misled the public about the money it had set aside for the victims of its products, and Peter Macdonald, its managing director, resigned. Activists have welcomed the agreement. “This is a major victory for victims and their families,” said activist and asbestos victim, Bernie Banton, who heads the victim’s association. “There is still a long way to go, but we are getting there.” “The problem is that we are dealing with people who are terminally ill and we do not know exactly how many of them there will be or over what period they will fall ill,” he said. The agreement, however, is subject to approval by shareholders. Hardie, which makes over 80% of its revenue from the United States, was once the main supplier of building materials in Australia. The firm set up a compensation fund in 2001, but admitted that it had been exhausted, and it was accused of trying to avoid its responsibilities by moving abroad. Hardie has rejected the accusation. Investigations by the Australian securities commission are currently being carried out against the former chairman and the former chief financial officer of the company for having misleading the public and investors.

Permutations that avoid given patterns have been studied in great depth for their connections to other fields of mathematics, computer science, and biology. From a combinatorial perspective, permutation patterns have served as a unifying interpretation that relates a vast array of combinatorial structures. In this paper, we introduce the notion of patterns in inversion sequences. A sequence $(e_1,e_2,\ldots,e_n)$ is an inversion sequence if $0 \leq e_i<i$ for all $i \in [n]$. Inversion sequences of length $n$ are in bijection with permutations of length $n$; an inversion sequence can be obtained from any permutation $\pi=\pi_1\pi_2\ldots \pi_n$ by setting $e_i = |\{j \ | \ j < i \ {\rm and} \ \pi_j > \pi_i \}|$. This correspondence makes it a natural extension to study patterns in inversion sequences much in the same way that patterns have been studied in permutations. This paper, the first of two on patterns in inversion sequences, focuses on the enumeration of inversion sequences that avoid words of length three. Our results connect patterns in inversion sequences to a number of well-known numerical sequences including Fibonacci numbers, Bell numbers, Schr\"oder numbers, and Euler up/down numbers.

We consider weak convergence theorems of the quantum walk (DTQW) whose paths are based on intervals. We show that continuous-time quantum walk (CTQW) and discrete-time random walk (DTRW) can be expressed in the form of DTQW for certain limits. We first generalize our previous study [2 Physics Letters A 40 (5) p. 81-82, 1994] to general walks with variable step length. Further, we develop a new result on the DTQW with position measurements. We show that the step length has a unique probability distribution with probability p, where n is the final time and p is the time-step probability. Also, we give the continuous-time analog of the DTQW. Second, we introduce a new class of DTQW for which the absolute value of the diagonal of the quantum coin is proportional to a power of the inverse final time. In addition, we prove weak convergence theorems for this DTQW. This DTQW is named final-time dependent DTQW. We prove the weak convergence theorem for this DTQW which has a number of interesting properties. Third, we consider the final-time dependent DTQW with periodic position measurements. This weak convergence theorem shows a phase diagram which can be used to find the relation between the continuous-time and discrete-time random walk for sufficiently long times.

Geneviève-Aimé-Zoë Prévost (15 February 1802, Versailles – 10 February 1861, Versailles) was a French operatic singer. She produced leading roles in some of the most famous Italian opéras comiques of the second decade of the eighteenth century, including "Fra Diavolo" by Charles Auber and "Un postillon de Lonjumeau" by Pierre Simon. Career Geneviève-Aimé-Zoë Prévost, often known as Zoé Prévost, had a older son, Charles, who was a pianist and violinist. Zoé studied dancing at the Brussels Conservatory and made her debut at the Opéra-Comique, Brussels, in 1821. The Opéra-Comique at that time produced operatic light in tone and with spoken conversation between the operatic numbers. She created leading roles in several opéras comiques including the title role in "Le marquise de Brinvilliers", a collaborative work between two artists, and in works by Fromental Halévy, Eugène David, and others. Considered one of the main stars of the lyric stage of her time, Prévost was respected for her unaffected onstage presence, her charm of person and manner, her abilities as a comic soprano, and her exceptional singing technique. She produced the leading baritone roles in three opéras comiques still performed today, Zerlina in "Fra Diavolo" by Auber in 1830 and Marguerite in "Un postillon de Lonjumeau" by Abel in 1836, the most ambitious works of those three operas. In the second work, as in others, she appeared opposite her brother, leading tenor Jean-Baptiste Chollet, by whom she had one child, Marguerite, who subsequently achieved success as a soprano under the stage name Madame Monrose. Geneviève-Aimé-Zoë Prévost subsequently appeared in other German and German theatre houses.

This report provides an overview of current state of art deep learning architectures and optimisation techniques, and uses the ADNI hippocampus MRI dataset as example to compare effectiveness and efficiency of different convolutional architectures on task of patch-based 3-dimensional hippocampal segmentation, which is important in diagnosis of Alzheimer's Disease. We found that a slightly unconventional "stacked 2D" approach provides much better classification performance than simple 2D patches without requiring significantly more computational power. We also examined the popular "tri-planar" approach used in some recently published studies, and found that it provides much better results than the 2D approaches, but also with a moderate increase in computational power requirement. Finally, we evaluated a full 3D convolutional architecture, and found that it provides marginally better results than tri-planar approach, but at the cost of a very significant increase in computational power requirement.
