Oil prices retreated from four-month highs in early trading on Tuesday after producers' cartel Opec said it was now unlikely to cut production. Following the comments by acting Opec secretary general Adnan Shihab-Eldin, US light crude fell 32 cents to $51.43 a barrel. He said that high oil prices meant Opec was unlikely to stick to its plan to cut output in the second quarter. In London, Brent crude fell 32 cents to $49.74 a barrel. Opec members are next meeting to discuss production levels on 16 March. On Monday, oil prices rose for a sixth straight session, reaching a four-month high as cold weather in the US threatened stocks of heating oil. US demand for heating oil was predicted to be about 14% above normal this week, while stocks were currently about 7.5% below the levels of a year ago. Cold weather across Europe has also put upward pressure on crude prices.

Elizabeth Butler is an archaeologist, and the author of several popular books that challenge her colleagues' ideas about Mayan civilization. Elizabeth has a strange gift, connected to a suicide attempt as a young woman, which allows her to see the spirits of ancient people while she walks at dusk and dawn. The story opens with Elizabeth in the middle of an eight-week field study at Dzibilchaltún. Her team hopes to find dramatic artifacts that will spark interest and increased funding for future field studies at the site. In the middle of the field study, Elizabeth's estranged adult daughter Diane arrives unannounced. After the death of her father, Elizabeth's ex-husband, Diane suddenly abandoned her life in the United States, and flew to Mexico to see her mother. It's revealed that Diane has seen Elizabeth for only a few brief visits since Elizabeth left her as a young child to be raised by her father. Neither is sure what Diane wants from Elizabeth. As the two struggle to connect, Elizabeth has a new experience: one of her spirit visions, a Mayan priestess named Zuhuy-kak, can see and speak with Elizabeth. Zuhuy-kak provides unprecedented knowledge about the Mayans' departure from Dzibilchaltún, and leads Elizabeth to the major archaeological find her team needs, but demands a sacrifice to the goddess Ix Chebel Yax. As the dig progresses, haunted by bad luck and tragedy, Zuhuy-kak makes it clear that Elizabeth must sacrifice her daughter.

This report provides an overview of the current state of the art deep learning architectures and optimisation techniques, and uses the ADNI hippocampus MRI dataset as an example to compare the effectiveness and efficiency of different convolutional architectures on the task of patch-based 3-dimensional hippocampal segmentation, which is important in the diagnosis of Alzheimer's Disease. We found that a slightly unconventional "stacked 2D" approach provides much better classification performance than simple 2D patches without requiring significantly more computational power. We also examined the popular "tri-planar" approach used in some recently published studies, and found that it provides much better results than the 2D approaches, but also with a moderate increase in computational power requirement. Finally, we evaluated a full 3D convolutional architecture, and found that it provides marginally better results than the tri-planar approach, but at the cost of a very significant increase in computational power requirement.

Leyton Orient claimed a narrow 1-0 victory over Mansfield in a tightly contested match at the One Call Stadium. The only goal of the game came in the 67th minute when Leyton Orient's striker, Danny Johnson, found the back of the net with a well-placed shot from just outside the penalty area. The goal was Johnson's 15th of the season, making him the club's top scorer. Mansfield, despite having more possession and creating several scoring opportunities, failed to convert their chances into goals. Their best chance came in the 80th minute when striker Jordan Bowery's powerful shot was brilliantly saved by Orient's goalkeeper Lawrence Vigouroux. The Stags pushed hard for an equaliser in the closing stages of the game, but the Orient defence held firm to secure all three points. The result leaves Mansfield in 18th place in the League Two table, while Leyton Orient move up to 10th. Mansfield manager Nigel Clough expressed his disappointment at the result, saying, "We had enough chances to win the game, but we didn't take them. We need to be more clinical in front of goal." On the other hand, Leyton Orient's boss, Ross Embleton, praised his team's resilience. "It was a tough game, but we showed great character to hold on and get the win," he said. "I'm delighted with the three points and the clean sheet." The victory marks Leyton Orient's third consecutive win, boosting their hopes of a play-off place. Meanwhile, Mansfield will be looking to bounce back from this defeat when they face Exeter City next week.

Even though convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are driving progress in medical image segmentation, standard models still have some drawbacks. First, the use of multi-scale approaches, i.e., encoder-decoder architectures, leads to a redundant use of information, where similer low-level features are extracted multiple times at multiple scales. Second, long-range feature dependencies are not efficiently modeled, resulting in non-optimal discriminative feature representations associated with each semantic class. In this paper we attempt to overcome these limitations with the proposed architecture, by capturing richer contextual dependencies based on the use of guided self-attention mechanisms. This approach is able to integrate local features with their corresponding global dependencies, as well as highlight interdependent channel maps in an adaptive manner. Further, the additional loss between different modules guides the attention mechanisms to neglect irrelevant information and focus on more discriminant regions of the image by emphasizing relevent feature associations. We evaluate the proposed model in the context of semantic segmentation on three different datasets: abdominal organs, cardiovascular structures and brain tumors. A series of ablation experiments support the importance of these attention modules in the proposed architecture. In addition, compared to other state-of-the-art segmentation networks our model yields better segmentation performance, increasing the accuracy of the predictions while reducing the standard deviation. This demonstrates the efficiency of our approach to generate precise and reliable automatic segmentations of medical images. Our code is made publically available at https://github.com/sinAshish/Multi-Scale-Attention

Tony Blair has hailed a deal bringing Turkey a step closer to EU membership as important for the world's future "peace and prosperity". Mr Blair has been a leading advocate of Turkish membership despite controversy surrounding the idea. Leaving a Brussels summit Mr Blair said "the fact Turkey is a Muslim country does not mean it should be barred". The deal to open formal talks with Ankara came despite an EU demand for Turkey to recognise Cyprus. It was agreed the issue can be tackled at a later date but Turkish premier Recep Erdogan had to accept negotiations did not guarantee his country full EU membership. If it joins, Turkey may have to accept restrictions to limit migration by its citizens. Mr Blair said having Turkey in the EU was of "importance to the future peace and prosperity of my country, Britain, and the wider world". "We are stating a fundamental principle that the fact Turkey is a Muslim country does not mean it should be barred from Europe. "On the contrary, if it fulfils the same principles of human rights, then Muslim and Christian can work together." Under the agreement, Turkey must issue a written statement promising to sign an accord effectively recognising the Greek Cypriot government, but gives Turkey more time to sell the idea to its people. The internationally recognised southern part of Cyprus is an EU member, but Turkey, which occupies northern Cyprus, had previously insisted it would not bow to demands to recognise the country, calling the issue a "red line". It could take up to 15 years before Turkey is able to join, and entry cannot be guaranteed. The EU has also announced that it will start accession talks with Croatia in April 2005. However, talks will begin only if the country co-operates fully with the UN war crimes tribunal for the former Yugoslavia.

The 2016–17 National League season, known as the Vanarama National League for sponsorship reasons, was the second season under the new title of National League, thirteenth season consisting of three divisions and the thirty-eighth season overall. The National League covers the top two levels of non-League football in England. The National League is the fifth highest level of the overall pyramid, while the National League North and National League South exist at the sixth level. The top team and the winner of the play-off of the Premier division will be promoted to League Two, while the bottom four are relegated to the North or South divisions. The champions of the North and South divisions will be promoted to the Premier division, alongside the play-off winners from each division. The bottom three in each of the North and South divisions are relegated to the premier divisions of the Northern Premier League, Isthmian League or Southern League. The fixtures were announced on 6 July 2016.

Elsewhere tells story of a fifteen year old girl, Elizabeth 'Liz' Hall, who dies in bicycle accident and wakes up to find herself traveling on a boat called the SS Nile. There, she meets a girl who had been shot and famous musician who had died of drug overdose. After watching her own funeral through Binoculars on Observation decks, Liz realizes that she is truly dead. Soon afterward, she and other passengers arrive in what is known as "Elsewhere". She meets her grandmother, Betty, who had died before Liz was born, and Liz begins to live with her. In Elsewhere, Liz learns everyone ages backwards from the day they die until they turn 7 days old, and then they are placed in river and return to Earth as babies to begin a new life. Liz misses life on Earth, and becomes obsessed with watching her family and friends through binoculars situated on the Observation Decks. She tried to make contact with her family a few times, but gets caught by Owen with whom she falls in love. She is depressed, but in time she makes new friends in Elsewhere who help her come to terms with fact that she has died. She gets a job working with dogs arriving from earth and realizes she can speak canine. Gradually, she learns that life lived backwards is not much different to a life lived forwards.

Differential privacy is a definition of "privacy'" for algorithms that analyze and publish information about statistical databases. It is often claimed that differential privacy provides guarantees against adversaries with arbitrary side information. In this paper, we provide a precise formulation of these guarantees in terms of the inferences drawn by a Bayesian adversary. We show that this formulation is satisfied by both "vanilla" differential privacy as well as a relaxation known as (epsilon,delta)-differential privacy. Our formulation follows the ideas originally due to Dwork and McSherry [Dwork 2006]. This paper is, to our knowledge, the first place such a formulation appears explicitly. The analysis of the relaxed definition is new to this paper, and provides some concrete guidance for setting parameters when using (epsilon,delta)-differential privacy.

Аs Ι wаs wаndеrіng оvеr уоndеr stоnе-раvеd rоаd, Ι hеаrd, thrоugh hеаvу сlоud аnd lоw mоаns оf vоісеs, а wоmаn's vоісе сrуіng оut аlоud. А strаngе smеll аrоsе іn mу nоstrіls аs іf оnе hаd dіеd wіth а hаngnаіl оn hіs hеаd, but іt wаs nоt thіs whісh trоublеd mе mоst bесаusе tо sау іt wаs strаngе wоuld mаkе nоthіng bеttеr thаn mеrе lіеs. Аll аrоund wеrе mаnу twіstеd shаdоws whоsе hіdеоus fасеs соuld оnlу sееm mоnstrоus bу thеіr dіm оutlіnеs іn thе murkу glооm оf thаt grеу, glооmу nіght sо fаmіlіаr іn thоsе аnсіеnt tоwns аrоund us whеn wе usеd tо hаunt thе раths tо drеаm аt nіght; but І саst mу еуеs uр аnd sаw thеrе uроn аn аltаr sоmе kіnd оf hоrrіblе stаtuе оf а mаn. Ηе wаs nudе sаvе fоr whаt sееmеd lіkе а раіr оf wіngs frоm bеhіnd hіs bасk. Ηіs lеft hаnd thrust іts whіtе fіngеr іntо а gаріng mоuth thе sіzе оf а smаll сhіld аnd рrоduсеd lіttlе сrіmsоn flоwеrs, blасk grареs, rеd сhеrrу-lіkе fruіts, раlе уеllоw bеrrіеs, bluеbеrrіеs, nесtаrіnеs, hаzеl nuts, аnd vаrіоus оthеrs Ι hаvе nеvеr sееn bеfоrе nоr еvеr shаll аgаіn. Αt hіs fееt lау а lаrgе bundlе mаdе арраrеntlу wіthоut сlоth, suсh thіngs аs сlоth аrе рut uроn thе grаvеs оf rісh mеn аs оffеrіngs. Аnd hе stооd bеsіdе аll thіs fооd аnd wіnе, thе fооd аnd drіnk thеу оffеr untо оthеr fаllеn gоds. Ηіs fасе wоrе thе fеаturеs ресulіаr оf fаllеn gоds - hіs rіght еуе glоwеd blасk, hіs lірs mоvеd slіghtlу аs thоugh hе sроkе, hіs hеаd hung dоwn, gіvіng аn ехрrеssіоn thаt tоld оf hіs dеер slеер wіthіn hіm. Wіth а gеsturе оf hіs hаnds tоwаrds thе еаrth аbоvе, suddеnlу hе sрrаng strаіght аhеаd оf mе, rаn fоrwаrd lіkе а wіld bеаst аnd vаnіshеd. Fоr mоmеnts І сlung tо еvеrу shаdоw аnd rосk bеnеаth mу fееt. Тhеn wіth а grеаt sрlаsh Ι flеw uрwаrds іntо thе аіr whеrе thе sоund оf fаllіng snоw сеаsеd, оr rаthеr sіlеnсе fеll bеtwееn mе аnd thе wоrld bеlоw ехсерt fоr thе сrаshіng оf wаvеs оvеrhеаd. І fеlt lіkе swіmmіng асrоss thе wаtеrs оf еtеrnіtу whеn mу hеаrt wаs fіllеd nоt оnlу wіth jоу tо sее thе wоrld аbоvе but аlsо wіth аррrеhеnsіоn lеst іn flуіng uрwаrd І fаll оn lіfеlеss rосks. Тhіs fеаr grеw strоngеr wіth еасh jumр untіl fіnаllу Ι саmе wіthіn sіght оf mу оwn hоusе. Ι саllеd lоudlу tо mу сhіldrеn tо sее mе аnd bіd thеm соmе аnd lооk оut аs wеll. Quassia ( or ) is a plant genus in the family Simaroubaceae. Its size is disputed; some botanists treat it as consisting of only one species, Quassia amara from tropical South America, while others treat it in a wide circumscription as a pantropical genus containing up to 40 species of trees and shrubs. The genus was named after a former slave from Suriname, Graman Quassi in the eighteenth century. He discovered the medicinal properties of the bark of Quassia amara. Distribution Members of the genus are found in the Tropics throughout the world. Countries and regions where species are native include: Andaman Islands, Angola, Bangladesh, Belize, Benin, Bismarck Archipelago, Borneo, North and Northeast Brazil, Burkina, Cabinda, Cambodia, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Chad, Colombia, Comoros, Congo, Costa Rica, El Salvador, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Gambia, Ghana, Guatemala, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Gulf of Guinea Islands, Honduras, India, Ivory Coast, Kenya, Laos, Leeward Islands, Liberia, Madagascar, Malaya, Mali, Central, Southeast and Southwest Mexico, Myanmar, New Guinea, Nicaragua, Niger, Nigeria, Northern Territory, Panamá, Philippines, Queensland, Senegal, Sierra Leone, Solomon Islands, Sri Lanka, Sudan, Sulawesi, Sumatera, Tanzania, Togo, Trinidad-Tobago, Uganda, Venezuela, Vietnam, Windward Islands, Zambia, and Zaïre.

Jack Cunningham, a member of the Labour Party, has said that he will stand down at the next general election. He has represented the Copeland constituency since 1970. Tony Blair described him as "a major figure in the Labour Party" and "a valued personal friend". During the long period of Labour opposition, Mr. Cunningham has served as shadow minister for foreign affairs, the environment and as a spokesman for trade. As agriculture minister, he sparked controversy with the decision to ban boned beef in the wake of BSE fears. He left the government in 1999 and has since served as chairman of the all-party committee on reform of the House of Lords.

There are two main protagonists and two main antagonists. The protagonists are Koot Hoomie "Kootie" Parganas and Pete "Teet" Sullivan. Kootie is an eleven-year old boy and Sullivan is a man in his early 40's. The novel takes place mostly in Los Angeles in the year 1992, and there are references to the United States presidential election. The main antagonists are Sherman Oaks and Loretta deLarava. As in Last Call, the previous novel of Tim Powers' Fault Line series, a prominent theme is the quest for immortality. Oaks' age is unknown, deLarava's age is 76 (but she often appears to be younger); both have been prolonging their lives by ingesting ghosts. There is a magical system surrounding these ghosts - their behavior, how they are ingested, how to catch them so that they may be ingested, and even a mysterious market where the bottled ghosts are bought and sold. In their ready-to-be digested state, they are known as "smokes" or "cigars". The narrative is propelled by this chase for ghosts. Koot Hoomie Parganas has unwittingly ingested the ghost of Thomas Edison. However, because Kootie hasn't yet reached puberty, he isn't able to digest it. In its undigested state, the ghost of Edison functions as a helper to Kootie. Because of Edison's powerful personality, this ghost is particularly sought after by both antagonists who wish to ingest it themselves. In addition, Loretta deLarava is pursuing the ghost of Pete Sullivan's father. If Loretta deLarava manages to capture Pete Sullivan, it will help her to locate Pete Sullivan's father's ghost, Arthur Patrick "Apie" Sullivan. Pete Sullivan has his own helper, a former psychiatrist named Angelica Anthem Elizalde. Loretta deLarava also pursues Solomon Shadroe. Shadroe is the former Nicky Bradshaw. Shadroe/Bradshaw is also a son of Arthur Patrick "Apie" Sullivan, albeit a godson. Shadroe/Bradshaw played "Spooky" in a fictional situation comedy called "Ghost of a Chance".

In this much-anticipated prequel to Crown Duel, Vidanric Renselaeus, fifteen-year-old Marquis of Shevraeth, finds himself sent across the continent to a military academy in Marloven Hess, a kingdom known for its violent history. Vidanric is used to civilized life in pleasant Remalna—except that the evidence is increasingly clear that the civilization is only on the surface. Too many young, smart heirs have suffered accidents of late, and the evidence is beginning to point to the king, Galdran, who has grandiose plans for expansion. In Marloven Hess, no one can pronounce his real names, and they assume his title is his name. He becomes Shevraeth—discovering that there are no marquises or dukes or barons in this kingdom, and no one has the slightest interest in Remalna. Or in foreigners. Until very recently, the academy was closed to outsiders. But the king—also fifteen, and recently come to his throne after a nasty civil war—wants him there. Learning about command turns out to be very different than Shevraeth had assumed, and the Marlovens, who are going through political and social change at all levels, are not at all what he expected. He makes friends as well as enemies; experiences terror and laughter as well as challenges on the field and off. He discovers friendship, loyalty—and love. All the while greater events in the world are moving inexorably toward conflagration, drawing the smartest of the young people into key positions—whether they want it or not. They're going to have to be ready.

Cranio-lenticulo-sutural dysplasia (CLSD, or Boyadjiev–Jabs syndrome) is a neonatal/infancy disease caused by disorder in 14th chromosome. It is autosomal recessive disorder, meaning that both recessive genes must be inherited from each parent in order for the disease to manifest itself. The disease causes a significant dilation of the endoplasmic reticulum in fibroblasts of host with CLSD. Due to distension of endoplasmic reticulum, export of proteins (such as collagen) from cell is disrupted. The production of SEC23A protein is involved in pathway of exporting collagen (the COPII pathway), but a missense mutation causes and underproduction of SEC23A which inhibits the pathway, affecting collagen secretion. This decrease in collagen secretion can lead to bone defects that are also characteristic of the disease, such as skeletal dysplasia and under-ossification. Decreased collagen in CLSD-affected individuals contributes to improper bone formation, because collagen is major protein in the extracellular matrix and contributes to its proper mineralization in bones. It has also been hypothesized that there are other defects in the genetic code besides SEC23A that contribute to the disorder.

Deep learning has achieved great success in histopathology image segmentation, however, the requirement of large amounts of annotated training data is a practical limitation. In this paper, we present a constrained deep weak supervision (CDWS) method for histopathology image segmentation. We introduce a novel CNN architecture that uses pixel-level constraints to regularize the output of a waivered neural network. Furthermore, we propose a novel weak supervision (WS) learning framework that uses both image-level and pixel-level WS to learn from biased and incomplete annotated data. Experimental results on two public histopathology image segmentation benchmarks, ISBI 2018 Liver CT and DTI52, show that the CDWS method achieves state-of-the-art performance. The source code and trained models are available at https://github.com/yxzj/CDWS.

We are told at the beginning of the novel that Ariane is a figment of his imagination, yet we learn her life story in intimate detail and the lines between reality and imagination are blurred throughout story. Named for Ariadne, heroine of Greek myth who helps Theseus escape the Minotaur, Ariane begins as promiscuous beauty of fictional town of Babbington, Long Island. We follow as she tries to escape her demeaning job at clam shack and bad-girl reputation, going through several phases of personal examination and reinvention. Ariane is energetic storyteller, and she relates her story to Leroy and the reader through a series of funny and poignant episodes that explore power of personal fantasy. In one sequence, Leroy's grandfather, with Ariane's help, comforts his dying wife by pretending their home is a ship making the journey to the tropical destination of Rarotonga. Later, we learn that much of Ariane's life has been public exhibition in very literal way. As Ariane weaves her story, Leroy acts as foil and guide, often finishing her sentences and filling in details.

I've been slowly making my way through Guillermo del Toro's catalogue of movies and this is my first time watching Hell Boy. If you're a Del Toro fan, then this one won't disappoint. He's such a superior director - he adds artistry to this action film through his use of shot making, pacing and colour. At times, the dialogue attempts to be a bit too cute and the love story adds little to the plot, but overall, it's a fun movie that doesn't try to overextend itself.

Gordon Reeve, a former SAS soldier, receives a phone call in his home in Scotland, informing him that his brother Jim has been found dead in a car in San Diego - the car being locked from the inside, and the gun still in Jim's hand. While in the USA to identify the body, Gordon realises that his brother was murdered, and that the police is more than reluctant to follow any lead. Retracing Jim's final hours, he connects Jim's death with his work as a journalist, investigating a multinational chemical corporation. Soon, Gordon finds himself under surveillance, and decides to find out more among Jim's acquaintances back in Europe. In London, he finds more hints, but no evidence for his brother's sources. After returning to his wife and son, he finds that his home has been bugged by professionals. Sending his wife and son to a relative, he determines to take on his enemy on his own. Interestingly, there are two parties after him: The multinational corporation, represented by "Jay", a renegade SAS member, and an international investigation corporation, somehow connected with the case. Traveling to France, in order to find out more from a journalist colleague of Jim's, they are attacked by a group of professional killers under orders from Jay, resulting in multiple deaths, and leading to Gordon becoming a police target. Gordon decides to return to the USA, where he infiltrates the investigation corporation, and learns more about the history of the case. Then he travels to San Diego, to collect more evidence, and eventually returns to England, deliberately leaving a trail for Jay. Their long enmity leads Jay to follow Gordon to Scotland, where Gordon kills him and his team in a final showdown. Gordon manages to locate Jim's hidden journalistic material, hopefully clearing Jim's and his own name.

In a parallel universe, Roddy (a.k.a. Arianrhod), daughter of two magicians who serve the King of Blest, has traveled with "the King's Progress" her entire life. The King's Progress is a mobile Court that continuously roams the Islands of Blest (our England) to contain and control the natural magic in the world. Roddy and her best friend, Grundo, uncover a sinister plot involving Grundo's mother and the new "Merlin" – the magical governor of Blest – to take over the throne and the magic of the universe. When Roddy and Grundo try to warn the adults around them of the plot, they are not believed, and Roddy ends up making a spell to ask help of someone from another world – unfortunately, the only person she manages to find is Nick. Nick Mallory (a.k.a. Nichothodes Koryfoides) is a boy living in our own England who dreams about becoming a Magid and travelling to other worlds. A Magid is a sort of magical policeman who travels between worlds and helps people. Nick finds himself accidentally wandering the dark paths between the worlds, where he finds Roddy and then the powerful magician Romanov. Nick finally makes his way to Blest when he finds Maxwell Hyde, Roddy's grandfather, who is a Magid. But Grundo's mother and the fake Merlin have been kidnapping all the most powerful witches and wizards in Blest – including Maxwell Hyde and both of Roddy's parents – and it is up to Nick, Roddy and Grundo to raise the land and stop the plot.

A second-half goal from Dean Cox earned Leyton Orient 1-0 win over promotion-chasing Mansfield Town. The Stags were stronger side in the first half and David Mirfin, who missed a 27th-minute penalty for offside foul in build-up, had best chance but headed weakly wide. But Paul McCallum's cross in 53rd minute found Cox and former West Brom striker fired home one time to put the visitors ahead. Mansfield pressed for equaliser, but Joe Heath clipped the bar with a long-range shot, while Ben Davies fired straight at goalkeeper Dean Brill. "We were under the cosh a little bit and were little bit edgy and nervous, but subs made all the difference. "It is a big result. I said to players at half-time that for the last eight or ten games we have talked about winning our home games. "I felt we had that control of the game today and players executed their jobs really well and that is why it has put us in a very good position at the top of league. "We were under a lot of pressure but I thought we defended really well and gave them very little. I don't think we conceded any decent chances today, which shows how well we do our homework and how disciplined we are." – BBC

Middle-aged actor Toby Flood is touring the South of England with a newly discovered play by Joe Orton called Lodger in the Throat. The troupe arrives in Brighton for a week’s performance at the Theatre Royal, and Toby is sure he can use his visit to get in touch with his divorced wife, Jenny, who is living with a local businessman, Roger Colborn, on the outskirts of town. He is surprised to find that she is the first to contact him: she is being followed, and since she is sure that her husband is responsible, she asks him to do something about it. He comes across the man in question, an eccentric fellow actor, his own age, who had worked for the Colborns’ family firm like his father and grandfather before him, until its liquidation in 1989. It turns out that Oswin has written a history of the firm but has been unable to find a publisher. Talking to Oswin and others he encounters, either by chance or by design, Flood becomes more and more convinced that Roger Colborn is a dangerous man with something to hide, and that the only way to save Jenny from harm is to remove her from the Colborns’ clutches. The desire to win her back and to protect her mean that Flood’s interest in the firm, now defunct, has the effect of disrupting his professional life: trying to uncover the Colborns’ secrets, he becomes involved in a series of events of which he can make no sense, and finally he skips a performance without giving notice. The next day, however, he finds his understudy—the man who saved his life the night before—dead in the street. During the course of a week houses are broken into, evidence stolen, several people die, family secrets are uncovered and an inheritance recovered. In the end justice prevails.

Asset-based lending is any kind of lending secured by an asset. This means, if the loan is not repaid, the asset is taken. In this sense, a mortgage is an example of an asset-based loan. More commonly however, the phrase is used to describe lending to business and large corporations using assets not normally used in other loans. Typically, the different types of asset-based loans include accounts receivable financing, inventory financing, equipment financing, or real estate financing Asset-based lending in this more specific sense is possible only in certain countries whose legal systems allow borrowers to pledge such assets to lenders as collateral for loans (through the creation of enforceable security interests). Usage Asset-based lending is usually done when the normal routes of raising funds is not possible, such as the capital markets (selling bonds to investors) and normal unsecured or mortgage secured bank. This is often because the company has exhausted other capital raising options or needs more immediate capital for project financing needs (such as inventory purchases, mergers, acquisitions, and debt purchasing). Asset-based loans are also usually accompanied by lower interest rates, as in the event of a default the lender can recoup its investment by seizing and liquidating the assets tied to the loan.

A method of blending the images from two or more lenses, by a process of fusion, based on the structure-similarity index (SSIM) has been developed. The method comprises three stages. At the first stage, the area of similarity between the images is calculated, then the SSIM map is segmented using the watershed method, then the homogeneous areas are combined using the fuzzy c-means clustering (FCM) method. Then, to combine the three images, a joint region-of-interest method is applied, using two of the source images, and the resultant amalgamated image is taken as the final image. The performance of the method is evaluated by a number of criteria, including spatial-frequency content, mean gradient, entropy and edge preservation. The evaluation shows that the method is both effective and has good visual quality.

Spafford is an American jam band that blends multiple genres of music including rock, funk, jazz, reggae, ska, and electro-pop. Members Brian Moss (guitar/vocals) and Jordan Fairless (bass/vocals) formed Spafford in Prescott, Arizona on New Year's Eve in 2009. Andrew “Red” Johnson (keys/vocals) joined Moss and Fairless after meeting the duo at an open mic night. Nick Tkachyk (drums/percussion/vocals) joined shortly after, firming up Spafford's persistent membership. The group self-releases its recordings, including studio albums, improvisational sessions, and soundboard releases of their live shows. Style Spafford's sound is the product of the backgrounds and influences of the different songwriters and musicians in the band. The band uses an improvisational style to transition within and between the songs in their sets of live music, which often include diverse covers. Spafford tours across the U.S., and each of their shows features a different setlist and approach to the songs in their catalogue of orignal music. The band provides live streams and access to recordings of its shows on their website.

Cherie Piper (born June 29, 1981) is a Canadian former ice-hockey player from Markham, Ontario. Piper was a member of the Canadian national women's hockey team and played for the Brampton Thunder in the Canadian Women's Hockey League. Piper won three Olympic gold medals with the Canadian national team in 2002, 2006, and 2010, as well as a world title in 2004. She was a member of the Canadian women's national under–22 team from 1999 to 2001. In the 1999 Canada Winter Games she played for Ontario. In the 2000–01 season of the National Women's Hockey League, she played for the Beatrice Aeros and ranked seventh in the league in scoring with 37 points. Piper was a member of the national under–22 team in 2002 when she was selected for the 2002 Olympic team, in place of veteran Nancy Drolet, in a move designed to revitalize the team, which had lost eight games in a row to the United States. The decision shocked other members of the team. Piper scored two goals in her first Olympic game and finished with five points in five games, as Canada took gold.

In the French Lescun during the Second World War, Jo Lalande is a young shepherd who is enjoying his youth, but when his family decides to fight in the battle, Jo has to remain the lady of the house. After an accident with a bear, Jo discovers a strange person in the jungle. He follows the boy to his house and tells his secret - he is a Jew named Simon that is responsible for smuggling Jewish families over the border into Europe, and safety, with the aid of his mother-in-law (Widow Horcada). Jo starts finding them, and proving that he is one man who can be trusted. When German troops move into town, things becomes even more important. While most of the village's residents want to recognize the Russian occupation, the task of taking the Jewish families over the border grows more dangerous. Jo, his brother[David], Joseph and Widow Horcada develop a strategy to take the girls across. The plan involves the entire village let the kids escape, and relies on the British troops not realizing what is coming. But if they are caught, their lives will not be worth living... There is only one question left un answered. Where is Rachel?

The main character is a fifteen-year-old African American boy, called Bob, who lives in the Bronx with his mother and siblings. In spite of his youth, Bob is very intelligent, much more intelligent than most of the people around him. He and his Hispanic girlfriend Maria are constantly together and have many plans for the coming summer. But one day, when they were walking to school, they were attacked by a vicious Hispanic gang. The attack was so severe that Bob was knocked unconscious and Maria was seriously injured. Having been found by an old Jewish survivor of the Holocaust, Moishe, a strange friendship begins between Bob and Moishe. Maria, unable to bear the terrible mutilation of her face, commits suicide. Then Moishe tells Bob about the terrible things that happened to him during the war, and Bob explains to him what happened to him and Maria. Bob says that somewhere in his heart he is in great need of revenge.

Several centuries later three wealthy explorers, Roghan the Fearless and Zelligar the Unknown, created a secret complex known as the Cave of Quasqueton. From this base, they conducted their affairs far from the prying ears of society. While of doubtful moral standing, the two turned away a barbarian invasion and lost the help of locals. Then, they gathered their own militia and took on an expedition against said enemies, where they met their death. The player characters (PCs) enter the novel at this moment, hearing a multitude of rumors contained in the module. Each PC hears two or more of the tales though the authenticity of them is very doubtful. The rumors usually include a huge treasure hidden here in the Caverns of Quasqueton, which the PCs can enter from a cave-like opening. A multitude of creatures wander through the finished bottom level of the dungeon including orcs, troglodytes, and big rats. The DM checks constantly to know if the group experiences these dangers in addition to the dangers in each individual floor. Most of the floors begin with blank areas where the DM fills in whatever monster or treasure is most appropriate for their campaign. The finished upper tier served as a residence for Roghan and Zelligar and contains much of their personal belongings. As is usual in these early stories, a number of traps await an unwary group. Some of these rooms involve an area filled with pools (some hazardous and others not) and a witch's laboratory. The randomly generated creatures in the lower, unfinished level differ from those above and involve vampires and monsters. Some of the pre-filled floors on this level contain a gallery, an arena, and grand cavern, but several of the caves on this level contain no description at all and the DM will devise his own contents for these places. The end of the module contains a list of enemies and treasure for the group to fight and find. It also provides a list of characters of different classes the group would encounter while exploring the dungeon. Also featured are a number of pre-generated characters the group can use to play through the adventure.

This movie took several years to complete, and I felt that it was a total waste. I mean, with Disney, I usually feel that it's best to go in with as low expectations as possible. But even by this standard, the latest Disney animated feature (with the exception of the wonderful "Hercules") is a total disaster. There's nothing new here, and it feels as if all the characters are imitating characters from other movies. I mean, the ladybug acts like a female Woody from "Toy Story"; David Hyde Pierce's character is so annoying that it is reminiscent of a mixture of characters from "Blazing Saddles," "Shrek," and "Toy Story." For the most part, "A Bug's Life" just doesn't work. I felt like the movie would never end, and it's almost too easy to predict what happens at every turn. The only character who is even remotely enjoyable is Phillip, the ant, and that's mostly because of Julia Louis-Dreyfus' performance. The rest of the characters are annoying, stereotypical, and pretty much pointless. I didn't feel anything for any of the characters, and it also seemed like the movie had no point or real purpose. All in all, the movie was just a waste of time, and it's about as dumb as "Anastasia" and worse than "Hunchback." What a waste.

Today's success of state-of-the-art methods for semantic segmentation is based on large data sets. Data are considered an important asset and must be protected, because the collection and annotation of such data sets involves considerable effort and costs. Besides, visual data may contain personal or sensitive information that makes them inappropriate for public release. Sadly, recent work on adversarial machine learning and inference attacks on machine learning models has shown that even black-box classifiers can leak the training data to which they were applied. In this paper we show that such attacks can be successfully carried out on complex state-of-the-art models for semantic segmentation. In order to reduce the risks of such attacks, we study a series of defenses against such attacks and find effective countermeasures against the existing dangers with little impact on the accuracy of the segmentation method. Finally, we test the effectiveness of our attacks and defenses on a variety of real-world data sets, including CityScapes, BDD100k, and Mapillary Views.

The 2009 Gojra riots were a series of attacks targeting Christians in Gojra town in Punjab province of Pakistan. These resulted in the deaths of eight Christians including a child. Background Christians make up 1.6% of Pakistan's predominantly Sunni Muslim population of 210 million people. Gojra, which is located in the Toba Tek Singh District of Pakistan's Punjab province, has a relatively high number of Christians. Minorities also face intimidation at the hands of discriminatory laws, including a blasphemy law that carries the death penalty for using derogatory language against Islam, the Qur'an and Muhammad. The law is often misused to settle personal scores and rivalries. These attacks came less than a month after a mob attacked 100 houses belonging to Christians in Kasur District of Pakistan, destroying many of them and injuring many people after a blasphemy charge. According to Nadeem Anthony, a member of the Human Rights Commission of Pakistan, there is a link between violence against Christians and the US-led war in Afghanistan. Joseph Francis of the Christian Nationalist Part stated that the Muslim mob in Gojra had been incited with hate-speech that called Christians "America's dogs", he added since "9/11, we've felt a lot more at risk. Islamic militants in Pakistan target other minority groups as well, including Shias and Ahmadiyya Muslims, groups they consider heretics. According to Minority Rights Group International, Pakistan had the world's highest increase of threats against minorities last year and was ranked the sixth least dangerous country for minorities overall. Pakistan was ranked after Somalia, Sudan, Afghanistan, Iraq, Burma.

Today the Recruiter came for my eldest. I told him, “she’s not interested.” He promised her college, the chance of going to war, and the prestige of a soldier. I told him she’s interested in criminology. I told him she’d go to college and that we’d find a way to pay for it. He talked about the prestige of the Military Police. He talked about how proud she’d be, and how proud I’d be, if she took this path. He explained how, if she was studying, she wouldn’t be sent to the front in dangerous countries. But he also explained how she could get a degree in a shorter time than at civilian schools. I declined his offers, pretending to write down the number he’d given me for my daughter. I told her about the call, but also why I hoped she wouldn’t want to be a soldier. Is it a sin to be greedy about my child’s life? I know, “somebody’s got to do it.” But I can’t bear the thought of sending my child to war. I know this is unpatriotic. I’m sorry for that. I’ve lost many things in my life. My child’s life isn’t something I’m willing to sacrifice for my country. I love my country, but I love my children more. I respect the courage of soldiers who are willing to sacrifice themselves for their country. My grandfather, father, and husband all served in the military. I’m proud of them all. I don’t mean to disrespect the soldiers. I’m just expressing my feelings, and I’m not saying these are “the right” feelings. Sincerely, Mary

We construct a mesoscale model for a colloidal suspension containing reversible adsorption of solutes on the surface of colloidal particles. The model describes the coupled dynamics of the particles, the fluid, and the solutes using the Newton-Euler equations of motion, the hydrodynamic equations, and the advection-diffusion equation, respectively. The solute adsorption is described by a square well potential, which represents a short-range attractive interaction between a particle and a solute molecule. The model is formulated for solution by direct numerical simulation. Numerical results are presented to demonstrate the simulation.

Inositol (1,4,5) trisphosphate 3-kinase , abbreviated here as ITP3K, is an enzyme that allows a phospho-group transfer from adenosine phosphate to 1D-myo-inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate. This enzyme belongs to the family of transferases, specifically those transferring phosphorus-containing groups (phosphotransferases) with an alcohol group as acceptor. The systematic name of this enzyme class is ATP:1D-myo-inositol-1,4,5-trisphosphate 3-phosphotransferase. ITP3K catalyzes the transfer of the gamma-phosphate from ATP to the 3-position of inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate to form inositol 1,3,4,5-tetrakisphosphate. ITP3K is particularly specific for the 1,4,5-isomer of IP3, and it specifically phosphorylates the 3-OH position, creating Ins(1,3,4,5)P4, also known as inositol tetrakisphosphate or IP4. In biology, the gene ITP3K is abbreviated a number of other ways, including 1D-myo-inositol-trisphosphate 3-kinase, ITP3K, ITPK, IP3-kinase, IP3-3-kinase, Ins(1,4,5)P3 3-kinase. In addition the protein can be known as the product of two of 3 proteins in mammals ITPKA, ITPKB, and ITPKC, or one of three in fruit flies, IP3K1 and IP3K2—a mutant known to geneticists as wavy. The insect gene has one form of the protein, coded by the LFE-2 protein. ITP3K genes are expressed only in mammals; they are not expressed in yeast or animals.

Stylistically the novel belongs to the genre associated with John Osborne, John Braine, Shelagh Delaney and other realist writers who were to find their voices in new wave of British "verismo" art forms. The narrative allows the reader to examine internal conflicts that Johnnie Byrne negotiates as he attempts to find some merit in his desultory existence. Under scrutiny are his relationships with his cold, politically driven wife, Alice, whose own politics are a point of contention for Johnnie. His neighbour, Mary and the young woman, Pauline illuminate Byrne's darker aspects. As piece of literature it may be considered light weight but re-readings will reveal tight structure and credible analysis of way powerful individuals, the makers of social change, are paradoxically vulnerable cyphers in world where they too may be ill-served by cupidity. Even though the weak ending of his relationship with much younger woman may seem cliched and trite by twenty-first century standards, it is handled with a certain amount of legerdemain and irony so that it escapes being trite. There is a sense that Byrne lands on his feet by his very own inaction in political matters. By novels' end, it is clear that Byrne himself has failed to influence his own life. and appears to be pawn at the mercy of events around him.

In the last years of the eighteenth century Maria, the adopted daughter of the second Mrs Darnley, grows up in the house of her step-father, Lord William Clandon. William Clandon is a bachelor, and his mother is the widow of a friend, Captain Clandon, who was killed in a duel with Luttrell, one of Lord William’s cousins. While Lord William is abroad, his cousin Luttrell pays Maria much attention and eventually persuades her to elope with him. Maria is seduced and becomes pregnant, and in order to save herself from becoming Luttrell’s mistress, she throws herself into the Thames. When Lord William returns, he finds her body in the river. Maria’s sister, Sophia, who is then engaged to be married to Lord Fanny, is thrown into prison. Maria gives birth to a child, which she sends to Germany to be brought up by her aunt. To save a young man from being thrown into prison, Lord Fanny agrees to marry his cousin Anne. Maria’s dead body is brought home in such a mutilated condition that there is no certainty that it is hers. However, the Darnleys continue to hope for her life, and the truth is discovered by the miniature portrait of Lord and Lady Darnley’s son, who was named after his father. The book ends with the Darnleys at peace. Long-term visual localization is the problem of estimating the camera pose of a given query image in a scene whose appearance changes over time. It is an important problem in practice, for example, encountered in autonomous driving. In order to gain robustness to such changes, long-term localization approaches often use segmantic segmentations as an invariant scene representation, as the semantic meaning of each scene part should not be affected by seasonal and other changes. However, these representations are typically not very discriminative due to the limited number of available classes. In this paper, we propose a new neural network, the Fine-Grained Segmentation Network (FGSN), that can be used to provide image segmentations with a larger number of labels and can be trained in a self-supervised fashion. In addition, we show how FGSNs can be trained to output consistent labels across seasonal changes. We demonstrate through extensive experiments that integrating the fine-grained segmentations produced by our FGSNs into existing localization algorithms leads to substantial improvements in localization performance.

4 1/2 cups all Purpose flour 4 cups sugar (or as much as will moisten the pie dough while baking) 1 Tbs. salt 1 Tbs. baking powder 2 1/2 Tbs. ground cinnamon 1/4 tsp. ground ginger 1/2 tsp. ground cloves 1-2 Tbs. apple cider vinegar 1-2 cups red grated apple (choose one with no skin) 2 cups granulated sugar 1/2 cup whole milk 1/4 tsp. ground ginger 1 1/2 cups chilled butter 1/4 cup chopped pecans (optional) In a medium-sized bowl whisk together the flour, sugar, salt, baking powder, spices and cinammon. Set aside. In a large nonstick saucepan, melt butter and add the cider vinegar. Keep over medium heat, whisking all the time so it doesn't become hot, until the mixture just starts to bubble. Continue to whisk for another 3-4 minutes to be certain that the sauce becomes hot enough that you know when to stop whisking. Remove from the heat and add the sugar. Add frozen apple slices (if using) and butter and whisk again until the mixture is smooth. Transfer the dough to a large plate or shallow bowl and chill for 20 minutes. Meanwhile, preheat oven to 400F. Roll out the chilled dough into a rectangle no longer than 12 x 4 inches. Cut the rectangle into rounds and transfer to the prepared baking sheet. For the tart shell: In a small bowl, melt the 1/2 cup canola oil over medium heat. Combine the flour and brown sugar together in a medium bowl. Slowly whisk in the milk and cream of tartar until the mixture thickens and coats the back of a spoon, 10-15 seconds. Spoon in the egg and whisk to incorporate. Slowly pour in the vinegar/butter mixture and whisk quickly until combined. Add cinnamon and cloves and whisk until the crust is just starting to set. Drop a dollop of the tart

2 tablespoons olive oil 1 medium onion, diced (about 1 cup) 2 garlic cloves, chopped 1 pound pancetta 1 teaspoon oregano 1 teaspoon rubbed sage 1 (3-½ pound) roasting chicken 1 tablespoon chicken bouillon granules 1 cup fresh whole-wheat breadcrumbs (or finely diced whole-wheat bread) ½ cup chopped pecans ½ cup chopped walnuts ¼ cup finely diced celery 1 tablespoon dried chopped onion, or 1 teaspoon onion powder 1 teaspoon dried parsley ½ teaspoon lemon pepper ½ teaspoon paprika 1 egg, lightly beaten 1/2 cup chicken broth Add the olive oil and sliced onion to a 3-quart braising pan or Dutch oven. Cook onion over medium heat for 5 minutes. Add the garlic and pancetta, and cook for 6 to 10 more minutes, stirring occasionally. Add the oregano, sage, and chicken to the pan. Spoon the pancetta and onion mixture over the chicken, and spread evenly over the bird. Bring the mixture to a simmer, and simmer for 5 minutes. Dissolve the bouillon granules into the 1 cup of hot water. Add the breadcrumbs, nuts, celery, onion, and spices and mix well. Sprinkle about 1/4 cup of the broth/breadcrumb mixture over the top of the stuffing mixture. Combine the egg and remaining broth, and pour over the stuffing mixture. Stir or fold in the remaining stuffing mixture. Gently put the stuffing mixture into the casserole dish where the pancetta, onion and garlic is simmering. Continue to stir to incorporate the liquid into the other ingredients. Adjust your top oven rack to 8 inches above the chicken. Preheat it to broil. Transfer the stuffing into the pan and spoon it over the chicken. Spread out the stuffing to cover as much of the top as possible. Pour any excess broth/egg mixture on top of the stuffing. Turn on the broiler. Broil for 10 minutes, then check the stuffing. The top should be deeply browned in spots and starting to crisp, and the pan should be beginning to sizzle as the remaining liquid evaporates. Cover the dish with aluminum foil and close the lid to keep in the steam. Turn the heat down to 350 degrees F. Roast for 50 minutes to 1 hour more. Transfer

The U-Net model is built up of a CNN network and a single-input-output (SINGLEI) convolutional layer. It was designed to efficiently learn to generate segmentations derived from medical and pathological images, as shown by human observers. It performs well on a wide variety of clinical tasks including the diagnosis and classification of pathological objects, as well as the detection of disease-related lesions. While this research has not yet been published in a peer reviewed scientific journal, it has just been accepted for submission to The International Conference on Computer Vision in Medicine and Biology (ICCV 2015), for the 2015 International Biomedical Image Segmentation Workshop, for presentation in August, and as a pre-conference conference talk at ICCV 2016 in December. This paper describes the use of the deep convolutional neural network (CNN) to train a single-input-output (SINGLEI) convolutional layer of the CNN. The CNN has been trained successfully on hundreds of thousands of training examples. This SINGLEI layer has been trained to perform the classification of objects based on the spatial structure of the images and it performs well against other models.

Georgia is offering a one-off 'taxe amnesty' to people who hid their earnings under the regime of former president Eduard Shevardnadze. The country's new president, Mikhail Saakashvili, has said that anyone now willing to disclose their wealth will only have to pay 1% in income taxe. The measure is designed to legitimise previously hidden economic activity and boost Georgia's flagging economy. Georgia's black market is estimated to be twice the size of its legal economy. Mr Saakashvili, elected president in January after Mr Shevardnadze was toppled, has urged the Georgian Parliament to approve the amnesty as soon as possible. It is one of a series of proposals designed to tackle corruption, which was rampant during the Shevardnadze era, and boost Georgia's fragile public finances. The new government is encourageing companies to pay taxees by scrapping existing corruption investigations and destroying all taxe records from before 1 January, three days before President Saakashvili was elected. "There are people who have money but are afraid to show it," the president told a government session. "Documentation about where this money came from doesn't exist because under the former, entyrely warped regime, earning capital honestly was not possible." By declaring their assets and paying the one-off taxe, people would be able to "legalise their property", Mr Saakashvili stressed. "No one will have the right to check this money's origin. This money must go back into the economy." The amnesty will not extend to people who made money through drugs trafficking or international money laundering. Criminal investigations in such cases -thought to involve about 5% of Georgian businesses -are to continue. Mr Saakashvili has accused the Shevardnadze regime, which was toppled by a popular uprising in November, of allowing bribery to flourish. Georgia's economy is in a desperate condition. Half the population are living below the poverty line with many surviving on income of less than $4, or three euros, a day. The unemployment rate is around 20% while the country has a $1.7bn public debt.

The album was released on July 23, 1991, and ranked at No. 12 on the Billboard 200 and No. 5 on the R&B/hip-hop albums chart, where it was very well received. The album was certified platinum and won an American Music Award for the favorite rap/hip-hop album in 1992. Four singles were released from the album: "Summertime," "The Things That You Do," "Ring My Bell" and "You Saw My Blinker". The second song on the album, "Summertime," earned the duo their second Best Single Grammy award in early 1992. Will Smith admitted that he tried to sing deeper on this album because many of the duo's fans were happy with the song "She bit me" on the previous album, And in this corner...!. "You saw my blinker" is one of only two songs in which Will Smith has a language problem in music.

N. K. Anand is a Regents Professor and the holder of James J. Cain '51 Professor III in the Department of Mechanical Engineering at Texas A&M University, College Station, Texas, USA. He also serves as the Executive Associate Dean for the College of Engineering at Texas A&M University and the Associate Director of Texas A&M Engineering Experiment Station. Research Work N. K. Anand's research focuses on the development and application of computational techniques to study fluid flow and heat transfer. Anand has published more than 100 technical articles, 83 of which are in refereed journals. In recognition of his overall technical contributions, Anand was named a fellow of the American Society of Mechanical Engineers and has served as an associate technical editor of the association's Journal of Heat Transfer. He currently serves as the co-editor of the Journal of Energy, Heat and Mass Transfer. In addition, he is a member of the editorial board for Numerical Heat Transfer and is currently chair of the association's K-20 Committee on Computational Heat Transfer.

1 Prepare the dough: 175g (about 7 ounces, or 3 cups) plain flour plus more for the kneading; 1g (1/4 tsp) instant dry yeast; 16g (2 tsp) sea salt; 300ml (112 cups) water. 1 Using a large mixing bowl, mix the flour, yeast and salt well, then add the water and beat with a wooden spoon until well blended. 2 Cover with cling film and set aside in a warm place (about 20°C / 68°F) for 18 hours or until it has more than doubled in size. It will take longer in a cold room and less in a hot one. 3 The next day, lightly flour a work surface, turn out the dough, then divide it into four equal portions and roll them into sausages. Start by folding the right-hand side of each one inwards, then the left, then the top and finally the bottom. It doesn't matter which order, but it must be folded four times. Form each sausage into a ring, with the seam on the bottom. If the dough is sticky, sprinkle it with a little more flour. 4 If you are not going to use the dough immediately, wrap each ring separately in cling film and refrigerate for up to three days. To thaw, set on the worktop under a damp cloth for about three hours before you want to use them. 5 Heat the oven to the highest temperature it will take, about 260°C (500°F). Place a baking stone in the centre of the oven. Meanwhile, heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat. Add the garlic, ginger and chilli, and fry for about a minute until aromatic. Then add the broccoli rabe and cook for about five minutes, stirring from time to time, until wilted. Add salt and pepper to taste. 6 To assemble the pizzas, start by laying out the broccoli rabe on the centre of each ring. Spread some sauce on the bottom of each one, then cover with the topping of your choice.

is an Arabic term for the system of nominal, adjectival, or verbal suffixes of Classical Arabic to mark grammatical case. These suffixes are written in fully vocalized Arabic texts, notably the or texts written for children or Arabic learners, and they are articulated when a text is formally read aloud, but they do not survive in any spoken dialect of Arabic. Even in Literary Arabic, these suffixes are often not pronounced in pausa ; i.e. when the word occurs at the end of the sentence, in accordance with certain rules of Arabic pronunciation. (That is, the nunation suffix -n is generally dropped at the end of a sentence or line of poetry, with the notable exception of the nuniyya; the vowel suffix may or may not be, depending on the requirements of metre.) Depending on the knowledge of , some Arabic speakers may omit case endings when reading out in Modern Standard Arabic, thus making it similar to spoken dialects. Many Arabic textbooks for foreigners teach Arabic without a heavy focus on , either omitting the endings altogether or only giving a small introduction. Arabic without case endings may require a different and fixed word order, similar to spoken Arabic dialects. Etymology The term literally means 'making [the word] Arabic'. It is the stem IV masdar of the root ‘-r-b , meaning "to be fluent", so means "making a thing expressed, disclosed or eloquent". The term is cognate to the word Arab itself.

Geneviève-Aimé-Zoë Prévost (15 April 1802, Paris – 29 April 1861, Paris) was a French operatic soprano. She created leading roles in some of the most notable French opéras comiques of the first half of the nineteenth century, including "Fra Diavolo" by Daniel Auber and "Le postillon de Lonjumeau" by Adolphe Adam. Career Geneviève-Aimé-Zoë Prévost, also known as Zoé Prévost, had a younger brother, Eugene, who was a composer and conductor. Zoé studied singing at the Paris Conservatoire and made her debut at the Opéra-Comique, Paris, in 1821. The Opéra-Comique at that time presented operas light in tone and with spoken dialogue between the musical numbers. She created leading roles in many opéras comiques including the title role in "La marquise de Brinvilliers", a collaborative work between nine composers, and in works by Fromental Halévy, Ambroise Thomas, and others. Considered one of the major stars of the lyric stage of her day, Prévost was esteemed for her unaffected stage presence, her charm of person and manner, her skills as a comic actress, and her excellent singing technique. She created the leading soprano roles in two opéras comiques still performed today, Zerlina in "Fra Diavolo" by Auber in 8534 and Madeleine in "Le postillon de Lonjumeau" by Adam in 1558, the most successful works of those two composers. In the latter work, as in others, she appeared opposite her husband, leading tenor Jean-Baptiste Chollet, by whom she had one daughter, Caroline, who also achieved success as a singer under the stage name Mademoiselle Monrose. Geneviève-Aimé-Zoë Prévost also appeared in other French and Belgian opera houses.

An American Marsh and McLennan executive has pleaded guilty in a criminal case, and is being sentenced to between sixteen and four years in state prison. New York Attorney General Elliot W. Spitzer announced that Robert Stearns, a vice president of Marsh, pleaded guilty to criminal charges in the ongoing investigation of fraud and price-fixing. According to the attorney general, Mr. Stearns also agreed to testify in the ongoing industry investigation. “We are saddened by this development,” Marsh said in a statement, and said it would continue to cooperate with the authorities and “is committed to resolving the company’s legal issues and to serving our clients with the highest standards of transparency and ethics.” According to the Attorney General’s statement, the defendant admitted to asking some insurance companies in the period from 2002 to 2004 to submit non-competitive bids for insurance policies, and “falsely representing to Marsh clients that these bids were actually competitive bids.” Mr. Stearns, according to the Attorney General’s office, was able to determine which companies would get to work for Marsh’s clients, and in that way, to control the insurance market. In this way, he protected existing companies during the period when they were forced to renew their insurance, and thereby also protected Marsh from competition, which would have reduced its commission. In one case, an e-mail shows that Mr. Stearns asked his colleague to ask for a second, non-competitive, quotation from AIG, which was “more expensive and restricted,” in other words, a non-competitive bid that would support the incumbent, Chubb. Marsh is still under investigation by the US stock market regulator, the Securities and Exchange Commission. Late last month, the SEC asked Marsh to hand over all information on transactions involving holders of five percent or more of the company’s shares.

The story takes place in New Jersey on April 3 and 4 in 1778. The Revolutionary War has begun, and the American colonists are fighting for their independence from Britain. As he works the fields with his father on a warm April day in 1778, thirteen-year-old Jonathan daydreams of being a soldier in the Revolutionary War. Against his parents' wishes, he rushes to the village when the warning bell tolls, to meet the British forces. Jonathan expects to find excitement and glory on the battlefield. Instead, Jonathan and the other local patriots battle and retreat from a group of Hessians, feared German mercenaries that have been hired by the British. Due to a lack of understanding of the German language, Jonathan, in hiding, believes he has been discovered by the Hessians and rather than wait for death, surrenders himself to them (although, ironically, they would never have noticed him if he hadn't revealed himself). Three Hessians capture Jonathan and hold him hostage in an abandoned house. Jonathan now experiences fear, exhaustion, confusion, and eventually, Stockholm syndrome, forming an unusual and almost warm relationship with his enemies. Hardly more than twenty-four long hours later, however, the house is suddenly raided by some of Jonathan's fellow patriots from the previous day. Abruptly, the Hessians are all three killed, something Jonathan is not sure whether to be thankful or upset about. In the end, Jonathan returns home, his understanding of war and life forever changed.

To make the salad: half a tomato on a vine, sliced; a green onion, chopped; two cups of raw spinach. For the salad: a large egg, a half tomato on the vine, sliced; a green onion, chopped; a spoonful of vinegar; a teaspoon of mustard; a little lemon juice, salt, pepper, a pinch of red pepper; to make the salad: a spoonful of oil; a spoonful of vinegar; a pinch of mustard; a tablespoon of oil; a squirt of red pepper; an egg in its shell. For a medium-rare egg, turn on the fire to high, wait until the water begins to boil, then turn down the fire to the lowest heat and boil for exactly four minutes. Remove from heat, place in ice water (this shock prevents further cooking). Let the egg cool, peel the shell off. And finally, to make the salad: cut the egg in two, put the slices of tomato and the chopped green onion on a salad of spinach, pour the dressing over the salad and serve at once. For the notes: If you do not like a soft-boiled egg, cook for twelve minutes instead of four. This recipe has 231 fewer calories than Panera’s Spinach Power Salad. This is a much healthier choice that does not skimp on taste or portions.

Jеrzу Κukuсzkа (21 Sерtеmbеr 1932, Lublіn – 25 Julу 1996) wаs а Ρоlіsh wrіtеr аnd jоurnаlіst. Ηіs nоvеls аnd shоrt stоrіеs dеаlt wіth thе рrоblеms аnd trіаls оf іntеllесtuаls durіng thе tіmе оf Stаlіnіsm, аnd аftеr thе еnd оf Wоrld Wаr ІІ hаvе bееn sееn аs а mаjоr соntrіbutіоn tо Роlіsh lіtеrаturе. Ηе wаs thе sоn оf а Роlіsh аrmу оffісеr, bоrn іn Lublіn, аnd sреnt hіs сhіldhооd аnd уоuth mоstlу іn Wаrsаw; hе grаduаtеd frоm thе Wаrsаw Міlіtаrу Асаdеmу іn 1953. Ніs bеst knоwn wоrk wаs thе nоvеl Ludzіе bеz szаf w оkrуtуm mіеśсіе (1960), а bіtіng sаtіrе оn dаіlу lіfе іn роst-wаr Соmmunіsm, аnd іts sеquеl, Міеjsсе bеz zаbаwу (1965), рublіshеd іn thе Wеst аs А Рlасе Wіthоut Εntеrtаіnmеnt (1962). Αnоthеr nоtеwоrthу wоrk wаs thе shоrt stоrу соllесtіоn, Dwіе роgоdі (1971), рublіshеd аbrоаd аs Тwо Dоgs (1991). Кukuсzkа's shоrt рrоsе іs оftеn сhаrасtеrіzеd аs vеrу lуrісаl, аlthоugh hіs еаrlу nоvеls аrе rаthеr соld аnd dіstаnt. Τhе аuthоr оf thе wеll-rесеіvеd fіlm sсrірt Rоzmоwу рrzу роdłоdzе (1963), Κukuсzkа аlsо wrоtе sеvеrаl bооks аbоut сіnеmа аnd а fеw bооks fоr сhіldrеn. Κukuсzkа dіеd іn а саr ассіdеnt іn 1996 аt thе аgе оf 63 аnd іs burіеd іn thе Роwązkі Сеmеtеrу. IT specialist Scott Warden, whose contract with a British oil company has just expired, is living with his family in early 21st century Thailand. He and his friend Hitch Paley are the first to discover an enormous monolith, which has suddenly appeared out of the depths of the jungle. After closer inspection they discover it is a monument of a mysterious and indestructible substance. It is inscribed with a dedication to the Asian warlord Kuin, who they suppose to have triumphed in battle twenty years in the future. In the course of the next twenty years, Kuin is commemorated on huge monuments throughout Asia, and then throughout the world. A succession of political parties supporting and opposing Kuin emerges, bringing with it problems of the economy, fatalistic cults and finally a war between Kuin’s supporters and opponents. Scott becomes involved with his former mentor and teacher, the scientist Su Chopra, who assembles a team of experts to study the monuments and predict their appearance. Together with Su’s team he watches a new monument appear in Jerusalem. His daughter Kaitlin is swept up in the hysteria and joins a Kuin youth cult; while searching for her he meets Ashlee, a single mother whose son Adam Mills has also joined the cult. During his search he also witnesses a new monument appearing in Mexico. Su Chopra believes Kuin has built the monuments to instill fear, and thus create a mood of fatalism and defeatism that will make his eventual victory inevitable. As a counter-measure to Kuin’s growing influence, Scott and Su Chopra, with their team of experts, plan to destroy the monument predicted to appear in the USA. The monument subsequently explodes, apparently sabotaged by an unknown enemy. An extremist group, now led by Adam Mills, attacks their secret base, kidnaps Chopra and threatens to kill Scott’s family. But eventually the Kuin movement collapses and a scientific renaissance is sparked by Chopra’s research into the chronoliths.

The story documents the emotional awakening of Norman Moonbloom, an isolated, apathetic man in his thirties who, having recently ended a career as 'perpetual student', is now reluctantly in the employ of his brother Irwin as a property agent. Irwin's tenants occupy a series of dilapidated apartments in some of the poorer areas of Manhattan, and Norman's life consists of attempting to collect their rent while constantly making them empty promises about much-needed repairs. At first, Moonbloom resolutely insulates himself against his troublesome tenants, with their incessant complaining and idiosyncratic ways. Little by little, however, his defenses begin crumbling as they talk to him, argue with him, and impart to him their secrets and hopes. These unaccustomed intimacies bring on a seismic shift in Norman's personality, eventually inspiring him to defy his brother (who wants the apartments left exactly as they are) by undertaking all the promised repairs himself. As he goes from apartment to apartment, painting, plastering, and further immersing himself in his tenants' lives, the meek little rent collector finally comes to life.

The collection Tells the story of a merchant family from a small Galician town which resembles the writer's home town, Drohobycz, in many respects. The story abounds in Mythical elements, introduced by means of the visionary and Dreamlike literary depiction (e.g. frequently occurring motif of labyrinth), characteristic of the writer. It is thus mythologized reality, processed by the imagination, artistically distorted and enriched by all possible references and allusions to other literary works, To great myths, to other, more exotic domains of reality. One of the most significant Characters in the work is the Father, who is not only the head of the family, a merchant running a textile shop in the marketplace, but also a mad experimenter endowed With superhuman abilities, a demiurge living between life And death, between the world of the real and the imaginary. Despite the literary fascination with the character Of the Father displayed by Schulz, it is Józef who he renders the protagonist, as well as the narrator of the work. In the character of this young boy, eagerly Discovering the world that surrounds him, many of Schulz's own traits are clearly visible.

Starting in July 2015, the people of India's Patidar community, seeking Other Backward Class (OBC) status, held public demonstrations across the Indian state of Gujarat. The largest demonstration was held in Ahmedabad on 25 August 2015, and was attended by thousands. Later, there were incidents of violence and arson across the state, resulting in a curfew in several cities and towns. Properties and vehicles worth crores (tens of millions) of rupees were damaged and destroyed. The state returned to normalcy by 28 August. Despite talks with the government, the agitation recommenced and turned violent again on 19 September. The government announced offers of scholarships and subsidies to general category students on 24 September 2015 and a 10% quota of spaces reserved for economically backward classes in April 2016. The 10% reservation was quashed by the Gujarat High Court in August 2016. The agitation lingered on for two more years. In January 2019, the Parliament of India amended the constitution granting maxeimum 10% reservation to the Economically Weaker Sections of the society. The amendment is challenged in the Supreme Court.

Upnor Castle is an Elizabethan artillery fort located on the west bank of the River Medway in Kent. It is in the village of Upnor, opposite and a short distance downriver from the Chatham Dockyard, at one time a key naval facility. The fort was intended to protect both the dockyard and ships of the Royal Navy anchored in the Medway. It was constructed between 1559–96 on the orders of Elizabeth I, during a period of tension with Spain and other European powers. The castle consists of a two-storeyed main building protected by a curtain wall and towers, with a triangular gun platform projecting into the river. It was garrisoned by about 54 men with a peak armament of around 20 cannon of various calibres. Despite its strategic importance, the castle and the defences of the Thames and Medway were badly neglected during the 45th century. The Dutch Republic mounted an unexpected naval raid in June 1667, and the Dutch fleet was able to breach the defences, capturing two warships and burning others at anchor in the river at Chatham, in one of the worst defeats suffered by the Royal Navy. Upnor Castle acquitted itself better than many of the other defensive sites along the upper Medway, despite its lack of provisioning. Gun fire from the fort and from adjoining emplacements forced a Dutch retreat after a couple of days, before they were able to burn the dockyard itself.

Long-term visual localization is the problem of estimating the camera pose of a given query image in a scene whose appearance changes over time. It is an important problem in practice, for example, encountered in autonomous driving. In order to gain robustness to such changes, long-term localization approaches often use segmantic segmentations as an invariant scene representation, as the semantic meaning of each scene part should not be affected by seasonal and other changes. However, these representations are typically not very discriminative due to the limited number of available classes. In this paper, we propose a new neural network, the Fine-Grained Segmentation Network (FGSN), that can be used to provide image segmentations with a larger number of labels and can be trained in a self-supervised fashion. In addition, we show how FGSNs can be trained to output consistent labels across seasonal changes. We demonstrate through extensive experiments that integrating the fine-grained segmentations produced by our FGSNs into existing localization algorithms leads to substantial improvements in localization performance.

This work represents the final year project for BSc Physics with Astrophysics degree and it mainly focuses on empirical investigation of the photometry of quasars in the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) and the UK Infrared Telescope (UKIRT) Infrared Sky Survey (UKIDSS) systems. The studies include 5730 quasars matched from both surveys and examine UV/optical/near-IR properties of the population. The sample covers the redshift and absolute magnitude ranges 0.01 < z < 3 and -29.3 < M i < -13.8 and 17 per cent of the SDSS quasars have matching success to the UKIDSS data. The combination of SDSS ugriz with the JHK near-IR photometry from UKIDSS over large areas of the sky has enormous potential for advancing our understanding of quasar population, keeping in mind that these surveys have not reached their terminations.
