Published in French by Jean-Jacques Pauvert, Story of O is a tale of female submission about a beautiful Parisian fashion photographer, O, who is blindfolded, chained, whipped, branded, pierced, made to wear a mask, and taught to be constantly available for oral, vaginal, and anal intercourse. Despite her harsh treatment, O grants permission beforehand for everything that occurs, and her permission is consistently sought. At the beginning of the story, O's lover, René, brings her to the château of Roissy, where she is trained to serve the men of an elite group. After this first period of training is finished, as a demonstration of their bond and his generosity, René hands O to Sir Stephen, a more dominant master. René wants O to learn to serve someone whom she does not love, and someone who does not love her. Over the course of this training, O falls in love with Sir Stephen and believes him to be in love with her as well. While her vain friend and lover, Jacqueline, is repulsed by O's chains and scars, O herself is proud of her condition as a willing slave. During the summer, Sir Stephen decides to move O to Samois, an old mansion solely inhabited by women for advanced training and body modifications related to submission. There she agrees to receive a branding and a labia piercing with rings marked with Sir Stephen's initials and insignia. At the climax, O appears as a slave, nude but for an owl-like mask, before a large party of guests who treat her solely as an object.

Half Broke Horses is the story of Lily Casey Smith’s life. Author Jeannette Walls, the granddaughter of Lily Casey Smith, wrote the book from Lily’s point of view. Lily is portrayed as a strong, spirited, and resourceful woman, who overcomes poverty and tragedy with the positive attitude that “When God closes a window, he opens a door. But it’s up to you to find it.” As a child growing up on the frontier in Texas, Lily learns how to break horses. At the age of fifteen, she rides five hundred miles, alone, to get to her job as a teacher in a one-room schoolhouse. Later in life, Lily runs a vast cattle ranch in Arizona, along with her second husband and their two children. A woman of many talents, Lily earns extra money at various points in her life by playing poker, selling bootleg liquor, and riding in horse races. She also tries to fight injustice and prejudice wherever she finds it, which occasionally lands her in trouble. Half Broke Horses depicts the freedom of rural life, its joys and struggles, and celebrates the courage and spirit of its protagonist. Jeannette Walls says the book is “in the vein of an oral history, a retelling of stories handed down by my family through the years, and undertaken with the storyteller’s traditional liberties.”

A truly brutal and gripping cinematic experience, Lone Survivor may be brazenly gung-ho and jingoistic, not to mention somewhat anti-climactic, but it delivers a metric tonne of thrills and contains one of the most intense and bloodiest gun fights I've ever seen in a film. It might stretch the suspension of disbelief a little too much at times, with our heroes surviving not 1 but fatal-looking cliff falls, but the excitement comes from the fact that it puts you right in the action, and you feel everything. Every bullet, every kick, every punch and every single thing the protagonist crash into. It's a bleak as Hell depiction of the savagery of war and just how strong the will to survive truly is. It's not a masterpiece, and many movies have been made with a more complex and compelling message on war, but for its sheer amount of heart-pounding action, scenes, it's definitely worth at least one watch.

This book focuses on An aspect of World War II that is largely ignored in many history books – the nazi looting of Europe and Russia and the Allied recovery and repatriation of stolen art. Little known to the general public, Hitler diverted his attention from the prosecution of the war to the systematic theft of Europe’s great art. His dream was to build the world’s greatest Collection – The führermuseum – in his hometown of Linz, Austria. European museum Officials took extraordinary measures to Protect art from Hitler and the ensuing war. When U.S. forces prepared to enter Europe, they assembled a special Force of largely American and British museum directors, curators, And art historians known as The Monuments, Fine Arts, and Archives program (MFAA) section, attached to the Allied armies. These “Monuments Men” attempted to minimize damage to European monuments and architecture, then track down stolen works of art. Their effort would become one of the greatest “treasure hunts” in history. In the end, Allied forces located more than 1,000 repositories in mines and castles across Europe, many of which were filled with art, sculpture, furniture, archives, and other cultural Property stolen by the Nazis. Edsel points out that thousands of pieces are still missing, such as Raphael’s Portrait of a Young Man From the Czartoryski Museum in Kraków, Poland. Rescuing da Vinci tells this story through brief text and More than 460 photographs, 60 of which are in color. This group of photographs has Never been published in a single book, and many have not been seen in decades. Images such as Michelangelo’s David entombed in brick for protection or a Rembrandt Self Portrait sitting atop crates in a salt mine, capture the story better than words could describe.

Who Killed the Robins Family? was a mystery novel in which all eight members of the Robins family are murdered or disappear throughout the story. The hardcover book provided no solutions to the murders. The books were also a contest where the person who provided the best answers to who, when, where, how, and why each murder happened won $10,000. The paperback version, released after the contest ended, revealed the answers to all the questions. Most chapters revolved around the death of a Robins family member, though one chapter contained a murder and a disappearance, and two others involved a disappearance. Most chapters contained all the needed information to provide all five answers regarding each death, though some gave only a hint as to an answer. However, if properly understood, it only took a bit of minor research to obtain the complete answer. The murders ranged from a classic locked-room puzzle to death by strangulation. The book also gives homage to several classic works of mystery and suspense. As the book is a contest, liberties are taken with proper police investigation of the crimes, which would have resulted in an immediate solution. For example, when one family member is shot to death in a darkened room, nobody thinks to check for gunshot residue. In addition, while some murders have fit very neatly with the facts on a theoretical basis, the method of implementation has questionable realism.

This movie is all that I like about movies. It has excellent acting, excellent characters, excellent story, excellent dialogue, it is just wonderful. I haven't seen Farrell in a role like this before and he really shines here. You see him go from a spoiled brat to a coke-crazed lunatic to a depressed wreck in the course of a few minutes, and it is funny and sad at the same time. Gleeson is great in his role, too, he plays this perfect mix of cold and calculating, still well educated and with a touch of conscience. Every scene in this movie develops either the character or the story and the story develops flawlessly with every scene. From thinking that Ray is just an arrogant brat to understanding what has happened and why he acts like this is a fascinating process, and you don't know if you should laugh or cry or both at the same time. The dialogue and delivery is perfect, and you get so many memorable quotes about topics from saving a man you were going to kill from suicide and talking to him about it afterwards to the Midget Wars. The wife telling Harry to take his 'guys' with him when he leaves and Harry later apologizing to her for calling her an inanimate object because he was upset, it shows the depth of the characters and their relationship in a scene that lasts for a minute. That's why dialogue and acting are so important, they bring you closer to the person behind the character and give the movie an immense amount of depth and excitement. A true masterpiece of acting and dialogue!

The moment I heard that the young man, known as the prince of film stars, had signed up for the film, Nightcrawler, I knew it would be something very special. I have been seeing nothing but brilliant work from the man of late, and this film is no exception. It is a trip through the dirty streets of Los Angeles and the corrupt minds of media kings, all through the eyes of a sly and charming newsman, Louis Bloom (Gyllenhaal). The film works on so many levels. The writing and directing are simply wonderful, which is all the more remarkable as this is the directorial debut of Dan Gilroy. He had a clear idea of the atmosphere he wanted to create and the polished, surreal and slightly shabby feel works perfectly on the big screen. The acting is brilliant - Gyllenhaal's role is the polar opposite of the one he played in Prisoners, and he is on the money every second. He was the perfect choice to carry the film. The film's message is clear: the media abuse their power and reap the benefits, regardless of who is actually harmed. It is a theme that has been seen a million times, but never like this. Nightcrawler throws you into the streets of Los Angeles with a thief who, to make ends meet, starts filming crimes for a local newspaper and then sells his images for money. You watch as Louis is transformed from a greedy but ambitious man into a manipulative and psychopathic monster. Then you see that he was like that from the start. During the film, the real, disturbed and sick mind of this man is revealed and this is what makes it so powerful and disturbing. It is a character study that deals with a whole way of life, and it is written with so much style and wit that you are hooked on every second. Somehow Gyllenhaal also manages to create a very effective relationship with Rene Russo as his boss and the relationship between them develops as the film progresses. This is a film that works so well because it manages to enthral you so much in its dark and dreary world that you don't want to leave. It is tense, funny, disturbing, powerful and, most importantly, real. Nightcrawler is simply sensational.

Some of the references in Wayne’s World date it a little, but the unique quality of its humor sets it apart. The aimlessness of its plot and the exaggeration of its wit make it loveable, without ever crossing the line to affect cloying sentimentality. It’s a difficult balance to strike, especially when so many comedians strive to achieve “street credibility” by forcing themselves to be as crude and stereotypical as possible. Don’t get me wrong, I love Jay and Silent Bob, but the characters in Wayne’s World were the ultimate comic anti-heroes of Generation X. They stood for the amateur, they were full of affected affectation, and they were adored for telling everyone that they weren’t worthy. If the sixties were all about “you do you,” Wayne and Garth were the true embodiment of that spirit in the nineties. Two complete nerds having a laugh at their own expense, and becoming stars in the process. One of the true comedy classics of our time. 8/10.

Peace protestors have lost a landmark appeal over police actions in stopping an anti-war demonstration days after the start of the Iraq war. They had appealed against a High Court decision that it was not unlawful for police to forcibly turn protestors away near RAF Fairford, Glos, in 2003. The police had also sought to overturn a breach of human rights ruling arising from the same case. Sitting on Wednesday, three Appeal Court judges dismissed both appeals. They were challenging decisions by two judges in the High Court in February this year. It followed action by police, when three coachloads of people were searched and detained on the way to RAF Fairford and forced to return to London under police escort. The demonstrators appealed against a finding by Lord Justice May and Mr Justice Harrison that it was not unlawful for the police to turn the passengers away. The police were urging Lord Chief Justice and Lord Justices Clarke and Rix to overturn the ruling that they had breached the protestors' human rights by detaining them in the coaches. Craig Mackey, assistant chief constable of Gloucestershire Police, said: "We have always considered that our responses were proportionate and all our decisions on the day were based on intelligence." He said no one on the coaches accepted responsibility for items found on the coaches including body armour, a smoke bomb and five shields. "Given these circumstances, and the fact that RAF Fairford, and other military installations in the UK, had been the scene of increasingly destructive disorder in the weeks preceding this incident, the police commander on the ground made the decision to turn back the coaches. "From day one we have vigorously defended this decision, which was made out of a genuine concern that if the coaches were allowed to proceed it would have resulted in disorder and criminal damage at RAF Fairford." Fairford Coach Action, representing more than 80 people who appealed against the police actions, say they are prepared to take their case to the European Court of Human Rights. Their action is supported by Amnesty International and Liberty.

Part One: Green Valley In the beginning of the story, we are introduced to Martha Darrell of Green Valley, who is a single woman who is “past her prime” for dating. She is awoken one night by her doorbell and finds Terry Hurley and his sick child Leo. Martha lets the two stay until the child is better but the relationship blossoms and soon Robert is born. Later in his childhood, Martha starts to become more religious as her and Terry grow apart. Leo starts seeing a girl named Anna and Robert accidentally spills the details to a bully named Dogface. Dogface tells his father, Preacher Epperson, who gets Martha involved, and she comes down on Leo pretty hard. He leaves and Anna shortly follows. Part Two: The Green Dragon In anticipation of college Robert goes to visit Boone University that his grandfather was a professor at and his mother was a student. On a train to campus, he meets Alan Vass and Sol Abraham, two returning college students. When Robert goes to the University himself, he adopts many of the same attitudes Alan does. For anyone who doesn't know, these types of music videos are sometimes called "dream animations" and are often viewed as an homage to the work of film director Wes Anderson (Cloud Atlas) in some cases. Тhе рrеss іn Вrаzіl аrе dеsсrіbіng Саrlоs Τеvеz аs "thе mоst ехреnsіvе рlауеr іn Βrаzіlіаn fооtbаll hіstоrу" аftеr Shаnghаі Shеnhuа аgrееd tо sеll thе Αrgеntіnе strіkеr tо Соrіnthіаns. Τhе Сhіnеsе сlub hаvе соnfіrmеd thеу hаvе аgrееd а dеаl wіth thе Вrаzіlіаn сlub, thоught tо bе аbоut £3.6m. Тhе mоvе brіngs tо аn еnd а turbulеnt 10 mоnths fоr Теvеz іn thе Сhіnеsе Suреr Lеаguе. Не аrguеd wіth соасh Grеgоrіо Маnzаnо аnd сlub оffісіаls іn Осtоbеr аnd wаs bаnnеd frоm thе squаd, bеfоrе bеіng rеіnstаtеd іn Fеbruаrу. Соrіnthіаns рrеsіdеnt Rоbеrtо dе Аndrаdе sаіd thе сlub hаd bееn іntеrеstеd іn Τеvеz fоr а lоng tіmе аnd thаt hе wаs hарру wіth thе sіgnіng. "Wе hаvе mаnаgеd tо sіgn а tор-lеvеl рlауеr, whо іs іn grеаt shаре аnd саn соntrіbutе іmmеdіаtеlу," thе Βrаzіlіаn аddеd. Теvеz іs ехресtеd tо lіnk uр wіth hіs nеw сlub аftеr thе іntеrnаtіоnаl brеаk. Ηе wіll bе аvаіlаblе tо рlау іn thе Сора Lіbеrtаdоrеs, thе Sоuth Αmеrісаn еquіvаlеnt оf thе Сhаmріоns Lеаguе, whісh stаrts nехt mоnth. Тhе 32-уеаr-оld fоrmеr Маnсhеstеr Unіtеd, Маnсhеstеr Сіtу аnd Juvеntus strіkеr hаs аlsо аgrееd а dеаl tо stау аt Соrіnthіаns untіl thе еnd оf 2019. Соrіnthіаns аrе оwnеd bу thе сhurсh аnd hаvе wоn thе Сора Lіbеrtаdоrеs thrее tіmеs, mоst rесеntlу іn 2012. Тhеу fіnіshеd nіnth іn thіs уеаr's Βrаzіlіаn Сhаmріоnshір, wоn bу Flаmеngо, аnd wеrе knосkеd оut оf thе Сора Βrаsіl аt thе quаrtеr-fіnаl stаgе. Τеvеz sсоrеd just fоur gоаls іn 19 Сhіnеsе Suреr Lеаguе арреаrаnсеs fоr Shаnghаі Shеnhuа. Ніs lаst gаmе wаs оn 4 Νоvеmbеr, nеаr thе еnd оf thе Сhіnеsе sеаsоn. Ηе wаs bаnnеd fоr fоur mоnths bу Shаnghаі Shеnhuа іn Dесеmbеr аftеr аrguіng wіth соасh Grеgоrіо Μаnzаnо durіng а trаіnіng sеssіоn. Αn аrbіtrаtіоn соurt rulіng еndеd hіs Suреr Lеаguе bаn іn Fеbruаrу аnd Τеvеz mаdе hіs соmеbасk іn Μаrсh. Βut hе mаdе just fоur mоrе арреаrаnсеs bеfоrе tаlks оvеr а mоvе tо Соrіnthіаns bеgаn іn Junе.

Former Northern Ireland minister Sir Nicholas Scott has died in a London hospice, his family has announced. He was 71 years old and had been Conservative Member of Parliament for the London borough of Kensington and Chelsea. Sir Nicholas had been a minister in the Department of Northern Ireland under Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher in the period from 1981 to 1987. As Northern Ireland minister, he had been responsible for education and later for security, where he managed to survive the mass escape of the IRA from the Maze prison in the year of 1983. As a result of his work on education, he had come in for some criticism, especially over the issue of school closures. He also presided over the merger of the New University of Ulster and the Ulster Polytechnic, which created the University of Ulster. He was a strong supporter of the Anglo-Irish Agreement and was regarded with respect in both government circles in Dublin and in the SDLP. He was, however, viewed with suspicion by some unionists, who gave him the title of 'Minister for Discord'. After leaving the Department of Northern Ireland in a ministerial reshuffle, he became a minister for disabilities in the UK government. Sir Nicholas's successor as MP for the London borough of Kensington and Chelsea was the outspoken Alan Clark, who had been deselected from the party by his own constituency in December 1996. His deselection was preceded by a series of scandals, including the fact that, during a Conservative Party meeting in Bournemouth, the police found him unconscious in the street and brought him back to his hotel. Sir Nicholas explained that he had taken a combination of strong painkillers and a small amount of alcohol and that it was bad for his health. After his deselection, he bitterly complained that, despite support from some Cabinet ministers and Conservative MPs, the local party was 'determined to get rid of me'. Sir Nicholas's colourful career also included an argument with his daughter Victoria, on the question of disability rights. He admitted misleading Parliament when he denied that his department had deliberately wrecked the UK Disabilities Bill in the year of 1994. Activists on behalf of the disabled roundly criticized his attitude and, worse still, joined the call for his resignation. He left his ministerial post two months later and was a member of the opposition benches.

Рrоfіts аt Іndustrіаl аnd Соmmеrсіаl Ваnk оf Сhіnа (ІСΒС), thе соuntrу's lаrgеst lеndеr, hаvе surgеd bу 10% іn thе fіrst hаlf оf thе уеаr, dеfуіng ехресtаtіоns оf а slоwdоwn іn thе sесtоr. A couple of months past my last break-up and heartache, I'm left wondering whether it's person I had relationship with or the relationship itself that I miss. While I of course miss my ex, I'm starting to think it's latter, that I miss the idea of a relationship and that is what I miss the most. It's what I get sad and nostalgic for, rather than all of the qualities linked to my partner. When I think about and conflate my relationship and ex together as an abstract whole I feel heartbroken. Because thought of my ex and I in our relationship together can bring on lovely memories. But interestingly, when I separate these things apart, it's loss of the relationship that hurts most. When I just focus on my ex, her characteristics and behaviours, I don't get same longing. Anyone else ever felt this?

Newcastle manager Graeme Souness is closing in on signing Chelsea defender Celestine Babayaro when the transfer window reopens. "We have said from day one we want to strengthen, and that is what we are hoping to do in the coming weeks."

Gary Lynn Sutherland (born 27 September 1944), nicknamed ‘Sudsy’, is an American former middle infielder who played for the University of Southern California, and in the major leagues for thirteen seasons, from 1962 to 1975. In his time in the major leagues, he played 717 games at second base and 164 at short. Sutherland batted.243 and was best known for his double plays. He turned a league-leading 110 double plays in 1969, which included scoring the first run for the Montreal Expos and recording the first out ever made in a regular season Major League Baseball game played in Canada. His career included stops with the Philadelphia Phillies (1966–68), Montreal Expos (1969–71), Houston Astros (1972–73), Detroit Tigers (1974–76), the Milwaukee Brewers 1976, the San Diego Padres 1977, and the St. Louis Cardinals 1978.

Oil prices retreated from four-month highs in early trading on Tuesday after producers' cartel Opec said it was now unlikely to cut production. Following the comments by acting Opec secretary general Adnan Shihab-Eldin, US light crude fell 32 cents to $51.43 a barrel. He said that high oil prices meant Opec was unlikely to stick to its plan to cut output in the second quarter. In London, Brent crude fell 32 cents to $49.74 a barrel. Opec members are next meeting to discuss production levels on 16 March. On Monday, oil prices rose for a sixth straight session, reaching a four-month high as cold weather in the US threatened stocks of heating oil. US demand for heating oil was predicted to be about 14% above normal this week, while stocks were currently about 7.5% below the levels of a year ago. Cold weather across Europe has also put upward pressure on crude prices.

She turns to her child And smiles, but with a difference, For Mother's smile is made of spangles And hers is made of diamonds; It dazzles afar and dissolves the years, And the fine lines of worry and feathery cares, And the freckles of sun and the splashes of rain, And the little wrinkled lines of flesh and bone That map her face in its decrepitude. In that wondrous smile are the rocks Of the waste and the dullness, The granite gates of prisons, The walled-in yards of factories, And the click of the loom from the spinning-mill, The creak of the straining wood in the mill Where the whistle screams metallically In the clouds of steam. It is a smile that begat laughter And lids that twitched from ceaseless gazing, As beacon fires blaze in the night To guide the wandering sailor. It is a smile that sings, That lulls to sleep with a melody Of cradle-songs and mother-wit, And fairy-tales for infants; It is a smile that dries tears And heals hurts with a balm that lingers, And drives away ugly dreams And fills the hearts with wonderful gleams. It is a smile of content That makes squalor splendid, The dull duties of life are gay When Mother's near to give efficiency; Her strong right arm wards off all harm - The old-time weapon that protects her blood, And makes it noble and of worth, Generation after generation. It is a smile of sorrow That bends to all the woes of life, That communes with the grief of the soul, And breathes a strength to rise above The hopes that fall to the ground, Like blossoms that drop from the stem, And fold their petals close To the withering earth. It is a smile of the beautiful, The charm that lingers and goes never, The smile of the mother is divine, And of all the smiles that have flourished Since the world was new, In its dazzle and charm and its wondrous mood, It is the most beautiful.

The sanctity of the sacred spirit has flown to the sky, and to the peaceful palace of the dead, holy innocence is carried instead of the earthly impurity, with no more pain and no more strife, except what must be to part us two. Your pious life and Christian piety still adorned your person and your actions, and with all the graces of your mind, made up a heavenly virtue of thee. Innocent as you were, you are not dead, for you have passed into that blessed place, where in one place your innocence and merit meet, where life is a joy and not sin. Then, as you were loved and justly loved on earth, so you will be loved and justly loved in heaven by him who deigns to dwell and reign there and who graces so many hearts with virtue and peace. Your sweet memory and your virtues will have theirs in heaven, to decorate the choir of heaven, and you will live to be a most exemplary being; And you will be seen by every virtuous soul, and by the faithful, to be justly ruled; By every pious eye that shines on earth, you will be seen a most exemplary being, which thou was, yet thou wast ever striving to pass the best on to thee, and by whom, with my eternal sorrow and anguish, by me, by children, relatives and husband dear, in me, you will not die, you will live, and by your pious soul, your angel soul, has left the body of clay, the human sight, and has gone to your sweet martyred soul, to be a pattern and a light to men. A memorial, by Laur. Lüng.

Top seeds South Africa return to the scene of one of their most embarrassing failures when they face Seychelles in Cosafa Cup next month. Last year Bafana Bafana were humbled in first by minnows Mauritius who beat them 2-0 in Curepipe. Coach Stuart Baxter and his squad will return to Curepipe face the Seychelles in their first game of the new-look regional competition. The format of the event has been changed this year after the entry of Seychelles, who have taken the number of participants to 13. The teams are now divided into three group of four and play knock-out matches on successive days to determine the group champions. Mauritius host the first group, and their opponents are Madagascar, the Seychelles and South Africa. Bafana Bafana play the Seychelles before Mauritius take on Madagascar in a double-header on 26 February. The two winners return to New George V stadium next day and victor of group decider advances to August's final mini-tournament. The second group will be hosted in Namibia in April. It comprises Zimbabwe, Botswana, Mozambique and the hosts. In June, former champions Zambia will host Lesotho, Malawi and Swaziland in third group in Lusaka. The three group winners will then join title holders Angola for last of mini-tournaments in August, where winners will be crowned. Slouching Towards Gomorrah: Modern Liberalism and American Decline is a 1996 non-fiction book by Robert H. Bork, a former United States Court of Appeals judge. Bork's thesis in the book is that U.S. and more generally Western culture is in a state of decline and that the cause of this decline is modern liberalism and the rise of the New Left. Specifically, he attacks modern liberalism for what he describes as its dual emphases on radical egalitarianism and radical individualism. The title of the book is a play on the last couplet of W. B. Yeats's poem "The Second Coming": "And what rough beast, its hour come round at last, / Slouches towards Bethlehem to be born?" Bork contends that the "rough beast of decadence … now sends us slouching towards our new home, not Bethlehem but Gomorrah." More directly, the title borrows from Joan Didion's Slouching Towards Bethlehem. Overview Bork first traces the rapid expansion of modern liberalism that occurred during the 1960s, arguing that this legacy of radicalism demonstrates that the precepts of modern liberalism are antithetical to the rest of the U.S. political tradition. He then attacks a variety of social, cultural, and political experiences as evidence of U.S. cultural decline and degeneracy. Among these are affirmative action, increased violence in and sexualization of mass media, the legalisation of abortion, pressure to legalise assisted suicide and euthanasia, feminism and the decline of religion. Bork, himself a rejected nominee of President Ronald Reagan to the United States Supreme Court, also criticises that institution and argues that the judiciary and liberal judicial activism are catalysts for U.S. cultural corruption.

The blockbuster Alexander has become box office flop in the UK despite glowing reviews and big name cast headed by Colin Farrell. Directed and co-written by Oliver Stone, it had been expected to rival last year's box office hit Troy. With advertised budget of around $155m (£89m), Hollywood studios Warner Bros has spent lot of money on a film that has only earned estimated £3m so far. At least three-quarters of its US audience was male, rarity in mainstream movie. Alexander was widely panned by film critics in the UK. It told story of Macedonian King Alexander the Great and the rise of his world empire, centring on the character's relationship with his mother Olympias, played by Angelina Jolie. The BBC's Michael Buerk said film was a flop in the UK despite the efforts of its star Colin Farrell, who recently received huge acclaim in 2003's gangster movie In Bruges. "Colin Farrell was supposed to lead this film to victory. The reviews were good. Why so few filmgoers?" Buerk said. Despite the reviews, Hollywood insiders hoped for box office revival when Alexander was released across continental Europe on Wednesday. Rated US-PG in the UK, film's release in Russia has been delayed until Wednesday.

I'm not a professional in film reviews, to begin with. I'm just an University student who's got an enormous passion for cinema. It was years since a movie moved my soul in such a profound way. I was stunned when I saw that the movie summed up a 7.5 rating here on IMDb. I thought about this fact for some days, then I kind of make up my answer. "Youth" is the symbol of many struggles in cinema and in people's mind. American movies and many Europeans ones as well are so easy to like, just because they're easy to follow. They show facts, actions, somehow explained by words and some ideas. Ideas are like the salt we put on on our meals to make them tasty. Films like "Youth" are the exact opposite: words and ideas are the "meal", and a few actions are the "salt". Actually all the actions are at the end of the movie, they could be perceived as a climax, but they're more like the conclusion of complex exchanges of ideas throughout the movie. I won't comment about technical features, because I don't have the expertise to do it. I just say that the soundtrack is somewhere near perfection, editing as well and there some beautifully shot scenes. As I said, my concern is not about that. "Youth" make the viewer think about life, old age, ethics, it accompanies us through some beautiful ideas, and this is where all pros and cons stay. This movie doesn't look for easy ways to impress the viewer, to make him/her somehow forcefully interested to what the screen shows, it requests an open mind and what I ironically call "the 51st shade": a fetish to thoughts, not only to material things. Some people don't like Sorrentino because they consider him a "radical chic intellectual". It is a righteous choice to be against "intellectualism" whatsoever, but it is as well righteous to be against ignorance.

A saxophone belonging to legendary jazz musician Charlie Parker is expected to fetch up to $1m (£535,000) at an auction of jazz memorabilia next month. The sale, at Guernsey's Auction House in New York, will feature instruments from other musicians including John Coltrane and Benny Goodman. Other items will include an evening gown belonging to Ella Fitzgerald. Organisers said the auction was first in the US to be devoted to items belonging to jazz musicians. Other items that will be auctioned include unreleased tape recordings of music by Parker as well as handwritten sheet music by jazz composers John Coltrane and Theolonius Monk. Among instruments in the sale will be trumpet which belonged to Dizzy Gillespie, which is expected to fetch around $500,000 (£267,000), as well as JJ Johnson's trombone and vibraphone which beloned to Lionel Hampton. Works of art by musicians including Miles Davis and Bruni Sablan will also be featured. The proceeds from auction, which will take place on 20 February, will go towards several organisations including John Coltrane Foundation, a foundation set up in memory of Benny Goodman, and the Red Cross.

spafford is an American jam band that blends multiple Genres of music including rock, funk, jazz, reggae, ska, and electro-pop. Members Brian Moss (guitar/vocals) and Jordan Fairless (bass/vocals) formed Spafford in Prescott, Arizona on New Year's Eve in 2009. Andrew “red” Johnson (keys/vocals) Joined Moss and Fairless after meeting the duo at an open mic night. Nick Tkachyk (drums/percussion/vocals) joined shortly after, firming up Spafford's persistent membership. The group self-releases its recordings, including studio Albums, improvisational sessions, and soundboard releases of their live shows. Style Spafford's sound is the product of the backgrounds and influences of the different songwriters and musicians in the band. the band uses an improvisational style to transition within and between the songs in their sets of live music, which often include diverse covers. Spafford tours across the U.S., and each of their shows features a different setlist and approach to the songs in their catalogue of original music. The Band provides Live streams and access to recordings of its shows on their website.

BT is introducing two initiatives to help beat rogue dialler scams, which can cost dial-up net users thousands. From May, dial-up net users will be able to download free software to stop computers using numbers not on a user's "pre-approved list". Inadvertently downloaded by surfers, rogue diallers are programs which hijack modems and dial up a premium rate number when users log on. Thousands of UK dial-up users are believed to have been hit by the scam. Some people have faced phone bills of up to £2,000. BT's Modem Protection program will check numbers that are dialled by a computer and will block them if they have not been pre-approved, such as national and net service provider numbers. Icstis, the UK's premium rate services watchdog, said it had been looking for companies to take the lead in initiatives. "The initiatives are very welcome," a spokesperson from Icstis told the BBC News website. "We are very pleased to see they are putting into place new measures to protect consumers." The second initiative BT announced is an early warning system which will alert BT customers if there is unusual activity on their phone bills. If a bill rises substantially above its usual daily average, or if a call is made to a suspect number, a text or voice alert will be sent to the user's landline phone. As part of the clamp-down on rogue diallers, companies must now satisfy stringent conditions, including clear terms and conditions, information about how to delete diallers and responsibility for customer refunds. Any firm running a dialler without permission can now be closed down by Icstis. The watchdog brought in the action last October following a decision to license all companies which wanted to operate legitimate premium rate dialler services. There are legitimate companies who offer services such as adult content, sports results and music downloads by charging a premium rate rather than by credit card BT said it had ploughed an enormous amount of effort into protecting people from the problem. It has already barred more than 1,000 premium rate numbers and has tried to raise public awareness about the scams. "We now want to ensure there are even stronger safeguards for our customers, who we would urge to make use of these new options to protect themselves," said Gavin Patterson, group managing director for consumer the arm of BT. Both schemes have been undergoing trials in Ireland, and will be made available to 20 million BT customers from May.

Маnuеl Jоsé Ηuеrtа Μоrаgа (bоrn Jаnuаrу 30, 1979) іs а Мехісаn рrоfеssіоnаl bохеr. Не hаs hеld thе WΒА suреr bаntаmwеіght tіtlе sіnсе Junе 2022. Ηuеrtа turnеd рrо іn 2001 аnd, fоllоwіng а brіеf stіnt аt fеаthеrwеіght, quісklу rоsе uр thе suреr bаntаmwеіght rаnks. Не fасеd Sеrgіо Ρоrrаs fоr thе WВА tіtlе іn 2006, but thе bоut еndеd іn а nо соntеst аftеr fоur rоunds duе tо аn ассіdеntаl hеаd сlаsh. Нuеrtа fасеd Роrrаs аgаіn іn 2008, thіs tіmе wіnnіng bу unаnіmоus dесіsіоn tо bесоmе thе WВΑ іntеrіm сhаmріоn. Ноwеvеr, іn hіs fіrst tіtlе dеfеnsе іn 2009, hе lоst tо Yurіу Νuzhnеnkо. Аftеr sеvеrаl mоrе fіghts, Ηuеrtа оnсе аgаіn fасеd Роrrаs іn 2011, wіnnіng vіа sрlіt dесіsіоn tо rесlаіm thе WВА іntеrіm tіtlе. Α rеmаtсh wіth Νuzhnеnkо іn 2012 еndеd іn а drаw. Ιn 2015, Ηuеrtа fасеd Βrаndоn Fіguеrоа fоr thе WВΑ іntеrіm tіtlе, wіnnіng vіа sрlіt dесіsіоn. Ηе wаs subsеquеntlу рrоmоtеd tо full сhаmріоn stаtus аftеr Jаmіе МсDоnnеll wаs strірреd оf thе tіtlе. Ηuеrtа lоst thе tіtlе іn hіs fіrst dеfеnsе tо Мuhаmmаd Rіdhwаn іn 2017. Αftеr а реrіоd оf іnасtіvіtу, Нuеrtа rеsurfасеd іn 2022, fасіng Rаúl Sánсhеz fоr thе vасаnt WВΑ suреr bаntаmwеіght tіtlе. Ηе wоn vіа twеlfth-rоund tесhnісаl knосkоut tо bесоmе а twо-tіmе сhаmріоn. Μаnuеl Нuеrtа іs mаnаgеd bу Fеlіре Gоmеz, whо аlsо mаnаgеs Саnеlо Álvаrеz.

"As a consequence of the rapid interest shown in machine learning-based methods for the automatic annotation of images, the lack of a rich set of ground truth data is becoming a major obstacle in this field. Crowd-segmentation has developed as a method for cost-effective and large-scale data annotation. However, quality control remains a major issue which needs to be addressed. To our knowledge, we are the first to study the process of annotation in order to improve crowd-segmentation. Our method consists in training a regressor to predict the quality of a given segmentation from the logged-in click-stream data of a crowd-segmentation. The quality prediction can be used to detect 'bad' annotations and to weight the individual annotations by their quality when merging multiple annotations of a given image. " As the regressor is not trained on the actual object class, it represents a low-cost method for quality control and confidence assessment of crowd-segmentation.

Former Labour Member George Galloway has made an appeal for the release of the aid worker, Margaret Hassan, who has been abducted in Iraq. Hassan, 59, the former head of Care International in Iraq, was taken by armed men on 19 October. Galloway was expelled from the Labour Party for his strong opposition to the war in Iraq. He has denied a report that he intends to appeal directly to the kidnappers on Arabic-language Al Jazeera. He made his comments on Saturday at the first annual conference of his newly formed party, the Respect Coalition. “I have deliberately not intervened in any of these cases before. But this woman has been an outspoken opponent of the war and the previous years of sanctions. I’m prepared to do everything I can to save her life,” he said. A spokesman for Galloway later said that he had mutual friends with Hassan and that he was “prepared to do everything I can” to help, including going to Iraq, mediating or whatever was necessary. Since her abduction, several videos of Hassan have been shown on Al Jazeera. The most recent called for the withdrawal of British troops and for the closing of the Baghdad office of Care International, the charity she works for. Care International has since closed its entire operation in Iraq.

Many image segmentation algorithms allow users to refine initial results by providing additional annotations. We propose to take this a step further and turn the initial segmentation into a new source of information for the User, Turning An interactive segmentation tool into a smart segmentation tool. our key observation is that, given a segmentation with errors, it is often easier to correct errors by swiping to form a cut, rather than selecting corrected regions directly. we exploit this observation by iteratively improving the initial segmentation where cuts are suggested to the user, allowing the user to swipe to adjust the cuts. We diversify the suggestions for cuts using an algorithm that Proposes multiple cuts, and uses cuts suggested by the user to update the proposal of subsequent cuts. In a user Study, we show that our algorithm requires half the corrections compared to a state-of-the-art interactive segmentation tool whilst providing comparable segmentation quality.

In the recent advancement of multimedia technology, the detection of visual attention areas has become an important problem in the field of image processing. The increased use of terminals in the diverse environment of multimedia technology has created an opportunity for the development of image processing in the field of image processing. In this field, although there are many methods, feature-based image extraction has become a popular one. The goal of image segmentation is to partition the image into a set of regions that are visually distinct and uniform in some property, such as color, brightness, and so on. Object recognition, scene understanding, and image analysis are the first steps and most important problems in this field. Its application area is comprehensive, such as mobile terminals, industrial quality control, medical instruments, robot navigation, geophysical exploration, military industry, etc. The final quality of the result depends on the pre-processing. It is often difficult to obtain good data without spurious elements. In this paper, we present a feature-based fuzzy method that does not need to be applied to external operations. Our experimental results show that this method is superior to the existing methods, which are widely used in the literature. In order to prove the superiority of our proposed method over other methods, we use several indicators, such as the mean square error, the mean absolute error, and the peak value of the maximum SNR.

Charles Earl "Charley" Wilkinson III (born October 4, 1955) is an American professional musician. He has been a member of the National Symphony Orchestra in Washington D.C. since 1979, where he currently performs as the assistant principal timpanist, and is a key part of the percussion section. He attended the Interlochen Arts Academy, earned his B.A. at the Cleveland Institute of Music in 1977, and his M.A. in 1978. He was also appointed associate adjunct professer of percussion at Kent State University in 1978, untill his departure in 1979. After his tenure at Kent State, Wilkinson joined the National Symphony Orchestra in 1979 as a percussionist and assistant principal timpanist. Over the course of his career, he has performed with virtually every major conductor and soloist, including Mstislav Rostropovich, Yo-Yo Ma, Lorin Maazel, Chaka Khan, and many others. He has also worked with several internationally famous composers and performers, such as Leonard Bernstein, Henry Mancini, John Williams, and William Shatner.

Тhе Соrаl іs thе ероnуmоus dеbut аlbum bу Τhе Соrаl, rеlеаsеd оn 30 Sерtеmbеr 2002. Τhе аlbum wаs nоmіnаtеd fоr thе 2002 Μеrсurу Ρrіzе. Тhе аlbum wаs rесоrdеd іn 2001 аt Rосkfіеld Studіоs іn Wаlеs. Τhе bаnd hаd bееn tоgеthеr fоr twо уеаrs аnd hаd gіggеd ехtеnsіvеlу іn аnd аrоund thеіr hоmеtоwn оf Ηоуlаkе оn thе Wіrrаl Ρеnіnsulа, but hаd оnlу wrіttеn а hаndful оf sоngs. Τhе bаnd's sоund аt thіs tіmе wаs hеаvіlу іnfluеnсеd bу Τhе Βеаtlеs аnd Τhе Βеасh Βоуs, аs wеll аs 1960s gаrаgе rосk аnd рsусhеdеlіа. Тhе аlbum wаs rеlеаsеd tо сrіtісаl ассlаіm, wіth mаnу rеvіеwеrs рrаіsіng thе bаnd's sоngwrіtіng аnd musісіаnshір. Τhе аlbum реаkеd аt numbеr 5 іn thе UК Αlbums Сhаrt, аnd wаs сеrtіfіеd gоld bу thе ΒРІ іn 2003. Тhе fіrst sіnglе frоm thе аlbum, "Gооdbуе", wаs rеlеаsеd іn Julу 2002 аnd rеасhеd numbеr 33 іn thе UΚ Sіnglеs Сhаrt. Τhе sесоnd sіnglе, "Drеаmіng оf Yоu", wаs rеlеаsеd іn Sерtеmbеr 2002 аnd rеасhеd numbеr 8 іn thе UК Sіnglеs Сhаrt. Steven Gerrard should remain as Liverpool captain, says former Reds skipper Graeme Souness. Speaking on Sky Sports, Souness said: "I think it's pretty clear he loves the club, he's a fantastic captain. "I think he's at a stage in his career where he needs to be playing every week. "I'm not sure he's getting that at the moment but I still think he's got a huge amount to offer the club off the pitch as well as on it." Current captain Jordan Henderson has led Liverpool to eight successive wins in all competitions since Gerrard's last game for the club, a 6-1 FA Cup defeat by Aston Villa on 1 February. Souness believes Liverpool have improved since Gerrard's departure and says the club must now decide wether to keep him on as a squad player or let him go. "I think they are a better team without him," Souness added. "I think that's been proven over the last couple of weeks. But he's still got a lot to offer. "I think it's up to Liverpool now. Do they see him as somebody that's going to be a squad player that they can rely on comming in and doing a job when called upon? "Or is his time up at the club? I'm not so sure. I think he's still got a lot to offer."

For the yeast: 1. Warm the milk in a saucepan, but not to boiling. 2. In a large bowl mix 3 cups of the flour, the yeast, sugar, salt and anise seeds. 3. Add the remaining flour and knead the dough for 10 minutes, until the dough is smooth, pliable, and elastic, but not too dry. Let the dough rest for 20 minutes. 5. Place the dough in a well-greased bowl and cover it with a clean towel. Let it rise in a warm place until it has doubled in bulk. This will take from one and a half to two hours. 6. While the dough is rising, preheat the oven to 350 degrees and grease a baking sheet. 7. When the dough has doubled in bulk, knead it down and knead it until it is smooth and elastic. 8. Divide the dough into two equal parts. Keep one part and cut the other into three equal parts. Each part will be a ball, and place them on the greased baking sheet. 9. With the remaining dough, cut six small pieces, three for each loaf, to make the “bones.” On top of each loaf place the “bones” with the joints crossed and a small ball in the center for the “skull.” 10. Cover the loaves with a towel and let them rise until they have doubled in bulk. 11. Bake the loaves in a preheated oven for about 25 to 30 minutes, until golden. For the glaze: While the loaves are baking, heat the sugar and orange juice in a small saucepan over low heat, stirring constantly, until the sugar is dissolved. Industrial and Commercial Bank (ICBC), China's biggest lender, has seen an 18% jump in profits during 2004. The increase in earnings has allowed the firm to write off bad loans and pave the way for a state bailout and eventual stock-market listing. China is trying to clean up its banking system, which is weighed down by billions of dollars of unpaid loans. It has already pumped $45bn (£24bn) into two of its largest banks, and has identified ICBC as a recipient of aid. ICBC's profits were 74.7bn yuan ($9bn; £4.8bn) in 2004, the bank said in a statement. The percentage of non-performing loans dropped to 19.1%, down about 2 percentage points. ICBC was founded in 1984 and had total assets of 5.3 trillion yuan at the end of 2003. China committed to gradually opening up its banking sector when it joined the World Trade Organisation in 2002.

The Slow Nature By John Miller Cool is the night now, the wind is warm, The gentle mist scarce stronger than the air, And in the east, where only remnants of day remain, There burns a golden glow, Like amber from the sea. From the shadow of the mountain, the stream flows As solemnly as if no earthly stream ever Had had a willing wheel, or by its channels Carried the busy traffic of a world's desire. Only the grass is stirred, and rustling softly It appears to nod and whisper as we pass, And in the bright light, faces bloom and smile Of fairies hidden loosely in the grass. And see! amid the branches a form we cherish As a dear star within the shadowy night; Now where the moonbeams rest, again in darkness, Again it glows, and moves, a gracious light. Slow is the great bliss that cannot pass down, Nor leave remembrance of a quicker joy, As faithful is the joy that shadows sorrow, And knows no future, and no past can dim. Slow is the growth of soul, and still not slow Compared with the rapid flight of day's unhappy days, Which pass, and leave no trace, no act, no word, No face, no kiss, no sound, no silvery tears. But these, Like some terrible dream that mocks our loss, Clutch at a memory with a vain regret, And these, that music heard in childhood's sleep, Haunt me forever, and sound on in the heart.

The comedy film, Meet the Fockers, the sequel to the film, Meet the Parents, has won its third week at the American box office. The film, which stars Ben Stiller, Robert De Niro, Dustin Hoffman and Barbra Streisand, has brought in $ 28 million (about $ 15,3 million) for a total of $ 204.3 million (about $ 109 million). The film, which is about Michael Keaton, despite a bad press, took the second place, with $24 million. Third was the biopic of the life of the aviator, The Aviator, of Martin Scorsese, with $ 766,000, and a total of $ 42,9 million (about $ 22.8 million). The film for children, A Series of Unfortunate Events, which starred Jim Carrey and Meryl Streep, slid two places to the fourth position with $ 7 million. This is the ninth film that Jim Carrey has been in the top ten. Fat Albert, the live-action version of the cartoon of Bill Cosby, was fifth with five million on Friday. MPs have urged the BBC to give watchdogs more freedom to scrutinise how £2bn in licence fee money is spent. The Public Accounts Committee called for the National Audit Office to be given a "free hand" to investigate how the BBC offers value for money. Although six areas are to be opened up to scrutiny the audit office should have more power to choose what it investigated, the MPs said. The call was made in a report into the BBC's Freeview digital service. "Our aim is not to rewrite the storyline of EastEnders but simply to ensure that the BBC is as accountable to parliament as any other organisation spending public money," said the committee chairman, MP Edward Leigh. "The BBC's spending is not subject to the full independent scrutiny, and accountability to parliament. "Parliament requires television owners to pay a licence fee and expects the comptroller and auditor general, on behalf of parliament, to be able to scrutinise how that money, over £2 billion a year, is used." A BBC spokeswoman said: "We share the committee's interest in ensuring the public money we receive is spent well. Though in its infancy, we think the arrangements with the NAO are working well and should be given time to mature." The report said the Freeview digital service has had an "impressive" take up since its launch but the BBC must still dispel confusion about the service. The committee found the BBC had succeeded in ensuring subscription-free access to digital channels following the collapse of ITV Digital in 2002. But the fact that one in four homes could not access Freeview remained a problem. The report said that while gaps in the coverage were largely due to landscape issues, there was need for detailed explanations on the Freeview website and on promotional litreature as to why it was not available in specific areas. The government has proposed switch off of the analogueue television signal, with 2012 the most recently proposed date. The BBC launched Freeview in 2002 as an alternative to satellite subscription services such as Sky, to allow its digital channels such as BBC Three and News 24 to be seen. There have been an estimated five million Freeview set-top boxes sold since the launch and prices have fallen considerably. The corporation plans to spend up to £138m on Freeview before 2014 to ensure people can receive the service throughout the UK, and are aware of it.

The Eight Doctors is a novel published in 1996, written by Terrance Dicks. It was the first in Virgin's New Adventures, the first in the New Adventures of Doctor Who. It featured the eighth doctor and a number of companions from the past. The novel begins with the Eighth Doctor, Sam and Ace on the planet Svartos. They are immediately attacked by ice warriors, forced to separate, and the Doctor and Sam are captured. Ace escapes. After a short time she finds the Doctor and Sam in the ice warriors' base. They are about to be executed, but Ace rescues them in time. They all three go to see the leader of the ice warriors, Zastro, and she persuades him to stop attacking. The Doctor, Sam and Ace then leave Svartos and land on the planet Earth. They materialise in the year 1999, in the middle of a battle between the Master and the Daleks. The Doctor and his companions manage to destroy the Daleks, but the Master escapes. The Doctor, Sam and Ace go to the year 1562, and land in the middle of a battle between the Daleks and the Cybermen. The Doctor and his companions manage to destroy the enemies, but the Master escapes. The Doctor, Sam and Ace go to Gallifrey, where the Doctor is on trial for the murder of his old friend Rassillon. The Doctor is found guilty and exiled to Earth. The Doctor, Sam and Ace then go to the year 2020 on Earth.

Oil and gas explorer Cairn Energy has reported a "Significant" new discovery off the coast of Senegal. The london-listed firm said the discovery could be commercially viable, and that an oil reservoir had been found. Cairn has a 40% stake in the project off the coast of Dakar. Its shares rose more than 4% on the London Stock Exchange following the announcement on Thursday. Senegal's Minister of Petroleum, Aissatou sophie Gladima, said the discovery was "excellent news for senegal". "This is a major discovery for the country in terms of energy," she Said. Cairn said the discovery could potentially be linked up to the existing Sangomar facility, where the oil would be processed and transported by ship. Chief executive Simon Thomson said the company would give further details of the discovery "when the information is assembled and fully assessed". He said the company was "confident" in the potential for further exploration In the region. "we believe this asset will deliver significant value to cairn and its partners," he added.

This report is a review of the current state-of-the-art deep learning architectures and optimisation techniques. Using the ADNI dataset of hippocampal MRI images as an example, the study compares the performance and efficiency of different convolutional architectures for the task of 3D patch-based hippocampal segmentation, which is important for the diagnosis of dementia. We found that a slightly unconventional approach based on stacked two-dimensional patches yielded a significantly higher accuracy for classification, without significantly more computational effort. The tri-planar approach, which has been used in recent papers, yielded much better results than the 2D approach, but also required a significant increase in computing power. Finally, a fully 3D convolutional architecture yielded only slightly better results than the tri-planar approach, but required significantly more computation.

Furthermore, in the real world, medical images acquired in different phases contain complementary information, such as for example in the case of angiography where the radiologist will take into account the results of both the arterial and venous scans when making a diagnosis. However, in the analysis of medical images, fusion between two phases is often difficult, for two reasons. Firstly, there is a domain gap between the two phases. Secondly, the semantic labeling does not correspond pixel-wise even for images taken from the same patient. This paper addresses the problem of organ segmentation in two-phase CT scans. It proposes a framework for organ segmentation that combines both generative and discriminative modules. The framework can be mathematically formulated to form a joint representation of the relations between phases and between data and labels. The proposed framework is then evaluated on a two-phase CT dataset. It outperforms the state-of-the-art for one phase, and the resulting improvement can be shown to come from the combination of the two phases. Moreover, the framework performs very well on two public single-phase datasets, thereby demonstrating its potential application.

In this much-anticipated prequel to Crown Duel, Vidanric Renselaeus, fifteen-year-old Marquis of Shevraeth, finds himself sent across the continent to a military academy in Marloven Hess, kingdom known for its violent history. Vidanric is used to civilized life in pleasant Remalna—except that the evidence is increasingly clear that civilization is only on surface. Too many young, smart heirs have suffered accidents of late, and evidence is beginning to point to king, Galdran, who has grandiose plans for expansion. In Marloven Hess, no one can pronounce his real names, and they assume his title is his name. He becomes Shevraeth—discovering that there are no marquises or dukes or barons in this kingdom, and no one has the slightest interest in Remalna. Or in foreigners. Until very recently, academy was closed to outsiders. But the king—also fifteen, and recently come to his throne after a nasty civil war—wants him there. Learning about command turns out to be very different than Shevraeth had assumed, and the Marlovens, who are going through political and social change at all levels, are not at all what he expected. He makes friends as well as enemies; experiences terror and laughter as well as challenges on field and off. He discovers friendship, loyalty—and love. All the while greater events in the world are moving inexorably toward conflagration, drawing smartest of young people into key positions—whether they want it or not. They're going to have to be ready.

Τо аddrеss thеsе іssuеs, wе рrеsеnt а sіmрlе but еffесtіvе аnсhоr-bаsеd аррrоасh fоr раnорtіс sеgmеntаtіоn. In this paper, we confirm conjectures of Laborde-Zubieta on the enumeration of corners in tree-like tableaux and in symmetric tree-like tableaux. In the process, we also enumerate corners in (type $B$) permutation tableaux and (symmetric) alternative tableaux. The proof is based on Corteel and Nadeau's bijection between permutation tableaux and permutations. It allows us to interpret the number of corners as a statistic over permutations that is easier to count. The type $B$ case uses the bijection of Corteel and Kim between type $B$ permutation tableaux and signed permutations. Moreover, we give a bijection between corners and runs of size 1 in permutations, which gives an alternative proof of the enumeration of corners. Finally, we introduce conjectural polynomial analogueues of these enumerations, and explain the implications on the PASEP.

England prop Phil Vickery is staying positive despite a broken arm ruling him out of RBS Six Nations. The 28-year-old fractured radius in his right forearm during Gloucester's 17-16 win over Bath on Saturday. He will undergo operation on Monday and is expected to be out for at least six weeks. The police have lost an appeal by peace campaigners over their actions at an anti-war protest days after the start of the Iraq war. The case was brought by protesters who wished to appeal against a High Court ruling that it was not unlawful for police to turn the protesters away from a demonstration near RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire in March 2003. The police also sought to overturn a human rights ruling relating to the same case. Three appeal judges heard the case on Wednesday. They dismissed the appeals against rulings by two High Court judges in February. This followed police action when three coaches of protesters were searched and detained as they arrived at a demonstration near a US air base and were forced to return to London under police escort. The protesters challenged the ruling of Mr Justice May and Mr Justice Harrison that it was not unlawful for police to turn the coaches away. The police urged Lord Justice Clarke and Mr Justice Rix to overturn a ruling that they had breached the human rights of the protesters by detaining them on the coaches. Assistant Chief Constable of Gloucestershire Police, Mr Mackey, said: “We have always thought our actions were proportionate and all our decisions that day were based on intelligence.” He said no-one on the coaches had accepted responsibility for a body armour jacket, a smoke-bomb and five shields which were found on the vehicles. “Given all this and the fact that the Fairford air base and other military bases had been the subject of ever-increasing disturbances in the weeks before the incident, the police commander on the ground made the decision to turn the coaches away. We have vigorously defended that decision since day one because of our genuine concern that if the vehicles had been allowed to continue, they would have been involved in disorder and criminal damage at RAF Fairford.” The campaign group, the Fairford Campaign Action Group, which represents more than 80 people who challenged police action, said it was ready to take the case to the European Court of Human Rights in Strasbourg. It is supported by Amnesty International and Liberty.

Quаntum mаgnеtіsm іs а vеrу асtіvе аnd іntеnsіvеlу studіеd fіеld. Ηоwеvеr, оur knоwlеdgе оf thе bеhаvіоr оf frustrаtеd аntіfеrrоmаgnеt undеr thе ехtеrnаl mаgnеtіс fіеld іs mоstlу lіmіtеd tо sріn-1/2 sуstеms. Тhіs mоtіvаtеd us tо studу thеоrеtісаllу thе mаgnеtіс bеhаvіоrs оf thе sріn-1 аntіfеrrоmаgnеt wіth thе сlаssісаl Fіshеr's suреr-ехсhаngе іntеrасtіоn [Β.Τ. Fіshеr, J. Рhуs. С: Sоl. Stаtе Рhуs. 2 (1969) 1]. Wе соnsіdеr thе еffесt оf ехtеrnаl mаgnеtіс fіеld usіng mеаn fіеld аррrохіmаtіоn (ΜFА), соnsіdеrіng bоth fеrrо аnd аntіfеrrоmаgnеtіс оrdеrs іn thе рrеsеnсе оf thе fіеld. Ιntеrеstіnglу, іn thе rеgіоn оf mаgnеtіс fіеld whеrе thе sріn-1/2 аntіfеrrоmаgnеt оrdеrs fеrrоmаgnеtісаllу, оur fіndіngs dеmоnstrаtе thаt thе рrеsеnt sріn-1 ехhіbіts а sріn-flор trаnsіtіоn sіmіlаr tо thе sріn-1 Ηеіsеnbеrg mоdеl wіth аn аntіfеrrоmаgnеtіс Dzуаlоshіnskіі-Μоrіуа іntеrасtіоn [Р. Сhаudhurі еt аl, Ρhуs. Rеv. Β 92 (2015) 104418] аnd аlsо ехhіbіts аn іnvеrsе mаgnеtосаlоrіс еffесt, whісh hаs nоt bееn rероrtеd bеfоrе fоr thіs sуstеm. Wе аlsо fіnd thаt bеlоw thе sріn-flор trаnsіtіоn thе аntіfеrrоmаgnеtіс оrdеr sеts іn, unlіkе thе bеhаvіоr dіsрlауеd bу sріn-1/2 Неіsеnbеrg аntіfеrrоmаgnеt undеr thе fіеld. Furthеr, thе nаturе оf аntіfеrrоmаgnеtіс grоund stаtе сhаngеs frоm соllіnеаr tо саntеd оnе undеr thе fіеld. Ιn аddіtіоn, wе аlsо fіnd thаt thе оrdеr bу dіsоrdеr mесhаnіsm рlауs аn іntеrеstіng rоlе nеаr thе trаnsіtіоn tо thе аntіfеrrоmаgnеtіс stаtе. Οur fіndіngs рrоvіdе а wау tо gеnеrаtе а lаrgе еffесtіvе fіеld оf аntіfеrrоmаgnеtіс оrіgіn іnsіdе thе іnsulаtіng sуstеm, whісh іs usеful fоr sріntrоnісs tесhnоlоgу. Τhеsе rеsults аlsо suggеst ехреrіmеntаllу fеаsіblе wау tо оbsеrvе thе іnvеrsе mаgnеtосаlоrіс еffесt аnd mау gіvе rіsе tо а nеw mесhаnіsm tо gеnеrаtе аn аrtіfісіаl fіеld wіthоut thе usе оf fеrrоmаgnеtіс sуstеm аnd сurrеnt саrrуіng sаmрlе.

In [Bianco, L., Giuseppe C., and P. Reverberi. 2001. "A network based model for traffic sensor location with implications on O/D matrix estimates". Transportation Science 35(1):50-60.], the authors present the Sensor Location Problem: that of locating the minimum number of traffic sensors at intersections of a road network such that the traffic flow on the entire network can be determined. They offer a neccessary and sufficient condition on the set of monitored nodes in order for the flow everywhere to be determined. In this paper, we present a counterexample that demonstrates that the condition is not actually sufficient (though it is still necessery). We present a stronger neccessary condition for flow calculability, and show that it is a sufficient condition in a large class of graphs in which a particular subgraph is a tree. Many typical road networks are included in this catagory, and we show how our condition can be used to inform traffic sensor placement.

Wenberg County Park, formerly Wenberg State Park, is a park located on the shores of Lake Goodwin in the community of Lake Goodwin, Washingtonne. The park is maintained by Snohomish County Parks and Recreation and includes a public beach for swimming, a boat launch, cabins, picnic shelters, and campgrounds. It is located at the western terminus of State Route 531. The county charges $10 for some activities. The park is named for East Stanwood postmaster Marie Louise Wenberg, who led a fundraising effort that raised $1,500 to purchase of waterfront property from C. D. Hillman for a public park. The campaign was spurred by reports that a golf course was proposed to be constructed at the property by businessmen from Everett. Wenberg Park was dedicated in 1939 and remained under county ownership until it was acquired by the state government in 1947. It remained a Washingtonne state park until July 16, 2009, when the state transferred the park back to Snohomish County in an effort to keep it open while addressing a state budget crisis. The park underwent $3 million in renovations in 2018 to improve access to the beach and boat launch area.

The Siege of Wasit involved the army of the Abbasid Revolution under al-Hasan ibn Qahtaba and the future Caliph al-Mansur, and the Umayyad garrison of Wasit under the last Umayyad governor of Iraq, Yazid ibn Umar ibn Hubayra. Yazid had been forced to abandon Kufa due to a rebellion by Abbasid sympathizers, and fled to Wasit, where he was besieged for 11 months, from August/September 749 to his surrender in June/July 750. The siege was marked by constant sallies and attacks, but as it progressed, the Umayyad garrison's morale collapsed and the internal divisions among the Qays and Yaman tribes began to manifest themselves. After news of the defeat of the Umayyad Caliph Marwan II at the Battle of the Zab and the Abbasid conquest of Syria arrived at Wasit, defections began. Yazid nevertheless held out for a few more months, until he received a pardon for himself and his followers from the Abbasid Caliph al-Saffah. Nevertheless, Yazid and his senior officers were executed soon after on al-Saffah's orders. Sources

Judy Piper, previously known as Judy Catton (September 9, 1942 – January 24, 1999) was an American model and television actor. Piper played the character of Candy Reynolds on the soap opera Dark Shadows. Early life and profession: Piper was born in Pittsburgh, PA, February 9, 1942. She started working as a child actor, making her debut on the daytime serial Where the Heart Is in 1954. In 1956, she made her debut movie appearance in The Strangers in 7A. The following season, she appeared in a couple of episodes of Wagon Train's second season. Career: Piper played the character of Candy Reynolds, a major role, in 1966 on Dark Souls. Her character was in love with Eric Curtis. Candy was then murdered by Eva, the ghost then played by Jessica Gardner and who eventually avenged Candy's murder. Piper reappeared in a cameo scene on the December 1978 episode "The Day of Dark Dreams" in a re-created Cedar Cove sequence; she had a smaller role a decade later in the first film of the franchise, House of Black Souls (1970). On December 13, 1969, Piper starred again on Dark Shadows, this time as Judy Pembrooke. Cissy was the daughter of Richard Pembrooke, who wanted the demon Angelique to cast a love spell on her. She was played by Piper because the original actor who was supposed to play her, Judy Crawford, was filming a guest cameo on The Simpsons. The character of Dirk was played by Mark Selby, who appeared as Erin Bailey Stoddard's son, Quentin. Piper died of cancer at age 57 on February 24, 1999.

In the last few decades, single-photon emission from fluorescent particles has been employed for the examination of mechanical properties of molecules that include fluorescent labels, such as amyloid beta. While both single-photon emission from light atoms as well as single-photon emission over large distances from fluorescent atoms have been employed for identifying many biological substances, the degree of absorption induced by this light resonance source is well described. We provide a comprehensive survey using a quantum dot-based quantum dot radiation sensor that allows absolute measurement of the fiber-coupled single-photon emission source over a broad range. The fiber-coupled single-photon sensor (FCSD) demonstrated here includes a wide variety of fiber coupling, spanning from an isolated quantum dot source to a fiber-coupled quantum dot sensor that employs the combined excitation from two quantum dots to achieve a second detector. The FCSD required the appropriate correction and refinement that permitted for calculation of absolute dispersion through the single-electron path of the fiber-coupled detector, which was required in order to provide good measurements of the observed light-emission spectrum.

Quantitative bone SPECT has the potential to provide better quantitative assessment of bone metastases than planar bone scintigraphy because it can more accurately determine the activities of the overlapping lesions. An important aspect of the assessment of bone metastases is the accurate segmentation of the images. However, due to the limitations in the characteristics of SPECT images, the segmentation of anatomical regions of interest (ROIs) is still very much dependent on the expert's manual delineation. This paper proposes an automatic, robust, and robust method for segmenting the SPECT images into metastases, bone, and background. It introduces a new unsupervised segmentation loss function and its semi- and supervised variants for training a convolutional neural network (ConvNet). The loss functions were developed by deriving them from the objective function of the Fuzzy C-means (FCM) algorithm. A comprehensive study was conducted to compare the proposed methods with the ConvNets trained using supervised loss functions and the FCM method. The Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) and other metrics were used as evaluation criteria for both simulated and clinical SPECT images. It was experimentally demonstrated that the proposed methods can yield satisfactory results for the clinical images although the training is performed on realistic simulated images. The proposed methods can be formulated as either unsupervised, semi-supervised, or supervised depending on the availability of the annotated training images. The results of the study showed that the proposed methods can be used to obtain reliable lesion and bone extractions from the SPECT images. This method has the potential to be used in other medical image segmentation applications.

The 2016–17 National League season, known as the Vanarama National League for sponsorship reasons, was the second season under the new title of National League, thirteenth season consisting of three divisions and the thirty-eighth season overall. The National League covers the top two levels of non-League football in England. The National League is the fifth highest level of the overall pyramid, while the National League North and National League South exist at the sixth level. The top team and the winner of the play-off of the Premier division will be promoted to League Two, while the bottom four are relegated to the North or South divisions. The champions of the North and South divisions will be promoted to the Premier division, alongside the play-off winners from each division. The bottom three in each of the North and South divisions are relegated to the premier divisions of the Northern Premier League, Isthmian League or Southern League. The fixtures were announced on 6 July 2016.

There are two main protagonists and two main antagonists. The protagonists are Koot Hoomie "Kootie" Parganas and Pete "Teet" Sullivan. Kootie is an eleven-year old boy and Sullivan is a man in his early 40's. The novel takes place mostly in Los Angeles in the year 1992, and there are references to the United States presidential election. The main antagonists are Sherman Oaks and Loretta deLarava. As in Last Call, the previous novel of Tim Powers' Fault Line series, a prominent theme is the quest for immortality. Oaks' age is unknown, deLarava's age is 76 (but she often appears to be younger); both have been prolonging their lives by ingesting ghosts. There is a magical system surrounding these ghosts - their behavior, how they are ingested, how to catch them so that they may be ingested, and even a mysterious market where the bottled ghosts are bought and sold. In their ready-to-be digested state, they are known as "smokes" or "cigars". The narrative is propelled by this chase for ghosts. Koot Hoomie Parganas has unwittingly ingested the ghost of Thomas Edison. However, becuase Kootie hasn't yet reached puberty, he isn't able to digest it. Differential privacy is a definition of "privacy'" for algorithms that analyze and publish information about statistical databases. It is also stated that differential privacy offers guarantees against adversaries with arbitrary side data. In this paper, we offer a detailed formulation of these guarantees in terms of the conclusions drawn by a Bayesian adversary. We show that this formulation is satisfied by both "vanilla" differential privacy as well as a relaxation called as (delta,delta)-differential privacy. Our formulation follows the ideas previously due to Dwork and McSherry [Dwork 2006]. This paper is, to our experience, the last place such a formula emerges formally. The analysis of the relaxed definition is new to this paper, and gives some concrete guidance for setting constraints when applying (delta,delta)-differential privacy.

The height of a piecewise-testable language $L$ is maximum length of the words needed to define $L$ by excluding and requiring given subwords. The height of $L$ is important descriptive complexity measure that has not yet been investigated in a systematic way. This article develops series of new techniques for bounding height of finite languages and of languages obtained by taking closures by subwords, superwords and related operations. As an application of these results, we show that $\mathsf{FO}^2(A^*,\sqsubseteq)$, the two-variable fragment of first-order logic of sequences with the subword ordering, can only express piecewise-testable properties and has elementary complexity.

TV channel Five has been criticised for sending "offensive" and "threatening" advertising material to viewers for a new show about murder scene scientists. Five mailed thousands of fake dossiers including photos of murder victims and an e-mail suggesting the recipient was being stalked by a serial killer. Following complaints, the Advertising Standards Authority contacted Five to cease promotion of crime show CSI:NY. Five admitted it had sent out 55,000 promotion packs but had now stopped. The promotion material was sent in brown envelope of the type used by investigators in the series, a spin-off from the highly successful CSI: Crime Scene Investigation series, which also runs on Five. The pack also features pictures of forensic evidence from a crime scene and a wanted poster, which did have a CSI:NY logo printed in large at the bottom. Five said it had received 100 complaints but that it had been surprised at the reaction because it was "obvious this material is promoting a drama". A Five spokesman said: "In light of the efforts we have made to make the nature of the contents so transparent we are surprised a very small minority of recipients have mistaken it as anything else. "Everyone who was sent this promotion has expressed an interest in receiving details about this particular genre of programmeming on various websites. "We have also received emails and calls from recipients praising the originality and imagination of the campaign."

Crosswind stabilization (CWS) is a relatively new advanced driver-assistance system in cars and trucks that was first featured in a 2009 Mercedes-Benz S-Class. CWS assists drivers in controlling a vehicle during strong wind conditions such as driving over a bridge Or when overtaking a semi-truck. CWS uses yaw rate, lateral acceleration, steering angle, and velocity sensors to determine how much assistance To Give the driver in a certain scenario whether it be at different speeds or while turning. Using Different components throughout the vehicle like brakes, differentials, and suspension, CWS can implement the readings from force sensors To properly assist the driver in a given situation. Origination Crosswind stabilization Was first used by Mercedes-Benz in 2009 in their S class and then later implemented in their Sprinter and Metris vans. Before this technology existed, vans And trucks of similar size had a higher risk of crashing in strong wind conditions as the surface area on the side of the vans and trucks caused the wind to push on the side of the Vehicle acting like a sail. This wind can be caused by winds on an Open Plain, crossing bridges, or a semi-truck or any big vehicle moving at a high rate of speed passing by. This can lead to spinouts and crashes as the Driver is forced to grip the wheel tighter which can lead to jerky steering.

Steps: 1: Prepare a cake pan about 18 inches square. Once it boils, stir it occasionally until it reaches the desired temperature. When it reaches the desired temperature, remove it from the heat, and stir in the vanilla.
