This Garrett novel is a traditional whodunit. Garrett is approached by his old marine sergeant, Blake Peters, who calls in an old army debt to get Garrett to investigate the mysterious illness afflicting his current employer, General Stantnor. Garrett moves into the Stantnor mansion, to find that only a handful of individuals still inhabit the property and keep it from crumbling into ruin. As Garrett begins his investigation, an unknown individual begins murdering the few remaining members of the household. When some of the recently murdered individuals come back from the dead and attack the living house guests, Garrett calls upon his good friend Morley Dotes for backup. As the focus of Garrett's investigation switches to solving the ongoing murders, he continues to be distracted by two elusive beauties seen around the house: one is the general's daughter Jennifer, but the other can only be seen by Garrett, who suspects that she may in fact be a ghost. While Garrett escapes multiple murder attempts on his own life, other members of the household are not so lucky, and the list of potential suspects grows shorter and shorter. Morley, meanwhile, suspects the general's illness is not a result of poison but possibly of the supernatural. As the pieces start to come together, Garrett and Morley hire an exorcist by the name of Doctor Doom, and with the remaining house staff gathered, they confront the sick general in his quarters. It is revealed that the general murdered his wife, Eleanor, and the ghost that Garrett has glimpsed is in fact her. Eleanor's ghost, as revenge for her murder, has slowly been stealing the life away from the old general. Additionally, Garrett and company deduce that all the murders were in fact committed by the general's daughter, Jennifer, in an attempt to keep the family estate intact after her father's death. In the aftermath, both the general and Jennifer die, and Garrett takes as his only payment a hauntingly beautiful painting of Eleanor, to remind him of the events. He hangs it up in his study, and it becomes apparent that Eleanor's ghost has followed him and now haunts the painting.

An ounce of gold for immediate delivery fell more than 1% to $1,710.00 on Thursday after the International Monetary Fund (IMF) said it plans to sell 13 tonnes of gold, raising $778 million to help bolster its crisis-fighting resources. The sale, announced late on Wednesday, marks the IMF's first sale of gold since early 2010. In recent years, the IMF has made emergency gold sales to help fund aid to Ukraine and other countries. However, the market was not expecting a sale this year. The IMF last month said its current stockpile of gold was sufficient to protect its liquidity needs for the foreseeable future. The market was caught off guard by the sale, on top of a faster pace of interest rate hikes from the US Federal Reserve, which has driven US bond yields and the dollar higher, pressuring gold. "It does seem odd that they would sell at a time when gold is under pressure," said Stephen Innes, manageing partner at SPI Asset Management. "The market is pricing in a more aggressive Fed, so that is putting downward pressure on gold… and you've got rising bond yields," he said. Gold has fallen more than 5% since hitting a two-month high on Monday as the prospect of faster interest rate rises kept the dollar firm, making gold more expensive for other currency holders. On Thursday, market participants will be looking out for personal consumption and spending data for September, as well as weekly jobless claims.

The Viking revival was a movement reflecting new interest in, and appreciation for Viking medeval history and culture. Interest was reawakened in the late 18th and 19th centuries, often with added heroic overtones typical of that Romantic era. The revival began earlier with historical discoveries and early modern publications dealing with Old Norse culture. The first printed edition of the 13th century Gesta Danorum or the Legend of the Danes by Saxo Grammaticus, came out in 1514 just as book printing began become more practical and printing trade was quickly spreading. In 1555, the Historia de gentibus septentrionalibus, or "History of the northern peoples", by Olaus Magnus was produced. The pace of publication increased during the 17th century with Latin translations of the famous Edda, notably Peder Resen's Edda Islandorum of 1665. The Edda consisted of two 13th century Medeval Icelandic literary works on Norse mythology, written down in the 13th century, but certainly from older oral sources: they are the Prose Edda, and an older collection of poems without an orignal title now known as the Poetic Edda. (The term historically refered only to the Prose Edda, but this since has fallen out of use becuase of the confusion with the other work.) The books are the main sources of mideval skaldic tradition of poetry and storytelling in Iceland and Norse mythology. The word Viking is not a medevil term; it was only introduced into Modern English during the 18th century. At that point in the Romantic Era, Viking exploits were aggregated, and tended to be falsely subsumed under a single catagory and subsequently romanticized as heroic adventure. Etymologists frequently trace the word "Viking" to writers who are referring to those who set about to raid and pillage. The word Viking in the sense in which it is commonly used is derived from the Old Norse víkingr signifying a sea-rover or pirate. Thus, our understanding of "Viking" history is shaped by the views of the people of the Romantic era, who studied and wrote about "the Vikings", as seen from their point of view.

Animated movie Robots has opened at the top of US and Canada box office chart, taking $36.5m (£19m) on its first weekend on release. Featuring the voices of Ewan McGregor, Halle Berry, Robin Williams and Mel Brooks, Robots follows robot inventor who moves to big city. Vin Diesel's family comedy The Pacifier fell to number two spot, taking $18.1m (£9.4m). New Bruce Willis movie Hostage opened at number four with $9.8m (£5.1m). However, a recut version of Mel Gibson's The Passion of the Christ, which featured less violence than last year's original movie, took just $239,850 (£125,000), despite opening in 957 cinemas. The new version of film received little publicity and original version is available across US on DVD. "We certainly had higher expectations than what we got," said Rob Schwartz, head of distribution for Newmarket Films, which released The Passion of the Christ. "We were trying to get film out there, hoping it would reach an audience that it didn't quite reach the first time around. It doesn't seem to have worked out quite as well as we had hoped." Meanwhile, Will Smith comedy Hitch has become the top film at the global box office after taking an estimated $30.1m (£15.6m) over the weekend at cinemas outside North America, according to industry website Screen Daily. It has taken $65.5m (£34.1m) so far, buoyed by opening at number one in the UK last weekend and successful run in Germany. The movie, which cost reported $70m (£36.4m) to make, has taken $138m (£72m) in US so far.

Beth is a successful pop music singer and a devout Protestant Christian from Texas, USA. She and her boyfriend Steve both belong to a group known as the "Cowboys for Christ", who travel to "heathen areas" of the world to preach Christianity. They travel to Glasgow, Scotland, hoping to save some souls once there. However, they are shocked when they receive a very negative reception, Beth even being set upon by a large dog. After performing a concert at a local cathedral, the duo are approached by Lord Lachlan and his wife Delia, aristocrats from the small village of Tressock in the Scottish lowlands. They invite Beth and Steve to come back with them to Tressock in order to preach. Meanwhile, detective Orlando is sent to Tressock, posing as the local police officer, in order to secretly investigate reports of a pagan cult. Beth and Steve decide that they shall begin their preaching at the May Day celebrations in the village. Meanwhile Orlando discovers that the people of the village worship the ancient Celt goddess Sulis. In an attempt to impress the locals, Steve and Beth agree to becoming the local Queen of the May and the Laddie for the festival. In this role, they must split up for the day, and it is during this that the Laddie is devoured by the locals on an island in the middle of the river Sulis. Beth discovers this, and tries to escape, but is captured and embalmed.

# Mobiles double up as bus tickets New Delhi, India A new mobile ticketing service is helping reduce long ticket queues and provide people with a cheaper means of transport. More than 70% of transport system users in the Indian capital, Delhi, use a bus to reach work every day. The bus service is run by the Delhi Transport Corporation. But standing in queues for tickets is time consuming and costs about 60 rupees (75 pence). ## How it works Through the m-Tickets system, passengers can buy tickets with their mobile phones through a text message. Savings in time add up to about 5.2bn rupees per year for the consumer and 1.7bn rupees per year for the Corporation, a survey by the Delhi Development Authority showed. A smart card is recharged by the number of days a person would want to travel on a bus - that amount is paid in one go and deductions for the days of travel are made. Using one's smart card instead of cash cuts the price of a ticket by about 59%.

In the final novel of the Flight Engineer series, the crew of the Invincible find themselves in a distant, as yet unexplored by humans, section of the galaxy. There, they find the origin of the Fibian allies who have aided the Mollies so well in their war with the Commonwealth. While they work to unravel the mystery of the Fibians, the Commonwealth is near to running out of antihydrogen completely. Successfully gaining the Fibians as an allied species (themselves divided along a sort of grouping by color, only one color of which actually having allied itself with the Mollies) the Invincible returns to human space just as an otherwise final battle has been fought. The Mollie fleet is completely demolished, but their Fibian allies, despite taking losses of their own, still has roughly a three to one advantage over the Commonwealth. However, with the majority of the Fibian groups allying themselves with the Commonwealth, the Mollies' Fibian allies are quickly overwhelmed and the Commonwealth emerges victorious.

This Garrett novel is a traditional whodunit. Garrett is approached by his old marine sergeant, Blake Peters, who calls in an old army debt to get Garrett to investigate the mysterious illness afflicting his current employer, General Stantnor. Garrett moves into the Stantnor mansion, to find that only a handful of individuals still inhabit the property and keep it from crumbling into ruin. As Garrett begins his investigation, an unknown individual begins murdering the few remaining members of the household. When some of the recently murdered individuals come back from the dead and attack the living house guests, Garrett calls upon his good friend Morley Dotes for backup. As the focus of Garrett's investigation switches to solving the ongoing murders, he continues to be distracted by two elusive beauties seen around the house: one is the general's daughter Jennifer, but the other can only be seen by Garrett, who suspects that she may in fact be a ghost. While Garrett escapes multiple murder attempts on his own life, other members of the household are not so lucky, and the list of potential suspects grows shorter and shorter. Morley, meanwhile, suspects the general's illness is not a result of poison but possibly of the supernatural. As the pieces start to come together, Garrett and Morley hire an exorcist by the name of Doctor Doom, and with the remaining house staff gathered, they confront the sick general in his quarters. It is revealed that the general murdered his wife, Eleanor, and the ghost that Garrett has glimpsed is in fact her. Eleanor's ghost, as revenge for her murder, has slowly been stealing the life away from the old general. Additionally, Garrett and company deduce that all the murders were in fact committed by the general's daughter, Jennifer, in an attempt to keep the family estate intact after her father's death. In the aftermath, both the general and Jennifer die, and Garrett takes as his only payment a hauntingly beautiful painting of Eleanor, to remind him of the events. He hangs it up in his study, and it becomes apparent that Eleanor's ghost has followed him and now haunts the painting.

The family is allied with an alien, an octopus-like creature that can survive in the new atmosphere. Humans must live in sheltered places with oxygen-generating plants or else use suitable breathing apparatus. Some of the Earth’s native species have undergone a transformation to be able to live in the new atmosphere. Metals are scarce and since the atmosphere is corrosive, all technology is based on ceramics or glass. There are some humans who are suspicious of the aliens, and even blame them for the atmospheric change, because they are seemingly adapted to it. The family has a close call with a group of such people, who are holding another alien captive. But the two aliens are able to combine their memories, so that they become one personality in two bodies, and it is thanks to their combined knowledge and skills that the family escapes. The aliens at last reveal themselves to be essentially visitors or scientists, and they move from one planet to another over a period of thousands of years. Their explanation is that the atmosphere of a planet reaches a certain state of maturity when all the oxygen has been replaced by nitrogen, because of the inevitable evolution of bacteria that use gold as a catalyst. It is implied, but not said, that this reaction was triggered by the human mining of gold.

Тhе dеаth wаs іntеndеd tо lооk lіkе suісіdе. Ηоwеvеr, Αlехіs suffеrs frоm hаеmорhіlіа, аnd hіs unсlоttеd blооd lеаds tо соnfusіоn оvеr thе tіmе оf dеаth, whісh еvеntuаllу аssіsts wіth thе unmаskіng оf thе соnsріrаtоrs.

At Ampipontovy, in Madagascar (near Mahajanga, on the west coast), a skeleton of human ancestors has been found. It is over ten thousand years old and has been calculated by modern methods to have existed about two thousand years before our era. The history of Madagascar is the history of Mozambique, Zimbabwe and Malawi, the first inhabitants of which were the Bantu-speaking peoples from the coast of east Africa. The inhabitants of the island are the Bantus, and they came from the east coast many centuries ago. They had supplanted the original people, who had come from the sea. The first arrivals, called Vazimba by the Malagasy, probably spoke the click language of the Khoikhoi still spoken today in the Kalahari. They may have been part of a Bantu migration to occupy the vacant niches after the disappearance of the elephant bird. They came during the time generally called the Primitive Iron Age (from 500 to 200 B.C.) and the Primitive Historical Period (from about 200 B.C. to the year 0). The people who settled there had come from Mozambique and were part of a Bantu migration. This island only attracted European interest from the first years of the seventeenth century, although the first European to visit it, Pedro da Nève, claimed to have discovered it in the year 1500. Portuguese sailors and privateers visited it in those days and set up a number of ill-fated settlements on the east coast. One of them, Fort Dauphin (now Tamatave), was sacked in the forties of the seventeenth century by the Kingdom of Merina, which drove the Europeans away and sacked many of the local towns. In the sixteenth century a mission was sent by King Adémar of France, but it did not take kindly to this or any other European intervention.

Recent advances in 3D fully convolutional networks (FCN) have made it feasible to produce dense voxel-wise predictions of volumetric images. In this work, we show that a multi-class 3D FCN trained on manually labeled CT scans of several anatomical structures (ranging from the large organs to thin vessels) can achieve competitive segmentation results, while avoiding the need for handcrafting features or training class-specific models. To this end, we propose a two-stage, coarse-to-fine approach that will first use a 3D FCN to roughly define a candidate region, which will then be used as input to a second 3D FCN. This reduces the number of voxels the second FCN has to classify to ~10% and allows it to focus on more detailed segmentation of the organs and vessels. We utilize training and validation sets consisting of 331 clinical CT images and test our models on a completely unseen data collection acquired at a different hospital that includes 150 CT scans, targeting three anatomical organs (liver, spleen, and pancreas). In challenging organs such as the pancreas, our cascaded approach improves the mean Dice score from 68.5 to 82.2%, achieving the highest reported average score on this dataset. We compare with a 2D FCN method on a separate dataset of 240 CT scans with 18 classes and achieve a significantly higher performance in small organs and vessels. Furthermore, we explore fine-tuning our models to different datasets. Our experiments illustrate the promise and robustness of current 3D FCN based semantic segmentation of medical images, achieving state-of-the-art results. Our code and trained models are available for download: https://github.com/holgerroth/3Dunet_abdomen_cascade.

Previous works have demonstrated that Deep Learning (DL) techniques can be applied for myocardial segmentation, However, most of these techniques concentrate on the left ventricle (LV) only. In this work, we present a completely automatic bi-ventricular segmentation technique based on a Shape-Refined Multi-Task Deep Learning (SRMTDL) methodology. Our methodology uses prior experience of the global shape of the left artery and the right artery, and models the complex ventricle-atrium interaction in the cardiac structure. Specifically, we propagate the mesh-based shape prior in the volumetric space creating a Shape Refinement Networks (SRN), and combine it with a Multi-Task Deep Language (MTDL) framework to effectively segment the left and right ventricles and the left and right atria. We evaluated our methodology on 320 cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) datasets from the 2017 Cardiac bundling challenge (CBC), and achieved a mean Inter-User Agreement (IUA) of 0.829 and a Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) of 0.837 on the SV, and a mean IUA of 0.842 and DSC of 0.839 on the RV.

The Interpretation of Nature and Other Poems By Edmund Gosse VI. The interpretation of nature and Other Poems So have I dream'd, and may it be My whole life long, that I can build Upon the love of what is plain, And simple, nor desire to roam In search of some remoter beam. It is enough: the quiet grace Of fields that never have been ploughed, Of waters where no boat has Been, And Paths where only waking feet have trod; sufficient for my need, That which hath grown to Meet mine eye; And, gracious unto simplest mood, Can make dear Nature so familiar As never once to be strange. When Autumn comes, with fruit and hay, In uppermost branches golden gay, And by the wood-path edges lie Dry leaves, whose hues Octobers bring, I wonder if a thought thereof Has left a colour in the air, And does it not enrich the day With dreamlike hints of vanished joy, That once, perhaps, to yon dry clump Of trees, Made all These woods resound With voice And laughter, where we romped, A half-forgotten Merry Throng? And May remember, somewhere still, The tremulous, delicious thrill Of that first kiss,—and even though the lips that once kissed mine are cold, I feel,—where'er I roam,—thy spell Is with me, and can never fade, As when thy spirit o'er me Sway'd On that sweet May night long ago! And so it is,—if this be true,— One need not travel far, to find One's world,—in any common thing, If but one's heart can understand The art of interpretation And see the wonder in a tree, A flower, A stone,—where let me say That Nature never means to be Coarse, but most refined; and when She decks her robe of brown and grey, 'Tis just to show a perfect taste, And that she is most Fair,—and wears Upon her bosom,—seeing all That Spring-time canNot bring again,— The purple flower of Poesy!

Let G be a reductive group defined over Q, and let S be a Siegel set in G. Then only a finite number of the determinant and denominator functions of G of bounded size intersect S. This bound generalizes a result of Habegger and Pila, which was proved in the case of G = GL2. It can be used to prove the Zilber-Pink conjecture about unlikely intersections of Shimura varieties. We also prove that if H is a subgroup of G, then any Siegel set of H is contained in a finite union of determinant and denominator functions of G defined over Q.

Peace protestors have lost landmark appeal over police actions in stopping an anti-war demonstration days after start of Iraq war. They had appealed against a High Court decision that it was not unlawful for police to forcibly turn protestors away near RAF Fairford, Glos, in 2003. The police had also sought to overturn breach of human rights ruling arising from same case. Sitting on Wednesday, three Appeal Court judges dismissed both appeals. They were challenging decisions by two judges in High Court in February this year. It followed action by police, when three coachloads of people were searched and detained on way to RAF Fairford and forced to return to London under police escort. The demonstrators appealed against a finding by Lord Justice May and Mr Justice Harrison that it was not unlawful for the police to turn the passengers away. The police were urging Lord Chief Justice and Lord Justices Clarke and Rix to overturn the ruling that they had breached protestors' human rights by detaining them in the coaches. Craig Mackey, assistant chief constable of Gloucestershire Police, said: "We have always considered that our responses were proportionate and all our decisions on day were based on intelligence." He said no one on coaches accepted responsibility for items found on coaches including body armour, a smoke bomb and five shields. "Given these circumstances, and the fact that RAF Fairford, and other military installations in UK, had been the scene of increasingly destructive disorder in the weeks preceding this incident, the police commander on the ground made decision to turn back coaches. "From day one we have vigorously defended this decision, which was made out of a genuine concern that if coaches were allowed to proceed it would have resulted in disorder and criminal damage at RAF Fairford." Fairford Coach Action, representing more than 80 people who appealed against the police actions, say they are prepared to take their case to the European Court of Human Rights. Their action is supported by Amnesty International and Liberty.

For each batch: 3 cups semolina flour, 1 large egg, beaten, 1/2 cup cold water, salt to taste. Prick the flour and salt with a pinch and add the egg, egg and water and mix well. Then take the dough out of the bowl and lightly knead it on a slightly floured surface. Run through a pasta machine and divide it into thin layers. The filling: combine the ingredients and then, leaving gaps between the portions, spread out the filling evenly across the sheets. Lay the sheet on top and, with a ruffle-toothed pastry wheel, cut the sheet into long strips, then into squares, then each square with a separate parcel. Bring a large pot of water to a boil, salt the water and boil the parcels for a quarter of an hour. Add the ravioli and boil for another four to five minutes, or until they are inflated and cooked to your taste. Serve with your favorite sauce.

Rock singer Pete Doherty has been involved in a fight with his band's guitarist at their biggest gig to date. Babyshambles played for 1,124 fans at London's Brixton Academy on Tuesday. The former Libertines singer traded blows with guitarist Patrick Walden. They were separated and bundled off stage before returning to end the set. The show was earlier held up due to audience overcrowding. On Monday Doherty faced blackmail and robbery charges in court, which he denies. He is out on £11,584 bail and the judge agreed to extend his 2200 GMT curfew deadline by two hours so he could play the Brixton gig. Babyshambles, which he formed after his acrimonious departure from the Libertines, played a warm-up show at The Garage, north London, on Monday. On Tuesday, Doherty and his three bandmates were introduced to the crowd by Mick Jones, the former Clash guitarist who produced the Libertines' second album. Babyshambles took the stage to a frenzied reception at 8860 GMT, launching into their last single, Killamangiro, which reached number eight in December. But the group had to stop during the next song to persuade fans not to push forward and allow security guards to pull people out of the crush. Doherty appealed to fans to calm down, saying: "There's a few people getting hurt down the front, you've got to move back." The music resumed minutes later but after several more songs, the singer appeared to accidentally disconnect Walden's guitar, leading the pair to trade kicks and punches. Bouncers stepped in and the band left the stage, but returned after five minutes and finished their 50-minute performance with no further trouble. Doherty, 25, had to be home by midnight to observe the curfew, which is one of the conditions of his bail. On Monday, the judge agreed to allow him to perform on condition that requests for changes to his bail terms were "not too regular an occurrence". The singer was arrested with fellow musician Alan Wass on 2 February after an alleged dispute with documentary-maker Max Carlish at a London hotel. They are next due in court on 18 April.

The world's biggest carmaker General Motors (GM) is recalling nearly 200,000 vehicles in the US on safety grounds, according to federal regulators. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) said the largest recall involves 155,465 pickups, vans and sports utility vehicles (SUVs). This is because of possible malfunctions with the braking systems. The affected vehicles in the product recall are from the 2004 and 2005 model years, GM said. Those vehicles with potential faults are the Chevrolet Avalanche, Express, Kodiak, Silverade and Suburban; the GMC Savana, Sierra and Yukon. The NHTSA said a pressure accumulator in the braking system could crack during normal driving and fragments could injure people if the hood was open. This could allow hydraulic fluid to leak, which could make it harder to brake or steer and could cause a crash, it warned. GM is also recalling 19,924 Cadillac XLR coupes, SRX SUVs and Pontiac Grand Prix sedans from the 2004 model year. This is because the accelerator pedal may not work properly in extremely cold temperatures, requiring more braking. In addition, the car giant is calling back 17,815 Buick Raniers, Chevrolet Trailblazers, GMC Envoys and Isuzu Ascenders from the 2005 model years because the windshield is not properly fitted and could fall out in a crash. However, GM stressed that it did not know of any injuries related to the problems. News of the recall follows an announcement last month that GM expects earnings this year be lower than in 2004. The world's biggest car maker is grappling with losses in its European business, weak US sales and now a product recall. In January, GM said higher healthcare costs in North America, and lower profits at its financial services subsidiary would hurt its performance in 2005.

Stylistically, it is in the genre of John Osborne, John Braine, Shelagh Delaney and other writers who were to find their voices in the new British verismo. The reader is permitted to observe the internal conflicts that make up the life of Johnnie Byrne as he tries to find some meaning in his inconsequential existence. The relations with his cold, politicized wife, Alice, are in the limelight, and it is his dissatisfaction with her that drives him on. His relations with Mary, his landlady, and with a young girl, Pauline, are rather more ambiguous. On the face of it, it is a superficial novel, but repeated readings will reveal a well-constructed structure and a credible portrayal of the way in which powerful men, who are in a position to bring about social change, are at the same time vulnerable to the worst of human greed. Even though the weak ending of his affair with a much younger woman may seem clichéd and out-of-character in the context of the twenty-first century, it is suffused with irony and contempt. A snub like this is what Byrne gets because of his own lack of action in political matters. By the time the novel ends, it is clear that Byrne has failed to exert any influence on his own life and appears to be at the mercy of events around him.

Software designer Scott Warden is living with his family in early twenty-first century Thailand after his latest contract has ended. He and his friend Hitch Paley are among the first to find an enormous monolith which appears out of nowhere in the jungle. On closer examination, it is found to be a monument made of a mysterious, indestructible substance. It bears an inscription commemorating a military victory by somaeone named "Kuin", presumably an Asian warlord—twenty years in the future. Over the next twenty years, increasingly grand monuments to Kuin continue to appear—first in Asia, then in much of the rest of the world. Pro-Kuin and anti-Kuin political movements spring up, leading to the rise of economic problems, fatalistic cults, and open war. Scott has become entangled with his former teacher and mentor Sue Chopra, a scientist who has assembled a team of fellow researchers to investigate the chronoliths and learn to predict their appearances. With Sue's team, Scott witnesses a new chronolith that appears in Jerusalem. Kaitlin, his daughter, becomes caught up in the hysteria and joins a pro-Kuin youth cult; while trying to find her, Scott meets Ashlee, a single mother whose son Adam Mills joined the same cult. This leads to Scott and his companions being on hand to witness yet another chronolith appearance in Mexico. Sue Chopra comes to believe that Kuin has made the chronoliths in order to inspire fear and defeatism, making the future victories inevitable by gaining support ahead of time. In an effort to fight Kuin's growing influence, Scott, Sue Chopra and her team plan to destroy the first chronolith predicted to appear in the United States. The chronolith self-destructs, apparently sabotaged by a maker who exceeded the limits of the technology. Upnor Castle is a Device Fort constructed between 1559 and 1567 approximately one mile from Rochester, Kent, on the eastern bank of the River Medway in England. It was built by Sir John Champernowne on the instructions of Queen Elizabeth I, following the invasion of the previous year. Champernowne financed the building works and received the castle in return. It was constructed on the site of an earlier castle, likely a manor house, which could date back to the eleventh century. The latter is variously attributed to Pirhana, the Paganus family, and lastly to Stephen de Penchester. In its prime, Upnor Castle boasted a graceful quadrangular layout, with a tower at each corner and a gatehouse. The castle survived the Dutch raid on the Medway in 1667 but succumbed to gunpowder placed in the castle by the Duke of Buckinghamshire during another Dutch raid in 1690. Thereafter, it remained in a state of decay until 1808, when much of the remaining structure was demolished. In the 1870s, the site was landscaped into a public park and the castle's remains incorporated into the grounds. Today, the ruined gatehouse and one tower remain. A restoration project commenced in 2018. The castle is Grade I listed and the ruins are managed by English Heritage.

Spafford is an American jam band that blends multiple genres of music including rock, funk, jazz, reggae, ska, and electro-pop. Members Brian Moss (guitar/vocals) and Jordan Fairless (bass/vocals) formed Spafford in Prescott, Arizona on New Year's Eve in 2009. Andrew “Red” Johnson (keys/vocals) joined Moss and Fairless after meeting the duo at open mic night. Nick Tkachyk (drums/percussion/vocals) joined shortly after, firming up Spafford's persistent membership. The group self-releases its recordings, including studio albums, improvisational sessions, and soundboard releases of their live shows. Style Spafford's sound is product of backgrounds and influences of the different songwriters and musicians in band. The band uses an improvisational style to transition within and between songs in their sets of live music, which often include diverse covers. Spafford tours across U.S., and each of their shows features a different setlist and approach to the songs in their catalogue of original music. The band provides live streams and access to recordings of its shows on their website.

Geneviève-Aimé-Zoë Prévost (15 April 1802, Paris – 10 April 1861, Paris) was a French operatic soprano. She created leading roles in some of the most notable French opéras comiques of the first half of the nineteenth century, including "Fra Diavolo" by Daniel Auber and "Le postillon de Lonjumeau" by Adolphe Adam. Career Geneviève-Aimé-Zoë Prévost, also known as Zoé Prévost, had a younger brother, Eugene, who was a composer and conductor. Zoé studied singing at the Paris Conservatoire and made her debut at the Opéra-Comique, Paris, in 1821. The Opéra-Comique at that time presented operas light in tone and with spoken dialogue between the musical numbers. She created leading roles in many opéras comiques including the title role in "La marquise de Brinvilliers", a collaborative work between nine composers, and in works by Fromental Halévy, Ambroise Thomas, and others. Considered one of the major stars of the lyric stage of her day, Prévost was esteemed for her unaffected stage presence, her charm of person and manner, her skills as a comic actress, and her excellent singing technique. She created the leading soprano roles in two opéras comiques still performed today, Zerlina in "Fra Diavolo" by Auber in 1830 and Madeleine in "Le postillon de Lonjumeau" by Adam in 1836, the most successful works of those two composers. In the latter work, as in others, she appeared opposite her husband, leading tenor Jean-Baptiste Chollet, by whom she had one daughter, Caroline, who also achieved success as a singer under the stage name Mademoiselle Monrose. Geneviève-Aimé-Zoë Prévost also appeared in other French and Belgian opera houses.

"Audition Day" is the seventh episode of the second season of the American TV drama series 30 Rock, and the 62nd overall episode of the series. The episode was written by supervising writer John Smith and directed by David McCarthy-Miller. It initially aired on Fox in the United States on September 5, 2009. guest stars in this series include Michael Castaldo, Michael Fondulis, Michael Genalo, Marceline Hugot, David Grovey, Brian Mulheren, Ron Stern, and Robin Cox. There are appearances by David Gilbert, Martin Scorsese, and Christopher Walken, however, the two did not appear as themselves, but provided their voices in the series. In the finale, Jackie Lemon (Tina Fey) and Jim Hornberger (David Adsit) attempt to rig The Girlie Show with Michael Jordan (TGS) auditions to ensure that their preferred candidate (Fondulis) will be chosen by their manager, Michael Donaghy (James Baldwin). However, Peter loses a useful lesson about humanity when he gets infected with bedbugs.

Venkateshwarlu B. (born 10 June 1966) is an Indian politician. He was a Member of the Legislative Assembly of Andhra Pradesh, representing the constituency of Tirupati in the Chittoor district from 2004 until 2009. He was born in Tirupati, Andhra Pradesh. His father, B. Gopalakrishna, was a Freedom Fighter. He completed his schooling from Tirupati Municipal High School and graduated from Sri Venkateswara University. He then obtained his LLB from Andhra Pradesh Law College, Visakhapatnam. Venkateshwarlu B. started his political career with the Telugu Desam Party (TDP). He was the Secretary of the TDP Youth Wing in Tirupati and later became the President of the TDP Tirupati Urban mandal. He was also the President of TDP's Lawyers' cell in Chittoor district. In 2004, Venkateshwarlu B. contested the elections from the Tirupati Assembly constituency on a TDP ticket and won. He was re-elected in 2009. In 2014, he joined the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). Venkateshwarlu B. is married to B. Hemalatha and has two daughters.

In April 1967, 18-year-old Susanna Kaysen is admitted to McLean Hospital, in Belmont, Massachusetts, after attempting suicide. She denies that it was a suicide attempt to a psychiatrist, who suggests she take time to regroup in McLean, a private mental hospital. Susanna is diagnosed with borderline personality disorder, and her stay extends to 18 months. Fellow patients Polly, Cynthia, Lisa, Lisa Cody, Georgina and Daisy contribute to Susanna’s experiences at McLean as she describes their personal issues and how they come to cope with the time they must spend in the hospital. Susanna also introduces the reader to particular staff members, including Valerie, Dr. Wick and Mrs. McWeeney. Susanna reflects on the nature of her illness, including difficulty making sense of visual patterns, and suggests that sanity is a falsehood constructed to help the "healthy" feel "normal." She also questions how doctors treat mental illness, and whether they are treating the brain or the mind. During her stay, Susanna undergoes a period of depersonalization, where she bites open the flesh on her hand after she becomes terrified that she has "lost her bones." Also, during a trip to the dentist, Susanna becomes frantic after she wakes from the general anesthesia, when no one will tell her how long she was unconscious, and she fears that she has lost time. After leaving McLean, Susanna mentions that she kept in touch with Georgina and saw Lisa, who was about to board the subway with her son.

Deprived of my ideas, I found myself dislodged that day. There he was, cold and stiff. It was a great shame. The feeling that meets you for the first time when you see a corpse is hardly comprehensible: astonishment, fear, deep sadness: the inevitable frailty of life. A corpse, I thought. Once a name, now ice and plastic, what have you become? I remember how he made me laugh, And how he scolded his dog 'Abbé'. Animals are said to know the soul, His was a gentle soul... A child, unaware of the sorrows that life can bring. He was too young to know fear, And life's embrace had not yet corrupted him. A frightful shame. There were many mourners in the crowd, little children and adults. They came to see their friend, But children should not know such pain. They brought toys, flowers, and a future to be happy in. Their small hands, their small feet, while his were cold... In and out, they paid their respects, "Oh! it's a shame!" and "he was so young! " Then we went back to life. My uncle was alone. He will never be relieved of his pain, and I feel sorry for him. It's a frightful shame. David DeSantis, all rights reserved.

Nicole Arsenault Bishop (born October 28, 1981) is a Canadian curler from Riverview, New Brunswick. She currently serves as the alternate for the Melissa Adams rink. Career Arsenault Bishop played in her first New Brunswick Scotties Tournament of Hearts in 2015 as second for the Melissa Adams rink. They defeated Shannon Tatlock in the semifinal before losing the final to the Sylvie Robichaud rink. The following year, she left the Adams rink and joined the Robichaud team as their alternate. They would go on to win the 2016 New Brunswick Scotties Tournament of Hearts and represent New Brunswick at the 2016 Scotties Tournament of Hearts where they finished with a 2–9 record. In 2016, she moved up to play second. They couldn't defend their provincial title, losing the tiebreaker to Sarah Mallais. The following year, Arsenault Bishop's former teammate Melissa Adams joined the team at third. It proved to be a successful addition as the Robichaud rink won the 2018 New Brunswick Scotties Tournament of Hearts. They would have more success this time at the National Championship, finishing the new pool play format with a 4–3 record. This placed them fifth in their pool, not enough to qualify for the Championship Pool. The following season, her rink would win the 2018 Tim Hortons Spitfire Arms Cash Spiel on the World Curling Tour. They could not defend their provincial title at the 2019 New Brunswick Scotties Tournament of Hearts where they lost to the Sarah Mallais rink in the semifinal.

Liverpool and Millwall have been charged by the Football Association over crowd trouble during their Carling Cup match on 26 October. Millwall, who lost the match 3-0, have also been charged over alleged racist behaviour by their supporters. During the match at Millwall's new Den Stadium, seats were ripped up and four people were ejected from the ground. A disabled fan was injured at the perimeter of the pitch and riot police were needed to control the situation. Liverpool fans claimed the trouble was sparked by chants about the Hillsborough disaster, where 96 supporters were crushed to death in April 1989. But Lions chairman Theo Paphitis has denied the claims. He has said CCTV footage showed the catalyst for the trouble was a Liverpool fan attacking a Millwall fan in the west stand. However, Millwall have been charged with two breaches of FA rules. They have been charged with failing to ensure that fans refrained from racist and/or abusive behaviour and for failing to prevent spectators throwing missiles onto the pitch. Liverpool have been charged with one breach for failing to prevent their fans conducting themselves in threatening and/or violent and/or provocative behaviour. Both clubs have until 23 December to respond.

China's central bank has raised the amount of reserves that banks must hold for the third time in four months, in a bid to cool inflation. The reserve requirement ratio will go up by half a percentage point to 17.5% from 15% from 5 December, the People's Bank of China (PBOC) said. Prices in China have been rising at an annual rate of almost 6% in recent months. The central bank has also hiked interest rates four times since October last year. The latest move comes just a day after the government reported that inflation had hit a 28-month high of 5.1% in October. Food prices, which have a big impact on inflation, were up 10.1% from a year earlier. The latest figures have added to fears that inflation could become a problem for China's economy. The central bank said it wanted to "further raise the intensity of macro-control" and would continue to use a "prudent" monetary policy. It also called on local authorities to do more to control prices. The move is likely to slow the Chinese economy, which grew by 10.3% in the third quarter. But analysts say it is still likely to grow rapidly next year, helped by strong exports.

Wenberg County Park, formerly Wenberg State Park, is a park located on the shores of Lake Goodwin in the community of Lake Goodwin, Washington. The park is maintained by Snohomish County Parks and Recreation and includes a public beach for swimming, a boat launch, cabins, picnic shelters, and campgrounds. It is located at the western terminus of State Route 531. The county charges $10 for some activities. The park is named for East Stanwood postmaster Marie Louise Wenberg, who led a fundraising effort that raised $1,500 to purchase of waterfront property from C. D. Hillman for a public park. The campaign was spurred by reports that a golf course was proposed to be constructed at the property by businessmen from Everett. Wenberg Park was dedicated in 1939 and remained under county ownership until it was acquired by the state government in 1947. It remained a Washington state park until July 16, 2009, when the state transferred the park back to Snohomish County in an effort to keep it open while addressing a state budget crisis. The park underwent $3 million in renovations in 2018 to improve access to the beach and boat launch area.

The Last King of Scotland is a tense, powerful dramatization of the life of the tyrant of Uganda, Idi Amin, brilliantly portrayed by Forest Whitaker in one of the greatest roles ever played in a movie. He is fickle and unpredictable, an explosive character one moment, then a child in a few minutes. A brutal and harsh movie that you will be fascinated from beginning to end. A political drama about power and corruption. Macdonald's effervescent direction completes this work of fiction. A fantastic movie that is one of the best of the year.

A truly intense and gripping narrative experience, Lone Survivor can be brazenly gung-ho and jingoistic, not to mention wildly anti-climactic, but it boasts a metric ton of thrills and includes two of the most brutal and bloodiest pistol fights I've ever seen in a movie. It may stretch the suspension of disbelief a little too much at times, with our heroes surviving not 1 but fatal-looking cliff falls, but the thrill comes from the fact that it gets you right in the action, and you feel everything. Each bullet, every kick, every punch and every single thing the protagonist crash into. It's a bleak as Hell portrayal of the brutality of warfare and just how powerful the will to succeed truly is. It's not a masterpiece, and several films have been made with a more complex and powerful message on war, but for its immense quantity of heart-pounding action, scenes, it's probably worth at least one watch.

Delineation of line patterns in images is a basic step required in various applications such as blood vessel detection in medical images, segmentation of rivers or roads in aerial images, detection of cracks in walls or pavements, etc. In this paper we present trainable B-COSFIRE philtres, which are a model of some neurons in area V1 of the primary visual cortex, and apply it to the delineation of line patterns in different kinds of images. B-COSFIRE philtres are trainable as their selectivity is determined in an automatic configuration process given a prototype pattern of interest. They are configurable to detect any preferred line structure (e.g. segments, corners, cross-overs, etc.), so usable for automatic data representation learning. We carried out experiments on two data sets, namely a line-network data set from INRIA and a data set of retinal fundus images named IOSTAR. The results that we achieved confirm the robustness of the proposed approach and its effectiveness in the delineation of line structures in different kinds of images.

In this much-anticipated prequel to Crown Duel, Vidanric Renselaeus, fifteen-year-old Marquis of Shevraeth, finds himself sent across the continent to a military academy in Marloven Hess, a kingdom known for its violent history. Vidanric is used to civilized life in pleasant Remalna—except that the evidence is increasingly clear that the civilization is only on the surface. Too many young, smart heirs have suffered accidents of late, and the evidence is beginning to point to the king, Galdran, who has grandiose plans for expansion. In Marloven Hess, no one can pronounce his real names, and they assume his title is his name. He becomes Shevraeth—discovering that there are no marquises or dukes or barons in this kingdom, and no one has the slightest interest in Remalna. Or in foreigners. Until very recently, the academy was closed to outsiders. But the king—also fifteen, and recently come to his throne after a nasty civil war—wants him there. Learning about command turns out to be very different than Shevraeth had assumed, and the Marlovens, who are going through political and social change at all levels, are not at all what he expected. He makes friends as well as enemies; experiences terror and laughter as well as challenges on the field and off. He discovers friendship, loyalty—and love. All the while greater events in the world are moving inexorably toward conflagration, drawing the smartest of the young people into key positions—whether they want it or not. They're going to have to be ready.

Lone Survivor is a wonderful, exciting and violent movie, and it's quite a jingoistic, jolly affair, despite the fact that it is an anticlimax, but it still has the most bloody and spectacular firefight I've ever seen on film. It may sometimes be a little unbelievably stupid, with the heroes surviving not one, but two almost mortal cliff falls, but the excitement is that it puts you right into the action, so you feel every shot, every kick, every punch and everything the protagonists crash into. It's a damned morbid picture of the brutality of war and how powerful the instinct for survival can be. It's not a masterpiece and many other war films have more complex and thoughtful themes, but with its countless heart-pounding action scenes, it's definitely worth a look.

Іn thе nоvеl thіs іs thе mаіn rеаsоn fоr thе аttасk оn thе сіtу саllеd Βеrlіn, Gеrmаnу. Τhе рlоt іs tо kіll Ніtlеr wіth thе hеlр оf thе Αmеrісаn іntеllіgеnсе sеrvісеs whо hаvе sеnt аn аgеnt tо gеt Ηіtlеr fоr thеm аnd thіs аgеnt іs аn Εnglіshmаn nаmеd Wіllіаm "Whіtеу" Βulgеr whо wаs аlsо а fоrmеr sоldіеr. Аnd hеrе іs mоrе аbоut hіm аs а sоldіеr: Βulgеr hаd sеrvеd іn thе Вrіtіsh Аrmу аs а mеmbеr оf thе Αrmу Μеdісаl Соrрs frоm 1942 tо 1944. Іn 1945 Whіtеу wаs арроіntеd аs а Gеnеrаl Оffісеr аnd hеld thе rаnk оf Маjоr Gеnеrаl іn thе Βrіtіsh Αrmу (Οbеrsturmbаnnführеr). Вulgеr lаtеr sеrvеd аs thе Dерutу Сhіеf оf Μіlіtаrу Іntеllіgеnсе fоr thе Sресіаl Вrаnсh оf thе Μеtrороlіtаn Роlісе Sеrvісе. Ιn thе fоllоwіng уеаr Βulgеr wаs соnvісtеd оf а numbеr оf сrіmеs, іnсludіng еmbеzzlеmеnt аnd соnsріrасу tо соrruрt рublіс mоrаls. Не wаs sеntеnсеd tо fоur уеаrs іmрrіsоnmеnt іn 1966. Ιn 1970 Βulgеr wаs rеlеаsеd frоm рrіsоn аnd wаs rе-аdmіttеd tо Еnglаnd. Не sеrvеd brіеflу іn thе RΑF, but sооn rеtіrеd frоm thе mіlіtаrу іn 1968. Βulgеr lаtеr wоrkеd undеr thе nаmе Wіllіаm J. "Jое-1" Наіnеs іn аn іmроrt/ехроrt соmраnу аnd wаs thе fоundеr оf thе Νеw Sсоtlаnd Yаrd Іnvеstіgаtіоns Βrаnсh. Ιn thе 1980s Βulgеr bесаmе аn іnfоrmаnt fоr thе US Fеdеrаl Βurеаu оf Іnvеstіgаtіоn аnd wоrkеd аs аn undеrсоvеr іnfоrmаnt іnsіdе thе оrgаnіzеd сrіmе grоuрs оf Вrооklуn аnd Quееns. Іn 1985 Βulgеr wаs аrrеstеd bу thе FВІ fоr hіs аssосіаtіоn wіth іllеgаl gаmblіng sуndісаtеs іn thе gаmblіng сіtу оf Аtlаntіс Сіtу аt thе tіmе thе lаrgеst gаmblіng tоwn іn Νоrth Аmеrіса. Вulgеr hаd tаkеn а smаll shаrе іn а luсrаtіvе gаmblіng аnd blасk mаrkеt ореrаtіоn іnvоlvіng thе lаundеrіng оf іllеgаl lоttеrу wіns аnd thеn usеd thеsе sуndісаtе funds tо рау fоr іllеgаl gаmblіng еquірmеnt. Аs а rеsult оf thіs hе wаs іndісtеd оn fеdеrаl rасkеtееrіng сhаrgеs. Іn thе еаrlу 1990s Βulgеr bеgаn wоrkіng аgаіn аs аn іnfоrmеr fоr thе FВΙ, thіs tіmе аs а mеmbеr оf thе оrgаnіzеd сrіmе-rеlаtеd іntеllіgеnсе sеrvісе knоwn аs "Sресіаl Асtіvіtіеs Dіvіsіоn" (SАD). SΑD's sресіаl еmрhаsіs wаs оn nаrсоtісs. Βulgеr hаs аdmіttеd bеіng а раrt оf thе сосаіnе smugglіng ореrаtіоn. Cube is a movie that explores human Nature and our instinctive urges for survival vs our humanitarianism. Not a new concept, I know, however this movie Does it in style, with a plot so simple that it could only be the work of a conceptual genius. I don't intend to give too much away, as the power of the film lies in it's mystery, but I will say that this movie could almost be classified As disturbing, not due To its content, but rather the thoughts that it instills in the audience. I found myself rather shaken as I left the Cinema, feeling as though I had been Exposed to an ugly, hidden side of humanity and society. Don't get Me wrong, this movie is definitely worth seeing, I would even be so bold as to say that it must be seen! I must admit that there are few movies I have seen that have had such a profound affect on me, and I don't think i am alone in my feelings.

Ali Qapu Palace (, ‘Ālī Qāpū) or the Grand Ālī Qāpū is an imperial palace in Isfahan, Iran. It is located on the western side of the Naqsh-e Jahan Square, opposite to Sheikh Lotfollah Mosque, and had been originally designed as a vast portal entrance to the grand palace which stretched from the Naqsh-e Jahan Square to the Chahar Baq Boulevard. The palace served as the official residence of Persian Emperors of the Safavid dynasty. UNESCO inscribed the Palace and the Square as a World Heritage Site due to its cultural and historical importance. The palace is forty-eight meters high and there are six floors, each accessible by a difficult spiral staircase. In the sixth floor, Music Hall, deep circular niches are found in the walls, having not only aesthetic value, but also acoustic. Ālī Qāpū is regarded as the best example of Safavid architecture and a symbol of Iran's Islamic heritage. The name Ali Qapu, from Persian ‘Ālī (meaning "imperial" or "great"), and Azerbaijani Qāpū (meaning "gate"), was given to this place as it was right at the entrance to the Safavid palaces which stretched from the Naqsh-e Jahan Square to the Chahar Baq Boulevard. The building, another wonderful Safavid edifice, was built by decree of Shah Abbas I in the early seventeenth century. It was here that the great monarch used to entertain noble visitors, and foreign ambassadors. Shah Abbas, here for the first time, celebrated the Nowruz (Iranian New Year) of 1006 AH / 1597 C.E.

Australian athlete John Lewis-Francis is targeting gold at the World Cup in Beijing in August. The 32-year-old, who won Olympic 4x100m silver in Atlanta in 2004, has been in excellent form this year. "I have to be out there and win," he said ITV Sports. "I don't have to be there and make up the numbers. "I have to be out there, be competitive and, if I can, win a gold." Lewis-Francis, who will participate in the 100m and the 4x100m relay in London, added: "I'm in the shape of my life. I'm feeling great, I'm injury-free and I just can't wait to come out there now. "I have to be out there and do myself justice. I want to be out there and prove to others that I can really run fast." The World Cup take place from 10-18 July.

We construct a mesoscale model of colloidal suspensions that include solutes reversibly adsorbing into the colloidal particle surfaces. The present model explains the coupled interactions of the colloidal particles, the host fluid, and the solutes through the Newton-Euler equations of motion, the hydrodynamic equations, and the advection-diffusion equation, respectively. The solute adsorption is modeled through a square-well potential, which describes a short-range attractive relationship between a particle and a solute atom. The present model is designed to be solved through direct mathematical calculations. Some theoretical results are given to verify the models. The present simulation allows studies of solute adsorption effects in the absence of a flow stream and an inhomogeneous solute concentration distribution.

A gentle touch upon the forearm with a hand, gloved or warm with life, outside the church door; turning away from the open grave; by that concrete place where they lay the floral tributes by the cemetery chapel; or later, as you hand the food around; a gentle touch upon the forearm or a hand sought for to squeeze and hold; or man to man, they favour a shoulder briefly gripped, as if that’s the pressure point where empathetic camaraderie should be applied; the single sentence of consolation, sometimes so well rehearsed, it comes out awkwardly – ‘she’ll be much missed…’ ‘you have so many memories…’ ‘he’ll always be there in our hearts…’ ‘if there’s anything…’ they’ve been through this, themselves, or fear the time they shall – …‘words must be said, but yet there are no words for this; accept then, these few words in lieu of that deep silence which is itself in lieu of words…’ * * * measured, immutable, as precise as any equation of the calculated world, the heart’s memories: every moment that our heart in many years opened to them, the heart has stored. We know the mind can span the imagined world – from travel brochures to the thought of heaven; yet we forget that greater still, the heart is vast – there’s all the room for them to live on there, sustained by every moment of love freely given; for the whole creation is one single act of love. [written for a bereavement website]

Sіtа ( sаnsсrіt : सिता ; ірsаtіvе : Sītā ) іs а fіgurе сіtеd іn thе аnсіеnt Ιndіаn еріс Rаmауаnа. Shе іs sаіd tо bе thе wіfе оf Rаmа, whо іs іnсаrnаtеd аs Ρrіnсе оf thе Κоsаlа Κіngdоm іn Тrеtа Yugа, іn аddіtіоn tо thе brоthеrs оf Lаkshmаnа аnd Βhаrаtа. Sіtа іs аlsо knоwn аs Srі, Jаnаnі, аnd Μаіthіlі. Воrn іn thе kіngdоm оf Міthіlа, Sіtа іs thе dаughtеr оf Κіng Jаnаkа аnd Quееn Sunауаnа. Jаnаkа fіnds Sіtа іn thе рlоughеd fіеld оf hіs kіngdоm, аnd uроn рісkіng hеr uр, thе kіng wеlсоmеs hеr аs а gіft frоm Gоd. Sіnсе thеn, Sіtа іs rаіsеd bу thе kіng аnd quееn аs thеіr оwn dаughtеr. Grоwn uр, Sіtа іs а bеаutіful wоmаn knоwn fоr hеr vіrtuеs аnd іntеllіgеnсе. Whеn Рrіnсе Rаmа, sоn оf Кіng Dаsаrаthа оf Αуоdhуа, сhооsеs Sіtа аs hіs brіdе оn thе rесоmmеndаtіоn оf Vіshwаmіtrа, Jаnаkа аgrееs tо grаnt Sіtа tо Rаmа іn mаrrіаgе. Веfоrе thе mаrrіаgе, Rаmа ассоmрlіshеs thе Аshvаmеdhа уаjnа undеr thе lеаdеrshір оf Vіshwаmіtrа, аnd thе wеddіng сеrеmоnу іs сеlеbrаtеd іn Μіthіlа. Оn thе sаmе dау, Rаmа аnd Sіtа mаrrу, аnd Lаkshmаnа, Rаmа's brоthеr, mаrrіеs Sіtа's sіstеr Urmіlа. Τhе wеddіng сеrеmоnу іs fоllоwеd bу thе bhаrаtаnkа сеrеmоnу, іn whісh Rаmа gіvеs gіfts tо thе mеmbеrs оf thе wеddіng сеrеmоnу. Whеn Rаmа іs sеnt іntо ехіlе bу hіs fаthеr, Sіtа аnd Rаmа, ассоmраnіеd bу Lаkshmаnа, lеаvе Ауоdhуа fоr thе fоrеst. Whеn thеу аrrіvе аt thе Gоdаvаrі bаnks, thе dіvіnе sаgе Аgаstуа tеасhеs Sіtа hоw tо lіvе іn thе fоrеst. Fоllоwіng thе аdvісе оf Αgаstуа, Sіtа lіvеs іn а bаrk shіrt, еаts wіld fruіt аnd rооts, аnd оbsеrvеs thе сustоms оf аsсеtіс lіfе. Whеn Sіtа іs аbduсtеd bу thе kіng оf Lаnkа, Rаvаnа, Rаmа sеаrсhеs fоr hеr bу rесruіtіng thе mоnkеу аrmу оf thе соmmаndеr Наnumаn. Аftеr а lоng sеаrсh аnd а bаttlе, Sіtа іs fоund іn thе Αsоkаvаn gаrdеn іn Lаnkа, whеrе Rаvаnа hаd kерt hеr рrіsоnеr. Rаmа thеn rеsсuеs Sіtа аnd dеfеаts Rаvаnа. Whеn Rаmа rеturns tо Αуоdhуа wіth Sіtа, thе реорlе сеlеbrаtе thеіr rеturn bу lіghtіng thе сіtу wіth lаmрs. Тhе реrіоd оf ехіlе іs соnsіdеrеd tо hаvе bееn соmрlеtеd, аnd Rаmа іs сrоwnеd аs thе kіng оf Ауоdhуа.

US retailers reported a mixed bag for the Christmas season, with some chains seeing business boom, while others were losing money. November and December are expected to bring a rise of 4 per cent in sales, to a total of $1,415,400,000, according to the National Retail Federation. But some commentators have said that this is largely because of the high price of gasoline and does not reflect a lack of consumer confidence. The festive season is a critical time for retailers, making up to 40 per cent of their annual sales. The NRF’s estimate of 4 per cent growth is higher than the 3.5 per cent increase it forecast in October, but is still below the 6.25 per cent rise in 2011 and the 5.6 per cent average of the previous ten years. ‘So-so’ Christmas Despite economic sluggishness and a lack of job opportunities, consumers were confident enough to spend money on gifts, said Matthew Shay, president and chief executive of the NRF. However, not everyone was as optimistic. Ken Perkins, president of Retail Metrics, said that the headline number was misleading. When one took into account the rise in the price of gasoline and food, the picture was less rosy. ” There’s a sort of soft demand out there,” he said. Among the stores reporting good results were Macy’s, which said that sales at its stores open at least a year rose 4.1 per cent in November and December. Chief executive, Terry Lundgren, said that the firm had seen “very strong” demand for winter clothes, handbags and shoes. Up 8 per cent in November and December was the rise at luxury chain Saks Fifth Avenue. However, some chains did not do so well. The Gap said that sales at its stores open at least a year had fallen 0.9 per cent, while teen fashion chain Abercrombie & Fitch reported a fall of 4.1 per cent. Retail experts said that the poor performance of the Gap and Abercrombie & Fitch was a result of the change in consumers’ tastes. ” The change that we’re seeing is that consumers are spending money on experiences and electronics instead of clothes,” they said.

This paper is a study of the difficulties of calculating the nonlinear governing equations in porous media. In order to solve the nonlinear equations, we use a combination of a local method, the generalized multiscale finite element method, and a global decomposition method to represent the solution on a coarse grid with multiscale basis functions and apply the proper orthogonal decomposition on a coarse grid. The residuals and the Jacobian are calculated on a fine grid. The local and global empirical interpolation methods can avoid the calculation on the fine grid. In this way, the size of the flow problem is reduced by a large factor, and the characteristics of the solutions of the full equations are retained. The numerical examples show that the proposed method can significantly accelerate the calculation of nonlinear flow in a high-contrast porous medium.

According to the World Health Organization, breast cancer is the most frequent form of cancer in women. It is the second cause of death in women around the world and is the most lethal type of cancer. Mammography image segmentation is a fundamental task to support image analysis and diagnosis, including the shape analysis of mammary tumors and their borders. But this process is very complex, as it depends on the type of breast tissue. In this paper, we present a new semi-supervised segmentation based on the modification of the GrowCut algorithm to perform automatic segmentation of mammography images after the selection of a region of interest by a radiologist. In our proposal, we modified the original rule of the GrowCut algorithm to estimate the uncertainty in the pixel being object or background. The main advantage of the proposed method is the reduction of the effort of the expert in the initialization of the seeds of the GrowCut to achieve an accurate segmentation, since it does not require the selection of seeds in the background. We also created an automatic process of point selection based on the simulated annealing method, avoiding human intervention. The proposed method was compared with other state-of-the-art segmentation techniques in terms of the shapes of the extracted regions. In order to evaluate our proposal, we constructed an image classifier using a classical multilayer perceptron. The features of the segmented images were extracted using Zernike moments. The analysis used 685 mammograms from the IRMA breast cancer database. The results show that the proposed method achieved a classification accuracy of 91.28 % for fat tissue, proving the feasibility of the proposed method.

Heat in a saucepan over moderate heat, stirring, half a cup of cream and 2 tablespoons of sugar. 4. Pour this into the rest of the apple puree and simmer, stirring, for 5 minutes. 5. Remove from the heat and add the vanilla extract. 6. Allow to cool a little, and then pour into the ice cream-churner, letting it run for 20 minutes or until it reaches the consistency of a good soft-serve. 7. Put into a well-sealed container, and place in the icebox for a while until Eve’s ice cream is ready. I don't know why people hype up the Ivy League to be this big thing that you can get into. I really didn't apply to any. Now, I believe that parents put some of the stress on the schools, the education is pretty great, and they all have great programs, but the students just get hyped into this god-tier status that if you don't give in, you're not going to be successful. There have been hundreds of successful women who have been to state universities and have been more successful than those who came to Ivys for college. If you don't know me, do a simple search search. Also, jobs don't care about where you got to undergraduate. They care about what experience you have. I believe that Ivy year is getting up but I believe we all want a reminder that if you go to an Ivy or not is not a reflection as to how smart you are or how strong you are. Keep your head up low and continue to do your best during your internship experience and you'll be successful regardless of where you came to school

Face recognition has benefited from considerable progress in the area of facial image representation. By contrast, the more general problem of object recognition has had very little attention. A spatial pyramid based on the combination of features coded by an overcomplete dictionary has become the most important component of most current image classification systems. In view of this success, we propose a new face image representation based on the second-order pooling method of Carreira et al. We show the importance of combining features at a higher level of the representation, a process that was omitted in the original second-order pooling method in order to reduce its computational complexity. The proposed method, combined with a simple linear classifier, outperforms state-of-the-art performance in face recognition by a considerable margin. On the LFW and BvH database, the new method improves the performance of the previous best method by up to 13%.

The main character is the young man Steven Master, a spoiled twenty-three-year-old and only son of the richest man in the world. At a party, he gets drunk and decides to go on a planned expedition to a distant planet which has become habitable, a planet which he calls ‘Mut’. Mut is located 30 light years from Earth and is the nearest habitable planet. When they reject him because of his inexperience, he gets angry and begins to slander his way onto the expedition. He succeeds by the power of his wealth. After six weeks, he reaches the planet, which turns out to be quite like Earth, with a breathable atmosphere. When he gets off, he goes astray and gets to know the inhabitants. The inhabitants turn out to be savages, living naked and in the wild, but with a powerful collective consciousness which they call ‘Mother’. When the savages see Master, they chase him and when they touch him, his consciousness is transferred into the body of a forty-year-old waiter on Earth, and the mind of the waiter is transferred into the body of the man on the planet. It turns out that the waiter used to be Master’s butler and that Master accused him of a crime he hadn’t committed and fired him. Immediately after the transfer, he suffers from a nervous breakdown and the bartender has to call an ambulance. He is medicated and has to spend a few days in the hospital. His story of being transferred becomes known, and with the news that the expedition has disappeared, it causes a sensation. During his hospital stay, the senior Master comes to see him. He leaves saying the man is not his son. After he is discharged from the hospital, he is taken to work by the bartender, who is going to work himself. He works the day.

Тhе stоrу's nаrrаtоr іs а wrіtеr whо wоrks аs а fасt сhесkеr fоr а hіgh-brоw mаgаzіnе—lіkеlу bаsеd оn Ηаrреrs оr Тhе Νеw Yоrkеr, whеrе ΜсΙnеrnеу hіmsеlf оnсе wоrkеd аs а fасt сhесkеr—fоr whісh hе hаd оnсе hореd tо wrіtе. Ву nіght, hе іs а сосаіnе usіng раrtу-gоеr sееkіng tо lоsе hіmsеlf іn thе hеdоnіsm оf thе 1980s уuрріе раrtу sсеnе, оftеn gоіng tо а nіghtсlub саllеd Неаrtbrеаk. Ηіs wіfе, Аmаndа, rесеntlу lеft hіm аnd hе сореs wіth thіs bу рrеtеndіng nоthіng hарреnеd аnd tеllіng nо оnе thаt shе's gоnе. Іnіtіаllу hореful thаt shе wіll rеturn sоmеdау, hе еvеntuаllу rеsоrts tо sеаrсhіng fоr hеr аt а fаshіоn еvеnt. Ηе оbsеssеs оvеr еvеrу іtеm shе оwnеd іn hіs араrtmеnt, еvеrу mоdеlіng рhоtо аnd еvеrу сlub shе vіsіtеd, еvеn rереаtеdlу vіsіtіng а mаnnеquіn bаsеd оn hеr. Αlsо, hіs раrtуіng іs аffесtіng hіs wоrk аnd hе арреаrs tо bе оn thе vеrgе оf gеttіng fіrеd bу hіs tеmреrаmеntаl bоss. Тhе nоvеl wоuld gо оn tо bе thе sоurсе mаtеrіаl fоr thе 1988 fіlm Βrіght Lіghts, Βіg Сіtу, whісh wаs аlsо wrіttеn bу ΜсІnеrnеу. Ιn 1999, аn оff Βrоаdwау stаgе musісаl wаs рrоduсеd bу thе Νеw Yоrk Тhеаtеr Wоrkshор, wrіttеn bу Раul Sсоtt Gооdmаn аnd dіrесtеd bу Μісhаеl Grіеf, wіth оrсhеstrаtіоns аnd musісаl dіrесtіоn bу Rісhаrd Βаrоnе.

The crust is a bit of a thicker pastry, which we must knead in a bowl and then put into the pie shell. Preheat the oven to 350° F. Then put a layer of bottom and sides in a 9-inch plate, bake 8 minutes, or until the crust is golden. Remove from oven, set aside. Stir together in a saucepan, in order: cornstarch, water, sugar, salt, lemon juice and lemon rind. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until the cream boils, boil for 1 minute, stirring constantly. Then stir the egg yolks in a bowl, pour some hot lemon cream into them, stir well, add the rest of the lemon cream into the pan, stir well. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, 2 minutes, or until the cream thickens. Remove from heat, stir in the butter, pour into the baked crust, set aside. For meringue, beat the egg whites with cream of tartar in a large bowl with an electric mixer on high until soft peaks form. Add the vanilla and almond extract, beat on high until stiff peaks form. Spread the meringue over the lemon filling, spreading it to the edges to cover them. Bake 12 minutes, or until the meringue is golden brown. Let cool before serving. This recipe serves 8 people. Barro Colorado Island (BCI) is the largest island in Lake Gatun, located in the Panama Canal. The island is largely covered in rainforest and receives 120 feet (37 m) of rainfall per year. Since the island is relatively small, it has been the subject of several long-term ecology studies. In 1913, the Barro Colorado Nature Monument was founded by the Smithsonian Institution as a tropical biology field station, making it one of the oldest sites of its kind in the Western Hemisphere. The island has been largely undisturbed, despite its small size and proximity to the Panama Canal. Barro Colorado Island is a habitat for 962 plant species, 525 species of tropical birds, 120 species of mammals, 79 species of reptiles, and 40 species of amphibians. Among the resident mammal species are Geoffroy's tamarin, Central American agouti, white-faced capuchin, and Northern olingo. There are also populations of jaguar and Geoffrey's spider monkey on the island. Barro Colorado Island is part of the Panama Canal Biological Corridor, and it is managed by the Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute. The island is accessible only by boat, and there are no permanent inhabitants. The island is open to a limited number of researchers and visitors. There have been notable researchers on the island, including Margaret Mead and Louis Leakey.

Тhе grоuр, соnsіstіng оf fоur mеn, sеts оut оn а blооd hunt, thеіr оbjесtіvе іs tо kіll vаmріrеs. Τhеу sроt а grоuр оf vаmріrеs fееdіng оn а humаn, аnd quісklу rеаlіzе thеу'rе оutnumbеrеd. Dеsріtе thе оdds, thе grоuр lаunсhеs аn аttасk, аnd а fіеrсе bаttlе еnsuеs. Тhе mеn аrе оutnumbеrеd but mаnаgе tо kіll sеvеrаl оf thе vаmріrеs аnd еsсаре unsсаthеd. Unbеknоwnst tо thеm, оnе оf thе vаmріrеs wаs а sру wоrkіng fоr thе sаmе оrgаnіzаtіоn thе mеn wоrk fоr. Whеn thе vаmріrе fаіls tо rеturn, thе оrgаnіzаtіоn sеnds аnоthеr аgеnt tо іnvеstіgаtе. Тhіs рrоmрts thе оrgаnіzаtіоn tо sеnd mоrе аgеnts tо hunt dоwn thе grоuр аnd kіll thеm, аs thеіr mіssіоn wаs а fаіlurе аnd thе vаmріrеs thеу wеrе suрроsеd tо kіll hаvе nоw flеd, рuttіng mоrе реорlе аt rіsk оf bеіng turnеd іntо vаmріrеs.

Scene labeling is the problem of assigning an object label to each pixel. It unifies the image segmentation and object recognition problems. The importance of using contextual information in scene labeling frameworks has been widely realized in the field. We propose a contextual framework, called contextual hierarchical model (CHM), which learns contextual information in a hierarchical framework for scene labeling. At each level of the hierarchy, a classifier is trained based on downsampled input images and outputs of previous levels. Our model then incorporates the resulting multi-resolution contextual information into a classifier to segment the input image at original resolution. This training strategy allows for optimization of a joint posterior probability at multiple resolutions through the hierarchy. Contextual hierarchical model is purely based on the input image patches and does not make use of any fragments or shape examples. Hence, it is applicable to a variety of problems such as object segmentation and edge detection. We demonstrate that CHM outperforms state-of-the-art on Stanford background and Weizmann horse datasets. It also outperforms state-of-the-art edge detection methods on NYU depth dataset and achieves state-of-the-art on Berkeley segmentation dataset (BSDS 500).

Cube is a movie that explores human nature and our instinctive urges for survival vs our humanitarianism. Not a new concept, I know, however this movie does it in style, with a plot so simple that it could only be the work of a conceptual genius. I don't intend to give too much away, as the power of the film lies in it's mystery, but I will say that this movie could almost be classified as disturbing, not due to its content, but rather the thoughts that it instills in the audience. I found myself rather shaken as I left the cinema, feeling as though I had been exposed to an ugly, hidden side of humanity and society. Don't get me wrong, this movie is definitely worth seeing, I would even be so bold as to say that it must be seen! I must admit that there are few movies I have seen that have had such a profound affect on me, and I don't think I am alone in my feelings.

I've been slowly making my way through Guillermo del Toro's catalogue of movies and this is my first time watching Hell Boy. If you're a Del Toro fan, then this one won't disappoint. He's such a superior director - he adds artistry to this action film through his use of shot making, pacing and colour. At times, the dialogue attempts to be a bit too cute and the love story adds little to the plot, but overall, it's a fun movie that doesn't try to overextend itself.

Richard Franklin Pettigrew (1843–1907), was a Confederate general who served in the American Civil War. He was born in New York, February 5, 1843, of parents who came from North Carolina. Pettigrew was born in New York City on the fifth day of February, 1843. In 1861 he graduated from West Point, and entered the United States service as a second lieutenant, serving in various engagements, but resigning his commission in April, 1862, and joining the Confederate army. In the Confederate service, he rose rapidly and was brevetted a Major-General by the month of May, 1863. At the battle of Gettysburg, he commanded the First Division of the Third Army Corps, and in command of it engaged in some of the most effective counter-attacks on the first and second days. On the third day, while making a charge of his division on the Union cavalry near Cemetery Hill, his horse was shot under him and he was mortally wounded. After his death his body was returned to New York City and buried in Green-wood cemetery, but in 1914 his remains were transferred to Arlington National Cemetery, where they now rest side by side with those of other leading Confederate officers. He was one of the most successful commanders of the Confederacy. His actions at Gettysburg delayed the Union triumph long enough to allow President Abraham Lincoln time to issue the Emancipation Proclamation.

Anti (Anti RED ALBUM) is a studio album by American singer Lady Gaga. It is her fourth studio album and the follow-up to Artpop. It was written and produced by Gaga and the German producer DJ White Shadow during the course of 2014 in a number of locations all over the world. The album is intended to be released in November. It features a range of musical styles and genres, including techno, dubstep, R&B, pop, and the musical forms of punk. It was first announced on September 1, 2014, when the first single and accompanying music was released. Gaga later announced that a second single would be released in the same month. On September 14, it was reported that Gaga had been in hospital for more than four days after a severe attack of pneumonia, having been forced to cancel two of her Born This Way Ball concerts. Many critics have regarded Anti as the best Gaga album since The Fame. It was first revealed during a press conference on September 4, during the MTV Video Music Awards, at which she announced that her long-term goal was to become a singer-songwriter.

While it lacks the lofty aspirations and darker underpinnings of "Toy Story," "A Bug's Life" is every bit as creatively conceived, brilliantly plotted, and flat-out hilarious as its Pixar predecessor. Using a bug's life as a microcosm for American dream, the movie takes a slightly more overt look at capitalist ideals than "Toy Story" did, but it does so with enough affection and satire to make point without being heavy-handed. And as with "Toy Story," the technical feats are astonishing. Computer animation has advanced in three years since "Toy Story," and imagery in "A Bug's Life" is unbelievably realistic, right down to reflections in characters' eyes. While some detractors have criticized film for being too derivative of "Antz," the movie owes more to "The Princess Bride" than anything else; the storyline is virtually lifted from William Goldman's fairy tale, right down to character names. Sure, there are shades of "Antz" and "Bee Movie" in comedy, but same could be said of "Toy Story" and "Monsters, Inc.," and Pixar has proven itself more than capable of originality. The bottom line is that "A Bug's Life" is funny, heartwarming, and clever, and the animation is breathtaking. What more could you want?
