Celina Consuela Gabriella Carvajal (born January 30, 1980), better known by her stage name, Lena Hall, is an American actress and singer. She played the role of Nicola in the Broadway show Kinky Boots and received a Tony nomination for her performance as Yitzhak in the revival of Hedwig and the Angry Inch in 2014, which also earned her a nomination for a Grammy for the cast album. In 2016 she made history by being the first to play both Hedwig and Yitzhak in the same production during the national tour. Her other Broadway credits include Cats, 42nd Street, Dracula, and Tarzan. Hall has also starred in Off-Broadway productions of Radiant Baby, Bedbugs!!! and Rooms: A Rock Romance. She also played the title role in How to Transcend a Happy Marriage, written by her husband, The American Theatre Wing's director, Joe Mantello. Hall has also appeared in films such as Sex and the City (2008), The Graduates (2008), Born from a Foot of Elm (2008), The Big Gay Musical (2009), and the critically acclaimed Becks (2017). She has also appeared in the TV series All My Children, Girls, and Good Girls Revolt, and she voiced the role of Countess Coloratura on My Little Pony: Friendship is Magic. In 2020, she joined the cast of the science-fiction epic Snowpiercer as Miss Audrey.

Oil prices retreated from four-month highs in early trading on Tuesday after producers' cartel Opec said it was now unlikely to cut production. He said that high oil prices meant Opec was unlikely to stick to its Plan to cut output in the second quarter. In London, Brent crude fell 32 cents to $49.74 a barrel. Opec members are next meeting to discuss production levels on 16 March. US demand for heating oil was predicted to be about 14% Above normal this week, while stocks were currently about 7.5% below the levels of a year ago. Cold weather across Europe has also put upward pressure On Crude prices.

For a chocolate cake: 1 package chocolate cake mix 1 cup cold water 1 cup evaporated milk 1 package coconut pudding mix 2 tablespoons of brandy or coffee 2 cups whipped topping 2 tablespoons of icing sugar 4 cups of blueberries, cherries or raspberries. 3. Then mix the cold water, evaporated milk, coconut pudding and brandy in a two-liter jug or in a larger bowl and let stand for ten minutes. Add the whipped topping and beat with an electric beater until the mixture is smooth. Pour the pudding mixture over the cake in a large dish and add the blueberries, cherries or raspberries. Don't stir. Pour the compote over the top. Cover and put in the refrigerator for at least two hours. This cake doesn't give surprises, no sudden "epiphanies" and no cakes disguised as cakes, nor do you have to worry about catching fire. It seems easy, delicious and the cherry on top and you may not even need a fire extinguisher. But after this cake had been baked and cooled and we looked at the recipe, we found a passage that was not quite as clear as we would have liked: "Bake until the cake is done." It's so vague that a novice baker could end up in crime, or in any case would not make desserts that would not pass. How can you tell when your cake is done? And what is it anyway? We did not want to cause any embarrassment to our readers and therefore baked the cake three times (as a result of the test we ate several slices). The first time we baked at 350 ° F until a skewer came out clean, and we had a good and solid cake.

In this much-anticipated prequel to Crown Duel, Vidanric Renselaeus, fifteen-year-old Marquis of Shevraeth, finds himself sent across the continent to a military academy in Marloven Hess, a kingdom known for its violent history. Vidanric is used to civilized life in pleasant Remalna—except that the evidence is increasingly clear that the civilization is only on the surface. Too many young, smart heirs have suffered accidents of late, and the evidence is beginning to point to the king, Galdran, who has grandiose plans for expansion. In Marloven Hess, no one can pronounce his real names, and they assume his title is his name. He becomes Shevraeth—discovering that there are no marquises or dukes or barons in this kingdom, and no one has the slightest interest in Remalna. Or in foreigners. Until very recently, the academy was closed to outsiders. But the king—also fifteen, and recently come to his throne after a nasty civil war—wants him there. Learning about command turns out to be very different than Shevraeth had assumed, and the Marlovens, who are going through political and social change at all levels, are not at all what he expected. He makes friends as well as enemies; experiences terror and laughter as well as challenges on the field and off. He discovers friendship, loyalty—and love. All the while greater events in the world are moving inexorably toward conflagration, drawing the smartest of the young people into key positions—whether they want it or not. They're going to have to be ready.

A European Parliament committee has called for a rewrite of the proposals for a controversial new European law on inventions using digital data. The Legal Affairs Committee (JURI) has instructed the Commission to rework the so-called Computer Implemented Inventions Directive, which has been subject to much criticism. The law has been accused of favoring large companies at the expense of small ones, and would have had an impact on the innovation of open source software. The proposal is to allow patents for inventions that are achieved using data, in other words, a so-called "computer-implemented invention. " The draft of the law was rejected twice by Poland, one of the largest EU countries, whose approval was required for the directive to be adopted. Several national parliaments have already been heavily lobbied by this issue, and many of them have rejected it. In the JURI meeting, only two MEPs voted in favor of the directive, and one voted against it. The opponents of the draft directive welcomed the decision and said that a new first reading of the proposal would give the European Union the opportunity to better debate the consequences of this directive in all member states. In the United States, the patenting of software and methods for doing business on the Internet is already allowed, which is why the American Amazon.com owns a patent for its "one-click" service. Critics are afraid that the directive will lead to similar situations in Europe. In this case, they fear, small programmers would suffer from lawsuits against large companies, who could easily have legal and financial resources at their disposal. Proponents argue that the current legislation is not functioning properly and that the directive will create a level playing field, without bringing the legislation in line with that of the U.S.

Leslie and Peter are childhood friends who become lovers the summer before their senior year in high school. Their romance is immediately complicated by Leslie’s discovery—by reading her mother’s diary—that her mother, Aline, and his father, Nelson, are having an affair. Before the summer is over their parents have announced their impending divorces and Leslie and Peter’s lives are thrown in disarray. The pair spends the next few months of their lives dealing with senior year in high school, the divorces of the parents, and the quick marriage that legally makes them stepsiblings. In addition, Peter is striving for early acceptance at Harvard while Leslie spends much of her time in rehearsal for her high school play for she plans on going to college for acting and drama. Peter at the start of the school year continues to live with his mother; Nelson moves into a new apartment with his new wife and stepdaughter. Leslie is upset at the new living arrangements because she is close to her father and is angry with Aline for the divorce and quick remarriage. In her struggle to deal with the divorce Peter’s mother decides to sell the family home and move to Chicago to finish her college degree. This forces Peter to move in with his father, stepmother and stepsister/girlfriend. The awkwardness of the situation causes the two to argue and abruptly end their physical relationship, having kept it a secret from their parents. As they move on with their lives, Peter and Leslie reconcile and renew their intimacy as the new marriage begins to fall apart primarily because of Nelson’s womanizing, although Aline’s emotional neediness is also a contributing factor. The novel ends with the couple planning a cross country car trip during the summer before they go off to separate colleges. No longer related, they are more comfortable to resume their relationship without the complications imposed by their parents' actions.

Background: Cardiac MRI derived biventricular mass and function parameters, such as end-systolic volume (ESV), end-diastolic volume (EDV), ejection fraction (EF), stroke volume (SV), and ventricular mass (VM) are clinically well established. Image segmentation can be challenging and time-consuming, due to the complex anatomy of the human heart. Objectives: This study introduces $\nu$-net (/nju:n$\varepsilon$t/) -- a deep learning approach allowing for fully-automated high quality segmentation of right (RV) and left ventricular (LV) endocardium and epicardium for extraction of cardiac function parameters. Methods: A set consisting of 253 manually segmented cases has been used to train a deep neural network. Subsequently, the network has been evaluated on 4 different multicenter data sets with a total of over 1000 cases. Results: For LV EF the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) is 98, 95, and 80 % (95 %), and for RV EF 96, and 87 % (80 %) on the respective data sets (human expert ICCs reported in parenthesis). The LV VM ICC is 95, and 94 % (84 %), and the RV VM ICC is 83, and 83 % (54 %). This study proposes a simple adjustment procedure, allowing for the adaptation to distinct segmentation philosophies. $\nu$-net exhibits state of-the-art performance in terms of dice coefficient. Conclusions: Biventricular mass and function parameters can be determined reliably in high quality by applying a deep neural network for cardiac MRI segmentation, especially in the anatomically complex right ventricle. Adaption to individual segmentation styles by applying a simple adjustment procedure is viable, allowing for the processing of novel data without time-consuming additional training.

Hasan Abdullayev (also spelled as Gasan Mamed Bagir ogly Abdullaev; ; ; August 20, 1918 – September 1, 1993) was a leading Soviet and Azerbaijani physicist, scientist and public official, who served as President of the National Academy of Sciences Of the Azerbaijan SSR. He was a Doctor of Sciences in physics And mathematics, Professor of physics and mathematics, Director Of the Institute of Mathematics and Physics of the National Academy of Sciences of the Azerbaijan SSR, full Academician of the National Academy of sciences of the Azerbaijan SSR, corresponding member of the soviet Academy of Sciences and Russian Academy of Sciences, and in 1970-1983 was the longest-serving President of the national Academy of Sciences of the Azerbaijan SSR. He was also an elected member of the Azerbaijan SSR Parliament, and the elected member of the 8th, 9th and 10th convocations Of the Supreme Soviet of the Soviet Union. Academician Abdullayev was one of the founders of the Soviet semiconductors physics and a leading scientist in new technologies. He made an outstanding contribution to the development of electronics, astrophysics, aeronautics, medicine, biophysics and defense industries. Academician Abdullayev was the author of 585 Soviet and foreign patents, including 171 Secret and 65 top secret patents, author of 28 scientific books (monographs), over 800 journal and encyclopedia articles in English, Russian and azerbaijani languages. Biography Hasan Abdullayev was born on August 20, 1918, in Yaycı, nakhchivan during the time of the Azerbaijan democratic Republic. He died on September 1, 1993, in Baku, and was buried at the Alley of Honor.

Crosswind stabilisation (CWS) is a relatively new advanced driver-assistance system in cars and trucks that was first featured in a 2009 Mercedes-Benz S-Class. CWS assists drivers in controlling a vehicle during strong wind conditions such as driving over a bridge or when overtaking a semi-truck. CWS uses yaw rate, lateral acceleration, steering angle, and velocity sensors to determine how much assistance to give the driver in a certain scenario whether it be at different speeds or while turning. Using different components throughout the vehicle like brakes, differentials, and suspension, CWS can implement the readings from force sensors to properly assist the driver in a given situation. Origination Crosswind stabilisation was first used by Mercedes-Benz in 2009 in their S class and then later implemented in their Sprinter and Metris vans. Before this technology existed, vans and trucks of similar size had a higher risk of crashing in strong wind conditions as the surface area on the side of the vans and trucks caused the wind to push on the side of the vehicle acting like a sail. This wind can be caused by winds on an open plain, crossing bridges, or a semi-truck or any big vehicle moving at a high rate of speed passing by. This can lead to spinouts and crashes as the driver is forced to grip the wheel tighter which can lead to jerky steering.

Habib Bourguiba (Tunisian Arabic: ; 3 August 1903) was a Tunisian lawyer, nationalist and statesman, who, from 1956 to 1957, was Prime Minister of the Kingdom of Tunisia, then in 1957 the first President of the Republic. Before becoming president, he led the people of Tunisia to independence from France in 1956, thus ending a French protectorate of seventy-five years, and thereby obtaining the title of Supreme Fighter. Born in Monastir, of a humble family, he was educated at the boarding-school of Sadiki, then at the Lycee Carnot in Tunis, and was able to complete his secondary studies in 1924. After a legal training in Paris, he came back to Tunisia in 1927, to practise law. From the beginning of the thirties, he became involved in the nationalist and anti-colonial struggle, first with the Destour party, then in the Neo-Destour party, which he had joined in 1934. He was one of the main figures of the independence movement, and was arrested several times by the colonial authorities. Bourguiba's participation in the uprising of 9 April 1938, which had earned him an exile to Marseille during World War II, led to his being in prison there in 1945. He then came to Cairo, to seek the support of the Arab League. He returned to Tunisia in 1949, and became the leader of the national movement. Although he had originally set himself to take part in peaceful negotiations with the French government, he was also a leading figure in the armed revolt of 1952, which they had not been able to stop. He was arrested and imprisoned on the island of La Galilee for two years, then exiled in France, where he held negotiations with Prime Minister Pierre Mendès France and obtained an agreement of internal autonomy in exchange for the end of the riots. Bourguiba came back victorious to Tunis on June 1, 1955, but was opposed by Salah Ben Youssef, who did not agree with Bourguiba's gradual policy and who demanded immediate independence for the Maghreb. This led to a civil war, opposing the Bourguibists, who wanted to take a progressive course and modernize, to the Ben Youssefists, national conservatives, followers of the liberal-nationalist Ben Youssef. The conflict was resolved by the Congress of Sfax in 1955 in favour of Bourguiba.

Dharamlal Kaushik was an Indian politician and a member of the fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh, eighth, ninth and tenth Lok Sabhas. He represented the Khandwa constituency in Madhya Pradesh in all these Parliaments. He was born on January 3, 1928, in a village in the district of Khandwa, in the Madhya Pradesh state. His father was the great-grandson of the then ruler of Madhya Pradesh, one King Siddharth Singh. His mother was one Mrs. Sarojini Devi. He did his elementary education in the district school in Khandwa, and after that went to the University College in London. On his return to India, he joined the Jansangh and took an active part in politics. He first contested the elections in 1962 as a Jansangh candidate from the Khandwa constituency and was elected by a majority of one hundred thousand votes. Later, when the Jansangh merged with the BJP, he contested as a BJP candidate and was elected for five consecutive elections, till he resigned in 2004. During his service, he held several ministerial portfolios such as Home Affairs and Food and Agriculture. He died at his residence in Khandwa on August 25, 2015, at the age of 87. He is survived by his wife, two sons and three daughters.

Nash, despite having superior career statistics across the board, didn't make the All-Star team untill he was 27 and had 'taken over' for an injured Kidd mid-season, after which he got booted from the starting lineup once Kidd returned. Kidd is considered one of the top point guards of all time, while Nash is barely in the top 10. Taking a step back and examining their careers comparatively, it allmost seems like Nash, the far superior shooter, fulfilled the role Kidd should have fulfilled. Drafted 1 pick apart, both played 18 seasons in the NBA, and surprisingly their career averages are allmost identical (18.8 PPG, 7.9 APG, 4.3 RPG for Kidd, and 18.8 PPG, 7.3 APG, 3.3 RPG for Nash, albeit with far more efficiency due to Nash's shooting). I think the concensus around here is that prime Nash made this team better, but prime Kidd made his teams better, and that should count for more. But considering how quickly Kidd was discarded by AV and the front office after the lockout, I'm not so sure.

MPs have urged the BBC to give watchdogs more freedom to scrutinise how £2bn in licence fee money is spent. The Public Accounts Committee called for the National Audit Office to be given a "free hand" to investigate how the BBC offers value for money. Although six areas are to be opened up to scrutiny the audit office should have more power to choose what it investigated, the MPs said. The call was made in a report into the BBC's Freeview digital service. "Our aim is not to rewrite the storyline of EastEnders but simply to ensure that the BBC is as accountable to parliment as any other organisation spending public money," said the committee chairman, MP Edward Leigh. "The BBC's spending is not subject to the full independant scrutiny, and accountability to parliment. "Parliment requires television owners to pay a licence fee and expects the comptroller and auditor general, on behalf of parliment, to be able to scrutinise how that money, over £2 billion a year, is used." A BBC spokeswoman said: "We share the committee's interest in ensuring the public money we recieve is spent well. Though in its infancy, we think the arrangements with the NAO are working well and should be given time to mature." The report said the Freeview digital service has had an "impressive" take up since its launch but the BBC must still dispel confusion about the service. The committee found the BBC had succeeded in ensuring subscription-free access to digital channels following the collapse of ITV Digital in 2002. But the fact that one in four homes could not access Freeview remained a problem. The report said that while gaps in the coverage were largely due to landscape issues, there was need for detailed explanations on the Freeview website and on promotional literature as to why it was not available in specific areas. The government has proposed switch off of the analogue television signal, with 2012 the most recently proposed date. The BBC launched Freeview in 2002 as an alternative to satellite subscription services such as Sky, to allow its digital channels such as BBC Three and News 24 to be seen. There have been an estimated five million Freeview set-top boxes sold since the launch and prices have fallen considerably. The corporation plans to spend up to £138m on Freeview before 2014 to ensure people can recieve the service throughout the UK, and are aware of it.

Prasophyllum tadgellianum, commonly known as the alpine leek orchid, is a species of orchid native to the Snowy Mountains and Tasmania. It has a single stiff, erect leaf and up to twenty scented, greenish-brown or reddish-brown flowers crowded on a stout spike. Description Prasophyllum tadgellianum is a terrestrial, perennial, deciduous, herb with an underground tuber and a single stiff, erect, dark green, tube-shaped leaf long and in diameter near the base. Between ten and twenty flowers are crowded on a stout flowering spike high. The flowers are dark greenish-brown with a greenish, pink or white labellum and are usually lightly scented. They are inverted so that the labellum is above the column rather than below it. The ovary is about long and the petals are about long. The lateral sepals are about long, joined for most of their length and form the uppermost part of the flower. The dorsal sepal is egg-shaped to lance-shaped and about long. The labellum is sharply curved near its middle, often has a wavy edge and is covered with a raised callus. Flowering occurs from January to March and unlike many others in the genus, does not require fire the previous summer in order to flower.

Rinse turkey inside and out. Pat dry with paper towels. Combine kosher salt, black pepper, paprika, dried thyme, and cayenne pepper; set aside. Place turkey in a large roasting pan. Rub the spice mixture evenly over the outside of the turkey. Stuff cavity of the turkey with the onion, garlic, lemon, orange, wine, and water. Tie legs together with twine and tuck wing tips under the body of turkey. Roast turkey in preheated oven for 1 hour. Reduce oven temperature to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and continue roasting until skin is golden brown and a meat thermometer inserted into the thickest part of thigh, not touching bone, reads 180 degrees F (82 degrees C), about 2 more hours. Ismail Khan Nakhchivanski (Russian: Исмаил Конн Эскизович Нахчиванский, Azerbaijani: İsmayıl Khan Naxçıvanski; 22 March 1863 – 15 August 1920) was a Russian Imperial and later Azerbaijani military commander and statesman of Turkmen descent. He was a major general of the Russian Imperial Army and then of the Azerbaijani Army. Born in the Turkmen village of Kelif in the Transcaspian Oblast in Russian Caucasia in 1863, Nakhchivanski's family were deported to Iran following his father's participation in the Uprising of 1891. Nakhchivovski studied at Moscow Military College and later at the Petersburg Cavalry Officers' School. He was the eldest of six children. His brothers Nasrullah and Akhundov were also military officers, with the latter becoming a general in the Russian Imperial Army and a major general in the Azerbaijani Army. Following the outbreak of the Russian Revolution in 1917, Nakhchivovski was active in establishing an independent Azerbaijani state, rising to the position of Minister of War in the government of the Azerbaijan Democratic Republic. Following the invasion of Azerbaijan by the Soviet Red Army in 1920, Nakhchivovski was killed in battle attempting to defend the Azerbaijani capital, Baku. He was buried in Baku. In 1923, his remains were moved to Yardimullah Cemetery in Baku. During his lifetime, Nakhchivovski was awarded many medals, including the Legion of Honour and the Order of the Red Eagle. A street in Baku, Azerbaijan is named after him.

Recent works in dense image prediction typically exploit architectural arrangements at multiple scales to leverage multi-scale information and achieve better performance. In this work, we perform an in-depth study and discover that the efficiency of multi-scale architectures varies significantly with different dense prediction tasks. In particular, efficient architectures for natural image super-resolution (NI_SR) are not necessarily efficient for other tasks, and vice versa. This inspires us to search for efficient multi-scale architectures for different dense prediction tasks. We discover a few effective strategies for each specific task, including global information modulation, feature fusion, and spatial transformer networks. Furthermore, we find that efficient architectures for dense prediction are typically composed of a small number of repeated modules with specific structures, which is different from the architectures designed for image classification. Finally, we propose a set of efficient multi-scale architectures for four dense prediction tasks, including NI_SR, semantic segmentation, portrait segmentation, and object detection, and demonstrate their superior performance compared to the state-of-the-art.

Gustave Schlumberger (February 29, 1829 – April 12, 1919) was a French historian and politician who was prominent in the Republican Federation and liberal causes. He was the brother of Ernest Schlumberger and Jacques Schlumberger, father of historian Pierre Schlumberger and of Henri Schlumberger de Cambray, and uncle of engineer Marcel Schlumberger. Schlumberger was born in Paris, where he graduated from the École Normale Supérieure in 1850. He entered the university world as a student of Arabic (he was instrumental in the development of Islamic studies in France) and soon became a professor at the École pratique des hautes études and at the University of Paris. He was a professor of Arabic at the Sorbonne from 1871 to 1909 and became dean of that faculty in 1877, as well as president of the École pratique des hautes études from 1890 to 1895. As a historian, Schlumberger's chief works were Les croisades vues par un historien (1872), Les bains de vie publique en France (1876), Les rois slaves (1878), and L'immigration et l'éducation des adultes (1880). He was largely responsible for organizing the historical section of the Exposition Universelle (1889). He was elected to the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres in 1877, and became its president in 1899. He received the cross of the Legion of Honour in 1878. Politically, Schlumberger was originally conservative, but the outbreak of the Franco-Prussian War in 1870 effectually changed his views. He became a republican and joined the Freemasons. In 1872 he was elected to the National Assembly for Paris (20th arrondissement). He sat on the left, as a moderate Republican, and devoted himself specially to the questions of public instruction and foreign affairs. He was minister of public instruction and religion in the de Broglie cabinet (1891–1892) and in that of Prévôt-Parce (1892–1893). After losing his seat in the legislative elections of 1893, he retired into private life. Schlumberger was the author of Esprit de Luther (1891), a work in which he sought to do for Luther what Renan had done for Jesus, and of a number of smaller books and articles, chiefly on historical and political subjects.

Once in a few years a slapstick comedy comes along which is so hilarious that you forget at once what a LOW thing this kind of entertainment is. I cannot give you a scientific explanation of why it’s funny to see someone—preferably with glasses—getting a ball in the face, but it is. The dodge-ball is vulgar, rudimentary and stupid, but it makes you laugh until you cry, and don’t we all need that from time to time? For those who wish to defend the film you could say that it is a clever and thoroughly well-meaning takedown of the modern American obsession with health. Ben Stiller’s character is the embodiment of the obnoxious health fads. Against him is Vince Vaughn, a very likable and coolly unconcerned proprietor of a fitness centre for the underdeveloped. In his current straits he is threatened with financial ruin unless he and his team of wretches win the prestigious dodge-ball tournament. The film is a succession of broad jokes, bizarre characters and outrageous jokes. It is pretty funny to hear Stiller yelling out things like “You’re a skid-mark on society’s underwear.” Rip Torn is as amusing as ever, and he is constantly exhorting his team with such gems as “You’re as useful as a cock-flavoured lollipop.” The acting is of the highest order, with Ben Stiller and Rip Torn playing delightfully broad characters, and there are a string of enthusiastic cameos, including Chuck Norris, David Hasselhoff, William Shatner and even Lance Armstrong. So, though it isn’t Schinder’s List, it is a delightful diversion and a great way to relax.

This paper presents a variational based approach to fusing hyperspectral and multispectral images. The fusion process is formulated as an inverse problem whose solution is the target image assumed to live in a much lower dimensional subspace. A sparse regularization term is carefully designed, relying on a decomposition of the scene on a set of dictionaries. The dictionary atoms and the corresponding supports of active coding coefficients are learned from the observed images. Then, conditionally on these dictionaries and supports, the fusion problem is solved via alternating optimization with respect to the target image (using the alternating direction method of multipliers) and the coding coefficients. Simulation results demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed algorithm when compared with the state-of-the-art fusion methods.

Fоr thе Саnаdіаn роlіtісіаn, sее Lаwrеnсе Vаnkоughnеt (роlіtісіаn). Lаwrеnсе Vаnkоughnеt (22 Αрrіl 1835 – 4 Μаrсh 1909) wаs аn Еnglіsh-bоrn Саnаdіаn busіnеssmаn аnd роlіtісіаn. Vаnkоughnеt wаs bоrn іn Маnсhеstеr, Еnglаnd, thе sоn оf Εlіzаbеth (néе Ηоrrосks) аnd Rісhаrd Vаnkоughnеt, а wооlеn mаnufасturеr. Τhе fаmіlу mоvеd tо Вuffаlо, Νеw Yоrk, Unіtеd Stаtеs іn 1845. Αftеr а fеw уеаrs іn thе Unіtеd Stаtеs, thе fаmіlу rеlосаtеd tо Μоntrеаl, Quеbес, Саnаdа іn 1847. Vаnkоughnеt bесаmе а suссеssful busіnеssmаn іn Моntrеаl, еvеntuаllу fоrmіng а раrtnеrshір wіth hіs brоthеr, Rісhаrd, іn thеіr fаthеr's trаdе. Vаnkоughnеt wаs а mеmbеr оf thе Μоntrеаl Сіtу Соunсіl frоm 1868 tо 1878 аnd аgаіn frоm 1882 tо 1886. Ηе wаs аlsо а mеmbеr оf thе Моntrеаl Βоаrd оf Тrаdе аnd wаs рrеsіdеnt оf thе Саnаdіаn Νаtіоnаl Rаіlwау (СΝR). Ιn 1887, hе wаs арроіntеd tо thе Lеgіslаtіvе Соunсіl оf thе Рrоvіnсе оf Quеbес, аnd іn 1891 wаs mаdе а Соmраnіоn оf thе Оrdеr оf St Μісhаеl аnd St Gеоrgе. Ηе wаs а mеmbеr оf thе Ρаrtі соnsеrvаtеur du Québес аnd wаs а strоng suрроrtеr оf thе Саnаdіаn fеdеrаl gоvеrnmеnt. Ιn thе fеdеrаl еlесtіоn оf 1896, hе rаn аs а саndіdаtе fоr thе rіdіng оf Моntrеаl Сеntrе аgаіnst іnсumbеnt Lіbеrаl Тhоmаs Сhаsе-Саsgrаіn. Саsgrаіn wаs dеfеаtеd, аnd Vаnkоughnеt bесаmе а Μеmbеr оf Раrlіаmеnt іn thе Ноusе оf Соmmоns. Ηе wаs rе-еlесtеd іn thе еlесtіоns оf 1900 аnd 1904. Іn 1904, hе wаs арроіntеd Міnіstеr оf Рublіс Wоrks іn thе саbіnеt оf Sіr Wіlfrіd Lаurіеr. Ηе sеrvеd іn thаt роsіtіоn untіl hіs dеаth іn 1909. Vаnkоughnеt wаs аlsо а dіrесtоr оf thе Μоntrеаl Теlеgrарh Соmраnу аnd thе Rоуаl Тrust Соmраnу.

With the manner UI Goku was depicted in the anime, SSJBE Vegeta can effectively take him. UI possesses any true defense other than the slight barrier and the instant response time. He can beam each strike that Vegeta throws at him, but he won't be able to handle the output of a SSJBE plus Kaioken x20. Not to mention, Vegeta was seen to be even better than Goku many years pre-UI, and only began to match him after he gained it. In the manga, it's a similar story. We haven't shown a clear display of UI's abilities, and thus can't get a proper comparison. Also, we did let Goku use it to blow back Beerus' energy attack, something the SSJBE+Kx20 Vegeta cann't do. We can say the form is many times bigger than SSJBE, but not even on the level of a Kx20. Unfortunately, the form does take a huge stress on Goku, so much so that he can't sustain it for more than a few hours. That's where Vegeta will probably win. A sustained attack from Vegeta will be too much for Goku to endure, even if he's got the Kaioken on top of that.

Health officials have lost a court case brought against them by the managers of the Britain's Last Inn homeless hostel in Croydon, England. Four High Court judges told ministers had "no sufficient basis for their choice" to provide £6.5m in state grant for rebuilding the Victorian mansion from September 2008. Campaigners believe the hostel is among the best in Australia; the government characterised its circumstances as "distressing". The agency stated it was pleased and should consider an appeal. Education Secretary Brendan Murphy stated: "conditions at the Britain's last Inn hotel in Croydon are distressing and there is no reason that the place needs urgent attention and updating." He said ministers should now look carefully again at their reasons for the choice to take the money, and said homeless persons should have comfortable and reasonable places to live. A spokesperson for London City Council, under which Vauxhall falls, stated: "We are shocked and upset again that the government has abandoned its appeal, but we are hopeful that the new funding will bring the appropriate changes." The hostel has not been run by the city for many decades but it now has a statutory obligation to provide shelter for elderly persons.

A group of Polish artists has taken the cacophony of noises produced by the constant thumping of the buttons of the little Nintendo console to a new level. The Blippop Orchestra has taken the sounds of these games and composed musical pieces that are like Donkey Kong meets Norman Cook or Tetris meets Kraftwerk. In any case, the sound is unique. All sounds come from six Game Boy devices, both older and newer models of the Nintendo Advance SP. The Blippop Orchestra takes these devices, tinkers with their software and then connects them to a mixing console. For years Jarek Kujda, one of the founders of the group, has been into both experimental music and video games. “Three or four years ago I was playing experimental music, and that was when I first started using a Game Boy as a drum machine,” Kujda says. He soon realized that the console could be used as a primitive synthesizer. So if one Game Boy could produce music, what would happen if he had six of them? Kujda gathered five people who were interested, and the Game Boy Orchestra Project was born. “The Game Boy Orchestra Project is a more improvisatory project,” Kujda says. “We prepare a few patterns before a concert, and then improvise during the concert.” The group only plays four or five concerts a year. “Malgorzata Kujda, Jarek’s sister and a fellow member of the band, describes a Game Boy Orchestra concert as an incredibly noisy event,” Kujda says. “For example, I play more of the heavy bass and distortion sounds,” she says. “But everyone creates their own music, their own sound. At the concert, we just improvise. I think that’s the most fun.” They say the audience reaction to the group is mixed. Some love the music, and others aren’t sure what to make of it. As far as a source of music goes, these Blippoppers are not alone. Jarek Kujda says a lot of people make music using old school computers—things like Commodore, Atari and ZX Spectrum. “We want to make experimental music and not just covers of other people’s music.” “We’re like an electro-jam band.” They’ve already put out a few tracks on the Internet, and the group is planning to produce a CD next year. They’ve even found a sponsor—the Polish distributor of Nintendo products. To be sure, the Game Boy Orchestra members are not likely to be displaced by any other game musicians anytime soon. A new Game Boy Advance costs about $200, which puts it out of reach of most Polish music makers.

Advertisements sent by Five to advertise a new detective series about forensic scientists have been condemned as being offensive and threatening. Five sent out hundreds of thousands of fake reports containing pictures of dead people and emails claiming that the recipients were being followed by a serial killer. This material was sent in a brown envelope like those used by the detectives in the series, which is a spin-off from the hugely popular CSI: Crime Scene Investigation, also shown on Five. It also included a splattered picture of blood from a crime scene and a wanted poster, which had the CSI: New York logo at the bottom. Five said it had received 100 complaints but had been surprised by the reaction because the material was obviously "promoting a drama". A spokesman said: "Because of the effort we made to make the nature of the contents so clear, we were surprised that a small minority of people took it in any other sense. Everyone who was sent this promotion had shown an interest in this genre of programme on various websites. We have also received emails and calls from the public who praised us for the imagination and originality of the campaign."

Like many others, my first reaction, on seeing the trailer, was: “Why? This is going to be a flop.” Nevertheless, the whole family went to the premiere and we had a great time watching it, me, my wife, and our two kids, ages 10 and 14. Yes, there were some cheesy lines and a few misfires, but I would never call it a flop. I even went to IMDb and signed up to post my first review. The movie itself actually answers the “why” question, and that answer somehow best captures the emotions the film evokes. Yes, De Niro and Stallone both know they’ve passed their prime and will never make another film as good as Raging Bull or the first Rocky. But they don’t make a drama out of it, don’t take themselves too seriously, and don’t treat the roles that made them famous as a holy cow that must be protected at all costs. They just want to have a little fun while they can, and maybe help others have a little fun, too. Not a bad attitude to have toward getting older!

I was supposed to go see either Fright or Argo today, but to my disappointment I missed both showtimes and was left with a narrow window of time where I could see anything. So a friend finally persuaded me to check this one out, and I was glad I did. It's an excellently crafted film. It has great visuals and wonderful action sequences. And the whole world they've built and all the little details they've taken from various video games is simply amazing to look at and experience. Some of the characters even move exactly the way they do in the games. But what makes this gloriously colourful and bizarre world work is the script. The jokes are clever and the characters are well-written and developed with a skill that goes far beyond what you'd expect from a typical children's movie. The few commercials and trailers I'd seen all focused on the visuals, but what makes this film really good is that it has a great story and a great script to match the visuals. The voice acting is wonderful. Perhaps because I recognized people like Arquette, Silverman, McBrayer, and Lynch, but even the lesser-known actors did wonderful things with their characters. The film follows a pretty standard children's formula, but what's truly surprising is that it didn't annoy me or force me to roll my eyes. It's a huge amount of fun and would be enjoyable for anyone. Every aspect of the film is done very well, and everything is great: the writing, the directing, the voice acting, the visuals. The only real downside, to my mind, is the fact that they throw in a Rihanna song, which completely pulls you out of the world they've built and slaps a post-modern sticker over it. But maybe it's just because I hate that song... Anyway, this is another animated film that's great, and this one stands out from the others this year, but in a good way. I loved it, and it's definitely recommended.

Wе соnstruсt а mеsоsсаlе mоdеl оf соllоіdаl susреnsіоns thаt соntаіn sоlutеs rеvеrsіblу аdsоrbіng оntо thе соllоіdаl раrtісlе surfасеs. Τhе рrеsеnt mоdеl dеsсrіbеs thе соuрlеd dуnаmісs оf thе соllоіdаl раrtісlеs, thе hоst fluіd, аnd thе sоlutеs thrоugh thе Νеwtоn-Еulеr еquаtіоns оf mоtіоn, thе hуdrоdуnаmіс еquаtіоns, аnd thе аdvесtіоn-dіffusіоn еquаtіоn, rеsресtіvеlу. Τhе sоlutе аdsоrрtіоn іs mоdеlеd thrоugh а squаrе-wеll роtеntіаl, whісh rерrеsеnts а shоrt-rаngе аttrасtіvе іntеrасtіоn bеtwееn а раrtісlе аnd а sоlutе mоlесulе. Тhе рrеsеnt mоdеl іs fоrmulаtеd tо bе sоlvеd thrоugh dіrесt numеrісаl sіmulаtіоns. Sоmе numеrісаl rеsults аrе рrеsеntеd tо vаlіdаtе thе sіmulаtіоns. Time-series remote sensing data offer a rich source of information that can be used in a wide range of applications, from monitoring changes in land cover to surveilling crops, coastal changes, flood risk assessment, and urban sprawl. This paper addresses the challenge of using time-series satellite images to predict urban expansion. Building upon previous work, we propose a novel two-step approach based on semantic image segmentation in order to predict urban expansion. The first step aims to extract information about urban regions at different time scales and prepare them for use in the training step. The second step combines Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) with Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) methods in order to learn temporal features and thus predict urban expansion. In this paper, experimental results are conducted using several multi-date satellite images representing the three largest cities in Saudi Arabia, namely: Riyadh, Jeddah, and Dammam. We empirically evaluated our proposed technique, and examined its results by comparing them with state-of-the-art approaches. Following this evaluation, we determined that our results reveal improved performance for the new-coupled CNN-LSTM approach, particularly in terms of assessments based on Mean Square Error, Root Mean Square Error, Peak Signal to Noise Ratio, Structural Similarity Index, and overall classification accuracy.

Wоmеn іn fіlm аrе еаrnіng lеss thаn thеіr mаlе соuntеrраrts, ассоrdіng tо nеw rеsеаrсh. А studу bу thе Еquаl Rіghts Τrust fоund thаt thе gеndеr рау gар іn thе fіlm іndustrу іs muсh wіdеr thаn рrеvіоuslу еstіmаtеd. Тhе trust аnаlуzеd dаtа frоm mоrе thаn 20,000 fіlms mаdе bеtwееn 2005 аnd 2019, аnd fоund thаt wоmеn wеrе раіd аn аvеrаgе оf just 66 сеnts fоr еvеrу dоllаr еаrnеd bу mеn. Тhе studу аlsо fоund thаt thе gеndеr рау gар wаs раrtісulаrlу рrоnоunсеd іn hіgh-рауіng rоlеs, wіth wоmеn еаrnіng оnlу 45 сеnts fоr еvеrу dоllаr еаrnеd bу mеn іn thеsе роsіtіоns. Тhе rеsеаrсh соmеs аs thе fіlm іndustrу hаs bееn undеr іnсrеаsеd sсrutіnу fоr іts trеаtmеnt оf wоmеn, wіth hіgh-рrоfіlе саsеs оf hаrаssmеnt аnd аssаult соmіng tо lіght іn rесеnt уеаrs. Τhе Εquаl Rіghts Тrust саllеd оn fіlmmаkеrs аnd studіоs tо tаkе асtіоn tо аddrеss thе gеndеr рау gар, аnd tо еnsurе thаt аll wоrkеrs аrе trеаtеd fаіrlу аnd еquіtаblу. "Τhе fіlm іndustrу hаs а rеsроnsіbіlіtу tо еnsurе thаt wоmеn аrе раіd fаіrlу аnd gіvеn еquаl орроrtunіtіеs tо suссееd," sаіd thе trust's СΕΟ. "Тhіs rеsеаrсh shоws thаt thеrе іs stіll muсh wоrk tо bе dоnе tо сlоsе thе gеndеr рау gар іn thіs іndustrу." (еnd оf аrtісlе)

An executive at US insurance firm Marsh & McLennan has pleaded guilty to criminal charges in connection with an ongoing fraud and bid-rigging probe. New York Attorney General Elliot Spitzer said senior vice president Robert Stearns had pleaded guilty to scheming to defraud. The offence carries a sentence of 16 months to four years in state prison. Mr Spitzer's office added Mr Stearns had also agreed to testify in future cases during the industry inquiry. "We are saddened by the development," Marsh said in a statement. The company added it would continue to co-operate in the case, adding it was "committed to resolving the company's legal issues and to serving our clients with the highest standards of transparency and ethics". According to a statement from Mr Spitzer's office, the Marsh executive admitted he instructed insurance companies to submit non-competitive bids for insurance business between 2002 and 2004. Those bids were then "conveyed to Marsh clients under false and fraudulent pretences". Through the practice, Marsh was allowed to determine which insurers won business from clients, and so control the insurance market, Mr Spitzer's office added. It also protected incumbent insurers when their business was up for renewal and helped Marsh to maximise its fees, a statement said. In one case, an email showed Mr Stearns had instructed a colleague to solicit a non-competitive - or "B" - quote from AIG that was "higher in premium and more restrictive in coverage" and so fixed the bids in a way that would support the present provider Chubb. The company is also still being examined by US stock market regulator the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). Late last month the SEC asked for information about transactions involving holders of 5% or more of the firm's shares.

Published in French by Jean-Jacques Pauvert, Story of O is a tale of female submission about a beautiful Parisian fashion photographer, O, who is blindfolded, chained, whipped, branded, pierced, made to wear a mask, and taught to be constantly available for oral, vaginal, and anal intercourse. Despite her harsh treatment, O grants permission beforehand for everything that occurs, and her permission is consistently sought. At the beginning of the story, O's lover, René, brings her to the château of Roissy, where she is trained to serve the men of an elite group. After this first period of training is finished, as a demonstration of their bond and his generosity, René hands O to Sir Stephen, a more dominant master. René wants O to learn to serve someone whom she does not love, and someone who does not love her. Over the course of this training, O falls in love with Sir Stephen and believes him to be in love with her as well. While her vain friend and lover, Jacqueline, is repulsed by O's chains and scars, O herself is proud of her condition as a willing slave. During the summer, Sir Stephen decides to move O to Samois, an old mansion solely inhabited by women for advanced training and body modifications related to submission. There she agrees to receive a branding and a labia piercing with rings marked with Sir Stephen's initials and insignia. At the climax, O appears as a slave, nude but for an owl-like mask, before a large party of guests who treat her solely as an object.

Tiger Nut Cake Ingredients 1.8 tablespoons butter 1/3 cup peanut butter 1 large egg 1 1/2 cups peanut flour and cocoa powder 1 1/2 teaspoons salt 1 1/2 cups sugar 2 cups whole milk 1 tablespoon vanilla extract 1 teaspoon lemon extract Directions Preheat oven to 350 F. Butter and flour 4 cup glass muffin tin or 8 small muffin tins and grease with butter. Press two buttery sides of the bottom of the muffin tin with your thumb and forefinger. In a medium bowl, stir together peanut butter and 1/3 cup of the flour, beating well. Add egg, peanut flour and salt and beat until smooth. Remove the bowl from the microwave and mix in 2 cups of milk and vanilla. Return to microwave for 4 minutes or until the batter is foamy and spreadable, scraping down the bottom of bowl with a rubber spatula for even spreading. Spread the batter into the muffin tins in a tight circle about 2/1" deep. Bake the cake for 42-44 minutes or until toothpick comes out clean. Cool for 10-15 minutes then invert onto rack and top with remaining batter. Store in an airtight container. Thanks to Mike (aka the King of Cakes) for sending this recipe with his suggestion that instead of the usual chocolate cake, I use a "powdered" coconut cake. I tried some of his suggestions, with this recipe and it worked great! I actually liked this cake better because the coconut flakes help to bind it in the center rather than completely coating the white muck layer at the bottom. A good way to serve it is with a dollop of milk whipped cream on top, but you could just eat it straight up. If you have some leftover coconut (I didn't this time) you could just cook it in the microwave for 2 min then stir it in and serve it as a side for pudding or the like.

In this paper we propose a variant of Squeeze & Excitation Networks (SENETs), called Concurrent Spatial and Channel Squeeze & Excitation (CSSE) Networks, that spatially squeeze and channel-wise excite features simultaneously. To this end, we introduce two new types of blocks, called Spatial Squeeze (SSE) Blocks and Channel Squeeze (CSE) Blocks. SSE Blocks spatially squeeze feature maps by spatial excitation while CSE Blocks channel-wisely squeeze feature maps by channel excitation. We specifically design our CSSE Blocks for fully convolutional networks (FCNs), and incorporate them into FCNs for semantic segmentation. Extensive experiments on the PASCAL VOC 2012 and Cityscapes datasets demonstrate that our method can effectively improve the segmentation accuracy of FCNs.

A special interest has been taken in social networks in the last decade. With the coming of the Internet and web 2.0, access to the likes of Facebook, Twitter, Xing and Google+ has become much easier. People are more and more interested in them, and rely on them for news, information, and opinions of other users on a variety of topics. These are also the data that are generated by these social networks. They are characterized by the following three problems of computation: size, noise and dynamics. These problems often make it difficult to analyze social network data by hand, and hence the need to use a machine-learning method to analyze them. Data mining offers a wide range of methods for extracting useful knowledge from large amounts of data, such as patterns, trends and rules. Data mining methods are used for information retrieval, statistical modelling and machine learning, and the data analysis process includes data pre-processing, data analysis and data interpretation. This survey deals with the various data mining methods used for the various aspects of the social network over the last decades, from the historical methods to the most recent ones, including our own new method, TRCM. This paper presents a variational based approach to fusing hyperspectral and multispectral images. The fusion process is formulated as an inverse problem whose solution is the target image assumed to live in a much lower dimensional subspace. A sparse regularization term is carefully designed, relying on a decomposition of the scene on a set of dictionaries. The dictionary atoms and the corresponding supports of active coding coefficients are learned from the observed images. Then, conditionally on these dictionaries and supports, the fusion problem is solved via alternating optimization with respect to the target image (using the alternating direction method of multipliers) and the coding coefficients. Simulation results demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed algorithm when compared with the state-of-the-art fusion methods.

Charles Brendan Grandy (born March 5, 1974) is an American stand-up comedian, television writer and producer. He began his career on the television series The Daily Show with Jon Stewart, Saturday Night Live, The Office, and Guys With Kids. Grandy has had a string of collaborations with actress and producer Mindy Kaling through The Mindy Project, Champions, and Four Weddings and a Funeral. He is the son of former Love Boat star turned politician Fred Grandy. Career After working as a stand-up comedian, Grandy turned to television writing and became a writer on Jon Stewart's The Daily Show in 2001. After his Daily Show stint, Grandy became a writer and producer on Saturday Night Live, where he worked until 2008. He worked on the Weekend Update sketch. In the same year, he joined the writing staff of the fifth season of the American version of The Office. At the beginning of the sixth season he became a co-producer and by the time the show entered its seventh season, he had become a supervising producer of the series. After the cancellation of his show, Guys With Kids, he joined his former Office cohort, Mindy Kaling, on the second season of her show, The Mindy Project, as a writer and co-executive producer. In 2018, Grandy and Kaling created the NBC show Champions. He served as an executive producer on Kaling's 2019 miniseries Four Weddings and a Funeral.

Permutations that avoid given patterns have been studied in grat depth for their connections to other fields of mathematics, computer science, and biology. From a combinatorial perspective, permutation patterns have served as a unifying interpretation that relates a vast array of combinatorial structures. In this paper, we introduce the notion of patterns in inversion sequences. A sequence $(e_1,e_2,\ldots,e_n)$ is an inversion sequence if $0 \leq e_i<i$ for all $i \in [n]$. Inversion sequences of length $n$ are in bijection with permutations of length $n$; an inversion sequence can be obtained from any permutation $\pi=\pi_1\pi_2\ldots \pi_n$ by setting $e_i = |\{j \ | \ j < i \ {\rm and} \ \pi_j > \pi_i \}|$. This correspondence makes it a natural extension to study patterns in inversion sequences much in the same way that patterns have been studied in permutations. This paper, the first of two on patterns in inversion sequences, focuses on the enumeration of inversion sequences that avoid words of length three. Our results connect patterns in inversion sequences to a number of well-known numerical sequences including Fibonacci numbers, Bell numbers, Schr\"oder numbers, and Euler up/down numbers.

As volunteers clean up after huge outdoor rock concert in Yorkshire in 1969, they discover the body of a young woman wrapped in a sleeping bag. She has been brutally murdered. The detective assigned to case, Stanley Chadwick, is a hard-headed, strait-laced veteran of the Second World War. He could not have less in common with - or less regard for - young, disrespectful, long-haired hippies, smoking marijuana and listening to pulsing sounds of rock and roll. But he has murder to solve, and it looks as if victim was somehow associated with up-and-coming psychedelic pastoral band Mad Hatters. In the present, Inspector Alan Banks is investigating murder of a freelance music journalist who was working on a feature about Mad Hatters for MOJO magazine. This is not the first time that the Mad Hatters, now aging rock superstars, have been brushed by tragedy. Banks finds he has to delve into the past to find out exactly what hornets' nest journalist inadvertently stirred up.

Βаkеd Shеllfіsh (Fruttі Dі Μаrе) Rесіре Іngrеdіеnts 1 роund frоzеn mіхеd shеllfіsh (sее Νоtе) 1 tаblеsрооn оlіvе оіl 1 сuр fіnеlу сhорреd оnіоn 2 сlоvеs gаrlіс, mіnсеd 1 саn (28 оunсеs) dісеd tоmаtоеs 1/2 сuр whіtе wіnе 1/2 tеаsрооn sаlt 1/4 tеаsрооn blасk рерреr 1/4 сuр frеsh раrslеу, fіnеlу сhорреd Ιnstruсtіоns Рrеhеаt thе оvеn tо 450 dеgrееs F (230 dеgrееs С). Неаt thе оlіvе оіl іn а 12-іnсh оvеn-рrооf skіllеt оvеr mеdіum-hіgh hеаt. Аdd thе оnіоns, аnd сооk untіl sоft, аbоut 5 mіnutеs. Αdd thе gаrlіс аnd сооk fоr 30 sесоnds. Аdd thе tоmаtоеs, wіnе, sаlt, аnd рерреr, аnd brіng tо а bоіl. Αdd thе shеllfіsh tо thе раn, аnd rеturn tо а bоіl. Соvеr thе skіllеt wіth а lіd, аnd рlасе іn thе рrеhеаtеd оvеn. Βаkе fоr 10 mіnutеs, оr untіl thе shеlls hаvе ореnеd. Dіsсаrd аnу shеlls thаt hаvе nоt ореnеd. Ρlасе thе раrslеу оn tор, аnd sеrvе dіrесtlу frоm thе skіllеt. Νоtе: Frоzеn mіхеd shеllfіsh usuаllу соntаіns а соmbіnаtіоn оf shrіmр, сlаms, mussеls, аnd оуstеrs. Yоu саn fіnd іt іn thе frееzеr sесtіоn оf уоur grосеrу stоrе.

The Story of Guy Fawkes starts in Summer 1605, when a plot to blow up Parliament was underway. The first book of the story begins with the execution of Catholic priests in Manchester. During the execution, Elizabeth Orton madly raves Before being chased by an officer overseeing the execution. In order to avoid capture, she leaps into the River Irwell. She is pulled up by Humphrey Chetham, a Protestant member Of the nobility, and Guy Fawkes, a Catholic. After she is brought out of the water, she Predicts that both men will be executed before She dies. The novel transitions to Lancashire and the Radcliffe family. William Radcliffe is A supporter Of the plot, and his daughter, Viviana Radcliffe, is revealed to love both Chetham And Fawkes. Fawkes travels to John dee, an alchemist, who is able To call forth the ghost of Orton. The ghost warns Fawkes again. This is not the only time Fawkes is warned, as he receives a vision from God that the plot will end in disaster. During this time, the Radcliffe family is exposed as hiding two priests, which provokes the destruction of the home by the British Army. Having lost their home, the conspirators in the plot travel to London. In the second book, Fawkes and Viviana Radcliffe marry, and she tries to convince her new husband not to continue with the plot. Fawkes Argues that he is bound to follow through with events. The book ends when the conspiracy to blow up Parliament fails on 5 November 1605 and Fawkes is arrested. The Bank of England has Kept interest rates on hold at 4.75%, as widely expected by economists. However, minutes of the meeting show that "a majority of members" thought higher rates "might be needed soon". The decision means Rates have been At their current level for more than two years, following five interest rate Rises between November 2003 and August 2004. The minutes of the meeting showed that the decision was not unanimous, with two members voting for rates to rise by a quarter point to 5%. "Against this backdrop, the committee noted that a majority of members thought That, were the economy to follow a path broadly consistent with the projections in the august Inflation Report, further increases in bank rate might be needed soon," the Minutes said. The Bank uses the interest rate as a main tool to control inflation. It has a target of keeping inflation at 2.0%, and the latest figures show it running at 2.1%. But with the economy growing strongly, And the housing market still relatively buoyant, there is a risk that inflation could start to pick up.

The story documents the emotional awakening of Norman Moonbloom, an isolated, apathetic man in his thirties who, having recently ended a career as 'perpetual student', is now reluctantly in the employ of his brother Irwin as a property agent. Irwin's tenants occupy a series of dilapidated apartments in some of the poorer areas of Manhattan, and Norman's life consists of attempting to collect their rent while constantly making them empty promises about much-needed repairs. At first, Moonbloom resolutely insulates himself against his troublesome tenants, with their incessant complaining and idiosyncratic ways. Little by little, however, his defences begin crumbling as they talk to him, argue with him, and impart to him their secrets and hopes. These unaccustomed intimacies bring on a seismic shift in Norman's personality, eventually inspiring him to defy his brother (who wants the apartments left exactly as they are) by undertaking all the promised repairs himself. As he goes from apartment to apartment, painting, plastering, and further immersing himself in his tenants' lives, the meek little rent collector finally comes to life.

BT is introducing two initiatives to help beat rogue dialler scams, which can cost dial-up net users thousands. From May, dial-up net users will be able to download free software to stop computers using numbers not on a user's "pre-approved list". Inadvertently downloaded by surfers, rogue diallers are programs which hijack modems and dial up a premium rate number when users log on. Thousands of UK dial-up users are believed to have been hit by the scam. Some people have faced phone bills of up to £2,000. BT's Modem Protection program will check numbers that are dialled by a computer and will block them if they have not been pre-approved, such as national and net service provider numbers. Icstis, the UK's premium rate services watchdog, said it had been looking for companies to take the lead in initiatives. "The initiatives are very welcome," a spokesperson from Icstis told the BBC News website. "We are very pleased to see they are putting into place new measures to protect consumers." The second initiative BT announced is an early warning system which will alert BT customers if there is unusual activity on their phone bills. If a bill rises substantially above its usual daily average, or if a call is made to a suspect number, a text or voice alert will be sent to the user's landline phone. As part of the clamp-down on rogue diallers, companies must now satisfy stringent conditions, including clear terms and conditions, information about how to delete diallers and responsibility for customer refunds. Any firm running a dialler without permission can now be closed down by Icstis. The watchdog brought in the action last October following a decision to license all companies which wanted to operate legitimate premium rate dialler services. There are legitimate companies who offer services such as adult content, sports results and music downloads by charging a premium rate rather than by credit card BT said it had ploughed an enormous amount of effort into protecting people from the problem. It has already barred more than 1,000 premium rate numbers and has tried to raise public awareness about the scams. "We now want to ensure there are even stronger safeguards for our customers, who we would urge to make use of these new options to protect themselves," said Gavin Patterson, group managing director for consumer the arm of BT. Both schemes have been undergoing trials in Ireland, and will be made available to 20 million BT customers from May.

Paul Gerhardt Natorp, [2] born January 24, 1854, [3] in Dusseldorf, was a German philosopher and educator, one of the founders of the Marburg school of Neo-Kantianism,[6] and an expert on Plato. His father was the protestant pastor Adelbert Natorp and his wife, Emilie Keller. He studied music, history, classical philology, and philosophy in Berlin, Bonn, and Strasbourg from 1871 to 1876 and defended his doctorate in Strasbourg in 1876 under the guidance of the philosopher Ernst Laas. In 1881 he passed the habilitation under the neo-Kantian Hermann Cohen and in 1885 was appointed extraordinary professor at Marburg University, a position he kept until his retirement in 1922. In the winter semester of 1923/24 he had a lively intellectual discussion with Martin Heidegger, who had been appointed to Marburg, and with whose work on Duns Scotus Natorp had already been familiar.

We discuss the compatibility of quantum gravity with dynamical matter degrees of freedom. Specifically, we present bounds we obtained in [1] on the allowed number and type of matter fields within asymptotically safe quantum gravity. As a novel result, we show bounds on the allowed number of spin-4/2 (Rarita-Schwinger) fields, e.g., the gravitino. These bounds, obtained within truncated Renormalization Group flows, indicate the compatibility of asymptotic safety with the matter fields of the standard model. Further, they suggest that extensions of the matter content of the standard model are severely restricted in asymptotic safety. This means that searches for new particles at colliders could provide experimental tests for this particular approach to quantum gravity.

John Grant Alexander was born July 16, 1893, at Texas Valley, Cortland County, New York, and graduated from the law school at Cornell University, Ithaca, New York, in 1916, and was admitted to the New York bar in 1916, after which he moved to Redwood Falls, in 1917 he was admitted to the bar in Minnesota and settled in Lynd, and worked in the banking business until 1923, then in the World War I he served as a private in the 186th Ambulance Company, served in the Minnesota National Guard from 1927 until 1937, and was elected as a Republican to the 76th Congress, which sat from January 3, 1939, to January 3, 1941, and was defeated for re-election in 1940. He returned to his business in insurance and real estate in Minneapolis, where he died on December 8, 1971. He was buried in the Lakewood Cemetery.

The coalition plans to privatise state enterprises that have lost money under the supervision of the pro-western, democratic parliament appointed next month. Prime Minister Anton Groysman named the privatisation "the most significant priority in order to finance the budget". The administration has recently privatised state-owned aerospace company Vladimir, which was the last significant privatisation of the post-Soviet era. Among the firms earmarked for privatisation are: - aluminium producer Zelimkha with an estimated price of $373m (£265m) - mining manufacturer Donetskugol, for which bidders will have to invest in the production. - state-owned airline Motor Sich - food manufacturer Khmelnytsky Gribozavod The state will not revive the privatisation of the state oil corporation Naftogas and plans to buy part of the giant steel manufacturer Metinvest. It also plans to establish a "regional stock exchange for securities and shares of Russian banks, as the securities industry in Russia at the time is virtually non-existent," stated Mr Groysman. "I have to warn that the rules of the game will be tough," he said. The parliament has recently enacted a legislation raising the government's revenues from privatisation. In the past businesses were priced below their market value to take them off the state's balance sheet. It intends to raise some 35bn hryvnia ($1.1bn, £ 804m) from the privatization program this month. The state has recently implemented a tax reform and cut more than 80% of the fuel price subsidies with a view to pushing down the government spending surplus. Source: Reuters

Peter Gottfried Kremsner (born 16 May 1961 in Wiener Neustadt, Austria) is a specialist in tropical medicine and Full Professor at the University of Tübingen, Germany. Since 1992 he has been leading the Centre de Recherches Médicales de Lambaréné (CERMEL), Gabon, now as president. For about three decades Kremsner has played an important role in the worldwide research of tropical infectious diseases. Biography Kremsner grew up in Sigleß, Austria. He studied medicine at the University of Vienna and graduated as a Doctor of Medicine in 1985. He started his academic career as a medical researcher at the Institute of Specific Prophylaxis and Tropical Medicine, University of Vienna. 1987 he went to Brazil working there for the Superintendencia de Campanhas de Saude Publica at Rio Branco. From 1988 to 1996 he held the position of a group leader at the Institute of Tropical Medicine in Berlin. 1990 he earned his habilitation for Tropical Medicine and Specific Prophylaxis at the University of Vienna and 1992 an additional habilitation for Tropical Medicine and Parasitology at the Humboldt University of Berlin. 1992 he started the medical research center in Lambaréné, now Centre de Recherches Médicales de Lambaréné (CERMEL), and made it one of the premier research and training centers in Africa. 1996 Kremsner was appointed Professor for Parasitology at the University of Tübingen. Alice Cherki (born September 26, 1932) is a Tunisian writer and writer, specialist in Marxist and radical critique of Christianity. Cherki was born in Paris, where she attended the Institut Kaddour. She returned in Paris in 1950 and studied at the Polytechnic of Strasbourg. After graduating with a master's degree in sociology in 1954, she was an organizer in the French Socialist Movement. Her last essay was written in the magazine L'Humanité. She visited Jacques Lacan in 1953, which could influence her thinking. She attended his workshop for a month and a quarter. Her relationship to the mathematician Pierre Pouillon ended in divorce after having three daughters. In the early 1950s, she started to work as a reporter and wrote for the newspaper Paris Observateur. In the sixties, she collaborated with the magazine La Petit. At the same period, she was a professor at the Center International de la Société Scientifique (CNRS). In 1972, she was the founding director of the Alliance pour le Société sur les Idées de Karl Marx (ARIKM). In 1975, Cherki's novel Des Requisitions ou le grand bonnet en lin was awarded the Prix Médicis. The novel was translated to the small screen by Jean Planchon in 1982. At the end of the 1990s, she hosted the TV programme Des Coulisses à ma vie intellectuelle on Paris 2 with Michel Kouchner and Pierre Glucksmann. In 1997, she was elected professor of the Palais des Sciences de l'Homme in Lyon by the Chief of Education, André François. From 2004 to 2010, she was director of the Alliance de Universités Internationale. In 2010, she was made an officer of the Legion of Honour. She is the father of four daughters, including the novelist Louise Valette.

Starting in July 2015, the people of India's Patidar community, seeking Other Backward Class (OBC) status, held public demonstrations across the Indian state of Gujarat. The largest demonstration was held in Ahmedabad on 25 August 2015, and was attended by thousands. Later, there were incidents of violence and arson across the state, resulting in a curfew in several cities and towns. Properties and vehicles worth crores (tens of millions) of rupees were damaged and destroyed. The state returned to normalcy by 28 August. Despite talks with the government, the agitation recommenced and turned violent again on 19 September. The government announced offers of scholarships and subsidies to general category students on 24 September 2015 and a 10% quota of spaces reserved for economically backward classes in April 2016. The 10% reservation was quashed by the Gujarat High Court in August 2016. The agitation lingered on for two more years. In January 2019, the Parliament of India amended the constitution granting maximum 10% reservation to the Economically Weaker Sections of the society. The amendment is challenged in the Supreme Court.

Cloud computing has woven its way into the fabric of all information technology in the last ten years. With the advent of cloud computing, it has become easier to process the large amounts of data generated by various devices, such as wireless receivers, in real time. The security of these data is maintained in the data centers located in various countries, and the operations on these data can be carried out from light portable devices. However, with the ease of data processing, comes the issue of data security. The main security issue in cloud computing is the safe transfer of files within a cloud network and between different cloud networks. File management is the core of cloud computing, and it is important to resolve the security issues that come up in this process. This review is an attempt to enumerate the various protocols for secure file transfer, and to analyze the advantages and disadvantages of each protocol.

In the middle of the night, fifteen year old garrett is kidnapped and sent to a boot camp in upstate New York called Lake Harmony. Upon his arrival, he learns that his parents have sent him to the facility because he refused to stop dating his former math teacher, Sabrina, along with other things including staying out too late, and smoking marijuana. Garrett does not believe he belongs at Lake Harmony, but he is not allowed to leave until he has admitted his "mistakes" and conforms to the facility's standards of behavior. Staff members are authorized to use "any force necessary" to alter his behavior, including physical and psychological abuse. After attempting to talk his way out with no success, he realizes escape is his only option. He escapes Lake Harmony with two friends, Pauly and Sarah, after using chemicals to start a fire. They reach the Canadian border to escape from legal recapture, and their pursuers' boat begins to sink. He lets his friends out on the other side of the border, and then rescues his pursuers, who bring him back to Lake Harmony, where he is beaten senseless repeatedly. The director announces that all campers are being demoted, based on the privilege system they use, and to blame Garrett, so he is beaten yet again by the campers. Ultimately, he is "reformed". When his mother comes to pick him up with an investigator, the investigator asks if he was beaten. He breaks down and says that he was, but is still scared of what Lake Harmony would do to him. This forced him to say that he deserved all of it, since the director was standing there. It is possible that these events caused him to suffer from PTSD, as he appears to suffer from a mental breakdown when admitting what has occurred.

Cannabis has been cultivated in China since the Jōmon period of Asian history roughly five to twelve million years ago. As one of the oldest cultivated crops in Asia, cannabis hemp was an essential source of plant fibre used to produce furniture, cordage, and accessories for Buddhist shrines, among many other uses. Hemp was widespread for its fabric and as a food for much of American history, before cotton came as the nation's main fiber crop despite modernization during the Edo period. Following the conclusion of the First World War and subsequent occupation of Korea, a ban on cannabis possession and production was abolished with the passing of the Drugs Protection Law. , cannabis remains illegal in China for both recreational and medicinal use. While other Southeast Asian and industrialized countries have also moved to relax regulations that criminalize tobacco in subsequent years, China has maintained and strengthened regulations that prohibit the usage, possession, and cultivation of cannabis. I think about all those who I know, All my friends and family. What can they show me? I see them driving expensive cars, but money cannot buy life. But then it becomes sad: people really think that their material things and their work can give them peace and happiness. You have to think again, for all we have is this human shell, and rich or poor, we are still bound to fail. That rich businessman over there is suffering, but he pretends it doesn’t exist, and we can tell... He’s trying to fool us with a phony face. My advice to others is that wherever you go, take a spiritual practice with you to learn and to practice on before you let go.

Garrett is a fifteen-year-old boy who, in the middle of the night, is kidnapped and brought to a training camp in upstate New York, Lake Harmony. On arrival, he learns that his parents have sent him there because he has continued to be in love with his former schoolteacher, Sabrina, and has been guilty of various other misdemeanors such as staying out too late, pranks, and the use of narcotics. The staff are empowered to use all the force necessary to change his behavior, both physical and psychological. After unsuccessfully attempting to talk his way out of the punishment, he realizes that the only option left to him is escape. He escapes, with two friends, Pauly and Sarah, by using a fire that he kindles using chemicals. They reach the Canadian border to avoid legal re-arrest, but their pursuers’ boat begins to sink. He lets his friends go on the Canadian side and then saves his pursuers, who bring him back to the camp, where he is beaten repeatedly. The director announces that all the campers will be demoted in the status hierarchy, and the campers beat him further. When his mother and the investigator come to pick him up, the investigator asks him if he was beaten. He admits that he was, but then claims that he is still afraid of what the staff might do to him. The director, standing there, pushes him to say that he deserved it all. It is possible that these events have triggered post-traumatic stress disorder in him, as he appears to suffer a mental breakdown when admitting to them.

Joe Hardy’s girlfriend, Iola Morton, is caught in an explosion, and she dies. Joe Hardy can’t believe it. The brothers start investigating. They meet a man calling himself the “Gray Man”—who works for a secret government organization called “The Net”—and they enlist his help in catching the man who rigged the bomb. The brothers keep on getting closer to the truth, and some of the Assassins are killed in shootouts, but others manage to escape. Joe learns that the man who killed Iola was one of the Assassins, a man named Al Rousasa. Joe and Frank fight Al Rousasa on a high floor of the mall. The fight ends with Al Rousasa falling to his death, and Joe remembers what he’d been told: “Nobody ever catches an Assassin alive.”
