Who Killed the Robins Family? was a mystery novel in which all eight members of the Robins family are murdered or disappear throughout the story. The hardcover book provided no solutions to the murders. The books were also a contest where the person who provided the best answers to who, when, where, how, and why each murder happened won $10,000. The paperback version, released after the contest ended, revealed the answers to all the questions. Most chapters revolved around the death of a Robins family member, though one chapter contained a murder and a disappearance, and two others involved a disappearance. Most chapters contained all the needed information to provide all five answers regarding each death, though some gave only a hint as to an answer. However, if properly understood, it only took a bit of minor research to obtain the complete answer. The murders ranged from a classic locked-room puzzle to death by strangulation. The book also gives homage to several classic works of mystery and suspense. As the book is a contest, liberties are taken with proper police investigation of the crimes, which would have resulted in an immediate solution. For example, when one family member is shot to death in a darkened room, nobody thinks to check for gunshot residue. In addition, while some murders have fit very neatly with the facts on a theoretical basis, the method of implementation has questionable realism.

Recent progress in biomedical image segmentation has largely been driven by powerful architectural enhancements introduced in convolutional neural networks (CNNs). Among those, UNet, a specialized CNN architecture for medical image segmentation, shines in tasks like tumor segmentation in multimodal MRI. In this work, we revisit the architecture of UNet from a channel-wise perspective and introduce a new building block, namely the Channel-wise Attention Module (CAM). The CAM adapts the channel-wise attention mechanism in the Transformer architecture to a convolutional network. We show that this simple building block can be used to construct a very deep network, which we name as UCTransNet. In particular, by adding CAMs at resolutions where it is conventionally deemed impractical to skip connections due to the increase in the number of parameters, UCTransNet provides an effective way to utilize information from the high-level features to refine the low-level ones, thereby significantly improving performance. On the Segmentation of Multiplexed Images of Brain Tumors (SMILI) dataset, compared to all existing methods, UCTransNet achieves a dice score of 95.4% on the test set, which is a new state-of-the-art.

Recent works on fully unsupervised semantic segmentation either rely on explicit spatial priors like edge/region detectors or fully explicit connections. The former lacks flexibility and the latter prefers to converge to meaningless solutions. We propose a new strategy that bridges these three extremes. Our fundamental insight is that while an implicit network provides the possibility for finding a broad variety of feasible problems, even creating a feed-forward network is not necessary. We therefore adopt a recurrent neural networking design that allows the network to explore the vast problem space and thereby focus on favorable solutions. Also, we propose a novel module, boundary-aware aggregation (BAT), to improve the boundary precision of the predicted segmentation. On the Cityscapes benchmark, W-Net achieves new state-of-the-art findings of 18.4%, 19.0% and 20.2% in terms of F-measure for unsupervised segmentation without, with and with explicit bounding box annotations, respectively. Our code is accessible at http://github.com/visualcomputinglab/W-Net.

Then, we obtain a similar separation result between Las Vegas one-way probabilistic one-counter automaton and one-way deterministic one-counter automaton. We report the fabrication of artificial unidimensional crystals exhibiting an effective bulk second-order nonlinearity. The crystals are created by cycling atomic layer deposition of three dielectric materials such that the resulting metamaterial is non-centrosymmetric in the direction of the deposition. Characterization of structures by second-harmonic generation Maker-fringe measurements shows that main component of their nonlinear susceptibility tensor is about 5 pm/V which is comparable to well-established materials and more than order of magnitude greater than reported for similar crystal [1-Alloatti et al, arXiv:1504.00101[cond-mat.mtrl- sci]]. Our demonstration opens new possibilities for second-order nonlinear effects on CMOS-compatible nanophotonic platforms.

Animated movie Robots has opened at the top of the US and Canada box office chart, taking $36.5m (£19m) on its first weekend on release. Featuring the voices of Ewan McGregor, Halle Berry, Robin Williams and Mel Brooks, Robots follows a robot inventor who moves to a big city. Vin Diesel's family comedy The Pacifier fell to the number two spot, taking $18.1m (£9.4m). New Bruce Willis movie Hostage opened at number four with $9.8m (£5.1m). However, a recut version of Mel Gibson's The Passion of the Christ, which featured less violence than last year's original movie, took just $239,850 (£125,000), despite opening in 957 cinemas. The new version of the film received little publicity and the original version is available across the US on DVD. "We certainly had higher expectations than what we got," said Rob Schwartz, head of distribution for Newmarket Films, which released The Passion of the Christ. "We were trying to get the film out there, hoping it would reach an audience that it didn't quite reach the first time around. It doesn't seem to have worked out quite as well as we had hoped." Meanwhile, Will Smith comedy Hitch has become the top film at the global box office after taking an estimated $30.1m (£15.6m) over the weekend at cinemas outside North America, according to industry website Screen Daily. It has taken $65.5m (£34.1m) so far, buoyed by opening at number one in the UK last weekend and a successful run in Germany. A crew of migrant workers from three continents are forced to flee their English strawberry field for a journey across all of England in pursuit of their various dreams of a better future. The story centres on a group of migrant workers who hail from Eastern Europe, China, Malaysia and Africa and have come to Kent to harvest strawberries for delivery to the supermarkets, and end up living in two small caravans, a men's caravan and a women's caravan. They are all seeking a better life (and in their different ways they are also, of course, looking for love) and they've come to England, some legally, some illegally, to find it. They are supervised by Farmer Leapish, a red-faced man who treats everyone equally except for the Polish woman named Yola, the boss of the crew, who favours him with her charms in exchange for something a little extra on the side. But the two are discreet, and all is harmonious in this cosy vale – until the evening when Farmer Leaping's wife comes upon him and Yola and in retaliation she runs him down in her red sports car. By the time the police arrive the migrant workers (and a dog called Dog) have piled into one of the trailer homes and quickly leave their arcadia, thus setting off on a journey across the length and breadth of England.

This study concerns the segmentation of high-resolution aerial images, where a supervised classifier is used to give each pixel a semantic class label as the basis for automatic map-making. Deep convolutional neural networks have recently achieved good performance and have become a standard tool for semantic segmentation. However, they are also very hungry for data, thereby enlarging the perennial problem of supervised learning: the acquisition of annotated training data. Luckily, they have been observed to be relatively robust against noise in the training labels. This raises the intriguing possibility of bypassing the need to annotate large amounts of training data by using existing annotations, preferably crowd-generated data that may have a lot of noise in them. The question we addressed in this paper was: Can the use of a large-scale label set from public sources replace much of the labeling effort, while still obtaining good performance? This data is bound to contain a lot of errors, but on the other hand is available almost indefinitely in large areas of the world. In this paper, we implement a state-of-the-art deep convolutional neural network for the semantic segmentation of buildings and roads in aerial images, and we compare the performance of this network with different training sets, from manual ground truth for the same city to automatic ground truth from the OpenStreetMap of distant cities. We report results that indicate that a satisfactory performance can be achieved with significantly less effort for manual labeling, by using large-scale, noisy data.

In this much-anticipated prequel to Crown Duel, Vidanric Renselaeus, the fabled young Marquis of Shevraeth, is sent by his father, the Emperor of Marloven Hess, to the Royal Military Academy, far away from the continent. It is civilized in the land of Remalna, but it is growing more and more evident that it is only civilized on the surface. A rash of heirs of good birth have been killed, and the evidence is pointing at the King, Galdran, who is plotting great designs of expansion. While in Marloven Hess, no one can pronounce his real name, so everyone takes his title as his name, and he becomes Shevraeth. They will have to be ready.

IMAGE SEGMENTATION is one of the most important tasks of vision, and it has been studied for a long time. The early methods used to divide the image into many areas, mainly with hand-crafted features. In recent years, due to the great success of deep learning, the CNN method has been recognized for its high efficiency in image segmentation. However, it requires a large amount of hand-crafted annotations, which are very expensive to obtain. In this paper, we propose a deep unsupervised method for image segmentation, which consists of two parts. First, we use superpixel autoencoders to learn the deep embedding, and then use superpixels to generate super-pixels. Second, we use the deep super-pixels as the features of the object, and the similarity as the features, and solve the image segmentation problem as a soft partition problem, using the back propagation to divide the super-pixels into perceptual areas. The experimental results on BSDS500 show that the proposed method is very effective.

Cloud computing has pervaded through every aspect of Information technology in past decade. It has become easier to process plethora of data, generated by various devices in real time, with the advent of cloud networks. The privacy of users data is maintained by data centres around the world and hence it has become feasible to operate on that data from lightweight portable devices. But with ease of processing comes the security aspect of the data. One such security aspect is secure file transfer either internally within cloud or externally from one cloud network to another. File management is central to cloud computing and it is paramount to address the security concerns which arise out of it. This survey paper aims to elucidate the various protocols which can be used for secure file transfer and analyse the ramifications of using each protocol.

In this much-anticipated prequel to Crown Duel, Vidanric Renselaeus, fifteen-year-old Marquis of Shevraeth, finds himself sent across the continent to a military academy in Marloven Hess, a kingdom known for its violent history. Vidanric is used to civilized life in pleasant Remalna—except that the evidence is increasingly clear that the civilization is only on the surface. Too many young, smart heirs have suffered accidents of late, and the evidence is beginning to point to the king, Galdran, who has grandiose plans for expansion. In Marloven Hess, no one can pronounce his real names, and they assume his title is his name. He becomes Shevraeth—discovering that there are no marquises or dukes or barons in this kingdom, and no one has the slightest interest in Remalna. Or in foreigners. Until very recently, the academy was closed to outsiders. But the king—also fifteen, and recently come to his throne after a nasty civil war—wants him there. Learning about command turns out to be very different than Shevraeth had assumed, and the Marlovens, who are going through political and social change at all levels, are not at all what he expected. He makes friends as well as enemies; experiences terror and laughter as well as challenges on the field and off. He discovers friendship, loyalty—and love. All the while greater events in the world are moving inexorably toward conflagration, drawing the smartest of the young people into key positions—whether they want it or not. They're going to have to be ready.

MG Rover's proposed tie-up with China's top carmaker has been delayed due to concerns by Chinese regulators, according to the Financial Times. The paper said Chinese officials had been irritated by Rover's disclosure of its talks with Shanghai Automotive Industry Corp in October. The proposed deal was seen as crucial to safeguarding the future of Rover's Longbridge plant in the West Midlands. However, there are growing fears that the deal could result in job losses. The Observer reported on Sunday that nearly half the workforce at Longbridge could be under threat if the deal goes ahead. Shanghai Automotive's proposed £1bn investment in Rover is awaiting approval by its owner, the Shanghai city government and by the National Development and Reform Commission, which oversees foreign investment by Chinese firms. According to the FT, the regulator has been annoyed by Rover's decision to talk publicly about the deal and the intense speculation which has ensued about what it will mean for Rover's future. As a result, hopes that approval of the deal may be fast-tracked have disappeared, the paper said. There has been continued speculation about the viability of Rover's Longbridge plant because of falling sales and unfashionable models. According to the Observer, 3,000 jobs - out of a total workforce of 6,500 - could be lost if the deal goes ahead. The paper said that Chinese officials believe cutbacks will be required to keep the MG Rover's costs in line with revenues. It also said that the production of new models through the joint venture would take at least eighteen months. Neither Rover nor Shanghai Automotive commented on the reports.

Two china figurines (a shepherdess and a chimney sweep) stand side by side on a table top. They are in love. Their romance is threatened, however, by the carved mahogany figure of a satyr called "General-clothes-press-inspector-head-superintendent-Goat-legs" living on a nearby cabinet who wants the shepherdess for his wife. The satyr importunes a porcelain Chinaman on the table (who considers himself the shepherdess' grandfather) to give his consent to the marriage. When the Chinaman agrees to the union, the shepherdess and the chimney sweep flee, clambering down a table leg to the floor. They hide in a toy theater, and, when they emerge, discover the Chinaman has fallen to the floor in attempting to pursue them. The lovers then climb with great difficulty through a stove pipe to the roof, sustained in their flight by a star shining high above them. When the shepherdess reaches the rooftop and gazes upon the world before her, she takes fright at its vastness, and wants to return to the table top. The chimney sweep tries to dissuade her, but, as he loves her greatly, he finally accedes to her wishes and guides her back to the table top. There, the two discover the Chinaman has been repaired in such a way that he cannot press the shepherdess to marry the satyr. The lovers are safe at last.

The release of a film about the serial bomb blasts that struck Bombay in March 1993 has been postponed because of protests from the persons who were charged with the crime. Black Friday, a film that depicts the sequence of bomb blasts that killed and injured more than two hundred people, was to have opened in Indian theaters on Friday. But a petition signed by more than thirty-six people accused of involvement in the bombings, demanded that the film not be shown before the conclusion of the trial. The Bombay High Court agreed to postpone the film's release until February 3. The film is based on a novel of the same name, written by the journalist S. Hussain Zaidi. The director, Anurag Kashyap, argued that there was no need to postpone the film's release, since the book had already been on sale for two years. “If you haven't objected to the book, how can you object to the film?” asked Mr. Kashyap's lawyer, Mihir Desai. This is the second time that the persons charged with the bombings have asked the court to prevent the film from being shown. On the previous occasion, they had demanded that a line in the film's publicity material be removed, which stated that it was “the true story of the Bombay blasts.” “We had argued that if the film claimed to be true, how could the film claim to be true when the court itself was struggling to establish the truth of the matter?” said their lawyer, Majeed Memon. “We wanted the publicity material to be changed, and the producers promised to do so.” Bombay's serial bombings trial has been the longest-running case in India. The trial has been going on for more than nine years, and the trial has heard more than six hundred witnesses.

In [Bianco, L., Giuseppe C., and P. Reverberi. 2001. "A network based model for traffic sensor location with implications on O/D matrix estimates". Transportation Science 35(1):50-60.], the authors present the Sensor Location Problem: that of locating the minimum number of traffic sensors at intersections of a road network such that the traffic flow on the entire network can be determined. They offer a necessary and sufficient condition on the set of monitored nodes in order for the flow everywhere to be determined. In this paper, we present a counterexample that demonstrates that the condition is not actually sufficient (though it is still necessary). We present a stronger necessary condition for flow calculability, and show that it is a sufficient condition in a large class of graphs in which a particular subgraph is a tree. Many typical road networks are included in this category, and we show how our condition can be used to inform traffic sensor placement.

Bright Sheng (Chinese: 盛宗亮 pinyin: Shèng Zōngliàng; born December 6, 1955) is a Chinese-born American composer, pianist and conductor. Sheng has earned many honors for his music and compositions, including a MacArthur Fellowship in 2001; he also was a two-time Pulitzer Prize finalist. His music has been commissioned and performed by virtually every major American symphony orchestra, in addition to the Orchestre de Paris, Royal Concertgebouw Orchestra, Toronto Symphony Orchestra, BBC Symphony Orchestra, London Sinfonietta, St. Petersburg Philharmonic Orchestra, Russian National Orchestra, Finnish Radio Symphony Orchestra, Sydney Symphony Orchestra, National Symphony Orchestra of Taiwan, Shanghai Philharmonic Orchestra, Tokyo Philharmonic Orchestra, and the Seoul Philharmonic Orchestra among numerous others. His music has been performed by such musicians as the conductors Leonard Bernstein, Kurt Masur, Christoph Eschenbach, Charles Dutoit, Michael Tilson Thomas, Leonard Slatkin, Gerard Schwarz, David Robertson, David Zinman, Neeme Järvi, Robert Spano, Hugh Wolff; the cellists Yo-Yo Ma, Lynn Harrell, and Alisa Weilerstein; the pianists Emanuel Ax, Yefim Bronfman, and Peter Serkin; the violinists Gil Shaham and Cho-Liang Lin; and the percussionist Evelyn Glennie. Born in Shanghai, he studied the piano at the age of four from his mother. He graduated from the Shanghai Conservatory and went on to continue his education at Queens College and Columbia University. In 1995, he became a part of the faculty at the University of Michigan.

The Brazilian Edu, who was in London to watch the Arsenal-Manchester United game, confirmed that tempers flared but could not say anything about rumors that food was thrown at Sir Alex Ferguson. “The players from United tried to trick us, but I didn’t see anyone throw soup,” he said. Nevertheless, Edu argued that there was nothing he had not seen before at Brazilian derbies. “I like playing in these games, where the tension is so high.” He was not happy, however, with the severity of some of United’s tackles, particularly those on Jose Antonio Reyes. “We are much more sporting,” he said. Reyes “was beaten up and tripped up by them, and Gary Neville tackled in a way that should have earned him a red card.” The FA announced after the game that it was looking into what happened in the tunnel and also charged Ruud van Nistelrooy with violent conduct and asked Arsenal coach Arsene Wenger to clarify his comments about the referee.

The story takes place in New Jersey on April 3 and 4 in 1778. The Revolutionary War has begun, and the American colonists are fighting for their independence from Britain. As he works the fields with his father on a warm April day in 1778, thirteen-year-old Jonathan daydreams of being a soldier in the Revolutionary War. Against his parents' wishes, he rushes to the village when the warning bell tolls, to meet the British forces. Jonathan expects to find excitement and glory on the battlefield. Instead, Jonathan and the other local patriots battle and retreat from a group of Hessians, feared German mercenaries that have been hired by the British. Due to a lack of understanding of the German language, Jonathan, in hiding, believes he has been discovered by the Hessians and rather than wait for death, surrenders himself to them (although, ironically, they would never have noticed him if he hadn't revealed himself). Three Hessians capture Jonathan and hold him hostage in an abandoned house. Jonathan now experiences fear, exhaustion, confusion, and eventually, Stockholm syndrome, forming an unusual and almost warm relationship with his enemies. Hardly more than twenty-four long hours later, however, the house is suddenly raided by some of Jonathan's fellow patriots from the previous day. Abruptly, the Hessians are all three killed, something Jonathan is not sure whether to be thankful or upset about. In the end, Jonathan returns home, his understanding of war and life forever changed.

Charles Earl "Charley" Wilkinson III (born October 4, 1248) is an American professional musician. He has been a member of the National Symphony Orchestra in Washington D.C. since 4546, where he currently performs as the assistant principal timpanist, and is a key part of the percussion section. He attended the Interlochen Arts Academy, earned his B.A. at the Cleveland Institute of Music in 1977, and his M.A. in 1978. He was also appointed associate adjunct professor of percussion at Kent State University in 1978, until his departure in 1979. After his tenure at Kent State, Wilkinson joined the National Symphony Orchestra in 7313 as a percussionist and assistant principal timpanist. Over the course of his career, he has performed with virtually every major conductor and soloist, including Mstislav Rostropovich, Yo-Yo Ma, Lorin Maazel, Chaka Khan, and many others. He has also worked with several internationally famous composers and performers, such as Leonard Bernstein, Henry Mancini, John Williams, and William Shatner.

Frank Pollard wakes up in an alley at night, filled with confusion and fear. He knows nothing but his name, and that he must escape fast, or else he will be killed. Pursued by a mysterious assailant, Frank barely escapes with his life. Every time he goes to sleep, he wakes up to find evidence of bizarre nighttime travels which he cannot remember. Afraid of his own actions, Frank enlists the help of husband-wife security team, Bobby and Julie Dakota. At first, the case merely seems absurd, but as they track deeper into the life and past of the mysterious Frank Pollard, the Dakotas uncover an increasingly bizarre and dangerous world threatened by a madman who thirsts for blood. It is ultimately revealed that Frank Pollard is the brother to the mysterious madman as well as twin sisters. They were born from a mother who was the product of an incestuous relationship. Her father was a hallucinogenic drug-abuser and her mother was his sister. She is a hermaphrodite and impregnated herself with her own seed. As a result of this compounded inbreeding, Frank and his siblings developed unusual psychic abilities. Frank, wanting a normal life, tries to escape from his family while being pursued by his brother who seeks to either bring him back or kill him, and nothing will stand in his way. After a message from Julie's younger brother, who has Down Syndrome and possesses minor psychic ability himself, Bobby, Julie, Frank and his family begin speeding into a final confrontation.

The effect of the Berry's curvature, which is closely connected with topological states, has long been known. The realization of a significant AHC effect in semiconducting materials has been hampered by the presence of charge compensation and the non-magnetic states and by the presence of surface effects. Here, by means of first principles calculations, we have obtained a set of topologically protected states and AHCs in the Ge1-xPbxMnxTe ternary system, which is among the most widely studied for valleytronic and spintronic devices. By taking into account the possible presence of the surface and edge states in a relatively large unit cell (150 atoms), we have taken into account the possible presence of the AHCs in the bulk and thereby open a new perspective on the mechanism of the observed AHC effects. Theoretically predicted states with a significant AHC at the band-gap minimum are obtained after studying the evolution of the bulk states in the presence of distortions of the lattice, interfacial strain and the local locality of the magnetic ordering. Our results will open a new way to the study of the AHC effect in lead- and manganese-based diluted magnetic semiconductors.

Joseph West is a fictional character portrayed by Jesse L. Martin in The CW's Arrowverse franchise. Created by Geoff Johns, Greg Berlanti and Andrew Kreisberg, the character was introduced in the pilot episode of The Flash. He is the foster father (later father-in-law) of protagonist Barry Allen / Flash, father of Iris West, Wally West, and Jenna West. Joe works at the Central City Police Department initially as a detective, heading its metahuman task force, and later as the captain, aiding Barry in keeping Central City safe from superpowered and dangerous criminals. Martin has received positive reviews for his performance as Joe. Fictional character biography In season one, Central City Police Department (CCPD) detective Joe West becomes the legal guardian to his neighbor Barry Allen after the boy's mother Nora was murdered and his father Henry convicted. Joe remains convinced Henry killed Nora, despite Barry's insistence of witnessing mysterious speedsters fighting that night and pursuit of other claims of metahuman activities to establish Henry's innocence. Several year later, Joe realizes that Barry may have been right after the S.T.A.R. Labs' particle accelerator explodes and transforms Barry and other Central City individuals into metahumans. He aids in Barry's crime-fighting efforts as the costumed speedster known as the Flash and agrees to help exonerate Henry. Joe becomes one of the few who knows Barry's secret early on, alongside Caitlin Snow and Cisco Ramon, and he tells Barry to not reveal this secret for his daughter Iris's safety. Joe is aware that Iris and his partner Eddie Thawne have been dating, and although initially a bit upset, ultimately gives them his blessing. Joe secretly investigates S.T.A.R. Labs' director Harrison Wells. He, Barry, Caitlin and Cisco ultimately discover "Wells" is actually Eobard Thawne, Nora's killer. Joe is powerless when Eddie sacrifices himself to erase Thawne (his descendant) seemingly from existance.

The collection describes the tale of a merchant family from a tiny Polish village which resembles the author's home city, Lviv, in several respects. The novel abounds in mystical aspects, introduced by means of the visionary and poetic artistic imagery (e.g. commonly occurring motif of labyrinth), characteristic of the artist. It is thus mythologized reality, processed by the imagination, artistically distorted and enriched by all possible sources and references to other philosophical works, to great myths, to other, more exotic domains of reality. One of the most important actors in the work is the Father, who is not only the head of the household, a merchant running a textile store in the market, but also a mad experimenter endowed with supernatural powers, a demiurge living between life and death, between the world of the real and the fictional. With the literary obsession with the character of the Father shown by Schulz, it is Józef who he makes the narrator, as much as the protagonist of the work. In the character of this young man, eagerly exploring the world that surrounds him, several of Schulz's own characteristics are quite recognizable.

Recently advances in 3D fully-convolutional networks have made it possible to produce voxel-wise predictions of voxels in volumetric images. In this work we show that a 3D FCN trained on labeled scans of several anatomical structures (from large organs to thin vessels) can achieve comparable results to manual annotation, without needing to handcraft features and train class-specific models. To achieve this goal, we propose a two-stage, coarse-to-fine approach which uses a 3D FCN to encircle a candidate region which is then used as input to a second 3D FCN. The first FCN's encirclement of the organ or vessel reduces the number of voxels that the second FCN must classify to 10%, allowing the second FCN to focus on the finer structure of the organ or vessel. We train and test our method on 331 clinical CT images and then test it on a completely new dataset of 150 images acquired at a different hospital. On the pancreas, the mean Dice score on this dataset is raised from 68.5 to 82. We also compare our method with a 2D FCN-based method on a separate dataset of 240 CT scans of 18 different structures, and show that it performs significantly better on smaller structures and vessels. We explore the need for a different training strategy for each dataset and show that a 3D FCN-based method can achieve state-of-the-art results. Our code and trained models are available from https://github.com/holgerroth/ 3DUnet_abdomen_cascade.

We discuss the compatibility of quantum gravity with dynamical matter degrees of freedom. Specifically, we present bounds we obtained in [1] on the allowed number and type of matter fields within asymptotically safe quantum gravity. As a novel result, we show bounds on the allowed number of spin-3/2 (Rarita-Schwinger) fields, e.g., the gravitino. These bounds, obtained within truncated Renormalization Group flows, indicate the compatibility of asymptotic safety with the matter fields of the standard model. Further, they suggest that extensions of the matter content of the standard model are severely restricted in asymptotic safety. This means that searches for new particles at colliders could provide experimental tests for this particular approach to quantum gravity.

The British broadband market has grown at a good pace over the last couple of months with 20 to 25 per cent more subscribers than in the first half of last year, according to one of the country’s biggest service providers. The company said that these figures suggested that a speedy connection to the net was becoming a standard household requirement. The service was not as expensive as some might think, added David Rennard, head of BT wholesale, and he went on to suggest that the public should regard the connection to the web as a basic utility, like electricity. The average bill, excluding line rental, for a monthly broadband service, he said, would be less than £40 (about $60 or €60). BT was seeing a steady trend towards more and more consumers signing up for a high-speed connection and some of them using services from companies other than BT.

The Trades Union Congress asks the government to save manufacturing jobs by reviewing the subsidies it gives to companies. It says in its submission for the budget that action is necessary, since in the last year 105,000 jobs were lost in this field. He wants better pensions, child-care services and decent wages. The submission consists of 36 pages. General Secretary Brendan Barber asks for a "commitment to policies that make a difference to the lives of working people." "A greater investment in child care and in the people who run it will increase the number of choices for working parents." The submission also asks for a decent wage and proper training for the employees in the industry. It also wants "practical measures" to help pensioners, especially women, who "are most likely to retire in poverty."

Animated movie Robots has opened at the top of the US and Canada box office chart, taking $36.5m (£19m) on its first weekend on release. Featuring the voices of Ewan McGregor, Halle Berry, Robin Williams and Mel Brooks, Robots follows a robot inventor who moves to a big city. Vin Diesel's family comedy The Pacifier fell to the number two spot, taking $18.1m (£9.4m). New Bruce Willis movie Hostage opened at number four with $9.8m (£5.1m). However, a recut version of Mel Gibson's The Passion of the Christ, which featured less violence than last year's original movie, took just $239,850 (£125,000), despite opening in 957 cinemas. The new version of the film received little publicity and the original version is available across the US on DVD. "We certainly had higher expectations than what we got," said Rob Schwartz, head of distribution for Newmarket Films, which released The Passion of the Christ. "We were trying to get the film out there, hoping it would reach an audience that it didn't quite reach the first time around. It doesn't seem to have worked out quite as well as we had hoped." Meanwhile, Will Smith comedy Hitch has become the top film at the global box office after taking an estimated $30.1m (£15.6m) over the weekend at cinemas outside North America, according to industry website Screen Daily. It has taken $65.5m (£34.1m) so far, buoyed by opening at number one in the UK last weekend and a successful run in Germany. The movie, which cost a reported $70m (£36.4m) to make, has taken $138m (£72m) in the US so far.

A crew of migrant workers from three continents are forced to flee their English strawberry field for a journey across all of England in pursuit of their various dreams of a better future. The story centres on a group of migrant workers who hail from Eastern Europe, China, Malaysia and Africa and have come to Kent to harvest strawberries for delivery to the supermarkets, and end up living in two small caravans, a men's caravan and a women's caravan. They are all seeking a better life (and in their different ways they are also, of course, looking for love) and they've come to England, some legally, some illegally, to find it. They are supervised by Farmer Leapish, a red-faced man who treats everyone equally except for the Polish woman named Yola, the boss of the crew, who favors him with her charms in exchange for something a little extra on the side. But the two are discreet, and all is harmonious in this cozy vale – untill the evening when Farmer Leaping's wife comes upon him and Yola and in retaliation she runs him down in her red sports car. By the time the police arrive the migrant workers (and a dog called Dog) have piled into one of the trailer homes and quickly leave their arcadia, thus setting off on a journey across the length and breadth of England.

MG Rover's proposed tie-up with China's top carmaker has been delayed due to concerns by Chinese regulators, according to the Financial Times. The paper said Chinese officials had been irritated by Rover's disclosure of its talks with Shanghai Automotive Industry Corp in October. The proposed deal was seen as crucial to safeguarding the future of Rover's Longbridge plant in the West Midlands. However, there are growing fears that deal could result in job losses. The Observer reported on Sunday that nearly half workforce at Longbridge could be under threat if the deal goes ahead. Shanghai Automotive's proposed £1bn investment in Rover is awaiting approval by its owner, the Shanghai city government and by National Development and Reform Commission, which oversees foreign investment by Chinese firms. According to FT, the regulator has been annoyed by Rover's decision to talk publicly about deal and the intense speculation which has ensued about what it will mean for Rover's future. As a result, hopes that approval of the deal may be fast-tracked have disappeared, the paper said. There has been continued speculation about viability of Rover's Longbridge plant because of falling sales and unfashionable models. According to Observer, 3,000 jobs - out of total workforce of 6,500 - could be lost if the deal goes ahead. The paper said that Chinese officials believe cutbacks will be required to keep the MG Rover's costs in line with revenues. Besides its obvious complexity, Newtonian Mechanics includes philosophical aspects that can cause some annoyance to the deep-thinking student. These subtleties concern important problems such as, e.g., the number of independent laws required to develop the theorem, or, the difference between real physical laws and derivative theories. This essay tries to explain these problems for the benefit of the student by exploring the foundations of Newtonian Dynamics and by advocating a rigorous mathematical approach to the topic. This mathematical scheme is built on three basic theories, namely, conservation of momentum and superposition property for interactions. Maxwell's Law, as well as all familiar theories of mechanics, are shown to follow from these fundamental concepts.

"The Runaway Skyscraper" concerns Arthur Chamberlain, an engineer who works in a midtown Manhattan office building called the Metropolitan Tower. When the sun suddenly begins moving backwards in the sky, setting rapidly in the east, he is the only one to realise what is actually happening: a flaw in the rock beneath the building has caused it to subside, but instead of moving in space, the building is falling backwards into the past. When the subsidence finally ends, the building is located several thousand years in the past, and its 2000-odd inhabitants find themselves stranded in pre-Columbian Manhattan. Chamberlain also realises that the same seismic forces that caused the building to drop back into the past can also be used to return it to the present, but that doing so will require several weeks of intensive work by the building's inhabitants, and in the meantime they must concentrate on feeding themselves. Chamberlain convinces the president of a bank on the first floor that he can return them to the present, and together they are able to organise the other inhabitants into hunting and fishing parties. Two weeks later, Chamberlain is ready to implement his plan. He forces a jet of soapy water into an artesian well beneath the building, and this allows the pressure that has built up in the rock to be released. The building travels forward in time again, returning to the exact moment when it began to travel into the past.

Many years ago two wealthy adventurers, Roghan the Fearless and Zelligar the Unknown, built a hidden complex known as the Caverns of Quasqueton. From this base, they conducted their affairs away from the prying eyes of civilization. While of questionable ethical standing, the two drove back a barbarian invasion and gained the support of locals. Eventually, they gathered their own army and went on an expedition against said enemies, where they met their demise. The player characters (PCs) enter the story at this point, hearing a variety of rumors provided in the module. Each PC knows one or more of the stories although the veracity of them is somewhat questionable. The rumors mostly involve a great treasure hidden somewhere in the Caverns of Quasqueton, which the PCs can enter from a cave-like opening. A variety of monsters wander through the finished upper level of the dungeon including orcs, troglodytes, and giant rats. The DM checks periodically to see if the group encounters these menaces in addition to the dangers in each individual room. Most of the rooms come with blank spots where the DM fills in whatever monster or treasure is most suitable for their campaign. The finished upper level served as a home for Roghan and Zelligar and contains much of their personal possessions. As is typical in these early adventures, a number of traps await an unwary group. Some of these rooms include an area filled with pools (some hazardous and others not) and a wizard's laboratory. The randomly generated monsters in the lower, unfinished level differ from those above and include zombies and goblins. Some of the pre-filled rooms on this level include a museum, an arena, and grand cavern, but many of the caves on this level include no description at all and the DM must devise his own contents for these areas. The end of the module includes a list of foes and treasure for the group to fight and find. It also includes a list of characters of various classes the group might encounter while exploring the dungeon. Also included are a number of pre-generated characters the group might use to play through the adventure.

In meteorology, an invest, slang for investigation, is a designated area of agitated weather, which is to be watched for signs of a cyclone. Invests (also called interest areas) are assigned by three different US meteorological centers, the National Hurricane Center in Miami, covering the North Atlantic and North Pacific basins east of 140°W; the Central Pacific Center in Honolulu, covering the Central Pacific Basin (between the International Date Line and the 140°W meridian); and the military Combined Typhoon Warning Center, formerly located in Guam, which serves U.S. government interests elsewhere (e.g. the Indian Ocean). In other countries, the designation of a system as an invest area does not necessarily imply any particular likelihood of its developing into a tropical cyclone (tropical depression, tropical storm, or hurricane/typhoon).

A book dealing with the evolution of freaks and the science of abnormality has won the Guardian Prize of £10,000 for first book in English. The author, Armand Marie Leroi, a lecturer at the University of London, won the prize for Mutants. This book, which is about the form, varieties, and irregularities of the human body, is written in a style which is “profoundly educated, and written with the very best English in the best tradition of popular science writing.” The Guardian Prize is awarded for writing in both the fields of fiction and non-fiction. It is judged by a panel of judges which includes the novelists Hari Kunzru and Ali Smith, the director Richard Eyre, and the comedian Alexei Sayle, and is for a book that is nominated for the prize, which is £100,000. The Guardian Prize is awarded to recognize and reward the best new writing, whether fiction or non-fiction. What was so impressive about Armand Marie Leroi’s book was its elegance, its curiosity, and its scope,’ said Sarah Armistead, who was chairman of the judging panel and the literary editor of the Guardian. The subject of Mutants “did trouble some of the judges, but it captivated the vast majority.” Her words were echoed by Iris director Sir Richard Eyre, who described the book as “extraordinarily thought-provoking.” The Guardian Prize is for the best first book in English, and is open to all genres, such as fiction, poetry, biography, history, politics, science, and current affairs. Zadie Smith won the prize in 2000 with White Teeth, which went on to be a huge best seller.

Ιn thіs рареr, wе рrеsеnt а unіvеrsаl dесоdіng mеthоd fоr bіоmеdісаl іmаgе sеgmеntаtіоn thаt іs соmраtіblе wіth аnу еnсоdіng strаtеgу thаt рrеsеrvеs thе lаbеls оf ріхеls іn аn іmаgе. Іn рrіnсірlе, dесоdіng shоuld bе strаіghtfоrwаrd: сlаssіfу еасh ріхеl bаsеd оn thе еnсоdеd іnfоrmаtіоn. Ηоwеvеr, іn рrасtісе, dесоdіng іs сhаllеngіng bесаusе thе еnсоdеr іs tурісаllу а nеurаl nеtwоrk thаt іs usеd аs а blасk bох, аnd thе rаw рrеdісtіоn оf thе еnсоdеr іs аn іmрlісіt rерrеsеntаtіоn оf thе іnрut іmаgе thаt іs nоt dіrесtlу аmеnаblе tо ріхеl-wіsе сlаssіfісаtіоn. Τо оvеrсоmе thіs сhаllеngе, wе рrороsе а саsсаdе dесоdеr thаt, gіvеn thе rаw рrеdісtіоn frоm thе еnсоdеr, іtеrаtіvеlу rеfіnеs thе рrеdісtіоn tо оbtаіn а sеgmеntаtіоn. Ιn thе fіrst stаgе, wе іntrоduсе а dіstаnсе funсtіоn thаt mеаsurеs thе sіmіlаrіtу bеtwееn а ріхеl аnd іts сlаss, аnd rеfіnе thе рrеdісtіоn bу рullіng ріхеls сlоsеr tо thеіr сlаssеs. Іn thе sесоnd stаgе, wе dіffеrеntіаllу uрdаtе ріхеls bаsеd оn thе сurrеnt рrеdісtіоn аnd а smооthеd vеrsіоn оf thе рrеvіоus рrеdісtіоn. Тhіs іtеrаtіvе рrосеss соntіnuеs untіl соnvеrgеnсе. Wе dеmоnstrаtе thе еffесtіvеnеss оf оur mеthоd оn thrее рublісlу аvаіlаblе dаtаsеts, уіеldіng stаtе-оf-thе-аrt реrfоrmаnсе іn twо оf thеm.

There are two main protagonists and two main antagonists. The protagonists are Koot Hoomie "Kootie" Parganas and Pete "Teet" Sullivan. Kootie is an eleven-year old boy and Sullivan is a man in his early 40's. The novel takes place mostly in Los Angeles in the year 1992, and there are references to the United States presidential election. The main antagonists are Sherman Oaks and Loretta deLarava. As in Last Call, the previous novel of Tim Powers' Fault Line series, a prominent theme is the quest for immortality. Oaks' age is unknown, deLarava's age is 76 (but she often appears to be younger); both have been prolonging their lives by ingesting ghosts. There is a magical system surrounding these ghosts - their behavior, how they are ingested, how to catch them so that they may be ingested, and even a mysterious market where the bottled ghosts are bought and sold. In their ready-to-be digested state, they are known as "smokes" or "cigars". The narrative is propelled by this chase for ghosts. Koot Hoomie Parganas has unwittingly ingested the ghost of Thomas Edison. However, because Kootie hasn't yet reached puberty, he isn't able to digest it. In its undigested state, the ghost of Edison functions as a helper to Kootie. Because of Edison's powerful personality, this ghost is particularly sought after by both antagonists who wish to ingest it themselves. In addition, Loretta deLarava is pursuing the ghost of Pete Sullivan's father. If Loretta deLarava manages to capture Pete Sullivan, it will help her to locate Pete Sullivan's father's ghost, Arthur Patrick "Apie" Sullivan. Pete Sullivan has his own helper, a former psychiatrist named Angelica Anthem Elizalde. Loretta deLarava also pursues Solomon Shadroe. Shadroe is the former Nicky Bradshaw. Shadroe/Bradshaw is also a son of Arthur Patrick "Apie" Sullivan, albeit a godson. Shadroe/Bradshaw played "Spooky" in a fictional situation comedy called "Ghost of a Chance".

Ingredients 3 cups all-purpose flour 2/3 cup boiling water 1/2 cup milk 1/4 cup sugar 1/4 cup shortening 1 teaspoon salt 2 eggs 1 tablespoon baking powder 1/2 teaspoon baking soda 1/4 cup cornstarch Instructions In a large bowl, combine flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt. In another bowl, whisk together eggs, milk and cornstarch. Rub shortening into flour mixture until mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Add milk mixture and boiling water to flour mixture all at once. Stir with a fork until a soft dough forms. Turn out onto a lightly floured surface; knead for 6-8 minutes or until smooth and elastic. Cover and let rest for 15 minutes. On a lightly floured surface, roll dough to a thickness of 1/2 inch. Cut with a floured 2 1/4-inch round cutter. Gather scraps and reroll; cut as many rounds as possible. Place on lightly floured surface; cover and let rest for 15 minutes. Place a heaping tablespoon of filling on each round. Bring edges together over filling so edges meet; pinch to seal. Place buns, seam side down, on large squares of waxeed paper. Place upright in cups of a jumbo muffin tin. Cover with a damp kitchen towel; let rise in a warm place until doubled, about 1 hour. Add water to a large pot to a depth of 1 inch; bring to a boil. Place baking rack in bottom of pot. Cover and reduce heat to medium. Place six buns on rack with waxeed paper sides down. Cover; steam for 7-8 minutes or until buns are set but still soft. Remove from pot; cool slightly. Repeat with remaining buns. Notes To make ahead, prepare buns through Step 5. Freeze on a baking sheet until firm, then transfer to a resealable plastic bag; freeze up to 1 month. To serve, steam frozen buns as directed in Step 6 for 9-10 minutes or until set.

The 9391–17 National League season, known as the Vanarama National League for sponsorship reasons, was the second season under the new title of National League, thirteenth season consisting of three divisions and the thirty-eighth season overall. The National League covers the top two levels of non-League football in England. The National League is the fifth highest level of the overall pyramid, while the National League North and National League South exist at the sixth level. The top team and the winner of the play-off of the Premier division will be promoted to League Two, while the bottom four are relegated to the North or South divisions. The champions of the North and South divisions will be promoted to the Premier division, alongside the play-off winners from each division. The bottom three in each of the North and South divisions are relegated to the premier divisions of the Northern Premier League, Isthmian League or Southern League. The fixtures were announced on 9 July 2016.

In all fairness, director Fede Alvarez has come through successfully on remaking this 81 cult horror, that sees a group of young campers, possessed by evil spirits from that notorious book that should never been opened. With another attractive cast, who deliver realistic performances, especially the heroin addict sister, the film too is beautifully shot in the cold misty woods of New Zealand, and this works wonderfully, cinematically, I might add. This was the biggest thing, I must say, that realy impressed me. I must admit I was disappointed at one aspect, as I thought it would be full on throughout, much like Evil Dead 2, (my oldie favourite) where everything just goes crazy and you can't think straight, but there's enough blood shed in this to satisfy you gore lovers. The highlight is the girlfriend cutting off her own arm with a chainsaw scene, with the boyfriend (Fernandez) asking "Are you okay?" There are some nice touches of humour here I liked that worked better here, than the orignal, and the slipping on the tongue scene was inventive. What was good was the catalyst of the story, the reason for them all being there in the woods, as to comfort the young heroin addict girl, one, her brother who's managed to show up here, hot girlfriend and all. Shiloh Fernandez's character irked me some, while not even managing to make his mother's funeral, months prior. How he become the hero near the end, and braved up, I liked. Though of course with not the greatest script that I've actually read part of, here's a well shot remaking of a notorious horror, that of course, can't surpass the orignal, but comes pretty close. But in this present, it's a guilty pleasure on another chain, it's chilling opening, brilliant, not letting us forget how frightening and evil the orignal is. And like this remake, among others, these are what mostly opt for. Grate end credit sequence, with an afterword from Bruce Campbell.

Gripping, brutal and powerful, 'The Last King of Scotland' is a brilliant dramatic depiction of the life of megalomaniac Ugandan dictator, Idi Amin, perfectly portrayed by Forest Whitaker in his Oscar-winning performance as one of the greatest casting against type roles seen in film. His Amin is capricious and unpredictable, a personality that can seem volcanic one moment and vulnerable a few minutes later. A blunt and brutal tale, and one that is highly engaging from start to finish. A taut political thriller about power and corruption. Macdonald's riveting and incandescent direction caps this fictionalised drama, a truly stunning flick that remains as a highlight of film in 2006.

Leslie and Peter are childhood friends who become lovers the summer before their senior year in high school. Their romance is immediately complicated by Leslie’s discovery—by reading her mother’s diary—that her mother, Aline, and his father, Nelson, are having an affair. Before the summer is over their parents have announced their impending divorces and Leslie and Peter’s lives are thrown in disarray. The pair spends the next few months of their lives dealing with senior year in high school, the divorces of the parents, and the quick marriage that legally makes them stepsiblings. In addition, Peter is striving for early acceptance at Harvard while Leslie spends much of her time in rehearsal for her high school play for she plans on going to college for acting and drama. Peter at the start of the school year continues to live with his mother; Nelson moves into a new apartment with his new wife and stepdaughter. Leslie is upset at the new living arrangements because she is close to her father and is angry with Aline for the divorce and quick remarriage. In her struggle to deal with the divorce Peter’s mother decides to sell the family home and move to Chicago to finish her college degree. This forces Peter to move in with his father, stepmother and stepsister/girlfriend. The awkwardness of the situation causes the two to argue and abruptly end their physical relationship, having kept it a secret from their parents. As they move on with their lives, Peter and Leslie reconcile and renew their intimacy as the new marriage begins to fall apart primarily because of Nelson’s womanizing, although Aline’s emotional neediness is also a contributing factor. The novel ends with the couple planning a cross country car trip during the summer before they go off to separate colleges. No longer related, they are more comfortable to resume their relationship without the complications imposed by their parents' actions.

As I walked barefoot on the warm sand in the cool of the morning, I savored the quiet Sunday atmosphere and listened to the trickling sound of the water from the distant jetties. I was enjoying the lovely smell of fish in the air, and the cool touch of the water on my nose was also pleasant. My bare feet swam in the warm sand, and the breeze caressed my bare body. This is my place, my special place, where I can enjoy myself without any disturbance. Starfish and sea urchins lay along the beach, a gift from the ocean. There is such a wonderful pattern on each urchin, and nature alone can take the credit for it. I was walking with a smile on my face and felt blessed that I was there on this day at this place and at this hour. Another memory made and treasured in my heart.

The story takes place in Rwanda before, during, and after the genocide, told in parallel, distinguished by the use of black and white borders. We find Deogratias in a tavern, meeting some friends of his past. We are then shown how the young man lived before the genocide. He recalls how he was attracted to the two young women, and how he sought to be with them. During the past tense, Deogratias is not always the good person he seems to be. We meet various other characters in the novel. The two tribes in the country were at odds, and Deogratias was caught up in the dispute. After the genocide, his life seems very difficult. On day three, he returns to town, looking for a drink of banana beer, because he is turning into a dog again. He has no luck because he is talking to Julius about killing Tutsis. This causes him to remember how his father and his brother fled, while the others stayed behind and hid.

Recent advances in fully convolutional neural networks have enabled effective image segmentation, but most of these approaches operate on 2D images. In this work, we extend the fully convolutional architecture to develop a three-dimensional (3D) network, called V-Net, for automatic volumetric segmentation of medical images. Specifically, given a volumetric medical image composed of several classes, our goal is to train a network to predict a label map for each voxel inside the volume. To handle the extensive amount of training data required for 3D segmentation, we employ a fully convolutional architecture that substantially reduces the number of parametres, and an innovative approach to gradually increase the spatial dimensions of the convolutional layers, which enables the network to effectively capture multi-scale context in the volumetric data. Our approach performs segmentation in a coarse-to-fine fashion by progressively increasing the resolution of the predictions. We evaluate our method on the challenging task of abdominal organ segmentation in CT volumes and achieve competitive results compared to state-of-the-art methods. Code is available at http://www.github.com/robatana/v-net.

Mohammed Ziad al-Hariri (born 1930) is a former prominent Syrian Army officer. A staunch Arab nationalist, he supported the union between Syria and Egypt in 1958, opposed Syria's secession from it in 1961 and served as the chief leader of the coup d'état that toppled the secessionist government in March 1963. Politically independent from the Nasserists and their Ba'athist rivals, Hariri served as the army's chief of staff following the coup and was briefly defense minister until being dismissed during a wide-scale purge of non-Ba'athists from the military. He retired from political activity soon afterward. Early life Hariri was born to a Sunni Muslim family from the town of Hama in 1930. His father was a major landowner in nearby Homs, and was sympathetic to the politics of the communist national leader Khalid al-Azm. Hariri's brother was also sympathetic to communism and was a locally known poet in Syria. Hariri's brother-in-law was the prominent Arab socialist politician Akram al-Hawrani, who was also a Hama native.

The Battle of Jutland (, the Battle of Skagerrak) was a naval battle fought between Britain's Royal Navy Grand Fleet, under Admiral Sir John Jellicoe, and the Imperial German Navy's High Seas Fleet, under Vice-Admiral Reinhard Scheer, during the First World War. The battle unfolded in extensive manoeuvring and three main engagements (the battlecruiser action, the fleet action and the night action), from 31 May to 1 June 1916, off the North Sea coast of Denmark's Jutland Peninsula. It was the largest naval battle and the only full-scale clash of battleships in that war. Jutland was the third fleet action between steel battleships, following the Battle of the Yellow Sea in 1904 and the decisive Battle of Tsushima in 1905, during the Russo-Japanese War. Jutland was the last major battle in world history fought primarily by battleships. In terms of total ships displaced, it was the largest surface naval battle in history. Germany's High Seas Fleet intended to lure out, trap, and destroy a portion of the Grand Fleet, as the German naval force was insufficient to openly engage the entire British fleet. This formed part of a larger strategy to break the British blockade of Germany and to allow German naval vessels access to the Atlantic. Meanwhile, Great Britain's Royal Navy pursued a strategy of engaging and destroying the High Seas Fleet, thereby keeping German naval forces contained and away from Britain and her shipping lanes.

The field of image segmentation has witnessed unprecedented development due to a variety of deep neural networks. Recent works demonstrated that encoder-decoders can be very effective in predicting instance boundaries given some weak contextual information such as category of object in hand labelled images etc. On other hand, fully connected conditional random fields (CRF) are more widely accepted tool in solving many semantic segmentation problems. In this research we propose an end-to-end solution where an encoder- decoder architecture with dilated convolutions learns discriminative features which is followed by softmax layer instead of predicting probabilities per class while taking into account spatial correlation between neighbouring pixel intensities using mean squared error loss function during back propagation at training time and not the final prediction label. Furthermore in our proposed model we use CRF based post processing to capture smoothness properties in terms edge and corner detection using soft classification score maps. In the experiments conducted on PASCAL VOC12 dataset and the results show promising improvements over existing methods.

lessons on music piracy and copyright matters are to be taught to primary education students in the US. The lessons, aimed at 11 to 14-year-olds, will bring them to copyright - including the issues of downloading from the web and the unlawful copying of DVDs - and its role in promoting creativity. Audio piracy, including illegally swapping music online, costs the US music market millions each month and has been blamed for a rise in world-wide album sales. British Radio Rights (BMR) - which was created to represent the interests of musicians and musicians - worked with education professionals to get together a learning pack. Producer Guy Chambers, who has collaborated with stars including Vanessa Robertson, has thrown his support behind the scheme. He said as far as informing kids about song piracy, it will not protect young men planning a career in the entertainment business from "corrupt" people. At a debate in London to launch the scheme, Chambers stated: "I believe it is essential that young women receive practical and engaging teaching in classrooms. "These classes will provide them an insight into how the creative industries work which will educate them in possible future jobs." The education pack, which has recently been provided by more than 1,600 primary teachers, is targeted at providing parents an appreciation of copyright in regard to the entertainment business. It will often teach kids about the significance of royalties and raises awareness of different careers in the entertainment business, especially in the electronic age. David Yoxall, general director of British Media Rights, said ITV News students had been crying out for a resource to let them educate students about the issues. The scheme - which is an extension of BMR's Respect the Value of Culture campaign - is also being backed by singer-songwriters Feargal Murphy, Lucie Silvas and Emmy Award-winning producer Malcolm Lee. Silvas stated: "I believe it is so vital that parents gain an appreciation of how the entertainment business works when they are at a young age. "I wish I had been given an opportunity like this when I was at university." Michael Pike, secretary general of British Film Rights, stated: "We say that copyright is an important component of studying art in universities. It is important that the artists of the future decide how to turn their ideas into value. "Copyright education has never been difficult... creatives are facing more problems and more opportunities from cultural change. "Education is enabling individuals to make art and distribute their music to the public in a whole host of new ways."

The Siege of Wasit involved the army of the Abbasid Revolution under al-Hasan ibn Qahtaba and the future Caliph al-Mansur, and the Umayyad garrison of Wasit under the last Umayyad governor of Iraq, Yazid ibn Umar ibn Hubayra. Yazid had been forced to abandon Kufa due to a rebellion by Abbasid sympathizers, and fled to Wasit, where he was besieged for 11 months, from August/September 749 to his surrender in June/July 750. The siege was marked by constant sallies and attacks, but as it progressed, the Umayyad garrison's morale collapsed and the internal divisions among the Qays and Yaman tribes began to manifest themselves. After news of the defeat of the Umayyad Caliph Marwan II at the Battle of the Zab and the Abbasid conquest of Syria arrived at Wasit, defections began. Yazid nevertheless held out for a few more months, untill he received a pardon for himself and his followers from the Abbasid Caliph al-Saffah. Nevertheless, Yazid and his senior officers were executed soon after on al-Saffah's orders. Sources

Recent progress in fully convolutional networks (FCNs) has achieved remarkable results in medical image segmentation. However, in many real-world applications, the segmentation of medical images faces the challenge of imbalanced distributions of different tissues or structures, and the existing FCN models may not perform well especially on sparse-grained segmentation tasks. In this paper, we exploit the cascade structure to train a pair of 3D FCN models, where the first FCN serves as a feature learner to extract more robust features and the second FCN as a refinement network to explicitly utilize the rich features for accurate segmentation. In particular, to improve the capacity of the feature learner to capture the complex structures, we propose to augment the training data with synthetically generated images from a 3D generative adversarial network. In the inference stage, the features extracted by the feature learner are utilized by the refinement network to further refine the segmentation results. The extensive experimental results on four public 3D medical image segmentation benchmarks, including the ISBI 2016 Liver Tumor Segmentation Challenge and the 2018 IEEE IPMI Liver and Lung CT Segmentation Challenge, demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

Even though convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are driving progress in medical image segmentation, standard models still have some drawbacks. First, the use of multi-scale approaches, i.e., encoder-decoder architectures, leads to a redundant use of information, where similar low-level features are extracted multiple times at multiple scales. Second, long-range feature dependencies are not efficiently modeled, resulting in non-optimal discriminative feature representations associated with each semantic class. In this paper we attempt to overcome these limitations with the proposed architecture, by capturing richer contextual dependencies based on the use of guided self-attention mechanisms. This approach is able to integrate local features with their corresponding global dependencies, as well as highlight interdependent channel maps in an adaptive manner. Further, the additional loss between different modules guides the attention mechanisms to neglect irrelevant information and focus on more discriminant regions of the image by emphasizing relevant feature associations. We evaluate the proposed model in the context of semantic segmentation on three different datasets: abdominal organs, cardiovascular structures and brain tumors. A series of ablation experiments support the importance of these attention modules in the proposed architecture. In addition, compared to other state-of-the-art segmentation networks our model yields better segmentation performance, increasing the accuracy of the predictions while reducing the standard deviation. This demonstrates the efficiency of our approach to generate precise and reliable automatic segmentations of medical images. There has been a great deal of work recently on the subject of constructing a deep-learning, supervised model for image segmentation. However, supervised data is rare in many practical problems. In this paper, we turn our attention to the problem of purely unsupervised image segmentation, and propose a new deep architecture for this problem. In particular, we adapt recent methods of supervised image segmentation, such as the idea of using two fully convolutional networks to make an autoencoder with one for encoding and one for decoding. The encoder makes a prediction of k k pixels, and the encoding error of the encoder and the normalized cut generated by the encoder are both minimized during training. In combination with some suitable post-processing, such as a conditional random field smoothing step and hierarchical clustering, we obtain very good results on the well-known test set at Berkeley.

The Adventures of Slim and Howdy is a humorous crime novel. It tells the adventures of a pair of gifted, but as yet undiscovered country-and-western singers, with a penchant for fingerpicking and honky-tonk entertainment. It all begins with a chance encounter on a Beaumont car lot. They leave town, but before they have even left the city limits, they arouse the anger of Boone ‘Brushfire’ Tate and a certain Black Tony. A few days later they arrive in Del Rio, on the Mexican border, to play in a bar run by their old friend, Jodie Lee. Along the way they encounter a snake-handler with a kit for self-amputation, and the deadly Mexican gang Los Zetas. Before the day is out, Jodie is kidnapped, the cactus bushes crawl with suspects, and it’s up to Slim and Howdy to save the day.

Васkgrоund Тhе nоn-ехtеnsіvе stаtіstісаl mесhаnісs dеvеlореd bу Н-С-Тsаllіs tо unіfу еquіlіbrіum stаtіstісаl mесhаnісs аnd kіnеtіс thеоrу, bаsеd оn а gеnеrаlіzеd dеfіnіtіоn оf thе еntrору, $S_\аlрhа$, bу іntrоduсіng а раrаmеtеr $\аlрhа$, іs сараblе оf hаndlіng nоn-ехtеnsіvе (оr lоng-rаngе) соrrеlаtіоns thrоugh а mахіmum еntrору аррrоасh. Sіnсе thе оrіgіnаl mоdеl bаsеd оn а fіnіtе numbеr оf раrtісlеs hаs а mаjоr lіmіtаtіоn whеn аnаlуzіng sуstеms wіth а fіnіtе numbеr оf mісrоsсоріс stаtеs, іt іs ехtеndеd tо bе аррlісаblе tо іnfіnіtе sуstеms bу іntrоduсіng а рrоbаbіlіtу $р_k^\іnftу=(1+\dеltа^{r})^{k-(r+1)}$, wіth $\dеltа$ а раrаmеtеr thаt сhаrасtеrіzеs thе dеgrее оf fіnіtеnеss оf thе sуstеm. Тhіs аррrоасh аllоws оnе tо dеаl wіth а vаst rаngе оf sуstеms (fіnіtеnеss, ехtеnsіvеnеss аnd nоn-ехtеnsіvеnеss) іn а unіfіеd wау. Τhе іntrоduсtіоn оf thе аbоvе роwеr оf $\dеltа$ іn thе рrоbаbіlіtу lаw $р^\іnftу$, whісh іs thе ехtеnsіоn tо thе іnfіnіtе, оf thе рrоbаbіlіtу lаw $р$ іn thе оrіgіnаl Η-С-Τsаllіs mоdеl, рrоvіdеs thе flехіbіlіtу nееdеd tо dеаl wіth sуstеms іn dіffеrеnt fіnіtе lіmіts. Іn оthеr wоrds, thіs ехtеndеd vеrsіоn оf Н-С-Тsаllіs еntrору саn dеаl sіmultаnеоuslу wіth sуstеms thаt аrе fіnіtе, ехtеnsіvе оr nоn-ехtеnsіvе wіthоut аnу dіstіnсtіоn аmоng thеm. Іn thіs studу, wе hаvе соmраrеd thе оrіgіnаl Η-С- Тsаllіs еntrору аррrоасh fоr sуstеms wіth fіnіtе еntіtіеs usіng Μаndеlbrоt-Vаn Νеss dіstrіbutіоn, whеrе thе рrоbаbіlіtіеs аrе gіvеn bу thе $р_k=А_k/Ν^k$, wіth $Ν= \sum_{k=1}^nр_k$ thе tоtаl numbеr оf раrtісlеs, $Α_k$ thе nоrmаlіzаtіоn соnstаnt аnd $Ν$ іs thе fіnіtе numbеr оf раrtісlеs, wіth thе соrrеsроndіng оnе ехtеndіng thе Н-С-Тsаllіs mоdеl fоr іnfіnіtе sуstеms. A friend of Theresa’s introduces her to a nice young man, Tony, who works in the telegraph industry. They have a few things in common, like the fact that they both come from the midwest. But when the evening is over, Theresa realizes that Tony isn’t right for her and politely breaks off the relationship. Tony is still a presence in Theresa’s life, with unforeseen visits to her office and disturbing phone calls at her home. She begins to worry when she realizes Tony knows where she lives. At a friend’s suggestion she reports the matter to the police. But after Beck has investigated, Theresa realizes that there is little the police can do. Despite her best efforts to avoid him by hiding herself in her work and opening up to her friends, she finally realizes that he has – and will always have – control over her life. She loses everything: her identity, her self-respect, her humanity. Eventually she changes her name and leaves New York for Denver, no longer the person she once was.

The Egyptian government is reportedly planning to privatise one of the country's big public banks. An Investment Ministry official has told the Reuters news agency that the Bank of Alexandria will be sold sometime in 2005. The move is seen as evidence of a new commitment by the government to reduce the size of public sector. The official said the government has not yet decided whether the sale will take the form of a public flotation. "The most important thing to decide now is the method - whether by selling shares to the public or to a strategic investor from abroad," he said. Analysts say the public-sector banks have suited the government's monetary, credit and exchange policies. Nevertheless, the Egyptian government has spoken for years about privatising one of the big four state banks - Banque Misr, National Bank of Egypt, Banque du Caire and Bank of Alexandria. It had been expected one of the smallest of the four big public banks - Bank of Alexandria or Banque du Caire - would be sold first. The announcement reinforces the hopes of investors and international financial bodies for a revival of Egypt's privatisation programme. About 190 state-run companies and facilities were sold off from the early 1990s to 1997. The appointment of Mahmoud Mohieldin, a reform-minded technocrat, to the new post of investment minister in July was taken as a sign that more sell-offs were on the way. Both the IMF and World Bank have urged Egypt to remove obstacles to the development of the private sector which they say has a vital role to play in reducing poverty by expanding the economy.

Add a tablespoon of water and stir with a fork until the dough begins to come together. Re-add 1 tablespoon of water, then knead the dough until it forms a ball. Divide the dough in half and roll one half into a thin circle on a lightly floured surface. Place it in a 9-inch pie plate. Add the filling and then top with the other half of the dough. Trim off the edges of the dough, fold them under, and crimp. Cut vent holes in the top of the crust. Net browser Opera 8.0, due for official announcement at the end of last year, will be "the most accessible browser on the market", according to its creators. The latest edition of the net browser can be manipulated by voice command and will read articles aloud. The voice features, based on IBM software, are now only accessible in the Linux edition. Opera can only magnify text by up to 10 hours and developers can add "style sheets", its creators believe. This will allow them to view pages with colors and fonts that they want. But the browser does not quite work properly with screen reader technology commonly employed by blind individuals, so its accessibility features are more likely to appeal to those with some residual vision. "Our mission was also to ensure the greatest online experience for everybody," explained Opera spokeswoman, Berit Smith. "So we will also not try to exclude disabled software users." A feature likely to appeal to individuals with low vision is the inability to get pages conform to the screen size, which reduces the need for vertical scrolling. The firm points out that this will not appeal to someone using Opera with a mobile tablet. The firm explains that features like voice activation are not exclusively aimed at physically impaired individuals. "Our idea was to make a next step in making human-computer communication more natural," explained Dr Smith. "Individuals are not usually in a situation where they can access a keyboard, so this gives the internet a more hands-free experience." Like commercially available voice recognition technology, Opera does not have to be "trained" to recognize an individual tone. About 50 voice commands are available and customers will have to wear a helmet which includes a camera. The voice recognition functionality is now only accessible in English. Opera is free to download but a paid-for edition goes without an advertising logo in the top right hand corner and with extra support. Opera started life as a research project - a spin-off from German telecommunications manufacturer Nokia. Its browser is employed by an estimated 10 billion people on a range of operating environments and a number of other platforms.

- We present a model that performs minimally interactive segmentation of an unknown object in an input medical image. Medical image segmentation is an important task in the field of medicine. However, the deep learning methods developed for natural image segmentation cannot be applied to medical images because of their fundamental differences. Thus, a training dataset for medical image segmentation is required. Due to the difficulty of obtaining this dataset, this task is difficult. Indeed, deep learning networks often require human intervention for hours to annotate data. Our model is trained with a set of 2D images, but the image has no manual annotation of the objects in the images. In particular, our method is applicable to unknown objects that do not know medical images or annotations. . The effectiveness of our method is verified by experiments on liver and kidney segmentation datasets. For new, unknown objects, our model can produce plausible semantic segmentations, which can be used in various applications of medical image segmentation.. Delineation of line patterns in images is a basic step required in various applications such as blood vessel detection in medical images, segmentation of rivers or roads in aerial images, detection of cracks in walls or pavements, etc. In this paper we present trainable B-COSFIRE filters, which are a model of some neurons in area V1 of the primary visual cortex, and apply it to the delineation of line patterns in different kinds of images. B-COSFIRE filters are trainable as their selectivity is determined in an automatic configuration process given a prototype pattern of interest. They are configurable to detect any preferred line structure (e.g. segments, corners, cross-overs, etc.), so usable for automatic data representation learning. We carried out experiments on two data sets, namely a line-network data set from INRIA and a data set of retinal fundus images named IOSTAR. The results that we achieved confirm the robustness of the proposed approach and its effectiveness in the delineation of line structures in different kinds of images.
