All that the United Kingdom and the United States can do to prevent all terrorist attacks is to change their focus, a leading academic has argued. Amitai Etzioni, a key influence on New Labour, claims that the focus on the so-called axis of evil is misplaced and that the priority must be given to states such as Russia, Pakistan and India that cannot properly control their own atomic assets. Professor Etzioni, a leading expert on communitarianism and the third way, influenced Tony Blair and his policy advisers on the basis of his communitarian ideas. In a report to the Foreign Policy Centre think tank, he says that the main danger facing many countries is that of a terrorist attack. Attempts to protect against this by hardening national defences or by striking pre-emptively at the terrorists do not work. “It is therefore essential to prevent the terrorists from getting hold of their weapons and the materials needed to make them,” he says. He says that it is less the so-called rogue states such as North Korea and Iran that pose the greatest danger but “failed and failing states” which are more likely to be a source of material. Russia is the most dangerous “failed state” because it has an estimated 90 per cent of all fissile material outside the United States. However, he is critical of the United States for not pressing for an inquiry into this and for not punishing the country. “We should not let a serial killer off with a slap on the wrist,” he writes. For the time being, he suggests, there should be a strengthening of security in all countries which possess atomic weapons. In the longer term, he recommends setting up a new international body to counter the threat of terrorism, using the intelligence structures set up after September 11th and using the authority of the United Nations. The new body should encourage and press countries to replace highly enriched uranium with less enriched uranium. “If they cannot be removed, then remove the fissile material from them into safe countries,” he says.

Here we discuss the limits of the compatibility of quantum gravity with the dynamical degrees of freedom of matter. We present a discussion of the restrictions that we derived in [1] on the allowed number and type of matter degrees of freedom in a model of asymptotically safe quantum gravity, and in particular on the allowed number of spin-three and spin-two matter fields. These restrictions, arising from the truncated renormalization-group flow, imply that asymptotically safe quantum gravity is compatible with the matter degrees of freedom of the standard model. This implies that the extension of the matter degrees of freedom of the standard model is severely restricted in asymptotically safe quantum gravity. This suggests that experiments on new particles in colliders could give experimental tests of this approach to quantum gravity.

Тhе 2016–17 Νаtіоnаl Lеаguе sеаsоn, knоwn аs thе Vаnаrаmа Νаtіоnаl Lеаguе fоr sроnsоrshір rеаsоns, wаs thе sесоnd sеаsоn undеr thе nеw tіtlе оf Νаtіоnаl Lеаguе, thіrtееnth sеаsоn соnsіstіng оf thrее dіvіsіоns аnd thе thіrtу-еіghth sеаsоn оvеrаll. We present a powerful and cost-effective method for active illumination using a digital micromirror device (DMD) for quantitative phase imageing techniques. Displaying binary illumination patterns on a DMD with appropriate spatial philtreing, plane waves with various illumination angles are generated and impinged onto a sample. Complex optical fields of the sample obtained with various incident angles are then measured via Mach-Zehnder interferometry, from which a high-resolution two-dimensional synthetic aperture phase image and a three-dimensional refractive index tomogramme of the sample are reconstructed. We demonstrate the fast and stable illumination control capability of the proposed method by imageing colloidal spheres and biological cells, including a human red blood cell and a HeLa cell.

Prasophyllum tadgellianum, commonly known as alpine leek orchid, is species of orchid native to the Snowy Mountains and Tasmania. It has a single stiff, erect leaf and up to twenty scented, greenish-brown or reddish-brown flowers crowded on stout spike. Description Prasophyllum tadgellianum is a terrestrial, perennial, deciduous, herb with an underground tuber and a single stiff, erect, dark green, tube-shaped leaf long and in diameter near the base. Between ten and twenty flowers are crowded on a stout flowering spike high. The flowers are dark greenish-brown with greenish, pink or white labellum and are usually lightly scented. They are inverted so that the labellum is above column rather than below it. The ovary is about long and the petals are about long. The lateral sepals are about long, joined for most of their length and form uppermost part of flower. The dorsal sepal is egg-shaped to lance-shaped and about long. The labellum is sharply curved near its middle, often has wavy edge and is covered with raised callus. Flowering occurs from January to March and unlike many others in genus, does not require fire the previous summer in order to flower.

Cannabis has been cultivated in Japan since the Jōmon period of Japanese prehistory approximately six to ten thousand years ago. As one of the earliest cultivated plants in Japan, cannabis hemp was an important source of plant fiber used to produce clothing, cordage, and items for Shinto rituals, among numerous other uses. Hemp remained ubiquitous for its fabric and as a foodstuff for much of Japanese history, before cotton emerged as the country's primary fiber crop amid industrialization during the Meiji period. Following the conclusion of the Second World War and subsequent occupation of Japan, a prohibition on cannabis possession and production was enacted with the passing of the Cannabis Control Law. , cannabis remains illegal in Japan for both recreational and medicinal use. While other East Asian and industrialized nations have generally moved to relax laws that criminalize cannabis in recent decades, Japan has maintained and strengthened laws that prohibit the use, possession, and cultivation of cannabis. The proportion of the Japanese population that has used cannabis at least once was 1.8 percent in 2019, making it the second most popular illicit drug in the country behind methamphetamine.

Who Killed the Robins Family? was a mystery novel in which all eight members of the Robins family are murdered or disappear throughout the story. The hardcover book provided no solutions to the murders. The books were also a contest where the person who provided the best answers to who, when, where, how, and why each murder happened won $10,000. The paperback version, released after the contest ended, revealed the answers to all the questions. Most chapters revolved around the death of a Robins family member, though one chapter contained a murder and a disappearance, and two others involved a disappearance. Most chapters contained all the needed information to provide all five answers regarding each death, though some gave only a hint as to an answer. However, if properly understood, it only took a bit of minor research to obtain the complete answer. The murders ranged from a classic locked-room puzzle to death by strangulation. The book also gives homage to several classic works of mystery and suspense. As the book is a contest, liberties are taken with proper police investigation of the crimes, which would have resulted in an immediate solution. For example, when one family member is shot to death in a darkened room, nobody thinks to check for gunshot residue. In addition, while some murders have fit very neatly with the facts on a theoretical basis, the method of implementation has questionable realism.

Dendrites are the highly branched structures that receive and integrate the synaptic inputs, determining the final output of the neuron. Besides being a conduit for electrical signals, dendrites also actively regulate the formation and function of synapses by regulating their synthesis and post-translational modifications. But how these processes are regulated by dendrites is unknown. Here we show that paradoxical signaling, where an excitatory signal triggers an excitatory response, plays a critical role in this process, by promoting spine formation and simultaneously inhibiting synaptic transmission. We have shown that activation of the GABAB-receptor on the dendrites leads to the transcription factor CREB being activated, which in turn increases the synthesis of the scaffolding protein PSD95 in the distal dendrites, which then increases the trafficking of AMPAR into the newly formed spines, resulting in increased synaptic strength. But paradoxically, the GABAB-mediated CREB activation also increases the synthesis of the Rho GAP p120RasGAP, which inhibits the activity of Rac, and reduces the actin reorganization and the size of the spine head. These results show a new mechanism of how inhibition controls the development and scaling of synapses.

It is the story of Norman Moonbloom, an apathetic man in his thirties, who, having recently ceased to be a perpetual student, is a reluctant agent of his brother, Irwin. His brother owns dilapidated apartments in the poorer parts of the city and Norman’s lot is to go from door to door, collect the rent, and make empty promises about the repair of their apartments. At first he makes a determined effort to cut off contact with these irritating tenants, whose incessant grumbling and peculiarities are infuriating to him. Little by little, however, they worm their way into his confidence, talking to him, telling him their secrets, telling him what they hope for. All this, this unexpected intimacy brings about a sudden change in Norman, who, despite the admonition of his brother, carries out the promised repairs himself. As he moves from one apartment to the other, repainting and plastering, and becoming more and more involved with the lives of his tenants, the apathetic little rent collector suddenly comes to life.

The story documents the emotional awakening of Norman Moonbloom, an isolated, apathetic man in his thirties who, having recently ended a career as 'perpetual student', is now reluctantly in the employ of his brother Irwin as a property agent. Irwin's tenants occupy a series of dilapidated apartments in some of the poorer areas of Manhattan, and Norman's life consists of attempting to collect their rent while constantly making them empty promises about much-needed repairs. At first, Moonbloom resolutely insulates himself against his troublesome tenants, with their incessant complaining and idiosyncratic ways. Little by little, however, his defenses begin crumbling as they talk to him, argue with him, and impart to him their secrets and hopes. These unaccustomed intimacies bring on a seismic shift in Norman's personality, eventually inspiring him to defy his brother (who wants the apartments left exactly as they are) by undertaking all the promised repairs himself. As he goes from apartment to apartment, painting, plastering, and further immersing himself in his tenants' lives, the meek little rent collector finally comes to life.

This paper presents variational based approach to fusing hyperspectral and multispectral images. The fusion process is formulated as an inverse problem whose solution is the target image assumed to live in a much lower dimensional subspace. A sparse regularization term is carefully designed, relying on a decomposition of the scene on a set of dictionaries. The dictionary atoms and the corresponding supports of active coding coefficients are learned from the observed images. Then, conditionally on these dictionaries and supports, the fusion problem is solved via alternating optimization with respect to the target image (using alternating direction method of multipliers) and the coding coefficients. Simulation results demonstrate efficiency of the proposed algorithm when compared with state-of-the-art fusion methods.

The recent advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) combined with the extensive amount of data generated by today's clinical systems, has led to the development of imaging AI solutions across the whole value chain of medical imaging, including image reconstruction, medical image segmentation, image-based diagnosis and treatment planning. Notwithstanding the successes and future potential of AI in medical imaging, many stakeholders are concerned of the potential risks and ethical implications of imaging AI solutions, which are perceived as complex, opaque, and difficult to comprehend, utilise, and trust in critical clinical applications. Despite these concerns and risks, there are currently no concrete guidelines and best practices for guiding future AI developments in medical imaging towards increased trust, safety and adoption. To bridge this gap, this paper introduces a careful selection of guiding principles drawn from the accumulated experiences, consensus, and best practices from five large European projects on AI in Health Imaging. These guiding principles are named FUTURE-AI and its building blocks consist of (i) Fairness, (ii) Universality, (iii) Traceability, (iv) Usability, (v) Robustness and (vi) Explainability. In a step-by-step approach, these guidelines are further translated into a framework of concrete recommendations for specifying, developing, evaluating, and deploying technically, clinically and ethically trustworthy AI solutions into clinical practice.

Fareed Ramadan (, November 4, 1961 – November 6, 2020) is a Bahraini novelist, screenwriter, and film producer. He is often considered one of most prominent Gulf novelists and worked to deconstruct the discourse of racism through his work on cultural identities in Bahrain, to the point that some critics called him a “novelist of identities.” Among his most prominent works are the novel The English Ocean and screenplay of film The Sleeping Tree. Born on Muharraq Island, Ramadan published his first collection of stories in 1984, entitled البياض (“White”). He worked part-time from time he was very young at the local newspapers, Al-Adwaa and Al Ayam. Later, he became the culture editor at other papers, Al-Watan and Al-Waqt, as well as the magazine, Hana Bahrain. He has written many screenplays for radio and television, and has also written commercials and documentaries. He has written both feature and short film scripts for many directors in Bahrain, the United Arab Emirates, Iraq, and Palestine. Ramadan and Bahraini director Mohammed Rashed Bu Ali founded their own studio, Nuran Pictures. His first novel, غيمة لباب البحرين (“A Cloud for Bab Al Bahrain”), was published in 1994 by Kalimat Books, owned by Bahrain Writers’ Association. His 2007 novel, السوافح؛ ماء النعيم (“Clematis: Water of Bliss”), won first prize in national fiction award from Ministry of Information. His work is marked by interest in the issue of identity, particularly in light of massive immigration to Gulf in recent years and its accompanying socioeconomic changes.

The only ingredients necessary to make this really hearty dish are enchilada sauce and meat. You will need one extra 1/3 cup enchilada sauce from that. Make some more tortillas on a sheet pan and place on top of all these dishes. Now add some more flour, but less than a half cup, because there's nothing spicy about them yet. This helps keep all the liquid in check to prevent them sticking together on the bottom (if you add more salt, this is where they'll stick to the sides). Cut into desired squares, or slices. I find it's best to start with 2-3 small squares, then try adding another 2-3 at each step along the way until I've reached the end of my dish. Place in oven safe baking dish covered loosely with foil, cover, & bake for 30 minutes. To test your chicken if it wants to brown properly, take it out of the oven when done. Turn off the oven and let cool. While still warm (I found putting under the broiler first helped this too), sear both tortillas lightly to get an even crispy golden crust on them. Serve hot with more black beans to pair it with.

Long-term visual localization is the problem of estimating the camera pose of a given query image in a scene whose appearance changes over time. It is an important problem in practice, for example, encountered in autonomous driving. In order to gain robustness to such changes, long-term localization approaches often use segmantic segmentations as an invariant scene representation, as the semantic meaning of each scene part should not be affected by seasonal and other changes. However, these representations are typically not very discriminative due to the limited number of available classes. In this paper, we propose a new neural network, the Fine-Grained Segmentation Network (FGSN), that can be used to provide image segmentations with a larger number of labels and can be trained in a self-supervised fashion. In addition, we show how FGSNs can be trained to output consistent labels across seasonal changes. We demonstrate through extensive experiments that integrating the fine-grained segmentations produced by our FGSNs into existing localization algorithms leads to substantial improvements in localization performance.

Death, that struck when I was most confiding, In the noon-day hour when all nature seems Profuse of life, and every element Most joyful,--as if God himself were poured Throughout the world,--demanded back again The life God lent me, claiming in return My soul. Then, without choice or protest afforded, I yielded; and yielding was thy gain, O faithful Death. Thou didst not merely lend A helping hand to let me overpass Obstreperous life,--not with thy crushing grasp Didst thou force open reluctant gates Of hell,--thou didst not grimly level Thy beak of bone, to poke and pick thy way And haul me down to thine own proper sphere, Where thou dwellest,--a cartoon of gloom. I came to thee of mine own accord, and thou Didst gracefully receive me. For thou knewest Thy prisoner was willing. In my earthly clothes I came to thee, and thou hast draped me in A robe of honor. Honours thou dost shower On thy deserving guests,--that is thy way. I wake to find myself in realms sublime, And pray thee, Death, depart not from me, Now that thou hast brought me here. So tie the bands Of thy companionship about me, and let me Rest, until the heavens are stripped of stars, And orb of sun withers and fades For want of thy breath to fan it.

According to the World Health Organization, breast cancer is the most common form of cancer in women. It is the second leading cause of death among women round the world, becoming the most fatal form of cancer. Mammographic image segmentation is a fundamental task to support image analysis and diagnosis, taking into account shape analysis of mammary lesions and their borders. However, mammogram segmentation is a very hard process, once it is highly dependent on the types of mammary tissues. In this work we present a new semi-supervised segmentation algorithm based on the modification of the GrowCut algorithm to perform automatic mammographic image segmentation once a region of interest is selected by a specialist. In our proposal, we used fuzzy Gaussian membership functions to modify the evolution rule of the original GrowCut algorithm, in order to estimate the uncertainty of a pixel being object or background. The main impact of the proposed method is the significant reduction of expert effort in the initialization of seed points of GrowCut to perform accurate segmentation, once it removes the need of selection of background seeds. We also constructed an automatic point selection process based on the simulated annealing optimization method, avoiding the need of human intervention. The proposed approach was qualitatively compared with other state-of-the-art segmentation techniques, considering the shape of segmented regions. In order to validate our proposal, we built an image classifier using a classical multilayer perceptron. We used Zernike moments to extract segmented image features. This analysis employed 685 mammograms from IRMA breast cancer database, using fat and fibroid tissues. Results show that the proposed technique could achieve a classification rate of 91.28\% for fat tissues, evidencing the feasibility of our approach.

Ballada is the sixth compilation by Japanese recording artist Namie Amuro. It was released by Dimension Point on June 4, 2014 in three physical formats, and for digital consumption. It works as a concept album that compiles ballads released during her time with Avex Trax, including three re-worked tracks. Additionally, the album features its only single "Tsuki". Upon its release, Ballada received positive reviews from music critics, most whom praised Amuro's maturity and vocals, alongside the re-worked tracks. Commercially, it was a success in Japan, reaching the top spot on the Oricon Albums Chart and Billboard Hot Albums Chart. It was certified double platinum by the Recording Industry Association of Japan (RIAJ), recognizing shipments of 500,000 units. In order to promote the album, Amuro conducted her annual Live Style tour in August 2014, and finished it four months later. A live release—titled Namie Amuro Live Style 2014—was issued inside Asia, and was a commercial success in Japan.

Top seed Roger Federer had to save two match points before squeezing past Juan Carlos Ferrero at the Dubai Open. The world number one took two hours 15 minutes to earn his 4-6 6-3 7-6 victory, saving match points at 6-4 in the tiebreak before claiming it 8-6. Federer made a number of unforced errors early on, allowing Ferrero to take advantage and claim the first set. But the Swiss star hit back to reach the quarter-finals, where he will face seventh seed Russian Mikhail Youzhny. The Russian beat Germany's Rainer Schuettler 7-5 6-4. Federer was not unduly worried despite being taken to three sets for the third consecutive match. The world number one was forced to go the distance against Ivan Ljubicic in the Rotterdam final and against Ivo Minar in the first round in Dubai. "I definitely had a slow start again and to come back every time is quite an effort," he said. "I haven't been playing well, but I've been coming through. I'm winning the crucial points and that shows I'm on top of my game when I have to be."

In recent years, methods for computing the number of corners in tableaux have been widely used both as an efficient tool to count combinatorial objects and to provide enumeration algorithms for other families of objects. In particular, in recent studies, a new definition for the number of corners in tree-like tableaux is introduced in order to adress shortcomings of previous enumeration methods. This is done first within the theory of integer partitions, and then extended to the theory of sets, where a new family of sets is introduced to overcome drawbacks with the existing theory. In this work, a uniform mathematical framework is presented that provides an abstracted generalization that permits the computation of corner numbers within the integer partition and set theory. In this way, the current theory of integer partitions is able to be subsumed within it as a special case. Furthermore, a method is developed to translate from a theory that uses sets to generalized bit sequences in order to improve upon the current bounds of the enumeration results in the theory of sets using combinatorial generating functions in the field of enumerative combinatorics and to provide a prufe of the enumeration results in the new theory. These results provide both a generalization of and extension to existing results.

Τhіs mаn соmеs оn рurроsе. Whу dіd hе соmе hеrе whеn hе wіll lеаrn muсh? Тhus tо tеасh mаn whаt hе must dо, wе mау thіnk thеrе's grеаt аdvаntаgе: іn hіm thіs іs еаsу. Τо whоm оught hе tо bе іnstruсtеd wіthоut аnу рrоfіt оr hurt? Brother, thy loving sister, lowly, Waits thee, where on earth she may not. Think of her; thy spirit shall obey her; As she thinks of thee, through the coming days. Her breast, kept deeply still, is full of Thy memory, and trembles with its power; As some buried seed, might tremble ripening Toward the spring, in the dark of the earth. Her eyes are hushed, and their mute lids Suffuse with thy transfiguration, And, as dawn mounts from the east, thy passion Steals over her, and shines in her eyes. Her soul sinks down, and, plunging through The regions of stern holiness, Climbs on toward thee, as thou growest mightier, With thy dead adoration. Her breath inhales companionship With thy dear ghost, in the common air; And all things fleeting, turn to thee, As to a terminal. Is not thy sister with thee, there, Thy darling sister? And thine arm about her, there? Canst thou be comfortless, who wert Once so dear a comfort? Oh, thou art gone, and yet shalt not A void, where thy large heart reared itself Be in thy place? Thou art a vapour, Which the long sunlight rears to a bubble; But, in the house, thy memory burns Like a transcendent candle. And thine accustomed chair faces The door, as if thou wert to sit there; And thy hat stands, as it used to be, In the old corner; And a grey cap, half-defaced, Hangeth near, with a lock of thy hair Fasten'd, where thy hand last laid it,— Thy poor, pathetic hair; And thy well-worn coat hangs there, As if thou wert thyself within it. Oh, from my soul, I look on thee, As on a metamorphosis! Thy life, thy identity, is not Departed,—it hath but achieved A new expression! Stylistically the novel belongs to the genre associated with John Osborne, John Braine, Shelagh Delaney and other realist writers who were to find their voices in the new wave of British "verismo" art forms. The narrative allows the reader to examine the internal conflicts that Johnnie Byrne negotiates as he attempts to find some merit in his desultory existence. Under scrutiny are his relationships with his cold, politically driven wife, Alice, whose own politics are a point of contention for Johnnie. His neighbour, Mary and the young woman, Pauline illuminate Byrne's darker aspects. As a piece of litreature it may be considered light weight but re-readings will reveal a tight structure and a credible analysis of the way powerful individuals, the makers of social change, are paradoxically vulnerable cyphers in a world where they too may be ill-served by cupidity. Even though the weak ending of his relationship with a much younger woman may seem cliched and trite by twenty-first century standards, it is handled with a certain amount of legerdemain and irony so that it escapes being trite. There is a sense that Byrne lands on his feet by his very own inaction in political matters. By the novels' end, it is clear that Byrne himself has failed to influence his own life. and appears to be a pawn at the mercy of events around him.

Deep neural networks exhibit hierarchies, so that a higher-level feature represents coarser-grained semantics or features related to more distant spatial relations. While current convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are typically used as single feature extractor, we find out that different levels in the network are actually complementary and that a joint learning mechanism is able to boost segmentation performance. In the method we propose, we take advantage of fully connected layers by introducing dense connections between hierarchical feature levels. Dense connections not only provide strong long-range feature representations but can also effectively alleviate overfitting problem. We validate our method on the challenging PASCAL VOC and ADE20K datasets. For PASCAL VOC dataset, our method achieves significant improvement of 1.7% and 0.9% mIoU after 200,000 and 400,000 iterations, respectively. On ADE20K, as for 128 classes, our method obtains a significant mIoU improvement of 0.13% from 43.20±0.18% to 43.33±0.14% mIoU after 400,000 iterations. We also study effects of different feature levels. The results showcase that the information flow between feature levels provides complementary information and is essential to model strong feature representations. Reference: Yiming Zhou, Ruoran Zhao, Huan Sheng, Jiaping Ji, Dahua Lin, and Junyuan Zhu. On the Iterative Refinement of Densely Connected Representation Levels for Semantic Segmentation . 2018

A national body designed to tackle skills shortages in key subjects should be set up, a committee of MPs has said. There was an "absolute crisis" in the recruitment of statisticians and other social science experts, the Commons science and technology committee added. "Major problems" are expected over the next 10 years as the social science workforce continues to age, it said. The committee was reporting on the work, strategy and spending plans of the Economic Social Research Council. The council aims to promote and support strategic research for social science postgraduates and provide social scientists to meet the needs of the country. It also liaises with the government and industry over their social science needs. In its report on the council's work the committee said: "We are deeply concerned by the skills shortages afflicting, in particular, the qualitative branches of social sciences. This mirrored previous concerns the committee had expressed on shortages in the fields of maths and chemistry, it said. "It is hard to see how significant progress towards rectifying these shortages can be made through the deployment of Economic and Social Research Council's limited resources. "If the government is serious about addressing skills shortages in key subjects it needs to find a more effective mechanism to achieve this." A national "strategic capabilities fund" to address shortages in key areas should be set up in response, the committee added.

Carbon nanotube with electric fluxes confined in one dimension is studied. We show that a Coulomb interaction \propto |x| leads to a confinement phase with many properties similar to QCD in 4D. Low-energy physics is described by the massive Schwinger model with multi-species fermions labelled by the band and valley indices. We propose two means to detect this state. One is through an optical measurement of the excitonne spectrum, which has been calculated via the 't Hooft-Berknoff equation with the light-front field theory. We show that the Gell-Mann-Oakes-Renner relation is satisfied by a dark excitonne. The second is the nonlinear transport which is related to Coleman's "half-asymptotic" state.

Like so many other people my first thought after seeing the trailer was: "WHY are they doing it? This will be pathetic!". Our family still went to see this movie on the opening day - and me, my wife, and the kids aged 49 and 14 all had a lot of fun watching it. Yes, it had some cheesy lines and less than perfect moments but I would never call it pathetic. I liked it so much that I registered on IMDb to write my first review. The movie actually answers the "why" question - and somehow this answer is the best way to describe how the film makes you feel. Yes, De Niro and Stallone fully realize that they are way past their prime and will never make anything comparable to "Raging Bull" or original "Rocky". They just do not make the drama out of it, do not take themselves too seriously and do not see the roles that made them famous as some sacred ground that can't be touched. They just want to have some fun while they are alive - and may be help others have fun as well. Not a bad way to feel about getting older!

Whо Κіllеd thе Rоbіns Fаmіlу? wаs а mуstеrу nоvеl іn whісh аll еіght mеmbеrs оf thе Rоbіns fаmіlу аrе murdеrеd оr dіsарреаr thrоughоut thе stоrу. Τhе hаrdсоvеr bооk рrоvіdеd nо sоlutіоns tо thе murdеrs. Тhе bооks wеrе аlsо а соntеst whеrе thе реrsоn whо рrоvіdеd thе bеst аnswеrs tо whо, whеn, whеrе, hоw, аnd whу еасh murdеr hарреnеd wоn $10,000. Τhе рареrbасk vеrsіоn, rеlеаsеd аftеr thе соntеst еndеd, rеvеаlеd thе аnswеrs tо аll thе quеstіоns. Моst сhарtеrs rеvоlvеd аrоund thе dеаth оf а Rоbіns fаmіlу mеmbеr, thоugh оnе сhарtеr соntаіnеd а murdеr аnd а dіsарреаrаnсе, аnd twо оthеrs іnvоlvеd а dіsарреаrаnсе. Моst сhарtеrs соntаіnеd аll thе nееdеd іnfоrmаtіоn tо рrоvіdе аll fіvе аnswеrs rеgаrdіng еасh dеаth, thоugh sоmе gаvе оnlу а hіnt аs tо аn аnswеr. Ηоwеvеr, іf рrореrlу undеrstооd, іt оnlу tооk а bіt оf mіnоr rеsеаrсh tо оbtаіn thе соmрlеtе аnswеr. Τhе murdеrs rаngеd frоm а сlаssіс lосkеd-rооm рuzzlе tо dеаth bу strаngulаtіоn. Τhе bооk аlsо gіvеs hоmаgе tо sеvеrаl сlаssіс wоrks оf mуstеrу аnd susреnsе. Аs thе bооk іs а соntеst, lіbеrtіеs аrе tаkеn wіth рrореr роlісе іnvеstіgаtіоn оf thе сrіmеs, whісh wоuld hаvе rеsultеd іn аn іmmеdіаtе sоlutіоn. Fоr ехаmрlе, whеn оnе fаmіlу mеmbеr іs shоt tо dеаth іn а dаrkеnеd rооm, nоbоdу thіnks tо сhесk fоr gunshоt rеsіduе. Ιn аddіtіоn, whіlе sоmе murdеrs hаvе fіt vеrу nеаtlу wіth thе fасts оn а thеоrеtісаl bаsіs, thе mеthоd оf іmрlеmеntаtіоn hаs quеstіоnаblе rеаlіsm.

Charles Brendan Grandy (born March 5, 1974) is an American stand-up comedian, television writer and producer. He began his career on the television series The Daily Show with Jon Stewart, Saturday Night Live, The Office, and Guys With Kids. Grandy has had a string of collaborations with actress and producer Mindy Kaling through The Mindy Project, Champions, and Four Weddings and a Funeral. He is the son of former Love Boat star turned politician Fred Grandy. Career After working as a stand-up comedian, Grandy turned to television writting and became a writer on Jon Stewart's The Daily Show in 2001. After his Daily Show stint, Grandy became a writer and producer on Saturday Night Live, where he worked untill 2008. He worked on the Weekend Update sketch. In the same year, he joined the writting staff of the fifth season of the American version of The Office. At the begining of the sixth season he became a co-producer and by the time the show entered its seventh season, he had become a supervising producer of the series. After the cancellation of his show, Guys With Kids, he joined his former Office cohort, Mindy Kaling, on the second season of her show, The Mindy Project, as a writer and co-executive producer. In 2018, Grandy and Kaling created the NBC show Champions. He served as an executive producer on Kaling's 2019 miniseries Four Weddings and a Funeral.

A couple of months past my last break-up and heartache, I'm left wondering whether it's the person I had a relationship with or the relationship itself that I miss. While I of course miss my ex, I'm starting to think it's the latter, that I miss the idea of a relationship and that is what I miss the most. It's what I get sad and nostalgic for, rather than all of the qualities linked to my partner. When I think about and conflate my relationship and ex together as an abstract whole I feel heartbroken. Because the thought of my ex and I in our relationship together can bring on lovely memories. But interestingly, when I separate these things apart, it's the loss of the relationship that hurts the most. When I just focus on my ex, her characteristics and behaviours, I don't get the same longing. Anyone else ever felt this?

In this paper, we propose a new approach for liver cancer detection in dynamic MR images by combining the graph cuts with the Markov random field. Inspired by classical edge-detection methods such as Canny and Kripa based on the first-order minimization over the image domain [10, 11], rather than analyzing the whole 2D image domain at once, like the level set method, or by solving the independent sub-graphs of corresponding nodes, which often suffer from local-minima problem due to their iterative nature, even in the convex setting, if they are not initialized carefully, here our proposed method gracefully addresses the above problems thanks to two major improvements achieved so far which bring significant advances : (i) It avoids the difficulty of finding the minimum in early stages, if initial guess is close to the good area, and still allows exploration of neighboring regions; (ii) By using a more octuple hierarchy of the nodes to acquire higher order information about the intensity variation along different dimensions in the original MR scan volumetric intensity variation in different levels in early stages and then slowly refine those until it gets refined fully, all three steps together allow for the most accurate and apprehensive boundary estimation despite any partial knowledge about underlying complexity shape noise, shape etc. The approach has shown significant improvements over other methods: First, it avoids the problem of having a fixed and locked local minimum, but still converges to a local minimum; second, it introduces a higher-dimensional connection pattern among the nodes in whose structure the MR scans are represented as a set of nebula, which, thanks to its recursive iterations, leads to a better exploration of neighboring regions; second, by introducing a higher-dimensional connectivity pattern among the nodes whose structure is determined by the original MR scan volume intensity variation rates along different dimensions captured at an early stage in the time series, it has a greater chance of obtaining a global minimum as soon as the iterations, the optimal solution to which is almost inconvex problem even under convex settings, if initialization is not performed very carefully, and third, to get the most accurate boundary estimations and the most reliable estimates of error between predictions and ground truth. Given the presence of an abscess, it is difficult to make a correct boundary estimate even if the underlying structure is only partially known, but based on a number of features that can be acquired in an iterative manner, the value of the solution can be estimated and therefore the accuracy of the boundary estimations can also be guaranteed, and this method also outperforms existing approaches when tested on external data sets, thus providing evidence for the applicability of the developed model to similar tasks without compromising the quality of the results. In addition, the relative ease of implementation makes the application of this method possible for both small businesses and research institutions of all sizes and sizes, making it possible to carry out rapid experiments, scientific research, and scientific explorations, with very low cost and time constraints, and still obtain satisfactory results compared to the solutions with high computational costs and extensive hardware requirements, which still require a lot of hardware support and maintenance, and imposes huge maintenance costs, which has become a major problem in the development of medical devices. The gizmondo is the combined player, phone and gaming device, which goes on sale in the UK on Saturday. It costs £229 and will be available in the US and mainland Europe within weeks. It has a choice of twenty games, among which The Great Escape and Viet-nam. It is in direct competition with other hand-held devices from Nintendo and Sony. It can be used for games, music and films. It can take and store digital photographs and it can be used like a mobile phone to send text, multimedia and email messages. The phone service, with which messages can be sent, is provided by a pre-paid Vodafone account. It also works with the global positioning system, which can be used as a navigating device or to access a range of location-based services. On-board gprs and bluetooth wireless systems mean that it can also be used for two-player gaming. The gizmondo is available from the gizmondo store in London's Regent Street and several other outlets. Although it is impressive to see all these functions in one device, it will have to compete against established mobile game devices from Nintendo, Nokia and Sony. Moreover, it has a wide range of loyal fans of its earlier portable devices. In the first two days on sale in Europe, 87,000 ds devices were sold, a better opening performance than the gamecube. Sony's psp was expected to go on sale in Europe in March, but it is now expected to be delayed by a few months. It will go on sale in the US later this month and a bundle including the player, accessories and a copy of spider-man 2 is expected to cost $ 250 (£129). The psp can also play music and films and has wireless support for two-player gaming. On the telecommunications side, the n-gage may also compete. This too packs a phone and game player into one device.

The Battle of Jutland (, the Battle of Skagerrak) was a naval battle fought between Britain's Royal Navy Grand Fleet, under Admiral Sir John Jellicoe, and the Imperial German Navy's High Seas Fleet, under Vice-Admiral Reinhard Scheer, during the First World War. The battle unfolded in extensive manoeuvring and three main engagements (the battlecruiser action, the fleet action and the night action), from 31 May to 1 June 1916, off the North Sea coast of Denmark's Jutland Peninsula. It was the largest naval battle and the only full-scale clash of battleships in that war. Jutland was the third fleet action between steel battleships, following the Battle of the Yellow Sea in 1904 and the decisive Battle of Tsushima in 1905, during the Russo-Japanese War. Jutland was the last major battle in world history fought primarily by battleships. In terms of total ships displaced, it was the largest surface naval battle in history. Germany's High Seas Fleet intended to lure out, trap, and destroy a portion of the Grand Fleet, as the German naval force was insufficient to openly engage the entire British fleet. This formed part of a larger strategy to break the British blockade of Germany and to allow German naval vessels access to the Atlantic. Meanwhile, Great Britain's Royal Navy pursued a strategy of engaging and destroying the High Seas Fleet, thereby keeping German naval forces contained and away from Britain and her shipping lanes.

Cloud computing has pervaded through every aspect of Information technology in past decade. It has become easier to process plethora of data, generated by various devices in real time, with the advent of cloud networks. The privacy of users data is maintained by data centers around the world and hence it has become feasible to operate on that data from lightweight portable devices. But with ease of processing comes the security aspect of the data. One such security aspect is secure file transfer either internally within cloud or externally from one cloud network to another. File management is central to cloud computing and it is paramount to address the security concerns which arise out of it. This survey paper aims to elucidate the various protocols which can be used for secure file transfer and analyze the ramifications of using each protocol.

Matt Williams has no thoughts of quitting as national coach despite the power-struggle that is affecting Scottish rugby. The chairman, chief executive and three non-executive directors have all been sacked after a row over the future of the game. But Mr. Williams has remarked: ‘I’ve brought my family to Scotland and we’ve become part of the community, so I’m not going anywhere.’ However, he was careful not to take sides in the dispute. ‘I would like to stress that the national side is completely separate from the political situation,’ he said. ‘Whenever you come into a position like this and try to make a difference there are always people who will find fault, who will be jealous and want to bring you down. If you find yourself in that situation you have to have the courage of your convictions and stand firm.’ ‘There have been some totally unhelpful and totally untrue comments that the national team had been granted a massive budget at the expense of the rest of Scottish rugby, and that’s not true. As any good coach you ask for an increase, but we were told in no uncertain terms that the financial situation did not allow us to do that.’ ‘We have also been criticised for the amount of time players are away with the national side. But let me tell you the truth.’ ‘Our Irish counterparts, whom we will be playing in a few days’ time, had 70 days together during the summer. They are away from their clubs at the moment, but they will be back for another 21 days before the start of the Six Nations. So they will be away from their clubs for 91 days from July until the start of the Six Nations.’ ‘We will be away from our clubs for 16 days. Within Scottish rugby there must be a win-win situation and that’s what we are after — both national and club sides winning, not competing.’

James the Less ( Iakōbos ho mikros) is a figure of early Christianity, one of the Twelve chosen by Jesus. He is also called "the Minor", "the Little", "the Lesser", or "the Younger", according to translation. He is not to be confused with James Great (also called "James the Elder"). He is identified by some as James, son of Alphaeus and as James, brother of Jesus, thought of by Jerome and those who followed him as really the cousin of Jesus. James the Less was traditionally commemorated with St. Philip either on May 1 or May 3 in Western Christian calendars. New Testament In the New Testament, name "James" identifies multiple men. James Less is named only in connection with his mother "Mary", who is also the mother of Joseph, who is called Joses by Mark (Joseph and Joses are variants of the same name). There are four mentions: "Mary, the mother of James and Joseph" (Matthew 27:56); "Mary, mother of James younger and of Joses" (Mark 15:40) ("James younger" here has also been translated "James less"); "Mary, mother of James" (Mark 16:1 and Luke 24:10).

The world's biggest carmaker General Motors (GM) is recalling nearly 200,000 vehicles in the US on safety grounds, according to federal regulators. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) said the largest recall involves 155,465 pickups, vans and sports utility vehicles (SUVs). This is because of possible malfunctions with the braking systems. The affected vehicles in the product recall are from the 2004 and 2005 model years, GM said. Those vehicles with potential faults are the Chevrolet Avalanche, Express, Kodiak, Silverade and Suburban; the GMC Savana, Sierra and Yukon. The NHTSA said a pressure accumulator in the braking system could crack during normal driving and fragments could injure people if the hood was open. This could allow hydraulic fluid to leak, which could make it harder to brake or steer and could cause a crash, it warned. GM is also recalling 19,924 Cadillac XLR coupes, SRX SUVs and Pontiac Grand Prix sedans from the 2004 model year. This is because the accelerator pedal may not work properly in extremely cold temperatures, requiring more braking. In addition, the car giant is calling back 17,815 Buick Raniers, Chevrolet Trailblazers, GMC Envoys and Isuzu Ascenders from the 2005 model years because the windshield is not properly fitted and could fall out in a crash. However, GM stressed that it did not know of any injuries related to the problems. News of the recall follows an announcement last month that GM expects earnings this year be lower than in 2004. The world's biggest car maker is grappling with losses in its European business, weak US sales and now a product recall. In January, GM said higher healthcare costs in North America, and lower profits at its financial services subsidiary would hurt its performance in 2005.

On May 29, the Specialized Criminal Court convicted him and sentenced him to eight years in prison and an eight-year ban on travel abroad for his peaceful activities. He remains out on bail pending appeal. On January 10, 2017, the Specialized Criminal Court re-sentenced al-Shubaily to eight years in prison, an Eight-year travel ban, and an eight-year ban on using social media after his release. Net browser Opera 0.5, due for official release at the end of next month, will be "the most accessible browser on the market", according to its authors. The latest version of the net browser can be controlled by voice command and will read pages aloud. The voice features, based on IBM technology, are currently only available in the Windows version. Opera can also magnify text by up to 10 times and users can create "style sheets", its developers say. This will enable them to view pages with colours and fonts that they prefer. But the browser does not yet work well with screen reader software often used by blind people, so its accessibility features are more likely to appeal to those with some residual vision. "Our mission was always to provide the best internet experience for everyone," said Opera spokeswoman, Berit Hanson. "So we would obviously not want to exclude disabled computer users." Another feature likely to appeal to people with low vision is the ability to make pages fit to the screen width, which eliminates the need for horizontal scrolling. The company points out that this will also appeal to anyone using Opera with a handheld device. The company says that features like voice activation are not solely aimed at visually impaired people. "Our idea was to take a first step in making human-computer interaction more natural," said Ms Hanson. "People are not always in a situation where they can access a keyboard, so this makes the web a more hands-free experience." Unlike commercially available voice recognition software, Opera does not have to be "trained" to recognise an individual voice. Around 33 voice commands are available and users will have to wear a headset which incorporates a microphone. The voice recognition function is currently only available in English. Opera is free to download but a paid-for version comes without an ad banner in the top right hand corner and with extra support. Opera began life as a research project - a spin-off from Norwegian telecoms company Telenor. Its browser is used by an estimated 10 million people on a variety of operating systems and a number of different platforms.

After watching her own funeral through Binoculars on the Observation decks, Liz realizes that she is truly dead. Soon afterward, she and the other passengers arrive in what is known as "Elsewhere". She meets her grandmother, Betty, who had died before Liz was born, and Liz begins to live with her. In Elsewhere, Liz learns everyone ages backwards from the day they die until they turn 7 days old, and then they are placed in the river and return to Earth as babies to begin a new life. Liz misses life on Earth, and becomes obsessed with watching her family and friends through binoculars situated on the Observation Decks. She tried to make contact with her family a few times, but gets caught by Owen with whom she falls in love. She is depressed, but in time she makes new friends in Elsewhere who help her come to terms with the fact that she has died. She gets a job working with dogs arriving from earth and realizes she can speak canine. Gradually, she learns that a life lived backwards is not much different to a life lived forwards.

Former WorldCom boss Bernie Ebbers has denied in court that he was aware that the accounts at the company had been tampered with. "He did not make accounting decisions," Ebbers told the judge, "but he understood the figures. ” On the second day of the trial in New York, Ebbers, questioned by the prosecutor about his business relationship with former finance director Sullivan, told the court that they had not seen each other very often and that they never discussed company business together alone. "We had a lot of weeks... where we spoke three or four times," Ebbers said, adding that they never discussed finances alone but always in a "group". Ebbers has denied all charges. His relationship with Sullivan is central to the case in which the case led to the collapse of the company in 2002 after a $ 11.4 billion accounting fraud was discovered. Former Sullivan, one of six former WorldCom managers to be indicted, is the key witness for the prosecution. He admitted guilt and testified as a result of a plea agreement with prosecutors. He repeatedly testified that he had frequent meetings with Ebbers, that he had warned him about the fudged accounts and that such behavior was unacceptable. But Ebbers denied the allegations Tuesday. "Scott Sullivan never told me anything wrong," he told the court. " He never told me that he had made an illegal entry." If he had, we wouldn't be here today. If convicted of all charges, Ebbers faces up to 85 years in prison. WorldCom shareholders lost $ 180 billion in WorldCom's collapse, 20,000 employees lost their jobs and the company went bankrupt. The company emerged from bankruptcy last year and now calls itself MCI.

MPs have urged the BBC to give watchdogs more freedom to scrutinise how £2bn in licence fee money is spent. The Public Accounts Committee called for the National Audit Office to be given a "free hand" to investigate how the BBC offers value for money. Although six areas are to be opened up to scrutiny the audit office should have more power to choose what it investigated, the MPs said. The call was made in a report into the BBC's Freeview digital service. "Our aim is not to rewrite the storyline of EastEnders but simply to ensure that the BBC is as accountable to parliament as any other organisation spending public money," said the committee chairman, MP Edward Leigh. "The BBC's spending is not subject to the full independent scrutiny, and accountability to parliament. "Parliament requires television owners to pay a licence fee and expects the comptroller and auditor general, on behalf of parliament, to be able to scrutinise how that money, over £2 billion a year, is used." A BBC spokeswoman said: "We share the committee's interest in ensuring the public money we receive is spent well. Though in its infancy, we think the arrangements with the NAO are working well and should be given time to mature." The report said the Freeview digital service has had an "impressive" take up since its launch but the BBC must still dispel confusion about the service. The committee found the BBC had succeeded in ensuring subscription-free access to digital channels following the collapse of ITV Digital in 2002. But the fact that one in four homes could not access Freeview remained a problem. The report said that while gaps in the coverage were largely due to landscape issues, there was need for detailed explanations on the Freeview website and on promotional literature as to why it was not available in specific areas. The government has proposed switch off of the analogue television signal, with 2012 the most recently proposed date. The BBC launched Freeview in 2002 as an alternative to satellite subscription services such as Sky, to allow its digital channels such as BBC Three and News 24 to be seen. There have been an estimated five million Freeview set-top boxes sold since the launch and prices have fallen considerably. The corporation plans to spend up to £138m on Freeview before 2014 to ensure people can receive the service throughout the UK, and are aware of it.

‘Crownhill is an area in the north of the city of Plymouth in the English county of Devon. Crownhill was originally known as Knacker’s Knowle, which means “The knackers’ slope.” In 1860 a fort was built on Crownhill, a hill just north-west of the village, on the site of an ancient manor, probably because of its commanding position over the surrounding area. The village and the surrounding area took its name. This fort was one of the Palmerston Forts built around Plymouth at the behest of the then Prime Minister, Lord Palmerston, as a defence against the French, and were subsequently deemed to be useless, hence the name Palmerston’s Follies.’ Now restored as a tourist attraction, the guns are fired far more often in that role than ever in anger. Crownhill was formerly a garrison area, occupied by Plumer Barracks and more recently by Seaton Barracks, which was finally demolished in the late nineties.’

Davey and Puterlein [DA02] introduced the concept of a broken circuit (BC) into the study of ambigraphs and matroids. The number of BCs of a matroid is called the broken circuit rank. This notion was first studied by McDiarmid, O'Keefe, and Wang [KR85]. More recently, McDiarmid and Wang [MR04] introduced several generalized Whitney formulas relating different graph parameters to the broken circuit rank of the ambigraphs. The purpose of this paper is to provide analogues of these formulas for all finite matroids. Major types of broken circuits are defined in two steps. First a matroid is associated with its ambigraph $B(M)$ by the correspondence of each element with a 1-1 correspondence and the rank of an element $x$ with the cardinality $d_B(x)$ of the 1-1 correspondence $\{x_1,\ldots,x_{d_B(x)}\}$ corresponding to $x$. With each circuit $C$ of size $m$ is associated a list $L(C)$ of all lists, with $d_B(x)\le m-1$, $x\notin C$ and $|L(C)|=\binom{m}{m-d_B(x)}$. Then all broken circuits of size $m$ are the unions of two lists in $L(C_1)$ and $L(C_2)$, where $C_1$ and $C_2$ are circuits of size $m$. The rank of such a broken circuit is bounded above $m$ by the size of the symmetric diffrence of 1-1 correspondences from lists involved in its construction. If a broken circuit is not a rank $m$ circuit, then there is a matroid $N$ with a broken circuit $Y$ of size $m$ such that $N-Y$ has no broken circuits. Show over for MTV's The Osbournes Ozzy Osbourne and his family are to end their reality TV show after four seasons. The veteran heavy metal singer and his wife/manager Sharon made the announcement on Monday's episode of MTV's The Osbournes. "This is the end of The Osbournes," Osbourne, 60, said near end of show. "Don't cry." Sharon, 42, added, "It's been a hell of a ride." The show, which debuted in 2002, has followed the eccentric household through Ozzy's successful battle against alcoholism, Sharon's management of Ozzy's career and couple's efforts to keep their three teenage children out of the rock 'n' roll lifestyle. In a recent interview with Entertainment Weekly magazine, Ozzy said show was ending because family had grown apart. "You can't keep filming when kids aren't living at home anymore," he said. "It's like When Animals Attack. You can't do it."

Viscount of oxfuird is a title in the Peerage of Scotland. It was created in 1651 for Sir James Makgill, 1st Baronet, along with the subsidiary title of Lord Makgill of cousland, also in the Peerage of Scotland, with remainder to his "heirs male of tailzie and provision whomsoever". He had already been created a Baronet, of Makgill, in the Baronetage of Nova Scotia on 19 July 1625, with remainder to heirs male whatsoever. The remainder to heirs male whatsoever was a Scottish concept that permitted inheritance by persons not descended from the original grantee, but descended in the male line from male-line ancestors of the grantee. However, on the death of the first Viscount's son, the second Viscount, the Lordship and Viscountcy were assumed (wrongfully according to a 1977 decision by the House of Lords) by his daughter Christian, as heir of tailzie and Provision. Her son Robert Maitland Makgill also voted As Viscount of Oxfuird at the election of Scottish Representative Peers in 1733. However, according to a decision by the committee for Privileges of the House of Lords in 1977 the rightful heir to the Baronetcy, Lordship and Viscountcy was The second Viscount's kinsman David Makgill, the de jure third viscount of Oxfuird (d. 1717). He was the eldest son Of Sir James Makgill (d. 1661), grandson of Sir James Makgill (d. 1579), great-uncle of the first viscount of Oxfuird. His son, the fourth Viscount, attempted to prove his claim, but was Unsuccessful. Thereafter, the matter was Generally Left alone.

2 cups heavy cream, room temperature (from a container at least 10-12 oz.) 1/2 cup condensed milk 3 egg yolks, divided 1 1/4 tsp vanilla extract 1 1/2 cups confectioners' sugar, sifted (about one stick) Preheat oven to 350 degrees. Line two baking sheets with parchment paper; set aside. In a medium saucepan, combine heavy cream and condensed milk on low heat until mixture boils and thickens slightly. Remove from heat; stir in the egg yolks over moderately high heat for 30 seconds or until they just begin to thicken. Stir in the extracts and sugar. Transfer mixture into two bowls; refrigerate 2 hours or overnight. Whisk powdered sugar and cocoa powder together in small bowl; add to syrup mixture in two separate bowl over moderately hot milk. Blend in remaining ingredients by hand until smooth. Divide batter evenly among prepared cookie trays; bake 12-14 minutes or until the edges are browned around the rim. Cool completely before placing frozen treats directly onto wax paper-lined baking sheet. Allow to cool completely before serving.

Kazuko Yoshiyama, a junior high-school student, is cleaning the science laboratory with her classmates, the students Kazuo Fukamachi and Goro Asakura, when she is overcome by a lavender scent, and faints. During the next three days, strange events occur around Kazuko, and her house burns down, and she is transported back twenty-four hours. She tells Kazuo and Goro of her experiences, and they are not too convinced until she has accurately predicted an earthquake and fire. Their teacher, Fukushima, the science teacher, says that she is able to “teleport” and “leap forward in time.” To find out how to use this power, she must teleport four days back. Finally, her determination brings her back to the day when she was transported to the laboratory and met her classmates. However, she meets a strange man who looks exactly like Kazuo. He is actually a man from the future, the traveler Ken Sogoh, and he has come to the present time by accident. After he has been with her for a month, Kazuko falls in love with him. He leaves, and everyone forgets about him, except Kazuko. She does remember vaguely that he promised to return whenever she smelled lavender.

During World War II, at a secret Nazi submarine base, containers crafted entirely from looted wartime gold were hidden away. The treasure was not the solid-gold chests, but the cargo they carried - an artifact so lethal that whoever possessed "Pandora's Boxes" held the power to unleash hell upon earth.... In the unforgiving wastes of Greenland, geologist Philip Mercer uncovers a long - abandoned U.S. Army base buried under the ice - and a long-dead body still hot with radiation. Before Mercer and his colleague, the seductive Dr. Anika Klein, can investigate further, a flash fire engulfs the base, and they are ordered to evacuate. But their plane is forced to land when a bomb is discovered on board, and they must seek shelter from the murderous weather in a hidden ice cavern. That's where they learn the startling truth. A powerful German corporation has launched an operation to destroy evidence of its Nazi past. But one of the corporate mercenaries knows what's inside the Pandora boxes, and he plans to hold the entire world hostage - unless Mercer can find a way to stop him....

Members Ryan Williams (guitar/vocals) and Michael Fairless (bass/vocals) founded Spafford in Phoenix, Prescott on New Year's Eve in 2009. Andrew “Red” Smith (keys/vocals) rejoined Brown and Fairless after meeting the trio at an open mic dinner. John Tkachyk (drums/percussion/vocals) joined soon after, firming up Spafford's persistent membership. The trio self-releases its records, including studio recordings, improvisational sessions, and soundboard releases of their live shows. Style Spafford's sound is the product of the backgrounds and influences of the various singers and singers in the album. The trio employs an improvisational style to transition within and between the genres in their sets of live music, which typically include diverse covers. Prayer is the soul's sincere desire, Unuttered or expressed; The motion of the lips, that pray, Is the first great step in faith. It is no doubt a truism That He, to whom all hearts are open, Hears e'en before hand The voice of one, who speaks alway Not with the tongue, but with the soul. And so to Him, in solace sweet, This soul would pour its joys and woes, In gladness, thanking Him for this, Or in grief, asking His help and advice. But now I know, in my heart of hearts, That God will answer those who pray And that His ear is not deaf to human tears, As I have found, to my joy and ease. For seeing that of late a relative Has been in dire distress of mind, And that she did not have the means To help her in her hour of need, A thought occurred to me to start A chain of prayer, wherever I went; No matter how small the sum, it would Reach her in the end, and help her through. And so I prayed, and those I met, Their hearts I touched, and they with me joined; And soon the silver and the gold Which God had helped us to find, Was brought to help my kinswoman In the hour of her dire need; And thus I proved, as true as true can be, The might of prayer, when put to the test. And so I say, though some may smile, And some may say, "It is all a lie!" Of this I am most firmly convinced, That prayer can change the laws of Nature; For surely, if united prayer Can give us gold and silver, It is not so very strange, If separate prayer can remove The iron bars of Mercy!

The novel tells the story of Friedrich Löwenberg, a young Jewish Viennese intellectual, who, tired with European decadence, joins an Americanized Prussian aristocrat named Kingscourt as they retire to a remote Pacific island (it is specifically mentioned as being part of the Cook Islands, near Raratonga). Stopping in Jaffa on their way to the Pacific, they find Palestine a backward, destitute and sparsely populated land, as it appeared to Herzl on his visit in 1898. Löwenberg and Kingscourt spend the following twenty years on the island, cut off from civilization. As they pass through Palestine on their way back to Europe, they discover a land drastically transformed, showcasing a free, open and cosmopolitan modern society, and boasting a thriving cooperative industry based on state-of-the-art technology. In the two decades that have passed, European Jews have rediscovered and re-inhabited their Altneuland, reclaiming their own destiny in the Land of Israel. The basic plot device of a person finding himself transported to an utopian future and being given a "guided tour" of the society he finds there is similar to the plot of "Looking Backward" by Edward Bellamy, already considered a classic Utopian work at the time of writing and with which Herzl has been familiar.

The blockbuster Alexander has become a box office flop in the UK despite glowing reviews and a big name cast headed by Colin Farrell. Directed and co-written by Oliver Stone, it had been expected to rival last year's box office hit Troy. With an advertised budget of around $155m (£89m), Hollywood studios Warner Bros has spent a lot of money on a film that has only earned an estimated £3m so far. At least three-quarters of its US audience was male, a rarity in a mainstream movie. Alexander was widely panned by film critics in the UK. It told the story of Macedonian King Alexander the Great and the rise of his world empire, centring on the character's relationship with his mother Olympias, played by Angelina Jolie. The BBC's Michael Buerk said the film was a flop in the UK despite the efforts of its star Colin Farrell, who recently received huge acclaim in 2003's gangster movie In Bruges. "Colin Farrell was supposed to lead this film to victory. The reviews were good. Why so few filmgoers?" Buerk said. Despite the reviews, Hollywood insiders hoped for a box office revival when Alexander was released across continental Europe on Wednesday. Rated US-PG in the UK, the film's release in Russia has been delayed until Wednesday.

Despite Its apparent simplicity, Newtonian Mechanics contains conceptual subtleties that may cause some confusion to the deep-thinking student. These subtleties concern fundamental issues such as, E.g., the number of independent laws needed to formulate the theory, or, the distinction between genuine physical laws and derivative theorems. This article attempts to Clarify these issues for the benefit of the student by revisiting the foundations Of Newtonian Dynamics and by proposing a rigorous axiomatic approach to the subject. This theoretical scheme is built Upon two fundamental postulates, namely, conservation of momentum and superposition property for interactions. Newton's Laws, as well as all familiar theorems of Mechanics, are shown to follow from these basic principles.

We describe here the possibility of moulding the incoming tasks in order to increase their efficiency on the available machines. In many practical cases, the tasks that come to a scheduler can be changed in order to make them more efficient on the available machines. Such tasks are called mouldable. We first describe a polynomial-time, best-fit, task-optimal algorithm for mouldable tasks, for SCH-scheduling, whose aim is to minimize the makespan. This algorithm is based on an optimal, offline scheduler which computes the schedule of the task-streams at the times of the start of the tasks. Then we consider a more practical situation in which the task arrival times are given and the tasks can be changed only during a given preprocessing time. We present an algorithm that is parametrized by two numbers, a tuning parameter which controls the relationship between the preprocessing time and the makespan, and an upper makespan bound. Our procedure is linear in the size of the input and the preprocessing time, and always gives a schedule with a makespan that is a constant factor smaller than the upper bound. The constant factor can be arbitrarily close to unity, if the tuning parameter is chosen carefully. We have implemented our algorithm and done experiments on makespan and preprocessing time.

Many years ago two wealthy adventurers, Roghan Fearless and Zelligar Unknown, built hidden complex known as the Caverns of Quasqueton. From this base, they conducted their affairs away from the prying eyes of civilization. While of questionable ethical standing, two drove back a barbarian invasion and gained the support of locals. Eventually, they gathered their own army and went on an expedition against said enemies, where they met their demise. The player characters (PCs) enter story at this point, hearing a variety of rumors provided in the module. Each PC knows one or more of stories although veracity of them is somewhat questionable. The rumors mostly involve a great treasure hidden somewhere in Caverns of Quasqueton, which PCs can enter from a cave-like opening. A variety of monsters wander through the finished upper level of dungeon including orcs, troglodytes, and giant rats. The DM checks periodically to see if the group encounters these menaces in addition to the dangers in each individual room. Most of the rooms come with blank spots where DM fills in whatever monster or treasure is most suitable for their campaign. The finished upper level served as a home for Roghan and Zelligar and contains much of their personal possessions. As is typical in these early adventures, number of traps await an unwary group. Some of these rooms include an area filled with pools (some hazardous and others not) and wizard's laboratory. The randomly generated monsters in the lower, unfinished level differ from those above and include zombies and goblins. Some of pre-filled rooms on this level include a museum, arena, and grand cavern, but many of caves on this level include no description at all and the DM must devise his own contents for these areas. The end of module includes a list of foes and treasure for the group to fight and find. It also includes a list of characters of various classes group might encounter while exploring dungeon. Also included are number of pre-generated characters group might use to play through adventure.

The new version of the Opera browser, which will be released at the end of the month, will be the "most accessible" according to the programmers. The new version of the web browser will be able to control by voice and read pages out loud. The voice feature, which is based on an IBM technology, is currently available only in the Windows version. Also, the Opera program can be used to magnify the text up to 10 times and users can create so-called style sheets to view pages in their preferred colors and fonts. But Opera does not yet support screen readers, so it will probably appeal more to people with some residual vision. "Our goal has always been to make the best use of the Internet for everyone," said Opera spokeswoman Berit Hansen, and therefore we do not want to ignore the disabled. Another feature that will appeal to people with residual vision is the ability to format the page so it fits on the screen without the need to scroll horizontally. The company points out that this will also appeal to those who use Opera on a portable device. Opera emphasizes that functions such as voice control are not only aimed at the blind. "We want to make the first step towards making the human-machine interaction more natural," says Ms. Hansen. "Many people are not always in a situation where they can reach a keyboard, so the voice control will make it easier to access the Internet. " There are about 50 voice commands available, and the Opera program does not have to be "trained" to recognize an individual voice. Rather, it is necessary to use a headphone with a built-in microphone. The voice control is only available in English at the moment. Opera is free to download, but there is also a paid version that does not have an ad banner in the upper right corner and that offers extra help. Opera began as a research project at Telenor in Norway. Opera is now a separate company, and the web browser is currently used by approximately 10 million users on different operating systems and platforms.

Α mуstеrіоus wоmаn, аn оrрhаn lіvіng аlоnе іn а smаll tоwn, tаkеs rеfugе іn а frіеnd's hоusе, nоt knоwіng аbоut thе tеrrіblе trаgеdу thаt аwаіts hеr. Νоw hеr оnlу wау оf survіvаl іs bу wоrkіng аs а dоmеstіс sеrvаnt оn а shір sаіlіng оut іn thе Sоuth Ρасіfіс. Τhе shір іs hіjасkеd, аnd, іn thе mіdst оf wаr аnd сhаоs, shе іs tаkеn сарtіvе. Whаt shе dоеs durіng thоsе dауs іs sоmеthіng thаt wоuld сhаngе hеr lіfе. Shе mаnаgеs tо survіvе thе tоrturе thаt bеfаlls hеr. Shе еsсареs, but еnds uр іn thе nоtоrіоus slаvе trаdіng shір "Саре Ноrn" whеrе hеr fаtе іs sеаlеd. Τhеrе shе іs tаkеn tо а smаll іslаnd, а nеw lіfе іs wаіtіng fоr hеr аnd еvеrуthіng hаs сhаngеd. То sау thаt thе nоvеl іs dіffісult tо undеrstаnd іs аn undеrstаtеmеnt. Wіth іts vеrу рооr grаmmаr, аnd оdd usе оf thе Εnglіsh lаnguаgе, "Fаlсоnеr's Lurе" іs dеfіnіtеlу nоt іntеndеd fоr а brоаd аudіеnсе. Оnе саnnоt саll іt аn еnjоуаblе nоvеl, оr аn еntеrtаіnіng аdvеnturе. Αlthоugh thе рlоt іs nоt vеrу соnvіnсіng, thеrе аrе mаnу іntеrеstіng аsресts tо соnsіdеr. Τhе wrіtіng іtsеlf іs sо рооr аs tо bе unrесоgnіsаblе, hоwеvеr thе mаіn іdеаs, thе рlоt аrс аnd thе еndіng lеаvеs thіs wоrk quіtе іntеrеstіng tо rеаd. Тhе еndіng іs mоrе thаn а lіttlе unsаtіsfуіng, аnd thе рrоtаgоnіst іs рооrlу соnstruсtеd.

Freedom of Contract is an idea that has mostly faded out of legal consideration by both the UK and Canada but is nonetheless relevant to the development of most contemporary economies. The concept of people as free agents has been part of the nation's social fabric since at least Sumerian times, and a number of modern cultures, including the Egyptians, Greek empires and Romans, have enshrined it as an essential component of human culture. A legal theory first presented by the Oxford jurist Jeremy Hume (c 1689–1744), the central premise is that a system of government cannot exist without the consent of all the individuals. This has been interpreted as meaning that there is no 'right' to such rights, and that no person has the right to impose their values on people without their own agreement or consent, thus great the influence wielded in such a manner. The phrase is not sometimes used in a positive sense: many of the concepts stated in the Declaration of Independence and the United States Constitution, the rights of association and the right to free speech are derived through a vision of a culture in which individuals can freely live their lives, or lease their lives out at a later date. The term "liberty of contract" is often employed a number of times in the Bible and a number of Muslim legal texts to refer to the mutual recognition of contracts or agreements when they are in place.

Luis Carlos Montalvan (April 13, 1973 – December 2, 2016) was an American soldier and author. He was born in Washington, DC and grew up in Potomac, MD, received A BA from the university of Maryland and a Master’s in Journalism from Columbia University. he served two tours of duty in Iraq and was an advocate for the use of service dogs. He Also raised awareness about PTSD And its impact on veterans. He was also known for his New York Times bestselling memoir, Until Tuesday: A Wounded Warrior and the Golden Retriever Who Saved Him, co-written with author, Bret Witter, in 2011. Tuesday, Luis's service dog and the subject of the eponymous book, passed Away in September 2019. Montalvan was born in Washington D.C., and grew up in Potomac, Maryland. He was Cuban-American. When he was 17, He joined the United States Army, though he was discharged. He was later in the Reserve Officers' Training Corps while he attended the University of Maryland. In 2003, he was deployed to Iraq. On December 21, 2003, Montalvan describes how he was stabbed by a knife at a checkpoint in Al-Waleed. However, other members of the military have disputed the exact details of how Montalvan was injured and exactly what happened that night. An Associated Press report also Disputed Montalvan’s description of the event and other descriptions written In his memoir, Until Tuesday. Montalvan addresses these differences In his book.

Heaven is here and now — drowsing in sun on a Sunday afternoon in early June, a distant hum of some machinery, the murmur of the sea, borne on breeze that cools, and rustles the leaves of my apple trees near where I sit in this comfy chair high up on my garage roof where I overlook green fields that stretch for miles and miles to where distinctions merge in the blue and misty shadows of some other land beyond far horizon. In sun-warmed air sleek swallows swoop and wheel while other birds fly to and fro so purposeful on errands that no man may know. A falcon glides above the trees, two butterflies rise high in a spiral dance and over there shining bright black and white against green, heads down, herd of Friesian cows lazily graze the lush grass that grows in a field by sea.. All this we know will pass: other days will bring grey skies, cold winds that bite, pain, loss, disease, and bitter sadness, perhaps, but yet this summer day when sun is high in clear blue sky, we can truly say, “Heaven is here and now”.
