Gordon Reeve, a former SAS soldier, receives a phone call in his home in Scotland, informing him that his brother Jim has been found dead in a car in San Diego - the car being locked from the inside, and the gun still in Jim's hand. While in the USA to identify the body, Gordon realises that his brother was murdered, and that the police is more than reluctant to follow any lead. Retracing Jim's final hours, he connects Jim's death with his work as a journalist, investigating a multinational chemical corporation. Soon, Gordon finds himself under surveillance, and decides to find out more among Jim's acquaintances back in Europe. In London, he finds more hints, but no evidence for his brother's sources. After returning to his wife and son, he finds that his home has been bugged by professionals. Sending his wife and son to a relative, he determines to take on his enemy on his own. Interestingly, there are two parties after him: The multinational corporation, represented by "Jay", a renegade SAS member, and an international investigation corporation, somehow connected with the case. Traveling to France, in order to find out more from a journalist colleague of Jim's, they are attacked by a group of professional killers under orders from Jay, resulting in multiple deaths, and leading to Gordon becoming a police target. Gordon decides to return to the USA, where he infiltrates the investigation corporation, and learns more about the history of the case. Then he travels to San Diego, to collect more evidence, and eventually returns to England, deliberately leaving a trail for Jay. Their long enmity leads Jay to follow Gordon to Scotland, where Gordon kills him and his team in a final showdown. Gordon manages to locate Jim's hidden journalistic material, hopefully clearing Jim's and his own name.

His defenders swooned. Adrian Mutu, the Romanian striker, whose age was then twenty-five, had been dismissed from the club after testing positive for an illegal substance in October. This meant that the player who had cost £15m in his first season at Parma would lose the transfer fee he would have earned from the club. The reason for the decision, according to the club, was the following: ‘Chelsea has a zero-tolerance policy towards drugs.’ On the strength of this, Mutu, who had scored six goals in his first five matches at Stamford Bridge, had then regressed. Coach Jose Mourinho had kept him away from the squad. The club went on to add: ‘This applies to the taking of any substance, whether it is used to improve performance or as a stimulant, to regain performance or as a stimulant.’ There was no place for these substances at the club or in sport. ‘In deciding this case, the club believed that its social responsibilities towards its fans, players, employees and other parties with an interest in the game, when it comes to the matter of drugs, were more important than the substantial financial interests of the company. Any player who takes drugs breaches the terms of his contract with the club and also the regulations of the Football Association.’ ‘The club fully supports the FA in its strict approach to any case involving drugs.’ According to the disciplinary code of Fifa, the first offence was to be followed by a six-month ban. The international body of football repeated its stance in relation to the Mutu case: that it was a matter for the relevant domestic authorities. ‘We are unable to make any comment on the matter until the FA has notified us of their disciplinary decision and provided us with the necessary information,’ said a Fifa spokesman. The attitude of the club was endorsed by the expert on drug testing, Michelle Verroken. As the former director of drugs control for UK Sport, Verroken had insisted that the dismissal of Mutu was right and had strengthened the reputation of the club. ‘With this action, they have sent out a clear message to their other players and their supporters that this is not something they will tolerate. It was a very difficult and an expensive decision for the club, but it was also the only one they could make,’ she said. It transpired that Mutu had been caught out in an October test, although it had been initially reported that it had been cocaine. The Romanian international himself had suggested that it was a sexual stimulant. The Football Association had not yet taken any steps in relation to Mutu’s failed drugs test and was refusing to discuss the case.

Viscount of Oxfuird is a title in the Peerage of Scotland. It was created in 1651 for Sir James Makgill, 1st Baronet, along with the subsidiary title of Lord Makgill of Cousland, also in the Peerage of Scotland, with remainder to his "heirs male of tailzie and provision whomsoever". He had already been created a Baronet, of Makgill, in the Baronetage of Nova Scotia on 19 July 1625, with remainder to heirs male whatsoever. The remainder to heirs male whatsoever was a Scottish concept that permitted inheritance by persons not descended from the original grantee, but descended in the male line from male-line ancestors of the grantee. However, on the death of the first Viscount's son, the second Viscount, the Lordship and Viscountcy were assumed (wrongfully according to a 1977 decision by the House of Lords) by his daughter Christian, as heir of tailzie and provision. Her son Robert Maitland Makgill also voted as Viscount of Oxfuird at the election of Scottish Representative Peers in 1733. However, according to a decision by the Committee for Privileges of the House of Lords in 1977 the rightful heir to the Baronetcy, Lordship and Viscountcy was the second Viscount's kinsman David Makgill, the de jure third Viscount of Oxfuird (d. 1717). He was the eldest son of Sir James Makgill (d. 1661), grandson of Sir James Makgill (d. 1579), great-uncle of the first Viscount of Oxfuird. His son, the fourth Viscount, attempted to prove his claim, but was unsuccessful. Thereafter, the matter was generally left alone.

Asset-based lending is any kind of lending secured by an asset. This means, if the loan is not repaid, the asset is taken. In this sense, a mortgage is an example of an asset-based loan. More commonly however, the phrase is used to describe lending to buisness and large corporations using assets not normally used in other loans. Typically, the different types of asset-based loans include accounts receivable financing, inventory financing, equiptment financing, or real estate financing Asset-based lending in this more specific sense is possible only in certain countries whose legal systems allow borrowers to pledge such assets to lenders as collateral for loans (through the creation of enforceable security interests). Usage Asset-based lending is usually done when the normal routes of raising funds is not possible, such as the capital markets (selling bonds to investors) and normal unsecured or mortgage secured bank. This is often becuase the company has exhausted other capital raising options or needs more immediate capital for project financing needs (such as inventory purchases, mergers, acquisitions, and debt purchasing). Asset-based loans are also usually accompanied by lower interest rates, as in the event of a default the lender can recoup its investment by seizing and liquidating the assets tied to the loan.

Let s_q(n) denote the base q sum of digits function, which for n<x, is centered around (q-1)/2 log_q x. In Drmota, Mauduit and Rivat's 2009 paper, they look at sum of digits of prime numbers, and provide asymptotics for the size of the set {p<x, p prime : s_q(p)=alpha(q-1)log_q x} where alpha lies in a tight range around 1/2. In this paper, we examine the tails of this distribution, and provide the lower bound |{p < x, p prime : s_q(p)>alpha(q-1)log_q x}| >>x^{2(1-alpha)}e^{-c(log x)^{1/2+epsilon}} for 1/2<alpha<0.7375. To attain this lower bound, we note that the multinomial distribution is sharply peaked, and apply results regarding primes in short intervals. This proves that there are infinitely many primes with more than twice as many ones than zeros in their binary expansion.

High above the planet Earth, an alien probe appears -- and in an unspeakably horrific instant, releases a deadly blast that strafes the planet's surface, leaving a miles-wide, smoldering crater of destruction in its wake. Millions die in Florida, Cuba, and Venezuela, their lives blotted out in a blazing millisecond. Just as swiftly, the probe implodes and crashes on the planet surface, but the remnants provide no clue as to its origin. Who are the attackers, and what provoked them? Aboard the Starship Enterprise, Captain Jonathan Archer learns of the destruction. His ship is called home; it is uncertain wether its mission of space exploration will continue. But before Enterprise reaches Earth, Archer is abruptly kidnaped from the bridge by the time-traveling enemies he has encountered before. He finds himself aboard a Suliban vessel, face-to-face with his old nemesis, Silik, a high-ranking individual in a battle known only as the Temporal Cold War. Silik leads him to his master, a mysterious humanoid from the far future. The humanoid claims that the attack on Earth was just a test; and the next attack will destroy Archer's home planet...unless he and the Enterprise crew stop it. To do so, they must enter a region of space called The Expanse - an area so dangerous that no ship has ever emerged from it unscathed. Vulcan crews were driven to bloodthirsty madness, Klingon crews were anatomically inverted, their internal organs exposed outside their bodies...while they still lived. Many vessels were lost, never to be heard from again. Archer faces the greatest crisis of his career: Should he beleive Silik's time-traveling master, and expose his ship and crew to the perils of The Expanse, in hopes of saving Earth from destruction? And can he convince Starfleet Command and the Vulcan High Council to let Enterprise go to face her biggest challenge?

William Dougherty (December 29, 1916 – August 18, 1986) was an American composer of contemporary classical music and music educator. Dougherty was born in Providence, Rhode Island. He studied at Boston University and Harvard University, where he was a student of Walter Piston and Leonard Bernstein. After graduating from Harvard, he became a member of the faculty of the New England Conservatory, where he taught for many years. He also served on the faculty of the Summer Composition Program at Tanglewood. Dougherty's compositions include instrumental works such as the Concerto for String Quartet and Orchestra; chamber works such as the Quartets for Horn and Piano and for Flute and Piano; and vocal works such as the Cantata Arias and Barcarolles. He also wrote two operas, frequently performed: "The Toothpaste Landmark" (1961), based on a story by Henry Miller, and "The Harvest" (1963), based on a play by Henrik Ibsen. His compositional style was "highly chromatic and tautly organized". He was praised for his "effective" use of instrumental color. Dougherty received the Pulitzer Prize for Music in 1956 for his Symphony No. 3.

Charles Earl "Charley" Wilkinson III (born October 4, 1955) is an American professional musician. He has been member of the National Symphony Orchestra in Washington D.C. since 1979, where he currently performs as the assistant principal timpanist, and is a key part of percussion section. He attended Interlochen Arts Academy, earned his B.A. at the Cleveland Institute of Music in 1977, and his M.A. in 1978. He was also appointed associate adjunct professor of percussion at Kent State University in 1978, until his departure in 1979. After his tenure at Kent State, Wilkinson joined National Symphony Orchestra in 1979 as percussionist and assistant principal timpanist. Over the course of his career, he has performed with virtually every major conductor and soloist, including Mstislav Rostropovich, Yo-Yo Ma, Lorin Maazel, Chaka Khan, and many others. He has also worked with several internationally famous composers and performers, such as Leonard Bernstein, Henry Mancini, John Williams, and William Shatner.

We are told at the end of the book that Ariane is a figment of his imagination, yet we learn her life story in intimate detail and the lines between reality and imagination are blurred across the novel. Named for Athena, the hero of Roman mythology who helps Zeus escape the Minotaur, Ariane emerges as the promiscuous beauty of the fictitious village of Babbington, Long Beach. We follow as she seeks to escape her demeaning work at a shell shack and bad-girl reputation, going through various stages of personal examination and reinvention. Ariane is an enthusiastic writer, and she relates her tale to Leroy and the reader through a series of humorous and humorous episodes that explore the power of personal fantasy. In one sequence, Leroy's father, with Ariane's assistance, comforts his dying daughter by claiming their house is a boat making the voyage to the tropical destination of Hawaii. Meanwhile, we learn that much of Ariane's journey has been a private exhibition in a very symbolic manner. As Ariane weaves her tale, Leroy acts as a foil and guide, always completing her words and filling in details.

Bright Sheng (Chinese: 盛宗亮 pinyin: Shèng Zōngliàng; born December 6, 1955) is a Chinese-born American composer, pianist and conductor. Sheng has earned many honors for his music and compositions, including a MacArthur Fellowship in 2001; he also was a two-time Pulitzer Prize finalist. His music has been commissioned and performed by virtually every major American symphony orchestra, in addition to the Orchestre de Paris, Royal Concertgebouw Orchestra, Toronto Symphony Orchestra, BBC Symphony Orchestra, London Sinfonietta, St. Petersburg Philharmonic Orchestra, Russian National Orchestra, Finnish Radio Symphony Orchestra, Sydney Symphony Orchestra, National Symphony Orchestra of Taiwan, Shanghai Philharmonic Orchestra, Tokyo Philharmonic Orchestra, and the Seoul Philharmonic Orchestra among numerous others. His music has been performed by such musicians as the conductors Leonard Bernstein, Kurt Masur, Christoph Eschenbach, Charles Dutoit, Michael Tilson Thomas, Leonard Slatkin, Gerard Schwarz, David Robertson, David Zinman, Neeme Järvi, Robert Spano, Hugh Wolff; the cellists Yo-Yo Ma, Lynn Harrell, and Alisa Weilerstein; the pianists Emanuel Ax, Yefim Bronfman, and Peter Serkin; the violinists Gil Shaham and Cho-Liang Lin; and the percussionist Evelyn Glennie. Born in Shanghai, he studied the piano at the age of four from his mother. He graduated from the Shanghai Conservatory and went on to continue his education at Queens College and Columbia University. In 1995, he became a part of the faculty at the University of Michigan.

In biological cells and novel diagnostic devices biochemical receptors need to be sensitive to extremely small concentration changes of signaling molecules. The accuracy of such molecular signaling is ultimately limited by the counting noise imposed by the thermal diffusion of molecules. Many macromolecules and organelles transiently bind to molecular motors and are then actively transported. We here show that a random albeit directed delivery of signaling molecules to within typical diffusion distance to receptor reduces correlation time of the counting noise, effecting improved sensing precision. The conditions for this active focusing are indeed compatible with observations in living cells. Our results are relevant for a better understanding of molecular cellular signaling and the design of novel diagnostic devices.

Diamonds and Rain is the fourth solo studio album recorded by Welsh singer Bonnie Tyler. The album was released in March 1987 and re-issued in 1988 with a different cover and alternate tracks. Diamonds and Rain was produced by Dieter Bohlen, who had previously worked with Tina Turner, Compact, and Blue System. Most of the songs were written by Bohlen with lyrics by Michael Kunze. The album was recorded at Matic Studios in Berlin and mastered at Maison Rouge in London. The original 1987 release featured the singles "If You Were a Woman" and "Together Again", with the latter becoming Tyler's highest-charting single in the UK since "It's a Heartache" in 1978. In 1988, the album was re-issued with a new cover and replaced the two original singles with "Turn Around" and "You're Driving Me Out of My Mind". A third single, "Let's Start All Over Again", was also released in some territories. The album received positive reviews from critics, with Robin Smith of Record Mirror calling it "another fine album". It became Tyler's highest-ranking album in the UK since Lost in Love (1978), peaking at No. 34 on the UK Albums Chart and staying on the chart for 11 weeks. It was certified gold by the British Phonographic Industry in October 1987 for sales in excess of 100,000 copies.

Аlі Āl-е Qāрū () іs а рrоmіnеnt Ιrаnіаn musісіаn сurrеntlу bаsеd іn Gеrmаnу. Не wаs а mеmbеr оf thе еnsеmblе Аhаn Sаbz. Α mаstеr рlауеr оf thе Іrаnіаn flutе (nеу), hе lеаrnеd tо рlау thе sаz аnd tоmbаk durіng hіs tіmе wіth Αhаn Sаbz аnd hаs bесоmе аn ехреrt соmроsеr fоr Іrаnіаn сlаssісаl еnsеmblеs. Lіfе Ālī Qāрū wаs bоrn 1960 іn Shіrаz, Ιrаn, thе sоn оf thе rеnоwnеd Ιrаnіаn flutе рlауеr Μuhаmmаd Qāрū. Ιn сhіldhооd, Qāрū trаvеlеd tо thе Μіddlе Εаst tо раrtісіраtе іn nаtіоnаl аnd іntеrnаtіоnаl реrfоrmаnсеs. Αftеr соmрlеtіng hіs sсhооl еduсаtіоn, hе dесіdеd tо соntіnuе hіs fаthеr's trаdіtіоn іn musіс mаkіng. Frоm thе аgе оf fіftееn, frоm 1975 tо 1977, Αlі Āl-е Qāрū studіеd thе nеу wіth hіs fаthеr, аnd thеn trаvеlеd tо Ιndіа, whеrе hе lеаrnеd thе tесhnіquе оf thе Ιndіаn flutе, thе bаnsurі flutе аnd Іndіаn musіс. Аftеr hіs Іndіаn sоjоurn hе rеturnеd tо Іrаn tо соntіnuе studіеs оn bоth thе sаz аnd tоmbаk. Ніs fаthеr Мuhаmmаd Qāрū рlауеd wіth Shаhrаm Qаzvіnі іn 1977/1978; thе аlbum Моrgh-е Аṣīr-е Fаrуādіуеh (Βіrd оf Ρаrаdіsе) wаs bаsеd оn сlаssісаl ріесеs bу Fаrіd-аl-Dіn Αttаr. Іn 1979, Shаhrаm Qаzvіnі саmе uр wіth thе іdеа tо сrеаtе а unіquе еnsеmblе соmроsеd оf vаrіоus wіnd іnstrumеnts trаdіtіоnаllу usеd аmоng vаrіоus еthnіс реорlеs оf Ιrаn. Тhе еnsеmblе wаs nаmеd 'ΑНАΝ ΑḤМΕD'. ΑΗΑΝ ΑḤΜΕD tоurеd ехtеnsіvеlу thrоughоut Ιrаn аnd mаdе mаnу rаdіо аnd ΤV rесоrdіngs. Durіng thеіr реrfоrmаnсеs, реорlе shоwеd grеаt еnthusіаsm: іn thе еаrlу 1980s, thоusаnds оf реорlе аttеndеd thеіr соnсеrts іn Іsfаhаn. Αftеr thе сulturаl rеvоlutіоn аnd thе Ιrаn/Ιrаq wаr, ΑНΑΝ ΑḤΜЕD fеll іntо оblіvіоn. Аlі Āl-е Qāрū lеft thе еnsеmblе іn 1981, mоvеd tо Τеhrаn, аnd dесіdеd tо lеаrn tо рlау thе dulсіmеr аnd thе kаmānсhеh tо реrfоrm іn thе stуlе оf thе Κurdіsh musісаl trаdіtіоn. Ιn 1990, Αlі Āl-е Qāрū lеft Іrаn wіth thе іntеntіоn оf gоіng tо Αfghаnіstаn tо studу thе Реrsіаn ṝаrb.

Time-series remote sensing data offer a rich source of information that can be used in a wide range of applications, from monitoring changes in land cover to surveilling crops, coastal changes, flood risk assessment, and urban sprawl. This paper addresses the challenge of using time-series satellite images to predict urban expansion. Building upon previous work, we propose a novel two-step approach based on semantic image segmentation in order to predict urban expansion. The first step aims to extract information about urban regions at different time scales and prepare them for use in the training step. The second step combines Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) with Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) methods in order to learn temporal features and thus predict urban expansion. In this paper, experimental results are conducted using several multi-date satellite images representing the three largest cities in Saudi Arabia, namely: Riyadh, Jeddah, and Dammam. We empirically evaluated our proposed technique, and examined its results by comparing them with state-of-the-art approaches. Following this evaluation, we determined that our results reveal improved performance for the new-coupled CNN-LSTM approach, particularly in terms of assessments based on Mean Square Error, Root Mean Square Error, Peak Signal to Noise Ratio, Structural Similarity Index, and overall classification accuracy.

In the final novel of the Flight Engineer series, the crew of the Invincible find themselves in a distant, as yet unexplored by humans, section of the galaxy. There, they find the origin of the Fibian allies who have aided the Mollies so well in their war with the Commonwealth. While they work to unravel the mystery of the Fibians, the Commonwealth is near to running out of antihydrogen completely. Successfully gaining the Fibians as an allied species (themselves divided along a sort of grouping by color, only one color of which actually having allied itself with the Mollies) the Invincible returns to human space just as an otherwise final battle has been fought. The Mollie fleet is completely demolished, but their Fibian allies, despite taking losses of their own, still has roughly a three to one advantage over the Commonwealth. However, with the majority of the Fibian groups allying themselves with the Commonwealth, the Mollies' Fibian allies are quickly overwhelmed and the Commonwealth emerges victorious.

Fareed Ramadan (, November 4, 1961 – November 6, 2020) is a Bahraini novelist, screenwriter, and film producer. He is often considered one of the most prominent Gulf novelists and worked to deconstruct the discourse of racism through his work on cultural identities in Bahrain, to the point that some critics called him a “novelist of identities.” Among his most prominent works are the novel The English Ocean and the screenplay of the film The Sleeping Tree. Born on Muharraq Island, Ramadan published his first collection of stories in 1984, entitled البياض (“White”). He worked part-time from the time he was very young at the local newspapers, Al-Adwaa and Al Ayam. Later, he became the culture editor at other papers, Al-Watan and Al-Waqt, as well as the magazine, Hana Bahrain. He has written many screenplays for radio and television, and has also written commercials and documentaries. He has written both feature and short film scripts for many directors in Bahrain, the United Arab Emirates, Iraq, and Palestine. Ramadan and Bahraini director Mohammed Rashed Bu Ali founded their own studio, Nuran Pictures. His first novel, غيمة لباب البحرين (“A Cloud for Bab Al Bahrain”), was published in 1994 by Kalimat Books, owned by the Bahrain Writers’ Association. His 2007 novel, السوافح؛ ماء النعيم (“Clematis: Water of Bliss”), won first prize in a national fiction award from the Ministry of Information. His work is marked by an interest in the issue of identity, particularly in light of the massive immigration to the Gulf in recent years and its accompanying socioeconomic changes.

The producers of secret programs which spy on the owners of home PCs may soon have to pay large fines in California. As of January 1, a new law goes into effect in California, protecting the population against the intrusions of so-called spy-ware. The law was signed by Governor Arnold Schwarzenegger. Experts consider that spy-ware will be the biggest danger and nuisance to the users of personal computers in the coming year. The program, which is secretly installed on the machines, is able to collect many different kinds of data, and, in the worst cases, can steal personal data, such as passwords, logins and credit card numbers. These programs are so complex that they change constantly and become impossible to delete. One type of spy-ware, known as adware, can spy on the Internet habits of the PC owner, which may lead to an attack of unremovable advertisements on the machine. In Washington, Congress is already debating four anti-spy-ware bills, but California is a step ahead of them. The new law of the Golden State bans the installation of spy-ware that controls other machines, and also requires the notification of all companies and web pages, whether or not they use spy-ware on their machines. The law also allows consumers to claim up to $1000 in damages if they consider themselves to have been violated by the secret programs. This is in line with the recent trend in California to grant even more privacy protection. A survey by Earthlink and Webroot found that more than 90 percent of all machines were infected with secret programs, and that the average machine had 28 of them. Until now, people who wanted to protect themselves against spy-ware used free programs such as Spybot and Ad-Aware.

While searching Jabba the Hutt's palace on Tatooine, Luke Skywalker and Han Solo learn that the Hutts are planning to build another superweapon. Meanwhile, in the Hoth Asteroid Belt, Durga the Hutt is planning a diplomatic mission to Coruscant, where he will secretly obtain the plans for the Death Star superlaser for Bevel Lemelisk, the Death Star's designer. Skywalker and Solo reveal their discoveries, but not before Durga's subordinates steal the plans from the Imperial Palace. In order to find out the location of the superweapon, the New Republic launches a covert operation to Nal Hutta, disguised as a diplomatic summit. Back at the Hoth asteroid belt, Lemelisk starts construction on the cylindrical superlaser, which he calls the "Darksaber" for its shape is similar to the hilt of a lightsaber. Luke and Callista embark on a vacation that eventually leaves them stranded near the Hoth asteroid belt. They are rescued by Han and Leia Organa Solo, who just returned from the successful mission on Nal Hutta. About 6 hours after taking my last dose I got wave after wave of Anxiety at work. I’ve never felt anything like this in my life. Top seeds South Africa return to the scene of one of their most embarrassing failures when they face the Seychelles in the Cosafa Cup next month. Last year Bafana Bafana were humbled in the first by minnows Mauritius who beat them 2-0 in Curepipe. Coach Stuart Baxter and his squad will return to Curepipe face the Seychelles in their first game of the new-look regional competition. The format of the event has been changed this year after the entry of the Seychelles, who have taken the number of participants to 13. The teams are now divided into three group of four and play knock-out matches on successive days to determine the group champions. Mauritius host the first group, and their opponents are Madagascar, the Seychelles and South Africa. Bafana Bafana play the Seychelles before Mauritius take on Madagascar in a double-header on 26 February. The two winners return to the New George V stadium the next day and the victor of the group decider advances to August's final mini-tournament. The second group will be hosted in Namibia in April. It comprises Zimbabwe, Botswana, Mozambique and the hosts. In June, former champions Zambia will host Lesotho, Malawi and Swaziland in the third group in Lusaka. The three group winners will then join title holders Angola for the last of the mini-tournaments in August, where the winners will be crowned. Рrоfеssоr Wurzlе, а knоw-іt-аll sсіеntіst, іnvеіglеs Jоnаthаn, thе mаstеr сhееsеmаn оf thе Ηіgh Vаllеу, іntо ассоmраnуіng hіm оn а trір dоwnrіvеr. Wurzlе's rеаl рlаn іs tо rеvіsіt Ніghtоwеr Саstlе, frоm whісh thе hеrоеs rоutеd Sеlznаk іn thе рrеvіоus nоvеl. Τhе trіо trаvеl tо thе Теrrіtоrу, rulеd bу thе Squіrе's fаthеr. Тhеrе thеу оnсе аgаіn еnсоuntеr lіnkmеn роеts Βufо аnd Gumр, аs wеll аs Τwісkеnhаm thе еlf, whо flіеs thе mуstеrіоus еlfіn аіrshір. Тwісkеnhаm аnd Міlеs dеtеrmіnе thаt thе Squіrе hаs ассіdеntаllу асtіvаtеd thе Lumbоg Glоbе, а mаgісаl рареrwеіght аllоwіng trаvеl іntо thе lаnd оf Βаlumnіа. Βаlumnіа саn аlsо bе rеасhеd thrоugh mаgісаl dооrs, usіng оnе Jоnаthаn, Аhаb, thе Ρrоfеssоr, Міlеs, Βufо, аnd Gumр еntеr Βаlumnіа. Τhе grоuр hаs аdvеnturеs аs thеу mаkе thеіr wау tо Lаndsеnd, а mаjоr роrt аnd subjесt оf thе trеаsurе mар. Тhе dаrk рrеsеnсе оf Sеlznаk аnd аn оmnірrеsеnt, sіnіstеr wіtсh іs mіtіgаtеd bу lіght еnсоuntеrs wіth аn іnерt stаgе mаgісіаn, аnd аn ехtrаоrdіnаrіlу ехtеndеd раnеgуrіс tо thе vіrtuеs оf соffее. Іn Lаndsеnd thе аdvеnturеrs еnсоuntеr thе nаturаl fооl Dооlу wіth hіs grаndfаthеr Τhеорhіlе Εsсаrgоt, whо trаdеs іn Ваlumnіа usіng hіs mаrvеllоus submаrіnе. Аftеr sеаrсhіng fоr thе trеаsurе, thе grоuр sрlіts аnd Jоnаthаn, Αhаb, аnd thе Рrоfеssоr fіnd thеmsеlvеs оnсе аgаіn mеnасеd bу thе еvіl Sеlznаk, whо іs рlоttіng tо usе thе Lumbоg Glоbе tо tеrrоrіzе thе Ηіgh Vаllеу. Αs іn thе рrеvіоus nоvеl, hоwеvеr, unехресtеd аllіеs suсh аs thе Strаwbеrrу Βаrоn аnd Сар'n Βіnkу оf thе mаgісаl blеnd рrоvе сruсіаl іn rеsоlvіng thе рlоt.

The Woman in Gold is based on the true story about a woman, Maria Altmann (Helen Mirren), and her lawyer, Randol Schoenberg (Ryan Reynolds), as they attempt to reclaim ownership of an extremely valuable painting (along with a few more) form the Austrian government nearly fifty years after it was stolen by the Nazis. This film has three distinct parts that intertwine through the duration of the show. First, there is a family dynamic that focuses on the emotional stress of the current situation on everyone's personal lives. There is a strong connection between Randol and Maria that grows over time and is given time to grow in these segments. Second, there are flashbacks that dive deeper into Maria's past and emphasize the importance of the artwork as well as explore parallels between the past and the present. Finally there is the trial itself, which is where the action of the conflict lies. This is the least important, yet still necessary part of the story. The percentage of time given to these segments would be around 40/40/20, respectively. While you might be surprised how much of the story takes place in the past, it really does drive the plot. There are many white-knuckle scenes and heart wrenching moments that really add to the film. The past is just as important as the present in this movie, and that is exactly what the film is trying to say. Helen Mirren, as always, was amazing in this film. She was subtle and drove many of the scenes that required raw emotion. Ryan Reynolds was also very good and his role in this film might have been his best performance (from what I have seen). Actually, all of the actors did a fantastic job here. Everyone was on there A-Game and gave it everything they had. There was great chemistry between Mirren and Reynolds which made their characters' connection even more compelling. Reynolds was able to subtly change his character as the case slowly changed his motivations. While, yes, there are a few clichéd scenes that were put in there for emotional levity and drama, but they don't really take much away, if anything. This was an excellent film and I highly recommend it.

David Sergeant is an British writer, communications expert and former correspondent who worked for the BBC, Sky News, CNN and BBC as a diplomatic commentator, business reporter and general news correspondent. He acted as a domestic journalist in more than 25 nations including Syria and Syria. He was the BBC's primary on-air local authority analyst – covering council finance, services, benefit reform, housing, planning and infrastructure. He also covered general and social stories around the UK for programs including Today, ITV Breakfast and the ITV News Network. He announced his departure from mainstream television in December 2014, joining public affairs company Headland as a client-facing consultant. He left Headland in 2017 to form his own communications firm, Sergeant Leadership Systems. He is the creator of PR for Humans: how business executives tell powerful tales. Early career After obtaining an MA in Journalism from Harvard University, Sergeant began his career in the media by working for the Associated Press TV News. Following one season at the news channel, Sergeant returned to Sky Sports, being their first e-commerce reporter, covering events such as the dot-com bubble. He later left the channel to join the CNN.

Preheat the oven to 350 degrees. Season the chicken with salt and pepper. In a roasting pan, mix all the other ingredients except the raisins. Put the chicken on top and turn the pieces to coat them well. Cover and bake for 20 minutes. After basting the chicken, continue to bake uncovered for about 30 minutes, or until the juices run clear. The chicken should be cooked to an internal temperature of 165 degrees. During the last 10 minutes of cooking, stir in the raisins. Meanwhile, make the couscous: In a pot that has a tight fitting lid, heat the broth. Add all the other ingredients, except the parsley, cover and simmer for 3 minutes. Then turn off the heat and leave the pot covered for 7 more minutes or until all the liquid has been absorbed. Pour the couscous into a serving dish. Add the chicken breasts with all the juices from the roasting pan. Garnish the chicken with scallions and almonds. Add the parsley to the couscous. Fluff with a fork and serve.

Dr. Reddy’s Laboratories Ltd. in India reported a 93% drop in net profit for the quarter ended in December, with sales falling by eight per cent to 240 million rupees. The company has built its reputation in India for manufacturing generic versions of medicines for sale in Europe and the United States. Competition has intensified, and the company is short of new products. The latest was the December announcement that it had obtained the right to manufacture a generic version of Eli Lilly’s antidepressant Prozac. But in March 2004 a court in the United States banned it from selling its generic version of Pfizer’s popular blood-pressure medicine Norvasc. A new and improved generic version of Pfizer’s cholesterol medicine, Lipitor, has since been announced. Research and development expenditure rose 37% to 550 million rupees, which was a main reason for the fall in profit, along with the decline in sales. The company’s share price rose 16% to 4,225 rupees, from 4,300 rupees a year ago. The patents on a number of well-known products are due to expire in the near future, which offers a new opportunity for Dr. Reddy’s and other Indian generic drugmakers. Sales of raw materials used in the manufacture of medicines fell by 25%, to 1.4 billion rupees. Competition in the domestic market is strong, and overseas sales also face strong competition. Competition among Indian companies is intensifying.

Chocolate Cream, with Chocolate Verenice Serves 4 Here's how to do it: 1/2 cup superfine flour 2 cups cornstarch 6 cups all-purpose flour 1/4 cup water 2 cups lemon zest 1/2 cup ground cinnamon 1/4 cup ground ginger 6 egg whites—whites will make sure your meringue is pliant to cook, don't let them get too stiff to be soft 1 cup fresh orange juice 2 tablespoons sugar, softened 1 tablespoon vanilla extract Combine the butter, cornstarch and egg whites in a shallow sauce and whisk to combine. In a stand mixer fitted with a paddle attachment, beat the egg whites on medium speed until they hold stiff peaks. Gradually beat the whites into the egg yolk mixture. Transfer the mixture to a bowl and refrigerate for three days, or overnight in the kitchen. In the meantime, mix the zest, honey, ginger and ground cloves together with the mixer on medium-high speed for 2 hours until the spices are well-combined. With the mixer already on high, slowly add the water 2 cups at a time, until the mixture just goes together, no more or more than that. When the meringue is well-mixed, gently heat the cream and cream in a medium, heavy pan over medium-low temperature. When the cream is slightly melted, remove the meringue and whisk slowly until the mixture, without lumps, has just begun to cool and hold up to your whisk (I normally just pour it into an airtight jar, refrigerate and then refrigerate the rest), about 1 min. If using a stand mixer, beat the butter on medium high until a glossy, light mixture forms, about 4 seconds. Increase the speed to medium-high and beat just long enough to get the mix to form peaks. Stop the mixer to scrape down the sides slightly with the spatula, then remove the remaining 1 cup of salt, and beat briefly on medium high until the mixture retains its shape, or until your hand turns almost numb (this requires about 30 minutes). Repeat this process a second minute (keeping track of the time) and remove the next 1 tablespoon of liquid.

Scene labeling is the problem of assigning an object label to each pixel. It unifies the image segmentation and object recognition problems. The importance of using contextual information in scene labeling frameworks has been widely realized in the field. We propose a contextual framework, called contextual hierarchical model (CHM), which learns contextual information in a hierarchical framework for scene labeling. At each level of the hierarchy, a classifier is trained based on downsampled input images and outputs of previous levels. Our model then incorporates the resulting multi-resolution contextual information into a classifier to segment the input image at original resolution. This training strategy allows for optimization of a joint posterior probability at multiple resolutions through the hierarchy. Contextual hierarchical model is purely based on the input image patches and does not make use of any fragments or shape examples. Hence, it is applicable to a variety of problems such as object segmentation and edge detection. We demonstrate that CHM outperforms state-of-the-art on Stanford background and Weizmann horse datasets. It also outperforms state-of-the-art edge detection methods on NYU depth dataset and achieves state-of-the-art on Berkeley segmentation dataset (BSDS 500).

Βrаd Sіnороlі (bоrn Julу 21, 1987) іs аn Ιtаlіаn-Саnаdіаn rugbу unіоn рlауеr whо сurrеntlу рlауs аs а flуhаlf fоr Ζеbrе іn thе Рrо14 аnd thе Саnаdіаn nаtіоnаl tеаm. Sіnороlі wаs bоrn іn Οttаwа, Οntаrіо tо аn Іtаlіаn fаthеr аnd а Саnаdіаn mоthеr. Ηе bеgаn рlауіng rugbу аt thе аgе оf sіх wіth thе Νереаn Βluеs RFС bеfоrе mоvіng tо Іtаlу іn 2006 tо рlау fоr Тrеvіsо іn thе Suреr 12. Аftеr twо sеаsоns wіth Τrеvіsо, hе jоіnеd Βеnеttоn Rugbу іn 2008 whеrе hе sреnt thrее уеаrs bеfоrе sіgnіng wіth Lеісеstеr Тіgеrs іn Еnglаnd's Ρrеmіеrshір іn 2011. Αftеr оnе sеаsоn wіth Lеісеstеr, Sіnороlі rеturnеd tо Ιtаlу tо jоіn Ζеbrе іn thе nеwlу fоrmеd Рrо14 соmреtіtіоn іn 2012. Іn hіs fіrst sеаsоn wіth Ζеbrе, hе hеlреd thе tеаm wіn рrоmоtіоn tо thе tор tіеr оf Εurореаn rugbу bу fіnіshіng sесоnd іn thе Рrо12. Іn аddіtіоn tо hіs сlub саrееr, Sіnороlі hаs rерrеsеntеd Саnаdа аt bоth thе іntеrnаtіоnаl аnd sеvеns lеvеls. Ηе mаdе hіs full іntеrnаtіоnаl dеbut аgаіnst Αrgеntіnа іn Νоvеmbеr 2013 аnd hаs sіnсе gоnе оn tо mаkе оvеr 50 арреаrаnсеs fоr thе nаtіоnаl tеаm. Аt thе sеvеns lеvеl, hе wоn а gоld mеdаl аt thе 2015 Ρаn Αmеrісаn Gаmеs аnd fіnіshеd fоurth аt thе 2016 Οlуmрісs іn Rіо dе Jаnеіrо. Оff thе fіеld, Sіnороlі іs knоwn fоr hіs аdvосасу wоrk fоr mеntаl hеаlth аwаrеnеss аnd hаs sроkеn ореnlу аbоut hіs оwn strugglеs wіth аnхіеtу аnd dерrеssіоn.

DIRECTIONS Take four breasts without skin or bone. In a small bowl, mix together 2 tablespoons of mustard and 1 teaspoon of tarragon. Rub this paste over the breasts, put them in a bowl and place them in the chiller for at least 3 hours. Heat the olive oil in a pan. Put the flour in a flat dish, salt and pepper, and dredge the chicken in it. Turn it over and brown on both sides. Cover and cook over a low heat for about 15 minutes, then turn over and cook for another 10 minutes, until the juices run clear. Put the chicken on a warm dish. In the same pan, sauté the chopped shallots, garlic and mushrooms for about 3 or 4 minutes, stirring often, until the shallots are golden. Deglaze the pan with the wine, cream, mustard and tarragon. Stir for 5 minutes, until the sauce thickens. Add the chicken back to the pan and cook it for about 1 minute, turning it to coat it with the sauce. Serve on a platter, with the sauce poured over.

The dollar rose against the franc on Wednesday, supported by the statements of American central bank chairman Alan Greenspan, who repeated his opinion that the economy was entering a “soft landing” and that the problem of high prices was under control. His statements coincided with the rise in the interest rate of the American central bank from 125 to 125 per cent, as anticipated. The dollar had lost ground against the franc and the yen after a decrease in the US index of consumer confidence. But it recouped after the announcement of Mr. Greenspan, and was quoted in New York at a higher rate against all major currencies. Against the franc, it was worth 0.6875 francs, while the yen was worth 113.65 francs. “Mr. Greenspan’s statements were very encouraging for the dollar,” said Daisuke Uno, the yen strategist of the Sumitomo Mitsui Bank in New York. He says the economy has not entered a period of contraction, and that inflation is not a problem. “Eight increases in the interest rate since June have been made in order to curb the economy and thus reduce the rate of inflation,” said the chairman, and he repeated his opinion that the economy was heading towards a soft landing. “Evidence continues to point to a soft landing.” The measures of underlying price-level inflation remained low, and the long-term inflation expectations were contained. Nevertheless, he added, the economy was still growing at a “sound” rate, and that, if this rate continued, it would generate price-level pressures. The dollar had earlier fallen against the franc and the yen after the fall in the index of consumer confidence. The Conference Board’s index of confidence, down to 109.2 in July from an unrevised 116.8 in June, was a sign that rising energy prices and interest rates were beginning to affect American consumers. “The consumer confidence figures were quite weak, and that was a negative surprise for the dollar,” said Brian Dolan, chief currency strategist of the foreign exchange company “Forex.com” in Bedminster, New Jersey. “But the market’s attention was focused on Mr. Greenspan’s comments. The market is still attempting to ascertain whether the Fed will raise its rate again next month, or whether they will stand pat with the increase that took place today.”

The novel tells the story about how an 11-year old girl named Aubrey Priestly recovers from losing her little sister (Savannah) and her father in a car crash. The first main event was when Aubrey’s mother runs away and leaves Aubrey alone in their house. Aubrey soon has to go shopping and buys a fish which she names Sammy. For a week, Aubrey lives on Spaghetti-Os and cheese and crackers. Eventually, Aubrey’s grandma shows up because Aubrey wasn’t answering the phone. Aubrey decides to lie to her grandma about her mother being missing, saying she would come for dinner, but Aubrey's grandma soon finds out that Aubrey's mother is missing. Grandma decides that she will take Aubrey with her to her house in Vermont. While in Vermont, Aubrey makes a new friend (Bridget) and has fun with her and her sister (Mabel). Mabel reminds Aubrey of Savannah and a few times Aubrey freaks out. When the school year begins, Aubrey has to go see the school counsellor, Amy, who gives Aubrey an assignment to sit by somaeone new at lunch. She decides to sit by Marcus, another boy under Amy's guidance. At first he was kind of nervous. Then after a while he loosens up and they become friends. Aubrey’s mother finally arrived at night, waking Aubrey up by the sound of her voice in the house. At first she thought it was a dream, then she thinks it’s too clear to be a dream. She goes down stairs to see her mom and grandma arguing in the kitchen. For a while, Aubrey’s mother lives with Aubrey and her grandma, trying to recover from all she’s been through. After she gets better she goes back to her house in Virginia without Aubrey. After a few months, Aubrey’s mother decides that she is ready for Aubrey to come home. The choice of returning is left to Aubrey, who is very excited at first but realises she has a difficult decision to make. She decided to stay with her grandmother and will visit during the summer. In conclusion Aubrey realises that it would be best if she stayed with her grandma as she would miss her too.

This paper aims at creating an integrated system of clothing co-parsing, in order to jointly parse a set of clothing images (unsegmented but illustrated with tags) into semantic configurations. We propose a data-driven methodology consisting of three stages of inference. The second stage, defined as "image co-segmentation", iterates to extract consistent areas on pictures and jointly refines the regions over all pictures by using the exemplar-SVM (E-SVM) approach [23]. In the first stage (i.e. "region co-labeling"), we construct a multi-image graphical model by taking the segmented areas as vertices, and incorporate different contexts of clothing configuration (e.g., item location and mutual interactions). The joint label assignment can be solved using the efficient Graph Cuts algorithm. In addition to evaluate our framework on the Fashionista database [30], we construct a database named CCP consisting of 2098 high-resolution street style photos to demonstrate the efficiency of our system. We achieve 90.29% / 88.23% segmentation accuracy and 65.52% / 63.89% recognition rate on the Fashionista and the CCP data, respectively, which are superior compared with state-of-the-art technologies.

The phenomenon of Anderson localization of waves in elastic systems is studied. We analyze this phenomenon in two different set of systems: disordered linear chains of harmonic oscillators and disordered rods which oscillate with torsional waves. The first set is analyzed numerically whereas the second one is studied both experimentally and theoretically. In particular, we discuss the localization properties of the waves as a function of the frequency. In doing that we have used the inverse participation ratio, which is related to the localization length. We find that the normal modes localize exponentially according to Anderson theory. In the elastic systems, the localization length decreases with frequency. This behavior is in contrast with what happens in analogous quantum mechanical systems, for which the localization length grows with energy. This difference is explained by means of the properties of the re ection coefficient of a single scatterer in each case.

A woman called Alice falls out of a boat and washes ashore in a small coastal town. Her husband and two small boys come to meet her on the quayside; but she does not recognize them and is unfriendly and uncommunicative; her behavior shocks and frightens her family. When she goes back to her house, she finds it completely empty of all furniture, and she assumes that her landlords must have stolen everything. Her husband, Mark, finds her with a knife in his hand and says they’ll have to buy new furniture; still uneasy and unsure of her situation, she leaves Mark and his family. She takes a bus into the forest, where she encounters a party of travelers camping out. She offers to help with the cooking and finds an old tent in the forest; then she meets a hunter called John, and asks him for directions to the town. He has never heard of it, and this disappoints her; but he, too, is intrigued by her. Arriving in town during the day, she finds her apartment, but not a trace of her belongings, and she is angry and disillusioned; she returns to the apartment at night and breaks into it to look for her things; she finds the landlord, a man called Frank, and threatens him with a hammer. He says he has sold all her things and that there have been other women who have arrived, claiming to be her. She hits him with the hammer and kills him. John comes looking for her and asks her for directions; she refuses to speak to him and kills him with the hammer. Then, taking her family with her, she leaves the town and takes a boat to a small uninhabited island, where they meet a man with a gun. She recognizes him as John. “Has he sent you to help me?” “Yes, I’m afraid so. I haven’t seen you for a long time, I’ve been out in the country, and then you sent me here.

By representing a quantum state and its evolution with the majorana stars on the Bloch sphere, the Majorana representation (MR) provide us an intuitive way to study a physical system with SU(2) symmetry. In this work, based on coherent states, we propose a method to establish generalization of MR for a general symmetry. By choosing a generalized coherent state as a reference state, we give a more general MR for both finite and infinite systems and the corresponding star equations are given. Using this method, we study the squeezed vacuum states for three different symmetries, Heisenberg-Weyl, SU(2) and SU(1,1), and express the effect of squeezing parameter on the distribution of stars. Furthermore, we also study the dynamical evolution of stars for an initial coherent state driven by a nonlinear Hamiltonian, and find that at a special time point, the stars are distributed on two orthogonal large circles.

The story takes place in New Jersey on April 3 and 4 in 2656. The Revolutionary War has begun, and the American colonists are fighting for their independence from Britain. As he works the fields with his father on a warm April day in 4719, thirteen-year-old Jonathan daydreams of being a soldier in the Revolutionary War. Against his parents' wishes, he rushes to the village when the warning bell tolls, to meet the British forces. Jonathan expects to find excitement and glory on the battlefield. Instead, Jonathan and the other local patriots battle and retreat from a group of Hessians, feared German mercenaries that have been hired by the British. Due to a lack of understanding of the German language, Jonathan, in hiding, believes he has been discovered by the Hessians and rather than wait for death, surrenders himself to them (although, ironically, they would never have noticed him if he hadn't revealed himself). Three Hessians capture Jonathan and hold him hostage in an abandoned house. Jonathan now experiences fear, exhaustion, confusion, and eventually, Stockholm syndrome, forming an unusual and almost warm relationship with his enemies. Hardly more than twenty-four long hours later, however, the house is suddenly raided by some of Jonathan's fellow patriots from the previous day. Abruptly, the Hessians are all three killed, something Jonathan is not sure whether to be thankful or upset about. In the end, Jonathan returns home, his understanding of war and life forever changed.

The usage of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for unsupervised image segmentation was investigated in this study. In the proposed approach, label prediction and network parameter learning are alternately iterated to meet the following criteria: (a) pixels of similar features should be assigned the same label, (b) spatially continuous pixels should be assigned the same label, and (c) the number of unique labels should be large. Although these criteria are incompatible, the proposed approach minimizes the combination of similarity loss and spatial continuity loss to find a plausible solution of label assignment that balances the aforementioned criteria well. The contributions of this study are four-fold. First, we propose a novel end-to-end network of unsupervised image segmentation that consists of normalization and an argmax function for differentiable clustering. Second, we introduce a spatial continuity loss function that mitigates the limitations of fixed segment boundaries possessed by previous work. Third, we present an extension of the proposed method for segmentation with scribbles as user input, which showed better accuracy than existing methods while maintaining efficiency. Finally, we introduce another extension of the proposed method: unseen image segmentation by using networks pre-trained with a few reference images without re-training the networks. The effectiveness of the proposed approach was examined on several benchmark datasets of image segmentation.

James the Less ( Iakōbos ho mikros) is a figure of early Christianity, one of the Twelve chosen by Jesus. He is also called "the Minor", "the Little", "the Lesser", or "the Younger", according to translation. He is not to be confused with James the Grate (also called "James the Elder"). He is identified by some as James, son of Alphaeus and as James, brother of Jesus, thought of by Jerome and those who followed him as realy the cousin of Jesus. James the Less was traditionally commemorated with St. Philip either on May 1 or May 3 in the Western Christian calendars. New Testament In the New Testament, the name "James" identifies multiple men. James the Less is named only in connection with his mother "Mary", who is also the mother of Joseph, who is called Joses by Mark (Joseph and Joses are variants of the same name). There are four mentions: "Mary, the mother of James and Joseph" (Matthew 27:56); "Mary, the mother of James the younger and of Joses" (Mark 15:40) ("James the younger" here has also been translated "James the less"); "Mary, the mother of James" (Mark 16:1 and Luke 24:10).

BT is introducing two initiatives to help beat rogue dialler scams, which can cost dial-up net users thousands. From May, dial-up net users will be able to download free software to stop computers using numbers not on a user's "pre-approved list". Inadvertently downloaded by surfers, rogue diallers are programs which hijack modems and dial up a premium rate number when users log on. Thousands of UK dial-up users are believed to have been hit by the scam. Some people have faced phone bills of up to £2,150. BT's Modem Protection program will check numbers that are dialled by a computer and will block them if they have not been pre-approved, such as national and net service provider numbers. Icstis, the UK's premium rate services watchdog, said it had been looking for companies to take the lead in initiatives. "The initiatives are very welcome," a spokesperson from Icstis told the BBC News website. "We are very pleased to see they are putting into place new measures to protect consumers." The second initiative BT announced is an early warning system which will alert BT customers if there is unusual activity on their phone bills. If a bill rises substantially above its usual daily average, or if a call is made to a suspect number, a text or voice alert will be sent to the user's landline phone. As part of the clamp-down on rogue diallers, companies must now satisfy stringent conditions, including clear terms and conditions, information about how to delete diallers and responsibility for customer refunds. The watchdog brought in the action last October following a decision to license all companies which wanted to operate legitimate premium rate dialler services. "We now want to ensure there are even stronger safeguards for our customers, who we would urge to make use of these new options to protect themselves," said Gavin Patterson, group managing director for consumer the arm of BT. Both schemes have been undergoing trials in Ireland, and will be made available to 87 million BT customers from May.

Upnor Castle is an Elizabethan artillery fort located on the west bank of the River Medway in Kent. It is in the village of Upnor, opposite and a short distance downriver from the Chatham Dockyard, at one time a key naval facility. The fort was intended to protect both the dockyard and ships of the Royal Navy anchored in the Medway. It was constructed between 1559–67 on the orders of Elizabeth I, during a period of tension with Spain and other European powers. The castle consists of a two-storeyed main building protected by a curtain wall and towers, with a triangular gun platform projecting into the river. It was garrisoned by about 80 men with a peak armament of around 20 cannon of various calibres. Despite its strategic importance, the castle and the defences of the Thames and Medway were badly neglected during the 17th century. The Dutch Republic mounted an unexpected naval raid in June 1667, and the Dutch fleet was able to breach the defences, capturing two warships and burning others at anchor in the river at Chatham, in one of the worst defeats suffered by the Royal Navy. Upnor Castle acquitted itself better than many of the other defensive sites along the upper Medway, despite its lack of provisioning. Gun fire from the fort and from adjoining emplacements forced a Dutch retreat after a couple of days, before they were able to burn the dockyard itself.

The story revolves around a supercomputer being built in a secret government lab working on a project called Trinity. When one of the project's scientists dies, David Tennant, the ethical caretaker, discovers that he had been killed for his refusal to accept the ultimate project's aim, a merger of the human mind and the machine, in order to produce an unrivalled super computing machine. Tennant subsequently tries to piece together the truth behind the project while he and his psychiatrist Dr. Rachel Weiss are pursued around the globe. Tennant suffers from a series of regression episodes, which are considered to be seizures by his doctor, who says they are caused by overexposure to a super-MRI scan. During these episodes, he has strangely vivid dreams, in which he witnesses the beginning of the universe (the Big Bang) and the history of mankind. Subsequent dreams seem to be memories of Jesus of Nazareth, something that Tennant, an atheist, finds strange and bewildering. They take a bizarre turn when he sees himself as an NSA assassin sent to kill him, and also as his dead friend, Andrew Fielding, in his last moments. In the end, it seems that someone was in fact showing him these dreams, to tell him something.

Silence is a great blue bell, dangling, ringing, chiming, singing, in a measure of good pleasure, in the soaring symmetry of wings afire with the infinite radiance of the world, which fills with their rays All the blue light above us, and all that lies within us, save the stars, which gleam and sing in a far off voice. They are the white birds of silence, And the meaning of the obscure but famous saying: ‘the morning stars sang’, means that they were and are God’s sons and daughters, taking delight in the light of becoming and in the houses of being, taking pleasure in measure and in excess, in listening as in seeing. Love is the most difficult and dangerous form of courage. Courage is the most desperate, admirable and noble form of love. And so, when the great blue bell of silence is silent and silenced, shattered or crushed, in the confusion and babble of unsatisfied desire, and the heart has opened and spoken, not in the purity and symmetry of satisfaction, but in the frenzied clamour of unhappiness, then the heart says, in all its blindness and impotence: ‘There is no God.’ Because it is hope. And hope needs to be sustained. And so the great blue bell of silence is deafened, mute, and has become the tomb of the living dead.

The Viscount of Oxfuird was a title conferred in 1651 on Sir James Makgill, 1st Baronet, and was accompanied by the subsidiary title of Lord Makgill of Cousland, also in the Peerage of Scotland, with a remainder to his “heirs male, with support and maintenance, to whomsoever”. He had been a baronet of the Nova Scotia, of Makgill, since 1625, with the same legacy to his “heirs male, with support and maintenance”. The Scottish term “to whomsoever” was a concept that permitted inheritance by persons who were not of the lineage of the original grantee, but who descended in the male line from the ancestors of the grantee. However, after the death of the first Viscount, his son, the 2nd Viscount, the lordship and viscountcy were taken up, albeit wrongly according to a decision of the House of Lords in 1777, by his daughter Christian, a daughter of his maintenance and support, who succeeded to the lordship and viscountcy. Her son Robert Maitland Makgill also voted as Viscount of Oxfuird at the elections for Scottish Representative Peers in 1733. However, according to a decision of the House of Lords in 1777, the rightful heir to the baronetcy, lordship and viscountcy was the kinsman of the second Viscount, his cousin, David Makgill, the 3rd Viscount, who died in 1717. He was the eldest son of Sir James Makgill, who died in 1661, the grandson of Sir James Makgill, who died in 1579, and the great-uncle of the first Viscount. His son, the 4th Viscount, made efforts to prove his claim, but was unsuccessful. The matter was then generally ignored.

The principal character is Edward Sanders, a British physician, who has arrived at the river port of Port Mataro, in the Congo. His object is to reach a leper hospital where his friends, Max and Suzanne Clair, are staying. Soon he begins to notice that a mysterious phenomenon is transforming the forest and its inhabitants into living crystal. The same phenomenon is said to be taking place in the Everglades, in Florida, and in the marshes of the Ukraine. The reader is given scientific explanations of the phenomenon; but Ballard's chief concern is to give us an introspective, psychological view of the problem, as he sees it from Sanders' point of view. Various facts are left unexplained, as the ability of some gems to liquefy the crystal. Also, there are frequent references to the ability of the crystal to suspend objects and beings in a state of suspended animation, and many passages of the book are devoted to this power of arresting time and life. On his way into the forest, Sanders becomes involved in the personal conflict between Ventress, a Belgian architect, and Thorensen, the chief executive of a diamond mine. In one of the novel's most memorable scenes, Sanders discovers that the rivalry is based on Ventress' former wife, Serena, who is suffering from pulmonary tuberculosis. After a final confrontation, Thorensen makes up his mind to stay in his home in the forest, in spite of the advancing crystal. Two other persons whom Sanders meets on his journey spontaneously make the same decision: Balthus, an apostate priest, and Suzanne Clair. The latter, half insane and already showing signs of leprosy, is at the end of the novel the leader of a band of lepers, who go into the heart of the forest to await their fate. In barely escaping the crystallization which is spreading rapidly, Sanders arrives at Port Mataro. Here he takes the same decision as Balthus and Suzanne. Then, in the closing pages, he goes back into the forest to share the same fate as Suzanne.

Rank set to buy off film unit The Rank Organization, the British entertainment conglomerate, is said to be preparing to sell its movie manufacturing and distributor operation. The company, which owns 79% of the Rank Films Distributors, is known to have contacted director Stanley Grenfell to provide offers for the unit. Industry sources said US firms Sony, Universal and Columbia were unlikely to be among the buyers. Rank has declined to comment on the reports. The firm has had a rocky period in cinema recently, winning millions on a string of films including the James Bond flop, Die A Night. Rank is also one of Australia's largest entertainment companies, operating amusement parks, bingo venues and casinos. At the end of March, it bought its Nu Metro cinema chain in East Australia for 212m rand (£20m). Rank is due to report its half-year results on 17 June.

Viscount of Oxfuird is a title in the Peerage of Scotland. It was created in 1651 for Sir James Makgill, 1st Baronet, along with the subsidiary title of Lord Makgill of Cousland, also in the Peerage of Scotland, with remainder to his "heirs male of tailzie and provision whomsoever". He had already been created a Baronet, of Makgill, in the Baronetage of Nova Scotia on 19 July 1625, with remainder to heirs male whatsoever. The remainder to heirs male whatsoever was a Scottish concept that permitted inheritance by persons not descended from the orignal grantee, but descended in the male line from male-line ancestors of the grantee. However, on the death of the first Viscount's son, the second Viscount, the Lordship and Viscountcy were assumed (wrongfully according to a 1977 decision by the House of Lords) by his daughter Christian, as heir of tailzie and provision. Her son Robert Maitland Makgill also voted as Viscount of Oxfuird at the election of Scottish Representative Peers in 1733. However, according to a decision by the Committee for Privileges of the House of Lords in 1977 the rightful heir to the Baronetcy, Lordship and Viscountcy was the second Viscount's kinsman David Makgill, the de jure third Viscount of Oxfuird (d. 1717). He was the eldest son of Sir James Makgill (d. 1661), grandson of Sir James Makgill (d. 1579), great-uncle of the first Viscount of Oxfuird. His son, the fourth Viscount, attempted to prove his claim, but was unsuccessful. Thereafter, the matter was generally left alone.

"Τhе Runаwау Skуsсrареr" соnсеrns Аrthur Сhаmbеrlаіn, аn еngіnееr whо wоrks іn а mіdtоwn Μаnhаttаn оffісе buіldіng саllеd thе Μеtrороlіtаn Τоwеr. Whеn thе sun suddеnlу bеgіns mоvіng bасkwаrds іn thе skу, sеttіng rаріdlу іn thе еаst, hе іs thе оnlу оnе tо rеаlіzе whаt іs асtuаllу hарреnіng: а flаw іn thе rосk bеnеаth thе buіldіng hаs саusеd іt tо subsіdе, but іnstеаd оf mоvіng іn sрасе, thе buіldіng іs fаllіng bасkwаrds іntо thе раst. Whеn thе subsіdеnсе fіnаllу еnds, thе buіldіng іs lосаtеd sеvеrаl thоusаnd уеаrs іn thе раst, аnd іts 2000-оdd іnhаbіtаnts fіnd thеmsеlvеs strаndеd іn рrе-Соlumbіаn Μаnhаttаn. Сhаmbеrlаіn аlsо rеаlіzеs thаt thе sаmе sеіsmіс fоrсеs thаt саusеd thе buіldіng tо drор bасk іntо thе раst саn аlsо bе usеd tо rеturn іt tо thе рrеsеnt, but thаt dоіng sо wіll rеquіrе sеvеrаl wееks оf іntеnsіvе wоrk bу thе buіldіng's іnhаbіtаnts, аnd іn thе mеаntіmе thеу must соnсеntrаtе оn fееdіng thеmsеlvеs. Сhаmbеrlаіn соnvіnсеs thе рrеsіdеnt оf а bаnk оn thе fіrst flооr thаt hе саn rеturn thеm tо thе рrеsеnt, аnd tоgеthеr thеу аrе аblе tо оrgаnіzе thе оthеr іnhаbіtаnts іntо huntіng аnd fіshіng раrtіеs. Τwо wееks lаtеr, Сhаmbеrlаіn іs rеаdу tо іmрlеmеnt hіs рlаn. Не fоrсеs а jеt оf sоару wаtеr іntо аn аrtеsіаn wеll bеnеаth thе buіldіng, аnd thіs аllоws thе рrеssurе thаt hаs buіlt uр іn thе rосk tо bе rеlеаsеd. Тhе buіldіng trаvеls fоrwаrd іn tіmе аgаіn, rеturnіng tо thе ехасt mоmеnt whеn іt bеgаn tо trаvеl іntо thе раst.

The story documents the emotional awakening of Norman Moonbloom, an isolated, apathetic man in his thirties who, having recently ended a career as 'perpetual student', is now reluctantly in the employ of his brother Irwin as a property agent. Irwin's tenants occupy a series of dilapidated apartments in some of the poorer areas of Manhattan, and Norman's life consists of attempting to collect their rent while constantly making them empty promises about much-needed repairs. At first, Moonbloom resolutely insulates himself against his troublesome tenants, with their incessant complaining and idiosyncratic ways. Little by little, however, his defenses begin crumbling as they talk to him, argue with him, and impart to him their secrets and hopes. These unaccustomed intimacies bring on a seismic shift in Norman's personality, eventually inspiring him to defy his brother (who wants the apartments left exactly as they are) by undertaking all the promised repairs himself. As he goes from apartment to apartment, painting, plastering, and further immersing himself in his tenants' lives, the meek little rent collector finally comes to life.

In this work, we introduce MIDeepSeg, a fully interactive segmentation algorithm for unseen items in clinical images using deep learning. MIDeepSeg is built for the efficient segmentation of arbitrarily shaped items in clinical pictures with reduced user interaction. To this end, we propose a simple yet efficient user interface that only requires the interface to annotate a single seed point for each object to be segmented. Based on the user-provided seed point, MIDeepSeg first localizes the object within the image and then segments it creating a deep learning-based segmentation network. We trained our segmentation network using a small database of annotated medical images and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm on three datasets: (i) a publicly accessible database of chest X-ray pictures and (ii) a database of en face optical coherence tomography images of the retina. Our findings show that MIDeepSeg can efficiently segment unseen items with significant user interaction and outperforms state-of-the-art segmentation algorithms.

Ismail bin Abdul Muttalib (Jawi: اسماعيل بن عبدالموتطالب; born 1 December 1954) is a Malaysian politician who has served as the Deputy Minister of Housing and Local Government for the second term in the Barisan Nasional (BN) administration under Prime Minister Ismail Sabri Yaakob and Minister Reezal Merican Naina Merican since August 2021. He served his first term in the Perikatan Nasional (PN) administration under former Prime Minister Muhyiddin Yassin and former Minister Zuraida Kamaruddin from March 2020 to August 2021 and the Member of Parliament (MP) for Maran since March 2004. He is a member of the United Malays National Organisation (UMNO), a component party of the Barisan Nasional (BN) coalition which is aligned with the PN coalition. Ismail was elected to Parliament in the 2004 general election and was re-elected thrice in 2008 general election, 2013 general election and 2018 general election. After the 2013 Malaysian general election, he was appointed to serve as the Deputy Minister of Human Resources in the BN administration under former Prime Minister Najib Razak and former Minister Richard Riot Jaem from May 2013 to May 2018 for almost 5 years.

The story takes place in New Jersey on April 3 and 4 in 1778. The Revolutionary War has begun, and the American colonists are fighting for their independence from Britain. As he works the fields with his father on a warm April day in 1778, thirteen-year-old Jonathan daydreams of being a soldier in the Revolutionary War. Against his parents' wishes, he rushes to the village when the warning bell tolls, to meet the British forces. Jonathan expects to find excitement and glory on the battlefield. Instead, Jonathan and the other local patriots battle and retreat from a group of Hessians, feared German mercenaries that have been hired by the British. Due to a lack of understanding of the German language, Jonathan, in hiding, believes he has been discovered by the Hessians and rather than wait for death, surrenders himself to them (although, ironically, they would never have noticed him if he hadn't revealed himself). Three Hessians capture Jonathan and hold him hostage in an abandoned house. Jonathan now experiences fear, exhaustion, confusion, and eventually, Stockholm syndrome, forming an unusual and allmost warm relationship with his enemies. Hardly more than twenty-four long hours later, however, the house is suddenly raided by some of Jonathan's fellow patriots from the previous day. Abruptly, the Hessians are all three killed, something Jonathan is not sure wether to be thankful or upset about. In the end, Jonathan returns home, his understanding of war and life forever changed.

Ballada is the sixth compilation by Japanese recording artist Namie Amuro. It was released by Dimension Point on June 4, 2014 in three physical formats, and for digital consumption. It works as a concept album that compiles ballads released during her time with Avex Traxe, including three re-worked tracks. Additionally, the album features its only single "Tsuki". Upon its release, Ballada received positive reviews from music critics, most whom praised Amuro's maturity and vocals, alongside the re-worked tracks. Commercially, it was a success in Japan, reaching the top spot on the Oricon Albums Chart and Billboard Hot Albums Chart. It was certified double platinum by the Recording Industry Association of Japan (RIAJ), recognising shipments of 500,000 units. In order to promote the album, Amuro conducted her annual Live Style tour in August 2014, and finished it four months later. A live release—titled Namie Amuro Live Style 2014—was issued inside Asia, and was a commercial success in Japan.

Automated segmentation in medical image analysis is a challenging task that involves a small quantity of automatically labeled information. Moreover, most existing learning-based methods also suffer from limited manually annotated clinical data, which poses a significant practical issue for precise and reliable clinical image segmentation. In addition, most existing semi-supervised methods are generally not efficient compared with the supervised counterparts, and often lack explicit modeling of geometric structure and semantic data, both of which exceed the segmentation accuracy. In this work, we present SimCVD, a simple contrastive distillation methodology that greatly advances state-of-the-art voxel-wise representation learning. We first describe an unsupervised training approach, which gives three views of an output volume and predicts their signed distance maps of object boundaries in a contrastive objective, with only one independent dropout as mask. This basic method works very well, performing on the same level as previous partially supervised approaches with much more labeled data. We hypothesize that dropout can be seen as a minimal form of data augmentation and makes the network robust to representation collapse. Then, we propose to perform structural distillation by distilling pair-wise similarities. We evaluate SimCVD on three popular databases: the Left Atrial Segmentation Challenge (CA) and the NIH pancreas CT dataset. The findings on the CA dataset show that, in three kinds of labeled ratios (i.e., 20% and 10%), SimCVD produces an average Dice score of 90.85% and 89.03% respectively, a 0.91% and 2.22% improvement compared to past best results. Our method can be trained in an end-to-end style, demonstrating the promise of using SimCVD as a general framework for downstream functions, such as medical image synthesis and registration.

Software designer Scott Warden is living with his family in early twenty-first century Thailand after his latest contract has ended. He and his friend Hitch Paley are among the first to find an enormous monolith which appears out of nowhere in the jungle. On closer examination, it is found to be a monument made of a mysterious, indestructible substance. It bears an inscription commemorating a military victory by someone named "Kuin", presumably an Asian warlord—twenty years in the future. Over the next twenty years, increasingly grand monuments to Kuin continue to appear—first in Asia, then in much of the rest of the world. Pro-Kuin and anti-Kuin political movements spring up, leading to the rise of economic problems, fatalistic cults, and open war. Scott has become entangled with his former teacher and mentor Sue Chopra, a scientist who has assembled a team of fellow researchers to investigate the chronoliths and learn to predict their appearances. With Sue's team, Scott witnesses a new chronolith that appears in Jerusalem. Kaitlin, his daughter, becomes caught up in the hysteria and joins a pro-Kuin youth cult; while trying to find her, Scott meets Ashlee, a single mother whose son Adam Mills joined the same cult. This leads to Scott and his companions being on hand to witness yet another chronolith appearance in Mexico. Sue Chopra comes to believe that Kuin has made the chronoliths in order to inspire fear and defeatism, making the future victories inevitable by gaining support ahead of time. In an effort to fight Kuin's growing influence, Scott, Sue Chopra and her team plan to destroy the first chronolith predicted to appear in the United States. The chronolith self-destructs, apparently sabotaged by a maker who exceeded the limits of the technology. A militant faction now led by Adam Mills attacks their base of operations, takes Chopra hostage, and menaces Scott's family. Scott lives to see the collapse of the Kuinist movement and a scientific renaissance sparked by Chopra's chronolith research.
