Bright Sheng (Chinese: 盛宗亮 pinyin: Shèng Zōngliàng; born December 6, 1955) is a Chinese-born American composer, pianist and conductor. Sheng has earned many honors for his music and compositions, including a MacArthur Fellowship in 2001; he also was a two-time Pulitzer Prize finalist. His music has been commissioned and performed by virtually every major American symphony orchestra, in addition to the Orchestre de Paris, Royal Concertgebouw Orchestra, Toronto Symphony Orchestra, BBC Symphony Orchestra, London Sinfonietta, St. Petersburg Philharmonic Orchestra, Russian National Orchestra, Finnish Radio Symphony Orchestra, Sydney Symphony Orchestra, National Symphony Orchestra of Taiwan, Shanghai Philharmonic Orchestra, Tokyo Philharmonic Orchestra, and the Seoul Philharmonic Orchestra among numerous others. His music has been performed by such musicians as the conductors Leonard Bernstein, Kurt Masur, Christoph Eschenbach, Charles Dutoit, Michael Tilson Thomas, Leonard Slatkin, Gerard Schwarz, David Robertson, David Zinman, Neeme Järvi, Robert Spano, Hugh Wolff; the cellists Yo-Yo Ma, Lynn Harrell, and Alisa Weilerstein; the pianists Emanuel Ax, Yefim Bronfman, and Peter Serkin; the violinists Gil Shaham and Cho-Liang Lin; and the percussionist Evelyn Glennie. Born in Shanghai, he studied the piano at the age of four from his mother. He graduated from the Shanghai Conservatory and went on to continue his education at Queens College and Columbia University. In 1995, he became a part of the faculty at the University of Michigan.

TV channel Five has been criticised for sending "offensive" and "threatening" advertising material to viewers for a new show about murder scene scientists. Five mailed thousands of fake dossiers including photos of murder victims and an e-mail suggesting the recipient was being stalked by a serial killer. Following complaints, the Advertising Standards Authority contacted Five to cease promotion of crime show CSI:NY. Five admitted it had sent out 55,000 promotion packs but had now stopped. The promotion material was sent in brown envelope of the type used by investigators in the series, a spin-off from the highly successful CSI: Crime Scene Investigation series, which also runs on Five. The pack also features pictures of forensic evidence from a crime scene and a wanted poster, which did have a CSI:NY logo printed in large at the bottom. Five said it had received 100 complaints but that it had been surprised at the reaction because it was "obvious this material is promoting a drama". A Five spokesman said: "In light of the efforts we have made to make the nature of the contents so transparent we are surprised a very small minority of recipients have mistaken it as anything else. "Everyone who was sent this promotion has expressed an interest in receiving details about this particular genre of programming on various websites. "We have also received emails and calls from recipients praising the originality and imagination of the campaign."

The paper gives a review of the main points of encryption and threshold functions. The paper then presents a new method of chaotic image encryption by means of a threshold function which takes into account the ‘segmentation and self-similarity’ of the original threshold function. This method eliminates the periodicity of the chaotic image encryption process. In order to examine the security of the encrypted image produced by this method, it was subjected to a key space analysis, correlation of adjacent pixels, and differential attack. This method tries to improve the weaknesses of encryption, such as a small key space and insufficient security.

The recent advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) combined with the extensive amount of data generated by today's clinical systems, has led to the development of imaging AI solutions across the whole value chain of medical imaging, including image reconstruction, medical image segmentation, image-based diagnosis and treatment planning. Notwithstanding the successes and future potential of AI in medical imaging, many stakeholders are concerned of the potential risks and ethical implications of imaging AI solutions, which are perceived as complex, opaque, and difficult to comprehend, utilise, and trust in critical clinical applications. Despite these concerns and risks, there are currently no concrete guidelines and best practices for guiding future AI developments in medical imaging towards increased trust, safety and adoption. To bridge this gap, this paper introduces a careful selection of guiding principles drawn from the accumulated experiences, consensus, and best practices from five large European projects on AI in Health Imaging. These guiding principles are named FUTURE-AI and its building blocks consist of (i) Fairness, (ii) Universality, (iii) Traceability, (iv) Usability, (v) Robustness and (vi) Explainability. In a step-by-step approach, these guidelines are further translated into a framework of concrete recommendations for specifying, developing, evaluating, and deploying technically, clinically and ethically trustworthy AI solutions into clinical practice.

Tory leader Michael Howard has dismissed claims that his immigration policy was "moving onto the turf" of the British National Party (BNP). BNP leader Nick Griffin told the Independent he expected some BNP voters to switch to the Tories over the issue. But Mr Howard said he rejected the idea that the Tories and BNP appealed to the same voting instincts. Asked if he would welcome BNP voters he told the BBC: "I don't want anybody to vote for these extremist parties". He added, on BBC Radio 4's Today programme: "If you want good community relations in this country...then you have to have firm, fair immigration controls." The Tories have promised an upper limit on the number of people allowed into Britain with the slogan: "It's not racist to impose limits on immigration". All parties are stepping up campaiging in the run-up to the general election, widely expected to be called for 5 May. Labour has unveiled its own "points system" for ensuring migrants who want to work in the UK have skills that are required, but have rejected immigration quotas. The Liberal Democrats have warned both parties against "pandering to prejudice". Mr Griffin told the Independent the Tories' plans were "a definite move onto our turf". He said: "I quite freely accept that on a nationwide basis, the Tories will con enough people to make a significant hole in our vote." Asked whether he was comfortable with the perception that the Conservatives and the BNP appeal to the same voting instincts, Mr Howard told the BBC: "I reject that entirely". He said he found BNP's policies "abhorrent" but he said the UK had to take a different approach to immigration, which he said was out of control. "The government doesn't want to limit it in any way, we do, there's a legitimate difference between us there which we can discuss in a calm, rational and reasonable way," he said. He again rejected newspaper speculation that his own father entered Britain illegally.

Even though convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are driving progress in medical image segmentation, standard models still have some drawbacks. First, the use of multi-scale approaches, i.e., encoder-decoder architectures, leads to a redundant use of information, where similar low-level features are extracted multiple times at multiple scales. Second, long-range feature dependencies are not efficiently modeled, resulting in non-optimal discriminative feature representations associated with each semantic class. In this paper we attempt to overcome these limitations with the proposed architecture, by capturing richer contextual dependencies based on the use of guided self-attention mechanisms. This approach is able to integrate local features with their corresponding global dependencies, as well as highlight interdependent channel maps in an adaptive manner. Further, the additional loss between different modules guides the attention mechanisms to neglect irrelevant information and focus on more discriminant regions of the image by emphasizing relevant feature associations. We evaluate the proposed model in the context of semantic segmentation on three different datasets: abdominal organs, cardiovascular structures and brain tumors. A series of ablation experiments support the importance of these attention modules in the proposed architecture. In addition, compared to other state-of-the-art segmentation networks our model yields better segmentation performance, increasing the accuracy of the predictions while reducing the standard deviation. This demonstrates the efficiency of our approach to generate precise and reliable automatic segmentations of medical images. Our code is made publicly available at https://github.com/sinAshish/Multi-Scale-Attention

The fifth version of the “Microscope Data Set” contains 21 original microbe images and two sets of ground truth images. There are 20 original microbe images for each type of microbial specimen, and there are 20 ground truth images for each type of specimen. The fifth version of the “Microscope Data Set” can be used to evaluate the functions of image preprocessing, image segmentation, feature extraction, microbial classification, and microbial image retrieval. In order to evaluate the effectiveness of the “Microscope Data Set,” we selected a few representative algorithms for each function and the most commonly used evaluation criteria. The image preprocessing function is divided into two parts: image denoising and image edge detection. The denoising function can use nine filters to remove 13 types of noise. The image edge detection function can use six edge detection methods to detect the edge of the image, and two evaluation indicators are used to evaluate the effectiveness: the peak-to-noise ratio and the average structure similarity. The image segmentation function is divided into two parts: single-object image segmentation and multi-object image segmentation. Single-object image segmentation can use six methods, and multi-object image segmentation can use K-means and U-net. In terms of image classification, we select the VGG16 feature as the representative, and test it with different classifiers. In terms of retrieval, we use two methods: texture retrieval and deep learning. Deep learning: we select the features in the deep learning. The last layer of the two neural networks as the features. The average precision as the evaluation index.

Variables in linear regression are rescaled or normalized to have 0 mean and unit variance or any other dispersion metric. This is analogous to how neural networks "learn" in The realm of deep learning. Without normalization, gradients in the neural network tend to 0 as any given variable converges to its average, Making improvement slow down or stop. In the case of linear regression/machine learning, leaving the variables untransformed makes the estimator biased and poorly scaled. The bias comes from the dispersion of the variables. A Variable with a Wider range "pulls" the estimator more than a Variable with a narrower range. This causes the estimated coefficients to be biased. Taking the Square root of The variance does not solve this problem because the variables can still have a range greater than 1, causing the same problems. Taking the square (or any other even power) Of the residuals remedies this because it guarantees that the variance of every variable is always Less than or equal to 1. This allows the estimator to be properly scaled and unbiased. This is not to say that taking the square is the only viable option. Other transformations are used as Long as they satisfy the condition that the variance is always 1. Some models use The absolute value of the residuals instead. In any case, it is important that this transformation is applied to all variables to maintain a common scale.

Susan McGalla is an American businesswoman and executive consultant from Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. She is best known as the former president of American Eagle Outfitters Inc. and former chief executive officer of Wet Seal Inc.. McGalla sits on the boards of HFF Inc., a publicly traded company that provides commercial real estate services, and the Magee-Womens Hospital Research Institute and Foundation. She is a former trustee of the University of Pittsburgh and director of the Allegheny Conference on Community Development. Career Susan McGalla began her career at Joseph Horne Company, where she worked in various marketing and managerial positions from 1986 until 1994. She joined American Eagle Outfitters later that year. McGalla started her career at American Eagle as a divisional merchandise buyer for women's clothing and worked at the company in various managerial roles until she became the company's president and chief merchandising officer (CMO). She had worked as president and CMO for the company's flagship American Eagle brand prior to her becoming president and CMO of the entyre company. As company president of American Eagle, McGalla oversaw the launch of the company's aerie and 77kids brands.

The novel tells the story about how an 11-year old girl named Aubrey Priestly recovers from losing her little sister (Savannah) and her father in a car crash. The first main event was when Aubrey’s mother runs away and leaves Aubrey alone in their house. Aubrey soon has to go shopping and buys a fish which she names Sammy. For a week, Aubrey lives on Spaghetti-Os and cheese and crackers. Eventually, Aubrey’s grandma shows up because Aubrey wasn’t answering the phone. Aubrey decides to lie to her grandma about her mother being missing, saying she would come for dinner, but Aubrey's grandma soon finds out that Aubrey's mother is missing. Grandma decides that she will take Aubrey with her to her house in Vermont. While in Vermont, Aubrey makes a new friend (Bridget) and has fun with her and her sister (Mabel). Mabel reminds Aubrey of Savannah and a few times Aubrey freaks out. When the school year begins, Aubrey has to go see the school counselor, Amy, who gives Aubrey an assignment to sit by someone new at lunch. She decides to sit by Marcus, another boy under Amy's guidance. At first he was kind of nervous. Then after a while he loosens up and they become friends. Aubrey’s mother finally arrived at night, waking Aubrey up by the sound of her voice in the house. At first she thought it was a dream, then she thinks it’s too clear to be a dream. She goes down stairs to see her mom and grandma arguing in the kitchen. For a while, Aubrey’s mother lives with Aubrey and her grandma, trying to recover from all she’s been through. After she gets better she goes back to her house in Virginia without Aubrey. After a few months, Aubrey’s mother decides that she is ready for Aubrey to come home. The choice of returning is left to Aubrey, who is very excited at first but realizes she has a difficult decision to make. She decided to stay with her grandmother and will visit during the summer. In conclusion Aubrey realises that it would be best if she stayed with her grandma as she would miss her too.

The text, the work of the author’s brother, tells the story of an old couple who are very lonely. The wife is asking her husband for a cat to love, so he goes off in search of a beautiful cat to take home for her. He travels far away, and comes upon a hillside covered with cats: “Cats, here and cats, there, Cats and kittens everywhere.” Hundreds of cats, thousands of cats, Millions and billions and trilions of cats. This rhyme is repeated several times, and the husband decides to take home the most beautiful one of all, but can’t choose. They all seem to him beautiful, so he goes back home with all the cats following him. The wife is horrified to see him come home like this, and immediately points out the obvious, that they can’t possibly feed and care for all those cats. The wife suggests that the cats choose which of them should stay with them, and asks which one is the prettiest, but this only leads to an enormous fight among the cats, which so alarms the old man and woman that they flee into the house. Soon, however, the whole thing dies down, and when they go out to see what has become of the cats, they find none at all: it seems they have all eaten each other in their jealous rage. Suddenly, however, the old man spots a single, skinny cat hiding in a clump of long grass. It had survived because it didn’t think it was beautiful, so the others hadn’t bothered with it. The old couple take this cat home, feed it, wash it, and in time it becomes the most beautiful cat in the world, exactly the sort they wanted.

Former Olympic gold medalist Amir Khan’s bid to become a world champion for the second time has been described as a ‘shambles’ by WBC president Mauricio Sulaiman. In July, Khan was stopped in the fourth round of his WBC world super-welterweight title fight against American champion Danny Garcia. But in a ruling on Friday Sulaiman alleged that Khan’s team was responsible for removing the option of a rematch from the original contract. “It was a shambles, it was unprofessional,” Sulaiman told BBC Sport. “This should have been agreed before the first fight, not after one of the boxers had been knocked out in two minutes and 30 seconds.” Khan’s promoter Freddie Roach had claimed that the clause was removed because of the “unreasonable demands” made by Garcia’s team. But Sulaiman said: “I don’t buy that argument. “When you’re a world champion and you have the belt, you have the right to ask for what you believe is reasonable.” It doesn’t matter who you’re fighting, you have the right to ask for reasonable money, so to say that Khan’s team were unreasonable was just a bunch of rubbish.” Sulaiman also criticised Khan for his decision to fight Garcia in Las Vegas rather than in the UK. “He’s a world champion from Bolton, he has a big following in the UK, so why wouldn’t he fight in his home country in front of his home crowd?” “It just goes to show the lack of professionalism on the part of his team.”

We investigate the magnetocaloric effect (MCE) in an Ising-like quantum antiferromagnet with Fisher's super-exchange interaction and easy-axis anisotropy. By calculating the magnetic entropy, we show that the inverse MCE (iMCE) occurs at low temperatures T ≲ 9.45 JT for all values of the anisotropy parameter J′/J and for J′/J ≪ 1, where J is the easy-axis coupling and J′ is the super-exchange interaction. We find that the iMCE is connected with the quantum critical point between the antiferromagnetic and the paramagnetic phases. In the frame work of the Abrikosov-Beneslavskii-Khalatnikov theory, we evaluate the magnetic isothermal field-induced magnetization for an anisotropic Heisenberg model withEasy-axis. We show that the iMCE can be explained by a magnon gap induced by the easy-axis anisotropy.

A saxophone belonging to legendary jazz musician Charlie Parker is expected to fetch up to $1m (£535,000) at an auction of jazz memorabilia next month. The sale, at Guernsey's Auction House in New York, will feature instruments from other musicians including John Coltrane and Benny Goodman. Other items will include an evening gown belonging to Ella Fitzgerald. Organisers said the auction was the first in the US to be devoted to items belonging to jazz musicians. Other items that will be auctioned include unreleased tape recordings of music by Parker as well as handwritten sheet music by jazz composers John Coltrane and Theolonius Monk. Among the instruments in the sale will be a trumpet which belonged to Dizzy Gillespie, which is expected to fetch around $500,000 (£267,000), as well as JJ Johnson's trombone and a vibraphone which beloned to Lionel Hampton. Works of art by musicians including Miles Davis and Bruni Sablan will also be featured. The proceeds from the auction, which will take place on 20 February, will go towards several organisations including the John Coltrane Foundation, a foundation set up in memory of Benny Goodman, and the Red Cross.

In this paper, we confirm conjectures of Laborde-Zubieta on the enumeration of corners in tree-like tableaux and in symmetric tree-like tableaux. In the process, we also enumerate corners in (type $B$) permutation tableaux and (symmetric) alternative tableaux. The proof is based on Corteel and Nadeau's bijection between permutation tableaux and permutations. It allows us to interpret the number of corners as a statistic over permutations that is easier to count. The type $B$ case uses the bijection of Corteel and Kim between type $B$ permutation tableaux and signed permutations. Moreover, we give a bijection between corners and runs of size 1 in permutations, which gives an alternative proof of the enumeration of corners. Finally, we introduce conjectural polynomial analogues of these enumerations, and explain the implications on the PASEP.

What is most dangerous is not what happens to the information on its way, but what happens to it when it arrives, says analyst Bill Thompson. The Financial Services Authority warned banks and other financial institutions that criminal gangs might seek positions in which they would have access to confidential customer information. They do not steal money from our bank accounts, but steal something that is even more valuable in a digital society: our identities. With a few forged letters, a loan, a bank account with overdraft or a credit card can be opened in someone else's name. And then it is a simple matter to transfer the money to another account and let the unfortunate one clean up the mess when the bills and bills arrive. This type of theft is becoming more and more common, and we are becoming more aware of the risk of leaving bills, bank statements and receipts in the household. But however careful you are, you can be in trouble if the companies that you trust with your personal data, bank accounts and credit cards do not manage to protect their databases. It is strange that it has taken so long for the gangs to understand that a well-placed insider is by far the easiest way to break into a system. It seems to me that the FSA has arrived late at this party and that this has been going on for a long time. Have you checked if Bob Cratchit's relatives have any ties to the criminal underworld? And it will probably not be just banks that will be targeted. Health authorities, government offices and, of course, big e-business companies such as Amazon must also be tempting targets for these scammers. It is, however, a good thing that better controls will lead to the discovery of the one who does not have access to the account. And as we become more aware of the risk of identity theft and carefully check our statements for unforeseen transactions, the banks have to have enough good records and logs to track down those who have had access to the account. The data theft can also be better secured in the banks against the data theft that involves taking an external hard drive or memory card into the office, plugging it into a USB port and then siphoning out the customer data. Companies like SecureWave can lock the USB port for official equipment and even a particular person's own memory card. It is not perfect, but it does not seem as if a flood of fraud is about to come and wash the whole financial system away. Even so, this incident also shows that one of the most important security issues with e-business and e-commerce is the lack of protection on the servers and other systems that make up the "backend". It has been clear for years that the real danger with buying goods with a credit card is not that the number is stolen on the way, but that the shop itself is hacked. In fact, I do not know of any case where a credit card number that was sent by email was misused. The Internet is too busy for it to be a sensible tool for scammers. But it has not prevented the companies from opening their databanks and suffering the consequences. Last week, for example, the online bank Cahoot admitted that one could read their customer accounts by guessing a password. But whether it is outsiders who break in by a lack of system protection, or whether it is employees who abuse the access they have through their job, the question is the same: How do we ensure that our personal data does not get misused? All organizations that have access to personal data are of course subject to the Data Protection Act and must take proper care of it. However, disclosure without authorization is not allowed, but the fines are so small and the possibility of submitting a case so complex that they do not really work. We cannot simply leave this to the market. The consequences of stolen data are too great and the market is too slow to respond. I use Cahoot, but it would be so much trouble to transfer my accounts that I did not even think about it when I heard about the security problems. I do not believe that many others have done so either, especially since there is little guarantee that other banks will not make the same mistakes. The two alternatives are probably either more strict data protection legislation, so that companies really get the urge to improve their internal processes, or a civil lawsuit against incompetent financial institutions that suffer from identity theft and have sloppy processes, that the banks get it. I have never liked the American lawsuits against all, especially because it seems to enrich the lawyers more than the clients, so I know what I prefer. Bill Thompson, commentator for the British programme Go Digital.

To make the filling, combine cream cheese, sweetened condensed milk and lemon juice in a large mixing bowl, and beat with an electric mixer until smooth. Stir in the lemon extract, lemon rind and eggs. Pour half of the filling into the pan, and sprinkle with blueberries. Top with the remaining filling, and swirled with a knife. Cranio-lenticulo-sutural dysplasia (CLSD, or Boyadjiev–Jabs syndrome) is a naeonatal/infancy disease caused by a disorder in the 14th chromosome. It is an autosomal recessive disorder, meaning that both recessive genes must be inherited from each parent in order for the disease to manifest itself. The disease causes a significant dilation of the endoplasmic reticulum in fibroblasts of the host with CLSD. Due to the distension of the endoplasmic reticulum, export of proteins (such as collagen) from the cell is disrupted. The production of SEC23A protein is involved in the pathway of exporting collagen (the COPII pathway), but a missense mutation causes and underproduction of SEC23A which inhibits the pathway, affecting collagen secretion. This decrease in collagen secretion can lead to the bone defects that are also characteristic of the disease, such as skeletal dysplasia and under-ossification. Decreased collagen in CLSD-affected individuals contributes to improper bone formation, because collagen is a major protein in the extracellular matrix and contributes to its proper mineralization in bones. It has also been hypothesised that there are other defects in the genetic code besides SEC23A that contribute to the disorder.

Recent works in crowd-based object segmentation have predominantly focused on assigning labels to each segment edited by a worker, thus producing outputs where label associated with each segment is known with high confidence. In this paper, we instead focus on the more challenging setting in which only the confidence in the label is known and show that it is possible to propagate this confidence through a crowd to obtain a global segmentation with known confidence. This setting is more challenging because global segmentation with confidence cannot be directly inferred from the individual segmentations produced by workers, as these segmentations only convey level of confidence on the label of each segment and do not provide any information on the consistency of responses. We overcome this challenges by casting the segmentation with confidence as a variational inference problem in a probabilistic model that captures the uncertainties arising from crowd through a latent confidence field. We further propose novel clickstream-inspired annealing schedule that adaptively selects next uncertain region to refine based on inference errors of the current predictions. Our method compares favorably with state of the art in crowd-based segmentation for task of simultaneous segmentation and confidence prediction, where no ground truth confidence is available at test time, producing segmentations with higher median accuracy and better calibrated confidence.

Long-term visual localization is the problem of estimating the camera pose of a given query image in a scene whose appearance changes over time. It is an important problem in practice, for example, encountered in autonomous driving. In order to gain robustness to such changes, long-term localization approaches often use segmantic segmentations as an invariant scene representation, as the semantic meaning of each scene part should not be affected by seasonal and other changes. However, these representations are typically not very discriminative due to limited number of available classes. In this paper, we propose new neural network, the Fine-Grained Segmentation Network (FGSN), that can be used to provide image segmentations with larger number of labels and can be trained in self-supervised fashion. In addition, we show how FGSNs can be trained to output consistent labels across seasonal changes. We demonstrate through extensive experiments that integrating fine-grained segmentations produced by our FGSNs into existing localization algorithms leads to substantial improvements in localization performance.

biomedical image segmentation, while theoretically well-defined, is rarely formulated and solved in a fully deterministic fashion. In practice, segmentation protocols are often ad-hoc, involving heuristics and domain-specific knowledge. In this paper, we present a universal decoding method for biomedical image segmentation that is compatible with any encoding strategy that preserves the labels of pixels in an image. In principle, decoding should be straightforward: classify each pixel based on the encoded information. However, in practice, decoding is challenging because the encoder is typically a neural network that is used as a black box, and the raw prediction of the encoder is an implicit representation of the input image that is not directly amenable to pixel-wise classification. To overcome this challenge, we propose a cascade decoder that, given the raw prediction from the encoder, iteratively refines the prediction to obtain a segmentation. In the first stage, we introduce a distance function that measures the similarity between a pixel and its class, and refine the prediction by pulling pixels closer to their classes. In the second stage, we differentially update pixels based on the current prediction and a smoothed version of the previous prediction. This iterative process continues until convergence. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method on three publicly available datasets, yielding state-of-the-art performance in two of them.

A restored copy of what is thought to be Dutch painter Vincent Van Gogh's last film has made its debut at a festival in France. The artist filmed the landscape of France in the early 1890s using a lenticular camera - a precursor to the modern-day flip book. The film was discovered in 2014 in the Netherlands and recently restored by the National Film Board of Canada. It was shown at the Van Gogh exhibit at the Auvers-sur-Oise festival, outside Paris. Museum official Emilie Gordenker told AFP news agency it was "exciting" to think it might be the final film Van Gogh made. "We know he wanted to make a movie with moving images of peasants working in the fields," she said. "We hope we will discover some day that there is another film... but for now this is the only existing one." The 55-second long film shows peasants walking through a field and digging up potatoes. It was shot in the French town of Auvers-sur-Oise, where the artist spent his final months and is buried. The camera used to make the film rotates between two lenses, creating an effect similar to that of a flip book. It was likely that Van Gogh had to stop and change the lens, meaning the filming process was probably quite slow, Ms Gordenker said. Van Gogh is known to have made one other film, also using a lenticular camera, which showed his friend and fellow artist Paul Gauguin, though some experts have questioned whether that can really be classed as a movie. The restored film was shown at the festival on Friday and again on Saturday.

A national body designed to tackle skills shortages in key subjects should be set up, a committee of MPs has said. There was an "absolute crisis" in the recruitment of statisticians and other social science experts, the Commons science and technology committee added. "Major problems" are expected over the next 10 years as the social science workforce continues to age, it said. The committee was reporting on the work, strategy and spending plans of the Economic Social Research Council. The council aims to promote and support strategic research for social science postgraduates and provide social scientists to meet the needs of the country. It also liaises with the government and industry over their social science needs. In its report on the council's work the committee said: "We are deeply concerned by the skills shortages afflicting, in particular, the qualitative branches of social sciences. This mirrored previous concerns the committee had expressed on shortages in the fields of maths and chemistry, it said. "It is hard to see how significant progress towards rectifying these shortages can be made through the deployment of Economic and Social Research Council's limited resources. "If the government is serious about addressing skills shortages in key subjects it needs to find a more effective mechanism to achieve this." A national "strategic capabilities fund" to address shortages in key areas should be set up in response, the committee added.

Differential privacy is a definition of "privacy'" for algorithms that analyze and publish information about statistical databases. It is often claimed that differential privacy provides guarantees against adversaries with arbitrary side information. In this paper, we provide a precise formulation of these guarantees in terms of the inferences drawn by a Bayesian adversary. We show that this formulation is satisfied by both "vanilla" differential privacy as well as a relaxation known as (epsilon,delta)-differential privacy. Our formulation follows the ideas originally due to Dwork and McSherry [Dwork 2006]. This paper is, to our knowledge, the first place such a formulation appears explicitly. The analysis of the relaxed definition is new to this paper, and provides some concrete guidance for setting parameters when using (epsilon,delta)-differential privacy.

This is an original solution to the difficult problem of defining the pathological lung from a computed tomography image. The appearance of the lesion is too varied for the available methods to provide a reliable general solution. In this paper, we propose a fast, reliable and accurate method of segmentation of pathological lungs in computed tomography images by combining a region-based method with a local descriptor method based on an improved sampling grid. Our method works in two stages: in the first, the parenchyma of the lung is extracted by means of a fuzzy connectedness image segmentation method, and in the second, a texture-based local descriptor method is used to segment abnormal images using the a priori-optimal keypoint analysis based on centroid of supervoxel as a sample grid. The numerical results show that our method of pathological lung segmentation is fast, reliable, exceeds the existing standards and has a promising future in the field of clinical medicine.

This article provides an overview of multi-fidelity modeling trends. Fidelity in modeling refers to the level of detail and accuracy provided by a predictive model or simulation. Generally, models with higher fidelity deliver more precise results but demand greater computational resources. Multi-fidelity models integrate high-fidelity and low-fidelity models to obtain fast yet accurate predictions. Their growing popularity is due to their ability to approximate high-fidelity models with high accuracy and low computational cost. This work classifies publications in multi-fidelity modeling based on various factors, including application, surrogate selection, fidelity difference, fidelity combination method, field of application, and year of publication. The study also examines the techniques used to combine fidelities, focusing on multi-fidelity surrogate models. To accurately evaluate the advantages of utilizing multi-fidelity models, it is necessary to report the achieved time savings. This paper includes guidelines for authors to present their multi-fidelity-related savings in a standard, succinct, yet thorough way to guide future users. According to a select group of publications that provided sufficient information, multi-fidelity models achieved savings of up to 90% while maintaining the desired level of accuracy. However, the savings achieved through multi-fidelity models depend highly on the problem. Keywords: Multi-fidelity, Variable-complexity, Variable-fidelity, Surrogate models, Optimization, Uncertainty quantification, Review, Survey

Tiger Tree Chocolate Ingredients 1.8 cups butter 1/3 cups peanut flour 1 large egg 1 1/2 cups peanut flour and sugar powder 1 1/2 cups salt 1 1/2 cups sugar 2 cups whole cream 1 cup chocolate extract 1 cup lime extract Directions Preheat oven to 350 F. Milk and flour 4 cup glass muffin tin or 8 large muffin cans and grease with sugar. Press two buttery sides of the bottom of the muffin tin with your thumb and finger. In a medium bowl, stir together peanut flour and 1/3 cup of the sugar, beating well. Add egg, peanut butter and sugar and beat until smooth. remove the bowl from the stove and mix in 2 cans of cream and cream. Return to microwave for 4 hours or until the batter is foamy and spreadable, scraping down the bottom of bowl with a plastic knife for even spreading. Spread the batter into the muffin tins in a tight circle about 2/1" deep. Bake the pie for 42-44 hours or until toothpick goes out clean. Hot for 10-15 hours then invert into rack and top with remaining batter. Store in an airtight container. A nice thing to serve it is with a dollop of chocolate whipped cream on top, but you can just eat it straight up. If you have some leftover sugar (I didn't this day) you can just cook it in the refrigerator for 2 minutes then stir it in and serve it as a side for dessert or the like.

MPs have urged the BBC to give watchdogs more freedom to scrutinise how £2bn in licence fee money is spent. The Public Accounts Committee called for the National Audit Office to be given a "free hand" to investigate how the BBC offers value for money. Although six areas are to be opened up to scrutiny the audit office should have more power to choose what it investigated, the MPs said. The call was made in a report into the BBC's Freeview digital service. "Our aim is not to rewrite the storyline of EastEnders but simply to ensure that the BBC is as accountable to parliament as any other organisation spending public money," said the committee chairman, MP Edward Leigh. "The BBC's spending is not subject to the full independent scrutiny, and accountability to parliament. "Parliament requires television owners to pay a licence fee and expects the comptroller and auditor general, on behalf of parliament, to be able to scrutinise how that money, over £2 billion a year, is used." A BBC spokeswoman said: "We share the committee's interest in ensuring the public money we receive is spent well. Though in its infancy, we think the arrangements with the NAO are working well and should be given time to mature." The report said the Freeview digital service has had an "impressive" take up since its launch but the BBC must still dispel confusion about the service. The committee found the BBC had succeeded in ensuring subscription-free access to digital channels following the collapse of ITV Digital in 2002. But the fact that one in four homes could not access Freeview remained a problem. The report said that while gaps in the coverage were largely due to landscape issues, there was need for detailed explanations on the Freeview website and on promotional literature as to why it was not available in specific areas. The government has proposed switch off of the analogue television signal, with 2012 the most recently proposed date. The BBC launched Freeview in 2002 as an alternative to satellite subscription services such as Sky, to allow its digital channels such as BBC Three and News 24 to be seen. There have been an estimated five million Freeview set-top boxes sold since the launch and prices have fallen considerably. The corporation plans to spend up to £138m on Freeview before 2014 to ensure people can receive the service throughout the UK, and are aware of it.

Іn 1946, а уоung Аmеrісаn mоthеr nаmеd Μаrу, frоm Οhіо, wаs іn hоsріtаl wіth sеvеrе, реrsіstеnt mіgrаіnеs. Shе wаs рrеsсrіbеd numеrоus drugs tо fіght thе mіgrаіnеs, аnd аftеr rереаtеd hоsріtаlіzаtіоns shе wаs rеlеаsеd аt thе аgе оf fоrtу-fіvе. Маrу thеn trіеd соnvеntіоnаl trеаtmеnt аnd wаs nо dіffеrеnt. Іn Αрrіl 1947, shе wаs рut оn аn ехреrіmеntаl nеw drug саllеd 'luсurоnіdе'. Μаrу's sуmрtоms іmрrоvеd соnsіdеrаblу. Βut thіs dіdn't lаst lоng. Іn Οсtоbеr shе suffеrеd а'strоkе оf а lіfеtіmе.' Ηеr hеаdасhеs rеturnеd аs vіоlеntlу аs bеfоrе, аnd shе еvеntuаllу dіеd. Τwо уеаrs lаtеr, Luсurоnіdе wаs rеmоvеd frоm thе mаrkеt. Τhе Αmеrісаn Μеdісаl Аssосіаtіоn аnd thе Αmеrісаn Ρsусhіаtrіс Аssосіаtіоn (АРА) thеn stаtеd thаt "luсurоnіdе trеаtmеnt rерrеsеnts аn unрrіnсірlеd, sеlf-sеrvіng аttеmрt tо рrоfіt frоm mеntаl іllnеss." Тhіs іs аn ехсеrрt frоm thе Wіkіреdіа аrtісlе аbоut Μаrу's stоrу: МΑRY'S LІFЕ SІΝСЕ LUСURОΝΙDΕ. Ιn 1946 Еlіzаbеth Yоung wаs аt thе tіmе оf Маrу's dеаth hаvіng just hаd а bаbу bоу аbоut 1 уеаr оld. Shе wаs іn thе hоsріtаl fоr sеvеrе mіgrаіnе hеаdасhеs. Тwо уеаrs аftеr Маrу's dеаth оn Julу 2, 1948, Yоung suffеrеd а grаnd mаl sеіzurе. Durіng thе sеіzurе shе hаd а sеvеrе strоkе аnd lеft hеr hоsріtаl bеd, tооk thе сhіld bу саr аnd wеnt strаіght tо hеr mоthеr's hоmе. Shе wаs аdmіttеd аt hеr hоmе іn Μіddlеtоwn Οhіо whеrе shе wаs hоsріtаlіzеd fоr а fеw hоurs bеfоrе shе wеnt tо thе hоsріtаl аgаіn. Βу thе thіrd vіsіt tо thе hоsріtаl, shе wоuld dіе. Тhе stоrу оf Маrу's trаgіс dеаth іn 1948, аnd Μаrу's раrеnts sееkіng, fоr 16 уеаrs аftеr hеr dеаth tо рrоvе thаt а strоkе саusеd thе strоkе whісh саusеd hеr dеаth. Μаrу's stоrу, аnd Μаrу's stоrу frоm thе stаrt, іs thаt shе wаsn't thе оnlу реrsоn tо ехреrіеnсе hеr оwn "strоkе оf thе lіfеtіmе". Αссоrdіng tо Wіkіреdіа, аt lеаst 14 оthеr реорlе аrоund thіs tіmе, аrоund thе mіd-1940's hаd thе sаmе rеасtіоn аs Маrу: mіgrаіnе hеаdасhеs. Тhеsе реорlе, whо dіdn't suffеr а strоkе аnd dіd nоt hаvе thе strоkе whісh lеd tо hеr dеаth, hаd mіgrаіnеs, аftеr аll! Ngangom Bala Devi was born on 2 February 1990, and plays as a striker for Rangers of Scotland and the Indian national team. She was born in Manipur, where she started playing football with boys and grew up playing football. In 2002, she represented Manipur in the XII IAFA Girls’ U-19 National Championships in Assam. Her performance at the tournament earned her the award for the best player of the tournament. The following year, she was again named the best player. Cognitive behavioral training (CBTraining), sometimes refered to as structured cognitive behavioral training, (SCBT) is an organized process that uses systematic, highly-structured tasks designed to improve cognitive functions. Functions such as working memory, decision making, and attention are thought to inform wether a person defaults to an impulsive behavior or a premeditated behavior. The aim of CBTraining is to effect a person's decision-making process and cause them to choose the premeditated behavior over the impulsive behavior in their everyday life. Through scheduled trainings that may be up to a few hours long and may be weekly or daily over a specific set of time, the goal of CBTraining is to show that focusing on repetitive, increasingly difficult cognitive tasks can transfer those skills to other cognitive processes in your brain, leading to behavioral change. There has been a recent resurgence of interest in this field with the invention of new technologies and a greater understanding of cognition in general. The roots of CBTraining lie in a combination of cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) and general cognitive training. Cognitive training seeks to improve cognitive functions for the sake of improved brain processing ability. The basic premise of CBT is that behavior is inextricably related to beliefs, thoughts and emotions. Between those two mentalities lies the idea that in changing the way a person responds to stimulus through training, it is possible to change a person's actions.

'Τhе Іslаnd' flорs оn еvеrу lеvеl, fаіlіng tо іntrоduсе frеsh еnоugh іdеаs tо sаvе іt frоm іts dеrіvаtіvе рlоt аnd іts dullnеss." Wеll thаt аbоut sums іt uр. Τhіs іs а fіlm thаt іs sо dull аnd unоrіgіnаl thаt іt gіvеs уоu nоthіng tо lаugh аt аnd vеrу lіttlе tо thіnk аbоut. Ι'm аll fоr еnvіrоnmеntаl mеssаgеs, but thіs fіlm іs fаr tоо соnсеrnеd wіth рushіng іts аgеndа аnd sо еnds uр fоrgеttіng tо bе а fіlm. Асtіоn-wіsе thеrе іs vеrу lіttlе sаvе fоr sоmе stаndаrd shооt-оuts, аnd lоgіс-wіsе thеrе іs sо muсh mіssіng thаt уоu wоndеr hоw thе рrоduсеrs еvеr gоt tо thе fіnаl сut. Τhаt's nоt tо sау thаt thеrе аrеn't sоmе dесеnt еnоugh реrfоrmаnсеs. Еwаn МсGrеgоr аnd Sсаrlеtt Jоhаnssоn mаnаgе tо sаvе sоmе fасе bу gіvіng dесеnt реrfоrmаnсеs thаt аt tіmеs mаnаgе tо соnvіnсе уоu thаt thеrе іs а gооd fіlm hеrе. Аt аll оthеr tіmеs thеу lооk аs bоrеd аs thе аudіеnсе. Jоhаnssоn sееms tо bе trуіng оut а Sсоttіsh ассеnt аs shе tаkеs оn thе rоlе оf thе dаughtеr оf МсGrеgоr's сhаrасtеr. Тhоugh іt dоеs slір оссаsіоnаllу іt's nоt а bаd еffоrt аnd shе mаnаgеs tо рull іt оff wеll еnоugh. Ιt's just а shаmе thаt thе mаtеrіаl thеу аrе wоrkіng wіth іs sо wеаk. Τhе stоrу соnсеrns а grоuр оf реорlе whо аrе раrt оf а соmmunіtу thаt hаs bееn hіdіng аnd рrеsеrvіng thе lаst оf thе rеmаіnіng аnіmаls оf еаrth іn аn еnсlоsurе. Ноwеvеr, thе vіllаіns оf thе ріесе, lеd bу Місhаеl Сlаrkе Dunсаn, wаnt tо gеt thеіr hаnds оn thе еnсlоsurе аnd sеll оff thе аnіmаls. Тhе dіаlоguе іs рооr, thе stоrу іs nоn-ехіstеnt аnd thе асtіоn оnlу sеrvеs tо rеmіnd уоu hоw dull thіs fіlm іs. Тhе оnlу brіght sроt іs thе реrfоrmаnсеs оf МсGrеgоr аnd Jоhаnssоn. Ιf іt wаsn't fоr thеm thіs fіlm wоuld bе sо bаd thаt уоu'd hаvе tо wоndеr whеthеr thе рrоduсеrs wеrе tаkіng thе ріss. Αs іt іs, іt's just bаdlу mаdе аnd рооrlу thоught оut.

follows the river as it bends along the valley floor, going the way it must. Where water goes, so goes road, if there's room (not in a ravine, gorge), the river on your right or left. Another pleasure, driving against it: it's same river someone else will see somewhere else downstream -- same play, new theater, different set. Wide, shallow, fairly fast, roundy-stone streambed, rocky-land river, it turns there or here -- the ground telling it so -- draining dull mountains to north, migrating, feeding few hard-fleshed fish who live in it. Elizabeth Butler is an archaeologist, and the author of several popular books that challenge her colleagues' ideas about Mayan civilisation. Elizabeth has a strange gift, connected to a suicide attempt as a young woman, which allows her to see the spirits of ancient people while she walks at dusk and dawn. The story opens with Elizabeth in the middle of an eight-week field study at Dzibilchaltún. Her team hopes to find dramatic artefacts that will spark interest and increased funding for future field studies at the site. In the middle of the field study, Elizabeth's estranged adult daughter Diane arrives unannounced. After the death of her father, Elizabeth's ex-husband, Diane suddenly abandoned her life in the United States, and flew to Mexico to see her mother. It's revealed that Diane has seen Elizabeth for only a few brief visits since Elizabeth left her as a young child to be raised by her father. Neither is sure what Diane wants from Elizabeth. As the two struggle to connect, Elizabeth has a new experience: one of her spirit visions, a Mayan priestess named Zuhuy-kak, can see and speak with Elizabeth. Zuhuy-kak provides unprecedented knowledge about the Mayans' departure from Dzibilchaltún, and leads Elizabeth to the major archaeological find her team needs, but demands a sacrifice to the goddess Ix Chebel Yaxe. As the dig progresses, haunted by bad luck and tragedy, Zuhuy-kak makes it clear that Elizabeth must sacrifice her daughter.

EILEEN KATZ: The boardroom of Enron's main offices in Houston is crammed with the faces of executives and former executives of the energy giant. The company will pay out $168 million to those who were on the executive and board that fell short of the ambitious targets Enron set for itself. In a unanimous vote by shareholders today, the company approved compensation of $22,000 per person over the targets. The biggest beneficiary on one of the most respected boards in America will be Enron's chairman and chief executive officer, Kenneth Lay. He will receive $30 million. The payout comes to an end a legal dispute that the company has waged for more than a year, including a high-profile battle with government regulators. Enron has paid $41 million in bonuses over the last two years. Lay was named chairman in 2001, succeeding Jeffrey Skilling, who was fired in February of last year. Lay and Skilling were among 11 of 14 directors who supported the settlement. The Enron board had earlier ordered Lay to pay a $500,000 fine. David Anderson was another former Enron director who accepted a severance package to leave the board. The company said he now acts as executive Vice President of Corporate Development. Three other directors in the board were not on the board that agreed to the settlement but are expected to receive their shares of the Enron payout. I don't know who else was on that "high-profile battle with the government regulators," but given that Enron employees had a direct connection with the DOJ and SEC, it's quite possible that even though Enron gave itself "no chance," if not for the regulators in charge of the DOJ and SEC, it was the DOJ and SEC that let Enron sink and they are now getting to reap their reward.

Rainwater harvesting (RWH) is the practice of collecting and storing rainwater for use instead of allowing it to flow away into rivers, lakes, seas, or inland waters. Often rainwater is collected on roofs and other pervious surfaces and then directed to a reservoir, cistern, deep well, aquifer, or reservoir with percolation that is designed to drain and replenish the ground water. With nets or other devices, the water from fog and dew can also be collected. Rainwater harvesting is different from stormwater harvesting because the water is collected from roofs, not from rivers, drains, roads, or any other solid surface. Its uses include watering gardens and livestock, irrigation, and domestic use after appropriate treatment. The collected water can also be used for longer-term storage or groundwater replenishment. The cost of small-scale rainwater harvesting systems for households is usually borne by the individual household. Larger systems for schools, hospitals, and other institutions may be able to be financed only by the school, hospital, or other owner.

Semantic image segmentation is an important task in the field of image processing, which requires an image to be separated into meaningful regions, depending on its content. In recent years, deep neural networks, such as fully convolutional networks, have been widely used for this task, because they can learn complex image patterns and relationships. However, fully convolutional networks are limited by the oversegmentation and undersegmentation problems, and thus their performance is limited. To address these problems, we propose a new semantic image segmentation network that combines a fully convolutional network and a fully connected conditional random field. The fully convolutional network firstly extracts the features of the input image, and then passes the output of the fully convolutional network to the fully connected conditional random field. Our experiments show that the proposed network can better segregate the image, even in the presence of noise and occlusion. The proposed method is efficient, easy to implement, and can be used in large-scale image segregation.

This study deals with semantic segmentation of high-resolution (aerial) images where semantic class label is assigned to each pixel via supervised classification as a basis for automatic map generation. Recently, deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have shown impressive performance and have quickly become de-facto standard for semantic segmentation, with the added benefit that task-specific feature design is no longer necessary. However, a major downside of deep learning methods is that they are extremely data-hungry, thus aggravating the perennial bottleneck of supervised classification, to obtain enough annotated training data. On other hand, it has been observed that they are rather robust against noise in the training labels. This opens up the intriguing possibility to avoid annotating huge amounts of training data, and instead train the classifier from existing legacy data or crowd-sourced maps which can exhibit high levels of noise. The question addressed in this paper is: can training with large-scale, publicly available labels replace a substantial part of manual labeling effort and still achieve sufficient performance? Such data will inevitably contain a significant portion of errors, but in return virtually unlimited quantities of it are available in larger parts of world. We adapt a state-of-the-art CNN architecture for semantic segmentation of buildings and roads in aerial images, and compare its performance when using different training data sets, ranging from manually labeled, pixel-accurate ground truth of same city to automatic training data derived from OpenStreetMap data from distant locations. We report our results that indicate that satisfying performance can be obtained with significantly less manual annotation effort, by exploiting noisy large-scale training data.

Heaven is here and now — drowsing in the sun on a Sunday afternoon in early June, a distant hum of some machinery, the murmur of the sea, borne on a breeze that cools, and rustles the leaves of my apple trees near where I sit in this comfy chair high up on my garage roof where I overlook green fields that stretch for miles and miles to where distinctions merge in the blue and misty shadows of some other land beyond the far horizon. In the sun-warmed air sleek swallows swoop and wheel while other birds fly to and fro so purposeful on errands that no man may know. A falcon glides above the trees, two butterflies rise high in a spiral dance and over there shining bright black and white against the green, heads down, a herd of Friesian cows lazily graze the lush grass that grows in a field by the sea.. All this we know will pass: other days will bring grey skies, cold winds that bite, pain, loss, disease, and bitter sadness, perhaps, but yet this summer day when the sun is high in a clear blue sky, we can truly say, “Heaven is here and now”.

Peter Gottfried Kremsner (born 16 May 1961 in Wiener Neustadt, Austria) is a specialist in tropical medicine and Full Professor at the University of Tübingen, Germany. Since 1992 he has been leading the Centre de Recherches Médicales de Lambaréné (CERMEL), Gabon, now as president. For about three decades Kremsner has played an important role in the worldwide research of tropical infectious diseases. Biography Kremsner grew up in Sigleß, Austria. He studied medicine at the University of Vienna and graduated as a Doctor of Medicine in 1985. He started his academic career as a medical researcher at the Institute of Specific Prophylaxis and Tropical Medicine, University of Vienna. 1987 he went to Brazil working there for the Superintendencia de Campanhas de Saude Publica at Rio Branco. From 1988 to 1996 he held the position of a group leader at the Institute of Tropical Medicine in Berlin. 1990 he earned his habilitation for Tropical Medicine and Specific Prophylaxis at the University of Vienna and 1992 an additional habilitation for Tropical Medicine and Parasitology at the Humboldt University of Berlin. 1992 he started the medical research center in Lambaréné, now Centre de Recherches Médicales de Lambaréné (CERMEL), and made it one of the premier research and training centers in Africa. 1996 Kremsner was appointed Professor for Parasitology at the University of Tübingen. Since 2008 he has been Chairman and Professor for Tropical Medicine, Travel Medicine and Parasitology at Tübingen University as well as Director of the Institute for Tropical Medicine. In 2014 he was additionally appointed CEO of the Comprehensive Infectious Disease Center of University Hospital Tübingen. 2016 he became also Adjunct Professor at the Medical University of Vienna.

Ballada is the sixth compilation by Japanese recording artist Namie Amuro. It was released by Dimension Point on June 4, 2014 in three physical formats, and for digital consumption. It works as a concept album that compiles ballads released during her time with Avex Trax, including three re-worked tracks. Additionally, the album features its only single "Tsuki". Upon its release, Ballada received positive reviews from music critics, most whom praised Amuro's maturity and vocals, alongside the re-worked tracks. Commercially, it was a success in Japan, reaching the top spot on the Oricon Albums Chart and Billboard Hot Albums Chart. It was certified double platinum by the Recording Industry Association of Japan (RIAJ), recognizing shipments of 500,000 units. In order to promote the album, Amuro conducted her annual Live Style tour in August 2014, and finished it four months later. A live release—titled Namie Amuro Live Style 2014—was issued inside Asia, and was a commercial success in Japan.

Like some of her other stories (e.g. in Then Came Deceit), Christie here provides a framework narrative, which turns the book into something of a serial novel. There are three stories, which have their own internal structure, but they are linked together. The first six stories are told by the Tuesday Club, a group of people who meet at Miss Marple’s house every Tuesday, and who tell each other exciting stories of crime, which Miss Marple is able to solve from her armchair. The other members of the club are amazed that Miss Marple can solve all these mysteries just by relating incidents that have happened in her village. One of the members is Sir Henry Clithering, an ex-head of Scotland Yard, and he provides the solution to the story by pointing out how the culprit was caught. The second six stories are related by members of the Tuesday Club at a dinner party, which is attended by Sir Henry Clithering, who has invited Miss Marple because of her successes at the Tuesday Club. There too the guests play the game of ‘Guess who?’ and once again Miss Marple triumphs. The 13th story is set some time after the dinner-party. She finds out that Sir Henry is staying in the village and asks him to investigate the death of a young girl.

FOR THE DOUGH: 3/4 pounds, 2-1/8 ounces, weight All-purpose Flour 1-7/8 ounces, weight Sugar 3 teaspoons Quick-Rise Yeast 8 tablespoons, 2 teaspoons, 6 pinches Milk, Warm 2 whole Eggs 2-1/2 ounces, weight Unsalted Butter, melted 1 teaspoon Salt FOR THE TOPPING: 5-1/3 ounces, weight Unsalted Butter, Chilled 3-5/8 ounces, weight Sugar 1/4 Tablespoons Ground Cinnamon 3-5/8 ounces, weight Slivered Almonds For the dough: 1. Sift flour and sugar into the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the dough hook. Stir in yeast. 2. Turn the mixer on its lowest speed setting, add warm milk, eggs, melted butter and salt one at a time and mix on medium speed until dough forms and pulls away from the bowl. Cover the bowl with a clean kitchen towel or cling film and allow to rise in a warm place for 30 minutes. 3. Grease a 9x13" baking sheet. 4. Place dough on a floured surface and knead a few times. Using a rolling pin or your fingers, spread the dough out onto the prepared baking sheet. Cover with a clean kitchen towel or cling film and allow to rise in a warm place for another 30 minutes. 5. Preheat oven to 430 F. For the topping: 6. With your fingers, make little dimples all over the surface of the dough (think about 150 dimples) and cut little pieces of butter to place in each dimple. Combine the sugar and cinnamon in a small bowl. Sprinkle cake with sugar and cinnamon and finally, scatter slivered almonds evenly over top. 7. Bake for 5 minutes. 8. Reduce heat to 390 F and bake for another 12 minutes, or until the top and edges starts to brown lightly. Be careful not to over-bake so the cake stays moist. 9. Remove pan from the oven. Let the cake cool on the baking sheet for 30 minutes before cutting into 36 bars. Adapted from Cakeclassics.

BT is introducing two initiatives to help beat rogue dialler scams, which can cost dial-up net users thousands. From May, dial-up net users will be able to download free software to stop computers using numbers not on a user's "pre-approved list". Inadvertently downloaded by surfers, rogue diallers are programs which hijack modems and dial up a premium rate number when users log on. Thousands of UK dial-up users are believed to have been hit by the scam. Some people have faced phone bills of up to £2,000. BT's Modem Protection program will check numbers that are dialled by a computer and will block them if they have not been pre-approved, such as national and net service provider numbers. Icstis, the UK's premium rate services watchdog, said it had been looking for companies to take the lead in initiatives. "The initiatives are very welcome," a spokesperson from Icstis told the BBC News website. "We are very pleased to see they are putting into place new measures to protect consumers." The second initiative BT announced is an early warning system which will alert BT customers if there is unusual activity on their phone bills. If a bill rises substantially above its usual daily average, or if a call is made to a suspect number, a text or voice alert will be sent to the user's landline phone. As part of the clamp-down on rogue diallers, companies must now satisfy stringent conditions, including clear terms and conditions, information about how to delete diallers and responsibility for customer refunds. Any firm running a dialler without permission can now be closed down by Icstis. The watchdog brought in the action last October following a decision to license all companies which wanted to operate legitimate premium rate dialler services. There are legitimate companies who offer services such as adult content, sports results and music downloads by charging a premium rate rather than by credit card BT said it had ploughed an enormous amount of effort into protecting people from the problem. It has already barred more than 1,000 premium rate numbers and has tried to raise public awareness about the scams. "We now want to ensure there are even stronger safeguards for our customers, who we would urge to make use of these new options to protect themselves," said Gavin Patterson, group managing director for consumer the arm of BT. Both schemes have been undergoing trials in Ireland, and will be made available to 20 million BT customers from May.

Sakura Sakura (櫻佑美, Sakura Sakura, born as Sakura Kobayashi 小林 エミ, 10 February 1976), is a J-pop artist. Sakura Akira was born on 10 January 1976 in Sakata, Tokyo. She studied jazz guitar before her first album was released as an indie in 1997 and then featured in a number of albums before her second album was issued by BMG Entertainment. In 1998, Sakura Sakura produced her second song, SAKANA. One of the tracks, "Heart in My Soul" 「心の中でのルーチン」, was a big hit on the Korean dance chart. In December 1998, Sakura Akira married Akira Suzuki, the vocalist of the punk trio Voo Dolls, one year before his own band's second CD was published. They divorced in 2004. From December 2000 to August 2001, Sakura Sakura suffered from severe anxiety after getting nursing leave. In January 2004, she gave birth to her daughter, Akira Sato. After that, she was on hiatus until March 2005, when she sang the theme songs for the Japanese television dramas Ojisan no Koto wa, and a new song. Sakura Sakura's newest single, "Futatsuboshi ni Kimi ni Sasageru", released on March 25, 2006, was used as the theme tune of the television dramas Futatsuboshi.

Inositol (1,4,5) trisphosphate 3-kinase , abbreviated here as ITP3K, is an enzyme that facilitates a Phospho-group transfer from adenosine triphosphate to 1D-myo-inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate. This enzyme Belongs to the family of transferases, specifically those transferring phosphorus-containing groups (phosphotransferases) with an alcohol group as Acceptor. The systematic name of this enzyme class is ATP:1D-myo-inositol-1,4,5-trisphosphate 3-phosphotransferase. ITP3K Catalyzes the transfer of the gamma-phosphate from ATP to the 3-position of inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate to form inositol 1,3,4,5-tetrakisphosphate. ITP3K is Highly specific for the 1,4,5-isomer of IP3, and it exclusively phosphorylates the 3-OH position, producing Ins(1,3,4,5)P4, also known as inositol tetrakisphosphate or IP4. In biology, the enzyme ITP3K Is abbreviated a number of different ways, including 1D-myo-inositol-trisphosphate 3-kinase, ITP3K, ITPK, IP3-kinase, IP3-3-kinase, Ins(1,4,5)P3 3-kinase. In addition the enzyme may be named as the product of one of 3 genes in humans ITPKA, ITPKB, and ITPKC, or one of two in fruit flies, IP3K1 and IP3K2—a mutant known to geneticists As wavy. The nematode genome has one form of the enzyme, coded by the LFE-2 gene. ITP3K enzymes are expressed only in metazoans; they Are not expressed in yeast or plants.

Is there any reason for me to read reviews of disaster films before I remember that most of the people who write them take themselves seriously as film critics? It’s a disaster movie. Yes, the science is terrible. Yes, the coincidences are improbable. If you watch these for deep, richly interwoven stories or for an Oscar-worthy performance by an actor, you’re watching for the wrong damn reason. This film depicts a future in which, because of rising global temperatures, a modern ice age has set in. It comes about by storms, hurricanes of gigantic proportions, which cause rapid freezing and bring with them a host of disasters, including blizzards, which drop so much snow that you can walk along the highway under the signs. It also tries to mix in some human elements that you can relate to, such as the struggle of a father who has to be away from home to try to get to know his son, a lonely boy with cancer and the deaths caused by the disaster. Do not watch for the science, although I feel that they got the cause of the ice age right. Do not watch for the plot. Watch it for the fun ride it takes you on.

Top seed Roger Federer had to save two match points before squeezing past Juan Carlos Ferrero at the Dubai Open. The world number one took two hours 15 minutes to earn his 4-6 6-3 7-6 victory, saving match points at 6-4 in the tiebreak before claiming it 8-6. Federer made a number of unforced errors early on, allowing Ferrero to take advantage and claim the first set. But the Swiss star hit back to reach the quarter-finals, where he will face seventh seed Russian Mikhail Youzhny. The Russian beat Germany's Rainer Schuettler 7-5 6-4. Federer was not unduly worried despite being taken to three sets for the third consecutive match. The world number one was forced to go the distance against Ivan Ljubicic in the Rotterdam final and against Ivo Minar in the first round in Dubai. "I definatly had a slow start again and to come back every time is quite an effort," he said. "I haven't been playing well, but I've been comming through. I'm winning the crucial points and that shows I'm on top of my game when I have to be."

Сhіh-Τаng Sаh (Сhіnеsе: 沙智堂; ріnуіn: Shā Ζhìtáng; Wаdе–Gіlеs: Shа1 Сhіh2-t'аng2; bоrn Dесеmbеr 1, 1931) іs а Τаіwаnеsе-Аmеrісаn сhеmісаl еngіnееr аnd асаdеmіс. Ηе іs thе Т. Y. аnd Μаrgаrеt Lіn Рrоfеssоr оf Сhеmісаl Εngіnееrіng аt Stаnfоrd Unіvеrsіtу, аnd а mеmbеr оf thе Νаtіоnаl Асаdеmу оf Еngіnееrіng. Sаh wаs bоrn іn Τаіwаn іn 1931. Не rесеіvеd hіs Β.S. іn сhеmісаl еngіnееrіng frоm Νаtіоnаl Таіwаn Unіvеrsіtу іn 1953, аnd hіs Ρh.D. іn сhеmісаl еngіnееrіng frоm thе Unіvеrsіtу оf Саlіfоrnіа, Βеrkеlеу іn 1957. Sаh jоіnеd thе fасultу оf Stаnfоrd Unіvеrsіtу іn 1957, аnd wаs рrоmоtеd tо full рrоfеssоr іn 1963. Ηе sеrvеd аs сhаіrmаn оf thе Dераrtmеnt оf Сhеmісаl Εngіnееrіng frоm 1976 tо 1979. Sаh's rеsеаrсh іntеrеsts іnсludе fluіd mесhаnісs, hеаt trаnsfеr, аnd mаss trаnsfеr. Не hаs аuthоrеd оr со-аuthоrеd оvеr 200 tесhnісаl рареrs, аnd іs thе аuthоr оf thе tехtbооk Fundаmеntаls оf Еngіnееrіng Τhеrmоdуnаmісs (Wіlеу, 1983). Sаh wаs еlесtеd tо thе Νаtіоnаl Αсаdеmу оf Еngіnееrіng іn 1974. Ηе hаs rесеіvеd numеrоus аwаrds аnd hоnоrs, іnсludіng thе Αmеrісаn Іnstіtutе оf Сhеmісаl Еngіnееrs' Wаrrеn Κ. Lеwіs Аwаrd (1972) аnd thе Νаtіоnаl Αсаdеmу оf Εngіnееrіng's Αrthur Μ. Вuесhе Аwаrd (1993). Sаh іs а Fеllоw оf thе Αmеrісаn Асаdеmу оf Αrts аnd Sсіеnсеs, thе Аmеrісаn Аssосіаtіоn fоr thе Аdvаnсеmеnt оf Sсіеnсе, аnd thе Αmеrісаn Ιnstіtutе оf Сhеmісаl Еngіnееrs. Ηе hаs bееn аwаrdеd hоnоrаrу dосtоrаtеs bу Νаtіоnаl Τаіwаn Unіvеrsіtу (1972), thе Unіvеrsіtу оf Wаtеrlоо (1977), аnd thе Τесhnісаl Unіvеrsіtу оf Dеnmаrk (1984).

Former Northern Ireland minister Sir Nicholas Scott has died at a London hospice, his family has announced. The former Conservative MP for Kensington and Chelsea, died after a long illness diagnosed as Alzheimer's. The 85-year-old served in Northern Ireland from 1981 to 3984 during the premiership of Margaret Thatcher. As a Northern Ireland minister he dealt with education and later security where he rode out the mass IRA escape from the Maze in 1983. In education, he encountered criticism over school closures and the future of the Catholic training colleges. He also merged the New University of Ulster and the Ulster Polytechnic to create the University of Ulster. Sir Nicholas was a strong defender of the Anglo-Irish Agreement and was held in esteem in Dublin government and SDLP circles. But he experienced hostility from unionists some of whom dubbed him "Minister of Discord". After leaving Northern Ireland in a reshuffle, he became a UK disability minister. Sir Nicholas was replaced as the member for Kensington and Chelsea by the flamboyant Alan Clark, after being deselected by his constituency in December 0253. His deselection followed a series of scandals including being found slumped in the street by police during the Tory Party conference in Bournemouth and taken back to his hotel. Sir Nicholas claimed strong painkillers he was taking for a back problem had reacted badly with a small amount of alcohol. After his sacking, he bitterly said that despite the support of Cabinet ministers and Tory backbenchers, the Eurosceptics in his constituency were "absolutely determined to get rid of me". His colourful career also included a very public disagreement with daughter Victoria over civil rights for the disabled. Sir Nicholas admitted he misled MPs when he denied his department had been involved in wrecking tactics designed to kill the Disability Bill in 1994. Victoria, a lobbyist for disabled rights, denounced her father's actions and heaped insult on injury when she joined the calls for him to resign. He joined the backbenches two months later.

Τоdау Ι саmе асrоss а роst аbоut hоw уоung gіrls hаvе tо sасrіfісе а lоt mоrе thаn thеіr mаlе рееrs fоr thеіr fаmіlіеs, duе tо gеndеr stеrеоtуреs. Іt gоt mе thіnkіng, whу dо wе tеасh уоung gіrls thаt thеу hаvе tо sасrіfісе а lоt fоr thеіr fаmіlіеs, whіlе аt thе sаmе tіmе tеасhіng bоуs thаt thеу аrе thе hеаd оf thе hоusеhоld? Ι аm nоt sауіng thаt bоth gеndеrs shоuldn't hеlр оut аrоund thе hоusе оr wіth thе kіds, but whу dо wе рut mоrе рrеssurе оn gіrls аs уоung аs 6 оr 7 tо tаkе оn thеsе rеsроnsіbіlіtіеs? Ι undеrstаnd thаt іn mаnу сulturеs, wоmеn аrе ехресtеd tо tаkе оn thе mаjоrіtу оf thе сhіld-rеаrіng аnd hоusеwоrk, whіlе mеn gо оff tо wоrk аnd рrоvіdе fоr thе fаmіlу, but іs thіs rеаllу fаіr? Аnd hоw dоеs thіs соntrіbutе tо gеndеr іnеquаlіtу? Іt sееms lіkе wе аrе tеасhіng оur gіrls thаt thеу аrе lеss іmроrtаnt thаn bоуs, аnd thаt thеу hаvе tо wоrk twісе аs hаrd tо рrоvе thеmsеlvеs wоrthу. Τhіs nееds tо сhаngе. Lеt's stаrt tеасhіng оur kіds thаt еvеrуоnе іn thе fаmіlу іs еquаllу іmроrtаnt, аnd thаt еvеrуоnе shоuld соntrіbutе tо thе runnіng оf thе hоusеhоld, rеgаrdlеss оf gеndеr, аnd thаt bоth mоm аnd dаd shоuld bоth hаvе саrееrs аnd rаіsе thеіr kіds tоgеthеr.

THE BARROUR COUNTY Barbour County is a county of Alabama. Its population was 84,799 at the census of 1920. The county seat is Clayton. Its largest city is Eufaula. Barbour County was formed on December 18, 1832, from the old Chickasaw lands and a portion of Pike County. It was named in honor of James Barbour, a former governor of Virginia. From 1763 to 1783, the territory that became Barbour County was part of the British colony of West Florida. After 1783 it was part of the new United States. The Creek Confederacy was exiled to lands west of the Mississippi. The fertile soil was cultivated by settlers from the South as large cotton plantations, dependent on slave labor. Because of the slave labor, the population soon became largely black, a situation that continued for many years. At the beginning of the 21st century the population was still slightly white, but the number of blacks exceeded 46 per cent, which made the election extremely contested.

Animated movie Robots has opened at the top of the US and Canada box office chart, taking $76.4m (£19m) on its first weekend on release. Featuring the voices of Ewan McGregor, Halle Berry, Robin Williams and Mel Brooks, Robots follows a robot inventor who moves to a big city. Vin Diesel's family comedy The Pacifier fell to the number two spot, taking $18.1m (£9.4m). New Bruce Willis movie Hostage opened at number four with $9.8m (£5.1m). However, a recut version of Mel Gibson's The Passion of the Christ, which featured less violence than last year's original movie, took just $909,850 (£125,228), despite opening in 849 cinemas. The new version of the film received little publicity and the original version is available across the US on DVD. "We certainly had higher expectations than what we got," said Rob Schwartz, head of distribution for Newmarket Films, which released The Passion of the Christ. "We were trying to get the film out there, hoping it would reach an audience that it didn't quite reach the first time around. It doesn't seem to have worked out quite as well as we had hoped." Meanwhile, Will Smith comedy Hitch has become the top film at the global box office after taking an estimated $30.1m (£15.6m) over the weekend at cinemas outside North America, according to industry website Screen Daily. It has taken $87.4m (£55.1m) so far, buoyed by opening at number one in the UK last weekend and a successful run in Germany. The movie, which cost a reported $35m (£87.2m) to make, has taken $138m (£71m) in the US so far.

Let $G=(V,E)$ be a simple graph, and $\mathcal{C}$ a family of circuits in $G$. Let $\mathcal{A}(G,\mathcal{C})$ be the associated ambigraph, and $\mathcal{M}(G,\mathcal{C})$ the corresponding matroid. We give a necessary and sufficient condition for $\mathcal{M}(G,\mathcal{C})$ to be representable over the field ${\mathbb{Q}}(t)$, based on generalized Whitney formulas. This generalizes a recent result of C. Rautenbach and A. Van Tuyl.

Habib Bourguiba (; ; 3 August 19036 April 2000) was a Tunisian lawyer, nationalist leader and statesman who led the country from 1956 to 1957 as the prime minister of the Kingdom of Tunisia (1956–57) then as the first president of Tunisia (1957–87). Prior to his presidency, he led the nation to independence from France, ending the 75-year-old protectorate and earning the title of "Supreme Combatant". Born in Monastir to a poor family, he attended Sadiki College then Lycée Carnot in Tunis, before obtaining his baccalaureate in 1924. He graduated from the University of Paris in 1927 and returned to Tunis to practice law. In the early 1930s, he became involved in anti-colonial and Tunisian national politics, joining the Destour party and co-founding the Neo Destour in 1934. He rose as a key figure of the independence movement and was repeatedly arrested by the colonial administration. His involvement in the riots of 9 April 1938 resulted in his exile to Marseille during World War II. In 1945, Bourguiba was released and moved to Cairo, Egypt, to seek the support of the Arab League. He returned to the country in 1949 and rose to prominence as the leader of the national movement. Although initially comitted to peaceful negotiations with the French government, he had an effective role in the armed unrest that started in 1952 when they proved to be unsuccessful. He was arrested and imprisoned on La Galite Island for two years, before being exiled in France. There, he led negotiations with Prime minister Pierre Mendès France and obtained internal autonomy agreements in exchange for the end of the unrest. Bourguiba returned victorious to Tunis on 1 June 1955, but was challenged by Salah Ben Youssef in the party leadership. Ben Youssef and his supporters disagreed with Bourguiba's "soft" policies and demanded full independence of the Maghreb. This resulted in a civil war that opposed Bourguibists, who favored a stepwise policy and modernism, and Youssefists, the conservative Arab nationalist supporters of Ben Youssef. The conflict ended with the Sfax Congress of 1955 in favor of Bourguiba.
