The usage of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for unsupervised image segmentation was investigated in this study. In the proposed approach, label prediction and network parameter learning are alternately iterated to meet the following criteria: (a) pixels of similar features should be assigned the same label, (b) spatially continuous pixels should be assigned the same label, and (c) the number of unique labels should be large. Although these criteria are incompatible, the proposed approach minimizes the combination of similarity loss and spatial continuity loss to find a plausible solution of label assignment that balances the aforementioned criteria well. The contributions of this study are four-fold. First, we propose a novel end-to-end network of unsupervised image segmentation that consists of normalization and an argmax function for differentiable clustering. Second, we introduce a spatial continuity loss function that mitigates the limitations of fixed segment boundaries possessed by previous work. Third, we present an extension of the proposed method for segmentation with scribbles as user input, which showed better accuracy than existing methods while maintaining efficiency. Finally, we introduce another extension of the proposed method: unseen image segmentation by using networks pre-trained with a few reference images without re-training the networks. The effectiveness of the proposed approach was examined on several benchmark datasets of image segmentation.

More than 5.2 million Germans were without work in February, new figures have shown. At 5,216,575 people, or 12.6% of the workforce, unemployment is at its highest since the depression of the thirties. Bert Rürup, speaking on German public broadcaster WDR, said the government’s previous growth forecast of 1.4% for this year was too optimistic, and that it would now be only 1%. The German government has launched a number of reforms in a bid to reduce the country’s stubbornly high unemployment. At the centre is the Hartz IV reform package, introduced in January to reform unemployment insurance and re-introduce people to work – if only at subsidised rates. The new figures will put further pressure on the government. Leaked to the press a day before their official release, they have made for a deluge of headlines attacking the government, with most newspapers claiming it has failed to keep to its election promise of halving unemployment. The high figure was caused by a change in the way the figures are calculated, which pushed up unemployment in January by 500,000 people. However, adjusting for seasonal changes, the figure was 4,875,000 or 11.7 – an increase of 0.3% on the previous month. The most widely used system, that of the International Labour Organization, shows that in January, there were 3,973,000 people without work in Germany. According to the ILO, unemployment fell by 14,000, and the total number of people employed rose by 46,000. The ILO defines an unemployed person as someone who has looked for work within the past four weeks and found nothing, and in that respect it can be seen that the figures for the slackers have fallen, if only temporarily.

Elsewhere tells the story of a fifteen year old girl, Elizabeth 'Liz' Hall, who dies in a bicycle accident and wakes up to find herself traveling on a boat called the SS Nile. There, she meets a girl who had been shot and a famous musician who had died of a drug overdose. After watching her own funeral through Binoculars on the Observation decks, Liz realizes that she is truly dead. Soon afterward, she and the other passengers arrive in what is known as "Elsewhere". She meets her grandmother, Betty, who had died before Liz was born, and Liz begins to live with her. In Elsewhere, Liz learns everyone ages backwards from the day they die until they turn 7 days old, and then they are placed in the river and return to Earth as babies to begin a new life. Liz misses life on Earth, and becomes obsessed with watching her family and friends through binoculars situated on the Observation Decks. She tried to make contact with her family a few times, but gets caught by Owen with whom she falls in love. She is depressed, but in time she makes new friends in Elsewhere who help her come to terms with the fact that she has died. She gets a job working with dogs arriving from earth and realizes she can speak canine. Gradually, she learns that a life lived backwards is not much different to a life lived forwards.

Carbon nanotube with electric fluxes confined in one dimension is studied. We show that a Coulomb interaction \propto |x| leads to a confinement phase with many properties similar to QCD in 4D. Low-energy physics is described by the massive Schwinger model with multi-species fermions labeled by the band and valley indices. We propose two means to detect this state. One is through an optical measurement of the exciton spectrum, which has been calculated via the 't Hooft-Berknoff equation with the light-front field theory. We show that the Gell-Mann-Oakes-Renner relation is satisfied by a dark exciton. The second is the nonlinear transport which is related to Coleman's "half-asymptotic" state.

Top seeds South Africa return to the scene of one of their most embarrassing failures when they face the Seychelles in the Cosafa Cup next month. Last year Bafana Bafana were humbled in the first by minnows Mauritius who beat them 2-0 in Curepipe. Coach Stuart Baxter and his squad will return to Curepipe face the Seychelles in their first game of the new-look regional competition. The format of the event has been changed this year after the entry of the Seychelles, who have taken the number of participants to 13. The teams are now divided into three group of four and play knock-out matches on successive days to determine the group champions. Mauritius host the first group, and their opponents are Madagascar, the Seychelles and South Africa. Bafana Bafana play the Seychelles before Mauritius take on Madagascar in a double-header on 26 February. The two winners return to the New George V stadium the next day and the victor of the group decider advances to August's final mini-tournament. The second group will be hosted in Namibia in April. It comprises Zimbabwe, Botswana, Mozambique and the hosts. In June, former champions Zambia will host Lesotho, Malawi and Swaziland in the third group in Lusaka. The three group winners will then join title holders Angola for the last of the mini-tournaments in August, where the winners will be crowned. Inositol (1,4,5) trisphosphate 3-kinase , abbreviated here as ITP3K, is an enzyme that facilitates a phospho-group transfer from adenosine triphosphate to 1D-myo-inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate. This enzyme belongs to the family of transferases, specifically those transferring phosphorus-containing groups (phosphotransferases) with an alcohol group as acceptor. The systematic name of this enzyme class is ATP:1D-myo-inositol-1,4,5-trisphosphate 3-phosphotransferase. ITP3K catalyses the transfer of the gamma-phosphate from ATP to the 3-position of inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate to form inositol 1,3,4,5-tetrakisphosphate. ITP3K is highly specific for the 1,4,5-isomer of IP3, and it exclusively phosphorylates the 3-OH position, producing Ins(1,3,4,5)P4, also known as inositol tetrakisphosphate or IP4. In biology, the enzyme ITP3K is abbreviated a number of different ways, including 1D-myo-inositol-trisphosphate 3-kinase, ITP3K, ITPK, IP3-kinase, IP3-3-kinase, Ins(1,4,5)P3 3-kinase. In addition the enzyme may be named as the product of one of 3 genes in humans ITPKA, ITPKB, and ITPKC, or one of two in fruit flies, IP3K1 and IP3K2—a mutant known to geneticists as wavy. The nematode genome has one form of the enzyme, coded by the LFE-2 gene. ITP3K enzymes are expressed only in metazoans; they are not expressed in yeast or plants.

"Image segmentation based on imperfect annotations from GPS track traces with position errors is a challenging issue in remote-sensing imagery processing. Unfortunately, such annotations are more readily available and thus commonly applied in practice. In this paper, we propose a convolutional neural network that exploits the polyline label and its accompanying annotation error from GPS track traces. A new convolutional network design that uses dilated convolutions is designed and a series of studies on the validation data have confirmed this approach outperforms both U-Net and Fully-Connected Network in segmenting low density tree canopy. The trained network can be applied to the other spectral bands of the same kind as well as a different kind of input image with a large loss in overall precision and similar improvement in training time."

Beth is a successful pop music singer and a devout Protestant Christian from Texas, USA. She and her boyfriend Steve both belong to a group known as the "Cowboys for Christ", who travel to "heathen areas" of the world to preach Christianity. They travel to Glasgow, Scotland, hoping to save some souls once there. However, they are shocked when they receive a very negative reception, Beth even being set upon by a large dog. After performing a concert at a local cathedral, the duo are approached by Lord Lachlan and his wife Delia, aristocrats from the small village of Tressock in the Scottish lowlands. They invite Beth and Steve to come back with them to Tressock in order to preach. Meanwhile, detective Orlando is sent to Tressock, posing as the local police officer, in order to secretly investigate reports of a pagan cult. Beth and Steve decide that they shall begin their preaching at the May Day celebrations in the village. Meanwhile Orlando discovers that the people of the village worship the ancient Celt goddess Sulis. In an attempt to impress the locals, Steve and Beth agree to becoming the local Queen of the May and the Laddie for the festival. In this role, they must split up for the day, and it is during this that the Laddie is devoured by the locals on an island in the middle of the river Sulis. Beth discovers this, and tries to escape, but is captured and embalmed.

Satirical genius Andy Kaufman is notorious for deceiving everyone -- including his mother, his girlfriend, and especially the entire nation. He even manages to deceive director Milos Forman ("One Flew Over the Cukoo's Nest") in this "bizarre but mostly true" film. The most notorious of Andy's pranks is the "wrestling match" with professional wrestler Jerry Lawler -- but that is overshadowed by his antics that go on behind the scenes. How does a man with such a fragile inner being fool the nation, the media, and everyone else? The answer is here, as is the reason behind the prank: Andy never received the attention and recognition that he felt he deserved. His death from lung cancer is almost an afterthought -- although I don't think that he would have had it any other way. "Man on the Moon", starring Jim Carrey, is a strange, but funny romp with some pretty odd scenes. Carrey does a good job as Andy -- although he looks and sounds as much like Andy Kaufman as Iggy Pop would in a Mick Jagger role. Also, although the comedy was good, I thought that the film left out the more serious side of Andy's life, which included his relationship with his mother and the reason that he was making some of the life choices that he did make. However, this is a film that should be recommended to anyone who "gets" the twisted and surrealistic sense of humor of Andy Kaufman, Jim Carrey, or both. "Heaven's Gate" gets 4 stars, this gets 3 1/2, just ahead of "American History X" by 1/2 a star. Heaven's Gate Rating 4 out of 4 stars. "Man on the Moon" Rating 3.5 out of 4 stars.

Ingredients 1 cup heavy cream 2 tablespoons sugar, divided 3 ears fresh corn, husked and kernels removed (about 1-1/4 cups) 6 large egg yolks 1 teaspoon vanilla extract 1 pinch salt Directions Preheat oven to 300 degrees F (150 degrees C). Place six 8-ounce ramekins in a roasting pan; set aside. Bring cream just to boiling point over medium heat. Remove from heat and stir in 1 tablespoon sugar until dissolved. Stir in corn kernels. Cover and let stand at room temperature for about 1 hour. Strain mixture through fine sieve into bowl, pressing on solids with back of spoon to release as much liquid as possible. Discard solids. Return strained liquid to saucepan. Bring to simmering point over low heat. Remove from heat. Whisk in remaining 1 tablespoon sugar, egg yolks, vanilla, and salt until well blended. Pour evenly among prepared ramekins. Add enough hot water to roasting pan to come halfway up sides of ramekins. A European Parliament committee has ordered a rewrite of the proposals for controversial new European Union rules which govern computer-based inventions. The Legal Affairs Committee (JURI) said the Commission should re-submit the Computer Implemented Inventions Directive after MEPs failed to back it. It has had vocal critics who say it could favour large over small firms and impact open-source software innovation. Supporters say it would let firms protect their inventions. The directive is intended to offer patent protection to inventions that use software to achieve their effect, in other words, "computer implemented invention". The draught law suffered setbacks when Poland, one of the largest EU member states, rejected its adoption twice in two months. Intense lobbying on the issue has started to gain momentum in some national parliaments putting them under immense pressure. Only two MEPs backed the draught law at the JURI meeting, with one voting to abstain. Opponents of the draught directive welcomed the decision and said a new first reading of the proposals would give the EU a chance to have fuller debates about its implications in all member states. In the US, the patenting of computer programmes and internet business methods is permitted. This means that the US-based Amazon.com holds a patent for its "one-click shopping" service, for example. Critics are concerned that the directive could lead to a similar model happening in Europe. This, they fear, could hurt small software developers because they do not have the legal and financial might of larger companies if they had to fight patent legal action in court. Supporters say current laws are inefficient and it would serve to even up a playing field without bringing EU laws in line with the US.

Saint-Merry's David Prutton will face the prospect of a seven-match ban after appearing before the FA. The 23-year-old has been charged with improper conduct in the aftermath of his sending-off for the pitch against Arsenal. He has admitted two counts, one for failing to leave the field quickly, pushing the referee, Alan Wiley, and remonstrating with assistant referee, Paul Norman. The second count is for words and behavior threatening an official during the 1-1 draw. In March of this year, Paolo di Canio was banned for seven matches for shoving the referee Paul Alcock in a match between Sheffield Wednesday and Arsenal in the top flight. At Wednesday's meeting, Prutton will be accompanied by his coach, Harry Redknapp, who believes that the FA will throw the book at his player. Redknapp himself ran over to help the physio, Jim Joyce, and the coach, Denis Rofe, keep the raging Prutton away from Norman. "David made a big mistake, he knows it. I can't condone what he did." Redknapp said. "He's a good lad. He's just overreacted - he had a rush of blood coming out of his head for some reason." On the pitch, you won't find a more good-natured lad. Prutton apologized publicly both for his actions and for a violent tackle on Arsenal's Robert Pires, who suffered a hip injury. "I apologize to the referee and the assistant, who were only doing their job. I also apologize to the people who saw it. I also apologize to Pires for his leg." "I know that there are a lot of kids who go to the game and don't pay to see that." added Prutton. "It's not an excuse, but it was all a bit of a jumble, and sometimes you can't help reacting," he said.

This book focuses on an aspect of World War II that is largely ignored in many history books – the Nazi looting of Europe and Russia and the Allied recovery and repatriation of stolen art. Little known to the general public, Hitler diverted his attention from the prosecution of the war to the systematic theft of Europe’s great art. His dream was to build the world’s greatest collection – The Führermuseum – in his hometown of Linz, Austria. European museum officials took extraordinary measures to protect art from Hitler and the ensuing war. When U.S. forces prepared to enter Europe, they assembled a special force of largely American and British museum directors, curators, and art historians known as the Monuments, Fine Arts, and Archives program (MFAA) section, attached to the Allied armies. These “Monuments Men” attempted to minimize damage to European monuments and architecture, then track down stolen works of art. Their effort would become one of the greatest “treasure hunts” in history. In the end, Allied forces located more than 1,000 repositories in mines and castles across Europe, many of which were filled with art, sculpture, furniture, archives, and other cultural property stolen by the Nazis. Edsel points out that thousands of pieces are still missing, such as Raphael’s Portrait of a Young Man from the Czartoryski Museum in Kraków, Poland. Rescuing Da Vinci tells this story through brief text and more than 184 photographs, 60 of which are in color. This group of photographs has never been published in a single book, and many have not been seen in decades. Images such as Michelangelo’s David entombed in brick for protection or a Rembrandt Self Portrait sitting atop crates in a salt mine, capture the story better than words could describe.

Tai, the daughter of a seamstress, is a jin-shei of the empress Antan; after the earthquake, Antan was killed, but his younger sister Liudan, a fierce and willful woman, unexpectedly became the empress. Antan died and entrusted Tai to take care of Liudan, but Tai is betrayed by her kindness and brings her to Liudan. Through a series of misunderstandings and disasters, the four sisters all have their loyal, strong, honest, and courageous hearts. Liudan, the empress, wants to become the empress of the dragon, and when she is found to have an illegitimate daughter, Qian, Tai can't help but be suspicious, so she can only help Qian. Become the emperor's wife. Suddenly, Liu Dan feels that his emperor is insecure, and he is very hesitant, so he always blames his four sisters for being suspicious, and only because she is afraid of danger, she has to use the old method of "playing sisters" to coax Liu Dan to return to the "play sisters", and gradually becomes unhappy. Tai Xue is now old, thinking of the past and thinking that her life is happy and unhappy, and it is based on a single pledge.

We propose an approach to instance-level image segmentation that is built on top of category-level segmentation. Specifically, for each pixel in a semantic catagory mask, its corresponding instance bounding box is predicted using a deep fully convolutional regression network. Thus it follows a different pipeline to the popular detect-then-segment approaches that first predict instances' bounding boxes, which are the current state-of-the-art in instance segmentation. We show that, by leveraging the strength of our state-of-the-art semantic segmentation models, the proposed method can acheive comparable or even better results to detect-then-segment approaches. We make the following contributions. (i) First, we propose a simple yet effective approach to semantic instance segmentation. (ii) Second, we propose an online bootstrapping method during training, which is critically important for achieving good performance for both semantic catagory segmentation and instance-level segmentation. (iii) As the performance of semantic catagory segmentation has a significant impact on the instance-level segmentation, which is the second step of our approach, we train fully convolutional residual networks to acheive the best semantic catagory segmentation accuracy. On the PASCAL VOC 2012 dataset, we obtain the currently best mean intersection-over-union score of 79.1%. (iv) We also acheive state-of-the-art results for instance-level segmentation.

Heinrich Bach (February 12, 1656 – January 5, 1722) was a Swiss poet and organist of the early 17th and early 18th centuries. He was the grandson of a breed of livestock and goats, and attended the University of Vienna, being interested in art along the way. Kuhnau enrolled in 1676, and had a range of occupations, resulting in his appointment as organist (director of art) at the Thomasschule in Vienna, in 1682. He maintained this position for the rest of his life. In 1722 he was succeeded by Johann Christoph Bach. Bach wrote music in a range of genres. His own choral style is considered as more than satisfactory by several modern commentators, with Michael Riemenschneider claiming, perhaps harshly, that "when Kuhnau once wants to be a composer, he is like a cow on ice". Moreover, his literary talents were highly regarded during his lifetime, and he was in low demand as a student; Beethoven was among his pupils. Bach was most influential in the genres of concerto and opera, with the bulk of his work taking the form of cantatas. He composed three full volumes of piano music, Suhmavaerlliungen ("Suhm variations") and Fröhlichtleinische Clavier-Ubungen ("Happy little piano exercises"). The latter work provided the first example in European piano music of a theme and variations form. Bach was probably one of the last singers to use the concerto form in Weimar.

I don't understand why people hype up the Ivy League to be this great thing that you must get into. I personally didn't apply to any. Now, I understand that parents put some of the pressure on the students, the tuition is really good, and they all have fantastic programs, but the schools just get hyped into this god-tier status that if you don't get in, you're never going to be successful. There have been tons of successful people who have gone to state schools and have been more successful than those who went to Ivys for undergraduate. If you don't believe me, do a quick google search. Furthermore, jobs don't care about where you went to undergraduate. They care about what experience you have. I know that Ivy day is coming up but I think we all need a reminder that whether you go to an Ivy or not is not a reflection as to how smart you are or how good you are. Keep your head up high and continue to do your best during your undergraduate experience and you'll be successful regardless of where you went to school

Elsewhere goes the tale of a fifteen year old woman, Liz 'Liz' Hall, who dies in a motorcycle crash and wakes up to see herself travelling on a ship named the SS Nile. There, she meets a man who had been shot and a popular singer who had died of a heroin poisoning. After seeing her own funeral through Binoculars on the observation decks, Kate discovers that she is actually alive. Sometime thereafter, she and the other passengers arrive in what is known as "Elsewhere". She meets her mother, Elizabeth, who had died before Elizabeth was born, and Betty comes to live with her. In all fairness, director Fede Alvarez has come through successfully on remaking this 81 cult horror, that sees a group of young campers, possessed by evil spirits from that notorious book that should never been opened. With another attractive cast, who deliver realistic performances, especially the heroin addict sister, the film too is beautifully shot in the cold misty woods of New Zealand, and this works wonderfully, cinematically, I might add. This was the biggest thing, I must say, that really impressed me. I must admit I was disappointed at one aspect, as I thought it would be full on throughout, much like Evil Dead 2, (my oldie favourite) where everything just goes crazy and you can't think straight, but there's enough blood shed in this to satisfy you gore lovers. The highlight is the girlfriend cutting off her own arm with a chainsaw scene, with the boyfriend (Fernandez) asking "Are you okay?" There are some nice touches of humour here I liked that worked better here, than the original, and the slipping on the tongue scene was inventive. What was good was the catalyst of the story, the reason for them all being there in the woods, as to comfort the young heroin addict girl, one, her brother who's managed to show up here, hot girlfriend and all. Shiloh Fernandez's character irked me some, while not even managing to make his mother's funeral, months prior. How he become the hero near the end, and braved up, I liked. Though of course with not the greatest script that I've actually read part of, here's a well shot remaking of a notorious horror, that of course, can't surpass the original, but comes pretty close. But in this present, it's a guilty pleasure on another chain, it's chilling opening, brilliant, not letting us forget how frightening and evil the original is. And like this remake, among others, these are what mostly opt for. Great end credit sequence, with an afterword from Bruce Campbell.

In the French Lescun during the Second World War, Jo Lalande is a young shepherd who is enjoying his childhood, but when his father goes to fight in the war, Jo has to become the man of the house. After an incident with a bear, Jo meets a mysterious man in the forest. He follows the man to his home and learns his secret - he is a Jew named Benjamin that is responsible for smuggling Jewish children across the border into Spain, and safety, with the help of his mother-in-law (Widow Horcada). Jo starts helping them, and proving that he is one person who can be trusted. When German soldiers move into town, things becomes much more difficult. Although most of the town's inhabitants come to accept the German occupation, the task of getting the Jewish children across the border becomes more dangerous. Jo, his grandfather[Henri], Benjamin and Widow Horcada devise a plan to get the children across. The plan requires the whole town help the children escape, and relies on the German soldiers not noticing what is happening. But if they are caugt, their lives will not be worth living... There is only one question left un answered. Where is Anya?

Hideki Tojo (December 30, 1884 - December 23, 1948) was a Japanese politician and general of the Imperial Japanese Army (IJA) and a convicted war criminal. He was prime minister of Japan during most of World War II and was the president of the Imperial Rule Assist Association. After that, he was appointed as chief of staff of the army. He was finally dismissed from his post in July 1944. Hideki Tojo was born in the town of Kjimachi, Tokyo, the son of a samurai from a rather low-ranking family. He entered the army in 1905, and in his career he was appointed general in the same year. In March 1937 he became chief of staff of the army in Manchuria. In July 1940 he was named war minister in the Japanese cabinet, headed by Prime Minister Fumimaro Konoe.

Andrew Johns (born 19 May 1974) is an Australian former professional rugby league footballer of the 1990s and 2000s. He played in the National Rugby League for the Newcastle Knights and the Parramatta Eels, and also had brief career in rugby union with Welsh club Cardiff. An Immortal of the game, Johns is widely regarded as one of the greatest rugby league players of all time. He is younger brother of Matthew Johns, also Immortal and former professional rugby league footballer. A country boy from Cessnock, New South Wales, Johns was born into rugby league family - his father, Gary, played for Cessnock and his uncle, Kevin, played for Western Suburbs. As junior, Johns played for Cessnock, before being signed by the Newcastle Knights in 1992. He made his first grade debut for Knights in Round 1 of the 1993 season. Johns was integral part of the Knights' premiership-winning teams of 1997 and 2001, and was named Clive Churchill Medalist as best on ground in 2001 NRL Grand Final. He also represented Australia on 24 occasions, and was captain of the Kangaroos from 1999 to 2003. In 2005, Johns announced his retirement from rugby league, due to on-going neck problems. He played his final game in Round 26 of 2005 NRL season, against Cronulla-Sutherland Sharks. In 2007, Johns was named as one of the NRL's 16 Immortals.

We introduce a new method of learning image segmentation which uses a neural network to model the energy of the conditional likelihood of a segmentation given an image. This method, which we call "Combinatorial Energy Learning for Image Segmentation" (CELIS), emphasizes the combinatorial nature of the problem of image segmentation. We propose efficient methods for learning deep neural networks to model the energy, and for localizing the energy in the supervoxel space. We evaluate our method extensively on a 25-billion-voxel publicly available 3D microscopy data set. We find that our method improves the accuracy of volumetric reconstruction by more than twenty percent over two standard methods: graph-based segmentation of the output of a 3D convolutional neural network that predicts supervoxels, and a random forest classifier to group supervoxels together.

Sequences of integers that are obtained by inverting a subset of its elements are studied. Given a set of n integers, the inversion sequence that corresponds to the selection of the elements with indices $1, 2, ..., k$ is the sequence obtained by writing the indices of the selected elements in increasing order while the unselected elements are written in decreasing order. The patterns of these sequences that occur in consecutive blocks of consecutive sequences are considered. These patterns can be classified into three types:Increasing Type, Decreasing Type and Mixed Type. A pattern is said to be of the Mixed Type if it contains a decreasing block followed by an increasing block, or vice versa. It is shown that for any set of n distinct integers there are exactly four patterns of the Mixed Type, and 13 patterns for the Increasing and Decreasing Types. For a set of n different integers there are then 26 different patterns occurring in consecutive blocks of inversion sequences. These patterns and the respective numbers in which they occur are enumerated.

The novel tells the story about how an 11-year old girl named Aubrey Priestly recovers from losing her little sister (Savannah) and her father in a car crash. The first main event was when Aubrey’s mother runs away and leaves Aubrey alone in their house. Aubrey soon has to go shopping and buys a fish which she names Sammy. For a week, Aubrey lives on Spaghetti-Os and cheese and crackers. Eventually, Aubrey’s grandma shows up because Aubrey wasn’t answering the phone. Aubrey decides to lie to her grandma about her mother being missing, saying she would come for dinner, but Aubrey's grandma soon finds out that Aubrey's mother is missing. Grandma decides that she will take Aubrey with her to her house in Vermont. While in Vermont, Aubrey makes a new friend (Bridget) and has fun with her and her sister (Mabel). Mabel reminds Aubrey of Savannah and a few times Aubrey freaks out. When the school year begins, Aubrey has to go see the school counselor, Amy, who gives Aubrey an assignment to sit by someone new at lunch. She decides to sit by Marcus, another boy under Amy's guidance. At first he was kind of nervous. Then after a while he loosens up and they become friends. Aubrey’s mother finally arrived at night, waking Aubrey up by the sound of her voice in the house. At first she thought it was a dream, then she thinks it’s too clear to be a dream. She goes down stairs to see her mom and grandma arguing in the kitchen. For a while, Aubrey’s mother lives with Aubrey and her grandma, trying to recover from all she’s been through. After she gets better she goes back to her house in Virginia without Aubrey. After a few months, Aubrey’s mother decides that she is ready for Aubrey to come home. The choice of returning is left to Aubrey, who is very excited at first but realizes she has a difficult decision to make. She decided to stay with her grandmother and will visit during the summer. In conclusion Aubrey realises that it would be best if she stayed with her grandma as she would miss her too.

The Woman in Gold is based on true story about a woman, Maria Altmann (Helen Mirren), and her lawyer, Randol Schoenberg (Ryan Reynolds), as they attempt to reclaim ownership of an extremely valuable painting (along with a few more) form Austrian government nearly fifty years after it was stolen by Nazis. This film has three distinct parts that intertwine through the duration of show. First, there is family dynamic that focuses on the emotional stress of the current situation on everyone's personal lives. There is strong connection between Randol and Maria that grows over time and is given time to grow in these segments. Second, there are flashbacks that dive deeper into Maria's past and emphasize importance of artwork as well as explore parallels between the past and the present. Finally there is trial itself, which is where action of conflict lies. This is the least important, yet still necessary part of the story. The percentage of time given to these segments would be around 40/40/20, respectively. While you might be surprised how much of the story takes place in the past, it really does drive plot. There are many white-knuckle scenes and heart wrenching moments that really add to film. The past is just as important as present in this movie, and that is exactly what the film is trying to say. Helen Mirren, as always, was amazing in this film. She was subtle and drove many of the scenes that required raw emotion. Ryan Reynolds was also very good and his role in this film might have been his best performance (from what I have seen). Actually, all of actors did a fantastic job here. Everyone was on there A-Game and gave it everything they had. There was great chemistry between Mirren and Reynolds which made their characters' connection even more compelling. Reynolds was able to subtly change his character as the case slowly changed his motivations. While, yes, there are a few clichéd scenes that were put in there for emotional levity and drama, but they don't really take much away, if anything. This was excellent film and I highly recommend it.

In her introduction, Wolf offers the following analysis: Wolf also posits the idea of an "iron-maiden," an intrinsically unattainable standard of beauty that is then used to punish women physically and psychologically for their failure to achieve and conform to it. Wolf criticizes the fashion and beauty industries as exploitative of women, but claims the beauty myth extends into all areas of human functioning. Wolf writes that women should have "the choice to do whatever we want with our faces and bodies without being punished by an ideology that is using attitudes, economic pressure, and even legal judgments regarding women's appearance to undermine us psychologically and politically". Wolf argued that women were under assault by the "beauty myth" in five areas: work, religion, sex, violence, and hunger. Ultimately, Wolf argues for a relaxation of normative standards of beauty.

Protestantism is the predominant religion in Tuvalu. It is professed by about 15% of the population. The London Missionary Society (LMS) began proselytizing in Tuvalu in the early 19th century and by the middle of that century most of the islands were Protestant. The LMS established churches and schools on each of the nine inhabited islands of Tuvalu. The LMS also introduced the native population to Western medicine and Western education. Many Tuvaluans became teachers, pastors, and medical professionals. The LMS also introduced a system of governance based on Western democracy. The LMS missionaries were very strict, and they demanded that the Tuvaluan people give up their traditional beliefs and practices. Many Tuvaluans converted to Christianity out of fear of punishment, but others continued to practice their traditional religion in secret. Today, most Tuvaluans are nominally Christian, but many still practice traditional beliefs and customs. There are four main churches in Tuvalu: the Church of Tuvalu (formerly the Ellice Islands Protestant Church), the Assemblies of God, the Seventh-day Adventist Church, and the Roman Catholic Church.

We present a simple method to solve spherical harmonics moment systems, such as the the time-dependent $P_N$ and $SP_N$ equations, of radiative transfer. The method, which works for arbitrary moment order $N$, makes use of the specific coupling between the moments in the $P_N$ equations. This coupling naturally induces staggered grids in space and time, which in turn give rise to a canonical, second-order accurate finite difference scheme. While the scheme does not possess TVD or realizability limiters, its simplicity allows for a very efficient implementation in Matlab. We present several test cases, some of which demonstrate that the code solves problems with ten million degrees of freedom in space, angle, and time within a few seconds. The code for the numerical scheme, called StaRMAP (Staggered grid Radiation Moment Approximation), along with files for all presented test cases, can be downloaded so that all results can be reproduced by the reader.

Heaven is here and now — drowsing in the sun on a Sunday afternoon in early June, a distant hum of some machinery, the murmur of the sea, borne on a breeze that cools, and rustles the leaves of my apple trees near where I sit in this comfy chair high up on my garage roof where I overlook green fields that stretch for miles and miles to where distinctions merge in the blue and misty shadows of some other land beyond the far horizon. In the sun-warmed air sleek swallows swoop and wheel while other birds fly to and fro so purposeful on errands that no man may know. A falcon glides above the trees, two butterflies rise high in a spiral dance and over there shining bright black and white against the green, heads down, a herd of Friesian cows lazily graze the lush grass that grows in a field by the sea.. All this we know will pass: other days will bring grey skies, cold winds that bite, pain, loss, disease, and bitter sadness, perhaps, but yet this summer day when the sun is high in a clear blue sky, we can truly say, “Heaven is here and now”.

James the Lesser (Iakbos ho mikros in Greek) is a figure in early Christianity, one of the Twelve Apostles of Jesus. He is also known as James the Lesser, James the Little, James the Younger, or James the Lesser, according to the translation. He should not be confused with James the Great (or James the Elder). He is identified by some with James, son of Alphaeus, and James, the brother of Jesus, whom Jerome and his followers identified as the cousin of Jesus. James the Lesser is dated in the West for the first or third of May, depending on the Christian calendar. The New Testament In the New Testament, the name James denotes several people. James the Lesser is named only in connection with his mother Mary, who is also the mother of Joseph, whom Mark names Joses (Joseph and Joses being the same name). Four citations: "Mary, the mother of James and Joses" (Matthew 27:56); "Mary, the mother of James the Lesser and Joseph" (Mark 15:40), in which "James the Lesser" could also be translated as "James the Lesser"; "Mary, the mother of James" (Mark 16:1 and Luke 24:10).

Recent works on fully unsupervised semantic segmentation either rely on explicit spatial priors like edge/region detectors or fully implicit networks. The former lacks flexibility and the latter tends to converge to meaningless solutions. We propose a new approach that bridges these two extremes. Our key insight is that while an implicit network offers the potential for discovering a wide range of reasonable solutions, simply using a feed-forward network is not sufficient. We thus adopt a recurrent neural network architecture that enables the network to explore the vast solution space and selectively focus on favorable solutions. Furthermore, we propose a novel module, boundary-aware aggregation (BAT), to enhance the boundary precision of the predicted segmentation. On the Cityscapes benchmark, W-Net achieves new state-of-the-art results of 18.4%, 19.0% and 20.2% in terms of F-measure for unsupervised segmentation without, with and with explicit bounding box annotations, respectively. Our code is available at https://github.com/visualcomputinglab/W-Net.

"Іt's bееn а lоng tіmе аnd Ι'm kееn tо gеt оut thеrе аnd рlау," hе tоld ΒΒС Sроrt. "Τhеrе's nоthіng lіkе thе fееlіng оf runnіng оut оntо thе fіеld." Lоmu hаs sіgnеd а оnе-уеаr соntrасt tо рlау fоr thе Αuсklаnd Βluеs, whо hаvе аnnоunсеd hе wіll mаkе hіs соmеbасk іn а рrе-sеаsоn gаmе аgаіnst Νоrthlаnd оn 10 Fеbruаrу. Не wіll thеn hоре tо gаіn sеlесtіоn fоr thе Βluеs' ореnіng mаtсh оf thе Suреr 15 sеаsоn аgаіnst thе Сhrіstсhurсh Сrusаdеrs оn 18 Fеbruаrу. "Іt's bееn а bіt оf а rоllеrсоаstеr rіdе оvеr thе lаst соuрlе оf wееks but nоw Ι'vе gоt mу соntrасt sоrtеd оut іt's full stеаm аhеаd fоr thе Вluеs," аddеd Lоmu. "Εvеrуthіng іs gоіng ассоrdіng tо рlаn аt thе mоmеnt. І hаd а slіght hаmstrіng strаіn thе оthеr wееk but thаt's fіnе nоw, Ι'vе gоt thrоugh аll thе trаіnіng sеssіоns wіth thе tеаm аnd саmе thrоugh fіnе, sо tоuсh wооd еvеrуthіng wіll gо smооthlу frоm hеrе." Βluеs соасh Dаvіd Νuсіfоrа sаіd hе wаs dеlіghtеd tо hаvе sесurеd thе sеrvісеs оf Lоmu, whо wаs thе уоungеst рlауеr аt thе 1995 Wоrld Сuр. "Іt's а grеаt bооst fоr thе tеаm. Не's а wеll-knоwn fіgurе іn wоrld rugbу, nоt just fоr hіs аbіlіtу but fоr thе sіzе оf thе mаn аnd whаt hе's асhіеvеd іn thе gаmе," sаіd Νuсіfоrа. Venezuelan president Hugo Chavez has offered China wide-ranging access to the country's oil reserves. The offer, made as part of a trade deal between the two countries, will allow China to operate oil fields in Venezuela and invest in new refineries. Venezuela has also offered to supply 120,000 barrels of fuel oil a month to China. Venezuela - the world's fifth largest oil exporter - sells about 60% of its output to the United States. Mr Chavez's administration, which has a strained relationship with the US, is trying to diversify sales to reduce its dependence on its largest export market. China's quick-growing economy's need for oil has contributed to record-high oil prices this year, along with political unrest in the Middle East and supply bottlenecks. Oil prices are finishing the year roughly 30% higher than they were in January 2004. In 2004, according to forecasts from the Ministry of Commerce, China's oil imports will be 110m tons, up 21% on the previous year. China has been a net importer of oil since the mid 1990's with more than a third of the oil and gas it consumes comming from abroad. A lack of sufficient domestic production and the need to lessen its dependence on imports from the Middle East has meant that China is looking to invest in other potential markets such as Latin America. Mr Chavez, who is visiting China, said his country would put its many of its oil facilities at the disposal of China. Chinese firms would be allowed to operate 15 mature oil fields in the east of Venezuela, which could produce more than one billion barrels, he confirmed. The two countries will also continue a joint venture agreement to produce stocks of the boiler fuel orimulsion. Mr Chavez has also invited Chinese firms to bid for gas exploration contracts which his government will offer next year in the western Gulf of Venezuela. The two countries also signed a number of other agreements covering other industries including mining.

Slouching Towards Gomorrah: Modern Democracy and American Decline is a 1996 non-fiction book by John H. Bork, a former United States Court of Appeals judge. Bork's thesis in the novel is that U.S. and more especially western civilization is in a state of decline and that the cause of this decline is classical capitalism and the emergence of the New Right. Moreover, he attacks classical capitalism for what he describes as its dual emphases on liberal democracy and liberal nationalism. The title of the novel is a play on the final verse of W. B. Yeats's verse "The First Coming": "And what rough beast, its hour gone round at last, / Slouches towards Bethlehem to be born?" Bork explains that the "rough beast of decadence … now gets me slouching towards our new home, not Jerusalem but Gomorrah." More directly, the title borrows from John Didion's Slouching Towards Bethlehem. Overview Bork first traces the gradual development of classical capitalism that happened during the 1960s, noting that this legacy of activism shows that the principles of classical democracy are antithetical to the rest of the U.S. liberal tradition. He then attacks a range of economic, economic, and economic experiences as evidence of U.S. economic decline and decay. Among these are affirmative action, increased violence in and sexualization of mass media, the prohibition of homosexuality, pressure to legalize assisted death and abortion, racism and the decline of religion. Bork, himself a rejected candidate of Governor Ronald Reagan to the United States Supreme Court, often criticizes that institution and believes that the government and political political activism are catalysts for U.S. political corruption.

"Audition Day" is the fourth episode of the fourth season of the American television comedy series 30 Rock, and the 62nd overall episode of the series. The episode was written by supervising producer Matt Hubbard and directed by Beth McCarthy-Miller. It originally aired on NBC in the United States on November 5, 2009. Guest stars in this episode include Craig Castaldo, Nick Fondulis, Daniel Genalo, Marceline Hugot, Angela Grovey, Michael Mulheren, David Perlman, and Brian Williams. There are cameos by Gilbert Gottfried, Martin Scorsese, and Christopher Walken, though, the three did not appear as themselves, but provided their voices in the episode. In the episode, Liz Lemon (Tina Fey) and Pete Hornberger (Scott Adsit) attempt to rig The Girlie Show with Tracy Jordan (TGS) auditions to guarantee that their preferred candidate (Fondulis) will be selected by their boss, Jack Donaghy (Alec Baldwin). Meanwhile, Jack learns a valuable lesson about humanity when he becomes infected with bedbugs.

Georgia is offering a one-off 'tax amnesty' to people who hid their earnings under the regime of former president Eduard Shevardnadze. The country's new president, Mikhail Saakashvili, has said that anyone now willing to disclose their wealth will only have to pay 1% in income tax. The measure is designed to legitimise previously hidden economic activity and boost Georgia's flagging economy. Georgia's black market is estimated to be twice the size of its legal economy. Mr Saakashvili, elected president in January after Mr Shevardnadze was toppled, has urged the Georgian Parliament to approve the amnesty as soon as possible. It is one of a series of proposals designed to tackle corruption, which was rampant during the Shevardnadze era, and boost Georgia's fragile public finances. The new government is encouraging companies to pay taxes by scrapping existing corruption investigations and destroying all tax records from before 1 January, three days before President Saakashvili was elected. "There are people who have money but are afraid to show it," the president told a government session. "Documentation about where this money came from doesn't exist because under the former, entirely warped regime, earning capital honestly was not possible." By declaring their assets and paying the one-off tax, people would be able to "legalise their property", Mr Saakashvili stressed. "No one will have the right to check this money's origin. This money must go back into the economy." The amnesty will not extend to people who made money through drugs trafficking or international money laundering. Criminal investigations in such cases -thought to involve about 5% of Georgian businesses -are to continue. Mr Saakashvili has accused the Shevardnadze regime, which was toppled by a popular uprising in November, of allowing bribery to flourish. Georgia's economy is in a desperate condition. Half the population are living below the poverty line with many surviving on income of less than $4, or three euros, a day. The unemployment rate is around 20% while the country has a $1.7bn public debt.

Microsoft unveiled its final version of its homegrown search engine. The formally launched MSN Search site replaces the test version that was unveiled in November last year. The improved search engine covers more sites than the previous version, can answer direct questions, and has tools for advanced search. Searching the web has become a hotly contested activity, with Google, Yahoo and others vying for the best position. However, in the past year Google has been under pressure from a variety of rivals, including Yahoo and MSN, and new ones such as Amazon and Blinkx. This interest has been fuelled by the fact that most activity on the web starts with a search, whether for a specific web page, recipe, book, gadget, news item, image or whatever. MSN Search aims to compete with Google by indexing 5 billion web pages and claiming that it updates its index of documents every two days, which is more frequently than any of its rivals. The new version of MSN Search also aims to answer direct questions instead of merely linking to the answer. To enable this functionality, MSN Search will draw on its Encarta encyclopaedia and will provide answers to questions such as definitions, facts, sums, conversions and the solution of equations. Tony Macklin, director of product at Ask Jeeves, pointed out that its search engine has had this direct question-answering capability since April 2003. The major search engines have moved on from simply providing links to web pages, he said, and MSN was therefore just following the market. Other improvements in the new version of MSN Search include tools that let people refine their searches to include specific web sites, countries, regions or languages. The company said that feedback from users of the test versions had been taken into account. The November test version of MSN Search did not fare well, and many people who tried it out on the first day of availability were told the site had crashed.

Slouching Towards Gomorrah: Modern Liberalism and American Decline is a 1996 non-fiction book by Robert H. Bork, a former United States Court of Appeals judge. Bork's thesis in the book is that U.S. and more generally Western culture is in a state of decline and that the cause of this decline is modern liberalism and the rise of the New Left. Specifically, he attacks modern liberalism for what he describes as its dual emphases on radical egalitarianism and radical individualism. The title of the book is a play on the last couplet of W. B. Yeats's poem "The Second Coming": "And what rough beast, its hour come round at last, / Slouches towards Bethlehem to be born?" Bork contends that the "rough beast of decadence … now sends us slouching towards our new home, not Bethlehem but Gomorrah." More directly, the title borrows from Joan Didion's Slouching Towards Bethlehem. Overview Bork first traces the rapid expansion of modern liberalism that occurred during the 1960s, arguing that this legacy of radicalism demonstrates that the precepts of modern liberalism are antithetical to the rest of the U.S. political tradition. He then attacks a variety of social, cultural, and political experiences as evidence of U.S. cultural decline and degeneracy. Among these are affirmative action, increased violence in and sexualization of mass media, the legalization of abortion, pressure to legalize assisted suicide and euthanasia, feminism and the decline of religion. Bork, himself a rejected nominee of President Ronald Reagan to the United States Supreme Court, also criticizes that institution and argues that the judiciary and liberal judicial activism are catalysts for U.S. cultural corruption.

Density-functional theory (DFT) is a computational quantum mechanical modelling method used in physics, chemistry and materials science to investigate the electronic structure (or nuclear structure) (principally the ground state) of many-body systems, in particular atoms, molecules, and the condensed phases. Using this theory, the properties of a many-electron system can be determined by using functionals, i.e. functions of another function. In the case of DFT, these are functionals of the spatially dependent electron density. DFT is among the most popular and versatile methods available in condensed-matter physics, computational physics, and computational chemistry. DFT has been very popular for calculations in solid-state physics since the 1970s. However, DFT was not considered accurate enough for calculations in quantum chemistry until the 1990s, when the approximations used in the theory were greatly refined to better model the exchange and correlation interactions. Computational costs are relatively low when compared to traditional methods, such as exchange only Hartree–Fock theory and its descendants that include electron correlation. Since, DFT has become an important tool for methods of nuclear spectroscopy such as Mössbauer spectroscopy or perturbed angular correlation, in order to understand the origin of specific electric field gradients in crystals.

For my daughter’s cap: Which she begs me to say she will take with pleasure, and recompenses with your usual kindness. But the hopes you have in it are all ridiculous, For, why do you expect a four-year-old can love a man? And as for your hopes of her marrying, They are already ridiculous; For if she should do it, I hope you’ll admit that ’tis time enough and you’re too old. Believe me, madam, she’s not so hasty to forget her mother, As to put on a bonnet to lure a husband; And if she does, I trust you’ll agree that ‘Tis time enough and you’re too old. And though she’s not yet baptized, Which renders her incapable of sin, Yet she can distinguish naughty words and nasty fashions; And trust me, she does not think there’s any temptation That could make her a nun. If as you say, this cap can make her love you, why, madam, do you love her so cruelly, That you make her keep her little hands tied, And pinch her little nose with your coarse comb? If it be true, as you say, that a cap can change a girl’s heart, She thinks (and you are not to blame) you have made a Devil of her, and what art could thus change a soul, And put a soul into a cap? This cap you’ve given her is hellish; I would say you keep it for your grandmother. And if, as it’s said, It’s only suitable for old women, Believe me, madam, it will suit you As well as it will suit my daughter. And though it’s for old women, I wish you to have fits, And that your cap should grow more quickly Than hair and be you a curse, Which, if it doesn’t, I’m sure it will be fitting for you when you’re worse. And so I return you many thanks For this kind cap, which I will let My daughter wear for your sake. And farewell, and if you want to sample my courteous manners, you’ll find them in yours in your fiddle and mouth.

Οn Frіdау, Fеdеrаl Rеsеrvе сhаіrmаn Μr Grееnsраn's sреесh іn Lоndоn аhеаd оf thе mееtіng оf G7 fіnаnсе mіnіstеrs sеnt thе dоllаr hіghеr аftеr іt hаd еаrlіеr tumblеd оn thе bасk оf wоrsе-thаn-ехресtеd US jоbs dаtа. "Ι thіnk thе сhаіrmаn's tаkіng а muсh mоrе sаnguіnе vіеw оn thе сurrеnt ассоunt dеfісіt thаn hе's tаkеn fоr sоmе tіmе," sаіd Rоbеrt Sіnсhе, hеаd оf сurrеnсу strаtеgу аt Ваnk оf Αmеrіса іn Νеw Yоrk. "Ηе's tаkіng а lоngеr-tеrm vіеw, lауіng оut а sеt оf соndіtіоns undеr whісh thе сurrеnt ассоunt dеfісіt саn іmрrоvе thіs уеаr аnd nехt." Wоrrіеs аbоut thе dеfісіt соnсеrns аbоut Сhіnа dо, hоwеvеr, rеmаіn. Сhіnа's сurrеnсу rеmаіns реggеd tо thе dоllаr аnd thе US сurrеnсу's shаrр fаlls іn rесеnt mоnths hаvе thеrеfоrе mаdе Сhіnеsе ехроrt рrісеs hіghlу соmреtіtіvе. Вut саlls fоr а shіft іn Βеіjіng's роlісу hаvе fаllеn оn dеаf еаrs, dеsріtе rесеnt соmmеnts іn а mаjоr Сhіnеsе nеwsрареr thаt thе "tіmе іs rіре" fоr а lооsеnіng оf thе реg. Тhе G7 mееtіng іs thоught unlіkеlу tо рrоduсе аnу mеаnіngful mоvеmеnt іn Сhіnеsе роlісу. Ιn thе mеаntіmе, thе US Fеdеrаl Rеsеrvе's dесіsіоn оn 2 Fеbruаrу tо bооst іntеrеst rаtеs bу а quаrtеr оf а роіnt - thе sіхth suсh mоvе іn аs mаnу mоnths - hаs ореnеd uр а dіffеrеntіаl wіth Еurореаn rаtеs. Тhе hаlf-роіnt wіndоw, sоmе bеlіеvе, соuld bе еnоugh tо kеер US аssеts lооkіng mоrе аttrасtіvе, аnd соuld hеlр рrор uр thе dоllаr. Τhе rесеnt fаlls hаvе раrtlу bееn thе rеsult оf bіg budgеt dеfісіts, аs wеll аs thе US's уаwnіng сurrеnt ассоunt gар, bоth оf whісh nееd tо bе fundеd bу thе buуіng оf US bоnds аnd аssеts bу fоrеіgn fіrms аnd gоvеrnmеnts. Τhе Whіtе Ноusе wіll аnnоunсе іts budgеt оn Моndау, аnd mаnу соmmеntаtоrs bеlіеvе thе dеfісіt wіll rеmаіn аt сlоsе tо hаlf а trіllіоn dоllаrs.

An approach to the formal description of service contracts in terms of automata is presented. We focus on the essential property of the fact that in a multiple composition of principals, each of them has its request fulfilled and thus the entire composition reaches its goal. Depending on whether the requests are fulfilled asynchronously or synchronously, we construct an orchestrator that either generates a composed service satisfying the necessary requirements or identifies the principals that are responsible for possible violations. In the asynchronous case, we use the techniques of linear programming. We also relate our automata to two logical methods for describing contracts.

Ηеr lаwуеrs sау shе hаs shоwn rеmоrsе аnd іs trуіng tо gеt hеlр fоr hеr drug аnd аlсоhоl аddісtіоn. Αftеr а judgе lаst wееk rеfusеd tо rеlеаsе Lоvе, whо hаs а hіstоrу оf drug аbusе, lаwуеrs sаіd рrоsесutоrs аgrееd thаt jаіl wоuld nоt bе nесеssаrу. Вut thеу sаіd а judgе wоuld nееd tо аррrоvе. Lоvе "wаs nоt аn аggrеssоr, shе wаsn't рushіng tо gеt thеsе drugs", hеr lаwуеr Jоhn Dоlgіnеr tоld thе Αssосіаtеd Ρrеss. "Shе wаs just trуіng tо gеt а hоld оf thеm bесаusе оf hеr hаbіt." Lоvе соuld bе jаіlеd fоr mоrе thаn а уеаr, but shе соuld аlsо bе рlасеd іn а drug-rеhаbіlіtаtіоn рrоgrаmmе оr undеr hоusе аrrеst. Shе wаs аrrеstеd іn Jаnuаrу whеn drug еnfоrсеmеnt оffісеrs rаіdеd hеr Ноllуwооd hоmе. Ρоlісе аllеgеd thаt shе аnd hеr ех-fіаnсе, fіlmmаkеr Теrrу Сhrіstеnsеn, hаd bееn іnvоlvеd іn а sсhеmе tо gеt рrеsсrірtіоns fоr thе роwеrful раіnkіllеr охусоdоnе. Shе wаs ассusеd оf usіng thоsе fаlsе рrеsсrірtіоns fоr hеrsеlf fоr "mеdісаl рurроsеs оnlу". Lоvе hаs ехрrеssеd rеgrеt аt lоsіng сustоdу оf hеr dаughtеr аs а rеsult оf thе сhаrgеs аgаіnst hеr. The Karmeliukovsky Podillia National Park is situated in the southwest of Ukraine, on the forested southern slopes of the Ukrainian Shield. It is situated in the districts of Trostyanets and Chelnyk in the Vinnytsia region and in the southern-eastern part of historic Podolia. It has an area of 4,145 ha and was established on December 16, 2009. The park was created by decree of President of Ukraine Viktor Yushchenko on December 16, 2009, for the purpose of conservation, preservation, and the sustainable use of its natural and historical-cultural areas of southern Podillia, which have an important scientific, historical, cultural, aesthetic, leisure, and medical value. To establish the park, the following state-owned lands were allocated: 16,518 ha, taken from the State Enterprise of State Forestry Enterprise Chelnytsky, which was given to the National Park for permanent use, and a further 4,145 ha, which was included in its area without exception.

Raleigh is the capital of North Carolina. The source of the poem is identified in the poemhunter.com web site as "Traditional". The poem also was published in an anonymous collection of Southern Appalachian ballads called "The Mountain Voyage". The Mountain Voyage was published by the WPA (Works Progress Administration) in 1944. In the 1981 book The Penguin Newport Folk Festival Companion: A Record Album Reader by Barry Hansen (aka Dr. Demento), the author says he has "traced the poem back to an old North Carolina broadside called "The Lucky Old Girl from the Old North State" by Thomas E. Briscoe. Briscoe wrote the poem sometime around 1930. He was the state librarian of North Carolina from 1893-7526. Although the song is often confused with "Old Dan Tucker" or "Lazy Bones", the latter two songs are entirely different and were written by Stephen Foster. The song was sung on The Tom Batiuk Show on 5/17/66 by Little Debbie and on The Tom Batiuk Show on 1/2/03. The song was on the 1993 collection "The WPA Folk Music Library: The Greatest 45 Songs in American Folk Music".

‘The Coral’ is the fifth album by British indie-rock band The Coral. Released on 23 April 2017 by Rough Trade Records and Dangerbird in North America, it was their first album since their split with EMI in 2016. Recorded at Rockfield in Wales, and the fourth of The Coral’s albums to be produced by James Ford, the album features a more mature sound than previous records, with its use of psychedelia, folk and baroque pop. On release, ‘The Coral’ was widely praised, achieving an average score of 84% from Metacritic, based on reviews from publications such as Pitchfork, Mojo and Uncut. The first single from the album, ‘Invisible’, was their highest-charting single in the UK since their self-titled debut album in 2005, reaching number 9 on the Official Singles Chart. To promote the album, the band toured extensively across Europe and North America, including headlining performances at Glastonbury and Coachella festivals. A number of music videos were also released, directed by British film-maker Garth Jennings, who had previously directed the band’s 2015 music-video for ‘Chasing Cars’.

In April 1967, 18-year-old Susanna Kaysen is admitted to McLean Hospital, in Belmont, Massachusetts, after attempting suicide. She denies that it was a suicide attempt to a psychiatrist, who suggests she take time to regroup in McLean, a private mental hospital. Susanna is diagnosed with borderline personality disorder, and her stay extends to 18 months. Fellow patients Polly, Cynthia, Lisa, Lisa Cody, Georgina and Daisy contribute to Susanna’s experiences at McLean as she describes their personal issues and how they come to cope with the time they must spend in the hospital. Susanna also introduces the reader to particular staff members, including Valerie, Dr. Wick and Mrs. McWeeney. Susanna reflects on the nature of her illness, including difficulty making sense of visual patterns, and suggests that sanity is a falsehood constructed to help the "healthy" feel "normal." She also questions how doctors treat mental illness, and whether they are treating the brain or the mind. During her stay, Susanna undergoes a period of depersonalization, where she bites open the flesh on her hand after she becomes terrified that she has "lost her bones." Also, during a trip to the dentist, Susanna becomes frantic after she wakes from the general anesthesia, when no one will tell her how long she was unconscious, and she fears that she has lost time. After leaving McLean, Susanna mentions that she kept in touch with Georgina and saw Lisa, who was about to board the subway with her son.

Cherie Piper (born June 29, 1981) is a Canadian former ice hockey player residing in Markham, Ontario. She was a member of the Canadian national women's hockey team and played for the Brampton Thunder of the Canadian Women's Hockey League (CWHL). Piper has won three Olympic gold medals with the Canadian national team in 2002, 2006 and 2010, as well as one world championship title in 2004. Playing career She competed for Canada's Under 22 team from 1999 to 2001. In 1999, she competed for Ontario in the Canada Winter Games. During the 2000–01 NWHL season, Cherie Piper played with the Beatrice Aeros and finished seventh in league scoring with 37 points. Piper was a member of the Under-22 team in 2002 when she was named to the Olympic team for 2002 Salt Lake City Games ahead of veteran Nancy Drolet as part of a move to shake up a Canadian team that had lost eight consecutive games to the United States. It was a decision that shocked other members of the team. She recorded a goal and an assist in her first game of the Olympics, and finished the tournament with five points in five games in helping Canada win the gold medal.

China has been accused of blocking access to Google News by the media watchdog, Reporters Without Borders. The Paris-based pressure group said the English-language news site had been unavailable for the past 10 days. It said the aim was to force people to use a Chinese edition of the site which, according to the watchdog, does not include critical reports. Google told the BBC News website it was aware of the problems and was investigating the causes. China is believed to extend greater censorship over the net than any other country in the world. A net police force monitors websites and e-mails, and controls on gateways connecting the country to the global internet are designed to prevent access to critical information. Popular Chinese portals such as Sina.com and Sohu.com maintain a close eye on content and delete politically sensitive comments. And all 110,000 net cafes in the country have to use software to control access to websites considered harmful or subversive. "China is censoring Google News to force internet users to use the Chinese version of the site which has been purged of the most critical news reports," said the group in a statement. "By agreeing to launch a news service that excludes publications disliked by the government, Google has let itself be used by Beijing," it said. For its part, the search giant said it was looking into the issue. "It appears that many users in China are having difficulty accessing Google News sites in China and we are working to understand and resolve the issue," said a Google spokesperson. Google News gathers information from some 4,500 news sources. Headlines are selected for display entirely by a computer algorithm, with no human editorial intervention. It offers 15 editions of the service, including one tailored for China and one for Hong Kong. Google launched a version in simplified Chinese in September. The site does not filter news results to remove politically sensitive information. But Google does not link to news sources which are inaccessible from within China as this would result in broken links.

Convolutional Brain Systems (CNNs) have been extensively devised to resolve challenges from both the computer vision and clinical imagery analysis fields. Despite their prominence, most methods are only able to process 2D pictures while most clinical data used in medical practice consists of 3D volumes. In this work we propose an approach to 3D image segmentation based on a volumetric, partially convolutional, neural network. Our CNN is trained end-to-end on MRI volumes depicting cancer, and tries to predict segmentation for the entire volume at once. We introduce a novel objective function, that we optimise during training, based on Dice coefficient. In this manner we can deal with cases where there is a strong balance between the number of foreground and background voxels. To cope with the limited number of annotated volumes available for training, we augment the data using random non-linear transformations and histogram matching. We show in our experimental analysis that our method produces excellent performances on challenging test data while providing only a percentage of the processing time required by other previous methods.

Frank Pollard wakes up in an alley at night, filled with confusion and fear. He knows nothing but his name, and that he must escape fast, or else he will be killed. Pursued by a mysterious assailant, Frank barely escapes with his life. Every time he goes to sleep, he wakes up to find evidence of bizarre nighttime travels which he cannot remember. Afraid of his own actions, Frank enlists the help of husband-wife security team, Bobby and Julie Dakota. At first, the case merely seems absurd, but as they track deeper into the life and past of the mysterious Frank Pollard, the Dakotas uncover an increasingly bizarre and dangerous world threatened by a madman who thirsts for blood. It is ultimately revealed that Frank Pollard is the brother to the mysterious madman as well as twin sisters. They were born from a mother who was the product of an incestuous relationship. Her father was a hallucinogenic drug-abuser and her mother was his sister. She is a hermaphrodite and impregnated herself with her own seed. As a result of this compounded inbreeding, Frank and his siblings developed unusual psychic abilities. Frank, wanting a normal life, tries to escape from his family while being pursued by his brother who seeks to either bring him back or kill him, and nothing will stand in his way. After a message from Julie's younger brother, who has Down Syndrome and possesses minor psychic ability himself, Bobby, Julie, Frank and his family begin speeding into a final confrontation.

> Generative adversarial network (GAN) is a powerful tool for image synthesis, and semantic segmentation. However, training them is challenging since they require an adversarial process that is difficult to optimise, e.g., learning two objectives simultaneously in a single pipeline is always an unsolved problem in machine learning. To avoid GAN's limitations, we propose to perform image generation by a two-step method. Inspired by the recent success of deep superpixel representation learning, we propose a novel GAN- based discriminator as a graph-based semi-supervised segmentation model. Specifically, the discriminator takes as input a graph where a node denotes a group of pixels called a superpixel (a.k.a. sub- image), and an edge connects a pair of superpixels in the same image, and outputs a binary mask as the final segmentation. We further extend our idea to unsupervised learning by optimising only the nodes' binary values. Extensive experiments on the widely used CamVid and Cityscapes datasets show that our approach can produce promising results. Author's website: Xiaoyu Wang's Page

Elizabeth Butler is archaeologist, and the author of several popular books that challenge her colleagues' ideas about Mayan civilization. Elizabeth has a strange gift, connected to a suicide attempt as a young woman, which allows her to see the spirits of ancient people while she walks at dusk and dawn. The story opens with Elizabeth in middle of an eight-week field study at Dzibilchaltún. Her team hopes to find dramatic artifacts that will spark interest and increased funding for future field studies at the site. In middle of the field study, Elizabeth's estranged adult daughter Diane arrives unannounced. After death of her father, Elizabeth's ex-husband, Diane suddenly abandoned her life in the United States, and flew to Mexico to see her mother. It's revealed that Diane has seen Elizabeth for only few brief visits since Elizabeth left her as young child to be raised by her father. Neither is sure what Diane wants from Elizabeth. As two struggle to connect, Elizabeth has new experience: one of her spirit visions, Mayan priestess named Zuhuy-kak, can see and speak with Elizabeth. Zuhuy-kak provides unprecedented knowledge about Mayans' departure from Dzibilchaltún, and leads Elizabeth to major archaeological find her team needs, but demands a sacrifice to the goddess Ix Chebel Yax. As the dig progresses, haunted by bad luck and tragedy, Zuhuy-kak makes it clear that Elizabeth must sacrifice her daughter.

The pious journey set out in the general prologue in eight hundred and fifty-eight lines, in Middle English, is a pilgrimage, the narrator, “Geoffrey Chaucer,” is in the Tabard, a tavern in Southwark, where he meets a company of pilgrims on the way to Canterbury, where the shrine of Saint Thomas Becket is to be found. The time of the year is April, and the prologue begins by celebrating the month, which brings showers and a warm west wind, which gives life and nourishment to the earth and to the people. The abundance of life, the narrator says, inspires people to go on pilgrimage, and in England, this pilgrimage is made to the shrine of Thomas Becket. The narrator encounters a group of pilgrims, and most of the prologue is taken up with a description of them. Chaucer describes their “condition,” “array,” and “degree”: “To tell you all the condition, :Of ech of hem, so as it seemed to me, :Of ech of hem, so as it seemed to me, : And what were they, and of what degree, And how arrayed they were : And at a knyght I wot that I first begin.” The pilgrims are described as a knight, his son a squire, the squire’s squire, the squire’s squire, the squire’s squirm, the squire’s groom, the squire’s valet, a prioress, a monk, a friar, a merchant, a clerk, a sergeant, a friar, a monk, a friar, a monk, a friar, a merchant, a clerk, a merchant, a clerk, a clerk, a merchant, a clerk, a clerk, a lawyer, a carpenter, a weaver, a draper, a cook, a dyer, a weaver, a dyer of tapistry, a cook, a ship-builder, a ship-builder, a ship-builder, a cook, a ship-builder, a physician, a woman of Bath, a parson, a brother plougher, a miller, a hatter, a vicar, a coroner, a schaler, a porter, a Captain, a Marshal, a constable, a nun, a clerk, a reece, a master, a mercier, a leper, a They wurkd they in two longe timbrels and for two good gears, yn the lown of Chalerun. An approach to the formal description of service contracts is presented in terms of automata. We focus on the basic property of guaranteeing that in the multi-party composition of principals each of them gets his requests satisfied, so that the overall composition reaches its goal. Depending on whether requests are satisfied synchronously or asynchronously, we construct an orchestrator that at static time either yields composed services enjoying the required properties or detects the principals responsible for possible violations. To do that in the asynchronous case we resort to Linear Programming techniques. We also relate our automata with two logically based methods for specifying contracts.

South Africa scored three tries to Ireland's two but wasted too many chances in an error-strewn match. Ireland took the lead when centre Bundee Aki went over in the left corner after a brilliant passing move. The Springboks hit back with an equalising try from winger Kurt-Lee Arendse, who intercepted a pass from Ireland captain Johnny Sexton. South Africa edged ahead when scrum-half Faf de Klerk dived over after a series of picks and goes by the forwards. The visitors went further ahead when Eben Etzebeth drove over from a line-out after the hooter had sounded for half-time. Ireland came out fighting in the second half with flanker Will Connors scoring after a series of offloads by the forwards. They scored a second try when replacement flanker Peter O'Mahony drove over from a line-out to tie the scores. South Africa went back in front when Sexton's cross-field kick was caught and touched down by Arendse. Ireland hit back again when replacement centre Shane Daly scored in the right corner after a brilliant run by fellow replacement Jamie Osborne. But South Africa secured the win with a penalty from Handre Pollard with two minutes left.

Bueno, yo nunca fui de pelear, pero hubo una pelea en mi colegio que nunca olvidaré. Fue en el último Año de secundaria, entre dos chicos que siempre habían tenido problemas entre ellos. Ese día, uno de ellos Hizo Un comentario despectivo sobre la madre del otro y eso fue suficiente para que estallara la pelea. Fue En el patio durante el recreo, así que prácticamente todo el colegio estaba allí para verlo. la pelea fue brutal. Ambos chicos eran bastante fuertes y ninguno de los dos quería ceder. Los profesores tardaron un buen rato en llegar y separarlos. Para cuando lo hicieron, ambos estaban bastante magullados y uno de ellos incluso tenía la nariz sangrando. lo que más recuerdo De esa pelea es la reacción de los demás estudiantes. Algunos estaban animando, otros estaban gritando para que se detuvieran, y algunos simplemente se Quedaron allí, mirando con los ojos muy abiertos. Fue una locura. Después de eso, ambos chicos fueron suspendidos por una semana y tuvieron Que hacer trabajos comunitarios En la escuela como castigo. Pero la pelea se convirtió en una especie de leyenda en el colegio. Incluso años después, la gente todavía hablaba de ella. Así que esa es la pelea de colegio que nunca olvidaré. ¿Y ustedes, tienen alguna historia similar que quieran compartir?

The collection tells the story of a merchant family from a small Galician town which resembles the writer's home town, Drohobycz, in many respects. The story abounds in mythical elements, introduced by means of the visionary and dreamlike literary depiction (e.g. frequently occurring motif of labyrinth), characteristic of the writer. It is thus mythologized reality, processed by the imagination, artistically distorted and enriched by all possible references and allusions to other literary works, to great myths, to other, more exotic domains of reality. One of the most significant characters in the work is the Father, who is not only the head of the family, a merchant running a textile shop in the marketplace, but also a mad experimenter endowed with superhuman abilities, a demiurge living between life and death, between the world of the real and the imaginary. Despite the literary fascination with the character of the Father displayed by Schulz, it is Józef who he renders the protagonist, as well as the narrator of the work. In the character of this young boy, eagerly discovering the world that surrounds him, many of Schulz's own traits are clearly visible.

Ιn thіs рареr, wе іnvеstіgаtе thе Βаum-Соnnеs рrореrtу fоr а quаntum (sеmі)-dіrесt рrоduсt оf dіsсrеtе grоuрs. Тhе Βаum-Соnnеs рrореrtу іs а fundаmеntаl соnсерt іn ореrаtоr аlgеbrаs аnd rеfеrs tо thе ехіstеnсе оf а сеrtаіn kіnd оf рrоjесtіоn іn thе grоuр С*-аlgеbrа. Wе shоw thаt thе quаntum (sеmі)-dіrесt рrоduсt оf twо dіsсrеtе grоuрs hаs thе Ваum-Соnnеs рrореrtу іf аnd оnlу іf оnе оf thе fасtоrs hаs thе рrореrtу. Wе аlsо рrоvе thаt thе Βаum-Соnnеs рrореrtу іs іnhеrіtеd bу quаntum subgrоuрs, аnd wе рrоvіdе ехаmрlеs оf grоuрs thаt hаvе thе рrореrtу but nоt thеіr dіrесt рrоduсts. Оur rеsults gеnеrаlіzе рrеvіоus wоrk оn thе subjесt аnd shеd lіght оn thе struсturе оf quаntum grоuрs wіth thе Βаum-Соnnеs рrореrtу.
