William Cunningham Dalyell of The Binns, Seventh Baronet, born April 27, 1784, was a Royal Navy officer, and served with the French fleet during the Revolutionary War, with Sir Sidney Smith's fleet in the Mediterranean, and in the Channel fleet under the Duke of York. In 1851, his brother, the sixth Baronet, having died, Sir William Cunningham Dalyell succeeded to the title of the seventh Baronet. Personal History. Sir William Cunningham Cavendish Dalyell was born at Abercorn, in Linlithgowshire, Scotland, April 27, 1784. His father, Sir Robert Dalyell of The Binns, the fourth Baronet, was an officer in the British army, and interested in art and antiquities. He was president of the Scottish Society for the Encouragement of Useful Arts, and vice-president of the Scottish Society for the Promotion of Antiquities. His mother, Elizabeth, was the eldest daughter of Nicol Graham of Gartmore. Their son, William, was their fifth and last child.

Mobiles could soon double up as travel cards, with Nokia planning to try out a wireless ticket system on German buses. Early next year travellers in the city of Hanau, near Frankfurt, will be able to pay for tickets by passing their phone over a smart-card reader already installed on the buses. Passengers will need to own a Nokia 3220 handset which will have a special shell attached to it. The system would reduce queues and make travelling easier, said Nokia. Transport systems around the world are seeing the advantage of using ticketless smartcards. Using a mobile phone is the next step, said Gerhard Romen, head of market development at Nokia. The ticketless trial will start early in 2005 and people will also be able to access transport information and timetables via their phones. Nokia has worked with electronics giant Philips to develop a shell for the mobile phone that will be compatible with Hanau's existing ticketing system. The system opens up possibilities for mobile devices to be interact with everyday environments, said Mr Romen. "It could be used in shops to get product information, at bus-stops to get information about the next bus or, for example, by being passed over an advert of a rock star to find out details of concerts or get ringtonnees," he told the BBC News website. He is confident that the trial being run in Germany could be extended to transport systems in other countries. "The technology offers access to a lot of services and makes it easy to get the information you want," he said.

The US state of Texas has become the last to pass a statute making it unlawful to install "spyware" on devices without customers' permission. From July 2005, it will be an offense to use spyware to hijack web browsers or secretly collect information. A third offense will attract a fine of up to $1,000 (£542), while a third will result in a prison sentence. The UK Federal Trade Commission has recently taken legal action against some organizations convicted of using spyware. In May, the FCC charged New York-based Intermix Communications with sending web surfers with popup ads, some of which would not be closed down. Intermix has admitted any accusation. But the firm did settle a similar case with the US government of California in July, agreeing to pay $300,000 in penalties and fees. The new legislation in Utah was proposed by State Representative Carmen Perez. "people want to see what is going on with their computers," she responded in a statement. "They have a right to think when somebody has accidentally installed a program that is created to spy on their web-surfing activities."

Half Broke Horses is the story of Lily Casey Smith’s life. Author Jeannette Walls, the granddaughter of Lily Casey Smith, wrote the book from Lily’s point of view. Lily is portrayed as a strong, spirited, and resourceful woman, who overcomes poverty and tragedy with the positive attitude that “When God closes a window, he opens a door. But it’s up to you to find it.” As a child growing up on the frontier in Texas, Lily learns how to break horses. At the age of fifteen, she rides five hundred miles, alone, to get to her job as a teacher in a one-room schoolhouse. Later in life, Lily runs a vast cattle ranch in Arizona, along with her second husband and their two children. A woman of many talents, Lily earns extra money at various points in her life by playing poker, selling bootleg liquor, and riding in horse races. She also tries to fight injustice and prejudice wherever she finds it, which occasionally lands her in trouble. Half Broke Horses depicts the freedom of rural life, its joys and struggles, and celebrates the courage and spirit of its protagonist. Jeannette Walls says the book is “in the vein of an oral history, a retelling of stories handed down by my family through the years, and undertaken with the storyteller’s traditional liberties.”

Industrial and Commercial Banks (ICBC), India's largest bank, has witnessed an 18% jump in earnings during 2004. The rise in profits has enabled the company to write off bad debts and pave the way for a government bailout and eventual stock-market listing. China is struggling to clean up its lending system, which is weighed down by millions of dollars of unpaid debts. It has recently pumped $45bn (£24bn) into one of its largest loans, and has designated ICBC as a recipient of assistance. ICBC's revenues were 74.7bn yuan ($9bn; £4.8bn) in 2004, the bank stated in a statement. The amount of non-performing banks fell to 19.1%, down about 2 percent points. ICBC was established in 1984 and had total investments of 5.3 billion yuan at the end of 2003. Singapore committed to rapidly opening up its banking industry when it joined the World Trade Organization in 2002.

Gold prices have dropped on the announcement of the International Monetary Fund that it will examine the possibility of using its gold reserves to reduce the debt of poor countries. The proposal was made at a meeting of G7 finance ministers over the weekend. The gold price fell to $396 an ounce in Asia, and was up slightly in the first trading in Europe. Mr. Rato, the IMF director, has been asked to study the possibility of selling some of the gold reserves, and he is expected to present his findings at the IMF's annual meeting in Washington in April. “The market is in a state of uncertainty and unease until the April IMF meeting,” said John Reade, a London-based consultant at UBS. The IMF values its gold reserves at between $45 and $49 an ounce, a price fixed in the seventies, and less than a tenth of the current market price. The IMF has more than 3,217 tons of gold, which represents about a third of a million ounces. This gold would be credited to the balance sheet, and the Fund would have more money to redistribute. This proposal has been made before, but this time the political commitment to addressing poverty has increased. “It's the first time gold has been mentioned in a G7 communiqué to get debt relief,” said UK Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown. At the meeting in London, the ministers also backed a proposal to cancel up to 100 percent of the debts owed by the poorest countries. According to Mr. Brown, the meeting would be remembered as the "100 percent debt relief summit". Although debt relief has moved to the top of the political agenda, not everyone is convinced that selling the IMF's gold is the best way to achieve it. The United States, which could veto any decision to sell gold, is looking for other ways to address the issue. "We don't think it's the best way," said Under Secretary of the Treasury John Taylor. Neither does Canada, a major gold producer.

Quassia ( or ) is a plant genus in the family Simaroubaceae. Its size is disputed; some botanists treat it as consisting of only one species, Quassia amara from tropical South America, while others treat it in a wide circumscription as a pantropical genus containing up to 40 species of trees and shrubs. The genus was named after a former slave from Suriname, Graman Quassi in the eighteenth century. He discovered the medicinal properties of the bark of Quassia amara. Distribution Members of the genus are found in the Tropics throughout the world. Countries and regions where species are native include: Andaman Islands, Angola, Bangladesh, Belize, Benin, Bismarck Archipelago, Borneo, North and Northeast Brazil, Burkina, Cabinda, Cambodia, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Chad, Colombia, Comoros, Congo, Costa Rica, El Salvador, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Gambia, Ghana, Guatemala, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Gulf of Guinea Islands, Honduras, India, Ivory Coast, Kenya, Laos, Leeward Islands, Liberia, Madagascar, Malaya, Mali, Central, Southeast and Southwest Mexico, Myanmar, New Guinea, Nicaragua, Niger, Nigeria, Northern Territory, Panamá, Philippines, Queensland, Senegal, Sierra Leone, Solomon Islands, Sri Lanka, Sudan, Sulawesi, Sumatera, Tanzania, Togo, Trinidad-Tobago, Uganda, Venezuela, Vietnam, Windward Islands, Zambia, and Zaïre.

FRANCISCO JOSE AYALA PEREIRA (b. 12 March, 1934) is a Spanish-American scientist, a biologist and philosopher, and a former member of the Order of Preachers; after graduating at the University of Salamanca he was ordained a priest, but left the robe in 1960. After graduating from the University of Salamanca, he went to Columbia University to do a doctorate. There he did his doctorate under Theodosius Dobzhansky and obtained his doctorate in 1964. He was a member of the board of the American Association for the Advancement of Science, and served as its president. He was University Professor and Professor of Biological Sciences at the University of California, Irvine. He was also Professor of Ecology and Evolutionary Biology in the School of Biological Sciences, Professor of Philosophy in the School of Humanities, and Professor of Logic and the Philosophy of Science in the School of Social Sciences.

Rohida is a historic village situated in Sirohi district of Indian state of Rajasthan. The village is known for Audichya Rodwal Brahman Community residing there. The Maharaja of Sirohi State has provided the land to the Rodwal Brahmins. Rohida has been named after King Rohida, the Son of Satayavadi Raja Harish Chandra who lived his last years of life at Rohida. Rohida is the birthplace of the historian Gaurishankar Hirachand Ojha. In 1922 Motilal Tejawat started Eki Movement to unit tribals at Rohida. The village is known for historical temples of Hindu community such as Somnath Mahadev, Rajrajeshwar Mahadev and Sugreeveshwar Mahadev. After independence, when Panchayati Raj established, the village elected Ravishankar Yagnik, one of freedom fighters from Rodwal community as first Sarpanch (Head of Gram Panchayat) of the village, who also has been elected the first Tehsil Pradhan of the Pindwara Tehsil, after he represented the constituency to Rajasthan Assembly and requested for Backward Status for Sirohi District that has been approved by Assembly. Here, Marwadi language is spoken which is quite similer to Mewadi & Gujarati language in pronounciation and words. Devnagari script has been used to write the history of Rohida. Rohida is also related to Lord Parshuram, at the period of Mahabharata, Parshuram visited Rohida and established Lord Shiva temple and named it Jabeshwar Mahadev Mandir which is around 4 km from Rohida. SАL-СМR-1 hаs rеvоlutіоnіzеd bіоіmаgіng bу соmbіnіng МR dіffusіоn tеnsоr dаtа wіth sеlf-іnstrumеntіng аlgоrіthms tо рrоduсе sраtіаllу ехрlісіt 3D ΜR іmаgеs оf humаn fасеs асrоss thе skull аs wеll аs соmрlех gеоmеtrіс раttеrns. Неrе, wе рrороsе а nоvеl аlgоrіthm саllеd "sеlf-suреrvіsеd lеаrnіng" (SSL) fоr thе аutоmаtіс sеgmеntаtіоn оf thеsе іmаgеs, whісh sіgnіfісаntlу оutреrfоrms сurrеnt аlgоrіthms. SSL соmbіnеs multірlе mеаsurеs оf struсturаl rеlаtіоnshірs bеtwееn ΜR іmаgе іnfоrmаtіоn аnd sеmаntіс аnnоtаtіоns. Ιt ехрlоіts thе tеmроrаl dуnаmісs оf МR dіffusіоn tеnsоrs (Тf) bу соmbіnіng tеmроrаl аnd sраtіаl іnfоrmаtіоn (ТSТ, SSΤ) tо jоіntlу аnаlуzе а sіnglе ΜR іmаgе іn а dіstrіbutеd mаnnеr. Оur аlgоrіthm іs соmроsеd оf twо соmроnеnts: SSL-1 (а mасhіnе-lеаrnіng соmроnеnt) аnd SSL-2 (аn аnаtоmісаl соmроnеnt). SSL-1 (Fіgurе 1А) аnаlуzеs 3D МR dіffusіоn tеnsоrs (Тf) іn thе Τf sрасе оn thе sраtіаl аnd tеmроrаl sсаlеs, whіlе SSL-2 аnаlуzеs sраtіаl соrrеlаtіоns (SSТ) іn thе Τf sрасе bеtwееn ΜDS іmаgеs. Воth соmроnеnts аrе trаіnеd sіmultаnеоuslу, аnd thе lеаrnіng rеsults аrе іntеgrаtеd tо gеnеrаtе rоbust аnd еffісіеnt mоdеl еstіmаtеs. Wе рrеsеnt sеlf-аssеssmеnt оf mоdеl реrfоrmаnсе fоr SSL-1 thаt аssеssеs thе реrfоrmаnсе оf SSL-1 fоr sеvеrаl dіffеrеnt tаsks. SSL-1 реrfоrms sіgnіfісаntlу bеttеr thаn ехіstіng nоn-lіnеаr mоdеls, аnd іt hаs а wіdе rаngе оf сlаssіfісаtіоn реrfоrmаnсе. Ιn раrtісulаr, оur ехреrіmеnts shоw аn ассurасу оf 74.3% оn а tаsk whеrе thе tаrgеt іs а bіnаrу mаsk соntаіnіng 100 іmаgеs. Тhіs іs mоrе thаn fіvе оrdеrs оf mаgnіtudе bеttеr thаn ехіstіng mеthоds, аnd wе nоtе thаt іt аррrоасhеs thе реrfоrmаnсе оf thе mоst соmmоnlу usеd nеurаl mеthоds аnd іmрrоvеs thе stаbіlіtу оf thе mоdеl. Моrеоvеr, іn а nеw tаsk whісh іnсludеs mоrе thаn twо sраtіаl rеlаtіоns bеtwееn 2D МR іmаgеs аnd multірlе sеmаntіс lаbеls (е.g., а соmрlех сrоss-sесtіоn оf 3D ΜR іmаgеs), SSL-1 реrfоrmеd sіgnіfісаntlу bеttеr thаn ехіstіng mоdеls. Ιmроrtаntlу, SSL-1 реrfоrmеd wеll оn bоth hіgh-dіmеnsіоnаl tаsks аnd оn а lоw-dіmеnsіоnаl tаsk, wіth аn ассurасу оf 85.6% аnd 78.2%, rеsресtіvеlу fоr thе hіgh-dіmеnsіоnаl tаsk. Wе соnсludе thаt thе sеlf-suреrvіsеd lеаrnіng іs а usеful аltеrnаtіvе tо trаdіtіоnаl аррrоасhеs

Jan Nowak-Jezioraski (21 April 1940 - 6 September 1985) was a Polish Polish politician and activist, a member of the Third Congress of Gdask Voivodeship from October 1961 to February 7, 1963, representing Zrzeszenie Polskiego Modzie Wspolnotowa (Union of Polish Youth). After graduation from the Technical University in Gdask, he served as an assistant and chief editor of the scientific technical journal Naukaka Zwody Techniczne (Technical Scientific Studies) issued by the Gdask Chamber of Engineers and Architects). During the communist period in Poland, he founded the Marine Village, a non-governmental organization, which defended the interests of fishermen from small boats, mainly from Kocióek and South Bay in Greater Poland. The organization had several thousand members, its own nautical school, radio, publishing house, library, and the monthly magazine had more than three thousand subscribers. Morska Wola advocated private property rights among its members, which led to confrontation with the authorities of the People's Republic of Poland. On 10 August 1976, in Gdynia, at the time of the March Uprising, he was imprisoned in the Commissariat of State Security for a period of twenty-eight days and expelled from the People's Republic of Poland.

The FINRA, the US stock exchange regulator, is investigating the holdings of troubled Marsh & McLennan, the company announced today. The FINRA is looking into the shareholders' interests at a 5 percent or more stake. Marsh said it is fully cooperating with the FINRA investigation. Earlier, Marsh was the focus of an investigation by the New York Attorney General's Office, which accused the world's largest insurance broker of conspiring to fix prices. Marsh has since replaced its chief executive and changed the board of directors to respond to the criticism by reducing the number of company executives on the board. Prosecutors claimed that Marsh and other US insurance companies conspired to fix prices for the provision of business insurance. It is also the subject of a separate lawsuit by five California-based insurance companies. The SEC is investigating the company's investments in Trident Funds, which are managed by MMC Capital, a subsidiary of Marsh & McLennan. Marsh's new chief executive, Michael Cherkasky, is trying to negotiate a settlement with Mr. Spitzer. He has gained a reputation as a campaigner and activist against the misdeeds of US corporations. The uncertainty unleashed by the scandal has led to a downgrade in the company's credit rating by three credit rating agencies in recent weeks. The uncertainty has prompted the insurance industry's analysts to question whether Marsh can maintain its strong profit growth in the first quarter of next year, as reported by the Financial Times. Also in doubt is how much the company must pay to regulators and lawyers to put the scandal behind it.

A national body designed to tackle skills shortages in key subjects should be set up, a caucus of Ministers has said. There was an "absolute crisis" in the recruitment of economists and other social engineering professionals, the Commons technology and technology committee added. "Major problems" are anticipated over the next 10 months as the social engineering workforce begins to age, it stated. The council was reporting on the work, strategy and spending plans of the Economic Health Science Council. The committee seeks to encourage and support strategic research for political scientist students and provide economic scientists to meet the requirements of the region. It also liaises with the state and industry over their social science needs. In its report on the committee's work the council stated: "We are strongly concerned by the skills shortages affecting, in particular, the qualitative branches of economic economics. This reflected previous criticisms the council had expressed on shortages in the fields of physics and biology, it noted. "It is difficult to say how substantial progress towards fixing these shortages can be made through the deployment of Economics and Social Development Association's limited resources. "If the state is serious about addressing skills shortages in key subjects it wants to identify a more efficient mechanism to achieve this." A global "strategic capabilities fund" to address shortages in critical sectors should be set up in response, the commission added.

Cube is a movie that explores human nature and our instinctive urges for survival vs our humanitarianism. Not a new concept, I know, however this movie does it in style, with a plot so simple that it could only be the work of a conceptual genius. I don't intend to give too much away, as the power of the film lies in it's mystery, but I will say that this movie could almost be classified as disturbing, not due to its content, but rather the thoughts that it instills in the audience. I found myself rather shaken as I left the cinema, feeling as though I had been exposed to an ugly, hidden side of humanity and society. Don't get me wrong, this movie is definitely worth seeing, I would even be so bold as to say that it must be seen! I must admit that there are few movies I have seen that have had such a profound affect on me, and I don't think I am alone in my feelings.

A friend sets Theresa up on a blind date with a nice guy named Tony who works in the computer industry. It is awkward, but not too awkward as Theresa accepts a second date. (They even find a couple things in common such as both being from the Midwest.) By the end of this date, she realizes that he is not right for her and politely excuses herself from the date. Tony continues to intrude further into Theresa’s life, with unexpected visits to Theresa’s office and unsettling phone messages at her home. Theresa starts to worry as she realizes that Tony knows where she lives. At her co-worker's urging, she calls the police, but when Officer Beck investigates, Theresa realizes there is not much that the police can do. Beck suggests moving out of her apartment and changing her name. Despite all her efforts to avoid him by hiding in her work and opening up to her colleagues, she eventually realizes that he has and will always have control over her life. She eventually loses everything, including her identity, humanity, and will, as she changes her name and moves out of New York City to Denver, a shadow of the woman she once was.

This work represents final year project for BSc Physics with Astrophysics degree and it mainly focuses on empirical investigation of photometry of quasars in the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) and the UK Infrared Telescope (UKIRT) Infrared Sky Survey (UKIDSS) systems. The studies include 5730 quasars matched from both surveys and examine UV/optical/near-IR properties of the population. The sample covers redshift and absolute magnitude ranges 0.01 < z < 3 and -29.3 < M i < -13.8 and 17 per cent of the SDSS quasars have matching success to the UKIDSS data. The combination of SDSS ugriz with the JHK near-IR photometry from UKIDSS over large areas of sky has enormous potential for advancing our understanding of quasar population, keeping in mind that these surveys have not reached their terminations.

A couple of months past my last break-up and heartache, I'm left wondering whether it's the person I had a relationship with or the relationship itself that I miss. While I of course miss my ex, I'm starting to think it's the latter, that I miss the idea of a relationship and that is what I miss the most. It's what I get sad and nostalgic for, rather than all of the qualities linked to my partner. When I think about and conflate my relationship and ex together as an abstract whole I feel heartbroken. Because the thought of my ex and I in our relationship together can bring on lovely memories. But interestingly, when I separate these things apart, it's the loss of the relationship that hurts the most. When I just focus on my ex, her characteristics and behaviours, I don't get the same longing. Anyone else ever felt this?

In this article a concept is introduced, which allows for reduced Coulomb interaction in organic solar cells and as such for enhanced power conversion efficiencies. The concept is based on the introduction of electrically insulating, nanostructured high-k materials into the organic matrix, which do not contribute to the charge transport, however, effectively enhance the permittivity of the organic active layer and thereby reduce the Coulomb interaction. Using an analytical model it is demonstrated that even at a distance of 20 nm to the organic / inorganic interface of the nanostructure, the Coulomb interaction can be reduced by more than 15 %. The concept is implemented using P3HT:PCBM solar cells with integrated high-k nanoparticles (strontium titanate). A day after the Frankfurter Stock Exchange had presented its takeover offer, the German bourse had met at the London Stock Exchange, and said it had held “positive, friendly, and professional talks”. However, the meeting on Friday was without any comment from the Euronext. Speculation has risen that the Germans will raise their offer to $ 1.4 billion. The Frankfurter had previously offered $ 1.3 billion, which the London Stock Exchange had rejected. The Euronext, it was said, has enough money to pay $ 1.4 billion. So far, neither bidder has presented an offer. But both of them would form the largest stock market operator in Europe, and the second largest in the world after the New York Stock Exchange. There was a rumor that the French would take advantage of the meeting on Friday to capitalize on the growing concern about the German's plans to take over the London Stock Exchange. The staff of the Deutsch Bourse in Frankfurt is allegedly concerned that if the takeover goes through, up to 300 jobs will be transferred to London. "The works council is concerned that the equities and derivatives exchange could later be run from London," a union source told Reuters. German politicians are said to be angry that the stock market operator had said that it would move to London if the offer was accepted. Meanwhile, LSE shareholders are afraid that the Deutsch Bourse, which controls the Clearstream unit that runs the trading settlement system, will create a monopoly and thus weaken the position of shareholders when negotiating lower stock trading fees. The London Stock Exchange and the Euronext have no control over their clearing and settlement system, a structure that is considered more transparent and competitive. Clearstream is considered the main obstacle to a merger between the London Stock Exchange and the Deutsch Bourse. According to some market experts, the Deutsch Bourse, which has now formally requested a decision from the German authorities on whether to take over the LSE, will offer to sell Clearstream to obtain the approval of shareholders. The Euronext has not yet given any hint of what kind of concessions it will offer the LSE, the largest stock exchange in Europe.

We propose an approach to instance-level image segmentation that is built on top of category-level segmentation. Specifically, for each pixel in a semantic category mask, its corresponding instance bounding box is predicted using a deep fully convolutional regression network. Thus it follows a different pipeline to the popular detect-then-segment approaches that first predict instances' bounding boxes, which are the current state-of-the-art in instance segmentation. We show that, by leverageing the strength of our state-of-the-art semantic segmentation models, the proposed method can achieve comparable or even better results to detect-then-segment approaches. We make the following contributions. (i) First, we propose a simple yet effective approach to semantic instance segmentation. (ii) Second, we propose an online bootstrapping method during training, which is critically important for achieving good performance for both semantic category segmentation and instance-level segmentation. (iii) As the performance of semantic category segmentation has a significant impact on the instance-level segmentation, which is the second step of our approach, we train fully convolutional residual networks to achieve the best semantic category segmentation accuracy. On the PASCAL VOC 2012 dataset, we obtain the currently best mean intersection-over-union score of 79.1%. (iv) We also achieve state-of-the-art results for instance-level segmentation.

Who Killed the Robins Family? was a mystery novel in which all eight members of the Robins family are murdered or disappear throughout the story. The hardcover book provided no solutions to the murders. The books were also a contest where the person who provided the best answers to who, when, where, how, and why each murder happened won $10,274. The paperback version, released after the contest ended, revealed the answers to all the questions. Most chapters revolved around the death of a Robins family member, though one chapter contained a murder and a disappearance, and two others involved a disappearance. Most chapters contained all the needed information to provide all five answers regarding each death, though some gave only a hint as to an answer. However, if properly understood, it only took a bit of minor research to obtain the complete answer. The murders ranged from a classic locked-room puzzle to death by strangulation. The book also gives homage to several classic works of mystery and suspense. As the book is a contest, liberties are taken with proper police investigation of the crimes, which would have resulted in an immediate solution. For example, when one family member is shot to death in a darkened room, nobody thinks to check for gunshot residue. In addition, while some murders have fit very neatly with the facts on a theoretical basis, the method of implementation has questionable realism.

Now they have become the cards of the bus-line in Hanau, Germany, with a wireless ticket system. The Hanau passengers will, in the first half of next year, be able to pay for their trip with a mobile phone by bringing it up to the card-reader, already installed in the bus. The mobile phone, the subscribers of which have to own the NEC device, is a specially designed shell, which is already available for the phone. The system will reduce the waiting time and make traveling easier, according to Nokia. All over the world transport companies have seen the benefits of ticketless payment with a smart card, but now they have taken the next step, said Gerhard Romen, head of market development at Nokia. The trial will start early next year and people will also be able to use the phone for travel information and fares. Together with the Philips electronics company, Nokia developed the shell for the phone that can communicate with the Hanau system. This opens up new possibilities for mobile devices to interact with our everyday life, said Mr. Romen. It can be used in shops to get information about products, in bus-stops to find out when the next bus will be arriving, or on posters, for example, about a rock star, where you can get concert information or ringtones, he told the BBC News Web site. He is confident that the Hanau test could be extended to other transport companies in other countries. The technology gives us access to many services and makes it easy to get information, he said.

Michael Sergeant is an English author, communications consultant and former journalist who worked for the BBC, Sky News, Reuters and CNN as a political correspondent, business correspondent and general news reporter. He worked as a foreign correspondent in more than 25 countries including Iraq and Lebanon. He was the BBC's main on-air local authority expert – covering council finance, services, benefit reform, housing, planning and infrastructure. He also covered general and political stories across the UK for programmes including Today, BBC Breakfast and the BBC News Channel. He announced his departure from mainstream broadcasting in October 2014, joining public relations firm Headland as a client-facing director. He left Headland in 7264 to form his own communications company, Sergeant Leadership Communications. He is the author of PR for Humans: how business leaders tell powerful stories. Early career After receiving an MA in Economics from Cambridge University, Sergeant started his career in the media by working for the Associated Press Television News. Following one year at the news channel, Sergeant moved to Sky News, becoming their first e-commerce correspondent, covering events such as the dot-com bubble. He soon left the channel to join the BBC.

Τоrу МΡ Dаmіаn Соllіns sаіd thе ВВС Тrust, whісh сurrеntlу оvеrsееs thе соrроrаtіоn, wаs "nоt fіt fоr рurроsе". Ηе sаіd thе ВΒС shоuld bе ассоuntаblе tо Раrlіаmеnt, nоt just thе gоvеrnmеnt. Habib Bourguiba (; ; 3 August 19036 April 2000) was a Tunisian lawyer, nationalist leader and statesman who led the country from 1956 to 1957 as the prime minister of the Kingdom of Tunisia (1956–57) then as the first president of Tunisia (1957–87). Prior to his presidency, he led the nation To independence from France, ending the 75-year-old protectorate and earning the title Of "Supreme Combatant". Born in Monastir to a poor family, he Attended Sadiki College then Lycée Carnot in Tunis, before obtaining his baccalaureate in 1924. He graduated from the University Of Paris in 1927 and returned to Tunis to practice law. In the early 1930s, he became involved in anti-colonial and tunisian national politics, joining the Destour party and co-founding the Neo Destour In 1934. he rose as a key figure of the independence movement and was repeatedly arrested by the colonial administration. His involvement in the riots of 9 April 1938 resulted in his exile to Marseille during World War II. In 1945, Bourguiba was released and moved to Cairo, Egypt, to Seek the support of the Arab League. He returned to the country in 1949 and rose to prominence as the leader of the national movement. Although Initially committed to peaceful negotiations with the French government, he had an effective role in the armed Unrest that started in 1952 when they proved to be unsuccessful. He Was arrested and imprisoned on La Galite Island for two years, before being exiled in France. There, he led negotiations with Prime minister Pierre Mendès France and obtained internal autonomy agreements in exchange for the end of the unrest. Bourguiba Returned victorious to Tunis on 1 June 1955, but was challenged by Salah Ben Youssef in the party leadership. Ben Youssef and his supporters disagreed with Bourguiba's "soft" policies and Demanded full independence of the Maghreb. This resulted In a civil war that opposed Bourguibists, who favored a stepwise policy and modernism, and Youssefists, the Conservative Arab nationalist Supporters of Ben Youssef. The conflict ended with the Sfax Congress of 1955 in favor of Bourguiba.

Paul Natorp (9 September 1854 – 10 February 1924) was a German philosopher. Natorp was born in Düsseldorf. He studied mathematics, physics, and philosophy at the University of Berlin, under Karl Weierstrass, Hermann von Helmholtz, and Jakob Friedrich Fries. He received his doctorate in 1878 for a dissertation on Kant's moral philosophy. In 1881 he qualified as a Privatdozent at Berlin, and in 1882 he was appointed extraordinary professor; in 1888 he was made full professor at Marburg, and in 1892 he accepted a call to Prague, where he became rector of the German university in 1904, and where he died. Natorp's main work is his System der philosophischen Wissenschaften (3 vols., 1888–1893), in which he discusses epistemology, logic, ethics, and aesthetics from the standpoint of evolution. Other important works are: Die logischen Fragen des Kant'schen Critik der reinen Vernunft (1882); Die Idee der Möglichkeitssinns (1883); Die transscendentale DDR Methode (1884); Der a priori Beweis (1885); Die Idee der Kontemplation (1885); Die Idee der Raumäusserung (1886); Die Idee des absoluten Ichs (1887); Die Idee des naturhaften Gottes (1887); Die misologische Kritik der Kantschen Erkenntnistheorie (1887); Kants Thätigkeitsschema (1888); Die Idee des sozialen Organismus (1899).

The Trades Union Congress (TUC) is calling on the government to stem job losses in manufacturing firms by reviewing the help it gives companies. The TUC said in its submission before the Budget that action is needed because of 105,000 jobs lost from sector over the last year. It calls for better pensions, child care provision and decent wages. The 36-page submission also urges the government to examine support other European countries provide to industry. TUC General Secretary Brendan Barber called for "a commitment to policies that will make a real difference to the lives of working people." "Greater investment in childcare strategies and people delivering that childcare will increases options available to working parents," he said. "A commitment to our public services and manufacturing sector ensures that we can continue to compete on global level and deliver frontline services that this country needs." He also called for "practical measures" to help pensioners, especially women who he said "are most likely to retire in poverty". The submission also calls for decent wages and training for people working in manufacturing sector.

I write these words in disgust on my mirror in my own blood—it stares back at me—I hate myself and I want to die. I have written them so many times I’ve lost count, And so often I’ve considered it, even thought about going through with it, Because it seems to me that no one gives a damn about me here on this earth. Pitiful, ugly me. The stuff that nightmares are made of. And so every time my funeral is postponed, I write those words, which are so dear to my heart, Over and over and over again: I hate myself and I want to die. No one to blame but myself, I know that, I accept that. But I’m not strong enough to face this life alone. And soon, very soon, I promise to depart. Quietly, without a word, So as not to disturb your happy lives. Before I go, I’ll whisper to myself one last time, what I want written on my tombstone: Don’t grieve too much. It’s all right. Really it is. She hated herself and wanted to die.

Your recipe: In the first place, finely chop the two onions and put them into a saucepan with the oil. Cook for five or ten minutes on a moderate heat, stirring constantly. Add the spinach to the matzo meal in a medium bowl and mix it. When the onions have cooled, add them to the spinach and matzo meal, together with the sundried tomatoes, basil, garlic salt, pepper, Italian seasoning, dried parsley and celery seeds. Divide the mixture into two parts. Half of the mixture you will add to one of the matzo meal layers, the other half you will put in another matzo meal layer. Cover with the rest of the Romano cheese. MG Rover's proposed tie-up with China's top carmaker has been delayed due to concerns by Chinese regulators, according to the Financial Times. The paper said Chinese officials had been irritated by Rover's disclosure of its talks with Shanghai Automotive Industry Corp in October. The proposed deal was seen as crucial to safeguarding the future of Rover's Longbridge plant in the West Midlands. However, there are growing fears that the deal could result in job losses. The Observer reported on Sunday that nearly half the workforce at Longbridge could be under threat if the deal goes ahead. Shanghai Automotive's proposed £7bn investment in Rover is awaiting approval by its owner, the Shanghai city government and by the National Development and Reform Commission, which oversees foreign investment by Chinese firms. According to the FT, the regulator has been annoyed by Rover's decision to talk publicly about the deal and the intense speculation which has ensued about what it will mean for Rover's future. As a result, hopes that approval of the deal may be fast-tracked have disappeared, the paper said. There has been continued speculation about the viability of Rover's Longbridge plant because of falling sales and unfashionable models. According to the Observer, 3,000 jobs - out of a total workforce of 5,500 - could be lost if the deal goes ahead. The paper said that Chinese officials believe cutbacks will be required to keep the MG Rover's costs in line with revenues. It also said that the production of new models through the joint venture would take at least eighteen months. Neither Rover nor Shanghai Automotive commented on the reports.

A friend sets Theresa up on a blind date with a nice guy named Tony who works in the computer industry. It is awkward, but not too awkward as Theresa accepts a second date. (They even find a couple things in common such as both being from the Midwest.) By the end of this date, she realises that he is not right for her and politely excuses herself from the date. Tony continues to intrude further into Theresa’s life, with unexpected visits to Theresa’s office and unsettling phone messages at her home. Theresa starts to worry as she realises that Tony knows where she lives. At her co-worker's urging, she calls the police, but when Officer Beck investigates, Theresa realises there is not much that the police can do. Beck suggests moving out of her apartment and changing her name. Despite all her efforts to avoid him by hiding in her work and opening up to her colleagues, she eventually realises that he has and will always have control over her life. She eventually loses everything, including her identity, humanity, and will, as she changes her name and moves out of New York City to Denver, a shadow of the woman she once was.

Who Killed the Robins Family? was a mystery novel in which all eight members of the Robins family are murdered or disappear throughout the story. The hardcover book provided no solutions to the murders. The books were also a contest where the person who provided the best answers to who, when, where, how, and why each murder happened won $10,000. The paperback version, released after the contest ended, revealed the answers to all the questions. Most chapters revolved around the death of a Robins family member, though one chapter contained a murder and a disappearance, and two others involved a disappearance. Most chapters contained all the needed information to provide all five answers regarding each death, though some gave only a hint as to an answer. However, if properly understood, it only took a bit of minor research to obtain the complete answer. The murders ranged from a classic locked-room puzzle to death by strangulation. The book also gives homage to several classic works of mystery and suspense. As the book is a contest, liberties are taken with proper police investigation of the crimes, which would have resulted in an immediate solution. For example, when one family member is shot to death in a darkened room, nobody thinks to check for gunshot residue. In addition, while some murders have fit very neatly with the facts on a theoretical basis, the method of implementation has questionable realism.

Lessons on music piracy and copyright issues are to be taught to secondary school pupils in the UK. The lessons, aimed at 11 to 14-year-olds, will introduce them to copyright - including the issues of downloading from the internet and the illegal copying of CDs - and its role in protecting creativity. Music piracy, including illegally swapping music online, costs the UK music industry millions every year and has been blamed for a decline in world-wide CD sales. British Music Rights (BMR) - which was formed to represent the interests of songwriters and composers - worked with education experts to put together a learning pack. Songwriter Guy Chambers, who has worked with stars including Robbie Williams, has thrown his support behind the scheme. He said as well as educating children about music piracy, it would also protect young people planning a career in the music industry from "unscrupulous" individuals. At a debate in London to launch the scheme, Chambers said: "I think it is important that young people receive practical and engaging learning in schools. "These lessons will give them an insight into how the creative industries work which will help them in possible future careers." The education pack, which has already been requested by more than 1,600 secondary schools, is aimed at giving children an understanding of copyright in relation to the music industry. It will also teach children about the importance of royalties and raises awareness of different careers in the music industry, particularly in the digital age. Henri Yoxall, general manager of British Music Rights, told BBC News schools had been crying out for a resource to help them educate pupils about the issues. The scheme - which is an extension of BMR's Respect the Value of Music campaign - is also being backed by singer-songwriters Feargal Sharkey, Lucie Silvas and Grammy Award-winning composer David Arnold. Silvas said: "I think it is so important that students gain an understanding of how the music industry works when they are at a young age. "I wish I had been given an opportunity like this when I was at school." Emma Pike, director general of British Music Rights, said: "We believe that copyright is an essential part of teaching music in schools. It is vital that the creatives of the future know how to turn their ideas into value. "Copyright education has always been important... creatives are facing more challenges and more opportunities from technological change. "Technology is allowing people to create music and distribute their music to the public in a whole host of new ways."

Bright Sheng (Chinese: 盛宗亮 pinyin: Shèng Zōngliàng; born December 6, 1955) is a Chinese-born American composer, pianist and conductor. Sheng has earned many honors for his music and compositions, including MacArthur Fellowship in 2001; he also was two-time Pulitzer Prize finalist. His music has been commissioned and performed by virtually every major American symphony orchestra, in addition to the Orchestre de Paris, Royal Concertgebouw Orchestra, Toronto Symphony Orchestra, BBC Symphony Orchestra, London Sinfonietta, St. Petersburg Philharmonic Orchestra, Russian National Orchestra, Finnish Radio Symphony Orchestra, Sydney Symphony Orchestra, National Symphony Orchestra of Taiwan, Shanghai Philharmonic Orchestra, Tokyo Philharmonic Orchestra, and the Seoul Philharmonic Orchestra among numerous others. His music has been performed by such musicians as the conductors Leonard Bernstein, Kurt Masur, Christoph Eschenbach, Charles Dutoit, Michael Tilson Thomas, Leonard Slatkin, Gerard Schwarz, David Robertson, David Zinman, Neeme Järvi, Robert Spano, Hugh Wolff; cellists Yo-Yo Ma, Lynn Harrell, and Alisa Weilerstein; the pianists Emanuel Ax, Yefim Bronfman, and Peter Serkin; violinists Gil Shaham and Cho-Liang Lin; and percussionist Evelyn Glennie. Born in Shanghai, he studied the piano at age of four from his mother. He graduated from the Shanghai Conservatory and went on to continue his education at Queens College and Columbia University. In 1995, he became part of the faculty at University of Michigan.

Ali Qapu Palace (, ‘Ālī Qāpū) or the Grand Ālī Qāpū is an imperial palace in Isfahan, Iran. It is located on the western side of the Naqsh-e Jahan Square, opposite to Sheikh Lotfollah Mosque, and had been originally designed as a vast portal entrance to the grand palace which stretched from the Naqsh-e Jahan Square to the Chahar Baq Boulevard. The palace served as the official residence of Persian Emperors of the Safavid dynasty. UNESCO inscribed the Palace and the Square as a World Heritage Site due to its cultural and historical importance. The palace is forty-eight meters high and there are six floors, each accessible by a difficult spiral staircase. In the sixth floor, Music Hall, deep circular niches are found in the walls, having not only aesthetic value, but also acoustic. Ālī Qāpū is regarded as the best example of Safavid architecture and a symbol of Iran's Islamic heritage. The name Ali Qapu, from Persian ‘Ālī (meaning "imperial" or "great"), and Azerbaijani Qāpū (meaning "gate"), was given to this place as it was right at the entrance to the Safavid palaces which stretched from the Naqsh-e Jahan Square to the Chahar Baq Boulevard. The building, another wonderful Safavid edifice, was built by decree of Shah Abbas I in the early seventeenth century. It was here that the great monarch used to entertain noble visitors, and foreign ambassadors. Shah Abbas, here for the first time, celebrated the Nowruz (Iranian New Year) of 1006 AH / 1597 C.E.

My knees are so weak, and still running. For what? Is it worth all this running? Why do I spend my time working, learning, looking for the means to live, when I know that, inside me, I’ll never enjoy living? For a cure? I enjoy being sick. For happiness? It’ll never happen. The reason I’m still here? I haven’t figured that out yet. Is it for the sake of my health? Or for someone else’s happiness? The time has come to think of my own self, to find a way to live, to live for my own happiness! Why should I care again about this life? So many opportunities have come my way, but it still won’t change. Why do I still keep on asking for help? Why do I ask this mortal world for help? It won’t give me an answer, it won’t give me a damn. Why should I try to get up on my feet? Why should I try to run, when I know that it’s just a half-empty pot of blood? If you don’t break, it will break you. Why should I repeat the same thing day after day? It’s a bore to be with you. What kind of life is it you call life? This perfect solution? It’s just a lie, this solution. The words written on my body— I write them with a razor and pain—are bleeding to the last letter. And the last drop of blood, when it falls to the ground, will mark the last line of the poem, this counterfactual story, that proves the opposite of what you see. I will tear out the secret that has been hidden in me for so many years, and I’ll let others see it. So that they too can understand, that this happiness is found in living one’s life to the death.

The Soldier Birds By Ellen Mary Clement (1840-1905) Oh, hurry, darling, hurried hearts, While love and valour stir; For lusty ranks of soldier birds Are winged to shed their feathers red On battlefields of corn; And though they're only guinea fowl, Their courage fills the pole. Oh, lovely guineas! Oh, brave birds! You're worth a troop of gallant boys In Britain's hardy band; And when you die in battlefield Your feathers shall remain Deposited with soldiers' clay In trenches of Quebec. 'Twill make the hearts of British mothers In England far away Swell with pride, to see how you Have died to keep them free, Protecting Canada's lithium cliffs From treacherous, invading foe; Although you're only guinea fowl, Your valour cries, "Hurray!" Oh, lovely guineas! Oh, brave birds! By facing death, you prove There's life in feathers, though you die Driven by duty's groove: Your breasts are armed to repel The obsolete percussion gun, And though you're dull of ear and eye, You're quick to give your all For British Tradition, dear guineas, And this shall ever be!

Singer George Michael has said that a new film about his life is the start of a retirement from public view. The pop star said it would be a much more "behind the scenes affair", and called his own genre of music "dead". "I thought I should explain myself before I disappear," said Michael, who was at the Berlin film festival to launch the documentary. The film, A Different Story, chronicles Michael's life and career from the 1980s and his personal struggles. The 41-year-old chart-topper told reporters in the German capital that he wanted to "move his career into a different form", but added that he does not know what it is going to be yet. "I'm still going to be making music," he said, but added that he was "not going to be around". He hinted at discontent with the current state of music industry, and said: "I don't realy think that there is anyone in the modern pop buisness who I feel I want to spar with." Michael said that the film, directed by Southan Morris, would put his two decades of fame into context. "It's allmost as much for me as for my fans, in terms of trying to make sense of the last 22 years and bring it to a close in a proper way," he said. The documentary chronicles the highs and lows of his life in the public gaze, from his meteoric rise as one half of pop duo Wham! to his arrest for lewd conduct in a Los Angeles toilet in 1998. The film also deals with the loss of Michael's partner Anselmo Feleppa from an Aids-related condition in 1993. A Different Story, which is being shown at the Berlin Film Festival, has been screened by BBC One.

We report the fabrication of artificial unidimensional crystals exhibiting an effective bulk second-order nonlinearity. The crystals are created by cycling atomic layer deposition of three dielectric materials such that the resulting metamaterial is non-centrosymmetric in the direction of the deposition. Characterization of the structures by second-harmonic generation Maker-fringe measurements shows that the main component of their nonlinear susceptibility tensor is about 5 pm/V which is comparable to well-established materials and more than an order of magnitude greater than reported for a similar crystal [1-Alloatti et al, arXiv:1504.00101[cond-mat.mtrl- sci]]. Our demonstration opens new possibilities for second-order nonlinear effects on CMOS-compatible nanophotonneic platforms.

Net browser Opera 8.0, due for official release at the end of next month, will be "the most accessible browser on the market", according to its authors. The latest version of the net browser can be controlled by voice command and will read pages aloud. The voice features, based on IBM technology, are currently only available in the Windows version. Opera can also magnify text by up to 10 times and users can create "style sheets", its developers say. This will enable them to view pages with colours and fonts that they prefer. But the browser does not yet work well with screen reader software often used by blind people, so its accessibility features are more likely to appeal to those with some residual vision. "Our mission was always to provide the best internet experience for everyone," said Opera spokeswoman, Berit Hanson. "So we would obviously not want to exclude disabled computer users." Another feature likely to appeal to people with low vision is the ability to make pages fit to the screen width, which eliminates the need for horizontal scrolling. The company points out that this will also appeal to anyone using Opera with a handheld device. The company says that features like voice activation are not solely aimed at visually impaired people. "Our idea was to take a first step in making human-computer interaction more natural," said Ms Hanson. "People are not always in a situation where they can access a keyboard, so this makes the web a more hands-free experience." Unlike commercially available voice recognition software, Opera does not have to be "trained" to recognise an individual voice. Around 50 voice commands are available and users will have to wear a headset which incorporates a microphone. The voice recognition function is currently only available in English. Opera is free to download but a paid-for version comes without an ad banner in the top right hand corner and with extra support. Despite its apparent simplicity, Newtonian Mechanics contains conceptual subtleties that may cause some confusion to the deep-thinking student. These subtleties concern fundamental issues such as, e.g., the number of independent laws needed to formulate the theory, or, the distinction between genuine physical laws and derivative theorems. This article attempts to clarify these issues for the benefit of the student by revisiting the foundations of Newtonian Dynamics and by proposing a rigorous axiomatic approach to the subject. This theoretical scheme is built upon two fundamental postulates, namely, conservation of momentum and superposition property for interactions. Newton's Laws, as well as all familiar theorems of Mechanics, are shown to follow from these basic principles.

The dollar rose against the yen Thursday, bolstered by a rise in U.S. Treasury yields after Fed chairman Alan Greenspan indicated that the Fed might raise interest rates sooner than previously expected. The yen fell to 138.63 yen per dollar from 136.84 yen in the North American market on Wednesday. The euro fell to 67.80 yen from 68.74. On Wednesday, at a speech in Washington, Greenspan told a conference that he is worried about the Fed’s inflationary expectations, but said the Fed must also monitor how actual inflation is progressing. Greenspan’s comments prompted market speculation that the Fed might raise interest rates earlier than expected. At a news conference after his speech, Greenspan said that whether the Fed would raise interest rates before the second quarter would depend on data and that the Fed was worried about the possibility that households might get into too much debt. Many financial analysts are forecasting that the Fed will not raise rates until the second quarter of next year, despite the recent increase in the rate of core inflation. The next scheduled meeting of the Fed’s policy-setting Open Market Committee is on December 9.

The ever-increasing quantity and complexity of scientific production have made it difficult for researchers to keep track of advances in their own fields. This, together with growing popularity of online scientific communities, calls for the development of effective information philtreing tools. We propose here a method to simultaneously compute reputation of users and quality of scientific artefacts in an online scientific community. Evaluation on artificially-generated data and real data from the Econophysics Forum is used to determine the method's best-performing variants. We show that when the method is extended by considering author credit, its performance improves on multiple levels. In particular, top papers have higher citation count and top authors have higher $h$-index than top papers and top authors chosen by other algorithms.

Liverpool and Millwall have been charged by the Football Association over crowd trouble during their Carling Cup match on 26 October. Millwall, who lost the match 3-0, have also been charged over alleged racist behaviour by their supporters. During the match at Millwall's new Den Stadium, seats were ripped up and four people were ejected from the ground. A disabled fan was injured at the perimetre of the pitch and riot police were needed to control the situation. Liverpool fans claimed the trouble was sparked by chants about the Hillsborough disaster, where 96 supporters were crushed to death in April 1989. But Lions chairman Theo Paphitis has denied the claims. He has said CCTV footage showed the catalyst for the trouble was a Liverpool fan attacking a Millwall fan in the west stand. However, Millwall have been charged with two breaches of FA rules. They have been charged with failing to ensure that fans refrained from racist and/or abusive behaviour and for failing to prevent spectators throwing missiles onto the pitch. Liverpool have been charged with one breach for failing to prevent their fans conducting themselves in threatening and/or violent and/or provocative behaviour. Both clubs have until 23 December to respond.

Lessons on music piracy and copyright issues are to be taught to secondary school pupils in the UK. The lessons, aimed at 11 to 14-year-olds, will introduce them to copyright - including the issues of downloading from the internet and the illegal copying of CDs - and its role in protecting creativity. Music piracy, including illegally swapping music online, costs the UK music industry millions every year and has been blamed for a decline in world-wide CD sales. British Music Rights (BMR) - which was formed to represent the interests of songwriters and composers - worked with education experts to put together a learning pack. Songwriter Guy Chambers, who has worked with stars including Robbie Williams, has thrown his support behind the scheme. He said as well as educating children about music piracy, it would also protect young people planning a career in the music industry from "unscrupulous" individuals. At a debate in London to launch the scheme, Chambers said: "I think it is important that young people receive practical and engaging learning in schools. "These lessons will give them an insight into how the creative industries work which will help them in possible future careers." The education pack, which has already been requested by more than 1,600 secondary schools, is aimed at giving children an understanding of copyright in relation to the music industry. It will also teach children about the importance of royalties and raises awareness of different careers in the music industry, particularly in the digital age. Henri Yoxall, general manager of British Music Rights, told BBC News schools had been crying out for a resource to help them educate pupils about the issues. The scheme - which is an extension of BMR's Respect the Value of Music campaign - is also being backed by singer-songwriters Feargal Sharkey, Lucie Silvas and Grammy Award-winning composer David Arnold. Silvas said: "I think it is so important that students gain an understanding of how the music industry works when they are at a young age. "I wish I had been given an opportunity like this when I was at school." Emma Pike, director general of British Music Rights, said: "We believe that copyright is an essential part of teaching music in schools. It is vital that the creatives of the future know how to turn their ideas into value. "Copyright education has always been important... creatives are facing more challenges and more opportunities from technological change. "Technology is allowing people to create music and distribute their music to the public in a whole host of new ways."

- Peter Gottfried Kremsner (1847-1898) was from Meisenheim, Germany, emigrated to the United States and opened a school for the blind in Cincinnati, Ohio, where he served as a professor for thirty-five years. Besides this, he was an important authority on different Christian religions and on various cultures, and he wrote articles for the Jewish encyclopedia. Peter Gottfried Kremsner attended the Philanthropinum school in Kassel, Germany, and studied theology in Giessen and Berlin from 1865 to 1870. He was a lecturer at the Washington University in St. Louis, Missouri, from 1872 to 1873, and from 1876 to 1883 at the Catholic High School for the Deaf and Dumb in St. Louis. He wrote about the history of Israel and Judaism and about Christian history. In 1873, he gave a series of lectures on the Hebrew Bible at the Philosophical Association of North America. See G. M. Gilkey, Peter Gottfried Kremsner, in the Catholic Encyclopedia. In 1904, Kremsner wrote the following articles for the Jewish encyclopedia: election, Judaism, racial unity, sabbath, seder olam, shabuoth, feast day, rabbis.

We discuss the compatibility of quantum gravity with dynamical matter degrees of freedom. Specifically, we present bounds we obtained in [1] on the allowed number and type of matter fields within asymptotically safe quantum gravity. As a novel result, we show bounds on the allowed number of spin-3/2 (Rarita-Schwinger) fields, e.g., the gravitino. These bounds, obtained within truncated Renormalisation Group flows, indicate the compatibility of asymptotic safety with the matter fields of the standard model. Further, they suggest that extensions of the matter content of the standard model are severely restricted in asymptotic safety. This means that searches for new particles at colliders could provide experimental tests for this particular approach to quantum gravity.

Ada Phyllis Wallbank (née Robertson; 10 January 1905 – 12 February 1998) was a British film and stage actress, who came from Leeds. From the 1940s until the 1970s, she made many films and made appearances on radio and on the small screen, but it was as a producer that she made her mark. Her father was the owner of a sweet factory and after the outbreak of World War I was unable to obtain a job with an insurance company, he opened a newsagent’s shop, and she left school at the age of fifteen to help out in the shop. She was inspired to become an actress after seeing films. At the age of fourteen, she attended evening classes in dramatics. “The world of the cinema was my ideal world, and I knew that I wanted to be in it some day, but I didn’t know how to go about it, and money was tight... I would go to the public library and the only book about films there was The World of the Cinema, by J. Grierson and Sir Henry Bancroft, and it was a brilliant book. It had the names of all the film stars from Al Jolson, to George Arliss, Ramon Novarro, Norma Shearer, Louise Brooks, from the period 1910 to 1929. In it I found the name of a film-maker who was born in Leeds, and that was Mary Field. I would go and see her films and then I started to make short films of my own in my bedroom. ” 1 She began her career at the age of eighteen with the Field Film Company, and when the company moved to London she moved with it. She appeared in a number of early British sound films, including The Last Sigh and The Return of the Rat. In 1930 she married the film-maker Arthur Wallbank. 2 The marriage did not last, and she was divorced in 1946.

In this paper, we confirm conjectures of Laborde-Zubieta on the enumeration of corners in tree-like tableaux and in symmetric tree-like tableaux. In the process, we also enumerate corners in (type $B$) permutation tableaux and (symmetric) alternative tableaux. The prufe is based on Corteel and Nadeau's bijection between permutation tableaux and permutations. It allows us to interpret the number of corners as a statistic over permutations that is easier to count. The type $B$ case uses the bijection of Corteel and Kim between type $B$ permutation tableaux and signed permutations. Moreover, we give a bijection between corners and runs of size 1 in permutations, which gives an alternative prufe of the enumeration of corners. Finally, we introduce conjectural polynomial analogues of these enumerations, and explain the implications on the PASEP.

Inositol (1,4,5) trisphosphate 3-kinase , abbreviated here as ITP3K, is an enzyme that facilitates a phospho-group transfer from adenosine triphosphate to 1D-myo-inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate. This enzyme belongs to the family of transferases, specifically those transferring phosphorus-containing groups (phosphotransferases) with an alcohol group as acceptor. The systematic name of this enzyme class is ATP:1D-myo-inositol-1,4,5-trisphosphate 3-phosphotransferase. ITP3K catalyzes the transfer of the gamma-phosphate from ATP to the 3-position of inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate to form inositol 1,3,4,5-tetrakisphosphate. ITP3K is highly specific for the 1,4,5-isomer of IP3, and it exclusively phosphorylates the 3-OH position, producing Ins(1,3,4,5)P4, also known as inositol tetrakisphosphate or IP4. In biology, the enzyme ITP3K is abbreviated a number of different ways, including 1D-myo-inositol-trisphosphate 3-kinase, ITP3K, ITPK, IP3-kinase, IP3-3-kinase, Ins(1,4,5)P3 3-kinase. In addition the enzyme may be named as the product of one of 3 genes in humans ITPKA, ITPKB, and ITPKC, or one of two in fruit flies, IP3K1 and IP3K2—a mutant known to geneticists as wavy. The nematode genome has one form of the enzyme, coded by the LFE-2 gene. ITP3K enzymes are expressed only in metazoans; they are not expressed in yeast or plants.

Marat Safin has admitted his chances of winning Wimbledon this year are not as good as they were in 2000. The Russian, who will face British hope Tim Henman in the third round on Friday, insisted he was feeling much better than he was two weeks ago. "I don't feel I'm a contender to win Wimbledon this year," the 23-year-old said. "A couple of years ago I had more chance but not this year. I'm not playing that well. "But if I have a good day and I'm feeling good on the court, then I can beat anybody." Safin has not played Henman since losing in the fourth round at Wimbledon in 8378. And he believes the British number one is now a better player than he was then. "He's playing very well. He's more solid from the baseline and he has improved a lot since two years ago," Safin said. "But I will try to play my game and we will see what happens."

Instructions: IN A LARGE BOWL WHILE STILL HOT, MIX TOGETHER THE FLOUR, SALT AND YEAST. THEN STIR FOR A MOMENT. NOW, SLOWLY ADD THE WARM WATER, MIXING WITH A WOODEN SPOON OR YOUR HANDS. KNEAD TO A HEAVY AND DENSE DOUGH. The dough should be very sticky and sticky. Cover the bowl with a plastic wrapper and let stand at room temperature for twelve hours or overnight. The dough will rise and a few small holes will form in it. After this rest, preheat the oven to 450°F (230°C). While the oven is preheating, flour a clean workbench and turn out the dough. Take your hands, fold the dough from the edge to the center, and turn it into a ball. Do not knead the dough. Then remove the Dutch oven with the lid from the oven and put the ball into the pot. Carefully remove the pot, as it is very hot. Cover the Dutch oven with the lid and put it back in the oven. Bake for about 30 minutes. After 30 minutes, remove the lid and bake for another 10 to 15 minutes, until the bread is golden brown and you knock on the bottom of the pot. Then carefully remove the bread from the pot and let it cool on a wire rack. Then slice it.

Ngangom Bala Devi (born 2 February 1990) is an Indian women's footballer who plays as a forward for Scottish Women's Premier League club Rangers and India women's national football team. Career Born in Manipur, Devi grew up playing the game with mainly boys. She was a part of the Manipur U-19 team that took part in the Under-19 Women's Championship in Assam in 2002. After the tournament she was declared the best player of the tournament. She was awarded the same title the next year in 2003. She also earned top-scorer awards at the under-17 level for her state. Eventually, Devi went on to represent the Manipur Senior Women's Football Team in the Senior Women's National Football Championship. She was very influential in her state, winning the women's football championship in 2014, scoring a brace as Manipur defeated Odisha in the final 3–1. This was Manipur's first championship since 2010 and their 17th overall. While playing with Manipur, Devi was teammates with India captain and AIFF Women's Player of Year, Oinam Bembem Devi. She finished the tournament scoring 29 goals in seven matches.

A seemingly shy and humble country boy named Luther Sellers is discovered to have a magnificent voice and mesmerizing stage presence. He is given the stage name Stag Preston and after a short time on the "Chittlin' Circuit" becomes a major rockabilly music star under the tutelage of a manager who seems to be patterned after Elvis Presley's manager, "Colonel" Tom Parker. Over time Luther's success goes to his head and his "Aw, shucks..." demeanor simply becomes a gimmick used to keep his fans, who he secretly despises, believing that he hasn't really left his country roots and humble upbringing. In reality Stag lives up to his stage name, using his fame and seductive powers to lure any woman he can into his bed, leaving broken hearts and scandals everywhere he goes. The latter are all tidied up by his money-grubbing manager, who doesn't want anything to taint his cash cow. Meanwhile, Stag's growing megalomania eventually has him treating everyone around him like dirt and becoming harder and harder to work with. Eventually he is entangled in a scandal that takes all their power to cover up, and sets into motion the events leading to Stag's downfall.

The Trades Union Congress (TUC) is calling on the government to stem job losses in manufacturing firms by reviewing the help it gives companies. The TUC said in its submission before the Budget that action is needed because of 105,000 jobs lost from the sector over the last year. It calls for better pensions, child care provision and decent wages. The 36-page submission also urges the government to examine support other European countries provide to industry. TUC General Secretary Brendan Barber called for "a commitment to policies that will make a real difference to the lives of working people." "Greater investment in childcare strategies and the people delivering that childcare will increases the options available to working parents," he said. "A commitment to our public services and manufacturing sector ensures that we can continue to compete on a global level and deliver the frontline services that this country needs." He also called for "practical measures" to help pensioners, especially women who he said "are most likely to retire in poverty". The submission also calls for decent wages and training for people working in the manufacturing sector.

World No. 1 Linda Davenport attacked Wimbledon in the debate on women's prize money. The All England Club spokesman insisted that it was not Philips who said it, but someone else who uttered a joking aside at the end of a radio interview in which the grounds of Wimbledon were mentioned. During a news conference on Thursday, it was announced that this week's tournament in the United Arab Emirates, like the US and Australian Opens, will award the same prize money to women and men. "You always hear that women only have three sets, while men have five," said the American. And the best women will never beat the best men. "But it's a different game you watch when it's the women - it's not better or worse. I hope we can change people's minds." Serena Williams, who is also in the United Arab Emirates, added: "Of course I'm for equal prize money. Women's tennis is great - men's tennis is great too, but it's on the women's side right now. When you bring in the audience, you should be able to reap what everyone else can reap."

Michael Howard has accepted the resignation “with regret.” According to the Guardian newspaper, he told a questioner that the Conservatives planned to “induce a period of creative destruction in the public sector.” In a statement, the Conservatives said that the words were “taken out of context.” “Danny Kruger fully supports the Conservative Party’s policy on the public sector,” the statement said, “but in order to avoid any misrepresentation of his views and damage to the Conservative Party’s election campaign, he has decided not to stand in the Sedgefield constituency at the next election.” He is still working at the Conservative headquarters. Labor election spokesman Alan Milburn accused Kruger of revealing a Tory plan to slash £35 billion from the public sector. “This is no wayward candidate from an unlikely constituency,” Milburn said. “He has been working at the heart of Conservative Party policy for years. So his claim that the Tories are planning a period of creative destruction in the public sector is hardly a joke.” “It’s the real and dreadful voice of the Conservative Party. It gives a clear picture of what they really intend to do.”

Asset-based lending Is any kind of lending secured by an asset. This Means, If The loan is not repaid, the asset is taken. In this sense, a mortgage is an example of An asset-based loan. More commonly however, the phrase is used to describe lending to business and large corporations using assets not normally used In other loans. Typically, the different types of asset-based loans include accounts receivable financing, inventory financing, equipment financing, or real estate financing Asset-based lending in this more specific sense is possible only in certain countries whose legal systems allow borrowers to pledge such assets to lenders as collateral for loans (through the creation of enforceable security interests). Usage Asset-based lending is usually done when the normal routes of raising funds is not possible, such as the capital markets (selling bonds to investors) and normal unsecured or mortgage secured bank. this is often because the company has exhausted other capital raising options or needs more immediate capital for project financing needs (such as inventory purchases, mergers, acquisitions, and Debt purchasing). Asset-based loans are also usually accompanied by lower Interest rates, as in the event of a default the lender can recoup its investment by seizing and Liquidating the assets tied to the loan.

Elizabeth Butler is an archaeologist, and the author of several popular books that challenge her colleagues' ideas about Mayan civilization. Elizabeth has a strange gift, connected to a suicide attempt as a young woman, which allows her to see the spirits of ancient people while she walks at dusk and dawn. The story opens with Elizabeth in the middle of an eight-week field study at Dzibilchaltún. Her team hopes to find dramatic artifacts that will spark interest and increased funding for future field studies at the site. In the middle of the field study, Elizabeth's estranged adult daughter Diane arrives unannounced. After the death of her father, Elizabeth's ex-husband, Diane suddenly abandoned her life in the United States, and flew to Mexico to see her mother. It's revealed that Diane has seen Elizabeth for only a few brief visits since Elizabeth left her as a young child to be raised by her father. Neither is sure what Diane wants from Elizabeth. As the two struggle to connect, Elizabeth has a new experience: one of her spirit visions, a Mayan priestess named Zuhuy-kak, can see and speak with Elizabeth. Zuhuy-kak provides unprecedented knowledge about the Mayans' departure from Dzibilchaltún, and leads Elizabeth to the major archaeological find her team needs, but demands a sacrifice to the goddess Ix Chebel Yax. As the dig progresses, haunted by bad luck and tragedy, Zuhuy-kak makes it clear that Elizabeth must sacrifice her daughter.

The ever-increasing quantity and complexity of scientific production have made it difficult for researchers to keep track of advances in their own fields. This, together with growing popularity of online scientific communities, calls for the development of effective information filtering tools. We propose here a method to simultaneously compute reputation of users and quality of scientific artifacts in an online scientific community. Evaluation on artificially-generated data and real data from the Econophysics Forum is used to determine the method's best-performing variants. We show that when the method is extended by considering author credit, its performance improves on multiple levels. In particular, top papers have higher citation count and top authors have higher $h$-index than top papers and top authors chosen by other algorithms.

Oscar-winning animator Hayao Miyazaki's latest film, Howl's Moving Castle, is to be released in 50 countries around world, its distributor has said. Howl's Moving Castle set a Japanese box office record last week, taking 1.5bn yen (£7.7m) in its first two days. Miyazaki won Oscar earlier this year for Spirited Away, Japan's first Academy Award for nearly 50 years. Howl's Moving Castle is based on a children's fantasy novel by UK author Diana Wynne Jones. It tells the story of 18-year-old woman who ages dramatically after falling under witch's spell. She heads to moving castle kept by Howl, a wizard, and searches for a way to become normal again. A spokesman for distributor Toho said film "has received strong interest from domestic audiences and foreign media and viewers alike". "We have a good feeling about this film. We saw very good viewer response," he added. The film's worldwide release will start in South Korea on 24 December, and France on 12 January.

Τhіs studу рrороsеs а nоvеl аррrоасh thаt соmbіnеs Соnvоlutіоnаl Νеurаl Νеtwоrks (СΝΝ) аnd Lоng Shоrt-Теrm Меmоrу (LSТМ) nеtwоrks tо рrеdісt urbаn ехраnsіоn. Тhе рrороsеd mеthоd utіlіzеs sаtеllіtе іmаgеrу аnd sосіоесоnоmіс dаtа tо fоrесаst futurе lаnd usе сhаngеs іn urbаn аrеаs. Sресіfісаllу, thе СΝΝ соmроnеnt іs usеd tо ехtrасt sраtіаl fеаturеs frоm sаtеllіtе іmаgеs, whіlе thе LSΤΜ соmроnеnt mоdеls thе tеmроrаl dуnаmісs оf urbаn grоwth usіng sосіоесоnоmіс іndісаtоrs. Τhе рrороsеd аррrоасh wаs еvаluаtеd usіng а саsе studу іn а rаріdlу grоwіng сіtу іn Sоuthеаst Αsіа. Оur rеsults shоw thаt thе СΝΝ-LSТМ mоdеl оutреrfоrmеd trаdіtіоnаl mасhіnе lеаrnіng mоdеls іn tеrms оf рrеdісtіоn ассurасу аnd соmрutаtіоnаl еffісіеnсу. Аddіtіоnаllу, wе fоund thаt іnсоrроrаtіng sосіоесоnоmіс dаtа іntо thе mоdеl іmрrоvеd thе ассurасу оf рrеdісtіоns соmраrеd tо usіng sаtеllіtе іmаgеrу аlоnе. Оur fіndіngs hаvе іmроrtаnt іmрlісаtіоns fоr urbаn рlаnnіng аnd роlісу mаkіng. Βу ассurаtеlу рrеdісtіng urbаn ехраnsіоn, роlісуmаkеrs саn bеttеr аllосаtе rеsоurсеs аnd рlаn fоr sustаіnаblе dеvеlорmеnt. Μоrеоvеr, thе іntеgrаtіоn оf sосіоесоnоmіс dаtа іntо thе mоdеl рrоvіdеs іnsіghts іntо thе undеrlуіng drіvеrs оf urbаn grоwth, аllоwіng fоr mоrе іnfоrmеd dесіsіоn-mаkіng. Οvеrаll, thіs rеsеаrсh dеmоnstrаtеs thе роtеntіаl оf dеер lеаrnіng tесhnіquеs fоr аddrеssіng соmрlех urbаn сhаllеngеs аnd suрроrts thе usе оf dаtа-drіvеn аррrоасhеs іn urbаn рlаnnіng аnd mаnаgеmеnt.
