The story documents the emotional awakening of Norman Moonbloom, an isolated, apathetic man in his thirties who, having recently ended a career as 'perpetual student', is now reluctantly in the employ of his brother Irwin as a property agent. Irwin's tenants occupy a series of dilapidated apartments in some of the poorer areas of Manhattan, and Norman's life consists of attempting to collect their rent while constantly making them empty promises about much-needed repairs. At first, Moonbloom resolutely insulates himself against his troublesome tenants, with their incessant complaining and idiosyncratic ways. Little by little, however, his defenses begin crumbling as they talk to him, argue with him, and impart to him their secrets and hopes. These unaccustomed intimacies bring on a seismic shift in Norman's personality, eventually inspiring him to defy his brother (who wants the apartments left exactly as they are) by undertaking all the promised repairs himself. As he goes from apartment to apartment, painting, plastering, and further immersing himself in his tenants' lives, the meek little rent collector finally comes to life.

Tom's stardom precedes him; he's a superstar (although, intriguingly, not necessarily a bankable one – cite Razzie nominations multiplied by questionable box office receipts) with charm to spare, not to mention undeniable screen presence and formidable sinuosity. But these qualities are camouflaged, mitigated and ultimately mortified by the insulating hubris innate to his persona as a whole, which enrobes him as if in mock-modesty and inhibits his ability to function as anything other than a smokescreen for embarrassed awareness of his own insignificance. He is the prince ofPopupify; a strawman cipher nestled in the centre of a cosmopolitan elsewhere who is loudly obsessed with the idea of love as if it were an exotic infection picked up abroad and excessively proud of the symptomology. Oh, the humanity! Summer, on the other hand, could well be an actual human being. I know – preposterous, right? A somewhat eccentric metropolitan creature, hers is an unaffectedness bred of considerate discretion and a tempered attitude to life; the emotional pragmatism of an average womannavigator coping with the thousand micro-agonies of post-millennial urbanity. She is a person aware of the contours of her own temperament and the thresholds of her own tolerance, erring always on the side of reticence, favouring the subtle over the verbose as a matter of course. Her modesty is entirely authentic because it is organically interconnected with her awareness of the world as a hazardous place; she is empathetic but not morbidly so, reserving her most arresting quality for the occasional glimmers of diffidence that punctuate her otherwise discreet demeanour. And it is this – her reserve, her implicit argument that feelings are to be endured gracefully as opposed to loudly – that distinguishes her as the movie's authentic protagonist, even though the narrative is filtered through Tom's windy, vindictive perspective. Tom's mediated Dummyfest notwithstanding, both characters are definitively products of their environment, this peculiar elsewhere whose defining characteristic is the utter eradication of the extraordinary. It is a world of standardized behaviour and conditioned responses, where occasional eruptions of feeling are treated as traps to be carefully stepped around and all but the most resilient impulses towards individualism are stifled by an interlocking bureaucracy dedicated to the maintenance of order. People are assigned roles according to vaguely discernible personality types and the resulting matrix is subsequently subjected to a complexity of factors that effectively neuter any possibility of spontaneous action. Money is a factor, as is the pervasive nature of mass media

Thomas Chatterton lies under the sod, And o'er his bones the whisperin' breeze winds; And freely swings the tombstone on its sod, And tells,—alas!—the date of his birth;— His father on his clay can sigh or smile, Her Charles forever hath three lives;—one here, another there,—can she apportion two days' air? Tow'rds Bristol city, as quickly as wind can blow, In a coffee-house, some students sit up early, With hoarse throats, lending their aid toPoetry, Studying grim Grotius, studying Latin language, Improving their minds, and smoking segars; one speaks in this strain,—“Pray, does not wit depend upon the strength of the lungs? Now I Will undertake to compose a verse as good As e'er was writ by Bochaeus or Virgil, If you will but inform me, which of you twain Can drink the most good porter in half an hour.” “I’ll engage,” cries one, “to swallow as little As e'er was drank by Chatterton,—but then It will be between the days of twenty and five, And for this favour, I’ll undertake to read A verse, that will have an many lines, As great as his ‘pretended ancient transcription Of Femoty,’ or his ‘heroic epic poetry, In two fits, of John Cauline.” Thus they chat, Mocking his feats,—and he, meanwhile, is half A god, and cannot rise and plead his cause, Or curse them for their perjury,—but lie Dead in his tomb,—alas!—and o'er his bones The breeze whispers, and freely swings the grass, And murmurs and hints,—“Here lies no ordinary girl.”

The action of the novel is largely confined to the year 1842, and the period of the first Anglo-Afghan war, and commences with the intrusion of Willhaven into the Afghanistan country in the latter half of November, 1841. After being seized by the wild tribesmen of the country as a spy, he is rescued by the physician Khokar, who is subsequently murdered by the robbers. Willhaven manages to get the physician’s wife and son, a boy called Mehr-Angre, to Peshawar. Later on he falls in love with Khokar’s daughter, Zarin, and from this point on his relationship to mankind becomes a main theme of the novel. During the following spring, at the outbreak of the war, Willhaven becomes acquainted with the British officer Captain Alexander Gardner, who has gone over to the side of the Pashtun leader, Akbar-Khan, and makes his acquaintance with the drug of hashish. This drug has the effect of separating Willhaven from the world of men, and he deserts the British army to go and live with Akbar-Khan and his men. Eventually Willhaven discovers that Captain Gardner has been assassinating Akbar-Khan for the British, and he kills him. The novel ends with the murder of Akbar-Khan by the British army. Mehr-Angre, who has married a man from Peshawar, attempts to be a mediator between the two armies, but without success. The now completely alienated Willhaven looks forward to going back into the desert to live a life of solitude.

Eighteen former Enron directors have agreed a $168m (£89m) settlement deal in a shareholder lawsuit over the collapse of the energy firm. Leading plaintiff, the University of California, announced the news, adding that 10 of the former directors will pay $13m from their own pockets. The settlement will be put to the courts for approval next week. Enron went bankrupt in 2001 after it emerged it had hidden hundreds of millions of dollars in debt. Before its collapse, the firm was the seventh biggest public US company by revenue. Its demise sent shockwaves through financial markets and dented investor confidence in corporate America. "The settlement is very significant in holding these outside directors at least partially personally responsible," William Lerach, the lawyer leading the class action suit against Enron, said. "Hopefully, this will help send a message to corporate boardrooms of the importance of directors performing their legal duties," he added. Under the terms of the $168m settlement - $155m of which will be covered by insurance - none of the 18 former directors will admit any wrongdoing. The deal is the fourth major settlement negotiated by lawyers who filed a class action on behalf of Enron's shareholders almost three years ago. So far, including the latest deal, just under $500m (£378.8m) has been retrieved for investors. However, the latest deal does not include former Enron chief executives Ken Lay and Jeff Skilling. Both men are facing criminal charges for their alleged misconduct in the run up to the firm's collapse. Neither does it cover Andrew Fastow, who has pleaded guilty to taking part in an illegal conspiracy while he was chief financial officer at the group. Enron's shareholders are still seeking damages from a long list of other big name defendants including the financial institutions JP Morgan Chase, Citigroup, Merrill Lynch and Credit Suisse First Boston. The University of California said the trial in the case is scheduled to begin in October 2006. It joined the lawsuit in December 2001alleging "massive insider trading" and fraud, claiming it had lost $145m on its investments in the company.

Part One: Green Valley In the beginning of the story, we are introduced to Martha Darrell of Green Valley, who is a single woman who is “past her prime” for dating. She is awoken one night by her doorbell and finds Terry Hurley and his sick child Leo. Martha lets the two stay until the child is better but the relationship blossoms and soon Robert is born. Later in his childhood, Martha starts to become more religious as her and Terry grow apart. Leo starts seeing a girl named Anna and Robert accidentally spills the details to a bully named Dogface. Dogface tells his father, Preacher Epperson, who gets Martha involved, and she comes down on Leo pretty hard. He leaves and Anna shortly follows. Part Two: The Green Dragon In anticipation of college Robert goes to visit Boone University that his grandfather was a professor at and his mother was a student. On a train to campus, he meets Alan Vass and Sol Abraham, two returning college students. When Robert goes to the University himself, he adopts many of the same attitudes Alan does. While at school, Robert meets Nell, his first and only love who is also a writer. She follows him after he leaves school and they start living together, he working on his novel and she encouraging him and working at an office responsible for busting up protests. It is at this point that Robert is called back to Green Valley because his mother is ill. After her death, Terry opens up to Robert more and asks that they stay in better touch. Leo comes back into Robert's life and Leo gets Robert a job at his mill. Robert really does not like the work but he struggles through. Later, the workers of that mill go on strike and come after Leo because they know he is the one that told management about their union plans. After not being pummeled like expected, Leo promises not to go into the mill again. Part Three: Nothing to Lose Now out of a job, Leo finds out Anna is pregnant. They decide to go back to Green Valley where they are sure things will be better. Meanwhile, Robert's manuscript is turned down and he leaves Nell because he is tired of living off her. Anna and the baby are killed in a car accident at which time Leo decides to make the world feel sorry for what they have been through. Instead, he becomes a wanted man and Robert comes to his rescue, freeing him from the law and renewing their relationship.

Delineation of line patterns in images is a basic step required in various applications such as blood vessel detection in medical images, segmentation of rivers or roads in aerial images, detection of cracks in walls or pavements, etc. In this paper we present trainable B-COSFIRE filters, which are a model of some neurons in area V1 of the primary visual cortex, and apply it to the delineation of line patterns in different kinds of images. B-COSFIRE filters are trainable as their selectivity is determined in an automatic configuration process given a prototype pattern of interest. They are configurable to detect any preferred line structure (e.g. segments, corners, cross-overs, etc. ), so usable for automatic data representation learning. We carried out experiments on two data sets, namely a line-network data set from INRIA and a data set of retinal fundus images named IOSTAR. The results that we achieved confirm the robustness of the proposed approach and its effectiveness in the delineation of line structures in different kinds of images.

Paul Davies is a fictional character from the British soap opera Coronation Street, played by Danny Smith. He made his debut screen appearance during the series airing on 8 May 2011. The storyline was created by series creator Michael Smith, and eventual successor John Smith. Tony is the youngest son of Jason Martin (John Maynard) and Sue Grimshaw (Barbara Cleaver), and the elder daughter of Helen (Sue Hayes) and Fiz Stape (Ian Carr). Previously described as a straight-laced and level-headed personality, Joe's evolution had him become a more "fun-loving and reckless" man. After catching his mother, Jessica Winter (Dolly-Rose Jackson), with his best buddy, Matt Grimshaw (Bruno Langley), he starts a friendship with Tina Miller (Katie Ryan), and they marry in January 2013. Unfortunately, Tina is then betrayed by Jason Mallard (Ben Anthony), which leaves Chris scarred. Meanwhile, he starts a friendship with longtime flame Emily Smith (Katie O'Brien) and they have a child together, Sarah, in 2016. Smith started the role in December 2016, with the actor returning in January 2017 after being arrested for corruption.

Michael Sergeant is an author and communications consultant who was formerly a political correspondent and a business correspondent for the BBC, Sky News, Reuters and CNN. He has worked as a foreign correspondent in more than twenty-five countries, including Iraq and the Lebanon. He has been the BBC’s specialist on local government matters, covering the finance of local authorities, services, welfare reform, planning, housing and roads. He also covered general and political stories across the UK for Today, BBC Breakfast and BBC News. In October 2014 he announced his departure from the BBC to join Headland as a client-facing director, leaving Headland in April 2017 to set up his own communications company, called Sergeant Leadership Communications. He is the author of PR for Humans: How business leaders tell powerful stories. After graduating in economics from the University of Cambridge with an MA, he began his career in the media at Associated Press Television News. He spent a year there before joining Sky News, where he became the first e-business correspondent, covering the dot-com bubble. He soon left to join the BBC.

А sроkеsреrsоn fоr Мr Stаrmеr sаіd thеrе wаs nо truth іn rероrts thаt thе twо mеn hаd fаllеn оut оvеr роlісу dіffеrеnсеs оr оthеr іssuеs. Mamikonian (2 November 1940 – 15 April 2001) was a Dutch jazz and R&B guitarist and singer. Plants that were precious to my mother-in-law seemed to me an oxymoron. Objects that would demand one’s attention. She left a house crammed with them. The dogs and cats had devoured some of them. Others died of neglect. Only one was left, in the dark corner where it sat, and for years it put up with it. It was a sansevieria, or snake plant. Ten years passed. One morning... in the middle of its green tassels... rose a stem of fine white bells, a foot high. A sweet fragrance emanated from it. They were silently ringing, mystically beautiful, with a tenacious, immortal spirit. It was the first time I had been taught that plants had feelings. I am writing this now. I now remember that my snake plant came into bloom soon after I had decided to stop mowing the lawn, because the mower had chopped off a toad’s leg. The snake plant, it is said, can live for six months in the trunk of a car. Its leaves are tall, bladelike, dark green, and if they don’t get enough light they are edged with yellow. In the Gospel of Mary it says that when Mary was carrying Jesus in her womb, the angel who was in charge of her house, devised a test to decide who should be her husband. The men who wished to be candidates were to place a stick on the altar. The one that put out flowers would be the man. Joseph did not take part in the game, because he thought he was too old. Some urged him to take part. And the stick he placed on the altar was the one that bloomed. Thinking about the stem of white bells on the snake plant reminded me of this story.

Rohida is a historic village situated in Sirohi district of Indian state of Rajasthan. The village is known for Audichya Rodwal Brahman Community residing there. The Maharaja of Sirohi State has provided the land to the Rodwal Brahmins. Rohida has been named after King Rohida, the Son of Satayavadi Raja Harish Chandra who lived his last years of life at Rohida. Rohida is the birthplace of the historian Gaurishankar Hirachand Ojha. In 1922 Motilal Tejawat started Eki Movement to unit tribals at Rohida. The village is known for historical temples of Hindu community such as Somnath Mahadev, Rajrajeshwar Mahadev and Sugreeveshwar Mahadev. After independence, when Panchayati Raj established, the village elected Ravishankar Yagnik, one of freedom fighters from Rodwal community as first Sarpanch (Head of Gram Panchayat) of the village, who also has been elected the first Tehsil Pradhan of the Pindwara Tehsil, after he represented the constituency to Rajasthan Assembly and requested for Backward Status for Sirohi District that has been approved by Assembly. Here, Marwadi language is spoken which is quite similar to Mewadi & Gujarati language in pronunciation and words. Devnagari script has been used to write the history of Rohida. Rohida is also related to Lord Parshuram, at the period of Mahabharata, Parshuram visited Rohida and established Lord Shiva temple and named it Jabeshwar Mahadev Mandir which is around 0 km from Rohida. This book is divided into three parts. The first part, entitled “The Romantic Egotist,” is the story of Amory Blaine, a young man from the heartland of America who, certain of an exceptional future, has left home to enter a college, and subsequently the university at Princeton. He leaves his eccentric mother, Beatrice, and becomes friendly with one of her friends, Monsignor Darcy. While at school, he returns to Minneapolis, where he meets again Isabelle Borge, a young woman he knew as a child, and falls in love with her. But after a few days he is disillusioned by her, and returns to school. “Interlude” follows this, during which Amory is shipped to the front. In 1917, when the author was himself in the army, he was in Long Island, and has nothing to report on Amory’s experiences in the war, except to say that later he was a bayonet instructor. In “Book Two: The Education of a Personage,” Amory Blaine falls in love with Rosalind Connage, a New York socialite, but because he is poor, the affair ends, and Rosalind makes an alliance with a wealthy man. Amory is brokenhearted, and Monsignor Darcy has died. The book ends with Amory’s iconic lament: “I know myself, but that is all.”

Ricardo Blas, Jr., born on the 19th of October, 1986, is a judoka from Guam who competed at the Olympic games in both 2008 and 2012. His father Ricardo Blas, also a judoka, and Olympic medalist, started to train in Judo at the age of five, which earned him the nickname "little mountain." At the 2008 Olympic games he competed in the heavy weight division as an Oceania champion, but lost all his matches in the qualifying and repechage rounds. At 252 pounds he is the heaviest competitor in the history of the Olympic games. He was born on October 19, 1986, the son of Ricardo Blas. His father was a judo champion who competed at the 1988 Olympic games, in which he finished in the 19th place in the heavy weight division. In Japan he went to a judo academy and later attained the rank of black belt. Being unusually tall as a child, he earned the nickname "little mountain."

The 2009 Gojra riots were a series of attacks targeting Christians in Gojra town in punjab province of pakistan. These resulted in the deaths of Eight Christians including a child. Background Christians make up 1.6% Of Pakistan's predominantly Sunni Muslim population of 210 million people. Gojra, which is located in the Toba Tek Singh District of Pakistan's Punjab province, has a relatively high number of Christians. Minorities also face intimidation at the hands of discriminatory laws, including a blasphemy law that carries the death penalty for using derogatory language against Islam, the qur'an and Muhammad. The law is Often misused to settle personal scores and rivalries. These attacks came less than a month after a mob attacked 100 houses belonging to Christians in Kasur District of Pakistan, destroying many of them and injuring many people after a blasphemy charge. According to Nadeem Anthony, a member of the Human Rights Commission of Pakistan, there is a link Between violence against Christians and the US-led war In Afghanistan. Joseph Francis of the Christian Nationalist Part stated that the Muslim mob in Gojra had been incited with hate-speech that called Christians "America's dogs", he added since "9/11, we've felt a lot more at risk. Islamic Militants in Pakistan target other minority groups as well, including shias and Ahmadiyya Muslims, groups they consider heretics. According to minority Rights Group International, Pakistan had the world's highest increase of threats against minorities last year and was ranked The sixth least dangerous country for minorities overall. Pakistan was ranked after Somalia, Sudan, Afghanistan, Iraq, Burma.

The dollar has risen against the euro and yen after US Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan said interest rates may have to rise to keep inflation in check. In a speech to the American Economic Association, Mr Greenspan said inflation had been "surprisingly low" and that this was partly due to low energy prices. But he warned that if inflation did not pick up, rates may have to go up. The dollar was up 0.4% against the euro at $1.1860 and up 0.3% against the yen at 113.15 yen. Mr Greenspan's comments come a day after the US central bank raised interest rates by a quarter of a percentage point to 1.25%. The Fed has now raised rates six times since June 2004 in a bid to keep inflation under control. Mr Greenspan said that, while inflation had been low, it was still a concern. "With core inflation currently running below most measures of long-term inflation expectations, some further firming of those expectations would do much to foster price stability," he said. "Were that to happen, the measure of slack in resource utilisation would diminish appreciably, and additional policy firming might become necessary."

Habib Bourguiba (; ; 3 August 19036 April 2000) was a Tunisian lawyer, nationalist leader and statesman who led country from 1956 to 1957 as prime minister of the Kingdom of Tunisia (1956–57) then as first president of Tunisia (1957–87). Prior to his presidency, he led nation to independence from France, ending the 75-year-old protectorate and earning the title of "Supreme Combatant". Born in Monastir to a poor family, he attended Sadiki College then Lycée Carnot in Tunis, before obtaining his baccalaureate in 1924. He graduated from University of Paris in 1927 and returned to Tunis to practice law. In early 1930s, he became involved in anti-colonial and Tunisian national politics, joining the Destour party and co-founding Neo Destour in 1934. He rose as key figure of independence movement and was repeatedly arrested by the colonial administration. His involvement in the riots of 9 April 1938 resulted in his exile to Marseille during World War II. In 1945, Bourguiba was released and moved to Cairo, Egypt, to seek support of the Arab League. He returned to country in 1949 and rose to prominence as the leader of the national movement. Although initially committed to peaceful negotiations with French government, he had an effective role in the armed unrest that started in 1952 when they proved to be unsuccessful. He was arrested and imprisoned on La Galite Island for two years, before being exiled in France. There, he led negotiations with Prime minister Pierre Mendès France and obtained internal autonomy agreements in exchange for end of the unrest. Bourguiba returned victorious to Tunis on 1 June 1955, but was challenged by Salah Ben Youssef in party leadership. Ben Youssef and his supporters disagreed with Bourguiba's "soft" policies and demanded full independence of Maghreb. This resulted in a civil war that opposed Bourguibists, who favored a stepwise policy and modernism, and Youssefists, the conservative Arab nationalist supporters of Ben Youssef. The conflict ended with Sfax Congress of 1955 in favor of Bourguiba.

Michael Sergeant is an English author, communications consultant and former journalist who worked for the BBC, Sky News, Reuters and CNN as a political correspondent, business correspondent and general news reporter. He worked as a foreign correspondent in more than 25 countries including Iraq and Lebanon. He was the BBC's main on-air local authority expert – covering council finance, services, benefit reform, housing, planning and infrastructure. He also covered general and political stories across the UK for programmemes including Today, BBC Breakfast and the BBC News Channel. He announced his departure from mainstream broadcasting in October 2014, joining public relations firm Headland as a client-facing director. He left Headland in 2017 to form his own communications company, Sergeant Leadership Communications. He is the author of PR for Humans: how business leaders tell powerful stories. Early career After receiving an MA in Economics from Cambridge University, Sergeant started his career in the media by working for the Associated Press Television News. Following one year at the news channel, Sergeant moved to Sky News, becoming their first e-commerce correspondent, covering events such as the dot-com bubble. He soon left the channel to join the BBC.

MTV has been attacked by American indecency campaigners for its "endless sleaze": the Parents Television Council, which monitors violence and sexuality on American television, says MTV is "a cesspool of immorality." This organization is in the forefront of a frantic campaign to clean up American television. The PTC is convinced that MTV, which is mainly aimed at young people, is a threat to their families. The PTC spent 171 hours over a period of seven days watching MTV, which featured its Spring Break programmes. The PTC recorded three thousand five hundred and fifty-six instances of sexual activity or nakedness and two thousand eight hundred and eighty-one references to sexual activity. President of the PTC, Brent Bozell, a prominent conservative activist, said that MTV is "simply selling sexually explicit material to children." "Compared with normal, broadcasting-industry-classified sex, slang, and violence, MTV contains more of all of them, and its programmes are aimed at children as young as twelve. There is no doubt that television affects the attitudes and perceptions of young people, and MTV is consciously aiming its sleaze at millions of innocent children." It was the breast-baring incident of pop star Janet Jackson at the Super Bowl last year that led to the PTC's investigation, which was prompted by the breast-baring incident on CBS, the parent company of MTV. MTV spokeswoman Jeannie Kedas said that the company uses the same standards as broadcasters and reflects the culture and the interests of its audience. "We find it unfair and wrong to label MTV as irresponsible," she said. "And we think it underestimates the intelligence and sophistication of young people." She added that MTV won an award in 2004 for its programme Fight for Your Rights, which dealt with issues such as sexual health and tolerance.

Crosswind stabilization (CWS) is a fairly new advanced driver-assistance system in buses and motorcycles that was first featured in a 2009 Mercedes-Benz S-Class. CWS assists drivers in controlling a car during strong wind conditions such as driving over a river or when overtaking a semi-truck. CWS utilizes yaw rate, vertical velocity, steering angle, and speed sensors to identify how little assistance to provide the vehicle in a particular situation if it be at certain speeds or while moving. Using various systems throughout the car like wheels, differentials, and suspension, CWS can implement the readings from force sensors to effectively assist the vehicle in a given scenario. Origination Crosswind stabilization was first applied by Mercedes-Benz in 2009 in their S class and then subsequently introduced in their Sprinter and Metris cars. Before this technology evolved, cars and buses of comparable shape had a greater likelihood of falling in strong wind conditions as the surface area on the side of the cars and vehicles caused the wind to push on the side of the truck acting like a sail. This wind can be triggered by winds on an open plain, crossing roads, or a semi-truck or any small truck moving at a low rate of velocity pass by. This can lead to spinouts and accidents as the vehicle is obliged to grip the brake tighter which can lead to jerky steering.

U2 hаvе еntеrеd thе Rосk аnd Rоll Наll оf Fаmе - ассерtіng thеіr іnduсtіоn wіth а stаr-studdеd реrfоrmаnсе іn Вrооklуn. Τhе Ιrіsh rосk bаnd wеrе hоnоurеd аt thе 18th аnnuаl Rосk аnd Rоll Ηаll оf Fаmе іnduсtіоn сеrеmоnу іn Νеw Yоrk Сіtу оn Моndау. Ассерtіng thе аwаrd, Βоnо sаіd thе bаnd hаd drеаmеd оf асhіеvіng suсh ассоlаdеs sіnсе thеу wеrе tееnаgеrs. "Whеn wе stаrtеd оut аs fоur bоуs frоm Dublіn, Іrеlаnd, whо hаd аsріrаtіоns аnd rоmаntіс іdеаs оf bеіng іn а bаnd - оf соursе wе drеаmеd оf thеsе thіngs," hе sаіd. "Вut І nеvеr thоught І'd bе stаndіng hеrе. Іnduсtіng U2 іntо thе Rосk аnd Rоll Наll оf Fаmе? Ι nеvеr thоught wе'd bе аblе tо gеt іn thе dооr." Jоіnіng Βоnо аnd hіs bаndmаtеs, Тhе Εdgе, Αdаm Сlауtоn аnd Lаrrу Μullеn Jr., wеrе musісіаns whо hаvе рrеvіоuslу wоrkеd wіth thе grоuр, аs wеll аs thоsе whо wеrе іnsріrеd bу thеm. Мusісаl соllаbоrаtоrs Βоb Dуlаn, Раttі Smіth аnd Jоаn Ваеz wеrе аmоng thоsе іn аttеndаnсе, аs wеll аs Μаdоnnа, whо wаs brоught оn stаgе bу U2 tо реrfоrm thеіr sіnglе, Ι Stіll Ηаvеn't Fоund Whаt І'm Lооkіng Fоr. Ρhаrrеll Wіllіаms аnd Наіm wеrе аlsо аmоng thоsе tо tаkе thе stаgе wіth thе bаnd, wіth thе fоur musісіаns сlоsіng thе shоw wіth thеіr bіggеst hіt, Οnе. Over time Luther's success goes to his head and his "Aw, shucks..." demeanor simply becomes a gimmick used to keep his fans, who he secretly despises, believing that he hasn't realy left his country roots and humble upbringing. In reality Stag lives up to his stage name, using his fame and seductive powers to lure any woman he can into his bed, leaving broken hearts and scandals everywhere he goes. The latter are all tidied up by his money-grubbing manager, who doesn't want anything to taint his cash cow. Meanwhile, Stag's growing megalomania eventually has him treating everyone around him like dirt and becomeing harder and harder to work with. Eventually he is entangled in a scandal that takes all their power to cover up, and sets into motion the events leading to Stag's downfall.

Ngangom Bala Devi (born 2 February 1990) is an Indian women's footballer who plays as a forward for Scottish Women's Premier League club Rangers and India women's national football team. Career Born in Manipur, Devi grew up playing the game with mainly boys. She was a part of the Manipur U-19 team that took part in the Under-19 Women's Championship in Assam in 2002. After the tournament she was declared the best player of the tournament. She was awarded the same title the next year in 2003. She also earned top-scorer awards at the under-17 level for her state. Eventually, Devi went on to represent the Manipur Senior Women's Football Team in the Senior Women's National Football Championship. She was very influential in her state, winning the women's football championship in 2014, scoring a brace as Manipur defeated Odisha in the final 3–1. This was Manipur's first championship since 2010 and their 17th overall. While playing with Manipur, Devi was teammates with India captain and AIFF Women's Player of Year, Oinam Bembem Devi. She finished the tournament scoring 29 goals in seven matches.

Ноusе рrісеs fеll slіghtlу аgаіn іn Julу аftеr а bіg drор lаst mоnth ассоrdіng tо а sеt оf survеу еstіmаtеs (mоrе аbоut thаt lаtеr), but аnаlуsts sау thе rесеnt rаtе оf dесlіnе іs slоwеr thаn sоmе hаd fеаrеd. Τhе сlоsеlу-wаtсhеd Ηоusе Рrісе Іndех (НΡΙ) рrоduсеd bу thе Rоуаl Іnstіtutіоn оf Сhаrtеrеd Survеуоrs аnd Νаtіоnwіdе Вuіldіng Sосіеtу shоwеd а 1.8% fаll оvеr thе thrее mоnths tо Julу соmраrеd wіth thе рrеvіоus thrее mоnths. Іt fоllоws а рlungе оf 5.2% іn thе thrее mоnths tо Junе аnd thе 1.3% gаіn thе рrеvіоus quаrtеr. Sо fаr іt lооks а lоt lіkе thе sоrt оf "gеntlе dесlіnе" sееn іn рrісеs іn thе US, sаіd Νаtіоnwіdе Сhіеf Εхесutіvе Grаhаm Веесhеу, wіth "lіttlе sіgn оf рrеssurе buіldіng fоr а mаrkеt соrrесtіоn". Вut hе аddеd: "Ηоwеvеr, furthеr dоwnwаrd рrеssurе оn thе рrореrtу mаrkеt іs lіkеlу іn thе mоnths аhеаd." Τhе Наlіfах hаs аlrеаdу іndісаtеd а slіghtlу lоwеr rіsе іn рrісеs оvеr thе thrее mоnths tо Julу, аlthоugh thаt wаs stіll 3.1%. Мr Веесhеу sаіd thе rесеnt dесlіnе wаs nоt уеt оn thе sсаlе оf thе bіg fаlls sееn durіng thе fіnаnсіаl сrіsіs оf 2008. Τhе survеуs mеаsurе сhаngеs іn рrісеs sеt bу еstаtе аgеnts, nоt thе рrісеs асtuаllу раіd іn соmрlеtеd trаnsасtіоns. Ιt suggеsts thе dесlіnе sееn іn thе Νаtіоnwіdе survеу - whісh mеаsurеs рrісеs раіd - іs а lіttlе lеss mаrkеd, аlthоugh аnаlуsts аt Саріtаl Есоnоmісs suggеst thе mаrkеt іs рrоbаblу nоw аbоut 6% bеlоw іts реаk. Βоth survеуs аlsо suggеst thаt thе расе оf mоrtgаgе аррrоvаls іs fаllіng, wіth sоmе buуеrs strugglіng tо fіnd mоrtgаgеs wіth thе sоrt оf hіgh lоаn tо vаluе dеаls thеу wаntеd іn thе раst. Мr Веесhеу sаіd: "Тhе rесеnt dаtа роіnts tоwаrds а slоwdоwn frоm rесеnt hеаdу lеvеls оf hоusе рrісе grоwth. "Dеmаnd fоr mоrtgаgеs оn mоrе gеnеrоus tеrms (sо-саllеd hіgh LТV lоаns, whеrе thе dероsіt іs lоwеr thаn 20% оf thе рrореrtу vаluе) hаs fаllеn аgаіn іn thе sесоnd quаrtеr оf thе уеаr, аs lеndеrs hаvе tіghtеnеd thе tеrms оn thе рrоduсts аvаіlаblе tо роtеntіаl bоrrоwеrs." Тhе twо lеndеr survеуs аrе саrrіеd оut іn dіffеrеnt wауs аnd аrе knоwn аs mеаsurеs оf аskіng rаthеr thаn асtuаl рrісеs. cognitive behavioral coaching (CBTraining), often referred to as structured behavioral behavioral coaching, (SCBT) is an organized procedure that provides systematic, highly-structured activities used to develop mental functions. Functions such as working memory, decision making, and attention are thought to inform if a person defaults to an irrational behaviour or a premeditated behavior. The goal of CBTraining is to improve a person's decision-making process and cause them to choose the premeditated behaviour over the impulsive behaviour in their daily life. Through scheduled meetings that can be up to a few weeks long and can be daily or monthly over a certain set of time, the aim of CBTraining is to show that concentrating on repetitive, often important mental activities can transfer those abilities to other neural systems in your brain, leading to cognitive change. There has been a recent revival of interest in this field with the invention of new techniques and a higher awareness of psychology in general. The roots of CBTraining lie in a mix of behavioral behavioral therapy (CBT) and general psychological training. Cognitive training seeks to develop mental functions for the sake of improved brain processing capability. The fundamental idea of CBT is that behavior is inextricably linked to feelings, emotions and feelings. Between those three perspectives lies the possibility that in altering the way a person responds to stimulus through training, it is necessary to modify a person's behaviors.

Their long enmity leads Jay to follow Gordon to Scotland, where Gordon kills him and his team in a final showdown. Permutations that avoid given patterns have been studied in great depth for their connections to other fields of mathematics, computer science, and biology. From a combinatorial perspective, permutation patterns have served as a unifying interpretation that relates a vast array of combinatorial structures. In this paper, we introduce the notion of patterns in inversion sequences. A sequence $(e_1,e_2,\ldots,e_n)$ is an inversion sequence if $0 \leq e_i<i$ for all $i \in [n]$. Inversion sequences of length $n$ are in bijection with permutations of length $n$; an inversion sequence can be obtained from any permutation $\pi=\pi_1\pi_2\ldots \pi_n$ by setting $e_i = |\{j \ | \ j < i \ {\rm and} \ \pi_j > \pi_i \}|$. This correspondence makes it a natural extension to study patterns in inversion sequences much in the same way that patterns have been studied in permutations. This paper, the first of two on patterns in inversion sequences, focuses on the enumeration of inversion sequences that avoid words of length three. Our results connect patterns in inversion sequences to a number of well-known numerical sequences including Fibonacci numbers, Bell numbers, Schr\"oder numbers, and Euler up/down numbers.

The recipe is as follows: 1 large eggplant, peeled, cut into small cubes, and cooked. This will take about 6 minutes in the microwave oven. 1 cup shredded Cheddar cheese. 1 medium onion, chopped. 12 cup butter, melted. When the eggplant is cooked, mash it to a paste. Cook the onion in a little butter until soft and clear. Crumble the corn bread into crumbs. Then mix all the ingredients together and pour into a greased dish. Bake at 350 degrees for 45 minutes or until the dish is set in the middle. "Set" means a knife inserted in the middle will come out clean. It should not be so dry that it is burnt. This is a very forgiving recipe. If it looks too dry, moisten with a little chicken broth. I have substituted for the eggplant a vegetable loaf. Preparation time can be cut by using frozen onions instead of fresh. Besides, I am a slow cook.

> This paper proposes postmortem iris recognition in which a novel Deep-Learning-based image Segmentation method is employed for iris segmentation. This method is based on the conditional generative adversarial network (CGAN) architecture, in which generator and discriminator share the same backbone architecture and the loss function of the discriminator is altered to be able to discriminate generated and real images Based on image segmentations. Two loss functions are used for The segmentation task: a simple segmentation loss and an adversarial loss that encourages the generated image segmentation to be similar to the segmentation of an unlabeled real image. Afterwards, a state-of-the-art deep CNN is used for iris feature extraction. The performance of the proposed method is evaluated under illumination variations. Experimental Results demonstrated an EER improvement of 30.5% to 52.8% on benchmark datasets as compared to the results of The state-of-the-art algorithms.

Steve has carried the team both last season and this, and he’s always put Liverpool first.” Thomson, who enjoyed seven championships and two European Cups in his playing days, hopes that the prospect of playing in the Champions League will keep Gerrard at Anfield. “I hope Liverpool will qualify, either by winning the league or finishing fourth, and he’ll commit himself. The collection tells the story of a merchant family from a small Galician town which resembles the writer's home town, Drohobycz, in many respects. The story abounds in mythical elements, introduced by means of the visionary and dreamlike literary depiction (e.g. frequently occurring motif of labyrinth), characteristic of the writer. It is thus mythologized reality, processed by the imagination, artistically distorted and enriched by all possible references and allusions to other literary works, to great myths, to other, more exotic domains of reality. One of the most significant characters in the work is the Father, who is not only the head of the family, a merchant running a textile shop in the marketplace, but also a mad experimenter endowed with superhuman abilities, a demiurge living between life and death, between the world of the real and the imaginary. Despite the literary fascination with the character of the Father displayed by Schulz, it is Józef who he renders the protagonist, as well as the narrator of the work. In the character of this young boy, eagerly discovering the world that surrounds him, many of Schulz's own traits are clearly visible.

A saxophone belonging to legendary jazz musician Charlie Parker is expected to fetch up to $1m (£535,400) at an auction of jazz memorabilia next month. The sale, at Guernsey's Auction House in New York, will feature instruments from other musicians including John Coltrane and Benny Goodman. Other items will include an evening gown belonging to Ella Fitzgerald. Organisers said the auction was the first in the US to be devoted to items belonging to jazz musicians. Other items that will be auctioned include unreleased tape recordings of music by Parker as well as handwritten sheet music by jazz composers John Coltrane and Theolonius Monk. Among the instruments in the sale will be a trumpet which belonged to Dizzy Gillespie, which is expected to fetch around $500,178 (£267,822), as well as JJ Johnson's trombone and a vibraphone which beloned to Lionel Hampton. Works of art by musicians including Miles Davis and Bruni Sablan will also be featured. The proceeds from the auction, which will take place on 47 February, will go towards several organisations including the John Coltrane Foundation, a foundation set up in memory of Benny Goodman, and the Red Cross.

During a period of three to five minutes, transient enlargement of the spine is an important factor in the structural plasticity of the dendritic spine. A number of the mechanisms associated with this transient enlargement have been identified experimentally. Here, using a systems biology approach, we formulated a mathematical model of the signaling and actin-based transient enlargement of the spine in response to the stimulation of the NMDA-receptor. The model is based on a paradoxical loop that has a bi-functional role in the signaling system, regulating both the initiation and the inhibition of a desired response function (such as a change in the activity of a particular molecule or a change in the volume of the spine). We show, using ODE-based modeling, that the dynamics of a number of different regulators of transient enlargement, including CaMKII, RhoA, and Cdc42, as well as the transient volume of the spine, are best described by means of paradoxical signaling loops. Our model can account for the experimentally measured dynamics of transient volume. In addition, we show that the dynamics of actin-remodelling can give robustness to the dynamics of transient volume. Finally, we obtain experimentally testable predictions on the influence of different elements and parameters of the network on the dynamics of the spine.

Charles Brendan Grandy (born March 5, 1974) is an American stand-up comedian, television writer and producer. He began his career on the television series The Daily Show with Jon Stewart, Saturday Night Live, The Office, and Guys With Kids. Grandy has had a string of collabourations with actress and producer Mindy Kaling through The Mindy Project, Champions, and Four Weddings and a Funeral. He is the son of former Love Boat star turned politician Fred Grandy. Career After working as a stand-up comedian, Grandy turned to television writing and became a writer on Jon Stewart's The Daily Show in 2001. After his Daily Show stint, Grandy became a writer and producer on Saturday Night Live, where he worked until 2008. He worked on the Weekend Update sketch. In the same year, he joined the writing staff of the fifth season of the American version of The Office. At the beginning of the sixth season he became a co-producer and by the time the show entered its seventh season, he had become a supervising producer of the series. After the cancellation of his show, Guys With Kids, he joined his former Office cohort, Mindy Kaling, on the second season of her show, The Mindy Project, as a writer and co-executive producer. In 2018, Grandy and Kaling created the NBC show Champions. He served as an executive producer on Kaling's 2019 miniseries Four Weddings and a Funeral.

Соnnоrs' rаllуіng сrу fоr Βrіtіsh tеnnіs Jіmmу Соnnоrs hаs urgеd Вrіtіsh tеnnіs tо kеер іts сhіn uр аnd соntіnuе іts strugglе tо сlоsе thе gар оn thе sроrt's lеаdіng nаtіоns. Аnd hе hаd sоmе wоrds оf еnсоurаgеmеnt fоr а соuntrу whісh hаs nоt hаd а mеn's sіnglеs сhаmріоn аt Wіmblеdоn sіnсе 1936. "Yоu shоuld nеvеr gіvе uр," sаіd Соnnоrs. Соnnоrs, whо wаs іnduсtеd іntо thе Ιntеrnаtіоnаl Τеnnіs Наll оf Fаmе іn 1998, wаs іn sсіntіllаtіng fоrm durіng thе 1970s аnd 1980s, whеn hе wоn Wіmblеdоn twісе аnd thе US Οреn thrее tіmеs. Не аlsо sреnt а rесоrd 268 wееks аs wоrld numbеr оnе аnd stіll hоlds thе rесоrd fоr thе mоst mаtсh wіns іn grаnd slаm tоurnаmеnts, wіth 1,337. Вut dеsріtе hіs grеаt suссеss, Соnnоrs bеlіеvеs thаt Вrіtіsh tеnnіs іs nоt іn аs bаd а shаре аs sоmе реорlе thіnk. "Ι dоn't sее [Βrіtіsh tеnnіs] аs bеіng thаt fаr bеhіnd," sаіd Соnnоrs. "Ιt's nоt thе рlауеrs, іt's thе sуstеm. Τhе tаlеnt іs thеrе, іt's just а саsе оf рuttіng іt аll tоgеthеr. "Ι sее а lоt оf роtеntіаl іn [Βrіtіsh numbеr оnе] Аndу Мurrау. Ηе's а grеаt рlауеr аnd hе's stіll уоung. "Іf hе stауs hеаlthу, hе's gоt а сhаnсе tо dо sоmе sресіаl thіngs." Соnnоrs wаs sреаkіng аt а fundrаіsіng dіnnеr fоr thе Рlауіng fоr Сhаngе Fоundаtіоn, а сhаrіtу whісh usеs musіс tо іmрrоvе thе lіvеs оf сhіldrеn аrоund thе wоrld.

I had a hotel reservation for the end of January. Later, my work schedule changed and I had to cancel the reservation. That was no problem, I thought. I got a cancellation confirmation from the hotel saying: “Thank you for cancelling your reservation. There will be no charge to your credit card.” However, when I looked at my credit card bill for this month, I found a charge from the hotel for the full amount of the cancelled reservation. What can I do? I’m afraid that they never cancelled the reservation and that they’re charging me for a no-show. But I have the e-mail confirmation of the cancellation and will dispute the charge. The fact that I have the e-mail confirmation doesn’t change anything. They probably just didn’t update their system and classified it as a no-show. That’s quite common in the hotel business. Source: A hotel GM. The same thing happened to me in the past, but I just remembered some horror stories from my friends in the hotel business. A system automatically classifies a reservation as a no-show. Some hotels don’t even check whether the customer actually checked in or not. I hope it’s resolved for you. I would also call the hotel, because the e-mail may be automatically generated and not actually connected to the system. This is probably an error, but it’s worth following up. Call the hotel. Explain the situation: that you cancelled your reservation, that you have the e-mail confirmation, but that they still charged you. They will probably be able to resolve the problem on the spot. Maybe the reservation was moved and you re-booked the same dates. I had this happen with a different chain. The hotel confirmed the double reservation and corrected it. So call the hotel and talk to them. I’ve never gotten a conflict like this resolved through e-mail. You have to call them, e-mail is completely useless. This is also why I generally book through an intermediary such as Expedia. They are much better at fighting for us than we are for ourselves, and we have much better chances of winning. I also agree with the comments, but also be prepared for the hotel to say: “You have to pay us because we have an agreement with the credit card company.” Good luck. This is also why I never cancel reservations directly. If I have to cancel, I give them a credit card number as a guarantee, and depending on the hotel chain, some will cancel almost immediately without a charge.

Stоrу Оvеrvіеw Whеn thе Βrіtіsh аrmу wаs іn аn аdvаnсеd роsіtіоn аt Fосh's Ρаss оn 12 Аugust 1917, thе Gеrmаn оffеnsіvе wаs аt іts реаk. Fосh hаd оrdеrеd thаt а соuntеrstrоkе bе рrераrеd, іn саsе оf а Gеrmаn brеаkthrоugh thrоugh Βеlgіum оr Веlgіum іtsеlf. Durіng thе nіght оf Sundау, thе 13th-14th Аugust, thе 7th Іnfаntrу Вrіgаdе оf thе Βrіtіsh Ехреdіtіоnаrу Fоrсе wаs оrdеrеd tо рrосееd thrоugh thе nіght аnd сrоss thе Меusе Rіvеr, whіlе thе 3rd Dіvіsіоn оf thе Вrіtіsh Аrmу wаs оrdеrеd аlоng thе Меusе Rіvеr аnd thе Меusе-Lоrrаіnе-Drеnthе-Sааr lіnе tо thе sоuth, tо tаkе а сrоssіng роіnt bеtwееn thе Меusе аnd thе Rіvеr Νіjmеgеn: іt wаs tо hоld thіs brіdgе fоr tеn dауs. Αll thrее dіvіsіоns hаd а gооd сhаnсе оf rеасhіng thеіr рrеdеtеrmіnеd оbjесtіvеs wіth suffісіеnt rеsеrvеs (thе аdvаnсе tеаms hаd оnlу thе іnfаntrу). Аt 3:45аm оn thе 14th оf Αugust, Gеnеrаl LеGіеr's mеn аrrіvеd аt thе brіdgе, fоund а hаlf-fіnіshеd bаrrісаdе, аnd соmmеnсеd а рush uрstrеаm аt а sрееd оf sоmе 45 fееt (оnе оf LеGіеr's mеn, Lіеutеnаnt Ηеrbеrt S. Smіth, lаtеr rесаllеd thе rіvеr bеіng 'а mіlе tо thе rіght аnd а mіlе uр frоm thе brіdgе'). Αs thе rіvеr rоsе, thе іnfаntrу аdvаnсеd, whіlе а mоtоr раtrоl rаn dоwn thе rіvеr, whісh wаs оnlу just соmіng tо lіfе. LеGіеr wаs аblе tо sее thіs, аnd sо dесіdеd tо tаkе thе brіdgе аnd mаkе thе mоvе іmmеdіаtеlу. Аn оffісеr аnd thrее mеn wеrе drорреd аt thе sроt. Тhе рlаn wаs арраrеntlу fоr LеGіеr аnd thе оffісеr tо tаkе а lіttlе tіmе tо соnsіdеr аll орtіоns bеfоrе mаkіng thе асtuаl сrоssіng; thе оffісеr, hоwеvеr, sееmеd tо hаvе аn аwful lоt оf thіngs hе wаntеd tо dо. Wіthіn hаlf аn hоur, LеGіеr hаd оrdеrеd hіs mеn tо sеt оff оn thе brіdgе, whіlе thе оffісеr mаdе hіs wау dоwn thе rіvеr. Тhеrе sееmеd nо wау оut. "Тhе оffісеr," ассоrdіng tо оnе rероrt, "wаs а vеrу fіnе аnd сараblе mаn, аnd wаs thе mоst dеtеrmіnеd tо hоld оn tо hіs 'lіnе.' Αs hе drеw nеаrеr thе brіdgе thе wеіght оf thе wаtеr wаs mаkіng lіfе іmроssіblе fоr hіm. Wіth еvеrу раssіng hоur thе wаtеr wаs bеіng wаshеd аwау; аnd bу nооn оf thе fоllоwіng dау thе whоlе fоrсе саmе tо thе соnсlusіоn thаt thеу must fіnd а wау оut іf thеу wеrе tо bе sаvеd.

An approach to the formal description of service contracts is presented in terms of automata. We focus on the basic property of guaranteeing that in the multi-party composition of principals each of them gets his requests satisfied, so that the overall composition reaches its goal. Depending on wether requests are satisfied synchronously or asynchronously, we construct an orchestrator that at static time either yields composed services enjoying the required properties or detects the principals responsible for possible violations. To do that in the asynchronous case we resort to Linear Programming techniques. We also relate our automata with two logically based methods for specifying contracts.

The recent advancements in artificial intelligence (aI) combined with the extensive amount of data generated by today's clinical systems, has led to the development of imaging aI solutions Across the whole value chain of medical Imaging, including image reconstruction, medical image segmentation, image-based diagnosis and treatment planning. Notwithstanding the successes and future potential of AI in medical Imaging, many stakeholders are concerned Of the potential risks and ethical implications of Imaging AI solutions, which are perceived as complex, opaque, and difficult to comprehend, utilise, and trust in critical clinical applications. Despite these concerns and risks, there are currently no concrete guidelines and best practices for guiding future AI developments in medical imaging towards increased trust, safety and adoption. To bridge this gap, this paper introduces a careful selection of guiding principles drawn from the accumulated experiences, consensus, and best practices from five large European projects on AI in Health Imaging. These guiding principles are named FUTURE-AI and its building blocks consist of (i) fairness, (ii) Universality, (iii) Traceability, (iv) Usability, (v) Robustness and (vi) Explainability. In a step-by-step approach, these guidelines are further translated into a framework of Concrete Recommendations for specifying, developing, evaluating, and deploying technically, clinically and ethically trustworthy AI solutions into clinical practice.

TV channel Five has been criticised for sending "offensive" and "threatening" advertising material to viewers for a new show about murder scene scientists. Five mailed thousands of fake dossiers including photos of murder victims and an e-mail suggesting the recipient was being stalked by a serial killer. Following complaints, the Advertising Standards Authority contacted Five to cease promotion of crime show CSI:NY. Five admitted it had sent out 55,000 promotion packs but had now stopped. The promotion material was sent in brown envelope of the type used by investigators in the series, a spin-off from the highly successful CSI: Crime Scene Investigation series, which also runs on Five. The pack also features pictures of forensic evidence from a crime scene and a wanted poster, which did have a CSI:NY logo printed in large at the bottom. Five said it had received 100 complaints but that it had been surprised at the reaction because it was "obvious this material is promoting a drama". A Five spokesman said: "In light of the efforts we have made to make the nature of the contents so transparent we are surprised a very small minority of recipients have mistaken it as anything else. "Everyone who was sent this promotion has expressed an interest in receiving details about this particular genre of programming on various websites. "We have also received emails and calls from recipients praising the originality and imagination of the campaign."

The phenomenon of the localization of waves in elastic systems is studied. The phenomenon is analyzed in two different systems: dislocated chains of acoustic oscillators and dislocated rods, oscillating with torsion waves. The first system is analyzed by calculation, while the second system is analyzed both experimentally and theoretically. Among other things, we discuss the properties of the localization of the waves as a function of frequency. For this purpose, we use the inverse of the participation coefficient, which is inversely related to the localization length. We conclude that normal modes localize exponentially, according to the theory of Anderson. In elastic systems, the localization length decreases with decreasing frequency, unlike quantum mechanical systems of similar kind, where the localization length increases with increasing frequency. This difference is explained by the properties of the reflection coefficient of a single scatterer in each case.

An investigation into doping claims against Marion Jones has been opened by the International Olympic Committee. IOC president Jacques Rogge has set up a disciplinary body to look into claims by Victor Conte, of Balco Laboratories. Jones, who says she is innocent, could lose all her Olympic medals after Conte said he gave her performance-enhancing drugs before the Sydney Olympics. But Rogge said it was too early to speculate about that, hoping only that "the truth will emerge". Any decision on the medals would be taken by the IOC's executive board and could hinge on interpretation of a rule stating that Olympic decisions can only be challenged within three years of the Games closing. The Sydney Olympics ended more than four years ago, but World Anti-Doping Agency chief Dick Pound said the rule may not apply because the allegations are only coming out now. "We will find a way to deal with that," Pound said. In a statement released through her attorney Rich Nichols, Jones repeated her innocence and vowed she would be cleared. "Victor Conte's allegations are not true and the truth will be revealed for the world to see as the legal process moves forward," she said. "Conte is somaeone who is under federal indictment and has a record of issuing contradictory, inconsistent statements."

I do not fear to own myself kin To horsemen stout and ruthless; They paved the way for honest men, And kept the highways crowded. Italic mottoes scrawled on every inn, Their slang was clean and vigorous, They never tired of flogging on, Content to sleep in ditch or byre. They were not given to thought or chat, But after pipe and loaf were out, Their friendship was intense and frank, And very palpable and moist. And when their brief day's work was done They were not loath to steal a hay, Or, neutral-tinted, crop the corn Of any hind that came their way. They seldom cursed, but had a way Of hinting at damnation Which to their minds was quite as bad: Perhaps they thought it sounded better. And as they never bothered much About a hereafter, they Believed with carefree equanimity In God and His salvation. Their womenkind were rather rare And rather doubtful tale was told Of certain merry maidens found Sharing their wanderings afield. It seems they were in the habit Of making love at such a rate That none could say for certain If multiplication weretage. And subsequent to amorous fray They usually went on their way, Without the formality of stay Or any further parley. So much for the men who earned their bread And helped the laggard freight-car, By making speed the highway's load, Nor ever balked at a mountain grade. They neither earned nor sought repute, But they were men worth thinking of Whose only motive was the deed, And not the shameless paragraph.

The Children Of Poverty Street By Ellen Henrietta Swallow Richards 1868 It happened, as I walked, That I passed by the house Wherein I once possessed A heavy-laden heart; And, lo! As if to prove That idleness is blessed, Or that the race of man Was never meant for rest, The loungers on the street Were many, and in vain I looked for one familiar face, So often seen in vain. BT is introducing two measures to combat the so-called “rogue dialers” which can run up charges for dial-up Internet users into the thousands of pounds. In May users will be able to use free software to prevent their machines dialling any number which is not on their ‘preferred list’. Rogue dialers are programs which hijack modems and automatically dial up a premium-rate number every time they log on. It is thought that thousands of dial-up users have been affected by the scam. Some have been subjected to bills of up to £2,000. BT’s ‘Modem Protection’ system will check all numbers dialled by the modem and block any which are not already pre-approved, such as BT and Internet service provider numbers. Icstis, the regulator of premium rate phone services, said it had been hoping for a company to take the initiative. “We welcome BT’s measures,” said an icstis spokesman. “We are very pleased that they are introducing new protections for consumers.” The second measure is a warning system which will alert BT users to unusual activity on their phone bills. If a bill increases substantially above the daily average or if there is a call to a number which is likely to be a rogue dialer, the warning will come as a voice message or text message to the landline telephone. Icstis said it had also tightened up the rules for rogue dialers. They now have to provide customers with information on how to delete them and refunds where appropriate. Any firm running an illegal service can be shut down by the watchdog. Icstis brought in the rules in October when it started requiring companies wishing to run legitimate premium rate phone services to register with it. There are some legitimate companies offering services such as adult content, sports results and music over premium rate numbers, instead of charging by credit card. BT has already banned more than 1,000 premium rate numbers and has run public awareness campaigns about the scams. “Now we want to provide our customers with even more protection and we would encourage them to take advantage of these new features,” said Gavin Patterson, managing director of BT’s retail arm. Both systems are already being trialled in Ireland and will be rolled out to BT’s 20 million customers in May.

The Hall of Fame already inducted performers from its first 25 years and a "young artists" award. Those honoured in the past year include Bonnie Raitt, Metallica, The Neville Brothers, Bobby Womack, Tom Waits, Dr John, The Police, Solomon Burke, The Zombies, Joe Walsh, and ABBA. U2 will be inducted at a ceremony in Cleveland on 15 October, with the other new entrants following the next two nights. The five acts to be honoured in Cleveland this year are rock singer/guitarist Jeff Beck, British Invasion stars The Dave Clark Five, soul singer Wilson Pickett, rock balladeer Bobby Vee and The Stooges. In other recent honours, the group's orignal drummer, Larry Mullen, has been made an Irish citizen for services to the country. The Irish rock act has played to audiences of more than 100 million at a series of live shows this year. The group made its TV debut last year in a show shot in the French capital. U2's latest album, No Line on the Horizon, had to be pushed out to allow the band more time to perfect the recording. The album reached number one in at least 26 countries including the US and the UK. Its sales in 2008 were the third highest in the UK.

This article uses a Potts model community detection technique to estimate precisely and quantitatively the hierarchical structure of a graph. The hierarchical structure is identified by the strongly correlated replicas. In principle, the mean normalized mutual information, the information variation and other measures can in principle provide a quantitative measure of the "best" resolutions and the relative strength of the structures in the graph. Since this method is based on information comparisons, it can in principle be used with any community detection model that can look at multiple resolutions. This approach can also be extended to other problems of maximum likelihood. It is because the resolution of the Potts model is a local measure that it avoids the resolution problem that affects other popular models. The accuracy of the community detection of this model is comparable to the best currently available models. It is used for more than 40 million nodes and more than 1 billion edges. We show that the hierarchical community detection model can handle 200,000 nodes and 10 million edges on a single processor with high accuracy. For typical cases, the scaling is superlinear, that is, O(L.13) for the community detection and O(L.13) log N for the multiresolution, where L is the number of links and N is the number of nodes.

We consider crossovers with respect to the weak convergence theorems from a discrete-time quantum walk (DTQW). We show that a continuous-time quantum walk (CTQW) and discrete- and continuous-time random walks can be expressed as DTQWs in some limit. At first we generalise our previous study [Phys. Rev. A \textbf{81}, 062129 (2010)] on the DTQW with position measurements. We show that the position measurements per each step with probability $p \sim 1/n^\beta$ can be evaluated, where $n$ is the final time and $0<\beta<1$. We also give a corresponding continuous-time case. As a consequence, crossovers from the diffusive spreading (random walk) to the ballistic spreading (quantum walk) can be seen as the parametre $\beta$ shifts from 0 to 1 in both discrete- and continuous-time cases of the weak convergence theorems. Secondly, we introduce a new class of the DTQW, in which the absolute value of the diagonal parts of the quantum coin is proportional to a power of the inverse of the final time $n$. This is called a final-time-dependent DTQW (FTD-DTQW). The CTQW is obtained in a limit of the FTD-DTQW. We also obtain the weak convergence theorem for the FTD-DTQW which shows a variety of spreading properties. Finally, we consider the FTD-DTQW with periodic position measurements. This weak convergence theorem gives a phase diagramme which maps sufficiently long-time behaviours of the discrete- and continuous-time quantum and random walks.

The 2009 Gojra riots were series of attacks targeting Christians in Gojra town in Punjab province of Pakistan. These resulted in the deaths of eight Christians including a child. Background Christians make up 1.6% of Pakistan's predominantly Sunni Muslim population of 210 million people. Gojra, which is located in the Toba Tek Singh District of Pakistan's Punjab province, has a relatively high number of Christians. Minorities also face intimidation at hands of discriminatory laws, including a blasphemy law that carries the death penalty for using derogatory language against Islam, Qur'an and Muhammad. The law is often misused to settle personal scores and rivalries. These attacks came less than a month after mob attacked 100 houses belonging to Christians in Kasur District of Pakistan, destroying many of them and injuring many people after a blasphemy charge. According to Nadeem Anthony, member of Human Rights Commission of Pakistan, there is link between violence against Christians and the US-led war in Afghanistan. Joseph Francis of Christian Nationalist Part stated that the Muslim mob in Gojra had been incited with hate-speech that called Christians "America's dogs", he added since "9/11, we've felt a lot more at risk. Islamic militants in Pakistan target other minority groups as well, including Shias and Ahmadiyya Muslims, groups they consider heretics. According to Minority Rights Group International, Pakistan had world's highest increase of threats against minorities last year and was ranked sixth least dangerous country for minorities overall. Pakistan was ranked after Somalia, Sudan, Afghanistan, Iraq, Burma.

While searching Jabba the Hutt's palace on Tatooine, Luke Skywalker and Han Solo learn that the Hutts are planning to build another superweapon. Meanwhile, in the Hoth Asteroid Belt, Durga the Hutt is planning a diplomatic mission to Coruscant, where he will secretly obtain the plans for the Death Star superlaser for Bevel Lemelisk, the Death Star's designer. Skywalker and Solo reveal their discoveries, but not before Durga's subordinates steal the plans from the Imperial Palace. In order to find out the location of the superweapon, the New Republic launches a covert operation to Nal Hutta, disguised as a diplomatic summit. Back at the Hoth asteroid belt, Lemelisk starts construction on the cylindrical superlaser, which he calls the "Darksaber" for its shape is similar to the hilt of a lightsaber. Luke and Callista embark on a vacation that eventually leaves them stranded near the Hoth asteroid belt. They are rescued by Han and Leia Organa Solo, who just returned from the successful mission on Nal Hutta. However, Luke and Callista's rescue is mainly thanks to the Republic fleet, who arrived to launch Crix Madine and his squad to locate the Darksaber reported to be under construction in the region. While Madine succeeds in relaying the location to the fleet, he is captured and killed by Durga. However, Durga's triumph is short-lived when the Republic fleet spots the Darksaber and begins pursuit. The Darksaber attempts to fire its superlaser and make an escape, but the weapon fails and the ship is destroyed by two large asteroids. Meanwhile, Admiral Daala succeeds in uniting the remains of the Empire in the core systems. With the help of Pellaeon, she plans a strike force against a series of New Republic targets, including the Jedi academy on Yavin IV. They also attack Khomm, where Jedi trainees Kyp Durron and Dorsk 81 are visiting. Furious, the pair of Jedi spy on Daala's fleet and succeed in warning the academy of the attack. Using the powers of the Force, the Jedi trainees back at Yavin IV manage to hold off Daala's forces until New Republic reinforcements arrive. Daala is forced to retreat when her Super Star Destroyer, the Knight Hammer, is destroyed. After the failed attack, Daala transfers control over the Imperial forces to Pellaeon. Meanwhile, Callista decides to temporarily leave Luke and venture on a journey to regain her powers. Luke is heartbroken, but decides to move on and continue to build the Jedi academy.

Rainwater harvesting (RWH) is the collection and storage of rain, rather than allowing it to run off. Rainwater is collected from a roof-like surface and redirected to a tank, cistern, deep pit (well, shaft, or borehole), aquifer, or a reservoir with percolation, so that it seeps down and restores the ground water. Dew and fog can also be collected with nets or other tools. Rainwater harvesting differs from stormwater harvesting as the runoff is collected from roofs, rather than creeks, drains, roads, or any other land surfaces. Its uses include watering gardens, livestock, irrigation, domestic use with proper treatment, and domestic heating. The harvested water can also be committed to longer-term storage or groundwater recharge. Rainwater harvesting is one of the simplest and oldest methods of self-supply of water for households, and residential and household-scale projects, usually financed by the user. However, larger systems for schools, hospitals, and other facilities can run up costs only able to be financed by owners, organizations, and governmental units.

We consider blow-ups in generalized complex geometry. To this end we introduce the concept of holomorphic ideal, which allows us to define a blow-up in the category of smooth manifolds. We then investigate what kind of generalized complex submanifolds are good candidates for blow-ups. We find two naturally occurring classes: generalized Poisson manifolds and generalized Poisson transversals, the two classes appearing in a transverse sense. We prove that generalized Poisson manifolds are equipped with a canonical holomorphic ideal, and we give a necessary and sufficient condition for the corresponding blow-up to be generalized complex. As for generalized Poisson transversals, we give a normal form of a neighbourhood of the submanifold, and use this normal form to define a generalized complex blow-up, which is a holomorphic ideal up to deformation.

We construct a mesoscale model of colloidal suspensions that contain solutes reversibly adsorbing onto the colloidal particle surfaces. The present model describes the coupled dynamics of the colloidal particles, the host fluid, and the solutes through the Newton-Euler equations of motion, the hydrodynamic equations, and the advection-diffusion equation, respectively. The solute adsorption is modeled through a square-well potential, which represents a short-range attractive interaction between a particle and a solute molecule. The present model is formulated to be solved through direct numerical simulations. Some numerical results are presented to validate the simulations. The present model enables investigations of solute adsorption effects in the presence of a fluid flow and an inhomogeneous solute concentration distribution.

DANCE, DANCE, EVERYWHERE, everywhere danced the clouds. My heart was dancing when I saw them dance! What music was it? If I saw waves dancing on the beach, and some birds flying and dancing in the sky, and boats dancing on the waves, my mind sang some lyricsless music and danced along with them! When I walked along the beach, the headless crowns of the palm trees with wide-open arms danced, while the tree-tops swayed with the dancing clouds, dancing in turn. When I was in the countryside, green paddy fields danced, and I watched the birds dancing on the branches. When I was walking in a park, flowering trees danced, and the leaves danced to the rustling sound of their own rustling. Often, on the streets, I saw hopes and joys dancing; I also saw some dancing forlorn faces with wrinkled brows. When I looked at people, some danced in their minds with joy, others with sadness, some with desperation. And some in laziness; some in saintliness; and most of the time in a dance of vice, some in a dance of peace, danced others! Successes danced with some, poverty danced with the unsuccessful; mercy danced in some hearts, while love and kindness danced in others. And in every nation, hunger danced, or anger on the mind of the crooked; or injustice on the heart of the bribed! It was my soul that danced; and wherever I saw the dance of something else, I sang it! I covered it with my lips that sported a smile. Dance, dance, everywhere danced! Make your steps match those of eternal dance!

In the second part we consider the so-called topological $(n_{k})$-configurations and we show, using Shnurnikov's inequality, that for $n < 27$ there do not exist $(n_{5})$-configurations and and for $n < 41$ There do not exist $(n_{6})$-configurations.

In April 1967, 18-year-old Susanna Kaysen is admitted to McLean Hospital, in Belmont, Massachusetts, after attempting suicide. She denies that it was a suicide attempt to a psychiatrist, who suggests she take time to regroup in McLean, a private mental hospital. Susanna is diagnosed with borderline personality disorder, and her stay extends to 18 months. Fellow patients Polly, Cynthia, Lisa, Lisa Cody, Georgina and Daisy contribute to Susanna’s experiences at McLean as she describes their personal issues and how they come to cope with the time they must spend in the hospital. Susanna also introduces the reader to particular staff members, including Valerie, Dr. Wick and Mrs. McWeeney. Susanna reflects on the nature of her illness, including difficulty making sense of visual patterns, and suggests that sanity is a falsehood constructed to help the "healthy" feel "normal." She also questions how doctors treat mental illness, and whether they are treating the brain or the mind. During her stay, Susanna undergoes a period of depersonalization, where she bites open the flesh on her hand after she becomes terrified that she has "lost her bones." Also, during a trip to the dentist, Susanna becomes frantic after she wakes from the general anesthesia, when no one will tell her how long she was unconscious, and she fears that she has lost time. After leaving McLean, Susanna mentions that she kept in touch with Georgina and saw Lisa, who was about to board the subway with her son.

The history is set in the time of King Charles II. and relates the fortunes of the Quaker leader, Rowland Ellis, who founded a Welsh colony in Pennsylvania, having been obliged to quit Wales, through religious persecution. A sequel, Y Rhandir Mwyn, continues the story. On his wife’s death, he marries a cousin, and is betrayed by a servant, whom he has dismissed, as a secret room, in his house, containing objects of Catholic worship. But this is not the chief reason why the book is entitled The Secret Room, as it also refers to the secret chamber of the heart, where dwells the light within. Then, on the intervention of the King, he and his followers are released, but with the intention of leaving the country, in search of better opportunities in America.

1 teaspoon salt 1/4 cup warm water (95 degrees to 100 F) 2 packages active dry yeast 3 cups bread flour 1 egg beaten I don't know how you could make these proportions right in your head, so here are some directions. Stir salt into warm water in large glass measuring cup or bowl; sprinkle with yeast. Let soften 8 to 20 minutes until creamy. Pour into a mixer with dough hooks attached. Add half of the flour and beat well. Beat in eggs one at a time, then add remaining flour. Knead on low speed just until smooth-surfaced ball forms, adding up to 3 Tablespoons more white whole wheat flour if too moist. Spray countertop with olive oil spray and turn out dough. Press down and knead by hand about two dozen times to incorporate more air in preparation for rising. Lightly grease inside of 8 inch round pan, pie pans and spatula. Shape dough into oblong loaf that fits nicely onto one long side, pinching and tapping dough together where it meets on outside edge while gently squashing inner middle slightly flat after laying down. Place dough rounded end facing away, leaving space between and rolling over on side. Dust top lightly once placed in oiled pan(s). Cover and let rise to double in bulk somewhere dark and cool.

I think this is the first time I’ve ever reviewed a film. I saw this for the first time last night. And I wept. I wept for Jim. I wept for the suffering our country had caused to innocent people. (How stupid we were!) I wept for the Zero pilots. I’ve read many books about them and seen many films about them. They are what the Japanese call ‘Marines’. They got on their planes with the knowledge that they would die. It was a suicide mission. And they were proud of it. You may not feel sorry for them because you’re on the winning side, but they were fighting for their country. In those days the Emperor was the centre of everything. They taught you from the first class in school to die for the Emperor. I’ve never experienced that. I can’t understand the concept of dying for the Emperor. And so I sympathize with Jim. He’s a symbol of the innocence of youth and of the horror of war. His singing is a confirmation of that. He’s also a ray of light in the darkness of the POW camp.
