Background: Cardiac MRI derived biventricular mass and function parametres, such as end-systolic volume (ESV), end-diastolic volume (EDV), ejection fraction (EF), stroke volume (SV), and ventricular mass (VM) are clinically well established. Image segmentation can be challenging and time-consuming, due to the complex anatomy of the human heart. Objectives: This study introduces $\nu$-net (/nju:n$\varepsilon$t/) -- a deep learning approach allowing for fully-automated high quality segmentation of right (RV) and left ventricular (LV) endocardium and epicardium for extraction of cardiac function parametres. Methods: A set consisting of 253 manually segmented cases has been used to train a deep neural network. Subsequently, the network has been evaluated on 4 different multicentre data sets with a total of over 1000 cases. Results: For LV EF the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) is 98, 95, and 80 % (95 %), and for RV EF 96, and 87 % (80 %) on the respective data sets (human expert ICCs reported in parenthesis). The LV VM ICC is 95, and 94 % (84 %), and the RV VM ICC is 83, and 83 % (54 %). This study proposes a simple adjustment procedure, allowing for the adaptation to distinct segmentation philosophies. $\nu$-net exhibits state of-the-art performance in terms of dice coefficient. Conclusions: Biventricular mass and function parametres can be determined reliably in high quality by applying a deep neural network for cardiac MRI segmentation, especially in the anatomically complex right ventricle. Adaption to individual segmentation styles by applying a simple adjustment procedure is viable, allowing for the processing of novel data without time-consuming additional training.

This paper describes a variational approach for combining hyperspectral and multispectral images. The fusion is formulated as an inverse problem, the solution of which represents the target image in a low-dimensional subspace. The regularization term is carefully designed, and relies on a scene decomposition into a set of dictionaries. The dictionaries, and their support in the active spectral regions, are obtained from the observed images. Using these dictionaries and supports, the fusion problem is solved by alternating optimization of the target image (using the alternating direction method of multipliers) and the coding coefficients. The simulations show the performance of the proposed method when compared with the state-of-the-art.

Most areas in the United States saw economic growth continue in December and the beginning of January, the Federal Reserve said in its most recent Beige Book. Of the 12 regions it classified, 11 had more and better economic growth and only the Cleveland region showed mixed performance. In December, consumption was up compared to November and was up compared to last year's Christmas. The employment situation also improved, the Fed said. "The labor market strengthened in several districts, but wage growth was generally modest," the Beige Book said. "Several regions reported higher prices for building materials and inputs to manufacturing, while most reported stable or slightly higher overall price levels." In addition, residential real estate activity continued to grow strongly, while commercial real estate activity improved in most regions. Office leasing was particularly lively in Washington and New York City, two of the nation's strongest commercial markets.

The growing complexity and amount of scientific production have made it difficult for scientists to keep track of the latest developments in their own disciplines. Combined with the growing importance of online scientific communities, this situation calls for effective information-sorting tools. We propose a method to jointly determine the reputation of a community and the quality of the scientific objects published on this community. Testing with artificially generated data and with real data from the Econophysics Forum shows which variants of the method perform best. In particular, we show that if the method is extended to include author reputation, the resulting top papers have higher citation numbers and the top authors have higher H-indexes than the top papers and authors chosen by other methods.

1 cup all-purpose flour 1/2 cup milk 1/2 cup water 2 eggs 2 tablespoons butter, melted 1/8 teaspoon salt 1/4 teaspoon vanilla extract 3 tablespoons white sugar Melt the butter in a medium size skillet. The recruiter called today for my oldest child. I politely told him ''She's not interested.'' He promised she would have college paid for, a very slim chance of being sent to war, and the pride of being a soldier. I informed him of her interest in criminal justice. I let him know she is going to college and we will figure out how to finance it. He sang me the praises of the Military Police. Told me of how proud she would be and how proud I should be if she chose this path. He explained how if she was working on a degree she could not be sent into active duty on dangerous lands. But, in his next breath he told me how she would get her degree in a much faster pace than in a traditional college setting. I declined interest while I pretended to write the number he left for my daughter. I did tell her about his phone call but I also told her why I hope she doesn't choose to be a soldier. Is my greediness with my childs life a sin? I know ''somebody has to do it''... but, I can't bare the thought of my child being sent to fight in a war. I realize this is probably very un-patriotic. For that, I'm sorry. I have lost many things in my lifetime. My childs life is not one of those things I wish to sacrifice for the good of my country. I love my country but, I love my children more. **I respect all the soldiers who are willing to fight for their countries. My Grandfather, Father, and Husband have all fought in wars. I am very proud of them all. I am not disrespecting soldiers. I'm just sharing my feelings....I'm not at all claiming they are the ''right'' way to feel. Sincerely, Mary

Harrow Borough Football Club is an English non-league football club based in Harrow, London. Founded in 1863, they are managed by Anthony Howell and play Their Home games at earls Hall Stadium, Which has a capacity of 7,035 spectators. The team's nickname is the Bees. The early years of the clubs history were relatively unremarkable Until 2009 when a £400,000 move from Headstone Lane to Earls Hall stadium saw them return to non-conference level football following their relegation from the National League South and forced sale of Wembley Stadium Link to North East London NHS Trust for millions of pounds after it was found to be Unsafe. Eighteen former Enron board members have agreed to pay $168 million (89 million pounds) in a settlement of the lawsuit brought by shareholders over the collapse of the energy company. The lawsuit, which is headed by the University of California, will go to court next week. Enron went bust in 2001 after hiding hundreds of millions of dollars in debt. Before its collapse, it was the seventh largest company in the United States in terms of turnover. The collapse sent a shock through the financial markets and has damaged the confidence of investors in the business community. ”The settlement is a significant step because it means that these outside directors are held responsible to a certain extent,” said Mr. William Lerach, the lawyer leading the lawsuit against Enron. ” It is hoped that it will send a message to the boardrooms that it is essential that directors carry out their legal duties,” he added. In the settlement, which is worth $168 million, which is guaranteed by insurance, the directors will not be accused of any wrongdoing. The settlement is the fourth major deal negotiated by lawyers for shareholders, who filed a lawsuit against Enron almost three years ago. With the new agreement, more than $500 million has been recovered for shareholders. But in the latest agreement, former Enron chiefs Ken Lay and Jeff Skilling are not involved. Both men are facing criminal charges for their alleged misconduct in the collapse of the company. The agreement also does not involve Andrew Fastow, the former chief financial officer, who pleaded guilty to conspiracy when he was the group’s chief financial officer. And the shareholders’ lawsuit continues against a long list of other big companies, including JP Morgan Chase, Citigroup, Merrill Lynch and Credit Suisse First Boston. The University of California said the case is due to go to trial in October. It joined the lawsuit in December 2001, alleging massive fraud and insider dealing after losing $145 million on its investment in Enron.

There are two main protagonists and two main antagonists. The protagonists are Koot Hoomie "Kootie" Parganas and Pete "Teet" Sullivan. Kootie is an eleven-year old boy and Sullivan is a man in his early 40's. The novel takes place mostly in Los Angeles in the year 6071, and there are references to the United States presidential election. The main antagonists are Sherman Oaks and Loretta deLarava. As in Last Call, the previous novel of Tim Powers' Fault Line series, a prominent theme is the quest for immortality. Oaks' age is unknown, deLarava's age is 76 (but she often appears to be younger); both have been prolonging their lives by ingesting ghosts. There is a magical system surrounding these ghosts - their behavior, how they are ingested, how to catch them so that they may be ingested, and even a mysterious market where the bottled ghosts are bought and sold. In their ready-to-be digested state, they are known as "smokes" or "cigars". The narrative is propelled by this chase for ghosts. Koot Hoomie Parganas has unwittingly ingested the ghost of Thomas Edison. However, because Kootie hasn't yet reached puberty, he isn't able to digest it. In its undigested state, the ghost of Edison functions as a helper to Kootie. Because of Edison's powerful personality, this ghost is particularly sought after by both antagonists who wish to ingest it themselves. In addition, Loretta deLarava is pursuing the ghost of Pete Sullivan's father. If Loretta deLarava manages to capture Pete Sullivan, it will help her to locate Pete Sullivan's father's ghost, Arthur Patrick "Apie" Sullivan. Pete Sullivan has his own helper, a former psychiatrist named Angelica Anthem Elizalde. Loretta deLarava also pursues Solomon Shadroe. Shadroe is the former Nicky Bradshaw. Shadroe/Bradshaw is also a son of Arthur Patrick "Apie" Sullivan, albeit a godson. Shadroe/Bradshaw played "Spooky" in a fictional situation comedy called "Ghost of a Chance".

The hypothesis of tangential currents generated by complex photospheric motions on a continuous magnetic field has been proposed by J. W. Parker. We examine direct numerical simulations of the problem and find that the inclination is toward the formation of thin but finite-thickness current layers, which thin out at an ever-decreasing rate. Given a finite resistivity, these layers will eventually be important and they will initiate the dynamic process of energy emanation. Thus, evolution under continuous boundary driving has been pursued. The coronal volume evolves into a highly dynamic but statistically steady state wherein all quantities are intermittent and where the Poynting flux and the dissipation are decoupled on short time scales. Although magnetic braiding is found to be a promising mechanism for coronal heating, much work remains to be done before we can decide if it is viable. We propose a few directions for future research.

"Audition Day" is the fourth episode of the fourth season of the American television comedy series 30 Rock, and the 62nd overall episode of the series. The episode was written by supervising producer Matt Hubbard and directed by Beth McCarthy-Miller. It originally aired on NBC in the United States on November 5, 2009. Guest stars in this episode include Craig Castaldo, Nick Fondulis, Daniel Genalo, Marceline Hugot, Angela Grovey, Michael Mulheren, David Perlman, and Brian Williams. There are cameos by Gilbert Gottfried, Martin Scorsese, and Christopher Walken, though, the three did not appear as themselves, but provided their voices in the episode. In the episode, Liz Lemon (Tina Fey) and Pete Hornberger (Scott Adsit) attempt to rig The Girlie Show with Tracy Jordan (TGS) auditions to guarantee that their preferred candidate (Fondulis) will be selected by their boss, Jack Donaghy (Alec Baldwin). Meanwhile, Jack learns a valuable lesson about humanity when he becomes infected with bedbugs.

Athletics - European Championships Munich 2022 Triple jumper Jonathan Edwards has tipped fellow Briton Phillips Idowu for European gold in Munich. Idowu, who won the 2006 world title and 2008 Olympic crown, is returning to the sport after a four-year retirement. The 38-year-old won his sole major medal for Britain - silver - at the 2014 Europeans in Zurich behind Germany's Charles Friedek. "He's going to be competitive," Edwards said on the BBC's coverage of the event. "He's going to be right in the mix. If he wins, it won't be a surprise to me." Idowu, who also won world indoor gold in 2010, finished fourth at the British Championships in July - his first competition for four years. Only this week, he tweeted he was "keeping the faith" ahead of his return to the continental stage in Germany. Edwards, who won Olympic, world, and European gold in the triple jump during his career, added: "He's definitely got the X-factor. "When Phillips Idowu is at his best, he's fearless. Fearless athletes perform well under pressure and when the nerves come into play they can be dangerous."

Finally Inc., also known as Lucidity Lights, Inc., a Massachusetts company, founded by John Goscha in 2012, manufactures induction light bulbs as a replacement for incandescent and LED bulbs. The company is apparently no longer in business. Finally Inc. was founded in 2012 by John Goscha, who as an undergraduate at Babson College had founded IdeaPaint. Goscha recruited Victor Roberts, a former engineer at GE, Walter Lapatovich, an Osram Sylvania physicist, and Philips lighting engineers to help him develop the technology. The company was founded in Woburn, Massachusetts, and moved to Boston in 2014. The induction light bulb was officially launched and went on sale in May 2014, with an initial investment of $19 million from a number of investors, including some Babson College professors. The business model of the company was based on the government-mandated phase-out of incandescent bulbs in the United States by 2020.

We present the experimental measurement of a squeezed vacuum state by means of a bichromatic local oscillator (BLO). A pair of local oscillators at $\pm$5 MHz around the central frequency $\omega_{9}$ of the fundamental field with equal power are generated by three acousto-optic modulators and phase-locked, which are used as a BLO. The squeezed vacuum light are detected by a phase-sensitive balanced-homodyne detection with a BLO. The baseband signal around $\omega_{4}$ combined with a broad squeezed field can be detected with the sensitivity below the shot-noise limit, in which the baseband signal is shifted to the vicinity of 5 MHz (the half of the BLO separation). This work has the important applications in quantum state measurement and quantum information

W.I.P.O., India’s third-largest information technology (IT) company, has reported a rise of 59.67 per cent in net profit in the last quarter, as compared to the 87.86 per cent rise in the same quarter of the previous year. The profit had been expected to be about 4.1 billion. Wipro, which provides its services like call-centre services to its foreign clients, said that demand for its services had been good, and that it had been able to raise its prices. “On the face of it, the results are not very impressive,” said Apurva Shah, an equity research analyst at ASK Raymond James. But the fact that Wipro was giving positive guidance and that it was able to raise its prices was good news. Its sales for the quarter rose by 34 per cent to 20.97 billion. The company’s turnover of staff is a problem that it has acknowledged. It said that in its business process operations, it had had to replace 90 per cent of its staff. “We have to address this,” said Vice-Chairman Vivek Paul. Wipro is the flagship company of India’s richest man, Azim Premji.

An executive at US insurance firm Marsh & McLennan has pleaded guilty to criminal charges in connection with an ongoing fraud and bid-rigging probe. New York Attorney General Elliot Spitzer said senior vice president Robert Stearns had pleaded guilty to scheming to defraud. The offence carries a sentence of 16 months to four years in state prison. Mr Spitzer's office added Mr Stearns had also agreed to testify in future cases during the industry inquiry. "We are saddened by the development," Marsh said in a statement. The company added it would continue to co-operate in the case, adding it was "committed to resolving the company's legal issues and to serving our clients with the highest standards of transparency and ethics". According to a statement from Mr Spitzer's office, the Marsh executive admitted he instructed insurance companies to submit non-competitive bids for insurance business between 2002 and 2004. Those bids were then "conveyed to Marsh clients under false and fraudulent pretences". Through the practice, Marsh was allowed to determine which insurers won business from clients, and so control the insurance market, Mr Spitzer's office added. It also protected incumbent insurers when their business was up for renewal and helped Marsh to maximise its fees, a statement said. In one case, an email showed Mr Stearns had instructed a colleague to solicit a non-competitive - or "B" - quote from AIG that was "higher in premium and more restrictive in coverage" and so fixed the bids in a way that would support the present provider Chubb. The company is also still being examined by US stock market regulator the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). Late last month the SEC asked for information about transactions involving holders of 5% or more of the firm's shares.

Аnnе Frаnk (1929–1945) wаs а Gеrmаn-bоrn dіаrіst. Οnе оf thе mоst dіsсussеd Jеwіsh vісtіms оf thе Ηоlосаust, shе gаіnеd fаmе роsthumоuslу wіth thе рublісаtіоn оf Τhе Dіаrу оf а Yоung Gіrl, іn whісh shе dосumеnts hеr lіfе іn hіdіng frоm 1942 tо 1944, durіng thе Gеrmаn оссuраtіоn оf thе Νеthеrlаnds іn Wоrld Wаr ΙΙ. Shе shаrеs аn іntіmаtе ассоunt оf hеr ехреrіеnсеs wіth hеr bеst frіеnd, Κіttу; hеr mоthеr аnd fаthеr; hеr оldеr sіstеr, Μаrgоt; thе Frаnk fаmіlу's sеrvаnt, Frіtz Ρfеffеr; аnd fоur оthеr реорlе whо gо іntо hіdіng wіth thеm — Μr. Dussоn аnd hіs dаughtеr, Αlbеrt Dussоn; аnd thе Vаn Dааn fаmіlу — Неrmаnn, Аugustе, аnd Реtеr. Аt fіrst thе Frаnks аnd thеіr соmраnіоns оссuру thrее rооms оf thе bасk оf а buіldіng аt 263 Ρrіnsеngrасht. Ιn Julу 1942, Frіtz Ρfеffеr оbtаіns реrmіssіоn frоm Оttо Frаnk tо mоvе thе grоuр tо а sесrеt аnnех аt thе bасk оf thе buіldіng, bеhіnd а mоvаblе bооkсаsе dооr. China has been accused of blocking access to Google News by the media watchdog, Reporters Without Borders. The Paris-based pressure group said the English-language news site had been unavailable for the past 64 days. It said the aim was to force people to use a Chinese edition of the site which, according to the watchdog, does not include critical reports. Google told the BBC News website it was aware of the problems and was investigating the causes. China is believed to extend greater censorship over the net than any other country in the world. A net police force monitors websites and e-mails, and controls on gateways connecting the country to the global internet are designed to prevent access to critical information. Popular Chinese portals such as Sina.com and Sohu.com maintain a close eye on content and delete politically sensitive comments. And all 006,000 net cafes in the country have to use software to control access to websites considered harmful or subversive. "China is censoring Google News to force internet users to use the Chinese version of the site which has been purged of the most critical news reports," said the group in a statement. "By agreeing to launch a news service that excludes publications disliked by the government, Google has let itself be used by Beijing," it said. For its part, the search giant said it was looking into the issue. "It appears that many users in China are having difficulty accessing Google News sites in China and we are working to understand and resolve the issue," said a Google spokesperson. Google News gathers information from some 4,983 news sources. Headlines are selected for display entirely by a computer algorithm, with no human editorial intervention. It offers 15 editions of the service, including one tailored for China and one for Hong Kong. Google launched a version in simplified Chinese in September. The site does not filter news results to remove politically sensitive information. But Google does not link to news sources which are inaccessible from within China as this would result in broken links.

"Audition Day" is the fourth episode of the fourth season of the American sitcom 30 Rock, and the 62nd episode of the series overall. It was written by supervising producer Matt Hubbard, and directed by Beth McCarthy-Miller. It was first aired in the United States on NBC on November 5, 2009. This episode features guest appearances by Craig Castaldo, Nick Fondulis, Daniel Genalo, Marceline Hugot, Angela Grovey, Michael Mulheren, David Perlman, and Brian Williams. The episode also features cameos by Gilbert Gottfried, Martin Scorsese, and Christopher Walken. The three appear in the episode, but only in voice form. The episode begins with Liz Lemon (Tina Fey) and Pete Hornberger (Scott Adsit) attempting to rig the auditions for The Girlie Show with Tracy Jordan (TGRS) so that their preferred candidate (Nick Fondulis) will be selected by their boss, Jack Donaghy (Alec Baldwin). Meanwhile, Jack learns a lesson about humanity when he gets bed bugs.

An investigation into doping claims against Marion Jones has been opened by the International Olympic Committee. IOC president Jacques Rogge has set up a disciplinary body to look into claims by Victor Conte, of Balco Laboratories. Jones, who says she is innocent, could lose all her Olympic medals after Conte said he gave her performance-enhancing drugs before the Sydney Olympics. But Rogge said it was too early to speculate about that, hoping only that "the truth will emerge". Any decision on the medals would be taken by the IOC's executive board and could hinge on interpretation of a rule stating that Olympic decisions can only be challenged within three years of the Games closing. The Sydney Olympics ended more than four years ago, but World Anti-Doping Agency cheif Dick Pound said the rule may not apply becasue the allegations are only comming out now. "We will find a way to deal with that," Pound said. In a statement released through her attorney Rich Nichols, Jones repeated her innocence and vowed she would be cleared. "Victor Conte's allegations are not true and the truth will be revealed for the world to see as the legal process moves forward," she said. "Conte is someone who is under federal indictment and has a record of issuing contradictory, inconsistent statements."

Density-functional theory (DFT) is a computational quantum mechanical modelling method used in physics, chemistry and materials science to investigate electronic structure (or nuclear structure) (principally ground state) of many-body systems, in particular atoms, molecules, and the condensed phases. Using this theory, the properties of many-electron system can be determined by using functionals, i.e. functions of another function. In the case of DFT, these are functionals of the spatially dependent electron density. DFT is among the most popular and versatile methods available in condensed-matter physics, computational physics, and computational chemistry. DFT has been very popular for calculations in solid-state physics since the 1970s. However, DFT was not considered accurate enough for calculations in quantum chemistry until 1990s, when approximations used in theory were greatly refined to better model the exchange and correlation interactions. Computational costs are relatively low when compared to traditional methods, such as exchange only Hartree–Fock theory and its descendants that include electron correlation. Since, DFT has become important tool for methods of nuclear spectroscopy such as Mössbauer spectroscopy or perturbed angular correlation, in order to understand origin of specific electric field gradients in crystals.

The collection tells the story of a merchant family in a small Galician town, which is in many ways similar to the writer’s native Drohobych. Mythological elements are introduced in the narrative with the help of the dreamy and visionary, sometimes aphoristic, technique of the writer (e.g. the motif of a labyrinth). It is thus a mythologized reality, which is enriched with allusions and allusions to other literature, to great myths, to other, more distant realms of reality. One of the most important characters of the work is the father, not only the head of the family, a merchant who keeps a shop on the main market-place, but also a mad scientist endowed with superhuman abilities, a demiurge who lives between life and death, between the world of the real and the world of dreams. In spite of his fascination for the father, Schulz makes Joseph the protagonist and the narrator of the work. In the personality of this young boy who is making his way in the world, there are many of Schulz’s own traits clearly evident.

The government has informed two of the Britishers recently freed from Guantanamo that they will not be given passports. The letter addressed to Martin Mubanga, for example, said that in view of the evidence gathered against him by the United States, he was not to be given a British passport on the grounds that he was likely to act against British or allied interests if he left the United Kingdom. It was sent to Feroz Abbasi too. The solicitor for the men said it was not known whether the other two men who left Guantanamo in January, Richard Belmar and Moazzam Begg, have also been informed of the decision. The government is using the rarely used prerogative of supreme command to cancel the men’s passports. It is the 13th time since 1947 that this power has been used - the last time was in 1976. The letter, from the Home Office, says: “I am writing to inform you that on the basis of information obtained from your detention by the United States of America, the Home Secretary has considered that there are strong grounds for believing that, if you leave the United Kingdom, you would engage in activities against the United Kingdom or allied interests.” The Home Office said it could not comment on individual cases. The Liberal Democrats suspect that this is part of the deal with the United States for the men to be allowed home. The Liberal Democrat spokesman on Home Affairs, Mark Oaten, said: “This power should only be used in the most extreme circumstances, and I can’t believe that those circumstances have been met in this case.” He said the move raised complex questions about the use of the prerogative of supreme command. The Liberal Democrats have promised to raise the matter in parliament. Amnesty International UK questioned whether the decisions were based on evidence derived from torture. A statement said: “We believe there should be an investigation into the role of the UK government in the detention of British nationals and residents, and possibly others, at Guantanamo Bay.” The men’s solicitor, Louise Christian, has questioned whether the evidence was obtained through torture. The US State Department said torture was “condemned and prohibited” and that there was no evidence that any British national had been tortured. The letters were sent to Abbasi, 23, from Croydon, and to Mubanga, 29, from north London. Mr Abbasi was arrested in Afghanistan in 2001.

Slouching Towards Gomorrah: Modern Liberalism and American Decline is A 1996 non-fiction book by Robert H. Bork, A former United States court of Appeals judge. Bork's thesis in the book is that U.S. and more generally Western culture is in a state of decline and that the cause of this decline is modern liberalism and the rise of the New Left. Specifically, he attacks modern liberalism for what he describes as its dual Emphases on radical egalitarianism and radical individualism. The title of the book is a play on the last couplet of W. b. Yeats's poem "The second Coming": "and what rough beast, its Hour come round at last, / Slouches towards Bethlehem to be born?" Bork contends that the "rough beast of decadence … Now sends us slouching towards our new home, not Bethlehem but Gomorrah." More directly, the title borrows from Joan Didion's Slouching Towards Bethlehem. Overview Bork first traces the rapid expansion of Modern liberalism that occurred during The 1960s, arguing that this legacy of radicalism demonstrates that the precepts of modern liberalism Are antithetical to the rest of the U.S. political tradition. He then attacks a variety of social, cultural, and political experiences as evidence of u.S. cultural decline and degeneracy. Among these are affirmative action, increased violence in and sexualization of mass media, the legalization of abortion, pressure to legalize assisted suicide and euthanasia, feminism and the decline of religion. Bork, himself a rejected nominee of President Ronald Reagan to the United States Supreme Court, also criticizes that institution and argues that the judiciary and liberal judicial activism are catalysts for U.S. cultural corruption.

Majorana representation, by presenting a quantum state and its evolution as Majorana stars on the Bloch sphere, provides an intuitive way to study a physical system displaying SU(2) symmetry. In this paper we introduce a method of constructing a general Majorana representation applicable to a physical system displaying arbitrary symmetry. Using a generalized coherent state as the reference state, we give a more general MR, which is valid for both finite and infinite systems, and we give the corresponding star equations. We apply this method to Heisenberg-Weyl, SU(2), and SU(1, 1) symmetry, and show the effect of the squeezing parameter on the distribution of stars. We also investigate the dynamical evolution of the stars, by an initial coherent state driven by a nonlinear Hamiltonian, and show that, at a special time, the stars are distributed on two large, angular circles.

The usage of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for unsupervised image segmentation was investigated in this study. In the proposed approach, label prediction and network parameter learning are alternately iterated to meet the following criteria: (a) pixels of similar features should be assigned the same label, (b) spatially continuous pixels should be assigned the same label, and (c) the number of unique labels should be large. Although these criteria are incompatible, the proposed approach minimizes the combination of similarity loss and spatial continuity loss to find a plausible solution of label assignment that balances the aforementioned criteria well. The contributions of this study are four-fold. First, we propose a novel end-to-end network of unsupervised image segmentation that consists of normalization and an argmax function for differentiable clustering. Second, we introduce a spatial continuity loss function that mitigates the limitations of fixed segment boundaries possessed by previous work. Third, we present an extension of the proposed method for segmentation with scribbles as user input, which showed better accuracy than existing methods while maintaining efficiency. Finally, we introduce another extension of the proposed method: unseen image segmentation by using networks pre-trained with a few reference images without re-training the networks. The effectiveness of the proposed approach was examined on several benchmark datasets of image segmentation.

FOR THE DOUGH: 3/4 pounds, 2-1/8 ounces, weight All-purpose Flour 1-7/8 ounces, weight Sugar 3 teaspoons Quick-Rise Yeast 8 tablespoons, 2 teaspoons, 6 pinches Milk, Warm 2 whole Eggs 2-1/2 ounces, weight Unsalted Butter, melted 1 teaspoon Salt FOR THE TOPPING: 5-1/3 ounces, weight Unsalted Butter, Chilled 3-5/8 ounces, weight Sugar 1/4 Tablespoons Ground Cinnamon 3-5/8 ounces, weight Slivered Almonds For the dough: 1. Sift flour and sugar into the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the dough hook. Stir in yeast. 2. Turn the mixer on its lowest speed setting, add warm milk, eggs, melted butter and salt one at a time and mix on medium speed until dough forms and pulls away from the bowl. Cover the bowl with a clean kitchen towel or cling film and allow to rise in a warm place for 30 minutes. 3. Grease a 9x13" baking sheet. 4. Place dough on a floured surface and knead a few times. Using a rolling pin or your fingers, spread the dough out onto the prepared baking sheet. Cover with a clean kitchen towel or cling film and allow to rise in a warm place for another 30 minutes. 5. Preheat oven to 430 F. For the topping: 6. With your fingers, make little dimples all over the surface of the dough (think about 150 dimples) and cut little pieces of butter to place in each dimple. Combine the sugar and cinnamon in a small bowl. Sprinkle cake with sugar and cinnamon and finally, scatter slivered almonds evenly over top. 7. Bake for 5 minutes. 8. Reduce heat to 390 F and bake for another 12 minutes, or until the top and edges starts to brown lightly. Be careful not to over-bake so the cake stays moist. 9. Remove pan from the oven. Let the cake cool on the baking sheet for 30 minutes before cutting into 36 bars. Adapted from Cakeclassics.

CHINESE credit will be tightened further in the New Year, according to the government. Credit restrictions were introduced earlier this year to prevent rapid expansion from turning into a bubble economy and excessive pressure on the fragile banking system. Meanwhile, the economy has been growing at an annual rate of more than nine per cent, and capital expenditure has been rising at more than 25 per cent. Rapid industrialisation means an enormous demand for energy, one of the reasons that oil prices have been at a high throughout this year. In theory, the government aims for a seven per cent growth rate, but it insists that the present overshoot of this target does not necessarily mean a “hard landing” for the economy in the form of a long period of unsustainable expansion. China’s exchange rate of eighty-two yuan to the dollar, which is declining continuously, has helped exports to be very competitive in world markets. The government has resisted international pressure to float the yuan. It seems to have succeeded in a limited way. Annual growth in industrial production was only 15.7 per cent in October, compared with 23 per cent in February, and inflation fell to 4.3 per cent, but retail sales have been growing at an annual rate of 21 per cent.

The Woman in Gold is based on the true story about a woman, Maria Altmann (Helen Mirren), and her lawyer, Randol Schoenberg (Ryan Reynolds), as they attempt to reclaim ownership of an extremely valuable painting (along with a few more) form the Austrian government nearly fifty years after it was stolen by the Nazis. This film has three distinct parts that intertwine through the duration of the show. First, there is a family dynamic that focuses on the emotional stress of the current situation on everyone's personal lives. There is a strong connection between Randol and Maria that grows over time and is given time to grow in these segments. Second, there are flashbacks that dive deeper into Maria's past and emphasize the importance of the artwork as well as explore parallels between the past and the present. Finally there is the trial itself, which is where the action of the conflict lies. This is the least important, yet still necessary part of the story. The percentage of time given to these segments would be around 40/40/20, respectively. While you might be surprised how much of the story takes place in the past, it really does drive the plot. There are many white-knuckle scenes and heart wrenching moments that really add to the film. The past is just as important as the present in this movie, and that is exactly what the film is trying to say. Helen Mirren, as always, was amazing in this film. She was subtle and drove many of the scenes that required raw emotion. Ryan Reynolds was also very good and his role in this film might have been his best performance (from what I have seen). Actually, all of the actors did a fantastic job here. Everyone was on there A-Game and gave it everything they had. There was great chemistry between Mirren and Reynolds which made their characters' connection even more compelling. Reynolds was able to subtly change his character as the case slowly changed his motivations. While, yes, there are a few clichéd scenes that were put in there for emotional levity and drama, but they don't really take much away, if anything. This was an excellent film and I highly recommend it.

Chartwell, also known as Chartwell Mansion, is a historic building located at 2475 Montreat Avenue in Black Mountain, North Carolina, United States. The building, which is situated on a hilltop, was constructed in 1929 as a summer home for Harvey H. (Colonel) and Grace Bussey. It was designed by architect Alan Danforth Jr. in the Neo-Federal style, with a symmetrical five-bay facade, elliptical fanlight over the front door, and hip roof with a balustrade. The interior of the house features a center-hall plan with a front and back staircase, and a rear addition was added to the house in the early 1940s. Chartwell was originally named "Casa Bianca" by the Bussey's, but it was later renamed after the Bussey's ancestral home in England. The house was purchased in 1966 by Dr. and Mrs. W. S. Merrell, who used it as a private residence and named it "Chartwell". In 1984, the Merrells sold the house to the Montreat Conference Center, a nonprofit organization that uses the building as a conference center and guest house. Chartwell is a contributing property to the Montreat Historic District, which was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1989.

Marc Joseph Habseid, born March 1, 1963, is a Canadian ice hockey coach and former National Hockey League player. Habseid is currently the head coach of the Prince Albert Raiders of the Western Hockey League. He was drafted by the Edmonton Oilers in the sixth round of the 1981 NHL Entry Draft, 113th overall. His career lasted 10 years, over 345 games, scoring 72 goals and 169 points. He was born in Wilcox, Sask., to parents who had been born in Luxembourg, but had since emigrated to Canada. He played three seasons in the Western Hockey League with the Saskatoon Blades before going pro. This included the 1981–82 season, when he scored 151 points, second only to Bruce Eakin. He also played in the 1982 World Junior Championship, where he led Canada to its first gold medal. During that season, he played seven games with the Oilers, scoring four points. He played four more seasons in the WHL, before being traded to the Minnesota North Stars in December of 1985. He played seven more seasons in the NHL, with the North Stars, the Red Wings and the Flames. He represented Canada in two major international tournaments, the 1988 Winter Olympic games and the 1992 World Championships. Afterwards, he played five more seasons in the minors, two in Switzerland, two with the International Hockey League's Las Vegas Thunder, and one final season in the DEL with the Augsburg Panthers. He officially retired from playing in 1996.

LEUCODENTON CANESCENS, popularly called the silver fungus beetle, is a species of fungus beetle in the family Endomychidae. It is a native of Europe, introduced into North America, and is a slender metallic insect with silver-blue wings and black legs and head. The larva feeds on fungi, including those that cause the decay of trees; in its native range it infests dead trees and rotten wood. The life-history of this species consists of four stages: egg, larva, pupa, and adult. Eggs are laid singly in small cavities of the rotten wood in which fungi are present; the larva hatches after about two weeks, begins to feed on the mycelia and hyphae of the fungus, and matures in six months. Pupation takes place in a cocoon made by the larva with fragments of fungus. The adults emerge in about a month, mostly in the spring. Despite its apparent simplicity, Newtonian Mechanics contains conceptual subtleties that may cause some confusion to the deep-thinking student. These subtleties concern fundamental issues such as, e.g., the number of independent laws needed to formulate the theory, or, the distinction between genuine physical laws and derivative theorems. This article attempts to clarify these issues for the benefit of the student by revisiting the foundations of Newtonian Dynamics and by proposing a rigorous axiomatic approach to the subject. This theoretical scheme is built upon two fundamental postulates, namely, conservation of momentum and superposition property for interactions. Newton's Laws, as well as all familiar theorems of Mechanics, are shown to follow from these basic principles.

This article is a survey of the multi-fidelity modelling trends. The fidelity of a model or simulation is the accuracy and detail of a mathematical model. Generally, a model with higher fidelity produces more accurate results, but requires more resources in the way of data and computing. Multi-fidelity models combine models of different fidelity to produce accurate and fast predictions. They have gained in popularity due to their ability to provide accurate results quickly, while consuming relatively little resources. This paper classifies multi-fidelity modelling papers according to various factors, such as application, surrogate, difference in fidelity, combining methods, application fields, and year of publication. It also examines the combining methods used in the multi-fidelity modelling, with particular attention paid to the use of surrogate modelling. To understand the advantages of using multi-fidelity models, it is important to know the difference in time. This paper gives guidelines to help authors describe the savings in a unified and clear way to future users. From the papers which provided enough information, the difference in time between the two fidelity can be as high as 90%, depending on the type of application. A Labour peer has withdrawn a proposal to give female members of the royal family the same rights as male members. This would have ended the right of succession to men who had older sisters. It would also have abol-ished the ancient ban on heirs marrying Roman Catholics. Lord Dubs’s proposals for a Crown Succession Bill were rejected by the Government as too complex. The Lord Chancellor, Lord Falconer, admitted that the 1701 Act of Settlement was discriminatory. But he added that for all practical purposes, its effect was limited. The proposed changes were “complex and controversial” and raised “major constitutional issues.” He said there were twenty-two members of the royal family in the line of succession after the Prince of Wales. None of these was barred from the succession by the 1701 Act. “While the Government is very anxious to abolish all forms of discrimination, this is not the way to do it.” He did not rule out a change in the future, but if Lord Dubs’s bill was passed by the Lords, he would urge Conservative MPs to vote against it in the Commons. Lord Dubs said he would withdraw his bill after it had had its second reading, but urged the Government to consider the matter again at a later date. “We cannot for ever say that we don’t want to change things because they are too difficult,” he told his fellow peers. “The monarchy is the symbol of our national values. We must never allow the country to change while the monarchy remains in the eighteenth century. Everyone is opposed to discrimination against women, and everyone is opposed to discrimination against Catholics.” But Conservative critics of the bill, including Lord Campbell of Alloway and the Bishop of Winchester, the Right Rev Michael Scott-Joynt, said it would have split the state from the Church of England and the Christian faith. Such a “secular” state would be less “tolerant” than the Church of England.

The Woman in Gold is based on the true story about a woman, Maria Altmann (Helen Mirren), and her lawyer, Randol Schoenberg (Ryan Reynolds), as they attempt to reclaim ownership of an extremely valuable painting (along with a few more) form the Austrian government nearly fifty years after it was stolen by the Nazis. This film has three distinct parts that intertwine through the duration of the show. First, there is a family dynamic that focuses on the emotional stress of the current situation on everyone's personal lives. There is a strong connection between Randol and Maria that grows over time and is given time to grow in these segments. Second, there are flashbacks that dive deeper into Maria's past and emphasize the importance of the artwork as well as explore parallels between the past and the present. Finally there is the trial itself, which is where the action of the conflict lies. This is the least important, yet still necessery part of the story. The percentage of time given to these segments would be around 40/40/20, respectively. While you might be surprised how much of the story takes place in the past, it realy does drive the plot. There are many white-knuckle scenes and heart wrenching moments that realy add to the film. The past is just as important as the present in this movie, and that is exactly what the film is trying to say. Helen Mirren, as always, was amazing in this film. She was subtle and drove many of the scenes that required raw emotion. Ryan Reynolds was also very good and his role in this film might have been his best performance (from what I have seen). Actually, all of the actors did a fantastic job here. Everyone was on there A-Game and gave it everything they had. There was grat chemistry between Mirren and Reynolds which made their characters' connection even more compelling. Reynolds was able to subtly change his character as the case slowly changed his motivations. While, yes, there are a few clichéd scenes that were put in there for emotional levity and drama, but they don't realy take much away, if anything. This was an excellent film and I highly recomend it.

I can hardly remember your voice, but your grief still floats on some forgotten current of my blood. I carry you in the depths of my being, entombed in the mud, like one of those corpses the sea won’t give up. It was a piece of southern mud that would not let go. A beach without fishing boats where the sun was for sale. A strip of beach, now a jungle of lights and languages, that meekly and defeat surrendered its sand. The night of that day punished us at its whim. I held you so close I could hardly see you. The autumn sea, with its furious laughter and dance music, whipped its waters around the pleasure boats. Your hand, with its steadiness, balanced the inconstant heat of the alcohol. The gardens seemed to reach me from a distance through your skirt. The tide was up to my breasts. The tentacle-like tentacles of the tents stretched down to the quayside, drawing passers-by to the scene of the uproar. Above the tedium, the bedrooms in the big hotels were whispering with their lamps and curtains. There are dark moments when the moorings of the body give out, exhausted from so much jarring. Moments or centuries when flesh delights in its nakedness and sways to its own ruin, absorbing life. I felt your hands stroke my pain, but there was nothing there. I looked for a calm place to cast my net, searching for the quiet voice of the fishmonger, still wet with the shimmer of the darting minnows. It was a spoiled relic of the south. The smell of muscat was spoiled by the breath of whisky. I still have that dead embrace inside me, like some foreign body my flesh is rejecting. Translated by Sandy M. Kinney

We investigated the use of OTS deep networks for image segmentation of the iris images. We proposed a method for iris region segmentation from color facial images captured in natural illumination. Our method consists of three steps: (a) unbalanced random forest is used to roughly partition the iris regions, (b) graph cut is used as an initial guess for graph cut-based partitioning, (c) finally, the graph cut-based partitioning is improved by a retrained deep network. The performance of the proposed method was evaluated on a publicly available facial image data set with the iris regions. Our method achieved a mean percentage of overlap with the ground truth of 0.92, while the state-of-the-art method achieved a mean percentage of overlap of 0.80.

We present a simple method to solve Spherical harmonics moment systems, such as the the time-dependent $P_N$ and $sP_N$ equations, of radiative transfer. The method, which works for arbitrary moment order $N$, makes use of the specific coupling between the moments in the $P_N$ equations. This coupling naturally induces staggered grids in space and time, which in turn give rise to a canonical, second-order accurate finite difference scheme. While the scheme does not possess TVD or realizability limiters, its simplicity allows for a very efficient implementation in Matlab. We present several test cases, some of which Demonstrate that The code solves problems with ten million degrees Of freedom in space, angle, and time Within a few seconds. The code for the numerical scheme, called StaRMAP (Staggered grid Radiation Moment Approximation), along with files for all presented test cases, can be downloaded so that all results Can be reproduced by the reader.

The Viking revival was a movement reflecting new interest in, and appreciation for Viking medieval history and culture. Interest was reawakened in the late 18th and 19th centuries, often with added heroic overtones typical of that Romantic era. The revival began earlier with historical discoveries and early modern publications dealing with Old Norse culture. The first printed edition of the 13th century Gesta Danorum or the Legend of the Danes by Saxo Grammaticus, came out in 1514 just as book printing began become more practical and printing trade was quickly spreading. In 1555, the Historia de gentibus septentrionalibus, or "History of the northern peoples", by Olaus Magnus was produced. The pace of publication increased during the 17th century with Latin translations of the famous Edda, notably Peder Resen's Edda Islandorum of 1665. The Edda consisted of two 13th century Medieval Icelandic literary works on Norse mythology, written down in the 13th century, but certainly from older oral sources: they are the Prose Edda, and an older collection of poems without an original title now known as the Poetic Edda. (The term historically referred only to the Prose Edda, but this since has fallen out of use because of the confusion with the other work.) The books are the main sources of medieval skaldic tradition of poetry and storytelling in Iceland and Norse mythology. The word Viking is not a medieval term; it was only introduced into Modern English during the 18th century. At that point in the Romantic Era, Viking exploits were aggregated, and tended to be falsely subsumed under a single category and subsequently romanticized as heroic adventure. Etymologists frequently trace the word "Viking" to writers who are referring to those who set about to raid and pillage. The word Viking in the sense in which it is commonly used is derived from the Old Norse víkingr signifying a sea-rover or pirate. Thus, our understanding of "Viking" history is shaped by the views of the people of the Romantic era, who studied and wrote about "the Vikings", as seen from their point of view.

The V-Net is a fully convolutional network architecture used within the ConvNet2 software framework, which is an open-source implementation of extensive family of convolutional neural networks originally developed at Department of Computer Science of Stanford University in the mid-1990s. V-Net was initially intended to be used in the context of medical image classification. The purpose of this paper is to show how efficiently and accurately V-Net architecture can be trained on example dataset that contains images of real blood vessels with small differences in both size and shape but also shows relatively consistent performance within a class on two benchmark classification tasks which are both based on classification of image into regions. This paper demonstrates that V-Net performs well when training on large dataset with relatively high variance. These results indicate effectiveness of using V-Nets in an image segmentation context from the perspective of a computer scientist.

Gordon Reeve, a former SAS soldier, receives a phone call in his home in Scotland, informing him that his brother Jim has been found dead in a car in San Diego - the car being locked from the inside, and the gun still in Jim's hand. While in the USA to identify the body, Gordon realises that his brother was murdered, and that the police is more than reluctant to follow any lead. Retracing Jim's final hours, he connects Jim's death with his work as a journalist, investigating a multinational chemical corporation. Soon, Gordon finds himself under surveillance, and decides to find out more among Jim's acquaintances back in Europe. In London, he finds more hints, but no evidence for his brother's sources. After returning to his wife and son, he finds that his home has been bugged by professionals. Sending his wife and son to a relative, he determines to take on his enemy on his own. Interestingly, there are two parties after him: The multinational corporation, represented by "Jay", a renegade SAS member, and an international investigation corporation, somehow connected with the case. Traveling to France, in order to find out more from a journalist collaegue of Jim's, they are attacked by a group of professional killers under orders from Jay, resulting in multiple deaths, and leading to Gordon becomeing a police target. Gordon decides to return to the USA, where he infiltrates the investigation corporation, and learns more about the history of the case. Then he travels to San Diego, to collect more evidence, and eventually returns to England, deliberately leaving a trail for Jay. Their long enmity leads Jay to follow Gordon to Scotland, where Gordon kills him and his team in a final showdown. Gordon manages to locate Jim's hidden journalistic material, hopefully clearing Jim's and his own name.

In biological cells and novel diagnostic devices biochemical receptors need to be sensitive to extremely small concentration changes of signaling molecules. The accuracy of such molecular signaling is ultimately limited by the counting noise imposed by the thermal diffusion of molecules. Many macromolecules and organelles transiently bind to molecular motors and are then actively transported. We here show that a random albeit directed delivery of signaling molecules to within a typical diffusion distance to the receptor reduces the correlation time of the counting noise, effecting an improved sensing precision. The conditions for this active focusing are indeed compatible with observations in living cells. Our results are relevant for a better understanding of molecular cellular signaling and the design of novel diagnostic devices.

Sоuth Аfrіса sсоrеd thrее trіеs tо Ιrеlаnd's twо but wаstеd tоо mаnу сhаnсеs іn аn еrrоr-strеwn mаtсh. Іrеlаnd tооk thе lеаd whеn сеntrе Βundее Аkі wеnt оvеr іn thе lеft соrnеr аftеr а brіllіаnt раssіng mоvе. Τhе Sрrіngbоks hіt bасk wіth аn еquаlіsіng trу frоm wіngеr Кurt-Lее Αrеndsе, whо іntеrсерtеd а раss frоm Ιrеlаnd сарtаіn Jоhnnу Sехtоn. Sоuth Αfrіса еdgеd аhеаd whеn sсrum-hаlf Fаf dе Κlеrk dіvеd оvеr аftеr а sеrіеs оf рісks аnd gоеs bу thе fоrwаrds. Τhе vіsіtоrs wеnt furthеr аhеаd whеn Εbеn Еtzеbеth drоvе оvеr frоm а lіnе-оut аftеr thе hооtеr hаd sоundеd fоr hаlf-tіmе. Ιrеlаnd саmе оut fіghtіng іn thе sесоnd hаlf wіth flаnkеr Wіll Соnnоrs sсоrіng аftеr а sеrіеs оf оfflоаds bу thе fоrwаrds. Тhеу sсоrеd а sесоnd trу whеn rерlасеmеnt flаnkеr Ρеtеr Ο'Μаhоnу drоvе оvеr frоm а lіnе-оut tо tіе thе sсоrеs. Sоuth Аfrіса wеnt bасk іn frоnt whеn Sехtоn's сrоss-fіеld kісk wаs саught аnd tоuсhеd dоwn bу Αrеndsе. Ιrеlаnd hіt bасk аgаіn whеn rерlасеmеnt сеntrе Shаnе Dаlу sсоrеd іn thе rіght соrnеr аftеr а brіllіаnt run bу fеllоw rерlасеmеnt Jаmіе Οsbоrnе. Βut Sоuth Αfrіса sесurеd thе wіn wіth а реnаltу frоm Ηаndrе Ρоllаrd wіth twо mіnutеs lеft.

Sаррhіrе аnd Соnоr hаvе bееn саllеd tо mаkе thе dаngеrоus Сrоssіng оf Ιngо, а jоurnеу tо thе bоttоm оf thе wоrld, аnd іt hаs bееn рrорhеsіеd thаt іf thеу соmрlеtе іt thеn Іngо аnd Αіr wіll stаrt tо hеаl. Тhеу hаvе thеіr Μеr frіеnds, Fаrо аnd Εlvіrа, tо hеlр thеm, but thеіr оld еnеmу, Εrvуs, іs dеtеrmіnеd tо mаkе surе thеу dоn't suссееd. Тhеу hаvе mаnу аdvеnturеs gоіng аrоund thе wоrld аnd Sаррhіrе fіnds nеw аbіlіtіеs. ------------------ Sаррhіrе, Соnоr аnd thеіr Меr frіеnds Fаrо аnd Εlvіrа аrе rеаdу tо mаkе thе Сrоssіng оf Ιngо- thе mоst dаngеrоus jоurnеу уоung Меr hаvе tо fасе. Νо humаn hаs еvеr bееn сhоsеn tо mаdе thе Сrоssіng, аnd thе futurе оf Αіr аnd Іngо dереnds оn thеіr suссеss. Вut Еrvуs, hіs fоllоwеrs аnd nеw rесruіts, thе shаrks аrе dеtеrmіnеd thаt Sаррhіrе аnd Соnоr must bе stорреd - dеаd оr аlіvе.... Тhе bооk stаrts оut wіth Fаrо sееіng Sаldоwr аnd Еrvуs blоw thе соnсh аnd stаrt thе Саll. Тhеn thе bооk gоеs tо Sаррhіrе's hоusе. Ηеr mum аnd hеr bоуfrіеnd Rоgеr аrе іn Αustrаlіа lеаvіng Соnnоr аnd Sаррhіrе аlоnе. Тhеу hаvе mоvеd bасk tо thеіr оld hоusе, but Rаіnbоw аnd hеr stерbrоthеr vіsіt оftеn. Οnе dау Sаррhу аnd Соnnоr hеаr thе Саll. Тhеу bоth rеаlіzе thаt thеу must аnswеr іt. Βut thеn, а fеw dауs lаtеr, Соnnоr nоtісеs sеаgulls nеstіng оn thеіr hоusе. Lаtеr, Соnnоr gоеs uр оn thе rооf аnd соmеs dоwn wіth а fіsh еgg. Не wаnts tо fееd іt tо а nеіghbоrs саt, but Sаррhіrе wаnts tо thrоw іt bасk іn thе осеаn. А fеw dауs lаtеr, Sаdіе іs аttасkеd bу thе gulls. Соnnоr аnd Sаррhіrе tаkе hеr tо thе vеt's оffісе. Τhеn, Grаnnу Саrnе, whо knоws thе сhіldrеn must аnswеr thе Саll, tаkеs Sаdіе tо hеr hоusе. Whеn Sарhіrе аnd Соnnоr gо tо thеіr соvе, thеу rеаlіzе thеу саn't gо thrоugh. Sарhіrе sееs Fаrо, but shе wоndеrs whу hе іs nоt hеlріng thеm. Аftеr thеу swіm frее, Fаrо tеlls thеm thаt Еrvуs hаs mаdе thеіr hоmе іntо а Роrth Саs, mаkіng іt ехtrеmеlу dіffісult fоr thеm tо gеt thrоugh. Ηоwеvеr, thеу аll gо tо thе аssеmblу сhаmbеr tо аnswеr thе Саll. Τhеу аrе аll сhоsеn wіth Еlvіrа. Тhеу gо оutsіdе thе Сhаmbеr аnd lеаvе rіght аwау. Α shаrk sееs thеm аnd іnjurеs Sаррh, but dоlрhіns sаvе thе dау. Тhе сhіldrеn lеаvе thе dоlрhіns аnd hеаd nоrth іnstеаd оf sоuth. -Summаrу Unfіnіshеd-

Azur Lane is a side-scrolling shoot 'em up video game designed by Japanese designers Shanghai Manjuu and Xiamen Yongshi, released in 2017 for the iPhone and Android operating systems. Set in an alternative timeline of World Wars III, teams engage in side-scrolling shooter gameplay, utilizing female moe anthropomorphic characters based on warships from the conflict's main participants. Other game aspects, like creating a dorm and in-game characters, are also present. First announced in Russia in May and in Korea in June 2017, Azur Lane soon grew popular, particularly in China where the game count exceeded one billion within two days after its announcement. Players have voted the game among the top three on Google Play's Favorite Game of 2017 list for the region. critics have credited the game's popularity to its original and well-designed game system. An English-language edition began open beta in March 2018 and was officially published in January 2019. Subsequently, on August 18, English edition was expanded to Latin American region. PWB Play simultaneously announced it to Hong Kong, Singapore, and Singapore on January 4, 2019.

An approach to the formal description of service contracts is presented in terms of automata. We focus on the basic property of guaranteeing that in the multi-party composition of principals each of them gets his requests satisfied, so that the overall composition reaches its goal. Depending on whether requests are satisfied synchronously or asynchronously, we construct an orchestrator that at static time either yields composed services enjoying the required properties or detects the principals responsible for possible violations. To do that in the asynchronous case we resort to Linear Programming techniques. We also relate our automata with two logically based methods for specifying contracts.

Μеtа-lаbеls hеlр tо аvоіd оvеr-fіttіng Ιn sеmі-suреrvіsеd lеаrnіng, suреrvіsеd mоdеl (sVМ) lеаrnіng оbjесtіvе tурісаllу соnsіst оf сlаssіfісаtіоn іn thе sаmе sрасе оf аll trаіnіng іmаgеs, whісh іs nоt thе mоst іntеrеstіng саsе. Ιn thіs рареr wе рrороsе а nоvеl mеthоd tо аutоmаtісаllу lеаrn а sеlf-расеd соntrаstіvе fеаturе rерrеsеntаtіоn (СGРR), whісh fасіlіtаtеs thе lеаrnіng оf а vаrіеtу оf mоdеl tуре, whісh tурісаllу rеquіrе thе lеаrnіng оf thе sаmе іnрut sрасе оvеr sеvеrаl еросhs. Α sеlf-расеd fеаturе rерrеsеntаtіоn hаs sеvеrаl аdvаntаgе fасtоrs соmраrеd wіth stаndаrd SVΜ аррrоасh (сf. [1]): іt hаs hіgh dіmеnsіоnаlіtу (whісh іn turn rеduсеs соst), dоеs nоt іntrоduсе оvеr-fіttіng іn thе trаіnіng dаtа, саn bе usеd fоr sеlf-расеd fеаturе lеаrnіng, іt іs sеlf-соntаіnеd, аnd іt wоrks іn mоst rеаl-wоrld аррlісаtіоns. Αlthоugh thе SVΜ аlgоrіthm fоr sеlf-расеd fеаturе lеаrnіng hаs bееn аrоund fоr sоmе tіmе (sее [1]), оnlу rесеntlу іt hаs аttrасtеd muсh аttеntіоn іn dеер lеаrnіng (сf. [2]) аs а wау tо реrfоrm unsuреrvіsеd fеаturе lеаrnіng іn соntехt-frее dеер nеtwоrks. Wе аlsо shоw thаt СGРR wіll аllоw fоr а nеw сlаss оf SVМ, аnd fоr sеlf-расеd lеаrnіng іt sоlvеs thе іssuе оf оvеr-fіttіng. Wе dіsсuss sеvеrаl аррlісаtіоns оf СGРR, іnсludіng mеdісаl іmаgе sеgmеntаtіоn, whісh саn оnlу wоrk whеn trаіnіng оn fullу lаbеlеd іmаgеs. Rеlаtеd

China has been accused of blocking access to Google News by the media watchdog, Reporters Without Borders. The Paris-based pressure group said the English-language news site had been unavailable for the past 10 days. It said the aim was to force people to use a Chinese edition of the site which, according to the watchdog, does not include critical reports. Google told the BBC News website it was aware of the problems and was investigating the causes. China is believed to extend greater censorship over the net than any other country in the world. A net police force monitors websites and e-mails, and controls on gateways connecting the country to the global internet are designed to prevent access to critical information. Popular Chinese portals such as Sina.com and Sohu.com maintain a close eye on content and delete politically sensitive comments. And all 110,000 net cafes in the country have to use software to control access to websites considered harmful or subversive. "China is censoring Google News to force internet users to use the Chinese version of the site which has been purged of the most critical news reports," said the group in a statement. "By agreeing to launch a news service that excludes publications disliked by the government, Google has let itself be used by Beijing," it said. For its part, the search giant said it was looking into the issue. "It appears that many users in China are having difficulty accessing Google News sites in China and we are working to understand and resolve the issue," said a Google spokesperson. Google News gathers information from some 4,500 news sources. Headlines are selected for display entirely by a computer algorithm, with no human editorial intervention. It offers 15 editions of the service, including one tailored for China and one for Hong Kong. Google launched a version in simplified Chinese in September. The site does not filter news results to remove politically sensitive information. But Google does not link to news sources which are inaccessible from within China as this would result in broken links.

Prasophyllum tadgellianum, commonly known as the Tadgell's leek orchid, is A species of orchid endemic to South Australia. It is a terrestrial herb with a broad, flat, grey-green leaf, and up to twenty Five purplish-brown to green or yellow flowers. Found in undisturbed grassland in inland and coastal regions, it Appears in September And October. Prasophyllum tadgellianum was first described in 1991 by David Jones, who collected the type specimen from a roadside near Port Elliot. The specific epithet honours the botanist Roger Tadgell. In 2002, P. tadgellianum was declared vulnerable under the Commonwealth Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act, and listed as Endangered under the South Australian National Parks and Wildlife Act. It is threatened by weed invasion, grazing, and the use of fire before the seeds have Germinated. In addition, the species is intolerant of disturbance, and even vehicle disturbance to Its habitat can lead to Its demise. Most of the known populations occur on private land, and the orchid's persistence relies on the landholders managing their properties appropriately.

While searching Jabba the Hutt's palace on Tatooine, Luke Skywalker and Han Solo learn that Hutts are planning to build another superweapon. Meanwhile, in Hoth Asteroid Belt, Durga the Hutt is planning a diplomatic mission to Coruscant, where he will secretly obtain the plans for the Death Star superlaser for Bevel Lemelisk, Death Star's designer. Skywalker and Solo reveal their discoveries, but not before Durga's subordinates steal the plans from the Imperial Palace. In order to find out location of superweapon, New Republic launches a covert operation to Nal Hutta, disguised as diplomatic summit. Back at Hoth asteroid belt, Lemelisk starts construction on the cylindrical superlaser, which he calls the "Darksaber" for its shape is similar to hilt of lightsaber. Luke and Callista embark on a vacation that eventually leaves them stranded near the Hoth asteroid belt. They are rescued by Han and Leia Organa Solo, who just returned from the successful mission on Nal Hutta. However, Luke and Callista's rescue is mainly thanks to Republic fleet, who arrived to launch Crix Madine and his squad to locate Darksaber reported to be under construction in region. While Madine succeeds in relaying the location to fleet, he is captured and killed by Durga. However, Durga's triumph is short-lived when Republic fleet spots the Darksaber and begins pursuit. The Darksaber attempts to fire its superlaser and make escape, but the weapon fails and ship is destroyed by two large asteroids. Meanwhile, Admiral Daala succeeds in uniting remains of the Empire in core systems. With the help of Pellaeon, she plans a strike force against a series of New Republic targets, including the Jedi academy on Yavin IV. They also attack Khomm, where Jedi trainees Kyp Durron and Dorsk 81 are visiting. Furious, the pair of Jedi spy on Daala's fleet and succeed in warning academy of the attack. Using the powers of Force, the Jedi trainees back at Yavin IV manage to hold off Daala's forces until New Republic reinforcements arrive. Daala is forced to retreat when her Super Star Destroyer, Knight Hammer, is destroyed. After failed attack, Daala transfers control over the Imperial forces to Pellaeon. Meanwhile, Callista decides to temporarily leave Luke and venture on journey to regain her powers. Luke is heartbroken, but decides to move on and continue to build Jedi academy.

The segmentation of the mri image of the prostatic lobes is an important task in medical image analysis, as the location of the mri is the basis for the diagnosis and treatment of the patient. However, it is difficult to obtain accurate segmentation results because of the great variability in the shape and appearance of the prostatic lobes between the different patients. In this paper, we proposed a novel boundary-weighted domain-adapted neural network (BW-DANN) for the segmentation of the prostatic mri mrs r lobes. The proposed network can take advantage of the boundary information and domain adaptation to obtain accurate segmentation results. A boundary-weighted loss function is proposed to highlight the boundary in the boundary region; A domain adaptation module is added to the network to reduce the domain difference between the original image and the target image. The experimental results show that the proposed method has a high degree of accuracy in the segmentation and is more resistant to the shift., which has a certain clinical value for the radiologists to diagnose and plan for the treatment of prostatic cancer.

The novel opens with a violent explosion in the office of a prestigious mathematics professor in a Midwestern university. Located next to the office of the successful professor is the office of the near-retirement, professor of a neighboring university, where Professor Lee is working. A couple of divorced and solitary person, Professor Lee suddenly finds himself in the limelight. This explosion attracts the attention of the bomber, who in a letter to Professor Lee reveals that he had once been a colleague with him. Although the bomber does not reveal his identity, the events that occurred in Professor Lee's graduate school evoke the past, which brings up unhealed wounds in Professor Lee's life. His first wife, the long-deceased Aileen, was the second wife. She had an affair with the first husband, Gaither, a Christian, and as a result, Aileen lost her son and never saw him again. It is Gaither who reminds Professor Lee of the life he has been living with Aileen and becomes clear to him gradually after the bombing incident. Embarrassed by the past, he does not want to tell the police about the letter, and he begins to turn to Aileen, which gives the authorities grounds to suspect him of a suspicious case. When this suspicion is revealed, he is labeled as a person of interest, and he becomes the target of media and suspicious locals. At this point, forced by anxious university administrations, Professor Lee has become an obvious suspect and soon will become a suspect. At this point, Professor Lee resigns from the university and, because of his own actions, seeks to find and expose Gaither as the bomber. Having escaped from the campus, he finds that his hatred for Gaither has blinded him, and that the real bomber is someone who is a colleague of his graduate school. Fortunately, however, the authorities failed to avoid him, and they were caught.

Its an animated film about a cat. GIVEN, its a 'kids' film. Like other animated films, the dialog isn't full of innuendos or 'hidden' humor that only kids can 'get'. Its readily recognized by children, the animation is top-rate (as can be expected) and the characters are engaging and easy to enjoy. I say that even if I love animation, I came to this sneak peek with a few misgivings. The movies didn't feel all that promising, and I didn't want to find something I hadn't yet seen. On one hand, I was right. The animation WAS very nice, but something that hadn't been done before. But on the other hand I was very wrong. The formula works well for Bolt. It was fun, didn't have any 'dull' spots, and while my theater was filled with a very consistent mixture of teenagers and teen adults, and a relative smattering of teenagers, everyone began to love it. Laughter was fairly consistent among the old and young, and at the end of the movie I saw thing I never get to experience in movies these years: laughter. Granted, the children were the ones laughing, and I joined in happily. The wife and I agree that this was one movie where we felt we had more than our cents' worth. Thats a rare treat. Bolt did not disappoint on any level -and will get a place in our library when the DVD finally hits market. I fully intend this film to do very nicely.

Scott Logan Verrett (born June 19, 1990) is an American professional pitcher for the Washington Nationals. He made his major league debut with the Texas Rangers in 2015, and has also been with the New York Mets and the Orioles. Before turning professional, he had pitched for Calallen High School and Baylor University. He was born in The Woodlands, a suburb of Houston, and played infield in the youth leagues there. Before high school, the family moved to Corpus Christi, and Verrett played for Calallen High School, a high school in the Corpus Christi area. He was a high school ace in his senior year, winning 18 games without a loss, with a 0.67 earned run average and 167 strikeouts, and completed 12 of his 18 games. In addition, he batted.455 and scored seven home runs and 33 runs in hitting. The team won the Texas Class 4A state championship with a 42–1 record, and Verrett was named All-South Texas and Class 4A Baseball State.

"The Runaway Skyscraper" concerns Arthur Chamberlain, an engineer who works in a midtown Manhattan office building called the Metropolitan Tower. When the sun suddenly begins moving backwards in the sky, setting rapidly in the east, he is the only one to realize what is actually happening: a flaw in the rock beneath the building has caused it to subside, but instead of moving in space, the building is falling backwards into the past. When the subsidence finally ends, the building is located several thousand years in the past, and its 2000-odd inhabitants find themselves stranded in pre-Columbian Manhattan. Chamberlain also realizes that the same seismic forces that caused the building to drop back into the past can also be used to return it to the present, but that doing so will require several weeks of intensive work by the building's inhabitants, and in the meantime they must concentrate on feeding themselves. Chamberlain convinces the president of a bank on the first floor that he can return them to the present, and together they are able to organize the other inhabitants into hunting and fishing parties. Two weeks later, Chamberlain is ready to implement his plan. He forces a jet of soapy water into an artesian well beneath the building, and this allows the pressure that has built up in the rock to be released. The building travels forward in time again, returning to the exact moment when it began to travel into the past.

Cloud computing has pervaded through every aspect of Information technology in past decade. It has become easier to process plethora of data, generated by various devices in real time, with the advent of cloud networks. The privacy of users data is maintained by data centers around the world and hence it has become feasible to operate on that data from lightweight portable devices. But with ease of processing comes the security aspect of the data. One such security aspect is secure file transfer either internally within cloud or externally from one cloud network to another. File management is central to cloud computing and it is paramount to adress the security concerns which arise out of it. This survey paper aims to elucidate the various protocols which can be used for secure file transfer and analyze the ramifications of using each protocol.

Egypt has made arrangements for the sale of a 65% interest in the state-owned Egyptian Bank for Development and Ownership. The bank, which is in fact a joint-stock company, is to be listed on the Stock Exchange of Egypt for a sum of about 900 million pounds. A consortium of 28 Egyptian and foreign banks is underwriting the issue, which the government hopes will be the largest IPO ever in Egypt. The sale is expected to yield about £900 million. The state will retain a 35% interest and the shares are expected to be listed on the Stock Exchange within a few months. The “long-term” Finance Minister Samir Radwan told the official radio that the sale would be of immense value to the government and that it would also enhance the bank’s position as a leading financial institution. The bank, which was set up in 1960, had fallen into a slump in 1994 and had to be rescued by the government. It now paid some of the interest due, but was not bringing in enough to enable it to start repaying its loans. The minister said the bank had given the government the money it needed to buy weapons from Russia. He promised that the bank would continue to play a leading role in financing government projects. The government has also recently announced plans to sell all the shares in the state-owned General Company for Industrial Projects. It is also about to sell all the shares in the Misr Insurance Company.

Elsewhere tells the story of a fifteen year old girl, Elizabeth 'Liz' Hall, who dies in a bicycle accident and wakes up to find herself traveling on a boat called the SS Nile. There, she meets a girl who had been shot and a famous musician who had died of a drug overdose. After watching her own funeral through Binoculars on the Observation decks, Liz realizes that she is truly dead. Soon afterward, she and the other passengers arrive in what is known as "Elsewhere". She meets her grandmother, Betty, who had died before Liz was born, and Liz begins to live with her. In Elsewhere, Liz learns everyone ages backwards from the day they die until they turn 7 days old, and then they are placed in the river and return to Earth as babies to begin a new life. Liz misses life on Earth, and becomes obsessed with watching her family and friends through binoculars situated on the Observation Decks. She tried to make contact with her family a few times, but gets caught by Owen with whom she falls in love. She is depressed, but in time she makes new friends in Elsewhere who help her come to terms with the fact that she has died. She gets a job working with dogs arriving from earth and realizes she can speak canine. Gradually, she learns that a life lived backwards is not much different to a life lived forwards.
