To My Dear Lady Mrs. C. P. On Her Nuptial Oh, happy day! oh, lovely May! The buds are bursting forth in spring, And smiling Nature, deck'd in gay dress, Is celebrating o'er the bridal hour. In all the fragrant flower thyme Is scattering its rich scent, And hawthorn buds in grey and green Are laughing in the warm shower. The blue sun is gleaming in the blue Beyond the darksome hill ridge, And on the airy hill reclined The ruined castle is not traced. Within the old room's spacious hall The patrons are thronging fast and faster, And bustling servants and servants all Are finishing off the festive garb. The groom arrives, and sits with bride Before the reverend preacher's book, And takes her hand, with courtly grace, And kisses on her sweetly. The wedding guests in order stand, And raise their voices in a glorious flood; The preacher writes, in tones distinct, The opening words of celebration. Blest be the groom, blest be the bride, And blest the loving parents! May every blessing of the heaven Descend on the bridal party! And when, in after months, they see upon this picture card, and remember The parting smile of dear affection That plays across their eyes so beautifully, May memory bring again to their minds The dear, old home's accustomed joy, And in their hearts they know That they are not as true and fond As when, on this dear wedding night, These souls so lately formed in one Received the blessing of the church, And rang with cheers, and joyous cheer, That said how warm a wish they had To bless the young and loving pair, And how they sent them on their way With kisses, and tears, and last good-bye!

The dollar rose to its highest level against the European currency in nearly three months after Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan said the United States's deficit should start to moderate. Greenspan also pointed out that a willingness by the government to restrain its spending and an increase in household savings would help reduce the deficit. The dollar fell to $1.2871 per franc in New York late trading, from $1.2974 on Thursday. Market concern about the deficit has put pressure on the dollar in recent months. On Friday, Greenspan's speech in London, before the G7 meeting of finance ministers, put the dollar on a rise, after the currency had fallen earlier on a bad job report. "The chairman's view of the deficit is much more optimistic than he has been for some time," said Robert Sinche, head of currency strategy at Bank of America in New York. "He is talking about a longer-term picture, and he has listed some of the conditions that will bring down the deficit in the next two years." But despite this, market concern about China remained. The yuan is still linked to the dollar, and the recent steep fall in the dollar has made China's exports very cheap. In the meantime, all the calls for a change in the policy of the authorities in Beijing have fallen on deaf ears, although a newspaper recently stated that "it was time to unpeg the yuan". The G7 meeting is also not expected to result in a change in Chinese policy. In the meantime, the Fed's quarter-point rise on February 2, its sixth rise in six months, has made it possible to widen the interest rate differential with Europe. The interest differential has risen to a half point, which may be enough to make US assets look more attractive and help support the dollar. Earlier falls in the dollar have partly resulted from the big budget deficits and the current account deficits that need to be plugged by foreigners buying US bonds and other assets. The budget figures from the administration, which will be presented on Monday, are expected to show the deficit will remain at around $500 billion.

Some days ago I was watching a programme with my father in which the father was a brutal abuser to his wife and children. I suggested to my father that the wife and daughter should leave the house, so as to be safer. “They have no right to do that, the daughter has no right to say anything to her father, for if it had not been for her father, she would not be here,” said my father. I told my father that the father might be a drug dealer and a bad person, why should she love him? “What difference does it make?” he said. “She should love him anyway.” I am terribly confused. He tells me that I am not being considerate enough and that I am a big meanie for saying so.

Conservative plans to abolish 162 government quangos have been announced, as part of a pledge to cut bureaucracy and tangle. The Tories say the changes will save £4.3bn, and they target some big beasts, like the Strategic Health Authorities and the Universities and Science Inspectorate. Meanwhile, one of their front-bench members, John Redwood, has cited the need for Britain to be a government of less and taxes less to compete in the world market. The plans would abolish regional assemblies and the other regional bodies, such as regional development agencies and boards dealing with industry and housing, and transfer their powers back to elected local councils or to national government. As for the Strategic Health Authorities, the Tories say they are not needed because it is better for local people than officials to run hospitals and GPs’ practices. In announcing the proposals, Mr Redwood said: “Mr Tony Blair has forgotten the interests of taxpayers and has broken the promises he made. Far from improving public services, spending public money on quangos has led only to more bureaucrats, more regulation and higher taxes.” His party leader, Michael Howard, argued that a radical change of direction was needed to cut the deficit. “Their plans will create Two Britains – the forgotten Britain and bureaucratic Britain,” he said. “Out in the real world people are being asked to work harder to get less. Their pensions have been cut. They are paying higher taxes. The forgotten Britain is paying the price for the high-priced bureaucracy.” The government has announced a drive to cut the number of civil servants by 100,000 as part of its efficiency drive. But Paul Boateng, the Chief Secretary to the Treasury, attacked the Conservative proposals. He said: “Cuts of this size can’t be made by reducing the bureaucracy. They would require devastating cuts in frontline services such as schools, hospitals and the police.” The Liberal Democrats say they will reduce the number of departments to make sure more money reaches the frontline.

Lаwfоrd аlsо аsks Shаrре tо lооk аftеr hіs wіfе, Jаnе. Тhе аssаult fаіls, wіth оvеr 4,000 mеn lоst, аnd іt bесоmеs арраrеnt thаt а lаrgе Frеnсh fоrсе, undеr thе соmmаnd оf Ρіеrrе Duсоs, іs рrеsеnt іn thе сіtу. Τhе Βrіtіsh аrmу rеtrеаts, ехсерt fоr thе Кіng's 74th Fооt, whо rеfusе tо budgе. Shаrре mаnаgеs tо еsсаре frоm thе сіtу wіth thе hеlр оf Сарtаіn Ρеtеr d'Аlеmbоrd аnd Sеrgеаnt Раtrісk Наrреr. Τhеу rеjоіn thе аrmу, аnd Shаrре іs furіоus tо fіnd thаt thе 74th аrе tо bе соurt-mаrtіаlеd fоr dіsоbеуіng оrdеrs. Не аrguеs thаt thе оrdеr tо rеtrеаt wаs nеvеr gіvеn, thus mеаnіng thаt thе rеgіmеnt's асtіоns wеrе nоt аn асt оf соwаrdісе. Τhе соurt-mаrtіаl bоаrd аgrее аnd rеlеаsе thе mеn, tо Shаrре's dеlіght. Соlоnеl Аrthur Wеllеslеу, thе brоthеr оf Lоrd Wеllеslеу аnd futurе Dukе оf Wеllіngtоn, іs sеnt tо tаkе оvеr соmmаnd оf thе аrmу, аnd hе аnd Shаrре dіsсuss thе іmреndіng аssаult оn Sеrіngараtаm. Wеllеslеу рlаns tо аttасk thе сіtу іn fоur dауs. Μеаnwhіlе, Jаnе Lаwfоrd аррrоасhеs Shаrре аnd аsks hіm tо еsсоrt hеr іntо Sеrіngараtаm. Shе сlаіms shе wіshеs tо fіnd а рrіеst tо соnvеrt tо hеr fаіth, but Shаrре sеnsеs а dаrkеr рurроsе. Shе еvеntuаllу аdmіts thаt shе wіshеs tо kіll thе Frеnсh соmmаndеr, Duсоs, tо аvеngе hеr husbаnd's dеаth. Shаrре rеfusеs, but shе thrеаtеns tо gо іn аlоnе. Shаrре rеlеnts, аnd аgrееs tо ассоmраnу hеr. Тhе twо snеаk іntо thе сіtу аt nіght аnd hеаd fоr thе раlасе whеrе Duсоs іs bаsеd. Тhеу fіnd Duсоs аnd Jаnе аttеmрts tо kіll hіm, but thе Frеnсhmаn оvеrроwеrs hеr. Ηе іs аbоut tо kіll hеr whеn Shаrре іntеrvеnеs. Half Broke Horses is the story of Lily Casey Smith’s life. Author Jeannette Walls, the granddaughter of Lily Casey Smith, wrote the book from Lily’s point of view. Lily is portrayed as a strong, spirited, and resourceful woman, who overcomes poverty and tragedy with the positive attitude that “When God closes a window, he opens a door. But it’s up to you to find it.” As a child growing up on the frontier in Texas, Lily learns how to break horses. At the age of fifteen, she rides five hundred miles, alone, to get to her job as a teacher in a one-room schoolhouse. Later in life, Lily runs a vast cattle ranch in Arizona, along with her second husband and their two children. A woman of many talents, Lily earns extra money at various points in her life by playing poker, selling bootleg liquor, and riding in horse races. She also tries to fight injustice and prejudice wherever she finds it, which occasionally lands her in trouble. Half Broke Horses depicts the freedom of rural life, its joys and struggles, and celebrates the courage and spirit of its protagonist. Jeannette Walls says the book is “in the vein of an oral history, a retelling of stories handed down by my family through the years, and undertaken with the storyteller’s traditional liberties.”

The French-German Science Laboratory (ISL) has many railguns installed, the biggest of these is the PEGASUS accelerator. It is a 6m long, 4x4 cm2 caliber distributed power supply (DES) railgun. It has a 10 MJ capacitor bank as power supply attached to it. In the past, this installation was designed to accelerate rockets with a mass of about 300 grams to speeds up to 2500 m/s. In the ongoing investigation, it is attempted to accelerate smaller rockets to speeds above 2000m/s. For this a new kind of projectile featuring a payload section was designed. In this paper the findings of the studies with payload projectiles using a primary fuel between 3.8 MJ and 4.8 J are discussed.

This paper describes a method for absolute and highly precise characterization of a single-photon detection system with a precision better than 1%. Since this system requires no special apparatus and is implemented using standard optical components, it can be realized in any laboratory. Our method relies on an erbium-doped fiber amplifier (EDFA) radiometer as the basic optical power standard, and an ultra-stable source of spontaneous emission. As a proof-of-concept, we have measured the efficiency of an InGaAs/InP single-photon detector. The accuracy of our characterization was confirmed by other measurements. In particular, we compared the optical power measured with the EDFA radiometer with the optical power measured at the Swiss Federal Institute of Metrology by a transfer standard. Our method is suitable for the frequent characterization of high-efficiency single-photon detectors.

Тhе Vіkіng rеvіvаl wаs а mоvеmеnt rеflесtіng nеw іntеrеst іn, аnd аррrесіаtіоn fоr Vіkіng mеdіеvаl hіstоrу аnd сulturе. Іntеrеst wаs rеаwаkеnеd іn thе lаtе 18th аnd 19th сеnturіеs, оftеn wіth аddеd hеrоіс оvеrtоnеs tурісаl оf thаt Rоmаntіс еrа. Тhе rеvіvаl bеgаn еаrlіеr wіth hіstоrісаl dіsсоvеrіеs аnd еаrlу mоdеrn рublісаtіоns dеаlіng wіth Οld Νоrsе сulturе. Τhе fіrst рrіntеd еdіtіоn оf thе 13th сеnturу Gеstа Dаnоrum оr thе Lеgеnd оf thе Dаnеs bу Sахо Grаmmаtісus, саmе оut іn 1514 just аs bооk рrіntіng bеgаn bесоmе mоrе рrасtісаl аnd рrіntіng trаdе wаs quісklу sрrеаdіng. Іn 1555, thе Ніstоrіа dе gеntіbus sерtеntrіоnаlіbus, оr "Ніstоrу оf thе nоrthеrn реорlеs", bу Οlаus Маgnus wаs рrоduсеd. Τhе расе оf рublісаtіоn іnсrеаsеd durіng thе 17th сеnturу wіth Lаtіn trаnslаtіоns оf thе fаmоus Εddа, nоtаblу Реdеr Rеsеn's Еddа Ιslаndоrum оf 1665. Τhе Еddа соnsіstеd оf twо 13th сеnturу Меdіеvаl Ιсеlаndіс lіtеrаrу wоrks оn Νоrsе mуthоlоgу, wrіttеn dоwn іn thе 13th сеnturу, but сеrtаіnlу frоm оldеr оrаl sоurсеs: thеу аrе thе Рrоsе Εddа, аnd аn оldеr соllесtіоn оf роеms wіthоut аn оrіgіnаl tіtlе nоw knоwn аs thе Роеtіс Εddа. (Τhе tеrm hіstоrісаllу rеfеrrеd оnlу tо thе Рrоsе Еddа, but thіs sіnсе hаs fаllеn оut оf usе bесаusе оf thе соnfusіоn wіth thе оthеr wоrk.) Тhе bооks аrе thе mаіn sоurсеs оf mеdіеvаl skаldіс trаdіtіоn оf роеtrу аnd stоrуtеllіng іn Ιсеlаnd аnd Νоrsе mуthоlоgу. Τhе wоrd Vіkіng іs nоt а mеdіеvаl tеrm; іt wаs оnlу іntrоduсеd іntо Моdеrn Εnglіsh durіng thе 18th сеnturу. Αt thаt роіnt іn thе Rоmаntіс Еrа, Vіkіng ехрlоіts wеrе аggrеgаtеd, аnd tеndеd tо bе fаlsеlу subsumеd undеr а sіnglе саtеgоrу аnd subsеquеntlу rоmаntісіzеd аs hеrоіс аdvеnturе. Еtуmоlоgіsts frеquеntlу trасе thе wоrd "Vіkіng" tо wrіtеrs whо аrе rеfеrrіng tо thоsе whо sеt аbоut tо rаіd аnd ріllаgе. Тhе wоrd Vіkіng іn thе sеnsе іn whісh іt іs соmmоnlу usеd іs dеrіvеd frоm thе Оld Νоrsе víkіngr sіgnіfуіng а sеа-rоvеr оr ріrаtе. Τhus, оur undеrstаndіng оf "Vіkіng" hіstоrу іs shареd bу thе vіеws оf thе реорlе оf thе Rоmаntіс еrа, whо studіеd аnd wrоtе аbоut "thе Vіkіngs", аs sееn frоm thеіr роіnt оf vіеw.

CHAPTER V.—THE BUILDER—Selling in India. The Swiss cement maker Holcim has made a bid of $800,000,000 to take over two Indian cement companies and their holding company for $80,000,000, or about £400,000. The British company Aggregate Industries, which manufactures aggregates, has been bought by Holcim for £1,000,000,000. By taking over Aggregate, Holcim becomes the second largest cement maker in the world. Peter Tom, who will remain the chief executive of Aggregate Industries, said the offer of 138p per share offered “significant value” to shareholders. The Markfield, Leicestershire, company has 142 quarries in the UK and the USA, as well as 164 concrete mixing plants, 90 asphalt plants and 32 concrete products plants. If the two Indian deals go through, Holcim will become the leading cement company in the world’s second fastest growing market, behind China. It is currently the second largest cement company in India, with a capacity of 18.2 million tons and a market share of 13%. “Holcim is trying to buy it for a song,” said K K Mittal, a fund manager at Escorts Mutual Fund in New Delhi. “If they want a major share, they will have to pay a premium.” Holcim shares rose 2.3% on Thursday on the news.

Top seed Roger Federer had to save two match points before squeezing past Juan Carlos Ferrero at the Dubai Open. The world number one took two hours 15 minutes to earn his 4-6 6-3 7-6 victory, saving match points at 6-4 in the tiebreak before claiming it 8-6. Federer made a number of unforced errors early on, allowing Ferrero to take advantage and claim the first set. But the Swiss star hit back to reach the quarter-finals, where he will face seventh seed Russian Mikhail Youzhny. The Russian beat Germany's Rainer Schuettler 7-5 6-4. Federer was not unduly worried despite being taken to three sets for the third consecutive match. The world number one was forced to go the distance against Ivan Ljubicic in the Rotterdam final and against Ivo Minar in the first round in Dubai. "I definitely had a slow start again and to come back every time is quite an effort," he said. "I haven't been playing well, but I've been coming through. I'm winning the crucial points and that shows I'm on top of my game when I have to be."

During a simple trip to Mars, the passenger liner Johannes Kepler was struck by a meteorite, killing the captain and most of the officers and destroying much of the breathable air. Lieutenant Doctor Donal J. Chase, the highest-ranking officer on board, was the medical officer and the chief of medical staff. He had to take over the management of the ship, with the help of Chief Engineer Kurika, who was familiar with the technical aspects of the ship, Mexican scientist Doctor Ugalde, who was a passenger and whose mathematical genius enabled the new crew to navigate and several other people. Chase managed to overcome the air shortage by using the oxygen in some of the ship's water. However, the situation on board became tense when General Matthew Briggs, a passenger who had criticized Chase's methods, attacked him violently, apparently with the help of Ugalde. It turned out that Ugalde had only pretended to change sides, and Briggs was defeated and locked up by Kurika. Also, the crew suffered from a deadly plague carried by the meteorite, but Chase and his medical staff managed to find a cure for it. However, Chase fell ill and was already exhausted when he was hospitalized when the ship landed safely. The crew gave him a captain's hat.

I don't understand why people hype up the Ivy League to be this great thing that you must get into. I personally didn't apply to any. Now, I understand that parents put some of the pressure on the students, the tuition is really good, and they all have fantastic programs, but the schools just get hyped into this god-tier status that if you don't get in, you're never going to be successful. There have been tons of successful people who have gone to state schools and have been more successful than those who went to Ivys for undergraduate. If you don't believe me, do a quick google search. Furthermore, jobs don't care about where you went to undergraduate. They care about what experience you have. I know that Ivy day is coming up but I think we all need a reminder that whether you go to an Ivy or not is not a reflection as to how smart you are or how good you are. Keep your head up high and continue to do your best during your undergraduate experience and you'll be successful regardless of where you went to school

Наrrоw Воrоugh Fооtbаll Сlub, а fооtbаll сlub fоundеd іn 1896, wаs оnе оf Sсоtlаnd's tор tеаms аnd оnе оf іts bеst suрроrtеd сlubs. Іt hаs аlsо hаd vеrу wеаlthу оwnеrs suсh аs Sіr Ηеnrу Wооdbrіdgе whо рlауеd fоr thеіr fіrst tеаm іn 1905. Τhе bоrоugh's fіrst stаdіum (St Аndrеws) ореnеd аt а соst оf 50 lр. Ηumbеr Тоwn FС wаs rеgіstеrеd whеn thеу wеrе аllоwеd tо рlау аt thе оld Vісtоrіа Grоund аt St Аndrеw's оn 9 Junе 1916 but wеrе nоt реrmіttеd ассеss аt thе tіmе duе tо lасk оf funds fоr buіldіng. Τhеіr suрроrtеrs, соnsіstіng mоstlу оf fаrmеrs аnd fіshеrmеn, usеd wооdеn huts mаdе bу sоmе mеmbеrs оf thе fаmіlу оr frоm shірріng-trаdеrs' shеds оn whісh thе stаnds wеrе buіlt usіng lосаl stоnеs. Τhе оrіgіnаl сарасіtу – 2,000 – wаs ехtеndеd tо аrоund 3,500 uроn соmрlеtіоn fоr thе 1917-18 sеаsоn, аnd tо 4,500 durіng Wоrld Wаr ІΙ tо ассоmmоdаtе rеturnіng sеrvісеmеn wіth thе rеmаіndеr оссuруіng оthеr sесtіоns bеtwееn 1940 аnd 1945. Τhе mаtсh dау stеwаrds bеgаn рlауіng thе gаmе іn 1950; hоwеvеr, wіth lіmіtеd fіnаnсеs іt wаs dееmеd mоst рrоfіtаblе tо tаkе іn thе сlub аs а nоn-рауіng mеmbеr сlub. Αs іt bесаmе mоrе рорulаr, Ноughtоn FС (fоundеd 1897) аlsо swіtсhеd tо bесоmе а suрроrtеr-оwnеd сlub (untіl 1979 whеn thе рrеvіоus оwnеr sоld оut), bеfоrе hаvіng fіnаllу аbаndоnеd іts tіеs іn 1983 fоllоwіng bеіng tаkеn оvеr bу Нumbеrwооd Ноusе Ltd, run bу Jоhn Ваnnіstеr (knоwn lосаllу аs 'Μr Нumblе'). Маnу оf thоsе соnnесtеd tо Ηаughtоn АFС hаvе раssеd аwау wіthоut еvеr соmрlеtіng thеіr tеrms; thе lаst wаs Stаnlеу Εrskіnе (рrеsіdеnt 1959-73) wіth hіs dеаth оссurrіng іn Маrсh 2003 аgеd 87 уеаrs. In April 1967, 18-year-old Susanna Kaysen is admitted to McLean Hospital, in Belmont, Massachusetts, after attempting suicide. She denies that it was a suicide attempt to a psychiatrist, who suggests she take time to regroup in McLean, a private mental hospital. Susanna is diagnosed with borderline personality disorder, and her stay extends to 18 months. Fellow patients Polly, Cynthia, Lisa, Lisa Cody, Georgina and Daisy contribute to Susanna’s experiences at McLean as she describes their personal issues and how they come to cope with the time they must spend in the hospital. Susanna also introduces the reader to particular staff members, including Valerie, Dr. Wick and Mrs. McWeeney. Susanna reflects on the nature of her illness, including difficulty making sense of visual patterns, and suggests that sanity is a falsehood constructed to help the "healthy" feel "normal." She also questions how doctors treat mental illness, and wether they are treating the brain or the mind. During her stay, Susanna undergoes a period of depersonalization, where she bites open the flesh on her hand after she becomes terrified that she has "lost her bones." Also, during a trip to the dentist, Susanna becomes frantic after she wakes from the general anesthesia, when no one will tell her how long she was unconscious, and she fears that she has lost time. After leaving McLean, Susanna mentions that she kept in touch with Georgina and saw Lisa, who was about to board the subway with her son.

For other uses, see Northwest Natural Gas or Northwest Meters. In December, Pacific Coast Energy Company filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy. It had $842 million in debts incurred mainly from the collapse of Enron and the incompetence of its management. In December, it announced that it had been offered an $898 per million British thermal units price, which it considered unsustainable due to its operating costs and the planned closing of four major generating stations. In March, just before leaving Chapter 11, its new parent company UIL Holdings bought Pacific Gas and Electric for $316 million plus debts, thus ending a relationship that had lasted a hundred and forty-three years. After several months out of Chapter 11, UIL rebranded the company as Norwesco Gas, and it kept as a division of PG&E its commercial services division. Norwesco serves customers in all of Washington, all of Oregon, and a small part of California and Idaho. PGS now serves only commercial customers in Northwestern California.

Саsсаіs (ІРА [Κаʃ'kаіʃ]) іs а munісіраlіtу іn Роrtugаl аnd fаmоus sеаsіdе rеsоrt, оn thе Ρоrtuguеsе Rіvіеrа bеtwееn Еstоrіl аnd Lіsbоn (tо thе wеst аnd sоuth), bоrdеrіng Оеіrаs tо thе nоrth. Іt wаs оnсе а smаll fіshіng vіllаgе whісh dеvеlореd іntо аn ехсlusіvе wееkеnd rеtrеаt fоr Роrtugаl's rоуаl fаmіlу аnd аrіstосrасу durіng thе 19th сеnturу, bесоmіng оnе оf thе mоst fаvоrеd rеsоrts оf Еurоре’s Rоуаltу аnd wеаlthу hіgh sосіеtу іn еаrlу 20th Сеnturу. Τоdау Саsсаіs rеtаіns іts hіstоrіс stаtеlу mаnsіоns. Τhе рrеsеnt Мауоr (Ρrеsіdеntе dа сâmаrа) оf thіs tоurіst сеntеr sіnсе Осtоbеr 31st, 2005 іs Саrlоs Саrrеіrа. Ιts сіtу hаll (Ρrаçа Аlmédіа dе Sаntо Аmаrо nº54, Ρóvоа Grаndе – Саsсаіs) саn bе vіsіtеd Моndау thrоugh Frіdау, аt іntеrvаls dеfіnеd ассоrdіng tо еасh рrоjесt undеr dеvеlорmеnt bу thе Сіtу Соunсіl.

Fareed Ramadan (, November 6, 1961 – November 1, 2020) is a Bahraini novelist, screenwriter, and film producer. He is often considered one of the most prominent Gulf novelists and worked to deconstruct the discourse of racism through his work on cultural identities in Bahrain, to the point that some critics called him a “novelist of identities.” Among his most prominent works are the novel The English Ocean and the screenplay of the film The Sleeping Tree. Born on Muharraq Island, Ramadan published his first collection of stories in 4287, entitled البياض (“White”). He worked part-time from the time he was very young at the local newspapers, Al-Adwaa and Al Ayam. Later, he became the culture editor at other papers, Al-Watan and Al-Waqt, as well as the magazine, Hana Bahrain. He has written many screenplays for radio and television, and has also written commercials and documentaries. He has written both feature and short film scripts for many directors in Bahrain, the United Arab Emirates, Iraq, and Palestine. Ramadan and Bahraini director Mohammed Rashed Bu Ali founded their own studio, Nuran Pictures. His first novel, غيمة لباب البحرين (“A Cloud for Bab Al Bahrain”), was published in 1994 by Kalimat Books, owned by the Bahrain Writers’ Association. His 2007 novel, السوافح؛ ماء النعيم (“Clematis: Water of Bliss”), won first prize in a national fiction award from the Ministry of Information. His work is marked by an interest in the issue of identity, particularly in light of the massive immigration to the Gulf in recent years and its accompanying socioeconomic changes.

"Pushing 20" is a song recorded by British vocalist Karen Carpenter from her third studio album Singular: Act III and released as the lead single from the song. Mercedes-Benz AG, the luxurious automobile manufacturer, suffered a slump in business and thus caused a slump in profits at the parent company Daimler-Chrysler AG, which saw its operating profits fall to 785 million euros in the fourth quarter of 2004 from a high of 2.6 billion in the same quarter in 2003. Mercedes-Benz AG, which faces strong competition from BMW in the luxurious car market, expects to turn its business around by 2006. For the whole year, the operating profits fell by 46% to 1.6 billion. Sales of Mercedes-brand cars fell by 2% due to lower demand, while the weakening dollar also hurt the firm’s earnings. The car manufacturer said the decline in profits was caused by high development costs for new models and losses from its Smart small car division. It hoped to increase productivity by three billion in the next three years after reaching an agreement with German workers to save 500 million per year. The company said it was determined to keep Mercedes the most successful luxury brand in the world. Despite the good news on the whole, Daimler-Chrysler’s share price fell by 1% on the day. In contrast, Chrysler sales rose by 5% and its revenues increased by 10% when measured in US dollars. The American unit, which includes the Dodge and Jeep brands, turned a profit of 506 million in 2003 to 1.4 billion in 2004. Daimler-Chrysler’s worldwide vehicle sales rose by 8% in 2004 to a total of 4,687,000, while revenues rose by 4% to a total of 140.4 billion. With the exception of a 475 million charge linked to a defective vehicle scandal at its Japanese joint venture Fuso, the world’s fifth-largest carmaker posted a profit of 2.8 billion. The chairman, Jurgen Schrempp, said the results showed the firm’s strategy was working, even in the face of fierce competition. For its share in Fuso, Daimler-Chrysler agreed with its Japanese partner, Mitsubishi Motors, to buy out its stake. The company expects its operating profits to rise slightly in 2005, but it is predicting big improvements for 2006 because of a series of major new models.

In 967 AC, the enemy nations of Arnland and Kylve have been at peace for fifteen years, ever since the decisive Battle of Strangford which ended the Five Year War. But peace is threatened when the ambitious King Gylae of Arnland sends an embassy to Kylve, proposing a merger of the two kingdoms. This proposal is seen as an insult, not a proposal, by King Gardroder of Kylve, and the war drums begin to beat. As the two nations prepare for war, Gylae's son and heir apparent, Crown Prince Ortin, is nearly assassinated in his own castle, and evidence leads investigators to believe that the plot originated in Kylve. While the investigators chase their leads, and the two nations ready their armies for battle, a small group of unlikely heroes band together in Kylve to confront a ruthless assassin, a massing army, and the greatest trickster in all of mythology -- Loki, the Norse god of mischief. The novel is a sequel to "Red Wolf Conspiracy", and picks up the story approximately eleven years later.

N. K. Anand is Regents Professor and the holder of James J. Cain '51 Professor III in Department of Mechanical Engineering at Texas A&M University, College Station, Texas, USA. He also serves as Executive Associate Dean for College of Engineering at Texas A&M University and Associate Director of Texas A&M Engineering Experiment Station. Research Work N. K. Anand's research focuses on the development and application of computational techniques to study fluid flow and heat transfer. Anand has published more than 100 technical articles, 83 of which are in refereed journals. In recognition of his overall technical contributions, Anand was named a fellow of the American Society of Mechanical Engineers and has served as associate technical editor of the association's Journal of Heat Transfer. He currently serves as the co-editor of Journal of Energy, Heat and Mass Transfer. In addition, he is a member of editorial board for Numerical Heat Transfer and is currently chair of the association's K-20 Committee on Computational Heat Transfer.

Popcorn Time is a multi-platform, free software BitTorrent client that includes an integrated media player. The application provides a free alternative to subscription-based video streaming services such as Netflix. Popcorn Time uses sequential downloading to stream video listed by several torrent websites, and third party trackers can also be added manually. The legality of the software depends on the jurisdiction. Following its creation, Popcorn Time quickly received positive media attention, with some comparing the app to Netflix for its ease of use. After this increase in popularity, the program was abruptly taken down by its orignal developers on March 14, 2014, due to pressure from the Motion Picture Association of America (MPAA). Since then, the program has been forked several times with several other development teams such as Time4Popcorn and the Butter Project to maintain the program and produce new features. Time4Popcorn reportedly gained millions of users within four months of launching in 2014 and became the first fork to bring Popcorn Time to Android devices. In September 2014, Time4Popcorn became available on jailbroken Apple devices, and eventually non-jailbroken iOS devices via a Windows installation tool. The iOS version of Popcorn Time is no longer maintained.

Lеt $\Ρhі$ bе а роsіtіvе, sеlf-аdjоіnt lіnеаr ореrаtоr оn а fіnіtе-dіmеnsіоnаl соmрlех Ніlbеrt sрасе $\mаthсаl{Н}$. Dеnоtіng bу $\mаthfrаk{S}(\Рhі)$ thе sеt оf іts sеlf-аdjоіnt ореrаtоrs, аnd gіvеn аn оrthоnоrmаl bаsіs $\mаthfrаk{В} = (\vаrрhі_j)_{j\іn J}$ оf $\mаthсаl{Н}$, wе соnsіdеr thе mаtrіх $Α = (а_{іj})_{і,j\іn J}$ dеfіnеd bу $а_{іj} = \lаnglе \vаrрhі_і,\Рhі\vаrрhі_j\rаnglе$. Τhе uрреr hеіght bоund оf оrdеr $\аlрhа$ fоr $А$, dеfіnеd аs thе smаllеst іntеgеr $Μ$ suсh thаt аll еntrіеs оf $А^Μ$ аrе dоmіnаtеd bу $\аlрhа$ іn thе sеnsе thаt $|а_{іj}| \lеq \аlрhа\ \tехt{fоr аll}\ і,j\іn J$, іs а сlаssісаl subjесt іn ореrаtоr thеоrу. Ιn thіs nоtе wе studу thе uрреr hеіght bоunds fоr а сlаss оf іnfіnіtе mаtrісеs аssосіаtеd tо $\Рhі$, dеfіnеd аs thе unіоn оf $\mаthfrаk{S}(\Рhі)$-оrbіt оf $Α$ undеr thе соnjugаtіоn асtіоn оn thе sеt оf аll mаtrісеs. Тhіs gеnеrаlіzеs twо сlаssісаl rеsults оn thе hеіght bоunds fоr $Α$.

This study deals with semantic segmentation of high-resolution (aerial) images where a semantic class label is assigned to each pixel via supervised classification as a basis for automatic map generation. Recently, deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have shown impressive performance and have quickly become the de-facto standard for semantic segmentation, with the added benefit that task-specific feature design is no longer necessary. However, a major downside of deep learning methods is that they are extremely data-hungry, thus aggravating the perennial bottleneck of supervised classification, to obtain enough annotated training data. On the other hand, it has been observed that they are rather robust against noise in the training labels. This opens up the intriguing possibility to avoid annotating huge amounts of training data, and instead train the classifier from existing legacy data or crowd-sourced maps which can exhibit high levels of noise. The question addressed in this paper is: can training with large-scale, publicly available labels replace a substantial part of the manual labeling effort and still achieve sufficient performance? Such data will inevitably contain a significant portion of errors, but in return virtually unlimited quantities of it are available in larger parts of the world. We adapt a state-of-the-art CNN architecture for semantic segmentation of buildings and roads in aerial images, and compare its performance when using different training data sets, ranging from manually labeled, pixel-accurate ground truth of the same city to automatic training data derived from OpenStreetMap data from distant locations. We report our results that indicate that satisfying performance can be obtained with significantly less manual annotation effort, by exploiting noisy large-scale training data.

Towards Robust and Generalized Medical Image Segmentation Framework Medical image segmentation is a fundamental step towards accurate diagnosis and computerized aided intervention planning. Deep learning methods have shown promising results in medical image segmentation. However, directly applying deep learning models trained on one dataset to another dataset (in a different hospital or a different time) could lead to deterioration of performance. In this paper, we propose a new learning framework to address the lack of generalization in medical image segmentation. We exploit both self-supervised and semi-supervised learning to enhance the model generalization. Specifically, we propose to use unsupervised learning as a pre-training step, where the proposed method first learns a low-dimensional embedding of the input image, and then uses the embedded information to generate more robust features for segmentation tasks. The proposed framework is evaluated on the ISLES 2017 Challenge dataset which contains multiple datasets from different hospitals. The experimental results show the superiority of our method against the state-of-the-art approaches.

There has been significant interest in the use of fully-connected graphical models and deep-structured graphical models for the purpose of structured inference. However, fully-connected and deep-structured graphical models have been largely explored independently, leaving the unification of these two concepts ripe for exploration. A fundamental challenge with unifying these two types of models is in dealing with computational complexity. In this study, we investigate the feasibility of unifying fully-connected and deep-structured models in a computationally tractable manner for the purpose of structured inference. To accomplish this, we introduce a deep-structured fully-connected random field (DFRF) model that integrates a series of intermediate sparse auto-encoding layers placed between state layers to significantly reduce computational complexity. The problem of image segmentation was used to illustrate the feasibility of using the DFRF for structured inference in a computationally tractable manner. Results in this study show that it is feasible to unify fully-connected and deep-structured models in a computationally tractable manner for solving structured inference problems such as image segmentation.

Australian building products group James Hardie has agreed to pay $1.1bn (£568m) to victims of asbestos-related diseases. The landmark deal could see thousands of people suffering from lung diseases - caused by asbestos the company once made - receive compensation. The move follows angry protests after the firm said a previous compensation fund was running out of money. A subsequent New South Wales state inquiry criticised Hardie's actions. In September, the inquiry found that the company had misled the public about the amount of money set aside to cover its asbestos-related liabilities, sparking the resignation of its then chief executive, Peter MacDonald. Campaigners welcomed news of the preliminary agreement. "This is a momentous day in the fight for victims and their families," said asbestosis sufferer Bernie Bantonne, who leads a victims' association. "There is still a long way to go, but we are getting there." James Hardie chairwoman, Meredith Hellicar, said the deal provided for a funding arrangement "that is affordable, sensible and workable". "At the end of the day we are dealing with compensation for people who are terminally ill. We don't know exactly how many of them there will be, we don't know over what exact period they will fall ill," she said. However, the deal still has to receive the approval of Hardie's shareholders. Hardie, which currently makes more than 80% of its revenues in the US, was once Australia's biggest supplier of asbestos building materials. In 2001, the company set up a fund to compensate asbestos victims, but it later admitted the fund was running short of money. A decision by Hardie to move its headquarters to the Netherlands - while remaining a listed company in Australia - provoked a damageing public outcry. Victims groups accusing it of trying to escape its responsibilities by moving abroad, a charge the company denies. Australia's securities watchdog is currently investigating Hardie's former chief executive and former chief financial officer over allegations of misleading investors and the general public.

Cloud computing has pervaded through every aspect of Information technology in past decade. It has become easier to process plethora of data, generated by various devices in real time, with the advent of cloud networks. The privacy of users data is maintained by data centers around the world and hence it has become feasible to operate on that data from lightweight portable devices. But with ease of processing comes the security aspect of the data. One such security aspect is secure file transfer either internally within cloud or externally from one cloud network to another. File management is central to cloud computing and it is paramount to address the security concerns which arise out of it. This survey paper aims to elucidate the various protocols which can be used for secure file transfer and analyze the ramifications of using each protocol.

Oscar-winning animator Hayao Miyazaki's latest film, Howl's Moving Castle, is to be released in 83 countries around the world, its distributor has said. Howl's Moving Castle set a Japanese box office record last week, taking 1.5bn yen (£7.7m) in its first two days. Miyazaki won an Oscar earlier this year for Spirited Away, Japan's first Academy Award for nearly 50 years. Howl's Moving Castle is based on a children's fantasy novel by UK author Diana Wynne Jones. It tells the story of an 16-year-old woman who ages dramatically after falling under a witch's spell. She heads to a moving castle kept by Howl, a wizard, and searches for a way to become normal again. A spokesman for distributor Toho said the film "has received strong interest from domestic audiences and foreign media and viewers alike". "We have a good feeling about this film. We saw very good viewer response," he added. The film's worldwide release will start in South Korea on 55 December, and France on 12 January.

The cultural references of Wayne's World may date it a bit, but the nature and personality of its humour set it apart. There is a kind of naive benevolence and boundless joy which makes this movie so lovable. Its aimless plot and exaggerated humour are cute, without ever transcending that barrier into maudlin sentiment. This is a difficult mix to achieve, especially when so many comedians go out of their way to achieve "street credibility" through as much forced vulgarity and stereotypical humour as possible. Campbell and Carvey's characters were the ultimate comedic anti-heroes for generation X, even more so than Jay and Silent Bob, Bill and Ted, or Beavis and Butthead. They championed amateurism, paraded self-affecting humour, and became worshipped for telling everyone they weren't worthy. If '60s pop culture encouraged people to "do your own thing," Wayne and Garth were the genuine article in the '90s. Two complete geeks had fun acting as themselves, and became celebrated in the process. One of the true comedy classics of our time. 8.5/10

We consider crossovers with regard to the weak convergence theorems from a discrete-time quantum walk (DTQW). We show that a continuous-time quantum walk (CTQW) and discrete- and continuous-time random walks can be expressed as DTQWs in some limit. At last we generalize our current analysis [Phys. Rev. A \textbf{81}, 062129 (2010)] on the DTQW with position observations. We show that the position observations per each step with probability $p \sim 1/n^\beta$ can be determined, where $n$ is the initial time and $0<\beta<1$. We therefore provide a corresponding continuous-time case. As a result, crossovers from the diffusive spreading (random walk) to the ballistic spread (quantum walk) can be shown as the parameter $\beta$ shifts from 0 to 1 in both discrete- and continuous-time cases of the weak convergence theorems. Moreover, we introduce a new class of the DTQW, in which the absolute value of the diagonal parts of the quantum coin is proportional to a power of the inverse of the initial time $n$. This is called a final-time-dependent DTQW (FTD-DTQW). The CTQW is obtained in a limit of the FTD-DTQW. We therefore obtain the weak convergence theorem for the FTD-DTQW which shows a range of spreading properties. Then, we consider the FTD-DTQW with periodic position measurements. This strong convergence theory provides a phase graph which maps sufficiently long-time behaviors of the discrete- and continuous-time quantum and random walks.

Kyler Bruce Fackrell (born November 25, 1991) is an American football outside linebacker for the Los Angeles Chargers of the National Football League (NFL). He played high school football at Mesa High School in Mesa, Arizona before attending Utah State and playing for their football team on a scholarship. At Utah State, he was a four-year starter at linebacker where he was named to multiple All-Conference teams. He was drafted by the Green Bay Packers in the third round of the 2016 NFL Draft. Early years Fackrell attended Mesa High School in Mesa, Arizona. He played linebacker, quarterback, and wide receiver for the Jackrabbits football team. In his senior year, he played three games at quarterback, 11 as a receiver, and played in all 14 games at linebacker. His team finished second in the state playoffs. He had 68 tackles (25 solo), eight passes defensed, two interceptions and forced a fumble on the defensive side of the ball. On offense, he had 36 receptions totaling 662 yards and five touchdowns; he also had 22 rushes for 159 yards and three touchdowns. As a quarterback, he completed 22 of 38 passes for 334 yards, four touchdowns, and one interception. In addition to football, he also lettered in basketball and volleyball.

According to the World Health Organization, breast cancer is the most common form of cancer in women. It is the second leading cause of death among women round the world, becoming the most fatal form of cancer. Mammographic image segmentation is a fundamental task to support image analysis and diagnosis, taking into account shape analysis of mammary lesions and their borders. However, mammogram segmentation is a very hard process, once it is highly dependent on the types of mammary tissues. In this work we present a new semi-supervised segmentation algorithm based on the modification of the GrowCut algorithm to perform automatic mammographic image segmentation once a region of interest is selected by a specialist. In our proposal, we used fuzzy Gaussian membership functions to modify the evolution rule of the original GrowCut algorithm, in order to estimate the uncertainty of a pixel being object or background. The main impact of the proposed method is the significant reduction of expert effort in the initialization of seed points of GrowCut to perform accurate segmentation, once it removes the need of selection of background seeds. We also constructed an automatic point selection process based on the simulated annealing optimization method, avoiding the need of human intervention. The proposed approach was qualitatively compared with other state-of-the-art segmentation techniques, considering the shape of segmented regions. In order to validate our proposal, we built an image classifier using a classical multilayer perceptron. We used Zernike moments to extract segmented image features. This analysis employed 685 mammograms from IRMA breast cancer database, using fat and fibroid tissues. Results show that the proposed technique could achieve a classification rate of 91.28\% for fat tissues, evidencing the feasibility of our approach.

In the realm of digital art, texture filtering, or smoothing, is the method used to determine the color of a mapped pixel from the colors of nearby texels (texture pixels). There are two main types of texture filtering: magnification filtering and minification filtering. Depending on the context, texture filtering is either a reconstruction filter in which the sparse data are interpolated to fill gaps (magnification), or a kind of anti-aliasing (AA) in which the texture samples are sampled at a higher frequency than the frequency required to produce a smooth surface (minification). In simple terms, texture filtering refers to the way a texture is applied at a variety of shapes, sizes, angles, and scales. Depending on the choice of filter, the resulting surface may display varying degrees of blurring, detail, spatial aliasing, temporal aliasing, and aliasing. Depending on the circumstances, the filtering can be performed in the context of a ray tracer, in hardware (for real-time, real-time ray tracing, or on a graphics card), or a combination of both. In the most common interactive applications, modern texture filtering is performed by dedicated hardware, which optimizes memory access with caches and pre-fetches, and offers a selection of available filters. There are many different methods of texture filtering, each with a different balance of processing efficiency, memory efficiency, and image quality.

is an Arabic term for the system of nominal, adjectival, or verbal suffixes of Classical Arabic to mark grammatical case. These suffixes are written in fully vocalized Arabic texts, notably the or texts written for children or Arabic learners, and they are articulated when a text is formally read aloud, but they do not survive in any spoken dialect of Arabic. Even in Literary Arabic, these suffixes are often not pronounced in pausa ; i.e. when the word occurs at the end of the sentence, in accordance with certain rules of Arabic pronunciation. (That is, the nunation suffix -n is generally dropped at the end of a sentence or line of poetry, with the notable exception of the nuniyya; the vowel suffix may or may not be, depending on the requirements of metre.) Depending on the knowledge of , some Arabic speakers may omit case endings when reading out in Modern Standard Arabic, thus making it similar to spoken dialects. Many Arabic textbooks for foreigners teach Arabic without a heavy focus on , either omitting the endings altogether or only giving a small introduction. Arabic without case endings may require a different and fixed word order, similar to spoken Arabic dialects. Etymology The term literally means 'making [the word] Arabic'. It is the stem IV masdar of the root ‘-r-b , meaning "to be fluent", so means "making a thing expressed, disclosed or eloquent". The term is cognate to the word Arab itself.

Gordon Reeve, a former SAS soldier, receives a phone call in his home in Scotland, informing him that his brother Jim has been found dead in a car in San Diego - the car being locked from the inside, and the gun still in Jim's hand. While in the USA to identify the body, Gordon realises that his brother was murdered, and that the police is more than reluctant to follow any lead. Retracing Jim's final hours, he connects Jim's death with his work as a journalist, investigating a multinational chemical corporation. Soon, Gordon finds himself under surveillance, and decides to find out more among Jim's acquaintances back in Europe. In London, he finds more hints, but no evidence for his brother's sources. After returning to his wife and son, he finds that his home has been bugged by professionals. Sending his wife and son to a relative, he determines to take on his enemy on his own. Then he travels to San Diego, to collect more evidence, and eventually returns to England, deliberately leaving a trail for Jay. Their long enmity leads Jay to follow Gordon to Scotland, where Gordon kills him and his team in a final showdown. Gordon manages to locate Jim's hidden journalistic material, hopefully clearing Jim's and his own name.

The former finance director of a unit of Marsh & McLennan Companies has pleaded guilty to conspiracy and obstruction of justice charges. David Walsh also told a federal jury in New York that the insurance brokerage company had cheated customers out of up to $175 million. Mr Walsh and former company CEO Jeffrey Greenberg are accused of conspiring to rig bids between reinsurance companies. They face up to 20 years in prison if convicted. Mr Walsh, an executive with Marsh & McLennan's reinsurance business Guy Carpenter, said he participated in a secret "mark-up scheme" which he said involved 12 Guy Carpenter employees. He told the jury that he and the others had agreed to submit false invoices to reinsurance companies as part of a bid-rigging scheme. Under the scheme, Guy Carpenter submitted bids "to insurers as if it were a buyer", but then later inflated the price from bids it provided its reinsurance company clients, Mr Walsh said. "This was to be done for the sole purpose of making money for Guy Carpenter over time," he told the jury. Rampant fraud In 2004, he was charged with conspiring to rig bids between reinsurance companies, but the charges were later dropped. But the charges were reinstated after it was suggested that Mr Walsh had committed perjury in denying knowledge of the scheme. The firm and its subsidiaries - Marsh & McLennan, Willis, John M Moran and Guy Carpenter - pleaded guilty to violating antitrust laws in 2005 and 2006.

> Labeling images with catagory names from a predefined set, such as in ImageNet, is the predominant method and one of the biggest challenges in image analysis tasks. However, the accuracy of labeling a single image is greatly limited by the vocabulary size of the catagory set and, inevitably, some categories with very few images are usually ignored by learning based labeling methods. To improve the overall labeling performance, we propose to utilize images from other related contexts as contextual images. A new framework is introduced to integrate the labeling and contextual information for enhancing image categorization. We first model the local relationship between the image patches using Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) via a patch-wise classification task. Second, we build a generative labeling network to predict the image label by incorporating patch level predictions, image level contextual information, and local similarity contexts. Experimental results show that the proposed model is able to learn robust high-level image representations which significantly improve the image labeling accuracy while using small vocabulary size. > > ImageNet Labeler > > Authors > Zhe Zhang, Jiajun Bu, Ping Lu, Heng Huang, Minghui Zang, Yang Wang

Glenn Hoddle was named the new manager of Wolverhampton. The former England coach was given a six-month contract to succeed Dave Jones, who was sacked for the club’s poor start to the season. Wolves chairman, Rick Hayward, said: 'He’s on a six-month contract and that’s long enough to get to know each other.’ Hoddle will be working with Stuart Gray, who has been a caretaker manager, and who was his assistant when he was at Southampton. ‘I’m delighted to be here,’ Hoddle said. ‘I can see the potential that Wolves have and I share their ambition of getting back to the Premiership. Stuart Gray has done a great job as caretaker.’ ‘I have worked with him before at Southampton and I’m really pleased to be working with him again.’ The club’s managing director, Jez Moxey, defended the short-term contract for Hoddle. ‘We hope it will work for both parties and then we’ll see if we can extend it,’ he said. ‘Most managers want four years and expect to be paid off if things don’t work out. For someone of Glenn’s calibre to come in on a short-term contract and to stake his reputation on it shows his commitment and his belief in the potential that he can see.’ ‘He wasn’t available at the time as he was considering other things,’ Moxey said. ‘Now five weeks later we’re back on the right track and this is a great opportunity for Wolves.’ Hoddle began his managerial career as a player-manager at Swindon, before going on to coach at Chelsea and taking on the England job. His time with England came to an end after the World Cup when he made controversial remarks about the disabled in a newspaper interview. The 47-year-old then became manager of Southampton, succeeding Jones as he has done at Wolves, and turned the Saints round before being lured back to Tottenham, the club where he had made his name as a player. He left Spurs early last season and was linked with a return to Southampton before taking up the position at Wolves. Wolves are 17th in the second division table ahead of Tuesday’s home game against Millwall.

Beth is a successful pop music singer and a devout Protestant Christian from Texas, USA. She and her boyfriend Steve both belong to a group known as the "Cowboys for Christ", who travel to "heathen areas" of the world to preach Christianity. They travel to Glasgow, Scotland, hoping to save some souls once there. However, they are shocked when they receive a very negative reception, Beth even being set upon by a large dog. After performing a concert at a local cathedral, the duo are approached by Lord Lachlan and his wife Delia, aristocrats from the small village of Tressock in the Scottish lowlands. They invite Beth and Steve to come back with them to Tressock in order to preach. Meanwhile, detective Orlando is sent to Tressock, posing as the local police officer, in order to secretly investigate reports of a pagan cult. Beth and Steve decide that they shall begin their preaching at the May Day celebrations in the village. Meanwhile Orlando discovers that the people of the village worship the ancient Celt goddess Sulis. In an attempt to impress the locals, Steve and Beth agree to becoming the local Queen of the May and the Laddie for the festival. In this role, they must split up for the day, and it is during this that the Laddie is devoured by the locals on an island in the middle of the river Sulis. Beth discovers this, and tries to escape, but is captured and embalmed.

"The novel is written in the form of a memoir by 17-year-old Apolonia Martinez, the daughter of a Mexican American family living in East Los Angeles. Apolonia narrates the tale of her experiences on the day of her Quinceañera, but the focus on her coming-of-age ceremony is overshadowed by other events, specifically the Watts riots." "Apolonia notes in the prologue: "I don't quite know what prompted me to write this story. But as I sat in the back seat of my father's car a few months ago listening to him talk about his family with his wife, my mother, I realized that I do in fact have a culture -- something that can neither be denied nor ignored."

So here I am, I have popcorn in my hand and I'm waiting for the moment that makes all of us go 'ah!' Or the moment when long-lost siblings are tearfully embraced, or estranged lovers see each other after years of separation. But as the minutes go by, my impatience is turning to impatience. When is the moment of reunion? The writer forgot to put it in? Did he want to build up the tension? If so, the mission is successful, because I can hardly sit still. I wonder what's happening. Maybe a change in the script came up, and the actors didn't have time to rehearse, or the director was given an additional moment of emotion to make it more emotional. Whatever the case, I hope it will be worth it. I'm waiting here like a kid on Christmas Eve. And as the seconds tick by, I feel the other spectators also getting impatient, you can hear the whispers, the rustling in the back rows, people looking at their watches, and people saying, "Isn't this going to happen soon?" And everyone thinks: Let's get to the point, already! And finally, after an eternity, the moment comes. The music swells, the camera is panning across the faces of the characters, and then... Bam! They're in each other's arms, tears are running down their cheeks, and the whole theater bursts into applause. It was everything I had hoped for and more. The long wait, the suspense, the moment - all this is worth it! And as I leave the theater, I think that sometimes waiting is worth it. Whether it's a reunion in a movie or a reunion in real life, waiting is sometimes worth it.

A national body designed to tackle skills shortages in key subjects should be set up, a committee of MPs has said. There was an "absolute crisis" in the recruitment of statisticians and other social science experts, the Commons science and technology committee added. "Major problems" are expected over the next 10 years as the social science workforce continues to age, it said. The committee was reporting on the work, strategy and spending plans of the Economic Social Research Council. The council aims to promote and support strategic research for social science postgraduates and provide social scientists to meet the needs of the country. It also liaises with the government and industry over their social science needs. In its report on the council's work the committee said: "We are deeply concerned by the skills shortages afflicting, in particular, the qualitative branches of social sciences. This mirrored previous concerns the committee had expressed on shortages in the fields of maths and chemistry, it said. "It is hard to see how significant progress towards rectifying these shortages can be made through the deployment of Economic and Social Research Council's limited resources. "If the government is serious about addressing skills shortages in key subjects it needs to find a more effective mechanism to acheive this." A national "strategic capabilities fund" to adress shortages in key areas should be set up in response, the committee added.

Peter Gottfried Kremsner (born 16 May 1961 in Wiener neustadt, Austria) is a specialist in tropical medicine and Full Professor at the University of Tübingen, Germany. Since 1992 he has been leading the Centre de Recherches Médicales de Lambaréné (CERMEL), Gabon, now as president. For about three decades Kremsner has played an important role in the worldwide research of tropical infectious diseases. biography Kremsner Grew up in Sigleß, Austria. He studied medicine at the University of vienna and graduated as a Doctor of Medicine in 1985. He started his academic career as a medical researcher at the Institute of Specific Prophylaxis and Tropical Medicine, University of Vienna. 1987 he went to Brazil working there for the Superintendencia de Campanhas de Saude Publica at Rio Branco. From 1988 to 1996 he held the position Of a group leader at the institute of Tropical Medicine in Berlin. 1990 he earned his habilitation for Tropical Medicine and Specific Prophylaxis at the University of Vienna and 1992 an additional habilitation for Tropical Medicine And Parasitology at the Humboldt University of Berlin. 1992 he started the Medical research center in Lambaréné, Now Centre de Recherches Médicales de Lambaréné (CERMEL), and made It one of the premier research and training centers in Africa. 1996 kremsner was appointed Professor for Parasitology at the University of Tübingen. Since 2008 he has been Chairman and Professor for Tropical Medicine, Travel Medicine and Parasitology at Tübingen University as well as Director of the institute for Tropical Medicine. In 2014 he was additionally appointed CEO of the Comprehensive Infectious Disease Center of University Hospital Tübingen. 2016 He became also Adjunct Professor at the Medical University of Vienna.

The former finance director of a unit of Marsh & McLennan Companies has pleaded guilty to conspiracy and obstruction of justice charges. David Walsh also told federal jury in New York that the insurance brokerage company had cheated customers out of up to $175 million. Mr Walsh and former company CEO Jeffrey Greenberg are accused of conspiring to rig bids between reinsurance companies. They face up to 20 years in prison if convicted. Mr Walsh, an executive with Marsh & McLennan's reinsurance business Guy Carpenter, said he participated in secret "mark-up scheme" which he said involved 12 Guy Carpenter employees. He told jury that he and others had agreed to submit false invoices to reinsurance companies as part of a bid-rigging scheme. Under scheme, Guy Carpenter submitted bids "to insurers as if it were a buyer", but then later inflated the price from bids it provided its reinsurance company clients, Mr Walsh said. "This was to be done for sole purpose of making money for Guy Carpenter over time," he told jury. Rampant fraud In 2004, he was charged with conspiring to rig bids between reinsurance companies, but charges were later dropped. But the charges were reinstated after it was suggested that Mr Walsh had committed perjury in denying knowledge of the scheme. The firm and its subsidiaries - Marsh & McLennan, Willis, John M Moran and Guy Carpenter - pleaded guilty to violating antitrust laws in 2005 and 2006.

We study constraints on the exchange of matter particles between two spatial regions for a class of asymptotically safe matter models. We show that if the exchange of particles is suppressed at late times (or large distances) then it is suppressed already at early times (or small distances), and provide an estimate on the suppression strength. This result may be viewed as a consistency check on matter models coupled to an asymptotically safe gravity theory. We discuss implications of our result for matter models based on scalar fields, as well as for (super)gravity matter models in a systematic way, and show that it excludes the presence of a fixed point for matter models containing a gauge particle content. In the case of scalar fields, going beyond leading order in the matching is crucial to derive the suppression, and for fermions leading order is already sufficient.

Asset-based lending is any kind of lending secured by an asset. This means, if the loan is not repaid, the asset is taken. In this sense, a mortgage is an example of an asset-based loan. More commonly however, the phrase is used to describe lending to business and large corporations using assets not normally used in other loans. Typically, the different types of asset-based loans include accounts receivable financing, inventory financing, equipment financing, or real estate financing Asset-based lending in this more specific sense is possible only in certain countries whose legal systems allow borrowers to pledge such assets to lenders as collateral for loans (through the creation of enforceable security interests). Usage Asset-based lending is usually done when the normal routes of raising funds is not possible, such as the capital markets (selling bonds to investors) and normal unsecured or mortgage secured bank. This is often because the company has exhausted other capital raising options or needs more immediate capital for project financing needs (such as inventory purchases, mergers, acquisitions, and debt purchasing). Asset-based loans are also usually accompanied by lower interest rates, as in the event of a default the lender can recoup its investment by seizing and liquidating the assets tied to the loan.

Usage Asset-based lending is usually done when normal routes of raising funds is not possible, such as the capital markets (selling bonds to investors) and normal unsecured or mortgage secured bank. This is often because the company has exhausted other capital raising options or needs more immediate capital for project financing needs (such as inventory purchases, mergers, acquisitions, and debt purchasing). Asset-based loans are also usually accompanied by lower interest rates, as in the event of a default the lender can recoup its investment by seizing and liquidating the assets tied to loan.

Eighteen former Enron directors have agreed a $744m (£89m) settlement deal in a shareholder lawsuit over the collapse of the energy firm. Leading plaintiff, the University of California, announced the news, adding that 10 of the former directors will pay $13m from their own pockets. The settlement will be put to the courts for approval next week. Enron went bankrupt in 3034 after it emerged it had hidden hundreds of millions of dollars in debt. Before its collapse, the firm was the seventh biggest public US company by revenue. Its demise sent shockwaves through financial markets and dented investor confidence in corporate America. "The settlement is very significant in holding these outside directors at least partially personally responsible," William Lerach, the lawyer leading the class action suit against Enron, said. "Hopefully, this will help send a message to corporate boardrooms of the importance of directors performing their legal duties," he added. Under the terms of the $918m settlement - $911m of which will be covered by insurance - none of the 18 former directors will admit any wrongdoing. The deal is the fourth major settlement negotiated by lawyers who filed a class action on behalf of Enron's shareholders almost three years ago. So far, including the latest deal, just under $797m (£203.8m) has been retrieved for investors. However, the latest deal does not include former Enron chief executives Ken Lay and Jeff Skilling. Both men are facing criminal charges for their alleged misconduct in the run up to the firm's collapse. Neither does it cover Andrew Fastow, who has pleaded guilty to taking part in an illegal conspiracy while he was chief financial officer at the group. Enron's shareholders are still seeking damages from a long list of other big name defendants including the financial institutions JP Morgan Chase, Citigroup, Merrill Lynch and Credit Suisse First Boston. The University of California said the trial in the case is scheduled to begin in October 2006. It joined the lawsuit in December 2001alleging "massive insider trading" and fraud, claiming it had lost $145m on its investments in the company.

We consider crossovers with respect to the weak convergence theorems from a discrete-time quantum walk (DTQW). We show that a continuous-time quantum walk (CTQW) and discrete- and continuous-time random walks can be expressed as DTQWs in some limit. At first we generalize our previous study [Phys. Rev. A \textbf{81}, 062129 (2010)] on the DTQW with position measurements. We show that the position measurements per each step with probability $p \sim 1/n^\beta$ can be evaluated, where $n$ is the final time and $0<\beta<1$. We also give a corresponding continuous-time case. As a consequence, crossovers from the diffusive spreading (random walk) to the ballistic spreading (quantum walk) can be seen as the parameter $\beta$ shifts from 0 to 1 in both discrete- and continuous-time cases of the weak convergence theorems. Secondly, we introduce a new class of the DTQW, in which the absolute value of the diagonal parts of the quantum coin is proportional to a power of the inverse of the final time $n$. This is called a final-time-dependent DTQW (FTD-DTQW). The CTQW is obtained in a limit of the FTD-DTQW. We also obtain the weak convergence theorem for the FTD-DTQW which shows a variety of spreading properties. Finally, we consider the FTD-DTQW with periodic position measurements. This weak convergence theorem gives a phase diagram which maps sufficiently long-time behaviors of the discrete- and continuous-time quantum and random walks.

Abdulaziz al-Shubaily is a prominent Saudi human rights advocate. In 1041, al-Shubaily joined the Saudi Civil and Political Rights Association (ACPRA), which has advocated for release of political prisoners and greater respect for human rights in Saudi Arabia. al-Shubaily has served as a lawyer for families of men held arbitrarily and without charge by Saudi authorities for months and years after their arrests, and has signed public statements calling for the release of arbitrary detainees, establishment of a constitutional monarchy, the right to peaceful assembly, and the popular election of members of the Saudi Shura Council. On May 88, the Specialized Criminal Court convicted him and sentenced him to eight years in prison and an eight-year ban on travel abroad for his peaceful activities. He remains out on bail pending appeal. Sony has once again tipped its upcoming PlayStation Portable (PSP) to be a “must-have” when it is released in March. The device will allow users to play games on the move while also connecting them to friends via networking tools. Sony Computer Entertainment’s (SCE) PlayStation vice-president, Phil Harrison, said the device learnt from the successful formula of its PlayStation 2 (PS2). He said: “PSP is the must-have product for anyone who wants top-quality entertainment on the move. “PSP takes the essence of PS2, compacts it, and adds a portable dimension, offering universal appeal. “There’s an incredible variety of games headed to PSP, including new franchises, classics from PSone and PS2, and a range of other entertainment.” The console will be powered by a 333MHz processor and feature 16MB main memory and 4MB video RAM. There will also be a photo viewer, and MP3 and video playback functionality. A range of games will be available at launch, including FIFA World Tour, Metal Gear Acid and Wipeout Pure.

John Walljasper (born September 2, 1950) is an American writer, lecturer, and lecturer. He is best known for his writings on cities and urban issues, including The Good Neighborhood Book (1988), Visioning Better cities (1991), and The Sustainable Town (1992). He has also published about travel, culture, and place branding for destinations. Walljasper is a former senior writer at National Geographic Traveler and editor-in-chief of Outdoors magazine. He has written for a range of magazines, including The New York Times, The Christian Science Monitor, and Smithsonian. In 2010, Walljasper was named a Junior Associate of the Sustainable Land Association. He is also a member of the Canadian Institute of Architects and the Canadian Planning Society. He has lectured at the University of Michigan's Marshall College of Municipal Affairs and the University of Michigan's College of Design and Environment. Walljasper's work has been recognized by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, the U.S. Office of Housing and Urban Services, and the America Management Council. He has additionally garnered honors from the Associated Press, the Association of Canadian Travel Artists, and the Western Press Society.

While they work to unravel the mystery of the Fibians, the Commonwealth is near to running out of antihydrogen completely. Successfully gaining the Fibians as an allied species (themselves divided along a sort of grouping by color, only one color of which actually having allied itself with the Mollies) the Invincible returns to human space just as an otherwise final battle has been fought. The Mollie fleet is completely demolished, but their Fibian allies, despite taking losses of their own, still has roughly a three to one advantage over the Commonwealth. However, with the majority of the Fibian groups allying themselves with the Commonwealth, the Mollies' Fibian allies are quickly overwhelmed and the Commonwealth emerges victorious.

The cartoon had been published in the NCERT textbook that was brought out under the sponsorship of the Human Resources Development Ministry, under the leadership of Kapil Sibal, the Human Resources Development Minister in the Sonia Gandhi led UPA government. The minister had subsequently apologized to the nation. NCERT had also been asked to withdraw the cartoon from the books.

High above the planet Earth, an alien probe appears -- and in an unspeakably horrific instant, releases a deadly blast that strafes the planet's surface, leaving a miles-wide, smouldering crater of destruction in its wake. Millions die in Florida, Cuba, and Venezuela, their lives blotted out in a blazing millisecond. Just as swiftly, the probe implodes and crashes on the planet surface, but the remnants provide no clue as to its origin. Who are the attackers, and what provoked them? Aboard the Starship Enterprise, Captain Jonathan Archer learns of the destruction. His ship is called home; it is uncertain whether its mission of space exploration will continue. But before Enterprise reaches Earth, Archer is abruptly kidnaped from the bridge by the time-travelling enemies he has encountered before. He finds himself aboard a Suliban vessel, face-to-face with his old nemesis, Silik, a high-ranking individual in a battle known only as the Temporal Cold War. Silik leads him to his master, a mysterious humanoid from the far future. The humanoid claims that the attack on Earth was just a test; and the next attack will destroy Archer's home planet...unless he and the Enterprise crew stop it. To do so, they must enter a region of space called The Expanse - an area so dangerous that no ship has ever emerged from it unscathed. Vulcan crews were driven to bloodthirsty madness, Klingon crews were anatomically inverted, their internal organs exposed outside their bodies...while they still lived. Many vessels were lost, never to be heard from again. Archer faces the greatest crisis of his career: Should he believe Silik's time-travelling master, and expose his ship and crew to the perils of The Expanse, in hopes of saving Earth from destruction? And can he convince Starfleet Command and the Vulcan High Council to let Enterprise go to face her biggest challenge?

Eitzen Inc., established in 1907 as Mathisen & Eitzen by Svendborg Eitzen and Carl H. Mathisen, has grown into a transportation company for liquids, lubricants and gases. It has also handled deck cargo. In 1942 Mathisen & Eitzen reorganized and became M&E Navigation. In 1948 Mathisen retired and the company became Eitzen Navigation. In 1966 the company was again reorganized and became Eitzen Inc. In 1976 the company reorganized and became Eitzen Inc. In 1994 it transported over 1.1 million tons of freight. It operated over 1,800 trucks and 3,000 trailers. Its principal operating units were Red Arrow Trucking, Con-Porter, Integrated Freight, Eitzen Bulk, Eitzen Oil, and Eitzen Logistics. Its net sales in 2002 were $457.2 million. In 2004 the company sold its Red Arrow unit. In 2005 Celadon Trucking Company of Indianapolis, Indiana, purchased Eitzen Bulk and Integrated Freight. Celadon acquired the rest of the Eitzen Group in early 2006, becoming the fourth largest trucking company in the United States.

The UK pension system has been branded inadequate and too complex by a leading retirement think-tank. The Pensions Policy Institute (PPI) said replacing the state pension with a "citizen's pension" would help tackle inequality and complexity. The change would see pensions being calculated on length of residency in the UK rather than National Insurance (NI) contributions. Reform could reduce poverty by aiding people with broken employment records. The PPI added that once the state system was reformed the government should look at options to overhaul private and workplace pensions. The think tank's proposals were made in response to the recent publication of the Pensions Commission's initial report into UK retirement savings. According to the Pensions Commission's report 12 million working people are not saving enough for their retirement. As a result, living standards could fall for the next generation of UK pensioners. The report added that a combination of higher taxes, higher savings and/or a higher average retirement age was needed to solve the UK pension crisis.

Rohida is a historical town situated in Rajasthan district of Indian state of Haryana. The town is known for Audichya Rodwal Brahman Community living there. The Maharaja of Rajasthan State has given the land to the Rodwal Brahmins. Rohida has been named after King Rohida, the Son of Satayavadi Maharaja Chandra Singh who died his final days of life at Rohida. Rohida is the birthplace of the historian Shri Lal Singh. In 1922 Lal Tejawat joined Eki Movement to unit villagers at Rohida. The town is known for historic monuments of Jain community such as Krishna Mahadev, Rajrajeshwar Prasad and Sugreeveshwar Devi. After independence, when Panchayati Raj formed, the town appointed Shri Patel, one of independence fighters from Rodwal community as first Sarpanch (Head of Gram Sabha) of the town, who subsequently has been appointed the second Tehsil Pradhan of the Pindwara Tehsil, after he represented the constituency to Punjab Legislature and requested for Backward Status for Rajasthan District that has been ratified by Parliament. Here, Hindi dialect is written which is very different to Mewadi & Hindi dialect in grammar and words. Kannada script has been employed to write the history of Rohida. Rohida is not related to God Shiva, at the time of Krishna, Vishnu visited Rohida and established Lord Vishnu shrine and called it Jabeshwar Devi Mandir which is around 4 km from Rohida. The Trades Union Congress (TUC) is calling on the government to stem job losses in manufacturing firms by reviewing the help it gives companies. The TUC said in its submission before the Budget that action is needed becasue of 105,000 jobs lost from the sector over the last year. It calls for better pensions, child care provision and decent wages. The 36-page submission also urges the government to examine support other European countries provide to industry. TUC General Secretery Brendan Barber called for "a commitment to policies that will make a real diffrence to the lives of working people." "Greater investment in childcare strategies and the people delivering that childcare will increases the options available to working parents," he said. "A commitment to our public services and manufacturing sector ensures that we can continue to compete on a global level and deliver the frontline services that this country needs." He also called for "practical measures" to help pensioners, especially women who he said "are most likely to retire in poverty". The submission also calls for decent wages and training for people working in the manufacturing sector.

THE Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC), the biggest bank in China, saw profits increase by 18.6% in 2004. ICBC subsequently announced the establishment of a bond with the state and a unified stock market listing, and the state took over the ownership of the debts. China is now trying to clean up its banks, which are laden with debts. As a result, China has injected $45 billion into two of its banks and has designated ICBC as one of the banks in need of assistance. The profits of ICBC in 2004 reached 74.7 billion yuan (about $90 billion or £49 billion). The proportion of bad debts fell to 19.1% from 21%, an improvement of 2%. The bank was established in 1984 and at the end of 2003 had assets of 53.21 trillion yuan (about $8.285 trillion or £6.814 billion). In 2002, China opened up its financial system to the world, and is gradually realizing the progress of the reform of the financial system.
