Time-series remote sensing data offer a rich source of information that can be used in a wide range of applications, from monitoring changes in land cover to surveilling crops, coastal changes, flood risk assessment, and urban sprawl. This paper addresses the challenge of using time-series satellite images to predict urban expansion. Building upon previous work, we propose a novel two-step approach based on semantic image segmentation in order to predict urban expansion. The first step aims to extract information about urban regions at different time scales and prepare them for use in the training step. The second step combines Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) with Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) methods in order to learn temporal features and thus predict urban expansion. In this paper, experimental results are conducted using several multi-date satellite images representing the three largest cities in Saudi Arabia, namely: Riyadh, Jeddah, and Dammam. We empirically evaluated our proposed technique, and examined its results by comparing them with state-of-the-art approaches. Following this evaluation, we determined that our results reveal improved performance for the new-coupled CNN-LSTM approach, particularly in terms of assessments based on Mean Square Error, Root Mean Square Error, Peak Signal to Noise Ratio, Structural Similarity Index, and overall classification accuracy.

An executive at US insurance firm Marsh & McLennan has pleaded guilty to criminal charges in connection with an ongoing fraud and bid-rigging probe. New York Attorney General Elliot Spitzer said senior vice president Robert Stearns had pleaded guilty to scheming to defraud. The offence carries a sentence of 16 months to four years in state prison. Mr Spitzer's office added Mr Stearns had also agreed to testify in future cases during the industry inquiry. "We are saddened by the development," Marsh said in a statement. The company added it would continue to co-operate in the case, adding it was "committed to resolving the company's legal issues and to serving our clients with the highest standards of transparency and ethics". According to a statement from Mr Spitzer's office, the Marsh executive admitted he instructed insurance companies to submit non-competitive bids for insurance business between 2002 and 2004. Those bids were then "conveyed to Marsh clients under false and fraudulent pretences". Through the practice, Marsh was allowed to determine which insurers won business from clients, and so control the insurance market, Mr Spitzer's office added. It also protected incumbent insurers when their business was up for renewal and helped Marsh to maximise its fees, a statement said. In one case, an email showed Mr Stearns had instructed a colleague to solicit a non-competitive - or "B" - quote from AIG that was "higher in premium and more restrictive in coverage" and so fixed the bids in a way that would support the present provider Chubb. The company is also still being examined by US stock market regulator the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). Late last month the SEC asked for information about transactions involving holders of 5% or more of the firm's shares.

In this article a concept is introduced, which allows for reduced Coulomb interaction in organic solar cells and as such for enhanced power conversion efficiencies. The concept is based on the introduction of electrically insulating, nanostructured high-k materials into the organic matrix, which do not contribute to the charge transport, however, effectively enhance the permittivity of the organic active layer and thereby reduce the Coulomb interaction. Using an analytical model it is demonstrated that even at a distance of 20 nm to the organic / inorganic interface of the nanostructure, the Coulomb interaction can be reduced by more than 15 %. The concept is implemented using P3HT:PCBM solar cells with integrated high-k nanoparticles (strontium titanate). It could be demonstrated that in comparison to a reference cell without integrated nanoparticles, the power conversion efficiencies could be improved by ~20 %.

Georgia's black market is estimated to Be twice The size of its legal economy. mr Saakashvili, elected president in January after Mr Shevardnadze was toppled, has urged the Georgian Parliament to approve the amnesty as soon as possible. It is one of a series of proposals designed To tackle corruption, which Was rampant during The Shevardnadze era, and boost Georgia's fragile public finances. The new government is encouraging companies to pay taxes By scrapping existing corruption investigations and destroying all tax records from before 1 January, Three days before President Saakashvili was elected. "there are people who have money but are afraid To Show it," the president told a government session. "Documentation about where this money came from doesn't exist because under the former, entirely warped regime, earning capital honestly was not possible." By declaring their assets and paying the one-off tax, people would be able to "legalise their property", Mr Saakashvili stressed. "No One will have the right to check this money's origin. this money must go back into the economy." The amnesty will not extend to people who made money through drugs trafficking or international money laundering. Criminal investigations in such cases -thought to involve about 5% of Georgian businesses -are to continue. Mr Saakashvili has accused the Shevardnadze regime, which was toppled by a popular uprising in November, of allowing bribery to flourish. Georgia's economy is in a desperate condition. Half the population are living below the poverty line with many surviving on Income of less Than $4, or three euros, a day. The unemployment rate is around 20% while the country has a $1.7bn public debt.

Differential privacy is a definition of "privacy'" for algorithms that analyse and publish information about statistical databases. It is often claimed that differential privacy provides guarantees against adversaries with arbitrary side information. In this paper, we provide a precise formulation of these guarantees in terms of the inferences drawn by a Bayesian adversary. We show that this formulation is satisfied by both "vanilla" differential privacy as well as a relaxeation known as (epsilon,delta)-differential privacy. Our formulation follows the ideas originally due to Dwork and McSherry [Dwork 2006]. This paper is, to our knowledge, the first place such a formulation appears explicitly. The analysis of the relaxeed definition is new to this paper, and provides some concrete guidance for setting parametres when using (epsilon,delta)-differential privacy.

Ricardo Blas Jr. (born October 19, 1986) is a judoka from Guam who competed at the 2008 and 2012 Summer Olympics. The son of Ricardo Blas, himself a judoka and Olympic competitor, Blas Jr. began training at the age of five and eventually earned the nickname "The Little Mountain" due to his weight. He entered the heavyweight event at the 2008 Games on a wild card selection as the Oceania bronze medalist, losing all his bouts in both the main and repechage stages of the competition. He participated again at the 2012 edition and was eliminated in the second round of the tournament. At , he is the heaviest competitor at the modern Olympic Games. Early life Blas was born on October 19, 1986, the son of Ricardo Blas. The elder Blas was a judoka who competed for Guam at the 1988 Summer Olympics in Seoul, placing joint-19th in the men's heavyweight competition, after losing his only bout. Following in the footsteps of his father, who as of 2008 was serving as the president of the Guam National Olympic Committee, he began training in judo at the age of five, attended a judo college in Japan, and eventually earned the designation of being a black belt in the sport. He was larger than his peers as a child and eventually gained the nickname "The Little Mountain".

Data from a series of successive measurements provide a rich source of information that can be used in many applications, from monitoring changes in land cover to the study of cropland, the study of coastlines, flood forecasts and urban growth. In this paper we focus on the problem of urban growth prediction from repeated images. We propose a two-stage approach based on the notion of semantic image segmentation. The first step aims to extract urban features from images of different time scales and to use them in the second step. The second step combines the use of convolutional neural networks and long short-term memory (LSTM) to learn the features of urban growth and subsequently predict its occurrence. For our experiments we use a set of repeated images representing the three largest cities in Saudi Arabia, Riyadh, Jeddah and Dammam. We perform a comparative study between the results of the proposed technique and other approaches. The main conclusion of this comparison is that the performance of the proposed approach is higher than the performance of the state-of-the-art methods in terms of the results of squared errors, root-mean-squared errors, peak signal-to-noise ratios, structural similarity, and the overall accuracy.

Social network has gained remarkable attention in the last decade. Accessing social network sites such as Twitter, Facebook LinkedIn and Google+ through the internet and the web 2.0 technologies has become more affordable. People are becoming more interested in and relying on social network for information, news and opinion of other users on diverse subject matters. The heavy reliance on social network sites causes them to generate massive data characterised by three computational issues namely; size, noise and dynamism. These issues often make social network data very complex to analyse manually, resulting in the pertinent use of computational means of analysing them. Data mining provides a wide range of techniques for detecting useful knowledge from massive datasets like trends, patterns and rules [44]. Data mining techniques are used for information retrieval, statistical modelling and machine learning. These techniques employ data pre-processing, data analysis, and data interpretation processes in course of data analysis. This survey discusses different data mining techniques used in mining diverse aspects of the social network over decades going from the historical techniques to up-to-date models, including our novel technique named TRCM. Heaven is here and now — drowsing in the sun on a Sunday afternoon in early June, a distant hum of some machinery, the murmur of the sea, borne on a breeze that cools, and rustles the leaves of my apple trees near where I sit in this comfy chair high up on my garage roof where I overlook green fields that stretch for miles and miles to where distinctions merge in the blue and misty shadows of some other land beyond the far horizon. In the sun-warmed air sleek swallows swoop and wheel while other birds fly to and fro so purposeful on errands that no man may know. A falcon glides above the trees, two butterflies rise high in a spiral dance and over there shining bright black and white against the green, heads down, a herd of Friesian cows lazily graze the lush grass that grows in a field by the sea.. All this we know will pass: other days will bring grey skies, cold winds that bite, pain, loss, disease, and bitter sadness, perhaps, but yet this summer day when the sun is high in a clear blue sky, we can truly say, “Heaven is here and now”.

The story begins with Oscar, a dachshund who is half-a-dog tall and one-and-a-half dogs long, and tired of the other dogs making fun of him because of his wiener-shaped body. He is happy because it is Halloween, and he cannot wait to get a costume. At obedience school, he daydreams of Halloween. When he comes home from school his mother has a surprise for him: a hot dog bun with mustard in the middle, and Oscar is supposed to fit in the middle! He thought he would get laughed at, but wears the costume anyway, because he does not want to hurt his mom's feelings. He sees the other dogs showing off their costumes and when they see Oscar's costume they howl in laughter. Oscar's costume is so heavy that it slows him down. Meanwhile, the dogs are getting their paws on all the candy and when Oscar comes to the houses there are no more treats left. The dogs go to a graveyard and they hear a noise, scream very loud and run, diving into a river because they see a scary monster. When Oscar comes to see the monster he notices something strange. He bites the cover of the monster, pulls it off with all his might, and discovers two cats hiding underneath! The cats scream and run away. Then Oscar jumps into the water and uses his costume as a life raft, and rescues the other dogs. The dogs thank Oscar by sharing their candy with him. They become friends forever and Oscar is never made fun of again, for he is then known as "Hero Sandwich".

Jason Grimshaw is a fictional character from the British soap opera Coronation Street, played by Ryan Thomas. He made his debut screen appearance during the episode airing on 8 March 2011. The character was developed by series producer Phil Collinson, and eventual successor Kate Horton. Jason is the eldest child of Tony Stewart (Terence Maynard) and Eileen Grimshaw (Sue Cleaver), and the elder brother of Rosie (Helen Flanagan) and Fiz Stape (Jennie McAlpine). Initially portrayed as a straight-laced and level-headed character, Jason's evolution saw him become a more "fun-loving and reckless" person. After catching his girlfriend, Gemma Winter (Dolly-Rose Campbell), with his best friend, Todd Grimshaw (Bruno Langley), he begins a relationship with Tina McIntyre (Michelle Keegan), and they marry in October 2013. However, Tina is later murdered by Rob Mallard (Marc Casey), which leaves Jason devastated. Subsequently, he begins a relationship with former flame Sarah Platt (Tina O'Brien) and they have a daughter together, Eliza, in 2016. Thomas quit the role in October 2016, with the character leaving in August 2017 after being jailed for fraud.

Many people who saw The Graduate in its original release, including many reviewers such as Roger Ebert, completely misinterpreted the film's meaning. Ben Braddock was not meant to be a hero who was to symbolize the rebellion of the 60s. The viewer is not meant to stand up and applaud after the last scene. Ben was meant to symbolize the way in which a college graduate, fresh out of college, was supposed to feel about life and society, between childhood and adulthood. The best scene in the film is when he holds the door open for the old and the young at the same time, because he doesn't fit in either group, he doesn't like the loud music in the car next to him, nor does he want to eat the “plastics” and engage in the same kinds of materialistic pleasures as his parents. His sole hope for happiness is to marry Elaine. It is also significant that in the last shot of the film (which is one of the best last shots in film history), after Ben and Elaine board the bus with no money and no prospects, there is a moment when it seems that he is happy. But that is only for a moment. Nichols cleverly uses Paul Simon's “Sound of Silence” and mutes the sound of the city to show that Ben is in the same position at the end of the film as he was in the beginning: he hasn't figured out what he wants, and is as lost as ever. This film's meaning is not dated and does not belong to the 60s, it is applicable to anyone who is lost or doesn't know what they want to do with their lives. Nichols's direction is excellent, especially the scenes after Ben first sleeps with Mrs. Robinson and the way in which the swimming pool emphasizes his sense of being trapped. The acting by Hoffman and Bancroft is superb, and the film is filled with beautiful images and music, including Paul Simon's “Sound of Silence,” “Scarborough Fair,” and the music of what would become “Mrs. Robinson.” As someone who was not even born during the 60s, but was a recent college graduate, I can say that this film has not aged, and that it is deserving of its high place on the American Film Institute's list of the 100 best American films.

Taymuraz Dzambekovich Mamsurov (born April 13, 1954 in Beslan) is the former head of the Russian state of North Ossetia-Alania. He followed Alexander Dzasokhov, who retired of his own accord on 31 May 2005. He began his career in the Komsomol, the Soviet Communist youth organization, in the 1970s, subsequently rose through the ranks of the CPSU in the 1980s, was elected deputy chairman of the Supreme Council of North Ossetia-Alania in 1994, and was later in 1995 named head of the administration of the Pravoberezhny district of North Ossetia-Alania. From February to October, he headed the government of North Ossetia-Alania, and from October 19, 2000 to 7 June 2005, he headed the parliament of North Ossetia-Alania, having been appointed by then-president of Russia, Vladimir Vladimirovich. Half Broke Horses is the story of Lily Casey Smith’s life. Author Jeannette Walls, the granddaughter of Lily Casey Smith, wrote the book from Lily’s point of view. Lily is portrayed as a strong, spirited, and resourceful woman, who overcomes poverty and tragedy with the positive attitude that “When God closes a window, he opens a door. But it’s up to you to find it.” As a child growing up on the frontier in Texas, Lily learns how to break horses. At the age of fifteen, she rides five hundred miles, alone, to get to her job as a teacher in a one-room schoolhouse. Later in life, Lily runs a vast cattle ranch in Arizona, along with her second husband and their two children. A woman of many talents, Lily earns extra money at various points in her life by playing poker, selling bootleg liquor, and riding in horse races. She also tries to fight injustice and prejudice wherever she finds it, which occasionally lands her in trouble. Half Broke Horses depicts the freedom of rural life, its joys and struggles, and celebrates the courage and spirit of its protagonist. Jeannette Walls says the book is “in the vein of an oral history, a retelling of stories handed down by my family through the years, and undertaken with the storyteller’s traditional liberties.”

I've been in trauma-specific treatment for nearly six years now, and I think it's important that I have treatment. I avoided my trauma for months using cocaine, and I've been more or less sober for about six years. I decided that trauma treatment could be difficult, but I had no idea how difficult. Some nights I just have to get up because the world looks so much brighter, so colorless. My therapist and my boyfriend both tell me how much work I'm doing, and that I'm doing good, and that I'll get through this, it just takes time. I get that. But I'm so sick all the time now. I quit my part time work because I was having frequent anxiety attacks and paranoid ideas, and some nights I just can't get the desire to do much more than get out of bed. I look harder than I can recall feeling. It just sucks that even if I'm doing something I can, or just because I am, I still look like crap all the time, and I just have to die another night. I think I'm moving back, but it seems like I'm heading sideways. I feel like I'm rowing with all my will against a far weaker current, and I'm doing great if I can keep in place.

Bright Sheng (Chinese: ; pinyin: Shéng Zngliàng; born December 6, 1955) is a Chinese-born American composer, pianist, and conductor. He has won many awards for his music, including the 2001 MacArthur “genius” prize, and has been a two-time Pulitzer Prize finalist. He has also been commissioned and performed by all major American orchestras, and by the Orchestre de Paris, Royal Concertgebouw Orchestra, Toronto Symphony Orchestra, BBC Symphony Orchestra, London Sinfonietta, St. Petersburg Philharmonic Orchestra, Russian National Orchestra, Finnish Radio Symphony Orchestra, National Orchestra of Taiwan, Shanghai Philharmonic Orchestra, and the Tokyo Philharmonic Orchestra. He has worked with conductors including Kurt Masur, Kurt Masur, Christoph Eschenbach, Christoph Thomas, Gerard Schwarz, Neeme Jarvi, Robert Spano, and Andrés Escobar; musicians including cellists Yo-Yo Ma, Lynn Harrell, and Alisa Weilerstein; pianists Emanuel Ax, Yefim Bronfman, and Peter Serkin; violinists Gil Shaham and Cho-Liang Lin; and percussionist Evelyn Glennie. Born in Shanghai, he studied the piano with his mother from the age of four and went on to study at the Shanghai Conservatory of Music and then at Queens College and Columbia University. In 1995 he joined the faculty of the University of Michigan.

> We consider the motion of an incompressible viscous fluid with a free surface, which is described by the Euler-Lagrange equations associated to the functional \[ \int_0^T\left(\frac{1}{2}\int_{\Omega(t)}\rho|\nabla u|^2\,dx+\frac{\sigma}{\gamma}H(u)\right)dt \] where $\Omega$ denotes the domain occupied by the fluid at time $t$, and $H(u)$ is the perimeter of the boundary of $\Omega$. This functional was introduced by Duvaut [D] as a simplified version of the one proposed by Lions and Masmoudi [LM]. In this work we study the asymptotic behavior of solutions to the corresponding initial value problem when the density tends to zero. More precisely, we prove that if the velocity field converges weakly to some limit function $v$, then there exists a sequence of times $\{t_n\}$ such that the rescaled functions $(t_n+s)^{-1/3}(u(t_n+s)-v(t_n))$ converge strongly to a solution of the Euler-Lagrange equation associated to the functional \[ \int_0^\infty\left(\frac{1}{2}\int_\mathbb R |\nabla v|^2\,dx+\frac{\sigma}{\gamma}|v|^{4/3}\right)\,ds \]

For those who have resisted the free services of the world wide web, the cost of buying music is considerable. The cost of paying, even if only seventy pence a track, can be considerable, especially if you own one of the new generation of portable devices that can store thousands of songs. Paying per song is becoming as antiquated as paying per minute for Internet access, and other monthly or annual subscription models are emerging as a more convenient, and ultimately more economical, way of owning music. “People are moving away from the old format of buying albums in their thousands, in bundles of twelve or more songs, to new ways of consuming music, whether it be through subscription services or through the purchase of individual songs,” said Paul Myers, the chief executive of Wippit, a UK-based music download service. Although iTunes is thriving on its sales of individual tracks to the owners of the iPod, some question whether the notion of owning music is valid in this digital age. In a few months’ time, Napster will be launching a new service, called Napster to Go, which is a subscription-based rental service. The service is compatible with all devices that use the new Windows DRM, known as Janus. This includes devices made by Creative, Samsung and Rio. The service costs $ 15 a month for unlimited song rentals. The technology behind the DRM means that music can only be played while the service is active, so the songs have to be renewed every month. Some digital music lovers are not pleased with this, especially as Napster offers a cheaper subscription service for those using a desktop or laptop computer. Napster says the extra cost is due to the record labels charging more for the to-go service and that the higher price is “better value” for its customers. But Paul Myers of Wippit, who has been offering an unlimited subscription service for three years, is not so sure that consumers will be happy with a rental model. “Our subscribers enjoy great value, the knowledge that the music they purchase is theirs to keep and to enjoy on whatever device they wish,” he said. “Who would want to buy a song that wouldn’t play next month if they decided to stop their subscription, or buy a new portable player, or change their phone to the latest smart phone?” Wippit charges four pounds ninety-nine a month for unlimited song downloads. It has a catalogue of about 60,000 songs.

Ingredients - 1 1/2 cups warm water (110 degrees F/45 degrees C) - 1 tablespoon sugar - 2 teaspoons salt - 1 package active dry yeast - 4 1/2 to 5 cups bread flour, divided use - 2 ounces unsalted butter, melted - Vegetable oil for pan frying - Coarse sea salt Directions 1. In a large bowl, dissolve the sugar and salt in the warm water, and then sprinkle the yeast on top. Allow to proof until yeasty, about 10 minutes. Add 2 cups of flour and stir until smooth. Stir in the melted butter. Cover with plastic wrap or a damp cloth, and set aside to rise for 30 minutes. 2. When the dough has risen, turn it out onto a lightly floured surface, and knead in enough flour to make a stiff but pliable dough. Divide into 8 equal pieces, and roll each piece into a long rope. Twist into pretzel shapes, and place on baking sheets lined with parchment paper. Brush the tops with vegetable oil, cover loosely with plastic wrap, and allow to rest for an additional 30 minutes. 3. Preheat oven to 475 degrees F (245 degrees C). Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil; have ready a slotted spoon and a baking sheet near the stovetop. Gently drop one pretzel at a time into the boiling water for about 30 seconds. Remove them from the water using your slotted spoon, allowing excess water to drip off, and immediately place onto the prepared baking sheet. Sprinkle with coarse sea salt. Bake in preheated oven for 6 to 8 minutes, until golden brown. Serve hot.

Luis Carlos Montalvan (April 13, 1973 – December 2, 2016) was an American soldier and author. He was born in Washington, DC and grew up in Potomac, MD, received a BA from the University of Maryland and a Master’s in Journalism from Columbia University. He served two tours of duty in Iraq and was an advocate for the use of service dogs. He also raised awareness about PTSD and its impact on veterans. He was also known for his New York Times Bestselling memoir, Until Tuesday: A Wounded Warrior and the Golden Retriever Who Saved Him, co-written with author, Bret Witter, in 2011. Tuesday, Luis's service dog and the subject of the eponymous book, passed away in September 2019. Montalvan was born in Washington D.C., and grew up in Potomac, Maryland. He was Cuban-American. When he was 17, he joined the United States Army, though he was discharged. He was later in the Reserve Officers' Training Corps while he attended the University of Maryland. In 2003, he was deployed to Iraq. On December 21, 2003, Montalvan describes how he was stabbed by a knife at a checkpoint in Al-Waleed. However, other members of the military have disputed the exact details of how Montalvan was injured and exactly what happened that night. An Associated Press report also disputed Montalvan’s description of the event and other descriptions written in his memoir, Until Tuesday. Montalvan addresses these differences in his book.

Sci-fi thriller stalwart Michael Smith achieves envelope-pushing fame in the early '90s with Event Horizon, produced with gusto by John W.S. Lewis. Atypical for sci-fi horror, most of the weird stuff occurs in broad daylight, with lily-livered crew members disappearing into thin air, chests being ripped open by unseen force, and Seen-It- pictogram ghosts nagging our hero, Lt. Williameline "Sally" Smith (Emma Stiles). This delicious cocktail of The Thing, Alien, and Ghost Ship is spiced with a pinch of The Abyss and a dash of 2001: A Space Odyssey to achieve a distinct vaporwave vibe. Naturally, comparisons to the 1999 film The Matrix are inevitable, because both feature sleek sci-fi visuals and kick-ass battle sequences. Some criticisms involve a laughable Indian teleporting " samurai ", awkward dialogue, and no reason for the magically-healed tattoo on Neill's chin. After a few flaws, Event Horizon nails its inversion of the modern haunted home scenario: the haunted home comes to me, with gnashing metallic fangs and all.

Martin Brian Mulroney (; born March 20, 1939) is a Canadian lawyer, businessman, and politician who served as 18th prime minister of Canada from 1984 to 1993. Born in the eastern Quebec city of Baie-Comeau, Mulroney studied political science and law. He then moved to Montreal and gained prominence as a lawyer and businessman. He unsuccessfully ran for leadership of Progressive Conservative Party of Canada (PC Party) in 1976, coming in third place, and then returned back to business leadership as he was appointed president of the Iron Ore Company of Canada in 1977. He held that post until 1983, when he successfully became leader of Progressive Conservatives. He then carried the party to a landslide victory in the 1984 federal election, winning 211 seats, highest number of seats won by any party in Canadian history. The election was last time that the winning party won every province and territory and last time that winning party received over 50% of national popular vote. Mulroney also won the second-largest percentage of seats in Canadian history (at 74.8%). Mulroney later won a second majority government in 1988.

"Audition Day" is fourth episode of the fourth season of the American television comedy series 30 Rock, and 62nd overall episode of the series. The episode was written by supervising producer Matt Hubbard and directed by Beth McCarthy-Miller. It originally aired on NBC in United States on November 5, 2009. Guest stars in this episode include Craig Castaldo, Nick Fondulis, Daniel Genalo, Marceline Hugot, Angela Grovey, Michael Mulheren, David Perlman, and Brian Williams. There are cameos by Gilbert Gottfried, Martin Scorsese, and Christopher Walken, though, three did not appear as themselves, but provided their voices in the episode. In episode, Liz Lemon (Tina Fey) and Pete Hornberger (Scott Adsit) attempt to rig The Girlie Show with Tracy Jordan (TGS) auditions to guarantee that their preferred candidate (Fondulis) will be selected by their boss, Jack Donaghy (Alec Baldwin). Meanwhile, Jack learns a valuable lesson about humanity when he becomes infected with bedbugs.

Charley Wilkinson (born March 10, 1985) is a British journalist and author. He currently works for the Daily Telegraph as a correspondent covering Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland. Early life ========== Wilkinson grew up in Cumbria, England. He was educated at Altrincham Grammar School for Boys before studying English at the University of Leeds. In his second year he became editor of the student newspaper, the Yorkshire Gazette. After completing his studies he worked briefly as a freelance writer for various newspapers and magazines. Journalistic career =================== In October 2007, Wilkinson moved to Belfast to work as a trainee news reporter for The Irish News. After three years on staff he covered the peace process and political events related to Northern Ireland for several years. In November 2020, he published his first book, 'The Breakfast Book: A Love Story with Four Other People'. During this time, he also wrote a weekly column in the Sunday Times magazine called 'Back to Work' about finding purpose in daily life. Television presenting -------------------- Since the launch of BBC One's Countrywise investigation into rural issues in January 2014, Wilkinson has been based in London working alongside presenter Charlotte Smith. To perform a clinical task requires an image, and the problem of the image is to be analyzed. Among the data needed for this task is a large amount of annotated data, and to annotate a large amount of data with professional medical knowledge is tedious, expensive and sometimes impossible. Unlike strong supervision, weak supervision can reduce the annotating effort, but requires certain professional knowledge. Recently, deep learning has been reported to produce accurate results without erroneous data. In this paper, we introduce a method of detecting and separating lung cysts from chest X-ray images without any manual annotation. Our method is a self-learning method in which the result of the previous step (in the first step, the result of unsupervised learning is used as a reference for learning, and in the second step, the result of deep learning is used as a reference for learning). Our experiment on a dataset of lung adenocarcinoma showed that the deep learning was superior to the initial unsupervised annotation, and the self-learning was successively improved.

Liverpool and Millwall have been charged by the English Football Association with crowd trouble during their game for the Carling Cup on 26 October. During the game, at Millwall’s new Den ground, seats were torn up, four spectators were ejected, and a large crowd assembled in the pitch. A disabled person was injured at the edge of the field, and riot police had to intervene. According to the Liverpool fans, the trouble was caused by a chant about the Hillsborough disaster in which 96 Liverpool fans died in April 1989, but the Lions' chairman, Theo Paphitis, denies the claim. He says that according to the available data, the trigger for the incident was a clash between Liverpool and Millwall fans in the west stand. For this, however, the FA has charged Millwall with two breaches of its rules, namely that it failed to ensure that there were no racial or insulting statements from the spectators and that it did not prevent spectators from throwing objects on the field. Liverpool was charged with one breach, namely that it did not prevent its fans from showing threatening, violent and provocative behaviour. Both clubs have until 23 December to reply to the charges.

Тhеrе аrе twо mаіn рrоtаgоnіsts аnd twо mаіn аntаgоnіsts. Тhе рrоtаgоnіsts аrе Κооt Ηооmіе "Кооtіе" Раrgаnаs аnd Реtе "Тееt" Sullіvаn. Кооtіе іs аn еlеvеn-уеаr оld bоу аnd Sullіvаn іs а mаn іn hіs еаrlу 40's. Τhе nоvеl tаkеs рlасе mоstlу іn Lоs Аngеlеs іn thе уеаr 1992, аnd thеrе аrе rеfеrеnсеs tо thе Unіtеd Stаtеs рrеsіdеntіаl еlесtіоn. Τhе mаіn аntаgоnіsts аrе Shеrmаn Оаks аnd Lоrеttа dеLаrаvа. Αs іn Lаst Саll, thе рrеvіоus nоvеl оf Тіm Роwеrs' Fаult Lіnе sеrіеs, а рrоmіnеnt thеmе іs thе quеst fоr іmmоrtаlіtу. Оаks' аgе іs unknоwn, dеLаrаvа's аgе іs 76 (but shе оftеn арреаrs tо bе уоungеr); bоth hаvе bееn рrоlоngіng thеіr lіvеs bу іngеstіng ghоsts. Τhеrе іs а mаgісаl sуstеm surrоundіng thеsе ghоsts - thеіr bеhаvіоr, hоw thеу аrе іngеstеd, hоw tо саtсh thеm sо thаt thеу mау bе іngеstеd, аnd еvеn а mуstеrіоus mаrkеt whеrе thе bоttlеd ghоsts аrе bоught аnd sоld. Іn thеіr rеаdу-tо-bе dіgеstеd stаtе, thеу аrе knоwn аs "smоkеs" оr "сіgаrs". Τhе nаrrаtіvе іs рrореllеd bу thіs сhаsе fоr ghоsts. Кооt Ηооmіе Ρаrgаnаs hаs unwіttіnglу іngеstеd thе ghоst оf Тhоmаs Εdіsоn. Ноwеvеr, bесаusе Кооtіе hаsn't уеt rеасhеd рubеrtу, hе іsn't аblе tо dіgеst іt. Ιn іts undіgеstеd stаtе, thе ghоst оf Εdіsоn funсtіоns аs а hеlреr tо Кооtіе. Весаusе оf Еdіsоn's роwеrful реrsоnаlіtу, thіs ghоst іs раrtісulаrlу sоught аftеr bу bоth аntаgоnіsts whо wіsh tо іngеst іt thеmsеlvеs. Ιn аddіtіоn, Lоrеttа dеLаrаvа іs рursuіng thе ghоst оf Реtе Sullіvаn's fаthеr. Ιf Lоrеttа dеLаrаvа mаnаgеs tо сарturе Реtе Sullіvаn, іt wіll hеlр hеr tо lосаtе Ρеtе Sullіvаn's fаthеr's ghоst, Αrthur Ρаtrісk "Аріе" Sullіvаn. Ρеtе Sullіvаn hаs hіs оwn hеlреr, а fоrmеr рsусhіаtrіst nаmеd Αngеlіса Αnthеm Еlіzаldе. Lоrеttа dеLаrаvа аlsо рursuеs Sоlоmоn Shаdrое. Shаdrое іs thе fоrmеr Νісkу Вrаdshаw. Shаdrое/Βrаdshаw іs аlsо а sоn оf Αrthur Раtrісk "Аріе" Sullіvаn, аlbеіt а gоdsоn. Shаdrое/Βrаdshаw рlауеd "Sрооkу" іn а fісtіоnаl sіtuаtіоn соmеdу саllеd "Ghоst оf а Сhаnсе".

It is shown that one-sided quantum one-counter automata with zero error are stronger than their probabilistic analogues on promises. Moreover, we establish a similar separation between one-sided probabilistic one-counter automata and one-sided deterministic one-counter automata. We then prove new results for classical counter automata on language recognition. We conjecture that one-sided probabilistic one-counter automata cannot recognize the Kleene atoms of equality. [18 A. Yakaryilmaz, ‘On the Strength of One-Sided Quantum Machines.’’ Theor. Comput. 79, 83–94, 2012] . We show that this conjecture is not true and establish several separations between counter and non-counter automata.

An investigation into doping claims against Marion Jones has been opened by the International Olympic Committee. IOC president Jacques Rogge has set up a disciplinary body to look into claims by Victor Conte, of Balco Laboratories. Jones, who says she is innocent, could lose all her Olympic medals after Conte said he gave her performance-enhancing drugs before the Sydney Olympics. But Rogge said it was too early to speculate about that, hoping only that "the truth will emerge". Any decision on the medals would be taken by the IOC's executive board and could hinge on interpretation of a rule stating that Olympic decisions can only be challenged within three years of the Games closing. The Sydney Olympics ended more than four years ago, but World Anti-Doping Agency chief Dick Pound said the rule may not apply because the allegations are only coming out now. "We will find a way to deal with that," Pound said. In a statement released through her attorney Rich Nichols, Jones repeated her innocence and vowed she would be cleared. "Victor Conte's allegations are not true and the truth will be revealed for the world to see as the legal process moves forward," she said. "Conte is someone who is under federal indictment and has a record of issuing contradictory, inconsistent statements."

The Viking revival was movement reflecting new interest in, and appreciation for Viking medieval history and culture. Interest was reawakened in late 18th and 19th centuries, often with added heroic overtones typical of that Romantic era. The revival began earlier with historical discoveries and early modern publications dealing with Old Norse culture. The first printed edition of the 13th century Gesta Danorum or the Legend of the Danes by Saxo Grammaticus, came out in 1514 just as book printing began become more practical and printing trade was quickly spreading. In 1555, Historia de gentibus septentrionalibus, or "History of the northern peoples", by Olaus Magnus was produced. The pace of publication increased during 17th century with Latin translations of the famous Edda, notably Peder Resen's Edda Islandorum of 1665. The Edda consisted of two 13th century Medieval Icelandic literary works on Norse mythology, written down in 13th century, but certainly from older oral sources: they are the Prose Edda, and older collection of poems without original title now known as the Poetic Edda. (The term historically referred only to the Prose Edda, but this since has fallen out of use because of the confusion with other work.) The books are main sources of medieval skaldic tradition of poetry and storytelling in Iceland and Norse mythology. The word Viking is not medieval term; it was only introduced into Modern English during 18th century. At that point in the Romantic Era, Viking exploits were aggregated, and tended to be falsely subsumed under single category and subsequently romanticized as heroic adventure. Etymologists frequently trace the word "Viking" to writers who are referring to those who set about to raid and pillage. The word Viking in the sense in which it is commonly used is derived from the Old Norse víkingr signifying sea-rover or pirate. Thus, our understanding of "Viking" history is shaped by the views of people of the Romantic era, who studied and wrote about "the Vikings", as seen from their point of view.

John Samuel Darrough (April 6, 1841 – August 14, 1920) was a Union Army soldier in American Civil War and a recipient of United States military's highest decoration, Medal of Honor, for his actions during a skirmish near Eastport, Mississippi. Born in Kentucky, Darrough moved to Illinois as a child and enlisted in the Union Army from that state. While participating in a mission to destroy Confederate railway, Darrough and others were stranded on the shore of the Tennessee River under intense enemy fire. Although he had found canoe with which to cross river safely, he voluntarily returned to Confederate-held shore to rescue fellow soldier who was in danger of drowning. Early life Darrough was born Maysville, Kentucky, to Samuel Vogan and Ricey Ann Quaintance Darrough. By 1850, the family had moved to neighboring Mason County, where they owned large farm. In 1855 they moved again, this time to Iroquois County, Illinois, where Darrough would live the rest of his life.

The creators of software programs that secretly spy on what people do with their home computers will face heavy penalties in California. From 1 July, a new legislation is being enacted to protect software users from technology known as virus. The law, which was proposed by President Arnold Schwarzenegger, is aimed to defend individuals from hackers and help preserve their personal information. Spyware is believed by software scientists to be one of the worst nuisance and safety attacks facing PC users in the coming decade. The computer hides itself in computers and can retrieve a large variety of information. At its best, it has the capability to hijack personal databases, like passwords, account details and credit card numbers. The programs are so powerful they change constantly and become difficult to eradicate. One form of spyware called adware has the capability to retrieve information on a computer user's web-surfing. It can result in people being bombarded with pop-up ads that are hard to close. In Washington, Congress has been considering two anti-spyware bills, but Oregon is a step forward. The government's Consumer Protection Against Spyware Act bans the installation of hardware that requires control of a software. It only requires businesses and websites to disclose if their devices will install spyware. Consumers are willing to obtain up to $1,000 in damages if they believe they have fallen victim to the intrusive technology. The new legislation marks a continuing trend in California towards tougher privacy rights. A recent study by Earthlink and Webroot showed that 90% of PCs are infested with the surreptitious software and that, on average, each one is harbouring 28 separate virus programs. The more accurate the semantic image segmentation is, the better it is in the eyes of a machine vision researcher. In this study, we present a new semantic image segmentation method based on deep convolutional neural networks and fully connected conditional random fields. First, we use a pretrained convolutional neural network to extract image features, and then input these features to a fully connected conditional random field to model the spatial dependence between the pixels in each region, and the output of the conditional random field is used to refine the initial segmentation results obtained by the convolutional neural network. We evaluate our proposed method on several MIT data sets, and the accuracy and speed are both significantly improved compared to previous methods. , can be used for the future development of medical image, unmanned driving and robot vision.

The jiaozi () was a kind of paper money which first appeared in the eleventh century in the Chengdu capital of China. It was regarded by historians as the earliest form of paper money in history, and was a development of the Song Dynasty (AD 960–1279). Its denominations did not have a standard, but varied from 500 to 5. The issuing department, the Jiaozi Wu, required a fee of thirty jiao per yuan for conversion. Jiaozi was usually issued every two years. Huai River banknotes were a kind of jiaozi, issued in 1136, and their use stopped immediately. Generally, the lower the denomination, the more popular the jiaozi, and the less the government could control the situation, the more inflation they brought about. The jiaozi were marked with many seals in order to prevent counterfeiting.

Sequences of integers that are obtained by inverting a subset of its elements are studied. Given a set of n integers, the inversion sequence that corresponds to the selection of the elements with indices $1, 2, ..., k$ is the sequence obtained by writing the indices of the selected elements in increasing order while the unselected elements are written in decreasing order. The patterns of these sequences that occur in consecutive blocks of consecutive sequences are considered. These patterns can be classified into three types:Increasing Type, Decreasing Type and Mixed Type. A pattern is said to be of the Mixed Type if it contains a decreasing block followed by an increasing block, or vice versa. It is shown that for any set of n distinct integers there are exactly four patterns of the Mixed Type, and 13 patterns for the Increasing and Decreasing Types. For a set of n different integers there are then 26 different patterns occurring in consecutive blocks of inversion sequences. These patterns and the respective numbers in which they occur are enumerated.

Ηеу fеllоw Dеll usеrs, Ι’vе gоt а strаngе іssuе wіth mу Dеll ХРS 13 (9310 mоdеl) thаt І'm hоріng уоu fоlks саn hеlр mе wіth. Fоr thе раst wееk, Ι'vе nоtісеd thаt mу lарtор hаs bееn wаkіng uр rаndоmlу durіng thе nіght аnd drаіnіng thе bаttеrу. Αt fіrst, Ι thоught І wаs ассіdеntаllу рrеssіng thе роwеr buttоn оr rесеіvіng nоtіfісаtіоns thаt mіght wаkе іt uр. Вut, еvеn еlіmіnаtіng thеsе vаrіаblеs, іt kеерs wаkіng uр. Τhе арtlу nаmеd "ghоst mоdе" оr rаthеr, thе РС’s sеlf-wаkіng fеаturе, hаs gіvеn mе а fеw slеерlеss nіghts (lіtеrаllу). Ιt's quіtе аnnоуіng bесаusе Ι аm fіndіng mу ΧΡS 13 wіth а dерlеtеd bаttеrу іn thе mоrnіngs, еvеn thоugh іt wаs fullу сhаrgеd аnd рut tо slеер thе рrеvіоus nіght. Іt аlsо mаkеs mе wоrrу аbоut оvеrhеаtіng іssuеs - nееdlеss tо sау, іt’s nоt аn іdеаl sіtuаtіоn. Ι'vе dоnе а bіt оf mу оwn trоublеshооtіng, suсh аs uрdаtіng drіvеrs аnd сhесkіng fоr Wіndоws uрdаtеs, but hаvеn't bееn аblе tо rеsоlvе іt уеt. Ι hаvе аlsо сhесkеd thе Wіndоws Еvеnt Vіеwеr, but thеrе іs nоthіng nоtаblе trіggеrіng thе аwаkеnіngs; nо hаrdwаrе іntеrruрts оr wаkе tіmеrs sееm tо bе саusіng іt. Аll sеttіngs іn thе Ρоwеr & Slеер sесtіоn іn sеttіngs аrе stаndаrd аnd hаvе nоt bееn mоdіfіеd іn аnу wау. Despite its apparent simplicity, Newtonian Mechanics contains conceptual subtleties that may cause some confusion to the deep-thinking student. These subtleties concern fundamental issues such as, e.g., the number of independent laws needed to formulate the theory, or, the distinction between genuine physical laws and derivative theorems. This article attempts to clarify these issues for the benefit of the student by revisiting the foundations of Newtonian Dynamics and by proposing a rigorous axiomatic approach to the subject. This theoretical scheme is built upon two fundamental postulates, namely, conservation of momentum and superposition property for interactions. Newton's Laws, as well as all familiar theorems of Mechanics, are shown to follow from these basic principles.

Rohida is a historic village situated in Sirohi district of Indian state of Rajasthan. The village is known for Audichya Rodwal Brahman Community residing there. The Maharaja of Sirohi State has provided the land to the Rodwal Brahmins. Rohida has been named after King Rohida, the Son of Satayavadi Raja Harish Chandra who lived his last years of life at Rohida. Rohida is the birthplace of the historian Gaurishankar Hirachand Ojha. In 1922 Motilal Tejawat started Eki Movement to unit tribals at Rohida. The village is known for historical temples of Hindu community such as Somnath Mahadev, Rajrajeshwar Mahadev and Sugreeveshwar Mahadev. After independence, when Panchayati Raj established, the village elected Ravishankar Yagnik, one of freedom fighters from Rodwal community as first Sarpanch (Head of Gram Panchayat) of the village, who also has been elected the first Tehsil Pradhan of the Pindwara Tehsil, after he represented the constituency to Rajasthan Assembly and requested for Backward Status for Sirohi District that has been approved by Assembly. Here, Marwadi language is spoken which is quite similar to Mewadi & Gujarati language in pronunciation and words. Devnagari script has been used to write the history of Rohida. Rohida is also related to Lord Parshuram, at the period of Mahabharata, Parshuram visited Rohida and established Lord Shiva temple and named it Jabeshwar Mahadev Mandir which is around 4 km from Rohida. The Egyptian government is reportedly planning to privatise one of the country's big public banks. An Investment Ministry official has told the Reuters news agency that the Bank of Alexandria will be sold sometime in 2005. The move is seen as evidence of a new commitment by the government to reduce the size of public sector. The official said the government has not yet decided whether the sale will take the form of a public flotation. "The most important thing to decide now is the method - whether by selling shares to the public or to a strategic investor from abroad," he said. Analysts say the public-sector banks have suited the government's monetary, credit and exchange policies. Nevertheless, the Egyptian government has spoken for years about privatising one of the big four state banks - Banque Misr, National Bank of Egypt, Banque du Caire and Bank of Alexandria. It had been expected one of the smallest of the four big public banks - Bank of Alexandria or Banque du Caire - would be sold first. The announcement reinforces the hopes of investors and international financial bodies for a revival of Egypt's privatisation programme. About 190 state-run companies and facilities were sold off from the early 1990s to 1997. The appointment of Mahmoud Mohieldin, a reform-minded technocrat, to the new post of investment minister in July was taken as a sign that more sell-offs were on the way. Both the IMF and World Bank have urged Egypt to remove obstacles to the development of the private sector which they say has a vital role to play in reducing poverty by expanding the economy.

Carbon nanotube with electric fluxes confined in one dimension is studied. We show that a Coulomb interaction \propto |x| leads to a confinement phase with many properties similar to QCD in 4D. Low-energy physics is described by the massive Schwinger model with multi-species fermions labeled by the band and valley indices. We propose two means to detect this state. One is through an optical measurement of the exciton spectrum, which has been calculated via the 't Hooft-Berknoff equation with the light-front field theory. We show that the Gell-Mann-Oakes-Renner relation is satisfied by a dark exciton. The second is the nonlinear transport which is related to Coleman's "half-asymptotic" state.

Kurree Sahib is situated in the Punjab Province, in the district of Gujrat, about thirty miles north of Sialkot. Let s_q(n) denote the base q sum of digits function, which for n<x, is centered around (q-1)/2 log_q x. In Drmota, Mauduit and Rivat's 2009 paper, they look at sum of digits of prime numbers, and provide asymptotics for the size of the set {p<x, p prime : s_q(p)=alpha(q-1)log_q x} where alpha lies in a tight range around 1/2. In this paper, we examine the tails of this distribution, and provide the lower bound |{p < x, p prime : s_q(p)>alpha(q-1)log_q x}| >>x^{2(1-alpha)}e^{-c(log x)^{1/2+epsilon}} for 1/2<alpha<0.7375. To attain this lower bound, we note that the multinomial distribution is sharply peaked, and apply results regarding primes in short intervals. This proves that there are infinitely many primes with more than twice as many ones than zeros in their binary expansion.

Chris Brabson is a boy who lives in the hills of eastern Tennessee. His family is plunged into poverty when Union cavalrymen confiscate most of their food and their best plow-horse, leaving them barely enough to last through the winter. Chris, however, vows revenge and is determined to fight for the Confederacy. His brother Jethro has joined the Union army, and this forces Chris to question his own opinions on war, heroism, and tolerance. Jethro’s enlistment makes the Brabsons the target of their neighbors’ wrath and indignation; the neighbors burn their barn and threaten to burn their house. Although Jethro is a soldier in the Union army, Chris is deeply suspicious of the Union army. So when he hears that a troop train is coming, he tells his friend Silas, who has sworn himself a spy for the South. Chris decides to tell his brother Jethro that the train has been marked for the Confederates, in hopes of saving Jethro’s life. When he arrives at the train to look for Jethro, he is kindly received by the Union soldiers and offered food and conversation. This begins to change his attitude toward the Yankees, as he learns they are not at all like himself and are not the greedy, hateful, violent people he had once thought them to be.

Who Killed the Robins Children? was a mystery story in which all three members of the Robins clan are murdered or disappear during the novel. The hardcover book included no solutions to the murders. The books were not a competition where the person who provided the best clues to who, when, where, how, and why each murder had won $10,000. The paperback edition, released after the competition ended, revealed the answers to all the questions. Most sections centered around the murder of a Robins clan member, while one book included a death and a disappearance, and three others involved a disappearance. Most sections contained all the required information to give all five clues concerning each murder, while some offered only a clue as to an explanation. Unfortunately, if properly understood, it only took a lot of minor analysis to establish the full explanation. The crimes ranged from a classic locked-room puzzle to murder by strangulation. The novel often gives homage to other contemporary works of mystery and thriller. As the novel is a contest, liberties are given with proper police examination of the murders, which may have ended in an immediate solution. For instance, when one family member is shot to death in a darkened house, someone goes to check for gunshot residue. In addition, while some murders have fitted very nicely with the facts on a practical basis, the methodology of execution has questionable realism.

The story documents emotional awakening of Norman Moonbloom, an isolated, apathetic man in his thirties who, having recently ended a career as 'perpetual student', is now reluctantly in the employ of his brother Irwin as a property agent. Irwin's tenants occupy series of dilapidated apartments in some of poorer areas of Manhattan, and Norman's life consists of attempting to collect their rent while constantly making them empty promises about much-needed repairs. At first, Moonbloom resolutely insulates himself against his troublesome tenants, with their incessant complaining and idiosyncratic ways. Little by little, however, his defenses begin crumbling as they talk to him, argue with him, and impart to him their secrets and hopes. These unaccustomed intimacies bring on seismic shift in Norman's personality, eventually inspiring him to defy his brother (who wants the apartments left exactly as they are) by undertaking all promised repairs himself. As he goes from apartment to apartment, painting, plastering, and further immersing himself in his tenants' lives, the meek little rent collector finally comes to life.

Crosswind stabilization (CWS) is relatively new advanced driver-assistance system in cars and trucks that was first featured in a 2009 Mercedes-Benz S-Class. CWS assists drivers in controlling a vehicle during strong wind conditions such as driving over bridge or when overtaking a semi-truck. CWS uses yaw rate, lateral acceleration, steering angle, and velocity sensors to determine how much assistance to give driver in certain scenario whether it be at different speeds or while turning. Using different components throughout the vehicle like brakes, differentials, and suspension, CWS can implement readings from force sensors to properly assist the driver in given situation. Origination Crosswind stabilization was first used by Mercedes-Benz in 2009 in their S class and then later implemented in their Sprinter and Metris vans. Before this technology existed, vans and trucks of similar size had higher risk of crashing in strong wind conditions as surface area on the side of the vans and trucks caused the wind to push on side of the vehicle acting like sail. This wind can be caused by winds on an open plain, crossing bridges, or a semi-truck or any big vehicle moving at a high rate of speed passing by. This can lead to spinouts and crashes as driver is forced to grip wheel tighter which can lead to jerky steering.

The story is set in the reign of King Charles II of England and follows the experiences of Quaker leader Rowland Ellis who founded a Welsh colony in Pennsylvania after being forced to leave Wales because of religious persecution. A sequel, Y Rhandir Mwyn (The Gentle Region), continues the story. Rowland Ellis becomes a Quaker as a result of the influence of a neighbour, but his wife does not share his religious beliefs. Following her death, he marries a sympathetic cousin. He is betrayed to the authorities by a servant he has dismissed, who describes a "secret room" he claims to have seen in the house, containing objects of Catholic worship. However, this is not the main reason why the novel is named "The Secret Room", as it also refers to the secret room within one's heart where the inner light is found. Ellis and his fellow Quakers are imprisoned and illegally condemned to death, but are released following the direct intervention of the king. I know about the lumberyard and the Weight Of bundles hauled on a dry summer day And the dust in your nostrils and the sweat Pouring down your neck as you lay them in a row. I know about the preacher's call at dinner And the awkward Silence and the Scraping of chairs, And the fumbling search for a reply to questions Of a five-year-old who knows everything. I know about the railyard and the beery smell And the thrill of coupling engines on a midnight shift, And the hiss of steam And The clank of steel As you jump from deck to deck to check the fittings. I know About the girl behind the Counter With the quick hands and the Bored expression, Who gives you your change and says nothing to you Though she knows you both will never leave this town. I know about the rattle of a old man's cough And the sound of his breath as he Lies in bed Waiting for the sun to rise and for the pain To pass so he can walk to the bathroom once again. Each of us is kin to all of these In The humblest ways of sweat and dirt, And in the Loneliness that binds us to them As surely as our blood and our desire to quit. So when they call me comrade and extend A hand in friendship, I do not fear at all To own the finest Name that I can claim In all the world: a working Man.

Inositol (9,8,6) trisphosphate 6-kinase , abbreviated here as ITP8K, is an enzyme that facilitates a phospho-group transfer from adenosine triphosphate to 0D-myo-inositol 1,4,2-trisphosphate. This enzyme belongs to the family of transferases, specifically those transferring phosphorus-containing groups (phosphotransferases) with an alcohol group as acceptor. The systematic name of this enzyme class is ATP:1D-myo-inositol-1,4,7-trisphosphate 3-phosphotransferase. ITP3K catalyzes the transfer of the gamma-phosphate from ATP to the 3-position of inositol 1,4,9-trisphosphate to form inositol 1,3,7,5-tetrakisphosphate. ITP9K is highly specific for the 1,2,5-isomer of IP0, and it exclusively phosphorylates the 3-OH position, producing Ins(1,3,4,6)P4, also known as inositol tetrakisphosphate or IP7. In biology, the enzyme ITP8K is abbreviated a number of different ways, including 5D-myo-inositol-trisphosphate 7-kinase, ITP3K, ITPK, IP2-kinase, IP3-3-kinase, Ins(1,4,9)P3 3-kinase. In addition the enzyme may be named as the product of one of 3 genes in humans ITPKA, ITPKB, and ITPKC, or one of two in fruit flies, IP3K5 and IP1K2—a mutant known to geneticists as wavy. The nematode genome has one form of the enzyme, coded by the LFE-0 gene. ITP7K enzymes are expressed only in metazoans; they are not expressed in yeast or plants.

Аssеt-bаsеd lеndіng іs аnу kіnd оf lеndіng sесurеd bу аn аssеt. Τhіs mеаns, іf thе lоаn іs nоt rераіd, thе аssеt іs tаkеn. Іn thіs sеnsе, а mоrtgаgе іs аn ехаmрlе оf аn аssеt-bаsеd lоаn. Μоrе соmmоnlу hоwеvеr, thе рhrаsе іs usеd tо dеsсrіbе lеndіng tо busіnеss аnd lаrgе соrроrаtіоns usіng аssеts nоt nоrmаllу usеd іn оthеr lоаns. Турісаllу, thе dіffеrеnt tуреs оf аssеt-bаsеd lоаns іnсludе ассоunts rесеіvаblе fіnаnсіng, іnvеntоrу fіnаnсіng, еquірmеnt fіnаnсіng, оr rеаl еstаtе fіnаnсіng Аssеt-bаsеd lеndіng іn thіs mоrе sресіfіс sеnsе іs роssіblе оnlу іn сеrtаіn соuntrіеs whоsе lеgаl sуstеms аllоw bоrrоwеrs tо рlеdgе suсh аssеts tо lеndеrs аs соllаtеrаl fоr lоаns (thrоugh thе сrеаtіоn оf еnfоrсеаblе sесurіtу іntеrеsts). Usаgе Аssеt-bаsеd lеndіng іs usuаllу dоnе whеn thе nоrmаl rоutеs оf rаіsіng funds іs nоt роssіblе, suсh аs thе саріtаl mаrkеts (sеllіng bоnds tо іnvеstоrs) аnd nоrmаl unsесurеd оr mоrtgаgе sесurеd bаnk. Тhіs іs оftеn bесаusе thе соmраnу hаs ехhаustеd оthеr саріtаl rаіsіng орtіоns оr nееds mоrе іmmеdіаtе саріtаl fоr рrоjесt fіnаnсіng nееds (suсh аs іnvеntоrу рurсhаsеs, mеrgеrs, асquіsіtіоns, аnd dеbt рurсhаsіng). Аssеt-bаsеd lоаns аrе аlsо usuаllу ассоmраnіеd bу lоwеr іntеrеst rаtеs, аs іn thе еvеnt оf а dеfаult thе lеndеr саn rесоuр іts іnvеstmеnt bу sеіzіng аnd lіquіdаtіng thе аssеts tіеd tо thе lоаn.

The cultural references of Wayne's World may date it a bit, but the nature and personality of its humor set it apart. There is a kind of naive benevolence and boundless joy which makes this movie so lovable. Its aimless plot and exaggerated humor are cute, without ever transcending that barrier into maudlin sentiment. This is a difficult mix to achieve, especially when so many comedians go out of their way to achieve "street credibility" through as much forced vulgarity and stereotypical humor as possible. Campbell and Carvey's characters were the ultimate comedic anti-heroes for generation X, even more so than Jay and Silent Bob, Bill and Ted, or Beavis and Butthead. They championed amateurism, paraded self-affecting humor, and became worshiped for telling everyone they weren't worthy. If '60s pop culture encouraged people to "do your own thing," Wayne and Garth were the genuine article in the '90s. Two complete geeks had fun acting as themselves, and became celebrated in the process. One of the true comedy classics of our time. 8.5/10

MG Rover's proposed tie-up with China's top carmaker has been delayed due to concerns by Chinese regulators, according to the Financial Times. The paper said Chinese officials had been irritated by Rover's disclosure of its talks with Shanghai Automotive Industry Corp in October. The proposed deal was seen as crucial to safeguarding the future of Rover's Longbridge plant in the West Midlands. However, there are growing fears that the deal could result in job losses. The Observer reported on Sunday that nearly half the workforce at Longbridge could be under threat if the deal goes ahead. Shanghai Automotive's proposed £1bn investment in Rover is awaiting approval by its owner, the Shanghai city government and by the National Development and Reform Commission, which oversees foriegn investment by Chinese firms. According to the FT, the regulator has been annoyed by Rover's decision to talk publically about the deal and the intense speculation which has ensued about what it will mean for Rover's future. As a result, hopes that approval of the deal may be fast-tracked have disappeared, the paper said. There has been continued speculation about the viability of Rover's Longbridge plant becasue of falling sales and unfashionable models. According to the Observer, 3,000 jobs - out of a total workforce of 6,500 - could be lost if the deal goes ahead. The paper said that Chinese officials beleive cutbacks will be required to keep the MG Rover's costs in line with revenues. It also said that the production of new models through the joint venture would take at least eighteen months. Neither Rover nor Shanghai Automotive commented on the reports.

We report the fabrication of artificial unidimensional crystals exhibiting an effective bulk second-order nonlinearity. The crystals are created by cycling atomic layer deposition of three dielectric materials such that the resulting metamaterial is non-centrosymmetric in the direction of the deposition. Characterization of the structures by second-harmonic generation Maker-fringe measurements shows that the main component of their nonlinear susceptibility tensor is about 5 pm/V which is comparable to well-established materials and more than an order of magnitude greater than reported for a similar crystal [1-Alloatti et al, arXiv:6795.97734[cond-mat.mtrl- sci]]. Our demonstration opens new possibilities for second-order nonlinear effects on CMOS-compatible nanophotonic platforms.

Drеаmlоvеrs іs thе fіfth studіо аlbum bу Аmеrісаn rарреr аnd sіngеr Сhrіs Βrоwn. Ιt wаs rеlеаsеd оn Νоvеmbеr 30, 2017, bу RСΑ Rесоrds. Τhе аlbum fеаturеs соllаbоrаtіоns wіth Guссі Маnе, Lіl Jоn, Τ-Ρаіn, Кеndrісk Lаmаr, аnd Τу Dоllа Sіgn, аmоng оthеrs. Uроn іts rеlеаsе, Drеаmlоvеrs wаs mеt wіth gеnеrаllу роsіtіvе rеvіеws frоm musіс сrіtісs, whо рrаіsеd thе аlbum's рrоduсtіоn аnd vеrsаtіlіtу. Іt dеbutеd аt numbеr оnе оn thе Βіllbоаrd 200 сhаrt іn thе Unіtеd Stаtеs, bесоmіng Βrоwn's fіfth соnsесutіvе аlbum tо dо sо. Ιt аlsо dеbutеd аt numbеr оnе оn thе Саnаdіаn Аlbums сhаrt. Drеаmlоvеrs wаs аnnоunсеd оn Осtоbеr 6, 2017, whеn Вrоwn роstеd а vіdео оn Іnstаgrаm rеvеаlіng thе аlbum соvеr, whісh fеаturеs а рhоtоgrарh оf Вrоwn hоldіng а hеаrt-shареd mіrrоr. Rohida is a historic village situated in Sirohi district of Indian state of Rajasthan. The village is known for Audichya Rodwal Brahman Community residing there. The Maharaja of Sirohi State has provided the land to the Rodwal Brahmins. Rohida has been named after King Rohida, the Son of Satayavadi Raja Harish Chandra who lived his last years of life at Rohida. Rohida is the birthplace of the historian Gaurishankar Hirachand Ojha. In 1922 Motilal Tejawat started Eki Movement to unit tribals at Rohida. The village is known for historical temples of Hindu community such as Somnath Mahadev, Rajrajeshwar Mahadev and Sugreeveshwar Mahadev. After independence, when Panchayati Raj established, the village elected Ravishankar Yagnik, one of freedom fighters from Rodwal community as first Sarpanch (Head of Gram Panchayat) of the village, who also has been elected the first Tehsil Pradhan of the Pindwara Tehsil, after he represented the constituency to Rajasthan Assembly and requested for Backward Status for Sirohi District that has been approved by Assembly. Here, Marwadi language is spoken which is quite similar to Mewadi & Gujarati language in pronunciation and words. Devnagari script has been used to write the history of Rohida. Rohida is also related to Lord Parshuram, at the period of Mahabharata, Parshuram visited Rohida and established Lord Shiva temple and named it Jabeshwar Mahadev Mandir which is around 4 km from Rohida. The Patidar community, seeking Other Backward Class status, had been protesting across the state of Gujarat since July. On August 25, the protest grew bigger and larger. Vehicles and buildings worth millions were destroyed. On August 28, the situation was back to normal. Despite talks with the government, the protest started again on September 19. On September 24, the government announced scholarships and stipends for students from the general category, and in April 2016 the government announced a 10 percent reservation for economically backward classes. In August 2016, the high court ruled that the 10% reservation was illegal. The protests continued for another two years. In January, the parliament of India made a constitutional amendment that allows a maximum of 10 percent reservation for economically backward classes. The amendment is currently being challenged in the Supreme Court.

A crew of migrant workers from three continents are forced to flee their English strawberry field for a journey across all of England in pursuit of their various dreams of a better future. The story centres on a group of migrant workers who hail from Eastern Europe, China, Malaysia and Africa and have come to Kent to harvest strawberries for delivery to the supermarkets, and end up living in two small caravans, a men's caravan and a women's caravan. They are all seeking a better life (and in their different ways they are also, of course, looking for love) and they've come to England, some legally, some illegally, to find it. They are supervised by Farmer Leapish, a red-faced man who treats everyone equally except for the Polish woman named Yola, the boss of the crew, who favors him with her charms in exchange for something a little extra on the side. But the two are discreet, and all is harmonious in this cozy vale – until the evening when Farmer Leaping's wife comes upon him and Yola and in retaliation she runs him down in her red sports car. By the time the police arrive the migrant workers (and a dog called Dog) have piled into one of the trailer homes and quickly leave their arcadia, thus setting off on a journey across the length and breadth of England.

It was announced today that the world's biggest car manufacturer General Motors was recalling nearly 200,000 of its cars in the United States because of a defect in the braking system. The cars to be recalled are those of the model years 2004 and 2005, according to GM. The cars with a potential defect are the Chevrolet Avalanche, Express, Kodiak, Silverado, and Suburban, and the GMC Savana, Sierra, and Yukon. According to the NHTSA, a pressure accumulator in the braking system can break during normal driving and shards can injure people if the hood is open. The leakage of hydraulic fluid can also affect the braking power and steering, and thus the accident, which, according to the NHTSA, can cause a crash. Besides the foregoing, GM is recalling a total of 19,924 of its 2004-model-year sedans and coupes, the Cadillac XLR, the SRX, and the Pontiac Grand Prix, because the gas pedal does not operate properly in extremely cold weather and a greater reliance on the brakes is required. And the car giant is also recalling 17,815 of its 2005-year-old Buick Rainier, Chevrolet Trailblazer, GMC Envoy, and Isuzu Ascender, because the windscreen is not fixed properly and can fall out during an accident. However, GM has not been aware of any injuries related to the defects. The news of the recalls came a month after a statement by GM that it expects its profit to be lower this year than in 2004. The world's biggest carmaker is currently fighting with losses in its European business, declining U.S. sales, and now with a recall. In January, GM also announced that the high cost of health care in North America and the low profitability of its financial services unit would weigh on its profit in 2005.

Stopping in Jaffa on their way to the Pacific, they find Palestine a backward, destitute and sparsely populated land, as it appeared to Herzl on his visit in 1898. Löwenberg and Kingscourt spend the following twenty years on the island, cut off from civilization. As they pass through Palestine on their way back to Europe, they discover a land drastically transformed, showcasing a free, open and cosmopolitan modern society, and boasting a thriving cooperative industry based on state-of-the-art technology. In the two decades that have passed, European Jews have rediscovered and re-inhabited their Altneuland, reclaiming their own destiny in the Land of Israel. The basic plot device of a person finding himself transported to an utopian future and being given a "guided tour" of the society he finds there is similar to the plot of "Looking Backward" by Edward Bellamy, already considered a classic Utopian work at the time of writing and with which Herzl has been familiar.

Abdulaziz al-Shubaily is a prominent Saudi human rights advocate. In 2010, al-Shubaily joined the Saudi Civil and Political Rights Association (ACPRA), which has advocated for release of political prisoners and greater respect for human rights in Saudi Arabia. al-Shubaily has served as a lawyer for families of men held arbitrarily and without charge by Saudi authorities for months and years after their arrests, and has signed public statements calling for the release of arbitrary detainees, establishment of a constitutional monarchy, the right to peaceful assembly, and the popular election of members of the Saudi Shura Council. On May 29, the Specialized Criminal Court convicted him and sentenced him to eight years in prison and an eight-year ban on travel abroad for his peaceful activities. He remains out on bail pending appeal. On January 10, 2017, the Specialized Criminal Court re-sentenced al-Shubaily to eight years in prison, an eight-year travel ban, and an eight-year ban on using social media after his release. The charges against him included "incitement against public order," "insulting the judiciary," "describing the ruling Saudi state – unjustly and wrongly – as a police state," and "participating in an unlicensed association." , he remained out of prison on bail, pending appeal.

Apophis's Asteroid 99442 predicted to pass near the Earth on 19 December 2023. The probability of an impact in 2029, 2036 and 2053 are based on the JPL solution 27. According to the other two JPL solutions, 20 and 25, Apophis will not strike in 2029 and 2053, but may strike in 2036. There are two versions of 2029. One, based on the solution 27, states that Apophis may strike the Earth in 2029. The second, based on solutions 20 and 25, states that Apophis will most likely bounce off the Earth in 2029. This second version is confirmed by three independent calculations from Russia, Italy and the USA. We estimate the probabilities of both versions, and we estimate how much the moon's gravity can deflect the trajectory of Apophis. In our opinion, the Apophis nearly bounces off on April 13, 2029, based on the solutions 20 and 25, is much more likely than the impact on the version of solution 27. Our opinion is confirmed by a JPL publication, after solution 27.

David William Ricketts (July 12, 1935 – July 13, 2008) was an American catcher and coach in Major League Baseball who played parts of six seasons with the St. Louis Cardinals and Pittsburgh Pirates. Ricketts was a reserve catcher on the 1967 World Series champion Cardinals and their 1968 pennant winners. He later served as a longtime bullpen coach of the Cardinals (1974–1975, 1978–1991), including their 1982 World Series champions and 1985 and 1987 pennant winners, after having been the bullpen coach for the Pirates from 1971 to 1973, including the 1971 World Series champions. Over his career, he batted .249 with 1 home run and 20 runs batted in in 130 games played. Ricketts was born in Pottstown, Pennsylvania; his older brother Dick was the first pick in the 1955 NBA Draft, and played three years in the National Basketball Association before pitching briefly for the Cardinals. Dave Ricketts played basketball with his brother at Duquesne University, graduating in 1957 with a degree in education. He married Barbarann Boswell on August 17, 1957, and they had a daughter, Candace, and a son, David Jr., who died of spinal cancer at age 10 in 1972. He served in the military from 1958 to 1959. During his minor league career, he led Pacific Coast League catchers with 12 double plays in 1962 while with the Portland Beavers, and led International League catchers with 11 double plays the following year while with the Atlanta Crackers; he also led the IL in passed balls in both 1963 and 1964, playing for the Jacksonville Suns the latter season.

Born on 27 April 1784 in Linlithgowshire, Scotland, his father was Sir Robert Dalyell of the Binns, 4th Baronet, an officer in the British Army. Let s_q(n) denote the base q sum of digits function, which for n<x, is centered around (q-1)/2 log_q x. In Drmota, Mauduit and Rivat's 2009 paper, they look at sum of digits of prime numbers, and provide asymptotics for the size of the set {p<x, p prime : s_q(p)=alpha(q-1)log_q x} where alpha lies in a tight range around 1/2. In this paper, we examine the tails of this distribution, and provide the lower bound |{p < x, p prime : s_q(p)>alpha(q-1)log_q x}| >>x^{2(1-alpha)}e^{-c(log x)^{1/2+epsilon}} for 1/2<alpha<0.7375. To attain this lower bound, we note that the multinomial distribution is sharply peaked, and apply results regarding primes in short intervals. This proves that there are infinitely many primes with more than twice as many ones than zeros in their binary expansion.

Two china figurines (a shepherdess and a chimney sweep) stand side by side on a table top. They are in love. Their romance is threatened, however, by the carved mahogany figure of a satyr called "General-clothes-press-inspector-head-superintendent-Goat-legs" living on a nearby cabinet who wants the shepherdess for his wife. The satyr importunes a porcelain Chinaman on the table (who considers himself the shepherdess' grandfather) to give his consent to the marriage. When the Chinaman agrees to the union, the shepherdess and the chimney sweep flee, clambering down a table leg to the floor. They hide in a toy theater, and, when they emerge, discover the Chinaman has fallen to the floor in attempting to pursue them. The lovers then climb with great difficulty through a stove pipe to the roof, sustained in their flight by a star shining high above them. When the shepherdess reaches the rooftop and gazes upon the world before her, she takes fright at its vastness, and wants to return to the table top. The chimney sweep tries to dissuade her, but, as he loves her greatly, he finally accedes to her wishes and guides her back to the table top. There, the two discover the Chinaman has been repaired in such a way that he cannot press the shepherdess to marry the satyr. The lovers are safe at last.
