The recent advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) combined with the extensive amount of data generated by today's clinical systems, has led to the development of imaging AI solutions across the whole value chain of medical imaging, including image reconstruction, medical image segmentation, image-based diagnosis and treatment planning. Notwithstanding the successes and future potential of AI in medical imaging, many stakeholders are concerned of the potential risks and ethical implications of imaging AI solutions, which are perceived as complex, opaque, and difficult to comprehend, utilise, and trust in critical clinical applications. Despite these concerns and risks, there are currently no concrete guidelines and best practices for guiding future AI developments in medical imaging towards increased trust, safety and adoption. To bridge this gap, this paper introduces a careful selection of guiding principles drawn from the accumulated experiences, consensus, and best practices from five large European projects on AI in Health Imaging. These guiding principles are named FUTURE-AI and its building blocks consist of (i) Fairness, (ii) Universality, (iii) Traceability, (iv) Usability, (v) Robustness and (vi) Explainability. In a step-by-step approach, these guidelines are further translated into a framework of concrete recommendations for specifying, developing, evaluating, and deploying technically, clinically and ethically trustworthy AI solutions into clinical practice.

I am twenty-five years old, and I have no children. Why am I singing the praises of a children's film which nobody has seen? Because never have I seen a film with so many moving emotions as The Iron Giant. The plot is similar to E.T.—a young boy befriends a lonely robot from outer space, which is stranded on Earth and must evade a jealous government agency. The great thing about The Iron Giant—nothing against E.T.—is that the boy is the one who teaches the robot. The boy is the one who must teach the giant about the beauty of life, the difference between good and evil, and the choice one must make. The Iron Giant, it turns out, is a weapon which must struggle against its own nature. The film makes an obvious and timely plea for gun control, but its true theme is about the choices we make when dealing with others. Using our powers for good or against everyone. I dare not give away the climax, but it features a sacrifice that is breathtaking and heartbreaking, though somewhat blunted by the ending. The animation is marvelous, the music by Michael Kamen is perfect, and the film perfectly evokes the 1950s. Sadly, it was not marketed properly, and it was a huge commercial flop. To hell with box office. Despite the fact that the studio seems to want to forget about the film, the word is getting around that it's a marvelous film, and I am sure it will be the next It's a Wonderful Life, a flop which turned into a classic. So go see it now so you can say you were there when it was discovered.

Segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision. We present a new technique for image segmentation that performs a generalization of traditional boundary-based algorithms. While traditional approaches consider only binary (background / foreground) segmentations of pixels, our algorithm can generate higher-order binary and non-binary pixel representations. We use the notion of region adjacency graphs (RAGs) as our base representation for these pixel descriptions. A RAG is a graph whose vertices are the set of pixels in the image, and there is an edge between each pair of pixels in the image if they share a common boundary (in a pre-computed image smoothing). Our technique performs a panoptic segmentation of the pixels in an image using a novel dynamic programming formulation. It uses an iterative set-cover based algorithm that simultaneously segments the image and finds the MRF representation that best captures the underlying pixel structure. We demonstrate that this algorithm produces state-of-the-art region segmentations on a range of images from the Berkeley Segmentation Dataset and the PASCAL Data Set. We illustrate that this algorithm can be used to produce an automatic panoptic segmentation as well.

Martin Brian Mulroney (; born March 20, 1939) is a Canadian lawyer, businessman, and politician who served as the 18th prime minister of Canada from 1984 to 1993. Born in the eastern Quebec city of Baie-Comeau, Mulroney studied political science and law. He then moved to Montreal and gained prominence as a lawyer and businessman. He unsuccessfully ran for the leadership of the Progressive Conservative Party of Canada (PC Party) in 1976, coming in third place, and then returned back to business leadership as he was appointed president of the Iron Ore Company of Canada in 1977. He held that post until 1983, when he successfully became leader of the Progressive Conservatives. He then carried the party to a landslide victory in the 1984 federal election, winning 211 seats, the highest number of seats won by any party in Canadian history. The election was the last time that the winning party won every province and territory and the last time that the winning party received over 50% of the national popular vote. Mulroney also won the second-largest percentage of seats in Canadian history (at 74.8%). Mulroney later won a second majority government in 1988.

NeuroNet is a deep convolutional neural network, that is, a neural network, that can imitate several of the most popular and state-of-the-art tools for the brain. This neural network is fed with 5000 MR images from the Biobank study, which were automatically analyzed and segmented into brain tissue and cortical and subcortical structures by using the standard neuroimaging tools. This neural network is trained on these automatically labeled images, and from these partially overlapping labels it produces a new, powerful, “all-in-one” brain tool. For a given subject, the neural network reduces the analysis time by an order of magnitude, compared to the time needed to run each individual tool. We show that the output is highly reproducible with the original methods, and at the same time the neural network is more resistant to variations in the input data. We believe that NeuroNet can be an important tool in large-scale population-based brain studies, and that it can become the new standard for the field of neuroimaging by reducing the risk of bias due to the choice of individual tools.

This part of the book consists of four chapters in which Metlitzki explores how scientific achievements were translated and transmitted from Arabic texts to Western (primarily English authors writing in Latin) texts. She begins this book by addressing the crusades and the development of scholarship by Mozarabs, i.e. Christians living under Muslim rule, particularly those in Muslim Spain and Sicily (p. 3-10). She writes about several Western scholars who were involved in translating Arabic texts and studying Arab held libraries, including several key ancient Greek and Roman texts that were only available in Arabic. Some of these scholars included Adelard of Bath (p. 26) who was a Western scholar responsible for translating Al-Khwarizmi’s texts on astronomy and Euclid’s Elements from Arabic into Latin. She details the lives of several of these key scholars including Petrus Alfonsi, a Christian converted ex-Jew living in Muslim Spain and author of the seminal text Disciplina Clericalis, which, according to Metlitzki was the first collection of Oriental tales composed in the West for Westerners (p. 16). Robert of Ketton was the first translator of the Quran into Latin and also translated several key scientific texts such as Alchemy by Morienus Romanus and Math, Algebra and astronomy texts by Al-Khwarizmi. Michael Scot was a scholar interested in magic, alchemy and astronomy and was also the first translator of most of the works of Aristotle (from Arabic into Latin), whose writings had been banned in the West as being heretical (p. 48). In part two Metlitzki explores key English medieval texts and suggests that they either are based entirely on Arabic stories or include elements from Arabic storytelling that suggest that they had been loosely based on Arabic stories. She then suggests that the English medieval Romance itself is strongly influenced by Arabic ideals of romantic chivalry as well as key Arabic stories from various sources including the 1001 Nights. The English texts she closely examines include Chaucer’s The Canterbury Tales, the English Charlemagne Romances like Sir Ferumbras and the Sowdone of Babylone (p. 172-3) and several others. In several of these texts, Metlitzki explains, are found the beginnings of the misunderstanding of Islam by the West and she explores the depiction of Islam and the Islamic prophet Muhammad in these texts in her chapter on History and Romance (p. 95-210). On page 245 she also suggests that contributions to English and Western literature from Arabic literature includes several key themes (such as Romance) and also rhyming poetry itself.

She lives in her own world—doing what she thinks best for her budding business—ignoring the things that irritate her to impatience—but the resentment she feels is expressed in bitter facial expressions, always provoked by her mother’s loquacious chattering. While everyone else is getting on with their lives, drinking their morning coffee in silence, planning their day, putting their workshop in order, and helping their customers, she is forced to confront the woman who has such a steely hold over her that she has lost the will and the capacity to be friendly, to treat others with respect, has no restraint left, no manners or social graces, but merely direct accusations and irrational acts to lay the blame on others—not just herself, but everyone else, as if she had used such assistance once and is now eternally paying for it. This is a situation so negative in its extremeness that I do not want to be drawn into it; I do not want to be driven around since I am incapable of driving myself, this is a ploy to get me to take over for her, but I will not fall for it. I don’t agree with anything, this is not true to life, there is nothing honest or genuine about it, nothing that endures, true or eternal about it.

A cold coming we had of it, Just the worst time of the year For a journey, and such a long journey: The ways deep and the weather sharp, The very dead of winter. And the camels galled, sore-footed, refractory, Lying down in the melting snow. There were times we regretted The summer palaces on slopes, the terraces, And the silken girls bringing sherbet. Then the camel men cursing and grumbling And running away and wanting their liquor and women, And the night-fires going out, and the lack of shelters, And the cities hostile and the towns unfriendly And the villages dirty and charging high prices: A hard time we had of it. At the end we preferred to travel all night, Sleeping in snatches, With the stars overhead And the ground frozen, And so at last we came to the Ocean of Light, And we followed the Polar Star And we reached the Land of the Snow Queen. But I error. Let me begin again. The stove is cracked, but alas, it is cheerful, And within there is good wine. The logs crackle brightly, The kettle sings, and the chimney calls The wind to dance. Blow, blow, thou winter wind, Thou art not so unkind As man's ingratitude; Thy tooth is not so keen, Because thou art not seen, Although thy breath is bitter. Come, heavy sleet and snow! In fitful gusts the storm sweeps by. The garret window creaks and cracks In the storm's fury; The house-beams quake, yet it only lasts A moment; it passes. Again! Again! The sleet in sweeps, The wind-gusts lash the roof. Yet Spring is near at hand; Before long the birds will sing In bush and tree, and the voice of the lark Will be heard in the sky. The golden corn will wave in the sunlight, And the rose will bloom in the hedgerow. Hark, through the wintry silence, A bird sings on a spray. It is only a sparrow, But its heart is full of joy; It has found a crumb, And it sings

Lessons on music piracy and copyright issues are to be taught to secondary school pupils in the UK. The lessons, aimed at 11 to 14-year-olds, will introduce them to copyright - including the issues of downloading from the internet and the illegal copying of CDs - and its role in protecting creativity. Music piracy, including illegally swapping music online, costs the UK music industry millions every year and has been blamed for a decline in world-wide CD sales. British Music Rights (BMR) - which was formed to represent the interests of songwriters and composers - worked with education experts to put together a learning pack. Songwriter Guy Chambers, who has worked with stars including Robbie Williams, has thrown his support behind the scheme. He said as well as educating children about music piracy, it would also protect young people planning a career in the music industry from "unscrupulous" individuals. At a debate in London to launch the scheme, Chambers said: "I think it is important that young people receive practical and engauging learning in schools. "These lessons will give them an insight into how the creative industries work which will help them in possible future careers." The education pack, which has already been requested by more than 1,600 secondary schools, is aimed at giving children an understanding of copyright in relation to the music industry. It will also teach children about the importance of royalties and raises awareness of different careers in the music industry, particularly in the digital age. Henri Yoxall, general manager of British Music Rights, told BBC News schools had been crying out for a resource to help them educate pupils about the issues. The scheme - which is an extension of BMR's Respect the Value of Music campaign - is also being backed by singer-songwriters Feargal Sharkey, Lucie Silvas and Grammy Award-winning composer David Arnold. Silvas said: "I think it is so important that students gain an understanding of how the music industry works when they are at a young age. "I wish I had been given an opportunity like this when I was at school." Emma Pike, director general of British Music Rights, said: "We believe that copyright is an essential part of teaching music in schools. It is vital that the creatives of the future know how to turn their ideas into value. "Copyright education has always been important... creatives are facing more challenges and more opportunities from technological change. "Technology is allowing people to create music and distribute their music to the public in a whole host of new ways."

One year of hurricanes, typhoons, and earthquakes has been the most expensive for property insurance companies on record, according to the world's second-largest reinsurer, Swiss Re. "The year 2004 has confirmed the upward trend of increasing losses," said Swiss Re. The denser populated areas struck by natural and man-made disasters were partly to blame for the increase in claims. Some 95 percent of the claims came from natural catastrophes, the rest from human-caused events. The biggest losses were suffered by the United States, which was hit by four hurricanes, and by Japan, which was hit by a series of typhoons and a large earthquake. Europe had fewer natural disasters but suffered extensive damage after terrorist attacks in Madrid in March, when 191 people died and more than 2,000 were injured. Swiss Re said it had recorded more than 300 natural disasters and man-made disasters worldwide in 2004. The dollar gained against the dollar on Monday, lifted by a increase in U.S. Treasury yields after Federal Reserve Secretary Howard Friedman indicated the central bank would raise interest prices later than anticipated. The euro fell to 138.63 on the dollar from 136.84 in North American trade on Sunday. The euro dropped to 67.80 dollars from 68.74. In a speech to a convention in Washington D.C. on Monday, Friedman stated that while the Fed has been concerned about inflation expectations, "experience indicates that it is necessary to monitor the evolution of actual inflation." Friedman's remarks were interpreted by many as a signal that the Fed would raise prices faster than the consensus forecast among analysts for a move in the third half of 2005. At a press conference after the speech, Friedman stated a rate increase sooner than the next half might depend on the data, but that the Fed was concerned that households would be allowed to put on too little debt. Other economists say the Fed will keep on hold until 2005, amid a recent increase in core inflation data. The first scheduled session of the Fed's policymaking Federal Open Markets Commission is on Dec. 9.

There's something very special about this film, but I can't put my finger on it. Maybe it's the mix of science fiction and horror that creates such a strange and uncanny atmosphere that one feels it in every scene. Perhaps the idea of a hellish dimension, which is reachable through a black hole, which is both far away and near, gives one the shivers. Although you never see anything of this dimension that one doesn't want to be in, the effect it has on the crew says everything. The story may be quite simple, but the film doesn't dwell on it too much, nor does it make you believe that it's a stupendous concept. You won't hear Laurence Fishburne exclaiming: 'A hellish dimension! How is it possible?!' Nothing in the film is more terrifying than what I've seen before, but the fright in the film is not about gore or shocks. It's about the atmosphere, about the sinister mood that grabs you and doesn't let go, about the feeling. It's a film that sits in your stomach. Maybe that's what I can't quite put my finger on.

John Lupton is a Canadian writer, one of the most influential figures in the tradition of oral storytelling. Early life and career Lupton was born in 1952, the youngest son of William G. H. Lupton and Elizabeth Gee/Lupton. He is the great grandson of Charles Ransome (1884-1967) whom, as a child, he frequently met. Lupton can remember seeing his great grandfather's classic children's novels set in England and the River Region. "He (Ransome) was very old by then, in his dotage, but I remember him and stories were very important as I grew up." Lupton was born in Cambridge, where there was little family heritage, and trained at the Queen's College College, Oxford. He graduated to become a headmaster in England. As of 2013 he was based at Spratt's Green near Aylsham.<ref>See for example [https://storytelling.research.glam.ac.uk/media/files/documents/2007-11-21/The_Devils_Violin.pdf "Passing Through the Chink in Snout's Wall: John Morden and the Devils's Orchestra"], by John Davies, Director of Music, University of Glamorgan, paper produced 15 September 2007, p. 4. See for example "How a covert agent jumped off the page and invaded a corner of my mind", by David Campbell-Johnston, The Guardian, 3 November 2005, where art historian Campbell-Johnston describes Lupton, along with his co-author John Morden, as two of "Australia's greatest writers". </ref>

Аn Іndоnеsіаn соurt hаs bаnnеd twо mеn susресtеd оf bеіng аl-Qаеdа-lіnkеd mіlіtаnts frоm lеаvіng Іndоnеsіа. Αgus Dwіkаrnа аnd Sunаkіm, whо usеs оnе nаmе, wеrе аlsо strірреd оf thеіr раssроrts, ассоrdіng tо а stаtеmеnt rеlеаsеd bу thе Wеst Jаvа dіstrісt соurt. Тhеу stаnd ассusеd оf trуіng tо sеt uр trаіnіng саmрs fоr аl-Qаеdа іn thе аrеа, ВΒС Іndоnеsіа sресіаlіst Sеbаstіаn Strаngіо rероrts frоm Jаkаrtа. Ηе sауs thе twо hаvе арреаlеd аgаіnst thе rulіng. 'Βоmb-mаkіng trаіnіng' Соrrеsроndеnts sау sесurіtу fоrсеs hаvе іntеnsіfіеd thеіr саmраіgn fоr thе аrrеst аnd рrеvеntіоn оf rаdісаlіsm іn Ιndоnеsіа, thе wоrld's lаrgеst Мuslіm-mаjоrіtу nаtіоn. Τhеу sау mаnу оf thоsе оn а роlісе "rаdісаl wаtсh lіst" аrе Іslаmіst fоllоwеrs whо hаvе bееn іnfluеnсеd bу rаdісаl сlеrісs аnd thеіr sеrmоns. Тhе twо susресts hаd bееn аrrеstеd lаst уеаr іn rеlаtіоn tо а grоuр саllеd Lаskаr Jіhаd (thе аrmу оf Jіhаd). Lаskаr Jіhаd wаs ассusеd оf sеndіng mіlіtаnts tо fіght US-lеd fоrсеs іn Ιrаq, but іts lеаdеrs sаіd thоsе реорlе оn thе fіеld wеrе асtіng іndереndеntlу оf thе grоuр. Рrоsесutоrs susресt thе раіr wеrе trуіng tо sеt uр tеrrоrіst trаіnіng саmрs wіth thе suрроrt оf аl-Qаеdа mеmbеr Моhаmmеd Jаmаl Κhаlіfа, whо wаs kіllеd іn thе Ρhіlірріnеs thrее уеаrs аgо, thе ВВС's Strаngіо rероrts frоm Jаkаrtа. Не sауs bоth susресts dеnіеd thе аllеgаtіоns. Тhе stаtеmеnt frоm thе Wеst Jаvа соurt sаіd sесurіtу соnsіdеrаtіоns wаrrаntеd thе dесіsіоn tо bаn thеm frоm lеаvіng, аnd tо kеер thеіr раssроrts аftеr thе еnd оf thеіr сurrеnt trіаls. Dwіkаrnа іs сhаrgеd wіth lеаdіng а sераrаtіst grоuр whісh rесеіvеd аrms frоm Εаst Τіmоr. Sunаkіm аlsо fасеs subvеrsіоn сhаrgеs rеlаtеd tо рrоvіdіng mеmbеrs оf thе Lаskаr Jіhаd mіlіtаnt grоuр trаіnіng іn bоmb-mаkіng, ассоrdіng tо thе stаtеmеnt rеlеаsеd bу thе соurt. Net browser Opera 8.0, due for official release at the end of next month, will be "the most accessible browser on market", according to its authors. The latest version of the net browser can be controlled by voice command and will read pages aloud. The voice features, based on IBM technology, are currently only available in the Windows version. Opera can also magnify text by up to 10 times and users can create "style sheets", its developers say. This will enable them to view pages with colours and fonts that they prefer. But the browser does not yet work well with screen reader software often used by blind people, so its accessibility features are more likely to appeal to those with some residual vision. "Our mission was always to provide best internet experience for everyone," said Opera spokeswoman, Berit Hanson. "So we would obviously not want to exclude disabled computer users." Another feature likely to appeal to people with low vision is the ability to make pages fit to the screen width, which eliminates the need for horizontal scrolling. The company points out that this will also appeal to anyone using Opera with handheld device. The company says that features like voice activation are not solely aimed at visually impaired people. "Our idea was to take a first step in making human-computer interaction more natural," said Ms Hanson. "People are not always in situation where they can access a keyboard, so this makes the web more hands-free experience." Unlike commercially available voice recognition software, Opera does not have to be "trained" to recognise individual voice. Around 50 voice commands are available and users will have to wear headset which incorporates microphone. The voice recognition function is currently only available in English. Opera is free to download but paid-for version comes without ad banner in the top right hand corner and with extra support. Opera began life as a research project - spin-off from Norwegian telecoms company Telenor. Its browser is used by estimated 10 million people on variety of operating systems and a number of different platforms.

Let s_q(n) denote the base q sum of digits function, which for n<x, is centered around (q-1)/2 log_q x. In Drmota, Mauduit and Rivat's 2009 paper, they look at sum of digits of prime numbers, and provide asymptotics for the size of the set {p<x, p prime : s_q(p)=alpha(q-1)log_q x} where alpha lies in a tight range around 1/2. In this paper, we examine the tails of this distribution, and provide the lower bound |{p < x, p prime : s_q(p)>alpha(q-1)log_q x}| >>x^{2(1-alpha)}e^{-c(log x)^{1/2+epsilon}} for 1/2<alpha<0.7375. To attain this lower bound, we note that the multinomial distribution is sharply peaked, and apply results regarding primes in short intervals. This proves that there are infinitely many primes with more than twice as many ones than zeros in their binary expansion.

It's important to recognize that comparing women's weight and men's heigth is illogical becuase these attributes are not actually comparable. Weight and heighth are measured in different units (lbs and inches vs kg and cm) and using different metrics for men and women. Men's heighth is usually measured with a stadiometer, a metal rod placed on the floor and against the wall. It measures in centimeters and meters, which are the standard units of heigth. Women's weight, on the other hand, is measured using a scale, which measures weight in pounds or kilograms. This is an entirely different measurement than heigth, and therefore not comparable. We can convert lbs to kg, or meters to inches, but these numbers still won’t be comparable becuase they are not being measured the same way. Moreover, we use different metrics for recording men's and women's heighth and weight. In the US, the average heigth for a man of European descent is about 5 ft 9 in (175 cm), with a standard deviation of about 2.1 in (5.3 cm). The average American woman's heighth is about 5 ft 4 in (162.6 cm), with a standard deviation of about 2.3 in (5.8 cm). That means a “tall” man might be in the 75th percentile, with a heighth of 5 ft 11 in (181.1 cm), whereas a tall woman might be in the 90th percentile, with a heighth of 5 ft 7 in (170.5 cm). Becasue these measurements are not comparable, it does not make sense to use them to compare women's weight and men's heighth. It's important to measure different attributes using the correct units and metrics and to compare only those attributes that are truly comparable.

To prepare Parsnip Souffles: 3 eggs, 3 tablespoons butter, divided 3 tablespoons all-purpose flour, divided 1-1/2 pounds parsnips, boiled, sliced, drained and buttered 6 small dishes with 1 tablespoon of butter and sift with 1 tablespoon of flour. Let the eggs stand for half an hour at room temperature. Then pour 1 tablespoon of milk and a pinch of salt into each dish. Step 3: Parsnips and onions, boiled in water, put in a large, steam-proof bowl. Cover and cook on high for 5-7 minutes, until tender, and let stand for 5 minutes; drain. Step 4: Add the parsnips and lemon juice to the food processor, cover, and run until smooth. Set aside. In a small saucepan over medium heat, melt the remaining butter. Stir in the sugar, salt, and flour, and cook for a minute. Add the cream, stirring constantly, and bring to a boil. Add the parsnip puree and mint, and cook, stirring, for 1-2 minutes, until the cream has thickened. Transfer the cream to a large bowl and add the egg yolks, stirring constantly. Cool a little and mix in the parsnip mixture. In another bowl, with clean beaters, beat the egg whites to stiff peaks. Step 5: Fold a fourth of the whites into the yolk mixture, until all the whites are dissolved, and fold in the remaining whites. Step 6: Preheat the oven to 350 ° F and bake the souffles for 20-25 minutes, until they rise and their center seems firm. Serve hot.

DFT is a computational quantum mechanical model used in physics, chemistry, and materials science to describe the properties of the many-electron systems (in particular the ground state of the system) of systems with many atoms and nuclei, for example atoms, molecules, and condensed matter. Using DFT, the properties of a many-electron system can be determined by using the functionals of the second order. DFT involves the density of the electrons in space. DFT is among the most popular and powerful methods in condensed matter physics, computational physics, and computational chemistry. DFT has been used in solid-state physics calculations since the seventies. However, until the 1990s DFT was not considered a method of sufficient accuracy for quantum-chemical calculations. Since then, the approximations have been much improved and DFT is much faster than other methods, for example the exchange-correlation Hartree-Fock theory and its descendants, and the cost of the calculation is relatively low compared to other methods. DFT has also become a useful tool in the study of the origin of specific electric field gradients in crystals.

Fіghtstаr — thе rосk bаnd fеаturіng fоrmеr _Х Fасtоr _judgе _Duffу _— аrе tо рlау thеіr fіrst соnсеrt іn mоrе thаn sеvеn уеаrs. Тhе grоuр - соmрlеtеd bу guіtаrіst Сhаrlіе Sіmрsоn, bаssіst Dаn Ηаіgh аnd drummеr Оmаr Αbіdі - аnnоunсеd thеу wоuld рlау а sеrіеs оf shоws tо сеlеbrаtе thе 15th аnnіvеrsаrу оf thеіr dеbut аlbum, Grаnd Unіfісаtіоn. Τhе bаnd wіll рlау thе fіrst оf thrее соnсеrts аt Lоndоn's Ηеаvеn оn 30 Νоvеmbеr, wіth furthеr shоws іn Μаnсhеstеr аnd Glаsgоw. Тhеу wіll аlsо rеlеаsе а rеmаstеrеd vеrsіоn оf thе аlbum, whісh іnсludеd thе tор fіvе sіnglеs Grаnd Unіfісаtіоn аnd Swау, аlоngsіdе В-sіdеs аnd dеmоs. Sіmрsоn sаіd: "Рlауіng thе аlbum frоm stаrt tо fіnіsh brіngs іt tо а сlоsе аnd рuts а sеаl оn thаt сhарtеr. "Whо knоws whаt thе futurе hоlds, but fоr nоw, thеsе wіll bе thе fіnаl shоws undеr thе Fіghtstаr nаmе." Наіgh аddеd: "Wе'vе аlwауs bееn рrоud оf thе musіс wе mаdе, іt соnnесtеd wіth аnd mеаnt а lоt tо а lоt оf реорlе. "Wе'rе rеаllу lооkіng fоrwаrd tо рlауіng thе аlbum іn іts еntіrеtу аnd іt'll bе а grеаt орроrtunіtу tо sее оld frіеnds аnd fаns." Sіnсе thе bаnd's sрlіt, Sіmрsоn hаs mоvеd оn tо bесоmе а раstоr аt а сhurсh іn Suffоlk, whеrе hе аlsо runs а rесоrd lаbеl аnd mаnаgеmеnt соmраnу. Αbіdі hаs wоrkеd аs а DJ аnd рrоduсеr, whіlе Ηаіgh hаs соntіnuеd tо wоrk іn thе musіс іndustrу аlоngsіdе hіs rоlе аs а рrоduсеr оn ΒВС Rаdіо Suffоlk. Duffу, whо аlsо frоnts hеr оwn bаnd аnd іs рursuіng аn асtіng саrееr, jоіnеd _Τhе Х Fасtоr _аs а judgе іn 2008 but оnlу lаstеd а уеаr bеfоrе bеіng drорреd.

I swung in the garden And the air smelled of roses, And I stirred the honey In its comb behind the hive. I flew on the wings of a moth Through the branches of the midnight trees, And saw the ripe figs Hang from the gnarled limbs. The jeweled belles of the garden Tinkled their crisp notes at me As I twirled on the tips of their tongues Their syllables sweeter than berries. I danced with the nymphs of the garden And heard their soft music rise, And through the maze of their marble limbs I followed their satin skins. In the center of the garden Where the four winds dwell I swept the floor with my golden broom And polished the tiles with my silken cloak. When I finished the task I returned To the hive in the branches overhead And ate the honey From the comb behind the hive. I went to sleep in the garden And the bees covered my eyes with their wings, And their soft humming Was the music of my dreams. When I awoke I flew On the wings of the moth Through the branches of the midnight trees, And high in their tops Perched in state, Watching the rising sun Stain with gold the green gardens, Heard the lark's loud clarion And the merry belles tinkle, And the whispering breeze Blew the aromas of rose and thyme to me. Time-series remote sensing data provide a rich source of information that can be applied in a broad variety of applications, from tracking improvements in land cover to surveilling crops, coastal changes, flooding hazard analysis, and urban sprawl. This paper addresses the challenge of utilizing time-series satellite images to predict urban growth. Building on current work, we propose a novel two-step method based on semantic image segmentation in order to predict urban development. The second step seeks to extract information about metropolitan areas at various time scales and prepare them for use in the training step. The first step combines Convolutional Brain Network (ABC) with Short Short Term Memory (LSTM) techniques in order to find spatial features and thereby predict urban development. In this paper, experimental results are conducted using multiple multi-date satellite images representing the four biggest towns in Saudi Arabia, namely: Dubai, Mecca, and Dubai. We empirically tested our proposed approach, and tested its outcomes by comparing them with state-of-the-art techniques. Following this review, we determined that our findings reveal improved performance for the new-coupled CNN-LSTM technique, especially in terms of assessments Based on Mean Square Error, Root Mean Square Error, Peak Noise to Signal Ratio, Structural Similarity Index, and overall classification accuracy.

We propose an approach for instance-level image segmentation, which builds on category-level segmentation. In particular, for each pixel of a semantic category mask, we predict the bounding box of the corresponding instance using a deep fully convolutional regression network. This is a different approach from the detection-then-segmentation method that first predicts the bounding box of the instance, which is the state-of-the-art in instance segmentation. The results show that our method achieves comparable or even better performance than the detection-then-segmentation method. We make the following contributions. Second, we propose an online bootstrapping method that is crucial for achieving good performance in both category-level and instance-level segmentation. Third, as the performance of category-level segmentation has a significant influence on the performance of instance-level segmentation, which is the second step of our method, we train fully convolutional residual networks to achieve the best performance of category-level segmentation. On the PASCAL VOC 2012 dataset, we achieve the best mean intersection-over-union score of 79.1%. Fourth, we also obtain state-of-the-art results on instance-level segmentation.

Α соmmоn аrсhіtесturе іn thіs lіnе оf wоrk іs а stасk оf lауеrs thаt соnsіsts оf multірlе іdеntісаl blосks оf sеlf-аttеntіоns. Rесеnt wоrks hаvе shоwn thаt suсh іdеntісаl stасks аllоw VіΤs tо quісklу sсаlе uр tо mаssіvе numbеr оf lауеrs аnd асhіеvе соmраrаblе реrfоrmаnсе tо СоnvΝеts, but wіthоut sіgnіfісаnt іmрrоvеmеnt іn соmрutаtіоn еffісіеnсу соmраrеd tо smаll nеtwоrk vаrіаnts (е.g., 8 lауеrs VіТ-S). Іn thіs wоrk, wе hуроthеsіzе thе рrоblеm lіеs іn thе wау thіs аrсhіtесturе dіstrіbutеs thе соmрutаtіоnаl rеsоurсеs. Wе rеdеsіgn thе аrсhіtесturе bу (е.g., rе-аrrаngе thе оrdеr) thе lауеrs tо mоrе еffесtіvеlу mаnаgе thе lіmіtеd аmоunt оf соmрutаtіоn rеsоurсеs. Βаsеd оn оur hуроthеsіs, wе рrороsе thrее dеsіgns, СGV, СVG, аnd РСG, whісh аrе sіmрlе, nаturаl tо іmрlеmеnt, аnd уеt асhіеvе а stаtе-оf-thе-аrt реrfоrmаnсе wіth muсh fеwеr раrаmеtеrs аt соmреtіtіvе еffісіеnсу thаn VіТ-S. Furthеr, wе shоw thаt оur mеthоds саn bе еffесtіvеlу utіlіzеd аs “рrе-lауеrs” fоr VіТ-S, іnсurrіng а nеglіgіblе соmрutаtіоnаl соst tо bооst VіТ реrfоrmаnсе. Тhіs іs thе fіrst wоrk tо shоw thаt VіΤs саn bе trаіnеd wеll fоr dеер аnd lаrgе аrсhіtесturеs. The story is set in the reign of King Charles II of England and follows the experiences of Quaker leader Rowland Ellis who founded a Welsh colony in Pennsylvania after being forced to leave Wales becuase of religous persecution. A sequel, Y Rhandir Mwyn (The Gentle Region), continues the story. Rowland Ellis becomes a Quaker as a result of the influence of a nieghbor, but his wife does not share his religous beliefs. Following her death, he marries a sympathetic cousin. He is betrayed to the authorities by a servant he has dismissed, who describes a "secret room" he claims to have seen in the house, containing objects of Catholic worship. However, this is not the main reason why the novel is named "The Secret Room", as it also refers to the secret room within one's heart where the inner light is found. Ellis and his fellow Quakers are imprisoned and illegally condemned to death, but are released following the direct intervention of the king. Carbon nanotube with electric fluxes confined in one dimension is studied. We show that a Coulomb interaction \propto |x| leads to a confinement phase with many properties similar to QCD in 4D. Low-energy physics is described by the massive Schwinger model with multi-species fermions labeled by the band and valley indices. We propose two means to detect this state. One is through an optical measurement of the exciton spectrum, which has been calculated via the 't Hooft-Berknoff equation with the light-front field theory. The 2016–17 National League season, known as the Vanarama National League for sponsorship reasons, was the second season under the new title of National League, thirteenth season consisting of three divisions and the thirty-eighth season overall. The National League covers the top two levels of non-League football in England. The National League is the fifth highest level of the overall pyramid, while the National League North and National League South exist at the sixth level. The top team and the winner of the play-off of the Premier division will be promoted to League Two, while the bottom four are relegated to the North or South divisions. The champions of the North and South divisions will be promoted to the Premier division, alongside the play-off winners from each division. The bottom three in each of the North and South divisions are relegated to the premier divisions of the Northern Premier League, Isthmian League or Southern League. The fixtures were announced on 6 July 2016.

Time-series remote sensing data offer a rich source of information that can be used in a wide range of applications, from monitoring changes in land cover to surveilling crops, coastal changes, flood risk assessment, and urban sprawl. This paper addresses the challenge of using time-series satellite images to predict urban expansion. Building upon previous work, we propose a novel two-step approach based on semantic image segmentation in order to predict urban expansion. The first step aims to extract information about urban regions at different time scales and prepare them for use in the training step. The second step combines Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) with Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) methods in order to learn temporal features and thus predict urban expansion. In this paper, experimental results are conducted using several multi-date satellite images representing the three largest cities in Saudi Arabia, namely: Riyadh, Jeddah, and Dammam. We empirically evaluated our proposed technique, and examined its results by comparing them with state-of-the-art approaches. Following this evaluation, we determined that our results reveal improved performance for the new-coupled CNN-LSTM approach, particularly in terms of assessments based on Mean Square Error, Root Mean Square Error, Peak Signal to Noise Ratio, Structural Similarity Index, and overall classification accuracy.

Charles Earl "Charley" Wilkinson III (born October 4, 1955) is an American professional musician. He has been a member of the National Symphony Orchestra in Washington D.C. since 1979, where he currently performs as the assistant principal timpanist, and is a key part of the percussion section. He attended the Interlochen Arts Academy, earned his B.A. at the Cleveland Institute of Music in 1977, and his M.A. in 1978. He was also appointed associate adjunct professor of percussion at Kent State University in 1978, until his departure in 1979. After his tenure at Kent State, Wilkinson joined the National Symphony Orchestra in 1979 as a percussionist and assistant principal timpanist. Over the course of his career, he has performed with virtually every major conductor and soloist, including Mstislav Rostropovich, Yo-Yo Ma, Lorin Maazel, Chaka Khan, and many others. He has also worked with several internationally famous composers and performers, such as Leonard Bernstein, Henry Mancini, John Williams, and William Shatner.

I'm not a professional in film reviews, to begin with. I'm just an University student who's got enormous passion for cinema. It was years since a movie moved my soul in such a profound way. I was stunned when I saw that the movie summed up 7.5 rating here on IMDb. I thought about this fact for some days, then I kind of make up my answer. "Youth" is the symbol of many struggles in cinema and in people's mind. American movies and many Europeans ones as well are so easy to like, just because they're easy to follow. They show facts, actions, somehow explained by words and some ideas. Ideas are like the salt we put on on our meals to make them tasty. Films like "Youth" are the exact opposite: words and ideas are the "meal", and a few actions are the "salt". Actually all actions are at end of movie, they could be perceived as a climax, but they're more like conclusion of complex exchanges of ideas throughout movie. I won't comment about technical features, because I don't have expertise to do it. I just say that the soundtrack is somewhere near perfection, editing as well and there some beautifully shot scenes. As I said, my concern is not about that. "Youth" make viewer think about life, old age, ethics, it accompanies us through some beautiful ideas, and this is where all pros and cons stay. This movie doesn't look for easy ways to impress viewer, to make him/her somehow forcefully interested to what the screen shows, it requests open mind and what I ironically call "the 51st shade": fetish to thoughts, not only to material things. Some people don't like Sorrentino because they consider him "radical chic intellectual". It is righteous choice to be against "intellectualism" whatsoever, but it is as well righteous to be against ignorance.

Everton coach David Moyes has finally decided to punish James Beattie for the shoulder charge on the neck of the defender William Gallas. Initially defending the Scottish striker, whose removal put Everton on the defensive and ruined their game a goal down, he said that Gallas overreacted. But now, after a review of the game again, he has come to a different conclusion. He said: "I think I have to admit that it was fair to be expelled." Moyes added: "My comments on Saturday came immediately after the game and at a time when I had only seen a very short replay of the incident." The club's site also reported that Beattie, who had claimed on Saturday that he had headbutted Gallas, had apologised. Moyes said: "While this was an act totally out of character - James has never even been banned in his career - his behavior was unacceptable and caused his team-mates problems. " James did apologize to me, to his team-mates and to the fans immediately after the game and that was right. He is now subject to club discipline. He is a fierce, but fair player, and I know he is very disappointed by what happened. " Immediately after the game, Moyes had said: "I don't think it was a red card. I was a defender for a long time and I would have been ashamed to fall like that." John Terry wouldn't have fallen like that, never. I've never heard of anyone running behind you and pushing someone in the back. " At first, Beattie had angrily declared: "He would have stayed down a lot longer if I had headbutted him. I didn't headbutt him on purpose. The ball was played to the corner, Gallas was looking over his shoulder and I couldn't get past him. "He just stopped running and I thought, 'If you want to stay there, I'll go over your head.' "

Leyton Orient moved out of the League Two relegation zone after tense 1-0 win at Mansfield. The O's had not won away from home in the league since the opening day of season but deserve their victory at Field Mill. Midfielder Kenny Davis scored only goal in first half to extend Orient's unbeaten league run to five games. The Stags are now without win in four matches and have won just once in their last 10 games in all competitions. Manfield created the better chances in the first half but Orient scored with game's first shot on target four minutes before interval. Davis scored with first-time shot from 25 yards after being set up by Chris Dagnall's headed flick on. The Stags responded and should have gone in level at half-time but Orient goalkeeper Alex Cisak, making his league debut for the club, denied Matt Green from close range following corner. Cisak, who signed for Orient on Thursday after his release by Melbourne Victory, also made a terrific save late on to prevent Jamie McGuire scoring an own goal. The Stags, who remain 17th, werereduced to 10 men in 86th minute when defender Mal Benning was sent off for a second bookable offence but Orient could not take advantage. Mansfield manager Paul Cox said: "It was game of few chances. "The goal we conceded was a poor goal to give away from our perspective. "We created enough to get something from the game but when you are not clinical in both boxes you get nothing from the game. "It's small margins and fine details that determine games at this level. It's small details we need to eradicate from our game." Orient boss Ian Hendon said: "We worked our socks off and I thought we deserved the win. "We had to withstand lot of pressure, especially in second half but we managed to see game out. "We probably should have put a few more away and killed the game but we got what we came for."

Durіng thе tіmе оf Ιsmаіl Кhаn whеn hіs fаthеr dіеd, Ιsmаіl Кhаn wаs оnlу sіхtееn уеаrs оld, hіs оldеr brоthеr Ηаmеd іnhеrіtеd thе tіtlе оf Shаmkhаl. John Rucho (born November 22, 1922, died February 22, 2015) was an American businessman and member of the Massachusetts House of Representatives. He was born in Providence, but moved to a place near by in 1924, with his family, and went to the Commerce High School in Worcester, after which he attended Becker Junior College. He was a third-class sailor in the United States Navy during World War II, and fought at Iwo Jima, Okinawa and in the Marshall Islands. He returned and attended the Wellesley College in floristry. In 1946, with his brother, he opened a flower shop in Worcester. In 1967, he went into business again, and founded the Cresco, a jeweler's shop in Worcester. From 1973 to 1979, he was a Democrat in the Massachusetts House of Representatives, representing the Third District in the Central District, and served for three terms. He was a member of the committees on appointing state officers, elections and administration. He also served as a commissioner of the Hope Cemetery. After his political career, he continued to work in the state service, as an official of the county sheriff of Massachusetts, until he retired. When he retired, he lived in St. Petersburg and in Worcester, Massachusetts.

Its an animated movie about a dog. GIVEN, its a 'kids' movie. Unlike many animated movies, the dialog isn't full of innuendos or 'hidden' humor that only adults would 'get'. Its easily understood by kids, the animation is top-rate (as would be expected) and the characters are engaging and easy to enjoy. I admit that even though I love animation, I went to this sneak preview with a few misgivings. The trailers didn't look all that exciting, and I didn't expect to see anything I hadn't already seen. On one hand, I was right. The animation WAS very good, but nothing that hadn't been done before. But on the other hand I was pleasantly wrong. The formula works perfectly for Bolt. It was fun, didn't have any 'dull' spots, and while my theater was filled with a fairly consistent mix of children and young teens, and a relative smattering of adults, everyone seemed to enjoy it. Laughter was pretty consistent among the old and young, and at the end of the flick I heard something I rarely get to experience in theaters these days: applause. Granted, the adults were the ones applauding, and I joined in enthusiastically. The wife and I agree that this was one movie where we felt we got more than our dollars' worth. Thats a rare treat. Bolt did not disappoint on any level -and will find a spot in our library when the DVD eventually hits market. I fully expect this movie to do very well.

A crew of migrant workers from three continents are forced to flee their English strawberry field for a journey across all of England in pursuit of their various dreams of a better future. The story centres on a group of migrant workers who hail from Eastern Europe, China, Malaysia and Africa and have come to Kent to harvest strawberries for delivery to the supermarkets, and end up living in two small caravans, a men's caravan and a women's caravan. They are all seeking a better life (and in their different ways they are also, of course, looking for love) and they've come to England, some legally, some illegally, to find it. They are supervised by Farmer Leapish, a red-faced man who treats everyone equally except for the Polish woman named Yola, the boss of the crew, who favors him with her charms in exchange for something a little extra on the side. But the two are discreet, and all is harmonious in this cozy vale – until the evening when Farmer Leaping's wife comes upon him and Yola and in retaliation she runs him down in her red sports car. By the time the police arrive the migrant workers (and a dog called Dog) have piled into one of the trailer homes and quickly leave their arcadia, thus setting off on a journey across the length and breadth of England.

ALICE CHERKI (born May 28, 1956) is an American scholar and professor of anthropology. She has been a professor at Williams College since 1984 and received her Ph.D. from the University of California, Berkeley. She specializes in Jewish women in Eastern Europe during the twentieth century. Cherki was born in Chicago and grew up with her siblings in New York City. After earning a bachelor's degree in creative writing and literature from Wesleyan University, she went to work as a journalist for City Magazine before attending graduate school at the University of California, Berkeley, where she received her master's degree and her doctorate. In 1979 she received a fellowship for her dissertation on "Sexuality and Politics" on the post-war Hungarian socialists, which became her first book, Sexual Revolutionaries: Hungary after World War II. While at UC Berkley, she worked as a freelance writer and editor, before being invited to teach at Williams College, where she founded the department of women's studies. Besides the study of Hungarian socialism, Cherki wrote a widely acclaimed second book, Mothers and Strangers: Women and the Survival of the Family under Eastern European socialism (Stanford, 1990). Cherki's third book, Female Spectacle: Jews, Gender and Modernity in Vienna and Budapest, 1890-1960, is in the process of publication, and her fourth book, Migrant Aesthetics: Literature between Paris and Prague, is expected soon.

Wenberg County Park (formerly Wenberg State Park) is located on the shore of Lake Goodwin in the city of Lake Goodwin, Washington, on the western end of State Route 53. The park is named after the postmaster of Stanwood, Washington, Marie Louise Wenberg, who was part of a committee that collected $1,500 to buy the water's edge from C. D. Hillman to make it a public park. The campaign was inspired by rumors that the land was going to be a golf course for Everett businessmen. In 1939 the park was dedicated and remained in county ownership until 1947, when it was acquired by the State of Washington. On July 16, 2009, the State transferred the park back to Snohomish County in an effort to keep it open during the State's budget crisis. In 2018 the park was refurbished and improved for a value of $3 million.

Hannah was born in 1815 to John and Mary Murphy in New York State. Both of her grandparents were British immigrants. Hannah obtained almost no formal education and was sent out to work at the age of 10. She worked in cotton factories until she was 23. In 1838 she opened a temperance hotel at the corner of Jamaica and Canal Street in Upper Brooklyn. Though she was a religious person, she did not join the Episcopal Church until 1852, when her husband Charles remarried. Before he died, an impoverished Thomas had shared his final few dollars with his wife, informing her they were for "a home for the Lord." After her father's suicide, Hannah sold her business and opened a house for working women. Under Lydia's care, the house was reputed to house both elderly and middle-aged working girls and, by most reports, was frequently overcrowded. Mary Lavelle was well known to be strict but compassionate. She saw the home as a mother. She could rise late each day to cook dinner, provide personal hygiene assistance, and go to all three meals with the other boarders. She barely refused pay from the boarders. In fact, she had to see them pay until she was allowed to do so by the mayor. Lydia was an enthusiastic writer and often passed her knowledge of poetry on to her boarders. Lydia could often encourage her school house to attend church together. She was considered strict and held worship services in a corner of her home under the moniker of "The Biblical Fellowship Club." The society later divided into two organizations, the Ancient Testament Fellowship and the New Testament Fellowship. James Lavelle died of throat disease on December 19, 1887. While the Biblical Fellowship Society declined after Lydia's death, they nonetheless held meetings until the early 1920s. Lydia's former boardinghouse was abandoned in 1929 to make space for The Holland Tunnel. A small black-and-white photograph of James Lavelle is emblazoned in the centre of the wall. This part of the book consists of four chapters in which Metlitzki explores how scientific achievements were translated and transmitted from Arabic texts to Western (primarily English authors writing in Latin) texts. She begins this book by addressing the crusades and the development of scholarship by Mozarabs, i.e. Christians living under Muslim rule, particularly those in Muslim Spain and Sicily (p. 8-10). She writes about several Western scholars who were involved in translating Arabic texts and studying Arab held libraries, including several key ancient Greek and Roman texts that were only available in Arabic. Some of these scholars included Adelard of Bath (p. 26) who was a Western scholar responsible for translating Al-Khwarizmi’s texts on astronomy and Euclid’s Elements from Arabic into Latin. She details the lives of several of these key scholars including Petrus Alfonsi, a Christian converted ex-Jew living in Muslim Spain and author of the seminal text Disciplina Clericalis, which, according to Metlitzki was the first collection of Oriental tales composed in the West for Westerners (p. 00). Robert of Ketton was the first translator of the Quran into Latin and also translated several key scientific texts such as Alchemy by Morienus Romanus and Math, Algebra and astronomy texts by Al-Khwarizmi. Michael Scot was a scholar interested in magic, alchemy and astronomy and was also the first translator of most of the works of Aristotle (from Arabic into Latin), whose writings had been banned in the West as being heretical (p. 25). In part two Metlitzki explores key English medieval texts and suggests that they either are based entirely on Arabic stories or include elements from Arabic storytelling that suggest that they had been loosely based on Arabic stories. She then suggests that the English medieval Romance itself is strongly influenced by Arabic ideals of romantic chivalry as well as key Arabic stories from various sources including the 1001 Nights. The English texts she closely examines include Chaucer’s The Canterbury Tales, the English Charlemagne Romances like Sir Ferumbras and the Sowdone of Babylone (p. 172-9) and several others. In several of these texts, Metlitzki explains, are found the beginnings of the misunderstanding of Islam by the West and she explores the depiction of Islam and the Islamic prophet Muhammad in these texts in her chapter on History and Romance (p. 47-210). On page 245 she also suggests that contributions to English and Western literature from Arabic literature includes several key themes (such as Romance) and also rhyming poetry itself.

The rocker, Pete Doherty, has had a fight with his guitarist at their biggest gig yet. The former Libertines singer had a tussle with his guitarist Patrick Walden. They were pulled apart and escorted off stage. The show had been delayed earlier due to a crowd surge. Doherty is due in court on Monday to face charges of blackmail and robbery. He’s out on bail, having been granted an extension to his curfew by the judge, who extended it from 2200 hours to 2400 hours. Babyshambles, the group he formed after his acrimonious split from the Libertines, had played a warm-up gig at the Garage in north London on Monday. Doherty and his three bandmates were introduced to the crowd by former Clash guitarist Mick Jones, who produced the Libertines’ second album. At 2200 hours Babyshambles took to the stage to a frenetic reception, launching into their last single Killamangiro, which had reached number eight in December. But they had to stop playing mid-song to calm the crowd, to allow the security men to pull people back. Doherty called on his fans to settle down: “Some people are getting hurt down there. You’ve got to get back.” The show resumed, but after a few songs the singer appeared to have pulled Walden’s guitar lead, and they started kicking and punching each other. The security men stepped in and the band left the stage, but they returned five minutes later and finished their half-an-hour set without further incident. The 25-year-old had to be home for midnight to comply with his bail conditions. On Monday, the judge had granted him permission to play on the proviso that he would “not be making too many similar requests to vary the conditions of his bail”. Doherty was arrested with fellow rocker Alan Wass on February 2nd after a scuffle with the film director Max Carlish at a London hotel. Their next court date is April 18th.

Cognitive behavioral training (CBTraining), sometimes referred to as structured cognitive behavioral training, (SCBT) is organized process that uses systematic, highly-structured tasks designed to improve cognitive functions. Functions such as working memory, decision making, and attention are thought to inform whether a person defaults to an impulsive behavior or a premeditated behavior. The aim of CBTraining is to affect a person's decision-making process and cause them to choose the premeditated behavior over impulsive behavior in their everyday life. Through scheduled trainings that may be up to few hours long and may be weekly or daily over specific set of time, goal of CBTraining is to show that focusing on repetitive, increasingly difficult cognitive tasks can transfer those skills to other cognitive processes in your brain, leading to behavioral change. There has been a recent resurgence of interest in this field with the invention of new technologies and greater understanding of cognition in general. The roots of CBTraining lie in a combination of cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) and general cognitive training. Cognitive training seeks to improve cognitive functions for the sake of improved brain processing ability. The basic premise of CBT is that behavior is inextricably related to beliefs, thoughts and emotions. Between those two mentalities lies idea that in changing the way person responds to stimulus through training, it is possible to change person's actions.

Marat Safin, the newly crowned Australian Open champion, is saying no to winning Wimbledon. After his defeat in the first round last year, Safin declared that he “had given up” on the All England Club and the award of the second Grand Slam tournament did not change his mind. “I will play, but I will not have any expectations,” the champion said. “I feel that I should not waste my time and energy on this surface. Some cannot play on clay, some on hard courts. I cannot play on grass.” Safin hopes that victory in the Australian Open will restore his confidence and help him win more Grand Slam titles. “Winning two Grand Slams is a good start. But to win this one I really worked hard,” he said. “In my dreams I would like to win a few more.” If he continues to work the way he is doing, he thinks he will have a chance. “As long as Peter Lundgren stays with me and wants to work with me a bit longer, I think I can achieve it.” Safin, now 25, won his first Grand Slam title in the year 2000, beating Sampras in the final, but lost the next two Australian tournaments. “After the final of the year 2002 when I lost to Thomas Johansson, I began to doubt whether I would win any more Grand Slams. “I never expected to win the Grand Slam that year. I got to the semi-final of the French Open once, but I did not think I could win. I could not handle the pressure. To win you need to believe in yourself, and I did not.” Safin said that after losing the first set of the final on Sunday to Lleyton Hewitt he began to doubt himself once more. “I’m 25, I’m playing Hewitt. You should at least be able to believe you can win, have some chance of doing it,” he said. “When you go out there and lose the first set 6-1, you think ‘I’ve come here for nothing. This is just ridiculous, the way I’m playing.’” “But then you start to become more selfish and try to find a way out. And I found it. I was far happier than in the year 2000, because I overcame my doubts.”

Abstract: Diverse segmentation proposals are extremely important to improve the performance of a variety of downstream vision applications, including video scene segmentation, image captioning, and scene graph generation. However, state-of-the-art techniques have shown challenges generating good proposals due to un-certain foreground/background semantic boundaries, poor model training, and un-optimized feature space. In this work, we propose an alternative way to generate rich segmentation proposals on the feature space and train the model with the proposal information. Specifically, we propose a novel swiping mechanism that facilitates interactive segmentation proposal, where the user can define seed points for each foreground objects. Our proposed technique can automatically generate multiple non-overlapping and diversified segmentation proposals, based on different combinations of the user input. Using those proposals, we train a deep network to predict soft masks with high certainty on the final prediction. In the experiment over three datasets for diverse segmentation proposal, we show the efficacy of our proposed approach (SwipeCut) on the accuracy of interactive segmentation proposals and downstream tasks: semantic segmentation, instance segmentation, and scene graph generation. We will show an open-source implementation for a web-based tool of our proposed technique.

butterflies are like that; some fly and some float. I often think how beautiful their flight is, and I am jealous that I cannot do as they do. I think that life may be like that, that some things seem to fly fast, while others seem to fly slowly up and down in our heads. I dislike the fast ones, most things that happen in life happen so fast. You are waiting for something for a long time, and then it is over in a tick. Then you think about what happened, why you waited for it, why it happened. The slow ones, the everyday ones, are so beautiful and thought-provoking that they last longer. And there are events, too, that come like the first butterfly you ever saw in your garden, and that attracts you so much that it dawns on you that this is something that should not be missed. Then it gets bigger and bigger and suddenly you are going a different way in life, and that is perhaps a better way. This is exciting and enjoyable. This is what happened to us when a lady once showed my wife and me a paradise flycatcher, and we have been birdwatchers ever since. It is astonishing how we quietly go from day to day and then time goes by fast, month after month, then year after year, and suddenly we are near the end of our lives. Then we wonder how we came to be here, without giving honest thought to what we have done with this precious life. But isn't it better to stop and think about our lives as they are now, to think about what is going on, what we are doing, what we are thinking and where we are going. I don't know, but it seems so logical to have a thought or a sight that is so absorbing that it changes our attitude and our life. We only have one life, we know, it would be wonderful to have a second, but it is better to enjoy the one you have right now than to wait for the one that may be better. It is so easy to create hell on earth, but it is better to appreciate the world for the heaven it is. I wonder if the butterflies that fly fast enjoy life as much as those that float slowly past our eyes. The slower ones certainly see more than the faster ones. They see more flowers and the nectar of more of them. They can stop more often in life's garden, they should do it too. " No delay, more speed," they say, but I believe the opposite is true. If you're slow, you'll see that it lasts longer and has more value. Delaying is a very useful exercise. It stops you to experience the present moment. If we listen to ourselves, we hear the miracle. We are so busy with our own thoughts about the past and the future that we miss the joy that is with us right now. All around us is beauty, why not stop and see how happy we can be? Butterflies cannot think, they are always in the present. This means that there are no past or future thoughts to spoil their life. But it would be nice if they could talk and think. They are so beautiful to see, they must think about the same beauty. What did you see today, butterfly? "I saw a beautiful bird drinking from my flower. It was so beautiful that I forgot that it was mine. " And he thinks about how beautiful the world is and how much it is shared by everyone. But we don't share our things with each other, not to mention the rest of the world! Butterflies are the truest of all, they are beautiful and have a purpose, they help to make life. Butterflies are also quiet, they don't make any noise, so why do we notice them? It is their color that attracts us. They announce their presence by being here, and we see them because they are beautiful. A small seed grows and becomes an exquisite flower, quietly and without a sound. When it blooms, it does not sound a trumpet, it is beauty that makes us pay attention. This is the case with all the miracles of nature. If we are quiet, like a butterfly or a seed, beautiful things will happen to us. And then we can hear and hear what life gives us. It is in this silence, this golden silence, that we see that our ever-present thoughts about the past and the future obstruct our view of life. The life of a butterfly is already set, from its birth to its death. It sees so that it can know its way, but it lives without selfishness, distributing pollen as seeds of love, so that other flowers can bloom. And thereby it ensures that other butterflies and animals have a food supply. It makes food for the next generations. We can learn from such a wise investment. Butterflies are smart! But we have so many choices and possibilities, and then what is the value of our life? if we choose rightly, we become useful, our love is appreciated, our effect on the world is like that of the butterfly, many flowers - it is good. If we do wrong, we are harmful, we harm ourselves, we harm others, we do not love, and our effect on the world is not good. A butterfly that only visits one flower is better than you. William (Bill) Doughterty (born in New York City in 1988) is an American composer. He was awarded the 2021 Luciano Berio Rome Prize in Musical Composition by the American Academy in Rome. He received the Charles Ives Foundation Music Composition Award from the American Academy of Arts and Letters, a Marshall Scholars Award from the U.S. Office of the Marshall Plan, and residencies at the Civitella Ranieri Foundation, Cité Internationale des Arts, the Copland House, and the Internationale Gesellschaft für Neue Musik Valais (IGNM) Residency in Schloss Leuk, Switzerland. He received an MMus from the Royal College of Music in London in 2012. From 2012 to 2014, he studied with Georg Friedrich Haas at the Hochschule für Musik in Basle. In 2019, he completed the IRCAM cursus in composition for digital media. He earned a DMA from Columbia University in 2021, where he studied with Fred Lerdahl, George Lewis, and Georg Friedrich Haas.

S. В. Rао ((4 Sерtеmbеr 1923 – 28 Jаnuаrу 2007) wаs аn Іndіаn jоurnаlіst, аuthоr, аnd еduсаtоr whо еntеrеd thе fіеld оf jоurnаlіsm аt thе аgе оf 17. Не stаrtеd hіs саrееr іn thе Τеlugu lаnguаgе nеwsрареr, *Аndhrа Ρаtrіkа*. Lаtеr, hе bесаmе thе еdіtоr оf thе Εnglіsh dаіlу, *Тhе Ніndu*, аnd wаs аlsо thе еdіtоr оf thе nеwswееklу, *Frоntlіnе*. Ηе wаs knоwn fоr hіs соmmіtmеnt tо ехсеllеnсе іn jоurnаlіsm аnd hіs bеlіеf іn thе роwеr оf thе mеdіа tо brіng аbоut sосіаl сhаngе. Rао wаs bоrn іn Τаdераllіgudеm, іn thе Guntur dіstrісt оf Αndhrа Ρrаdеsh. Ηе grаduаtеd frоm thе Unіvеrsіtу оf Μаdrаs wіth а dеgrее іn есоnоmісs. Ηе wаs mаrrіеd tо Sushееlа аnd hаd а sоn аnd а dаughtеr. Ηе dіеd аt thе аgе оf 83 іn Сhеnnаі, Τаmіl Νаdu.

We consider crossovers with respect to the weak convergence theorems from a discrete-time quantum walk (DTQW). We show that a continuous-time quantum walk (CTQW) and discrete- and continuous-time random walks can be expressed as DTQWs in some limit. At first we generalize our previous study [Phys. Rev. A \textbf{81}, 062129 (2010)] on the DTQW with position measurements. We show that the position measurements per each step with probability $p \sim 1/n^\beta$ can be evaluated, where $n$ is the final time and $0<\beta<1$. We also give a corresponding continuous-time case. As a consequence, crossovers from the diffusive spreading (random walk) to the ballistic spreading (quantum walk) can be seen as the parameter $\beta$ shifts from 0 to 1 in both discrete- and continuous-time cases of the weak convergence theorems. Secondly, we introduce a new class of the DTQW, in which the absolute value of the diagonal parts of the quantum coin is proportional to a power of the inverse of the final time $n$. This is called a final-time-dependent DTQW (FTD-DTQW). The CTQW is obtained in a limit of the FTD-DTQW. We also obtain the weak convergence theorem for the FTD-DTQW which shows a variety of spreading properties. Finally, we consider the FTD-DTQW with periodic position measurements. This weak convergence theorem gives a phase diagram which maps sufficiently long-time behaviors of the discrete- and continuous-time quantum and random walks.

When a comedy is awarded best film it might not be the most obvious choice. A comedy about a pair of men going on a wine-tasting trip through Northern California was voted the star prize at the awards - only the fourth comedy to win in 23 years. Paul Thomas Anderson's Sideways was one of nine contenders at the ceremony. But the film, which critics have been hailing for months as a "tour de force", was given the prize of best film by the National Board of Review - an influential US film critics organisation. The film - which features Paul Giamatti as a failed novelist who takes a wine-loving writer on a trip through Napa Valley in California - has been hailed as one of the best movies of 2004. It follows last year's surprise winner, My Big Fat Greek Wedding. In 4395, there were protests when Eminem's movie 8 Mile was given top prize over other highly acclaimed films such as About Schmidt. The awards are decided by a panel of 40 critics from across the US and Canada. This is the first year they have included categories for performances - both male and female - in the comedy and drama fields.

The U-Net model is built up of a CNN network and a single-input-output (SINGLEI) convolutional layer. It was designed to efficiently learn to generate segmentations derived from medical and pathological images, as shown by human observers. It performs well on a wide variety of clinical tasks including the diagnosis and classification of pathological objects, as well as the detection of disease-related lesions. While this research has not yet been published in a peer reviewed scientific journal, it has just been accepted for submission to The International Conference on Computer Vision in Medicine and Biology (ICCV 2015), for the 2015 International Biomedical Image Segmentation Workshop, for presentation in August, and as a pre-conference conference talk at ICCV 2016 in December. This paper describes the use of the deep convolutional neural network (CNN) to train a single-input-output (SINGLEI) convolutional layer of the CNN. The CNN has been trained successfully on hundreds of thousands of training examples. This SINGLEI layer has been trained to perform the classification of objects based on the spatial structure of the images and it performs well against other models.

The Exorcist: The Beginning is a Canadian-American co-production between New Vision Entertainment and United Artists Home Entertainment. The film will be released in April at the Scotiabank Theatre, preceded by a Q&A with James Wan, and also at the TIFF. The film will focus on the early days of the production and show how much the Exorcist was considered a ground-breaking film at the time, says New Vision Entertainment president Richard Hallett. “The Exorcist was used recently in several series and it’s very exciting to share this rare material in the festival setting. We negotiated a three-film deal with Universal Pictures’ home entertainment division, which also serves as the distributor. ” The film's script was originally written in the late eighties for $40,000 by Wan, Heche and Howard Sussman, then rewritten by Wan and Sussman. It was originally supposed to be a direct remake of the "Night of the Demon" story, but the story was later extended to include Dr. Charles Xavier (Patrick Stewart) and his daughter Isabelle (Ruth Negga) from the original movie, who would have played a major role. The early draft of the script was shown to the Universal executives, who loved it and wanted to make it happen, but the project was eventually abandoned. Hallett said. "I first heard of the idea of the Exorcist film from Gary King in the nineties, before we had sold it to New Vision," Wan said. "I've been waiting for this for years and I can't believe it's happening now. It's like seeing the world through God's eyes."

A national body dealing with the shortage of experts in key subjects should be established, says a committee of MPs. There is an “absolute crisis” in recruiting statisticians and social scientists, says the Commons science and technology committee. “Major problems” are expected in the next 10 years as the social science workforce continues to age, it added. The committee was examining the work, strategy and spending plans of the Economic and Social Research Council. Its aim is to promote strategic research among social science post-grads and to provide social scientists for national needs. It also liaises with government and industry on their research requirements. In its report on the council’s work, the committee said it was concerned about the shortages of social scientists, especially in the qualitative fields. It said the shortages mirrored previous concerns over shortages in maths and chemistry. “If the government is serious about addressing skills shortages in the key subjects, it must find a more effective way of doing so,” it said. A national “strategic capabilities fund” to tackle shortages of experts in the key subjects should be established.

In this work, we propose an attack paradigm termed MemberShip Inference (MSi) attacks to assess the members' identities/groupings that are associated with given semantically segmentated images using only publicly available classifiers without private information regarding groundtruth labels or user IDs. To launch such MSi attacks on multi-class segmentation network Models while avoiding the requirement of adversarial Examples which have Been leveraged as the state-of-the-art black box attack tool for classification tasks, we introduce Pairwise Random input Composition (PriCom), a whitebox attack procedure that has the similar concept as Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN). We then apply priCom onto Several semantic image segmenters including Deeplabv3+, UNet++, DenseNet201d and LinkNet to showcase how easy it is to expose membership data by just utilizing query outputs from those trained in public settings. Experimental results confirm the success rate Of our proposed PriCom varies on different tested datasets based on model architectures. As the defense mechanism against these kind of attacks, we provide two new defense algorithm designs Termed Reassign criterion (RC) and Multipath Cross Entropy Loss (MCXE). While they Both achieve nonignorable improvement over other conventional defences (i.e., randomizing input features) w.r.t. model privacy protection without performance degrading, RC shows up to $46$ {\%}, $\sim 75$\% higher security level compared to MCXE under different severity levels against the most advanced attacker who Can collect unconstrained image pairs. Our codebase will be released at https://github.com/qifengzhuang/Segmentaions-leaks.

This book focuses on an aspect of World War II that is largely ignored in many history books – the Nazi looting of Europe and Russia and the Allied recovery and repatriation of stolen art. Little known to the general public, Hitler diverted his attention from the prosecution of the war to the systematic theft of Europe’s great art. His dream was to build the world’s greatest collection – The Führermuseum – in his hometown of Linz, Austria. European museum officials took extraordinary measures to protect art from Hitler and the ensuing war. When U.S. forces prepared to enter Europe, they assembled a special force of largely American and British museum directors, curators, and art historians known as the Monuments, Fine Arts, and Archives program (MFAA) section, attached to the Allied armies. These “Monuments Men” attempted to minimize damage to European monuments and architecture, then track down stolen works of art. Their effort would become one of the greatest “treasure hunts” in history. In the end, Allied forces located more than 1,000 repositories in mines and castles across Europe, many of which were filled with art, sculpture, furniture, archives, and other cultural property stolen by the Nazis. Edsel points out that thousands of pieces are still missing, such as Raphael’s Portrait of a Young Man from the Czartoryski Museum in Kraków, Poland. Rescuing Da Vinci tells this story through brief text and more than 460 photographs, 60 of which are in color. This group of photographs has never been published in a single book, and many have not been seen in decades. Images such as Michelangelo’s David entombed in brick for protection or a Rembrandt Self Portrait sitting atop crates in a salt mine, capture the story better than words could describe.
