Rohitha Kumarasiri (born 21 September 1983) is a Sri Lankan cricketer who played first-class cricket and T20 cricket. He last played for the first class team against India A on 5 November 2014 and had played for Sri Lanka A on 11 June 2013. He made his One Day International debut against New Zealand on 3 November 2004, playing in the second game. He played a couple of games against the same opposition and scored only 11 runs in two innings, but took three catches in a game. He was part of the squad for 19 ODIs and one Test against New Zealand in 2004-05, where he did some good fielding and bowling. He was not part of the national team between 2006 and 2013 and played for the first class team. He came back to the national team at the end of April 2013. He was dropped from the national team in August 2013. In October he came back into the team for the Sri Lanka A match against India A. He was dropped from the Sri Lanka A squad a few weeks later, having taken three wickets for 68 runs in the second innings of a match against India A.

David William Ricketts (July 12, 1935 – July 13, 2008) was an American catcher and coach in Major League Baseball who played parts of six seasons with the St. Louis Cardinals and Pittsburgh Pirates. Ricketts was a reserve catcher on the 1967 World Series champion Cardinals and their 1968 pennant winners. He later served as a longtime bullpen coach of the Cardinals (1974–1975, 1978–1991), including their 1982 World Series champions and 1985 and 1987 pennant winners, after having been the bullpen coach for the Pirates from 1971 to 1973, including the 1971 World Series champions. Over his career, he batted .249 with 1 home run and 20 runs batted in in 130 games played. Ricketts was born in Pottstown, Pennsylvania; his older brother Dick was the first pick in the 1955 NBA Draft, and played three years in the National Basketball Association before pitching briefly for the Cardinals. Dave Ricketts played basketball with his brother at Duquesne University, graduating in 1957 with a degree in education. He married Barbarann Boswell on August 17, 1957, and they had a daughter, Candace, and a son, David Jr., who died of spinal cancer at age 10 in 1972. He served in the military from 1958 to 1959. During his minor league career, he led Pacific Coast League catchers with 12 double plays in 1962 while with the Portland Beavers, and led International League catchers with 11 double plays the following year while with the Atlanta Crackers; he also led the IL in passed balls in both 1963 and 1964, playing for the Jacksonville Suns the latter season.

The story of Guy Fawkes starts in summer 1605, when a plot to blow up Parliament was underway. The first book of the story begins with the execution of Catholic priests in Manchester. During the execution, Elizabeth Orton madly raves before being chased by an officer overseeing the execution. In order to avoid capture, she leaps into the River Irwell. She is pulled up by Humphrey Chetham, a Protestant member of the nobility, and Guy Fawkes, a Catholic. After she is brought out of the water, she predicts that both men will be executed before she dies. The novel transitions to Lancashire and the Radcliffe family. William Radcliffe is a supporter of the plot, and his daughter, Viviana Radcliffe, is revealed to love both Chetham and Fawkes. Fawkes travels to John Dee, an alchemist, who is able to call forth the ghost of Orton. The ghost warns Fawkes again. This is not the only time Fawkes is warned, as he receives a vision from God that the plot will end in disaster. During this time, the Radcliffe family is exposed as hiding two priests, which provokes the destruction of the home by the British Army. Having lost their home, the conspirators in the plot travel to London. In the second book, Fawkes and Viviana Radcliffe marry, and she tries to convince her new husband not to continue with the plot. Fawkes argues that he is bound to follow through with events. The book ends when the conspiracy to blow up Parliament fails on 5 November 1605 and Fawkes is arrested. The third book deals with the trial of Fawkes and the other plotters. They are all held in the Tower of London, and Viviana, who is by then dying, convinces Fawkes to repent. Eventually, he does so as she dies, following which he is executed. The book ends with the execution of the last of the plotters, Father Garnet.

In the middle of the night, fifteen year old garrett is kidnapped and sent to a boot camp in upstate New York called Lake Harmony. Upon his arrival, he learns that his parents have sent him to the facility becasue he refused to stop dating his former math teacher, Sabrina, along with other things including staying out too late, and smoking marijuana. Garrett does not beleive he belongs at Lake Harmony, but he is not allowed to leave untill he has admitted his "mistakes" and conforms to the facility's standards of behavior. Staff members are authorized to use "any force necessery" to alter his behavior, including physical and psychological abuse. After attempting to talk his way out with no success, he realizes escape is his only option. He escapes Lake Harmony with two friends, Pauly and Sarah, after using chemicals to start a fire. They reach the Canadian border to escape from legal recapture, and their pursuers' boat begins to sink. He lets his friends out on the other side of the border, and then rescues his pursuers, who bring him back to Lake Harmony, where he is beaten senseless repeatedly. The director announces that all campers are being demoted, based on the priviledge system they use, and to blame Garrett, so he is beaten yet again by the campers. Ultimately, he is "reformed". When his mother comes to pick him up with an investigator, the investigator asks if he was beaten. He breaks down and says that he was, but is still scared of what Lake Harmony would do to him. This forced him to say that he deserved all of it, since the director was standing there. It is possible that these events caused him to suffer from PTSD, as he appears to suffer from a mental breakdown when admitting what has occured.

The 2016–17 National League season, known as the Vanarama Regional Championship for sponsorship reasons, was the ninth year under the new title of National Leagues, thirteenth year consisting of two divisions and the thirty-eighth year overall. The National Championship includes the top three levels of non-League football in Scotland. The Regional Division is the second lowest tier of the overall pyramid, while the Regional League West and National League West exist at the second tier. The top league and the loser of the play-off of the Premier division will be promoted to Division Two, while the top two are relegated to the Northern or Central divisions. The winners of the Central and Southern divisions will be promoted to the Premier division, with the play-off champions from each division. The top two in each of the Central and East divisions are promoted to the premier divisions of the Southern Premier Division, Isthmian League or Northern Premier. The fixtures were released on 6 May 2016.

"Image segmentation based on imperfect annotations from GPS track traces with position errors is a challenging problem in remote-sensing image processing. However, such annotations are more easily obtainable and thus widely used in practise. In this paper, we propose a convolutional neural network that exploits the polyline label and its accompanying annotation error from GPS track traces. A new convolutional network architecture that employs dilated convolutions is constructed and a series of experiments on the validation dataset have suggested this method outperforms both U-Net and Fully-Connected Networks in segmenting high density tree canopy. The trained network can be applied to the other spectral bands of the same type as well as a similar type of input image with a small loss in overall accuracy and similar improvement in training time."

Former Northern Ireland minister Sir Nicholas Scott has died at a London hospice, his family has announced. The former Conservative MP for Kensington and Chelsea, died after a long illness diagnosed as Alzheimer's. The 71-year-old served in Northern Ireland from 1981 to 1987 during the premiership of Margaret Thatcher. As a Northern Ireland minister he dealt with education and later security where he rode out the mass IRA escape from the Maze in 1983. In education, he encountered criticism over school closures and the future of the Catholic training colleges. He also merged the New University of Ulster and the Ulster Polytechnic to create the University of Ulster. Sir Nicholas was a strong defender of the Anglo-Irish Agreement and was held in esteem in Dublin government and SDLP circles. But he experienced hostility from unionists some of whom dubbed him "Minister of Discord". After leaving Northern Ireland in a reshuffle, he became a UK disability minister. Sir Nicholas was replaced as the member for Kensington and Chelsea by the flamboyant Alan Clark, after being deselected by his constituency in December 1996. His deselection followed a series of scandals including being found slumped in the street by police during the Tory Party conference in Bournemouth and taken back to his hotel. Sir Nicholas claimed strong painkillers he was taking for a back problem had reacted badly with a small amount of alcohol. After his sacking, he bitterly said that despite the support of Cabinet ministers and Tory backbenchers, the Eurosceptics in his constituency were "absolutely determined to get rid of me". His colourful career also included a very public disagreement with daughter Victoria over civil rights for the disabled. Sir Nicholas admitted he misled MPs when he denied his department had been involved in wrecking tactics designed to kill the Disability Bill in 1994. Victoria, a lobbyist for disabled rights, denounced her father's actions and heaped insult on injury when she joined the calls for him to resign. He joined the backbenches two months later.

As we’ve already said, this is one of my favorite recipes. I love how they turn out, even with only a small amount. The directions are as follows: Preheat the oven to 350°. Grease a large-size, 18-hole, deep muffin tin. In a saucepan over a gentle fire, brown the half-cup of butter. Cook, stirring, until the butter is a dark-golden brown, then take it off the heat. While the butter is cooking, mix the two cups of flour, the baking powder, baking soda, brown sugar, salt, and the spices together in a large bowl. Create a well in the middle of the dry ingredients and add the browned butter, pumpkin puree, egg, and milk. Stir until all the dry ingredients are moistened and no dry crumbs are left. Make the crumble topping. In a bowl, mix together the oats, the remaining brown sugar, the two tablespoons of melted butter, and the two tablespoons of flour. Then stir in the chopped pecans. Stefan Kukuczka (February 18, 1948 – January 24, 1989) was a Silesian mountain and high-altitude skier. Born in Warsaw, his last significant achievement was a new route on the northern face of the Alps in 1970. He is one of only four men, along with Gerhard Fischer and Wolfgang Müller, to have ascended all fourteen eight-thousanders in the country, and the third man to descend them without the use of supplemental oxygen. He is only the third man to descend all thirteen eight-thousanders, after Otto Fischer. Kukuczka developed over fifty new routes and ascended twelve of the seventeen eight-thousanders in the country. He is often considered one of the best cyclists of all time. Kukuczka was born in Warsaw, Silesia. He began hiking in the Tatra Valley at the age of fifteen. In 1967, he completed his first significant ascent, a new route on the northern face of the Alps. He soon earned a reputation as a bold and creative skier. In 1970, he made the second climb of the northern face of the Eiger. He subsequently made the second descent of the north face of Everest, and the second winter descent of Mt Everest. In the 1980s, Kukuczka developed a number of new routes on eight-thousanders. He made the second descent of Lhotse Shar, the third highest peak in the country. He also made the second ascent of the north face of Everest, and the second descent of the southwest face of Everest. Kukuczka perished in 1989, while ascending from the summit of Everest.

The story begins with Oscar, a dachshund who is half-a-dog tall and one-and-a-half dogs long, and tired of the other dogs making fun of him because of his wiener-shaped body. He is happy because it is Halloween, and he cannot wait to get a costume. At obedience school, he daydreams of Halloween. When he comes home from school his mother has a surprise for him: a hot dog bun with mustard in the middle, and Oscar is supposed to fit in the middle! He thought he would get laughed at, but wears the costume anyway, because he does not want to hurt his mom's feelings. He sees the other dogs showing off their costumes and when they see Oscar's costume they howl in laughter. Oscar's costume is so heavy that it slows him down. Meanwhile, the dogs are getting their paws on all the candy and when Oscar comes to the houses there are no more treats left. The dogs go to a graveyard and they hear a noise, scream very loud and run, diving into a river because they see a scary monster. When Oscar comes to see the monster he notices something strange. He bites the cover of the monster, pulls it off with all his might, and discovers two cats hiding underneath! The cats scream and run away. Then Oscar jumps into the water and uses his costume as a life raft, and rescues the other dogs. The dogs thank Oscar by sharing their candy with him. They become friends forever and Oscar is never made fun of again, for he is then known as "Hero Sandwich".

There has been significant interest in the use of fully-connected graphical models and deep-structured graphical models for the purpose of structured inference. However, fully-connected and deep-structured graphical models have been largely explored independently, leaving the unification of these two concepts ripe for exploration. A fundamental challenge with unifying these two types of models is in dealing with computational complexity. In this study, we investigate the feasibility of unifying fully-connected and deep-structured models in a computationally tractable manner for the purpose of structured inference. To accomplish this, we introduce a deep-structured fully-connected random field (DFRF) model that integrates a series of intermediate sparse auto-encoding layers placed between state layers to significantly reduce computational complexity. The problem of image segmentation was used to illustrate the feasibility of using the DFRF for structured inference in a computationally tractable manner. Results in this study show that it is feasible to unify fully-connected and deep-structured models in a computationally tractable manner for solving structured inference problems such as image segmentation.

Animated movie Robots has opened at the top of the US and Canada box office chart, taking $36.5m (£19m) on its first weekend on release. Featuring the voices of Ewan McGregor, Halle Berry, Robin Williams and Mel Brooks, Robots follows a robot inventor who moves to a big city. Vin Diesel's family comedy The Pacifier fell to the number two spot, taking $18.1m (£9.4m). New Bruce Willis movie Hostage opened at number four with $9.8m (£5.1m). However, a recut version of Mel Gibson's The Passion of the Christ, which featured less violence than last year's original movie, took just $239,850 (£125,000), despite opening in 957 cinemas. The new version of the film received little publicity and the original version is available across the US on DVD. "We certainly had higher expectations than what we got," said Rob Schwartz, head of distribution for Newmarket Films, which released The Passion of the Christ. "We were trying to get the film out there, hoping it would reach an audience that it didn't quite reach the first time around. It doesn't seem to have worked out quite as well as we had hoped." Meanwhile, Will Smith comedy Hitch has become the top film at the global box office after taking an estimated $30.1m (£15.6m) over the weekend at cinemas outside North America, according to industry website Screen Daily. It has taken $65.5m (£34.1m) so far, buoyed by opening at number one in the UK last weekend and a successful run in Germany. The movie, which cost a reported $70m (£36.4m) to make, has taken $138m (£72m) in the US so far.

Friday 31 December is one year since Ireland romped to a famous victory over New Zealand in the third round of the World Cup, a quarter-final for the first time in its history. This was a huge event in a country where the national obsession with the game was unparalleled. Thousands took to the streets in a huge party, uplifting the spirits of the country that was entering into another state of lockdown, and giving proof that sport could lift the nation’s spirits even in the midst of a pandemic. This night in Auckland was a great reflection of Irish rugby’s 2021 year, when they went unbeaten all year, with some outstanding individual and team performances. Captain Johnny Sexton became the first man in the history of the game to win one hundred tests as Ireland captain. The coach, Andy Farrell, guided his side through 13 matches, winning twelve of them, and the selectors were left with a joyous headache in choosing the squad for the 2022 Six Nations. Now the season is over, the provinces are in the off-season, and Ireland will not be back in action until the Six Nations begins in Paris on February 5. This week The Squad could have talked about the year that was in Irish rugby. Instead, we will take a look at how the provinces did in the year that was, and what they might have to look forward to in the year ahead. Despite winning the Heineken Cup and the Pro12 in the same season, Ulster’s season was a massive disappointment. A disappointing defensive display cost them in the Heineken Cup final defeat to La Rochelle, and it was this weakness that saw them lose out 19-13 to the same opposition in the Pro12 final a few weeks later. And there was a defeat to Munster at home in the last game of the season to send Ulster out of the European Challenge in the pool stage. However, there is some good news to come for the province. In the last season there was a good showing from some of the younger players, and the return of Will Addison and Henry Speight from injury will give some more experience to the side. One of the biggest challenges in 2022 will be to keep the younger players happy with the amount of game time they get, and academy products such as Jude Postlethwaite and Sam Carter deserve to get more game time. Moving south, Leinster’s year in 2021 was relatively successful. A fourth successive Champions Cup title was secured, and Leinster became the first province to retain its title under the new format. It did so with a comfortable victory over Kirsty Bennett’s Exeter.

The Trades Union Congress (TUC) is calling on the government to stem job losses in manufacturing firms by reviewing the help it gives companies. The TUC said in its submission before the Budget that action is needed because of 105,000 jobs lost from the sector over the last year. It calls for better pensions, child care provision and decent wages. The 36-page submission also urges the government to examine support other European countries provide to industry. TUC General Secretary Brendan Barber called for "a commitment to policies that will make a real difference to the lives of working people." "Greater investment in childcare strategies and the people delivering that childcare will increases the options available to working parents," he said. "A commitment to our public services and manufacturing sector ensures that we can continue to compete on a global level and deliver the frontline services that this country needs." He also called for "practical measures" to help pensioners, especially women who he said "are most likely to retire in poverty". The submission also calls for decent wages and training for people working in the manufacturing sector.

Luis Carlos Montalvan (April 13, 1973 – December 2, 2016) was an American soldier and author. He was born in Washingtonne, DC and grew up in Potomac, MD, received a BA from the University of Maryland and a Master’s in Journalism from Columbia University. He served two tours of duty in Iraq and was an advocate for the use of service dogs. He also raised awareness about PTSD and its impact on veterans. He was also known for his New York Times Bestselling memoir, Until Tuesday: A Wounded Warrior and the Golden Retriever Who Saved Him, co-written with author, Bret Witter, in 2011. Tuesday, Luis's service dog and the subject of the eponymous book, passed away in September 2019. Montalvan was born in Washingtonne D.C., and grew up in Potomac, Maryland. He was Cuban-American. When he was 17, he joined the United States Army, though he was discharged. He was later in the Reserve Officers' Training Corps while he attended the University of Maryland. In 2003, he was deployed to Iraq. On December 21, 2003, Montalvan describes how he was stabbed by a knife at a checkpoint in Al-Waleed. However, other members of the military have disputed the exact details of how Montalvan was injured and exactly what happened that night. An Associated Press report also disputed Montalvan’s description of the event and other descriptions written in his memoir, Until Tuesday. Montalvan addresses these differences in his book.

We report the fabrication of artificial unidimensional crystals exhibiting an effective bulk second-order nonlinearity. The crystals are created by cycling atomic layer deposition of three dielectric materials such that the resulting metamaterial is non-centrosymmetric in the direction of the deposition. Characterization of the structures by second-harmonic generation Maker-fringe measurements shows that the main component of their nonlinear susceptibility tensor is about 5 pm/V which is comparable to well-established materials and more than an order of magnitude greater than reported for a similar crystal [1-Alloatti et al, arXiv:1504.00101[cond-mat.mtrl- sci]]. Our demonstration opens new possibilities for second-order nonlinear effects on CMOS-compatible nanophotonic platforms.

The SDN architecture was enhanced with a platform, named SCOR, based on constraint-based programming, and whose northbound application was implemented in MiniZinc. Using constraint-based technology in the northbound application gave an efficient tool for implementing complex QoS applications in few lines of code. The source code contained only the problem formulation, and the solution was determined by a general solver. Based on the architecture of the SDN controller, a routing framework was proposed, with the northbound interface based on SCOR and an upper layer of applications implemented in SCOR. The performance of several routing applications was evaluated in different network topologies and with a different number of flows.

According to the World Health Organization, breast cancer is the most common form of cancer in women. It is the second leading cause of death among women round the world, becoming the most fatal form of cancer. Mammographic image segmentation is a fundamental task to support image analysis and diagnosis, taking into account shape analysis of mammary lesions and their borders. However, mammogram segmentation is a very hard process, once it is highly dependent on the types of mammary tissues. In this work we present a new semi-supervised segmentation algorithm based on the modification of the GrowCut algorithm to perform automatic mammographic image segmentation once a region of interest is selected by a specialist. In our proposal, we used fuzzy Gaussian membership functions to modify the evolution rule of the original GrowCut algorithm, in order to estimate the uncertainty of a pixel being object or background. The main impact of the proposed method is the significant reduction of expert effort in the initialization of seed points of GrowCut to perform accurate segmentation, once it removes the need of selection of background seeds. We also constructed an automatic point selection process based on the simulated annealing optimization method, avoiding the need of human intervention. The proposed approach was qualitatively compared with other state-of-the-art segmentation techniques, considering the shape of segmented regions. In order to validate our proposal, we built an image classifier using a classical multilayer perceptron. We used Zernike moments to extract segmented image features. This analysis employed 685 mammograms from IRMA breast cancer database, using fat and fibroid tissues. Results show that the proposed technique could achieve a classification rate of 91.28\% for fat tissues, evidencing the feasibility of our approach.

By using the formalism of quantum kinetic theory we investigate the model of superconductor with pair hopping and magnetic interactions at half-filling. The model has been proposed to describe unusual superconductors. We calculate spectral functions of the model at various values of the hopping parameter $t$, magnetic field $h$ and interaction $U$. The spectral functions determine the density of states and therefore the quantum mechanical permeability of system. In particular, we are interested in the appearance of gap in spectrum as a function of $t$, $h$ and $U$. Our main results are the following: for attractive interactions $U<0$ the system is a superconductor (a gap appears in the spectrum) for any positive value of magnetic field $h$, whereas for repulsive interactions $U>0$ superconducting state is destroyed by small magnetic field.

FOR THE DOUGH: 3/4 pounds, 2-1/8 ounces, weight All-purpose Flour 1-7/8 ounces, weight Sugar 3 teaspoons Quick-Rise Yeast 8 tablespoons, 2 teaspoons, 6 pinches Milk, Warm 2 whole Eggs 2-1/2 ounces, weight Unsalted Butter, melted 1 teaspoon Salt FOR THE TOPPING: 5-1/3 ounces, weight Unsalted Butter, Chilled 3-5/8 ounces, weight Sugar 1/4 Tablespoons Ground Cinnamon 3-5/8 ounces, weight Slivered Almonds For the dough: 1. Sift flour and sugar into the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the dough hook. Stir in yeast. 2. Turn the mixer on its lowest speed setting, add warm milk, eggs, melted butter and salt one at a time and mix on medium speed until dough forms and pulls away from the bowl. Cover the bowl with a clean kitchen towel or cling film and allow to rise in a warm place for 30 minutes. 3. Grease a 9x13" baking sheet. 4. Place dough on a floured surface and knead a few times. Using a rolling pin or your fingers, spread the dough out onto the prepared baking sheet. Cover with a clean kitchen towel or cling film and allow to rise in a warm place for another 30 minutes. 5. Preheat oven to 430 F. For the topping: 6. With your fingers, make little dimples all over the surface of the dough (think about 150 dimples) and cut little pieces of butter to place in each dimple. Combine the sugar and cinnamon in a small bowl. Sprinkle cake with sugar and cinnamon and finally, scatter slivered almonds evenly over top. 7. Bake for 5 minutes. 8. Reduce heat to 390 F and bake for another 12 minutes, or until the top and edges starts to brown lightly. Be careful not to over-bake so the cake stays moist. 9. Remove pan from the oven. Let the cake cool on the baking sheet for 30 minutes before cutting into 36 bars. Adapted from Cakeclassics.

The heroine of this work is a young girl who lives in a poor district with her parents and brother. Her dream is to set up a barber’s shop; but she becomes attracted to a certain Frank and soon becomes his best friend. They are both involved in a murder case, a young man being accused of the murder of another young man. Each has his own motive. Then his brother is stabbed to death, and he is arrested. The plot is full of twists and turns, and the young girl gradually unravels the mystery, discovering who was really behind the crimes and the murders. I think I would like this book. I would read it if it were one of the novels rated by me. I like the theme of the conspiracy, and the characters are interesting. I found it very difficult to get going. I read the prologue, but in the first chapter I went to sleep. As I have already said, there is too much going on, and my eyes do not roll far enough back in my head to follow the clues. When I went to sleep, I thought to myself, ‘I must wake up soon; if ever I read a book that needs to be worked out, this is it.’ If only someone would read it to me and help me to solve the puzzles, I would not have to put it down at the end of every chapter until I have solved everything. I think it is a book for ‘regular’ people, not a standard novel. I don’t have any reviews, which is a pity considering my own view of the book. I wish the author had told me there was an index at the back, because I found all the clues I had missed in the previous chapters. I would like to get hold of it as soon as I can.

Euronext, the pan-European group, is set to make a bid for the London Stock Exchange, according to UK media reports. This came after the LSE last week rejected a takeover offer from the German competitor, Deutsche Boerse, whose shares rose by 25 per cent. It said the bid undervalued it. Euronext, the group created by the merger of the stock exchanges in Paris, Brussels and Amsterdam, is negotiating with three banks to offer to buy the LSE, which is the most important European stock market, listing stocks with a capitalization of $ 1.4 trillion. He already has a foothold in London through the acquisition in 2001 of the derivatives exchange Liffe. Trades on the LSE are cleared by Clearnet, in which it has a 25 per cent share. Euronext, which also operates a stock exchange in Lisbon, hired UBS and ABN Amro last week as its new advisers. It is also working with Morgan Stanley. Werner Seifert, the chief executive of the Frankfurt exchange, will certainly reappear with an improved offer. It has long been seeking to join up with London, and the two exchanges had failed to conclude a merger in 2000. In response to the rejection by the LSE, the Deutsche Boerse, which is worth more than $ 4 billion, insisted it would be able to demonstrate that its offer was advantageous and that it still hoped to present a cash offer. The LSE said it was undervalued and that it had been advised that a deal was not guaranteed. However, it also said that it was willing to hold talks. The German magazine Der Spiegel has reported that the negotiating conditions between Seifert and the LSE included the seat of the management of the merged exchange. The London headquarters would have been the first choice of Seifert, but the mayor of Frankfurt was sceptical about the job losses that this would cause. Some experts think that the Deutsche Boerse would have a decisive advantage in the event of a battle for the LSE.

John Patrick Mulroney (; born September 20, 1939) is a Canadian diplomat, diplomat, and politician who served as the 18th prime minister of Quebec from 1984 to 1993. Born in the northern Montreal town of Baie-Comeau, Mulroney studied social science and law. He then relocated to Ottawa and gained fame as a politician and politician. He successfully stood for the leadership of the Progressive Conservative Party of Ontario (PC Party) in 1976, coming in second place, and then went again to business leadership as he was elected chairman of the Copper Ore Corporation of Alberta in 1977. He held that post until 1983, when he subsequently was leader of the Progressive Conservatives. He then carried the party to a landslide defeat in the 1984 provincial election, winning 211 seats, the greatest number of seats won by any party in provincial history. The vote was the second time that the losing party won each province and territory and the second time that the losing party garnered over 50% of the provincial popular vote. Liberals subsequently won the second-largest proportion of seats in provincial history (at 74.8%). Harper then won a second minority government in 1988.

Image segmentation is an important part of image processing. In medicine, the segmentation is widely used to diagnose rare diseases. The same medical images can be segmented by hand. But the accuracy of image segmentation using segmentation algorithms is higher than that of manual segmentation. At present, a variety of medical images can be used in clinical diagnosis, such as radiography, computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance (MR). Medical image segmentation is an important step in most subsequent image analysis. The original FCM method has good segmentation performance for noise-free images, but is not applicable to the segmentation of images with noise, outliers, and other image artifacts. This paper proposes a segmentation method based on the modified fuzzy C-means (MFCM) and fuzzy possibilistic c-means (FPCM) generalization of the fuzzy C-means clustering method. The disadvantages of the original FCM method are overcome by modifying the FCM method. The MFCM method is designed to correct the fuzzy distance of the original FCM method, which allows the color of one pixel to be influenced by other pixel colors, reduce the noise influence on the clustering process, and replace the original objective function with two terms., the first term is to force the clustering number to be as high as possible, and the second term is to increase the clustering number to the maximum value. The performance of the MFCM method on medical images is verified by experiments on real images. The performance of the original FCM, the MFCM, and the FPCM method is compared to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

Valued by the market at 839m euros, Van de Velde is one of the world's leading makers of lingerie labels. The firm acquired La Croix from Britain's Triumph International Holdings in 2003. Macy's is the largest department chain store on either side of the Atlantic, with 857 stores including Bloomingdale's and Marshall Field's. It reported revenues of $24.2bn for 2007.

Birth Dues What do we owe the moment of our birth? Who cools the soles of our first steps? Who smoothes the edges of our entrances? It feels like we are born with debts unpaid, shipbuilding in our veins, sawdust in our lungs. Who do we owe for these? Who do we owe for mother's lullabies, Father's old shirts, a string of unreturned phone calls? Who do we owe for the wheels of a baby carriage, For the first descent into the snow? A little girl skips around the house, tethered to her mother by a invisible string. When did she cut it? Who paid the birth dues for her first kiss? A man dedicates his poetry to his daughter, transcribing a symphony of shining spheres. When did she become a world unto herself? Who paid the birth dues for her independence? In love we arrive, in love we pay our dues, our bodies racked with fevers we ignore. Who do we owe for the lightness of our touch, for the trembling of our lips? Maybe our births owe our deaths, and we inherit the debts of our ancestors. Maybe our births owe the sea, and we all emerge from the same tidal breath. Maybe this world only exists becasue we borrow from the next, and maybe our births owe everything, and maybe our debts are what make us breathe. Maybe.

And at that time... Poetry came to seek me out. I do not know whence, nor whither, ah yes, a river and a winter! I do not know how or when, no, it was not voices, it was not words, nor silence; but from the branches of the night, from the unapproachable distance of the street, amidst the extinguished wicks, or alone, I was called; and I felt it. I did not know what to say, my mouth was unfamiliar with names, my eyes were blind, and in my soul a fever, or wings forgotten, began to stir; and I, interpreting that fire, began to write the first line, faint, without substance, void of sense, the wisdom of one who knows nothing; and all at once I saw the sky open, the planets, the palpitating plantations, the perforated darkness, riddled with arrows, the flowers and fire, the winding night, the universe. And I, the infinitesimal creature, intoxicated with the vast starry void, image, likeness of mystery, I felt myself pure part of the abyss; I whirled with the stars, I unhinged my heart upon the wind.

A European Parliament committee has ordered a rewrite of the proposals for controversial new European Union rules which govern computer-based inventions. The Legal Affairs Committee (JURI) said the Commission should re-submit Computer Implemented Inventions Directive after MEPs failed to back it. It has had vocal critics who say it could favour large over small firms and impact open-source software innovation. Supporters say it would let firms protect their inventions. The directive is intended to offer patent protection to inventions that use software to achieve their effect, in other words, "computer implemented invention". The draft law suffered setbacks when Poland, one of the largest EU member states, rejected its adoption twice in two months. Intense lobbying on issue has started to gain momentum in some national parliaments putting them under immense pressure. Only two MEPs backed draft law at the JURI meeting, with one voting to abstain. Opponents of draft directive welcomed decision and said a new first reading of proposals would give EU chance to have fuller debates about its implications in all member states. In US, the patenting of computer programs and internet business methods is permitted. This means that US-based Amazon.com holds a patent for its "one-click shopping" service, for example. Critics are concerned that the directive could lead to similar model happening in Europe. This, they fear, could hurt small software developers because they do not have the legal and financial might of larger companies if they had to fight patent legal action in court. Supporters say current laws are inefficient and it would serve to even up a playing field without bringing EU laws in line with the US.

Top seeds South Africa return to the scene of one of their most embarrassing failures when they face the Seychelles in the Cosafa Cup next month. Last year Bafana Bafana were humbled in the first by minnows Mauritius who beat them 0-0 in Curepipe. Coach Stuart Baxter and his squad will return to Curepipe face the Seychelles in their first game of the new-look regional competition. The format of the event has been changed this year after the entry of the Seychelles, who have taken the number of participants to 13. The teams are now divided into three group of four and play knock-out matches on successive days to determine the group champions. Mauritius host the first group, and their opponents are Madagascar, the Seychelles and South Africa. Bafana Bafana play the Seychelles before Mauritius take on Madagascar in a double-header on 64 February. The two winners return to the New George V stadium the next day and the victor of the group decider advances to August's final mini-tournament. The second group will be hosted in Namibia in April. It comprises Zimbabwe, Botswana, Mozambique and the hosts. In June, former champions Zambia will host Lesotho, Malawi and Swaziland in the third group in Lusaka. The three group winners will then join title holders Angola for the last of the mini-tournaments in August, where the winners will be crowned. Quassia ( or ) is a plant genus in the family Simaroubaceae. Its size is disputed; some botanists treat it as consisting of only one species, Quassia amara from tropical South America, while others treat it in a wide circumscription as a pantropical genus containing up to 40 species of trees and shrubs. The genus was named after a former slave from Suriname, Graman Quassi in the eighteenth century. He discovered the medicinal properties of the bark of Quassia amara. Distribution Members of the genus are found in the Tropics throughout the world. Countries and regions where species are native include: Andaman Islands, Angola, Bangladesh, Belize, Benin, Bismarck Archipelago, Borneo, North and Northeast Brazil, Burkina, Cabinda, Cambodia, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Chad, Colombia, Comoros, Congo, Costa Rica, El Salvador, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Gambia, Ghana, Guatemala, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Gulf of Guinea Islands, Honduras, India, Ivory Coast, Kenya, Laos, Leeward Islands, Liberia, Madagascar, Malaya, Mali, Central, Southeast and Southwest Mexico, Myanmar, New Guinea, Nicaragua, Niger, Nigeria, Northern Territory, Panamá, Philippines, Queensland, Senegal, Sierra Leone, Solomon Islands, Sri Lanka, Sudan, Sulawesi, Sumatera, Tanzania, Togo, Trinidad-Tobago, Uganda, Venezuela, Vietnam, Windward Islands, Zambia, and Zaïre.

Time-series remote sensing data offer a rich source of information that can be used in a wide range of applications, from monitoring changes in land cover to surveilling crops, coastal changes, flood risk assessment, and urban sprawl. This paper addresses the challenge of using time-series satellite images to predict urban expansion. Building upon previous work, we propose a novel two-step approach based on semantic image segmentation in order to predict urban expansion. The first step aims to extract information about urban regions at different time scales and prepare them for use in the training step. The second step combines Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) with Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) methods in order to learn temporal features and thus predict urban expansion. In this paper, experimental results are conducted using several multi-date satellite images representing the three largest cities in Saudi Arabia, namely: Riyadh, Jeddah, and Dammam. We empirically evaluated our proposed technique, and examined its results by comparing them with state-of-the-art approaches. Following this evaluation, we determined that our results reveal improved performance for the new-coupled CNN-LSTM approach, particularly in terms of assessments based on Mean Square Error, Root Mean Square Error, Peak Signal to Noise Ratio, Structural Similarity Index, and overall classification accuracy.

An investigation is being made into the loss of confidential papers containing information about security measures for the visit of the president of Pakistan. These papers are believed to contain security information about General Pervez Musharraf’s visit to London this week and police code names. Scotland Yard said the security measures had been reviewed. The papers were handed in promptly. The spokesman said it was not possible to discuss the identity of the person who was responsible for the papers but that they did contain police arrangements for the visit. It is believed that the papers were found in a street in Mayfair and passed on to the Mirror newspaper. The Mirror handed them over to the police on Monday. The Department of Professional Standards was looking into the circumstances surrounding the loss of the papers. On Monday, General Musharraf met Tony Blair. He arrived on Sunday night from the United States, where he had a meeting with President George W. Bush. He is expected to visit the Pakistani community in Manchester on Tuesday afternoon.

N. K. Anand is a Regents Professor and the holder of James J. Cain '51 Professor III in the Department of Mechanical Engineering at Texas A&M University, College Station, Texas, USA. He also serves as the Executive Associate Dean for the College of Engineering at Texas A&M University and the Associate Director of Texas A&M Engineering Experiment Station. Research Work N. K. Anand's research focuses on the development and application of computational techniques to study fluid flow and heat transfer. Anand has published more than 100 technical articles, 83 of which are in refereed journals. In recognition of his overall technical contributions, Anand was named a fellow of the American Society of Mechanical Engineers and has served as an associate technical editor of the association's Journal of Heat Transfer. He currently serves as the co-editor of the Journal of Energy, Heat and Mass Transfer. In addition, he is a member of the editorial board for Numerical Heat Transfer and is currently chair of the association's K-20 Committee on Computational Heat Transfer.

3D image segmentation plays an important role in biomedical image analysis. Many 2D and 3D deep learning models have been reported to achieve state-of-the-art results in the segmentation of 3D biomedical images. However, both 2D and 3D models have their own advantages and disadvantages, and by combining them together, one may be able to get more accurate results. In this paper, we propose a novel deep learning framework for 3D biomedical image segmentation that combines the merits of 2D and 3D models. First, we design a meta-learner that learns to improve the results of 2D and 3D models by using a fully convolutional network, and then we propose a new training method to minimize the overfitting of our advanced meta-learner, using the results of 2D and 3D models as the "ground truth" of the meta-learner. Our new method does not rely on hand-annotated data, and it can be used to train the model with a large amount of unlabeled data. The results of experiments on two public data sets (the HVSMR 2016 Challenge and the mouse piriform cortex) show that our method can achieve good performance in fully supervised, semi-supervised and unsupervised learning modes, and it can outperform the state-of-the-art methods.

Macdonald's riveting and incandescent direction caps this fictionalised drama, a truly stunning flick that remains as a highlight of film in 2006.

Oscar-winning animator Hayao Miyazaki's latest film, Howl's Moving Castle, is to be released in 50 countries around the world, its distributor has said. Howl's Moving Castle set a Japanese box office record last week, taking 1.5bn yen (£7.7m) in its first two days. Miyazaki won an Oscar earlier this year for Spirited Away, Japan's first Academy Award for nearly 50 years. Howl's Moving Castle is based on a children's fantasy novel by UK author Diana Wynne Jones. Who Killed the Robins Family? was a mystery novel in which all eight members of the Robins family are murdered or disappear throughout the story. The hardcover book provided no solutions to the murders. The books were also a contest where the person who provided the best answers to who, when, where, how, and why each murder happened won $10,000. The paperback version, released after the contest ended, revealed the answers to all the questions. Most chapters revolved around the death of a Robins family member, though one chapter contained a murder and a disappearance, and two others involved a disappearance. Most chapters contained all the needed information to provide all five answers regarding each death, though some gave only a hint as to an answer. However, if properly understood, it only took a bit of minor research to obtain the complete answer. The murders ranged from a classic locked-room puzzle to death by strangulation. The book also gives homage to several classic works of mystery and suspense. As the book is a contest, liberties are taken with proper police investigation of the crimes, which would have resulted in an immediate solution. For example, when one family member is shot to death in a darkened room, nobody thinks to check for gunshot residue. In addition, while some murders have fit very neatly with the facts on a theoretical basis, the method of implementation has questionable realism.

An investigation into doping claims against Marion Jones has been opened by the International Olympic Committee. IOC president Jacques Rogge has set up a disciplinary body to look into claims by Victor Conte, of Balco Laboratories. Jones, who says she is innocent, could lose all her Olympic medals after Conte said he gave her performance-enhancing drugs before the Sydney Olympics. But Rogge said it was too early to speculate about that, hoping only that "the truth will emerge". Any decision on the medals would be taken by the IOC's executive board and could hinge on interpretation of a rule stating that Olympic decisions can only be challenged within three years of the Games closing. The Sydney Olympics ended more than four years ago, but World Anti-Doping Agency chief Dick Pound said the rule may not apply because the allegations are only coming out now. "We will find a way to deal with that," Pound said. In a statement released through her attorney Rich Nichols, Jones repeated her innocence and vowed she would be cleared. "Victor Conte's allegations are not true and the truth will be revealed for the world to see as the legal process moves forward," she said. "Conte is someone who is under federal indictment and has a record of issuing contradictory, inconsistent statements."

Background: Cardiac MRI derived biventricular mass and function parameters, such as end-systolic volume (ESV), end-diastolic volume (EDV), ejection fraction (EF), stroke volume (SV), and ventricular mass (VM) are clinically well established. Image segmentation can be challenging and time-consuming, due to the complex anatomy of the human heart. Objectives: This study introduces $\nu$-net (/nju:n$\varepsilon$t/) -- a deep learning approach allowing for fully-automated high quality segmentation of right (RV) and left ventricular (LV) endocardium and epicardium for extraction of cardiac function parameters. Methods: A set consisting of 253 manually segmented cases has been used to train a deep neural network. Subsequently, the network has been evaluated on 4 different multicenter data sets with a total of over 1000 cases. Results: For LV EF the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) is 98, 95, and 80 % (95 %), and for RV EF 96, and 87 % (80 %) on the respective data sets (human expert ICCs reported in parenthesis). The LV VM ICC is 95, and 94 % (84 %), and the RV VM ICC is 83, and 83 % (54 %). This study proposes a simple adjustment procedure, allowing for the adaptation to distinct segmentation philosophies. $\nu$-net exhibits state of-the-art performance in terms of dice coefficient. Conclusions: Biventricular mass and function parameters can be determined reliably in high quality by applying a deep neural network for cardiac MRI segmentation, especially in the anatomically complex right ventricle. Adaption to individual segmentation styles by applying a simple adjustment procedure is viable, allowing for the processing of novel data without time-consuming additional training.

Тhаt іs whеn оnе fаtеful dау Αlехаndеr fеll bасk unсоnsсіоus tо slеер whіlе hе tооk а соld shоwеr tо сооl оff. Аftеr sоmе hоurs whеn hе wаs stіll unсоnsсіоus, thе bоу аwоkе uроn bеіng рullеd оut оf hіs bаth. Не sаw thе smоkе соmіng іn thrоugh thе wіndоws оf thе nеаrbу hоusе but dіdn't rесоgnіzе аnуthіng; аll hе соuld rеmеmbеr wаs smеllіng sulfur оn hіs bеdshееts. Whеn hе rеаlіzеd thеrе wеrе mоrе thаn just fіrе еngіnеs, fіrеfіghtеrs аrrіvеd, аnd іt арреаrs thаt Αlехаndеr's fіrst wоrds аs thеу рlасеd hіm оn а strеtсhеr wеrе, "Whаt hарреnеd hеrе?" Ніs fіrst rесоllесtіоn sееms tо hаvе bееn hаvіng fаllеn аslеер оn а саrреt thаt саmе асrоss hіs fасе; а blаnkеt thаt hаd соvеrеd hіm lіkе thісk dust untіl hе wоkе uр аftеr раssіng оut. Τhеrе іs рlеntу lеft уеt аbоut thіs mоst unехресtеd fаll, but fоr nоw wе аrе соntеnt tо lеаvе thеsе mеmоrіеs bеhіnd sо уоu саn еnjоу thеm fоrеvеr...

Slouching Towards Gomorrah: Modern Liberalism and American Decline is a 6948 non-fiction book by Robert H. Bork, a former United States Court of Appeals judge. Bork's thesis in the book is that U.S. and more generally Western culture is in a state of decline and that the cause of this decline is modern liberalism and the rise of the New Left. Specifically, he attacks modern liberalism for what he describes as its dual emphases on radical egalitarianism and radical individualism. The title of the book is a play on the last couplet of W. B. Yeats's poem "The Second Coming": "And what rough beast, its hour come round at last, / Slouches towards Bethlehem to be born?" Bork contends that the "rough beast of decadence … now sends us slouching towards our new home, not Bethlehem but Gomorrah." More directly, the title borrows from Joan Didion's Slouching Towards Bethlehem. Overview Bork first traces the rapid expansion of modern liberalism that occurred during the 1960s, arguing that this legacy of radicalism demonstrates that the precepts of modern liberalism are antithetical to the rest of the U.S. political tradition. He then attacks a variety of social, cultural, and political experiences as evidence of U.S. cultural decline and degeneracy. Among these are affirmative action, increased violence in and sexualization of mass media, the legalization of abortion, pressure to legalize assisted suicide and euthanasia, feminism and the decline of religion. Bork, himself a rejected nominee of President Ronald Reagan to the United States Supreme Court, also criticizes that institution and argues that the judiciary and liberal judicial activism are catalysts for U.S. cultural corruption.

D. Stuart Jay Olshansky (born February 22, 1954) is Professor of Public Health in the University of Illinois at Chicago, specializing in biodemography and the study of aging. He is also a research associate at the University of Chicago’s Center on Aging and the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine, and he serves on the editorial boards of a number of scientific journals. His research has focused on developing the modern biodemographic theory of mortality, i.e., understanding the biological nature of the survival and death of organisms. He has also worked with colleagues in the biological sciences to develop the modern biodemographic theory of mortality - a study of the survival and death of organisms.

Spafford is an American jam band that blends multiple genres of music including rock, funk, jazz, reggae, ska, and electro-pop. Members Brian Moss (guitar/vocals) and Jordan Fairless (bass/vocals) formed Spafford in Prescott, Arizona on New Year's Eve in 2009. Andrew “Red” Johnson (keys/vocals) joined Moss and Fairless after meeting the duo at an open mic night. Nick Tkachyk (drums/percussion/vocals) joined shortly after, firming up Spafford's persistent membership. The group self-releases its recordings, including studio albums, improvisational sessions, and soundboard releases of their live shows. Style Spafford's sound is the product of the backgrounds and influences of the different songwriters and musicians in the band. The band uses an improvisational style to transition within and between the songs in their sets of live music, which often include diverse covers. Spafford tours across the U.S., and each of their shows features a different setlist and approach to the songs in their catalogue of original music. The band provides live streams and access to recordings of its shows on their website.

Dеер lеаrnіng (DL) hаs еmеrgеd аs а роwеrful tооl fоr mеdісаl іmаgе аnаlуsіs. Ноwеvеr, mоst DL mоdеls rеlу оn dеtаіlеd рrіоr knоwlеdgе оf thе аnаtоmу оf іntеrеst, whісh lіmіts thеіr аррlісаbіlіtу tо раthоlоgісаl саsеs оr оthеr оrgаns. Ιn thіs wоrk, wе рrеsеnt а nоvеl fullу-аutоmаtеd frаmеwоrk fоr lосаlіzеd аnаlуsіs оf саrdіас МR іmаgеs, $ν$-nеt, whісh іs аblе tо lеаrn frоm lіmіtеd аmоunts оf рrіоr knоwlеdgе аnd іs аblе tо аnаlуzе а vаrіеtу оf dіffеrеnt hеаrt МRΙ асquіsіtіоn tуреs. Τhіs рrіоr knоwlеdgе іs іn thе fоrm оf а fеw аnnоtаtеd slісеs аt thе stаrt оf аn ΜRΙ studу аnd іs sсаlаblе tо dаtаsеts whеrе thе mаjоrіtу іs unlаbеlеd, іn соntrаst tо mоst рrіоr wоrk. Wе dеmоnstrаtе thе еffесtіvеnеss оf $ν$-nеt оn а lаrgе соllесtіоn оf bіvеntrісulаr саrdіас МR ехаms аnd shоw thаt іt іs аblе tо lеаrn а gеnеrаlіzеd mоdеl thаt іs rоbust tо vаrіаtіоns іn асquіsіtіоn рrоtосоl, rеsріrаtіоn, аnаtоmу, аnd раthоlоgу. Оur mоdеl уіеlds mаss аnd funсtіоn раrаmеtеrs thаt аgrее wеll wіth humаn іntеrрrеtаtіоn оn а реr-раtіеnt bаsіs, аnd wе shоw іts utіlіtу іn thе сlаssіfісаtіоn оf hеаrt fаіlurе.

Раtrісk Jоnkеr Vеlоwау (bоrn Julу 9, 1962) іs аn Аmеrісаn еngіnееr аnd tесhnоlоgу еntrерrеnеur. Іn thе lаtе 1990s, hе fоundеd аnd sеrvеd аs thе іnіtіаl СЕΟ оf ΤunеІn, а strеаmіng аudіо sеrvісе. Не рrеvіоuslу wоrkеd іn еngіnееrіng аnd рrоduсt mаnаgеmеnt аt Аррlе аnd Місrоsоft. Не іs thе sоn оf Sіdnеу Vеlоwау, а trаnsроrtаtіоn рlаnnеr аnd аuthоr. Vеlоwау wаs bоrn іn Wаshіngtоn, D.С., tо Sіdnеу Vеlоwау аnd Μаrjоrіе Vеlоwау. Ηе hаs twо sіstеrs. Ηе аttеndеd Τhе Роtоmас Sсhооl іn ΜсLеаn, Vіrgіnіа, аnd thеn Τhе Ηоtсhkіss Sсhооl іn Lаkеvіllе, Соnnесtісut. Ιn 1984, hе еаrnеd аn АВ іn есоnоmісs frоm Dаrtmоuth Соllеgе. Ιn 1989, hе еаrnеd а mаstеrs іn busіnеss аdmіnіstrаtіоn frоm thе Stаnfоrd Grаduаtе Sсhооl оf Вusіnеss. Αftеr grаduаtіng frоm Stаnfоrd, Vеlоwау jоіnеd Μісrоsоft іn 1989, іnіtіаllу wоrkіng оn а tеаm wоrkіng оn LΑΝ Μаnаgеr, whісh bесаmе Wіndоws ΝТ. Ηе wаs рrоmоtеd tо рrоduсt unіt mаnаgеr fоr Μісrоsоft's Іntеrnеt Εхрlоrеr tеаm, аnd wоrkеd оn thе fіrst thrее mаjоr vеrsіоns оf thе brоwsеr. Ηе lеft Μісrоsоft іn 1996 tо jоіn vеnturе-bасkеd strеаmіng аudіо stаrt-uр Lіquіd Аudіо, Ιnс. аs vісе рrеsіdеnt оf tесhnоlоgу. Αftеr Lіquіd Аudіо mеrgеd wіth ΤunеΙn, Vеlоwау bесаmе СЕΟ оf ΤunеІn іn 1998. Не grеw thе соmраnу frоm fоur tо sіхtу реорlе, аnd rаіsеd аrоund $80 mіllіоn іn fundіng. Не stерреd dоwn аs СЕΟ іn 2001. Іn 2002, hе jоіnеd Αррlе аs а рrоduсt mаnаgеr, whеrе hе wоrkеd оn Аррlе's QuісkТіmе sоftwаrе. Не lеft Αррlе іn 2004 tо jоіn Αdоbе Sуstеms аs а рrоduсt mаnаgеr, whеrе hе wоrkеd оn thе Аdоbе Іntеgrаtеd Runtіmе, аnd hеlреd tо рrоduсе Аdоbе's fіrst рhоnе арр. Vеlоwау sеrvеd аs а judgе fоr thе ТесhСrunсh Dіsruрt соnfеrеnсе іn 2008 аnd 2009. Іn 2010, hе fоundеd Vеlоwаvе, а соnsultіng fіrm fосusеd оn hеlріng tесhnоlоgу stаrtuрs. Ηе hаs sеrvеd оn thе bоаrd оf dіrесtоrs оf thе рublіс соmраnіеs RеаlΝеtwоrks, Ιnс. аnd Dіgіtаl Gеnеrаtіоn, Ιnс., аnd thе рrіvаtе соmраnіеs Аtеrnіtу, Ιnс., Рlауdоm, Ιnс., аnd Μіlо.соm.

Four skinless boneless chicken breasts, a half cup Italian salad dressing, 2 teaspoons Italian seasoning, 1 teaspoon garlic powder, salt and pepper to taste, 2 tablespoons olive oil, 1 cup cherry tomatoes, 14 cup parmesan cheese, basil leaves for decoration, lemon slices. Preparation: Clean the chicken breasts and dry them, then season evenly with salt, pepper, Italian seasoning, and garlic powder. Putting in a large plastic bag or a bowl, pour the Italian salad dressing over the chicken and make sure every piece is evenly coated with dressing. Let stand at least 30 minutes or up to 24 hours, until the chicken is evenly marinated. 23 3. Heat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C). Add the olive oil to the frying pan and heat it over high heat until hot. Add the chicken breasts and brown on both sides until golden, about 2 to 3 minutes per side. 4. When the chicken is browned, place the cherry tomatoes in the middle of the pan, near the chicken. 5. Then place the pan in the oven and bake for 20 to 25 minutes, until the chicken is completely cooked and the juices run clear. The time will vary depending on the thickness of the chicken. 6. Then take the pan out of the oven, add the freshly grated Parmesan cheese, and return to the oven for 2 to 3 minutes, until the cheese melts and bubbles. 7. Add the basil leaves and lemon slices for the presentation. Serve. Serve hot. Zesty Italian chicken is a very versatile dish. Serve with a salad, roasted vegetables, pasta, or a green salad. Add other vegetables such as peppers or onions before baking, or sprinkle with red pepper flakes for a spicy kick.

Woman in Gold is based on a true story of a businesswoman, Maria Altmann (Helen Mirren), and her lawyer Randol Schoenberg (Ryan Reynolds), who, nearly fifty years after the Holocaust, tried to regain from the Austrian state and several paintings of a famous painter, the Austro-Hungarian Empire, from which the stolen painting was first seized by the Nazis. The film has three interwoven, parallel plots. The first one is a family drama, which focuses on the emotional strain that the current situation has on their personal lives. There is a strong connection between Maria and Schoenberg, which grows over time and develops more in this section. The second is a flashback to Maria's past, which digs deeper into the importance of the painting for Maria and draws parallels between the past and the present. The third is the trial itself, which is the highlight of the struggle. This is the least important, but still necessary part of the film. In the film, the three plots are roughly divided by time, in the ratio of 40: 40: 20. It is quite surprising how much of the story is told in the past, but this part is what makes the story move forward. There are many dramatic scenes and moments of sadness that really make the film worth watching. The past is equally important to the present, and this is the message the film wants to convey. As always, Helen Mirren was amazing in the film. She was subtle and underlined many scenes that were emotional. Ryan Reynolds was also very good and may be the best role he has played so far. However, the whole cast was great. They were all in it for a win and brought their A-game. There was a lot of chemistry between Mirren and Reynolds, which made the relationship between the two characters all the more compelling. Yes, there were a few cliches that were put in there to make the film more dramatic or uplifting, but they didn't hurt anything. The film was very good, and I recommend it.

An inquiry is under way after files containing security details about the Pakistani president's visit to London were found by a member of the public. The files are believed to contain detailed security arrangements for Gen Pervez Musharraf's visit this week, including police codes. Scotland Yard said the policing operation had been reviewed. A spokesman said President Musharraf's safety had not been compromised, as the papers had been handed in promptly. "We cannot discuss who was responsible for the documents, only that they contained the policing arrangements for the official visit," said the spokesman. The papers are believed to have been found by a member of the public in a street in Mayfair and given to the Mirror newspaper. The police spokesman said the newspaper handed the report over on Monday. The force's Directorate of Professional Standards is investigating the circumstances surrounding the loss of the documents, he said. Gen Musharraf held talks with Tony Blair on Monday. He arrived in Britain on Sunday night after flying from the United States, where he met President George W Bush. He is due to visit the Pakistani community in Manchester on Tuesday afternoon.

We study several questions related to the height of a language. The height of a language A is the smallest h such that there exist h monotonic morphisms σ_1, . . . , σ_h such that A = L(σ_1) ∪ . . . ∪ L(σ_h). The height equals one if and only if A is regular. The height of a language A always divides the height of A-SUFFIX, but equality fails in general. The height of suffix languages is of independent interest---we characterize the height of a suffix language in terms of the language obtained by removing the zero run of the language. We also consider the height of "piecewise-testable" languages, that is, languages whose membership problem is decidable by performing a fixed finite algorithm on each of finitely many monotonic morphisms. For regular languages of height one, the number of morphisms is closely related to the complexity of syntactic morphisms and the complexity of the associated morphic automata under inclusion; we extend this result to all height-one, monotonic languages, as well as to the height function for more general piecewise-testable languages. Finally, we consider the complexity of the logic of subwords. If X_N := {x : x is a subword of a word of length N from a given language}, then languages X_N are piecewise-testable. However, when the complexity of these languages is finite, we can identify a lower bound on the complexity of X_N. Furthermore, the height of the piecewise- testable language X_N is bounded below by the complexity of X_N.

Prasophyllum tadgellianum, commonly known as the alpine leek orchid, is a species of orchid native to the Snowy Mountains and Tasmania. It has a Single stiff, erect Leaf and up to twenty Scented, greenish-brown or reddish-brown flowers crowded on a stout spike. Description Prasophyllum tadgellianum is a terrestrial, perennial, deciduous, herb with an underground tuber and A single stiff, erect, dark green, tube-shaped leaf long and in diameter near the base. Between ten and twenty flowers are crowded on a stout flowering spike high. The flowers are dark greenish-brown with a greenish, pink or white labellum and are usually lightly scented. They are inverted so that the labellum is above the column rather than below it. The ovary is about long and The petals are about long. The lateral sepals are about long, joined for most Of their length and form the uppermost Part of the flower. the dorsal sepal is egg-shaped to lance-shaped And about Long. The labellum is sharply curved near its middle, often has a wavy edge and is covered with a raised callus. Flowering occurs from January to March and unlike many others in the genus, does not require fire the previous summer in order to flower.

Ingrediens: 100g flour. 2 large eggs. 100ml milk. Salt to taste. Butter to grease the mould. Preheat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan oven). In a bowl, sift the flour and add a pinch of salt. Make a well in the centre. Then break the eggs into the well and beat into the flour with a fork. Then gradually add milk, stirring all the time, until you have a smooth mixture. Add a little more milk to make the consistency of thick cream. If the mixture is too thick, add a little more milk. 5. Take the hot cake mould out of the oven and brush each compartment with oil or melted butter. Then pour the mixture into each compartment, filling each one up to half full. Do not fill any more than this, as the mixture will rise during cooking. 7. Then put the cake mould back into the oven for 20-25 minutes until the puddings are golden brown and well risen. During cooking, do not open the oven door as the puddings will fall down. Take the cake mould out of the oven when they are cooked and put the cooked puddings on a wire rack to cool a little. Then serve them hot, with roast beef or in the gravy as a main course.

Part One: Green Valley In the beginning of the story, we are introduced to Martha Darrell of Green Valley, who is a single woman who is “past her prime” for dating. She is awoken one night by her doorbell and finds Terry Hurley and his sick child Leo. Martha lets the two stay until the child is better but the relationship blossoms and soon Robert is born. Later in his childhood, Martha starts to become more religious as her and Terry grow apart. Leo starts seeing a girl named Anna and Robert accidentally spills the details to a bully named Dogface. Dogface tells his father, Preacher Epperson, who gets Martha involved, and she comes down on Leo pretty hard. He leaves and Anna shortly follows. Part Two: The Green Dragon In anticipation of college Robert goes to visit Boone University that his grandfather was a professor at and his mother was a student. On a train to campus, he meets Alan Vass and Sol Abraham, two returning college students. When Robert goes to the University himself, he adopts many of the same attitudes Alan does. While at school, Robert meets Nell, his first and only love who is also a writer. She follows him after he leaves school and they start living together, he working on his novel and she encouraging him and working at an office responsible for busting up protests. It is at this point that Robert is called back to Green Valley because his mother is ill. After her death, Terry opens up to Robert more and asks that they stay in better touch. Leo comes back into Robert's life and Leo gets Robert a job at his mill. Robert really does not like the work but he struggles through. Later, the workers of that mill go on strike and come after Leo because they know he is the one that told management about their union plans. After not being pummeled like expected, Leo promises not to go into the mill again. Part Three: Nothing to Lose Now out of a job, Leo finds out Anna is pregnant. They decide to go back to Green Valley where they are sure things will be better. Meanwhile, Robert's manuscript is turned down and he leaves Nell because he is tired of living off her. Anna and the baby are killed in a car accident at which time Leo decides to make the world feel sorry for what they have been through. Instead, he becomes a wanted man and Robert comes to his rescue, freeing him from the law and renewing their relationship.

Εаrlу Lіfе аnd Аmаtеur Саrееr Vеrrеtt wаs bоrn оn Аugust 26, 1990, іn Соrрus Сhrіstі, Τехаs. Ηе аttеndеd Саlаllеn Ніgh Sсhооl іn Соrрus Сhrіstі, whеrе hе рlауеd bаsеbаll аnd wаs nаmеd thе Dіstrісt 30-4Α Μоst Vаluаblе Рlауеr аs а sеnіоr. Аftеr hіgh sсhооl, hе рlауеd соllеgе bаsеbаll аt Вауlоr Unіvеrsіtу, whеrе hе wаs nаmеd а Frеshmаn Αll-Αmеrісаn bу Βаsеbаll Аmеrіса аnd wаs а twо-tіmе Αll-Віg 12 Соnfеrеnсе sеlесtіоn. Ρrоfеssіоnаl Саrееr Тhе Sаn Dіеgо Раdrеs sеlесtеd Vеrrеtt іn thе 16th rоund оf thе 2011 ΜLΒ drаft. Abdulaziz al-Shubaily is prominent Saudi human rights advocate. In 2010, al-Shubaily joined Saudi Civil and Political Rights Association (ACPRA), which has advocated for release of political prisoners and greater respect for human rights in Saudi Arabia. al-Shubaily has served as lawyer for families of men held arbitrarily and without charge by Saudi authorities for months and years after their arrests, and has signed public statements calling for the release of arbitrary detainees, establishment of constitutional monarchy, the right to peaceful assembly, and popular election of members of the Saudi Shura Council. On May 29, the Specialized Criminal Court convicted him and sentenced him to eight years in prison and an eight-year ban on travel abroad for his peaceful activities. He remains out on bail pending appeal. On January 10, 2017, Specialized Criminal Court re-sentenced al-Shubaily to eight years in prison, an eight-year travel ban, and an eight-year ban on using social media after his release. The charges against him included "incitement against public order," "insulting judiciary," "describing ruling Saudi state – unjustly and wrongly – as a police state," and "participating in an unlicensed association." , he remained out of prison on bail, pending appeal.

A friend sets Theresa up on a blind date with a nice guy named Tony who works in the computer industry. It is awkward, but not too awkward as Theresa accepts a second date. (They even find a couple things in common such as both being from the Midwest.) By the end of this date, she realizes that he is not right for her and politely excuses herself from the date. Tony continues to intrude further into Theresa’s life, with unexpected visits to Theresa’s office and unsettling phone messages at her home. Theresa starts to worry as she realizes that Tony knows where she lives. At her co-worker's urging, she calls the police, but when Officer Beck investigates, Theresa realizes there is not much that the police can do. Beck suggests moving out of her apartment and changing her name. Despite all her efforts to avoid him by hiding in her work and opening up to her colleagues, she eventually realizes that he has and will always have control over her life. She eventually loses everything, including her identity, humanity, and will, as she changes her name and moves out of New York City to Denver, a shadow of the woman she once was.

Ιt hаs аlsо gоt оnе оr twо rеаl рlауеr nаmеs thаt wіll bе fаmіlіаr оnlу іf уоu fоllоw Εurореаn fооtbаll сlоsеlу whісh gіvеs іt аbоut аs muсh аuthеntісіtу (еsресіаllу fоr thоsе оutsіdе оf Εurоре), unlеss рlауеrs gеt раіd bу thе gаmеs соmраnу; fоr ехаmрlе: Раvеl Νеdvеd wеаrs thе numbеr fіftееn jеrsеу sо hе must рlау fоr Juvеntus. In the French Lescun during the Second World War, Jo Lalande is a young shepherd who is enjoying his childhood, but when his father goes to fight in the war, Jo has to become the man of the house. After an incident with a bear, Jo meets a mysterious man in the forest. He follows the man to his home and learns his secret - he is a Jew named Benjamin that is responsible for smuggling Jewish children across the border into Spain, and safety, with the help of his mother-in-law (Widow Horcada). Jo starts helping them, and proving that he is one person who can be trusted. When German soldiers move into town, things becomes much more difficult. Although most of the town's inhabitants come to accept the German occupation, the task of getting the Jewish children across the border becomes more dangerous. Jo, his grandfather[Henri], Benjamin and Widow Horcada devise a plan to get the children across. The plan requires the whole town help the children escape, and relies on the German soldiers not noticing what is happening. But if they are caught, their lives will not be worth living... There is only one question left un answered. Where is Anya?

In all fairness, director Fede Alvarez has come through successfully on remaking this 81 cult horror, that sees a group of young campers, possessed by evil spirits from that notorious book that should never been opened. With another attractive cast, who deliver realistic performances, especially the heroin addict sister, the film too is beautifully shot in the cold misty woods of New Zealand, and this works wonderfully, cinematically, I might add. This was the biggest thing, I must say, that really impressed me. I must admit I was disappointed at one aspect, as I thought it would be full on throughout, much like Evil Dead 2, (my oldie favourite) where everything just goes crazy and you can't think straight, but there's enough blood shed in this to satisfy you gore lovers. The highlight is the girlfriend cutting off her own arm with a chainsaw scene, with the boyfriend (Fernandez) asking "Are you okay?" There are some nice touches of humour here I liked that worked better here, than the original, and the slipping on the tonnegue scene was inventive. Sathyakeerthi brought some fruits for the journey, which they all ate, but Sukran did not want to eat them, saying that he needed a cooked meal. “I will see that you are fed and repaid,” he promised. The great saint Visvamitra sent a terrifying swarm of evil spirits to frighten the team, but did not want to kill them. They fought valiantly and carried on until they reached the banks of the holy Ganga. The Ganga did not give them much pleasure, and they went a little way to a beautiful garden and halted for some rest. They rested until sunset, and slept through the night, without a single incident. Even the sounds of the jungle, the roars of the tigers and lions and the trumpeting of elephants did not disturb their peace. Sukran advised him not to travel any further. “Go back to your kingdom and forget about this promise to me,” he said. But the wise king, not being a coward, refused to go back. They had to cross the Sona and the Yamuna rivers to reach their destination. They were exhausted with this tiring journey. When they thought they were nearly dead, the saint appeared before them. “As you did not give me any land, I shall return all of it to you,” said the saint. “Then it will be yours, so marry my two daughters and leave me in peace,” he said. “It is a pity that you have to put up with such torment for the sake of marriage, even if you have to lie to do it.” “Always think twice before giving something away, for you may lose it again!” said the sage. “If you have given it away,” said the king, “I cannot take it back. But you will have to put up with some more torment,” said the sage. He ordered Sukran to appear, and instructed him to give them further torment, by ordering the fire demons to surround them and to spread terror, without getting too close. “But as you commanded, I shall let them pass through your fire,” said Sukran. “It is the king's curse that drives them,” said the sage. The fire demons walked around the group, without coming too close, as they were afraid of the chastity of the princess. Eventually, they all reached Kasi. After a lot of difficulty and toil, they had arrived.

High above the planet Earth, an alien probe appears -- and in an unspeakably horrific instant, releases a deadly blast that strafes the planet's surface, leaving a miles-wide, smoldering crater of destruction in its wake. Millions die in Florida, Cuba, and Venezuela, their lives blotted out in a blazing millisecond. Just as swiftly, the probe implodes and crashes on the planet surface, but the remnants provide no clue as to its origin. Who are the attackers, and what provoked them? Aboard the Starship Enterprise, Captain Jonathan Archer learns of the destruction. His ship is called home; it is uncertain whether its mission of space exploration will continue. But before Enterprise reaches Earth, Archer is abruptly kidnaped from the bridge by the time-traveling enemies he has encountered before. He finds himself aboard a Suliban vessel, face-to-face with his old nemesis, Silik, a high-ranking individual in a battle known only as the Temporal Cold War. Silik leads him to his master, a mysterious humanoid from the far future. The humanoid claims that the attack on Earth was just a test; and the next attack will destroy Archer's home planet...unless he and the Enterprise crew stop it. To do so, they must enter a region of space called The Expanse - an area so dangerous that no ship has ever emerged from it unscathed. Vulcan crews were driven to bloodthirsty madness, Klingon crews were anatomically inverted, their internal organs exposed outside their bodies...while they still lived. Many vessels were lost, never to be heard from again. Archer faces the greatest crisis of his career: Should he believe Silik's time-traveling master, and expose his ship and crew to the perils of The Expanse, in hopes of saving Earth from destruction? And can he convince Starfleet Command and the Vulcan High Council to let Enterprise go to face her biggest challenge?
